jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
About Discovery Life Sciences:

Discovery Life Sciences (Discovery) is a leading provider of highly characterized human biospecimens and cellular starting materials to advance cell and gene therapy and precision medicine programs for cancer, infectious disease, and other complex conditions. We routinely manage hundreds of studies and expertly test thousands of biospecimens simultaneously. Leading biopharma, diagnostic and academic institutions trust us to quickly deliver high-quality biospecimens and reliable, reproducible biomarker data, so they can outpace their competition and push the leading edge of innovation using our Science at your Service TM business model.

Position Summary:

Discovery is looking for a talented and passionate Business Development Director to join our dynamic biospecimen products sales team. As a Business Development Director, you will be an individual contributor, responsible for growing top line revenue and increasing market share by supporting the use of our products in the fields of BioPharma Discovery, Translational, and Clinical Research. This will be accomplished by comprehensive planning and executing sales strategies in your assigned territory. We offer an exciting and collaborative work environment where you can unleash your creativity and make a real impact.

A Day in the Life of a Business Development Director at Discovery Life Sciences:

Prospect and source potential biopharma customers
Meet with potential customers to understand their scientific research and where our company can add value to their research.
Attend networking events.
Collaborate with scientific SMEs to obtain sales contracts.
Build and update business development strategy for current territory.

Position Qualifications (Education, Skills, Experience):

BSc, MSc, or PhD in a life science preferred
Minimum of five (5) years of field-based sales experience in Life Sciences, CDMO, or Biotech to biopharma customers.
Experience in human biospecimens OR cell and gene therapy sales required.
Proven track record of achieving 100% of quota.
Ability to work with clients, actively listen to needs, and translate into opportunities.
Ability to build and nurture relationships with clients and potential clients.
Team-first attitude and passion to achieve Commercial Team and company-wide goals.
Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational skills and the ability to prioritize multiple tasks.
Excellent computer skills to include Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Google Docs.
SalesForce.com experience is desirable but not required.
Must be located in the greater Boston, MA area.

Key Responsibilities:

Develop, propose, and implement monthly, quarterly and annual territory plans to meet revenue goals and achieve quota attainment.
Generate new business through a high level of customer and prospect contact including frequent direct customer visits and extensive networking.
Actively manage a pipeline of 100 opportunities, keeping information up to date, and logging call notes from field activity
Communicate clearly to executive stakeholders including operations, marketing, SMEs, and project management teams, to ensure that prospects are provided with well-orchestrated and timely information to ensure successful closure of opportunities.
Work closely and collaboratively with assigned Project Manager towards attainment of territory goal and 100% customer success
Develop and maintain deep product knowledge to sell consultatively and make recommendations to prospective clients on solutions that best meet their needs.
Maintain the integrity of the data in the CRM with updated contact and account information
Demonstrate strategic business awareness of the market to differentiate Discovery brand from the competition.
Attend conferences, trade shows, and seminars as required.
Respect the privacy of the personal information of patients, co-workers, and all individuals with whom the Company interacts.

Compensation and Benefits:

Discovery Life Sciences is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we strive to provide employees with total compensation packages that are market competitive. For this role, the anticipated total compensation range is $200,000-$240,000 (base + commission at 100% of target). The exact base pay offered for this role will depend on various factors, including but not limited to the candidate's qualifications, skills, and experience.

Your annual salary is only one part of your total compensation package. Other benefits:

Competitive salary and benefits package options, including a free dental, vision package, life insurance, and disability coverage which start on your first day of employment.
401(k) match program which starts on your first day of employment.
Time away from work (Generous vacation and paid time off, paid parental leave, paid family leave, etc.).
Professional development opportunities and reimbursement for relevant certifications and tuition.
Collaborative and inclusive work environment that values diversity.
Team-building activities and social events.
Employee Referral Program and Colleague Recognition Program.

Location:

Remote – must live near assigned territory (greater Boston, MA area)
Up to 50% travel domestic.

We are actively seeking motivated, dedicated individuals like you to join our thriving organization. As a leader in our industry, we offer unparalleled opportunities for professional growth and success.

jobs.title: Regional Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Regional Director of Operations

The Regional Director of Operations will report directly to the Regional Vice President and will oversee several branches across the region. While the role provides broader regional oversight, as the company continues to strengthen and expand its presence in this market, this position will drive operational performance, customer retention, financial improvement, leadership accountability, and regional growth while ensuring branch priorities are consistently executed.

Why This Role

This is an ideal opportunity for an operations leader who wants to take the next step in their career and have a visible impact on a growing region. The Regional Director of Operations will have direct exposure to regional leadership and will play a vital role in improving operations, strengthening client relationships, developing branch leaders, and driving growth throughout the region. This role offers the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful regional priorities, solve complex operational challenges, and directly influence the performance and direction of the business. Successful performance in this position can create opportunities for increased responsibility and advancement within the company. For a motivated leader who wants to grow beyond managing individual accounts or a single branch, this role provides the experience, visibility, and responsibility needed to advance their career.

Operational Focus

Maintain a consistent focus on customer retention by identifying account risks, addressing service concerns, and developing strategies to strengthen client relationships.
Review upcoming client rate increases and coordinate with operational and financial teams to ensure increases are implemented accurately and on schedule.
Review branch financial performance, including revenue, gross profit, labor performance, and budget variances, and develop corrective action plans where needed.
Audit payroll and invoice adjustments, identify recurring issues, and implement corrective measures to improve accuracy and reduce adjustments.
Audit regional vehicle inventory and related billing data to ensure accurate records, appropriate utilization, and proper client billing.
Audit overtime, unfilled shifts, and other labor hours, and develop strategies to reduce unnecessary labor costs and improve scheduling efficiency.
Analyze employee turnover trends and implement strategies to improve retention and reduce turnover.
Review regional equipment, uniform, technology, and supply usage to reduce unnecessary costs and ensure client requirements are met.
Oversee new account launches, major expansions, and client transitions to ensure staffing, training, equipment, and operational requirements are completed before implementation.
Provide regular updates and reports on branch leaders, including individual performance, progress against expectations, areas of improvement, and ongoing development needs.

Sales and Growth

Establish regional growth targets and regularly report progress, risks, and forecasted results to the Regional Vice President.
Track the regional sales pipeline, including lead status, proposal activity, expected revenue, and next steps, and hold branch leaders accountable for follow-up.
Submit weekly sales leads, audit lead-generation activity across the region, report on progress, and develop improvement plans where performance is below expectations.
Identify new business opportunities, target markets, and prospective clients that support regional growth objectives.
Identify opportunities to expand services, locations, hours, or solutions with existing clients.
Review lost opportunities and unsuccessful proposals to identify trends and improve future sales strategies.

Experience

Bachelor's degree in business or related field
3-5 years prior Branch Manager, Regional Manager, or similar
Certification is relevant fields a plus

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk
Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times

Compensation

$105,000.00 - $115,000.00 per year
Sales Commission Plan
Annual Discretionary Bonus
Other - Fuel Card

Benefits

Paid time off
Health insurance
Dental insurance
Vision insurance

jobs.description:
Future Tech Enterprise, Inc. is seeking a highly experienced, global-minded Chief Operating Officer to lead enterprise-wide operations across a complex, technology-driven organization. The COO will be responsible for aligning strategy with execution, improving operational performance, scaling global business processes, and ensuring disciplined execution across regions, business units, and functional teams.
The ideal candidate must have served as a Chief Operating Officer for at least 5 years, must have direct experience in the technology, IT services, enterprise solutions, systems integration, managed services, or closely related industry, and must have operated within a company generating more than $500 million in annual revenue.
This individual must also bring meaningful global operating experience, including responsibility for international teams, cross-border business operations, global customers, multinational delivery models, or operations spanning multiple countries or regions.
Required Qualifications
Minimum of 10 years of experience serving as a Chief Operating Officer.
Prior COO or equivalent executive operating leadership experience within the technology, IT services, enterprise solutions, systems integration, managed services, digital transformation, or related industry.
Demonstrated experience working for or operating within a company with annual revenue exceeding $500 million.
Proven global leadership experience, including responsibility for operations across multiple countries, regions, or international markets.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and managing cross-border business complexity.
Strong understanding of global operating models, international service delivery, regional compliance requirements, global customer support, vendor ecosystems, and multinational workforce management.
Demonstrated ability to standardize operations globally while adapting execution to local market needs.
Experience managing enterprise-scale operations, including P&L oversight, workforce planning, service delivery, operational transformation, and performance management.

The successful candidate must have a proven record of leading operations in a global or multinational environment. This includes experience with one or more of the following:
Managing operations across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East, or other international regions.

jobs.title: Director of Major Gifts
jobs.description:
Reports To:
Chief Development Officer

Classification:
Full-time | Exempt

Salary & Benefits:
$115,000 to $130,000. We offer a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer contribution, voluntary life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance, paid parental, family care, and gender affirming healthcare leave. We also offer a generous paid time off policy.

Schedule:
Work week and hours fluctuate based on events schedule and will include evenings and weekends on a regular basis. Generally, Monday through Friday; a typical schedule will be 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; flexibility required. We currently operate under a hybrid work schedule and this position must be on-site at a minimum from Tuesday through Thursday. On-site work days can shift depending on work needs.

Summary:
The Director of Major Gifts will oversee the organization’s individual giving vertical and development systems, with a primary focus on strategy development and execution of major gifts and planned giving programs. The Director will oversee and implement individual fundraising and direct response strategies that effectively move existing prospects along the donor pipeline. The Director will cultivate and manage relationships with mid-level donors that lead to annual fund giving upgrades and greater legacy giving commitments. They will also provide insight, reports and recommendations across the individual philanthropy vertical. The Director will manage the Individual & Planned Giving Manager and the Development Systems Manager.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Mid-Level Major and Planned Gifts Strategy & Execution
Develop a comprehensive mid-level major gifts and planned giving strategy.
Prospect, manage and continuously refine a portfolio of ~70 qualified major gift prospects with the capacity to give $1,500 and up.
Conduct donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities through a variety of channels to meet annual revenue targets.
Maintain overall Major Donor and planned giving mapping tools to ensure line of sight and collaboration with CDO.
Continuously research individual major donor prospects and leads and share with the CDO weekly to map outreach.

Individual Giving and Membership Donor Engagement
Supervise the Individual and Planned Giving Manager by supporting and guiding multi-channel, mid-level and sustaining/membership donor relationship building.
Supervise and support the efforts of the Individual and Planned Giving Manager, ensuring they have the tools and capacity to grow revenues on an annual basis.
Explore, recommend and test new strategies and tactics, including direct response (digital and mail), monthly giving, emergency appeal and digital advertising.
Develop and execute a planned giving strategy in partnership with Individual Planned Giving Manager that converts loyalty donors into legacy society members.
Track giving trends (within the organization and especially across peer institutions), assess fundraising performance, and adapt strategies to ensure goal attainment.
In partnership with the CDO and Communications and Marketing lead, craft compelling donor materials, proposals, and impact reports.

Individual Philanthropy Strategy & Leadership
Supervise and support the efforts of the Development Systems Manager to monitor workflow, gift volume and capacity needs, to ensure accurate and timely gift entry and reporting in Salesforce, and make process improvements as needed.
Support critical Development systems work, synthesizing and formatting gift data across the department’s verticals, creating useful tools for tracking performance in real time.
Provide high quality data inputs, management, and reporting to ensure accurate and timely summary of progress to goal achievement for the CDO, CEO and for reporting to the Board of Directors.
In collaboration with the Development Systems Manager create detailed and accurate revenue and expense reports for the department.
Work collaboratively with members of the Finance Team, to support reconciliation of revenues and expenses and the monthly revenue close, to improve efficiencies across teams.
Work collaboratively with colleagues on the TIDE (Technology, Information, Data and Evaluation) to ensure the team is maximizing the benefits of tech stack resources including Salesforce, Blackthorn, Donor Drive, Benevity, DAF Pay and other tools.

Other Collaboration & Internal Partnerships
Work closely with Comms and Marketing Lead to align messaging and donor engagement collateral, including design projects/visual representation of key initiatives, giving levels, campaigns, among other tools for consistency of storytelling and impact.
Work closely with CEO and CDO to brief and prepare for donor meetings.
Partner with program staff to understand impact stories and translate them into donor-facing opportunities for engagement and case for investment.
Other duties as assigned.

Position Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, or related field; or equivalent professional and/or educational experience.
Five (5) to seven (7) years of progressive experience in fundraising, individual and/or major gifts, or advancement leadership.
Demonstrated success securing $500,000 or more annually.
Proven track record of cultivating and closing major gifts of $5,000+.
Knowledge of individual direct marketing strategies and benchmarking.
Demonstrated ability to leverage digital platforms, thought leadership and professional networks to support donor engagement and pipeline development.
Proficiency with CRM and donor management systems (Salesforce preferred).
Ability to work on multiple projects at one time and to set and stick to priorities.
Excellent interpersonal skills; ability to interact with a wide range of personalities.
Knowledge, understanding and experience working with LGBTQ+, TGNC, POC, and Immigrant populations, including knowledge of the spectrum of gender identity, transgender issues, immigration, and POC issues.
Understanding of, and commitment to, undoing structural and institutional racism and bias and the spectrum of gender identity and bias. Thoughtful and articulate analysis of the above, and consideration of the impacts and outcomes in decision-making processes and on underserved and historically oppressed communities as it relates to our work.
A strong commitment to the mission of The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender Community Center.

jobs.description:
Key Law Office and Key Trial Lawyers are two affiliated Texas law firms with five offices across Buda, Austin, Bastrop, New Braunfels, and Victoria, serving clients in family law, estate planning, probate, personal injury, and plaintiff employment law. We are entering an ambitious growth phase and are looking for an experienced, hands-on Chief Executive Officer to lead that growth alongside our Owner and Managing Attorney.

The Opportunity

This is a rare chance to build and run the business side of an established, respected regional firm with a clear mandate: double the firm in size over the next four to five years. You will lead our Chief Operating Officer and the leads of our Intake, Billing, and Marketing departments, and own firm-wide strategy, financial performance, and operations, so our Owner can focus on legal work and professional leadership.

What You'll Do

• Own and execute a multi-year growth plan covering new offices, practice areas, and lateral hiring.
• Supervise and develop the COO and the Intake, Billing, and Marketing leads, building a real executive team.
• Manage firm-wide budgeting, financial reporting, and profitability across five offices.
• Design compensation and incentive structures that align staff performance with growth goals.
• Drive consistent systems, technology, and client experience across every office.
• Build the people, culture, and hiring infrastructure needed to scale without losing what makes the firm distinct.

What We're Looking For

• 10+ years of progressive business leadership, including 5+ years in an executive role with P&L ownership.
• A track record of scaling a professional services or multi-location service business, ideally through a doubling growth phase.
• Strong financial acumen and experience leading operations, sales or intake, finance, and marketing functions.
• Law firm, medical, dental, accounting, or other regulated professional practice experience is a plus, but not required.
• Comfort with a confidential, relationship-driven environment and a community-rooted brand.

Compensation

Competitive flat salary commensurate with experience, plus health coverage, retirement plan participation, PTO, and professional development support.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a resume and a brief cover letter describing relevant executive leadership experience to tyler@keylawoffife.com. Please include "CEO Application" in the subject line.

jobs.title: Chief Advancement Officer
jobs.description:
Partners Worldwide

Partners Worldwide (PW) is a global network of businesspeople working together to end poverty through entrepreneurship and job creation. We believe that all people are image bearers of God and have the right to live an abundant life. Through locally rooted, globally connected partnerships, we work to grow and sustain businesses that create jobs and strengthen communities.

As an employee of Partners Worldwide, you will be part of a global team that values each person as a true partner. Together, we celebrate entrepreneurs who are building businesses, providing for their families, and creating opportunities for others.

Our goal for 2030 is to equip partners in 30+ countries to serve over one million businesses, helping create and sustain 3 million jobs and enabling 15 million people to leave poverty behind.

The Role

The Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) is responsible for growing the relationships and resources that fuel Partners Worldwide’s global work. This role brings fundraising, marketing and communications, and volunteer engagement together under one strategy. It's a broad leadership role that connects resource development, engagement, and storytelling in a way that works together as a whole.

Over three decades, our work has grown through learning and partnership. In the last three years, we’ve more than doubled in scale, and we believe we can do it again. With a historic intergenerational wealth transfer underway, a committed global network, and strong momentum, we’re ready to take the next step together.

This is both a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will lead and develop a high-performing team while also personally engaging major donors and key partners. You will shape how Partners Worldwide tells its story, connects with supporters, and mobilizes people to give their time, skills, and resources to the mission. You will serve as a trellis, creating the structure that enables people, teams, and ideas to grow.

The work is entrepreneurial, global in scope, and time-sensitive. This is a real build opportunity at a moment when the organization is ready to move.

We're looking for a relational, entrepreneurially minded leader who builds real connections, inspires generosity, and equips others to do work that lasts.

The Work

Strategy & Team Leadership

Lead a unified strategy across fundraising, marketing and communications, and volunteer engagement
Partner with the CEO and leadership team to align priorities, messaging, and growth
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing, collaborative team
Establish clear goals and use data to track progress and inform decisions
Strengthen alignment across the advancement team so functions operate in an integrated, collaborative way
Create pathways that enable others to dream bigger and execute with excellence

Fundraising & Relationship Development

Lead a comprehensive fundraising strategy, including major gifts, campaigns, and grants
Personally manage key donor and partner relationships
Partner with the CEO and board on strategic engagement and giving opportunities
Create meaningful experiences that connect supporters to the mission and deepen long-term commitment

Engagement, Storytelling & Operations

Ensure clear, compelling communication and storytelling across donor and partner audiences
Elevate story as a core organizational resource alongside time, talent, and treasure, creating opportunities to share narratives that honor local partners and inspire action
Strengthen pathways for volunteers and business professionals to engage and contribute
Oversee systems and processes that support fundraising effectiveness, including CRM, reporting, and forecasting
Use data and insights to continuously improve performance and impact

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in fundraising, advancement, or related fields
Demonstrated success in major gifts fundraising (including six- and seven-figure gifts) and campaign leadership
Experience working with senior leaders and boards in fundraising and relationship development
Experience overseeing or partnering closely with marketing/communications and engagement functions
Experience in global or cross-cultural contexts preferred
Passion for business, businesspeople, and the marketplace as drivers of dignity and flourishing

Skills & Competencies

Integrated Leadership: Sees the whole system, aligning people, partnerships, and financial resources into a cohesive advancement approach.
Relational & Partnership-Oriented: Builds trust quickly and fosters strong, reciprocal relationships across the network, centering local partners and shared purpose.
Strategic Execution: Translates vision into clear plans and priorities, with disciplined follow-through and a focus on outcomes.
Communication & Story: Communicates with clarity and purpose, using story to engage diverse audiences and inspire meaningful action.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Leads across functions, integrating marketing, fundraising, and volunteer engagement in a coordinated way.
Team Leadership (Player–Coach): Leads and develops a high-performing team, balancing direct engagement with coaching and growth.
Change & Organizational Leadership: Leads thoughtful, phased integration that strengthens alignment while honoring culture and mission.
Cultural Intelligence & Global Perspective: Operates effectively across diverse geographies and faith contexts with awareness and respect.
Entrepreneurial & Data-Informed: Brings a business mindset, using curiosity, resourcefulness, and data to guide decisions and improve results.

Character

Mature Christian faith that is lived out in your life, work, and interactions
Deep alignment with PW’s mission and values
Humble, collaborative, and team-oriented leadership style
A learner’s mindset with openness to growth, feedback, and new approaches
Integrity and strong stewardship of relationships and resources

Our Investment

Meaningful, purpose-driven work that contributes to lasting global impact
Connection to a talented, mission-driven global team
Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits package
Flexible paid time off and a culture that supports healthy rhythms of work and rest
Professional development opportunities and ongoing learning

Additional Information

Travel:
The CAO is expected to travel up to 40% of the time — roughly every other week. Travel is primarily across North America with regular international travel as the global network grows. Travel supports donor cultivation, team partnership, and field engagement.

To Apply:
Please submit your résumé/CV and a brief statement (one page) describing your interest in the role and alignment with the mission of Partners Worldwide.

Location:
Grand Rapids, MI preferred; U.S.-based remote also considered. This is a high-travel role — candidates should expect to be mobile and proximate with donors, partners, and the global team regularly.

Learn more at partnersworldwide.org

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
International Transformation Foundation (ITF) is a nonprofit dedicated to empowering young people and fostering sustainable water resource development. Our mission focuses on improving access to clean water, promoting youth entrepreneurship, and creating economic opportunities in underserved communities. ITF engages young leaders in service projects that address real-world challenges, including clean water initiatives and community development efforts in Africa. Through these programs, participants gain leadership experience while contributing to meaningful global impact. Amherst Campus

Amherst has taken a leadership role among highly selective liberal arts colleges and universities in successfully diversifying the racial, socio-economic, and geographic profile of its student body. The College is similarly committed to enriching its educational experience and its culture through the diversity of its faculty, administration and staff.

Job Description

Amherst College invites applications for the Assistant Director of Advancement Communications position. The Assistant Director of Advancement Communications is a full-time, year-round position. The expected salary range for this job opportunity is: $60,000 to $65,000.

The salary offered will vary based on a number of factors, including but not limited to relevant education, training, and experience, tenure status, and other nondiscriminatory business considerations. Amherst College is pleased to provide a comprehensive, highly competitive benefits package that meets the needs of staff and faculty and their families. Click here for Benefits Information.

The Assistant Director of Advancement Communications plays a central role in strengthening connections between Amherst College and its alumni by developing and promoting compelling storytelling, visual media, and digital engagement. As a key member of a small, highly collaborative team, this position produces high-quality written, visual, and multimedia content that highlights alumni achievements, demonstrates the impact of Amherst, and fosters lifelong engagement with the College.

Reporting to the Director of Advancement Communications, the Assistant Director manages a broad content portfolio that includes feature stories, alumni profiles, multimedia assets, event-based coverage, and digital campaigns. The role also contributes to alumni-facing social media strategy and execution, ensuring alignment with institutional messaging and close coordination with colleagues across Alumni Relations, Major Gifts, Donor Relations, and other Advancement teams. The Assistant Director may also support additional Advancement communications priorities as needed, demonstrating flexibility and responsiveness to evolving strategic and project needs.

The Assistant Director of Advancement Communications is a creative and thoughtful communicator who brings strong judgment, curiosity, and a collaborative approach to their work. An exceptional writer and editor, they produce polished, persuasive content with a consistent voice and impeccable attention to tone, style, and accuracy. They are a careful listener and strategic thinker who excels at shaping clear, compelling narratives and translating complex ideas into engaging, audience-centered content across a variety of platforms. Comfortable managing multiple priorities with autonomy and attention to detail, this individual approaches projects with creativity, a problem-solving instinct, and a strong sense of responsibility to the institution and its constituents.

Advancement staff are expected to promote a positive, solutions-focused workplace culture through professional and constructive engagement in meetings, collaborations, and daily interactions. Advancement work also includes "all-hands-on-deck" events that require occasional evening and weekend participation to support key College events, including-but not limited to-Reunion and Homecoming.

Research, pitch, write, and edit stories and profiles that highlight alumni achievements, institutional priorities, and the impact of philanthropy; conduct interviews to produce authentic, mission-aligned narratives.

Support planning and day-to-day management of alumni-facing social media, including content creation, scheduling, community engagement, and basic performance tracking.
Uphold College editorial, brand, and accessibility standards, ensuring content reflects Amherst's values of inclusion, curiosity, and lifelong learning.
Maintain editorial calendars and manage timelines and deadlines to ensure consistent, timely delivery.
Stay current on digital storytelling formats, social media trends, and emerging tools to strengthen audience engagement.

Project Management

Partner with Advancement colleagues to identify and prioritize storytelling opportunities tied to key initiatives, alumni achievements, and institutional priorities.
Manage end-to-end project workflows by setting timelines, coordinating reviews/approvals, tracking deliverables, and ensuring on-schedule execution.
Maintain relationships with campus partners and external vendors to support collaborative projects and improve processes.
Use performance insights and analytics to inform content decisions and recommend engagement strategies.
Contribute to portfolio planning by identifying emerging needs and new content opportunities.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's Degree.

Strong skills in storytelling, writing, visual communication, and project management, with the ability to translate complex ideas into clear, engaging, audience-centered content.

Job Title
Executive Director of Technology Operations

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment

Partner with product management, engineering, IT, finance, HR, and business leaders to align technology operations with business priorities.
Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives and technology-enabled business growth.
Ensure effective coordination across global technology teams.

VIII. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead high-performing technology operations teams.
Develop leadership capabilities, succession planning, and talent development programs.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Promote employee engagement and collaboration across technology functions.

Qualifications
Education Background

Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related fields.
Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

Work Experience

Typically 18+ years of experience in technology operations, IT management, engineering operations, or related functions, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles.
Proven experience managing large-scale technology organizations, digital transformation programs, and enterprise operations.
Strong background in software development operations, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and technology governance.
Experience in multinational corporations or high-growth technology-driven organizations preferred.

The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.

The Bureau of Administration is committed to delivering strategic support services to strengthen and empower Office of the New York City Comptroller employees as they work toward ensuring the City's fiscal health. We provide service and support in a manner that promotes communication, transparency, and collaboration. These services include Human Resources, Procurement, Payment, Facilities Management, and Budget Management.

Reporting to the Assistant Comptroller for Employment Services, the Executive Director of Human Resources & Labor Relations will provide operational leadership for all human resources and labor relations activities at the Comptroller's Office.

This position develops and implements workforce strategies, employee engagement initiatives, and organizational development efforts that support the Comptroller's Office mission goals and operational objectives and works to build and maintain a high performing team.

Oversees HR operations and records management
Directs recruitment, onboarding and workforce development programs
Oversees performance management and employee evaluations programs
Leverages technology to accomplish unit goals
Develops and manages unit budgets
Ensures compliance with federal, state and local employment laws, collective bargaining agreements and DCAS rules & procedures.
Develops, updates and administers Standard Operating Procedures for operational units.
Perform other duties as may be required.

NOTE: This position is open only to current City of New York employees serving in a permanent Civil Service title of Administrative Staff Analyst or Administrative Manager.

To be considered for this position, PLEASE CLEARLY INDICATE YOUR CURRENT PERMANENT CIVIL SERVICE TITLE on your resume and cover letter.

A master's degree from an accredited college in economics, finance, accounting, business or public administration, public health, human resources management, management science, operations research, organizational behavior, industrial psychology, statistics, personnel administration, labor relations, psychology, sociology, human resources development, political science, urban studies or a Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school, and two years of satisfactory full-time professional experience in one or a combination of the following: working with the budget of a large public or private concern in budget administration, accounting, economic or financial administration, or fiscal or economic research; or in management or methods analysis, operations research, organizational research or program evaluation; or in personnel or public administration, recruitment, position classification, personnel relations, labor relations, employee benefits, staff development, employment program planning/administration, labor market research, economic planning, social services program planning/evaluation, or fiscal management. An associate degree or completion of 60 semester credits from an accredited college and six years of satisfactory full-time professional experience as described in “1” above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory experience, as described in “1” above.

Ability to leverage technology to drive strategic business outcomes.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Operations Maverick Creative | Remote | Full-time About Maverick Creative We are a TikTok Shop and AI affiliate agency that scales 8 and 9 figure e-commerce brands on Amazon, TikTok Shop, and Shopify. Since 2022 we have worked with over 100 brands and driven more than 500 million views.

We run two things for our clients: full TikTok Shop management, and AI affiliate campaigns where faceless AI creator pages drive tracked sales to a brand's Amazon listing. Recent results include a $500K TikTok Shop launch that grew to nearly $800K, an insole brand up 240% in month one, and a skincare brand up 800% in 60 days.

We move fast, we ship daily, and the client experience is the product.

The Role You own everything that happens after the deal is closed.

This is the most senior client-facing role in the company outside the founder. You run account management, delivery operations, onboarding, retention, and the internal team that executes the work. If a client is happy, renewing, and getting results, that is your win. If they are confused, quiet, or asking for a refund, that is your problem to solve.

You are the last set of eyes before anything reaches a client. Nothing goes out without you.

What You Own Account management and client relationships

Serve as the primary point of contact across 25 to 35 active accounts
Run weekly or biweekly client calls with 5-8 top clients, write recaps with clear action items and owners, and chase client inputs until they land
Know the status of every account at all times, including which ones are at risk

Client onboarding

Own the full onboarding flow from signed contract to first content live: contract execution, onboarding form, asset collection, platform access, kickoff call
Get new clients producing inside the first 7 to 10 days

Retention and account saves

Identify at-risk accounts before they churn and intervene
Handle refund requests, contract disputes, and difficult conversations directly
Restructure engagements to retain revenue where a straight refund is not the right outcome
Write graceful offboards when an account genuinely is not a fit

Internal team direction

Set daily priorities for the delivery team with named owners and deadlines
Direct account managers, TikTok Shop operators, content strategists, and the AI video production team
Run the daily and weekly operations calls
Unblock people fast and escalate what you cannot resolve

Quality control

Review all client-facing output before it ships: content, reports, roadmaps, proposals
Enforce content standards so quality issues never reach a client

Systems and SOPs

Build and maintain the processes that make delivery repeatable: onboarding docs, content folder structures, client trackers, campaign SOPs
Document what works so it survives you being out for a week

Vendor and tooling management

Own relationships with software and production vendors
Negotiate pricing, escalate service failures, and control cost exposure

Reporting

Produce a full client status rundown for the founder several times a week, segmented by service line, with blockers named
Maintain the master client dashboard so it is always accurate

Commercial support

Draft contracts and scopes of work
Design creator incentive and rewards programs with the unit economics worked out
Support upsells and expansion conversations with existing clients

What You Do Not Own Closing new business (we have a sales team)
Hiring and firing decisions (these sit with the founder, though your input matters)
Company finances and payroll

What Success Looks Like You will be measured on:

Client retention rate
and average client lifetime, which is the single most important number in this role
Time to first content live
for new clients
Delivery consistency
, meaning contracted content volume actually shipped on time
Blocker age
, meaning nothing sits stuck for weeks without resolution
Reporting reliability
, meaning the founder always knows the true state of the book

Who You Are Required

3+ years in agency operations, account management, or client success, ideally in e-commerce, performance marketing, or creator marketing
You have carried a real book of accounts and kept them alive
Strong written communication. You will be writing to 8 and 9 figure brand owners daily, and tone matters
Comfortable with hard conversations: refunds, missed deliverables, contract disputes
You build systems instead of holding everything in your head
Highly organized under volume. Thirty accounts moving at once does not rattle you
Self-directed. Nobody is going to hand you a task list

Strongly preferred

Working knowledge of TikTok Shop, Amazon Seller Central, or affiliate and creator programs
Experience managing remote teams across time zones
You have negotiated with vendors and held a line on pricing
Comfortable using AI tools to move faster

You will struggle here if

You need clear instructions before you act
You avoid conflict with clients
You are looking for a role with a narrow, well-defined lane

Compensation Base salary plus performance compensation tied to client retention and gross margin. We want this role paid well when the book is healthy and growing, so a meaningful portion of the upside is tied to outcomes you directly control.

On target earnings: $5,000 to $10,000 per month for first six months, depending on experience level. After that promotion to COO is possible as well as a significant salary increase up to $25,000 per month and beyond. 

Exact structure discussed on the call.

How to Apply Send us:

A short note on the largest book of accounts you have personally managed, including how many clients and what the retention looked like
One example of a client you saved from churning, and specifically what you did
One example of a system or SOP you built that outlived your involvement

\# Executive Director — Statewide Medical Specialty Society

\*\*Location:\*\* Kentucky (remote, with occasional in\-state travel)

\*\*Type:\*\* Part\-time, approximately 20–30 hours per week

\*\*Compensation:\*\* $40,000–$60,000 annually, commensurate with experience

\*\*Reports to:\*\* Board of Directors / Society President

\-\-\-

\#\# About the Organization

We are a statewide professional society representing physicians in a surgical subspecialty across Kentucky. Our members are practicing physicians and surgeons in private practice, hospital systems, and academic settings. The Society advances the profession through continuing medical education, an annual scientific meeting, member advocacy at the state level, and coordination with national specialty organizations.

The Society is governed by a volunteer physician Board of Directors. The Executive Director is our sole staff position and the operational center of the organization.

\#\# Position Summary

We are seeking an Executive Director to manage the day\-to\-day operations of the Society and serve as the primary point of contact for members, exhibitors, vendors, and partner organizations. This is a part\-time role performed largely remotely, with periodic travel within Kentucky for board meetings and the annual meeting.

The ideal candidate is a self\-directed administrator who can run a small organization independently — someone comfortable owning everything from membership records to event logistics to board correspondence, without a support staff.

\#\# Key Responsibilities

\*\*Governance and Board Support\*\*

\- Serve as primary staff liaison to the Board of Directors and Society officers

\- Schedule and coordinate board meetings; prepare agendas, materials, and minutes

\- Track and support execution of board decisions and strategic priorities

\- Maintain organizational records, bylaws, and corporate filings

\*\*Membership\*\*

\- Maintain the membership database and handle recruitment, renewals, and retention

\- Respond to member inquiries and serve as the Society's front\-line contact

\- Support committee activity and volunteer engagement

\*\*Annual Meeting and Continuing Education\*\*

\- Plan and execute the Society's annual scientific meeting, including venue coordination, registration, catering, and on\-site management

\- Coordinate speaker logistics, agendas, and program materials

\- Support continuing medical education accreditation requirements and documentation

\*\*Sponsorship and Exhibitor Relations\*\*

\- Recruit and manage industry exhibitors and sponsors

\- Develop and distribute exhibitor prospectus materials; manage sponsor agreements and fulfillment

\- Serve as the primary point of contact for industry partners

\*\*Finance and Administration\*\*

\- Manage accounts payable and receivable, dues billing, and meeting revenue

\- Work with the Treasurer on budgeting, financial reporting, and annual filings

\- Coordinate with the Society's accountant and any outside vendors

\*\*Communications and Advocacy\*\*

\- Produce member communications, newsletters, and website updates

\- Monitor state legislative and regulatory activity relevant to the specialty and keep the Board informed

\- Maintain relationships with allied state and national organizations

\#\# Qualifications

\*\*Required\*\*

\- Demonstrated ability to work independently and manage competing priorities with minimal supervision

\- Proficiency with standard office software, membership or CRM databases, and virtual meeting platforms

\- Ability to travel within Kentucky several times per year, including occasional weekends for the annual meeting

\- Reliable home office setup and internet connection

\*\*Preferred\*\*

\- Experience working with a volunteer board of directors

\- Background in healthcare, medical societies, or physician\-facing organizations

\- Familiarity with continuing medical education (CME) accreditation processes

\- Experience with sponsorship or exhibitor sales

\- Bookkeeping or basic nonprofit financial management experience

\#\# Compensation and Schedule

\- $40,000–$60,000 annually, depending on experience

\- Part\-time, approximately 20–30 hours per week

\- Primarily remote, with flexible scheduling around board meetings, member needs, and the annual meeting cycle

\- Occasional in\-state travel required; travel expenses reimbursed

\#\# To Apply

Please submit a resume and a brief cover letter describing your relevant experience to ryans@eyeconsultantsofkentucky.com. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.

\-\-\-

Pay: $40,000\.00 \- $60,000\.00 per year

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Lexington, KY 40509

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Planning
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN #TEAMRC

From its earliest days, the City of Rancho Cucamonga was dubbed the "City with a Plan" and over the past forty years, we have been creating a world-class community. In late 2021, the City adopted an updated General Plan that clarified the vision for the City's next chapter and an idea that has been simmering for over a decade: that the city can grow, providing new housing and economic opportunities and position itself for the next generation economy, while maintaining its wonderful single-family neighborhoods by focusing new growth onto key corridors and into key nodes.

The Planning Department plays a central role in advancing the City Council’s goals related to land use, urban design, and the long-term quality and sustainability of the built environment. As a senior leader within the department, the Deputy Director of Planning will help translate these goals into actionable policy, high-quality development outcomes, and places that matter.

Our work goes beyond managing individual development applications. We focus on creating places, not just projects—taking a holistic view of how buildings, streets, public spaces, infrastructure, and natural systems come together to shape daily life. The Deputy Director will help guide this approach, balancing technical requirements, design quality, community values, and economic vitality in both infill and redevelopment contexts.

The department leads complex long-range planning efforts addressing housing, transportation, economic development, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience. The Deputy Director plays a key role in shaping and implementing these initiatives, using data, policy analysis, and professional judgment to help guide decision-makers and ensure equitable and resilient growth.

What You Will Be Doing Here At Team Rc

This position supports the Planning Director in managing daily operations of the Planning Department, mentor staff, oversee complex planning initiatives, and ensuring high-quality customer service to residents, employers, developers, and partner agencies. The Deputy Director also helps guide policy development that shapes the community’s future.

Key Responsibilities

Execute the Planning Division’s operations, staffing, and work program
Oversee development review and entitlement processes, balancing efficiency, design quality, and community outcomes
Navigate politically sensitive and technically complex development proposals with professionalism and sound judgment
Mentor and develop professional planning staff and future leaders within the organization
Lead and manage complex planning initiatives, including zoning code updates, housing implementation, and infill development projects
Serve as an advisor to appointed bodies and elected officials on land use policy, development trends, and planning strategy
Represent the department on behalf of the Planning Director as needed, ensuring continuity in leadership and decision-making

We are seeking a planning leader who combines strategic vision with practical execution—someone who can guide day-to-day operations while keeping a clear focus on long-term outcomes. The ideal candidate brings a proven ability to shape and implement land use policies that create meaningful, livable places, along with the skill to clearly frame complex planning issues for policy makers and the public. This role calls for experience navigating the challenges of infill development, redevelopment, and community-scale change with professionalism and creativity. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership presence, the ability to step confidently into a director-level role when needed, and sound judgment in politically nuanced environments. Above all, we are looking for a collaborative, solutions-oriented professional with a deep commitment to public service and ethical planning practice.

This Position Might Be Perfect For You If

You are comfortable operating at both the strategic and operational levels of a planning organization
You have experience navigating infill development, redevelopment, and community-scale change
You thrive in politically nuanced environments and bring sound judgment and professionalism to sensitive issues
You enjoy mentoring staff and building strong, collaborative teams
You are motivated by meaningful work that has a lasting impact on a community’s future
You want to be part of a supportive, high-performing team that values learning, initiative, and shared success

Department Perks

We budget for renewals for professional certifications (AICP, CNU-A, etc.) for our staff.
We invest in your continued education and budget for conferences, educational courses and continuing professional certifications.
Where possible, we offer the flexibility of a hybrid schedule option so you can occasionally work from home.

For more information about this career opportunity, visit the job description here.

Recruitment Schedule

Application Deadline: Thursday, August 13, 2026

Application Screening completed by: Wednesday, August 19, 2026

1st Panel Interview: Thursday, August 27 , 2026

Ways we support our Team RC Family

To learn more about additional Team RC perks, please visit the benefits tab located at the top of the flyer – please note that some perks may not be available for certain positions and may require approval.

ARE YOU QUALIFIED

Education And/ Or Experience

Graduation from college with a Bachelor’s degree in urban and regional planning, public administration, or a related field, is required. A Master’s degree in Planning, Public Policy, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field is highly desirable. Six or more years of increasingly responsible professional planning and zoning experience, including employee supervision, project management, community participation, and related work. Professional certification by the American Institute of Certified Planners is highly desirable.

Examples of Acceptable Substitutions:
Minimum Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in urban and regional planning, public administration, or a related field, plus six
(6) years
of increasingly responsible professional planning and zoning experience, including employee supervision, project management, community participation, and related work. in current or advanced planning.Substitution: A total of ten

of increasingly responsible professional planning and zoning experience, including employee supervision, project management, community participation, and related work.

Knowledge of theories and principles of urban and environmental planning; organization and management of current planning, advanced planning, historic preservation, and zoning services; land use, physical design, demographic, environmental, and social/economic and statistical analysis techniques; State planning laws, Subdivision Map Act, California and National Environmental Quality Acts; principles of employee motivation and leadership; customer service practices; principles and practices of supervision, training, and evaluation; budgeting practices; contract administration practices; research and surveying methods; ability to plan, organize, direct and coordinate the work of professional and technical personnel; select, supervise, train and evaluate staff; identify and respond to Planning Commission, City Council, and staff issues, concerns and needs; analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals; research, analyze, and evaluate new service delivery methods, procedures and techniques; formulate work plans; prepare clear and concise administrative reports and make effective presentations at community, management and official levels; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; establish, maintain, and foster positive and harmonious working relationships with staff, management, developers, consultants, and other parties on behalf of the City; operate computer hardware and use word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software.

Licenses, Certificates; Special Requirements:

A valid Class C California driver's license and the ability to maintain insurability under the City's Vehicle Insurance Policy.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL DEMANDS

The physical and mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The employee occasionally reaches items above or below desk level, and lifts and carries records and documents, typically weighing less than 20 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

MENTAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this class, the employee is regularly required to use oral and written communication skills; read and interpret complex data; thoroughly analyze and solve problems; exercise sound judgment in the absence of specific guidelines; use math and mathematical reasoning; establish priorities and work on multiple assignments and projects concurrently; meet intense and changing deadlines given continual interruptions; and interact appropriately with staff, management, City officials, Commissions, developers, consultants, and others encountered in the course of work.

WORKING CONDITIONS

The employee works in both office and field settings. The noise level is usually quiet to moderately quiet within the office and at public counter. The employee may be required to work on weekends to attend various programs and events and during the evenings in order to attend City Council, Planning Commission and Design Review Committee meetings.

Resumes may be attached to completed application form as supplemental information and will not be accepted in lieu of an official application form. Applications will be screened and the most qualified candidates who best match the needs of the City will be invited to compete further in the examination process. All candidates will be notified of their application status by email throughout the recruitment process. Candidates invited to compete in the examination process, who successfully pass the examination process, will be place on an eligibility list. The candidate on the eligibility list who most closely meets the requirements of the City may be selected to receive a final offer. The City may conclude that none of the candidates, even those who meet the minimum qualifications, are appropriate for the position.

Degree Verification; and
Pass a pre-employment medical exam

jobs.title: Program Director, Nursing Excellence
jobs.description:
Department Overview

Join OHSU Health as we build the next chapter of nursing excellence. This newly created Program Director role will lead the development of a comprehensive system for nursing research, evidence-based practice, innovation, recognition, and professional governance. This is a rare opportunity to create infrastructure from the ground up, influence organizational strategy, and shape how nurses contribute to clinical excellence, scientific discovery, and healthcare innovation across an academic health system.

The Program Director, Center for Nursing Excellence & Innovation (CNEI) is a Registered Nurse (RN) responsible for advancing nursing excellence and innovation across OHSU Health. This role provides strategic, operational, financial, and human resource leadership for programs and initiatives that strengthen nursing practice, professional development, quality outcomes, and workforce capability across the health system.

Working in alignment with OHSU’s Mission, Vision, and Professional Practice Model, the Program Director collaborates with system nursing leadership, interprofessional partners, and professional governance structures to create and sustain a culture of safety, quality, engagement, inquiry, and professional growth. The Program Director oversees the design, implementation, and evaluation of initiatives that support evidence-based practice, nursing professional governance, nursing professional development, nursing quality, workforce development, and nursing excellence operations.

Function/Duties of Position

This position specifically serves as the OHSU Health Magnet Program Director and provides leadership for the operationalization and advancement of nursing excellence infrastructure across the health system, including Magnet designation and redesignation strategy, nursing professional governance operations, nursing inquiry and evidence-based practice structures, and nursing excellence program management. The role is responsible for creating sustainable systems that support shared decision-making, professional practice advancement, nursing engagement, and a culture of inquiry and innovation. In partnership with nursing and executive leadership, this position oversees the coordination and evaluation of professional governance councils, supports organizational alignment to Magnet principles and outcomes, advances structures that support evidence-based practice, quality improvement, research, and dissemination, and ensures effective management of nursing excellence operations that strengthen clinical excellence, workforce development, regulatory readiness, and strategic nursing priorities across OHSU Health.

The Program Director ensures regulatory and accreditation compliance related to nursing practice and education, manages resources efficiently, and leads teams to achieve organizational priorities in clinical excellence, workforce development, innovation, and nursing excellence.

I. Strategic & Program Development

Leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs that advance nursing excellence, innovation, and professional development across OHSU Health. Aligns initiatives with system goals, the Professional Practice Model, Magnet standards, and organizational strategic priorities. Develops workplans, performance indicators, and outcome metrics to monitor program effectiveness.

II. Operational Leadership & Integration

Provides operational oversight for assigned CNEI portfolios (ex: professional governance, competency infrastructure, nursing quality, education programs, research, or workforce development). Applies systems thinking to integrate initiatives across entities and service lines, ensuring alignment, collaboration, and sustainability.

III. Financial & Resource Management

Develops, manages, and monitors program budgets, grants, and contracts. Ensures responsible use of resources and alignment with organizational priorities. Prepares business cases and cost analyses to support program expansion, technology integration, and strategic investments.

IV. Human Resources & Team Leadership

Supervises and mentors' staff, fostering engagement, professional growth, and accountability. Recruits, orients, and evaluates team members; supports role clarity for Nursing Professional Development Practitioners, Nursing Practice Specialists, and other CNEI staff. Builds leadership capacity through coaching, feedback, and professional development planning.

V. Quality, Safety, And Regulatory Compliance

Collaborates with nursing, quality, and regulatory leaders to ensure compliance with accreditation and licensure standards (DNV, Magnet, ANCC). Leads or supports initiatives to improve nursing-sensitive indicators, preventable harm, and professional practice outcomes. Uses data analytics and evidence-based methods to evaluate and sustain improvements.

VI. Professional Practice & Education Infrastructure

Advances a culture of professional growth and lifelong learning through innovative educational models, competency systems, and recognition programs. Ensures structures are in place to validate nursing competence, support clinical inquiry, and disseminate best practices.

VII. Collaboration, Communication, & Organizational Engagement

Partners with executive nursing, interprofessional, and academic leaders to strengthen professional governance and system integration. Represents CNEI on organizational committees, councils, and task forces. Facilitates communication strategies that promote transparency, recognition, and the translation of strategy into practice.

Required Qualifications

Seven (7) years of relevant clinical experience AND
Five (5) years of progressive nursing leadership experience (NPD Practitioner, Nursing Practice Specialist, Clinical Nurse Specialist, Magnet Program Director, Nurse Scientist, Clinical Nurse Leader, Nurse Educator, Nurse Manager, or Nurse Director)
Demonstrated ability to lead in a large, matrixed health system.
Baccalaureate Degree in Nursing or Associate Degree in Nursing from a program accredited by the Commission of Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE), Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN), or Commission for Nursing Education Accreditation (CNEA).
Doctoral Degree in Nursing – DNP Preferred
Employees must be able to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodations.
Oregon Nurse Practice Act.
Current unencumbered Oregon RN license.
Professional certification in nursing
American Nurses Association (ANA) Scope and Standards of Practice, and the ANA Code of Ethics.

Additional Details

This position also comes with great benefits! Some highlights include:

Comprehensive health care plans that cover 100% for a full-time employee and 88% for dependents for .75 FTE and higher.
$50K of term life insurance provided at no cost to the employee
Two separate above market pension plans to choose from
Paid time off- 208 hours per year (full-time), prorated for part-time
Extended illness bank- 64 hours per year, prorated for part-time
9 paid holidays per year
Three weeks of paid parental leave
Adoption assistance program (up to 5k)
Substantial Tri-met and C-Tran discounts
Tuition Reimbursement
Innovative Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center.

In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

All are welcome.

OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply.

To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

Harm Reduction Sisters is entering an important period of organizational growth and leadership transition.

After years of visionary leadership under its founding Executive Director, the organization is preparing for its next chapter. Building on a strong foundation, the next Executive Director will help guide the organization through continued growth, evolving community needs, and a changing public health landscape.

At a time when harm reduction organizations are navigating shifting policy environments, funding uncertainty, and increasing public attention, the next Executive Director will build on Harm Reduction Sisters' trusted reputation while strengthening its voice, partnerships, and long\-term sustainability.

The next Executive Director will join an evolving leadership team that reflects the organization's commitment to collaboration, shared leadership, and long\-term sustainability.

This role is well suited for a leader who can honor the relationships, trust, and values that have shaped Harm Reduction Sisters while thoughtfully guiding its continued evolution with creativity and care.

The Executive Director guides the organization’s mission, vision, and strategic direction in partnership with the Board of Directors, Director of Operations, and senior leadership team helping Harm Reduction Sisters continue to grow while remaining true to its values and the communities it serves.

Senior Broadband ISP Program Director – Municipal Fiber Network

About Golden Tech and Services

Golden Tech and Services, LLC is a New York State\- and New York City\-certified Minority\-Owned Business Enterprise providing cybersecurity, cloud, information technology, consulting, and professional training services.

We are recruiting an experienced Senior Broadband ISP Program Director for an anticipated public\-sector broadband engagement involving a county\-owned fiber\-optic network.

This is an individual, contract\-contingent position. It is not a solicitation for companies, vendors, or business proposals. Employment or engagement will depend on contract award, final project requirements, verification of qualifications, and execution of an appropriate individual employment or consulting agreement.

Position Summary

The Senior Broadband ISP Program Director will provide technical, operational, regulatory, and program leadership for a potential municipal broadband initiative.

The anticipated network includes approximately 113 miles of county\-owned fiber, six central\-office locations, a 100 Gbps core ring, XPoN infrastructure, fixed\-wireless components, and residential, commercial, institutional, and government subscribers.

The selected professional should have substantial experience planning, launching, operating, or overseeing municipal, utility, open\-access, or commercial ISP networks.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead planning and implementation of a municipal broadband and ISP operations program.
* Coordinate the integration of a 100 Gbps core network with XPoN, middle\-mile, last\-mile, fixed\-wireless, and carrier\-interconnection infrastructure.
* Develop technical requirements for core\-network electronics, central\-office equipment, customer\-premises equipment, monitoring systems, and network\-management platforms.
* Coordinate network turn\-up, testing, acceptance, and service activation.
* Develop subscriber onboarding, installation, customer\-support, billing, and service\-assurance processes.
* Support residential, commercial, government, education, nonprofit, and institutional broadband offerings.
* Establish procedures for network operations, cybersecurity, incident management, maintenance, repair, and emergency restoration.
* Develop service\-level monitoring for speed, latency, availability, outages, and other performance requirements.
* Support a minimum symmetrical subscriber speed of 100/100 Mbps, latency below 20 milliseconds, and monthly network availability of at least 99\.5%.
* Coordinate with public officials, engineers, construction contractors, utilities, network operators, carriers, regulators, and community stakeholders.
* Support compliance with New York State ConnectAll Municipal Infrastructure Program requirements.
* Prepare program updates, implementation schedules, performance reports, subscriber reports, and required grant documentation.
* Participate in regular project meetings and government\-agency calls.
* Support customer\-record management, optical\-assignment records, geospatial information, and network documentation.
* Develop strategies for affordable broadband, low\-income service options, customer acquisition, community outreach, and subscriber retention.
* Assist with operating budgets, revenue projections, subscriber take\-rate assumptions, maintenance costs, and revenue\-sharing models.
* Help evaluate pole attachments, dark\-fiber access, interconnection arrangements, carrier hotels, wholesale services, fiber leases, and indefeasible rights of use.
* Maintain accurate technical, operational, financial, and regulatory documentation.

Required Qualifications

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in broadband, telecommunications, ISP operations, or fiber\-network management.
* Demonstrated leadership experience with municipal, public\-sector, utility, open\-access, rural, or large commercial broadband networks.
* Experience operating or supporting fiber\-to\-the\-premises, XPoN, middle\-mile, last\-mile, fixed\-wireless, or comparable broadband infrastructure.

**About Assured Women's Healthcare**

Assured Women's Healthcare is a Christ\-centered, life\-affirming 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization dedicated to serving women, men, and families facing unplanned pregnancies with compassion, excellence, and hope. Through professional medical services, education, advocacy, and practical support, Assured seeks to empower individuals to make informed decisions while experiencing the love and truth of Jesus Christ.


Located in the greater Orlando area, Assured Women's Healthcare provides a comprehensive range of services designed to care for both the physical and emotional needs of clients. Services include pregnancy testing, limited obstetrical ultrasounds, options education, parenting support, community referrals, and ongoing client care in a safe, confidential, and non\-judgmental environment.


As a growing ministry with increasing community impact, Assured is entering an exciting new season of strategic growth. The organization is strengthening its infrastructure, expanding donor engagement, increasing community partnerships, and positioning itself to reach more families throughout Central Florida.


The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to build upon a strong foundation while helping shape the future vision and long\-term sustainability of the ministry. The successful candidate will serve as both a spiritual and organizational leader, championing the mission, developing strategic partnerships, growing financial resources, and leading a dedicated team committed to protecting life and serving families.

Assessment & Strategic Support

Contribute to the development of resources, communications, and educational materials.
