jobs.description:
Summary

The Program Director (PD) is responsible for leading, managing, and implementing all aspects of assigned programs to ensure excellence, safety, and alignment with The Child Center of NY’s mission and contractual expectations. The PD ensures program goals are met, budgets are monitored, and all compliance, data, and reporting requirements are fulfilled. The PD also serves as the site’s Mental Health Lead, overseeing implementation of mental health supports in coordination with the host school, The Child Center’s Behavioral Health Division, and external partners.

Essential Functions

Program Leadership and Operations

Lead the development, implementation, and monitoring of all program components to ensure goals align with agency mission and community needs.
Maintain an active presence throughout program hours to ensure consistent safety, quality, and alignment with agency standards.
Supervise, coach, and evaluate staff to promote strong performance, professional growth, and adherence to agency expectations.
Oversee program documentation, reporting, and fiscal management to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and contract compliance.

Mental Health Role and Supports

Oversee implementation of all Mental Health Supports as required by DYCD, including ensuring all staff complete the one-hour DYCD Mental Health training and completing the two-hour DYCD training on the mental health spectrum, crisis response, and crisis navigation planning.
Work with agency leadership to promote hiring of staff with the New York State Youth Peer Advocate Credential or support eligible staff in obtaining it.
Develop and maintain a Mental Health Referral Plan in collaboration with the host school, The Child Center’s Behavioral Health Division (as the key Behavioral Health Partner), and any external partners. Update and share the plan with staff annually.
Communicate and coordinate with NYCPS social workers, school mental health staff, and community providers to ensure comprehensive participant support.
Facilitate referrals to mental health services using The Child Center’s QR code referral system and track and report de-identified, aggregate referral data to DYCD as required.
Create and implement a Crisis Navigation Plan for the site using the DYCD template, developed jointly with school-based and community mental health staff.
Ensure all staff understand and follow the Referral and Crisis Navigation Plans, responding appropriately when mental health needs are identified.

Partnerships and Program Quality

Collaborate with school leadership, families, and community organizations to maintain strong partnerships and shared accountability for participant outcomes.
Promote youth and family engagement through consistent communication, events, and inclusive practices.
Stay informed about trends and best practices in youth development, education, and mental health to ensure services remain relevant and effective.
Identify and maintain community partnerships that enhance program access and impact.

Training and Professional Development

Participate in all required DYCD and agency trainings, ensuring personal completion and staff compliance.
Support and document ongoing professional development for all site staff.
Foster a learning culture that integrates youth development, trauma-informed practice, and social-emotional learning.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Manages the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of program operations.
Supervises Assistant Program Directors, Group Leaders, Activity Specialists, and other staff as assigned.
Ensures adherence to agency policies, collective bargaining agreements, and all applicable laws and standards.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in education, Child Development, Public Administration, or related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in youth development or education, including 2 years in a supervisory role.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and strong administrative skills.
Ability to plan independently, meet deadlines, and manage multiple priorities.
Satisfactory background check, fingerprint clearance, and health screening.

Job Behavioral Expectations

Maintain consistent professional attendance, punctuality, and conduct.
Communicate effectively with staff, partners, and families.
Use data and feedback to inform improvement.
Uphold confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA and all agency policies.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

This role requires regular movement between classrooms, offices, and outdoor spaces during program hours. The employee may lift up to 20 pounds and must be able to supervise active youth settings. Work occurs primarily in school environments with standard conditions.

We Also Offer

Generous Paid Time Off
Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance
401k Pension and Employer Contribution
Flexible Spending and Commuter Benefits Accounts
Employer paid short-term & long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance
Commuter Benefits
Employee Assistance Program

jobs.description:
Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.

Job Description

Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Associate Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the daily operations. This position provides cause-driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal oversight, financial development, program administration, facility and equipment stewardship, community relations, and personal and professional development.

Qualifications

Strong business operations background with a proven track record for producing growth, annual giving and strong financial management
A Bachelor's Degree in a child related field or Sports Management/ Recreation/Health Sciences is preferred, or 48 semester hours or 72 quarter hours of college credit of which 12 semester hours or 18 quarter hours are in subjects relating to children.
Five or more years of successful management experience, preferably in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency in the health & wellness, business or related field
Supervision of full and part-time employees and accountability for annual budget exceeding $1 million
Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision, development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial development, marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
YMCA Multi-Team Leader certification preferred

Working Conditions

This role requires daily onsite work and occasional after-hours response; therefore, candidates must be able to reliably commute to the assigned location and reside within approximately 30 miles or 45 minutes of the worksite by their start date to meet operational needs
Requires a person of maturity and good judgment, who can operate with a minimum of guidance from the Division Vice President
Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgment, to assess facts and issues, and make non-routine decisions regarding day-to-day operational problems and issues
Requires effective team-building and team-leadership skills
Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
Must maintain positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals, and values
Must have ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management, including on-site presence in managing major operational problems
Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors, community leaders, etc.
Performs the duties of direct reports as needed

Environmental Factors, Physical Requirements

Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multi-tasking
Physically able to successfully complete required certifications

Essential Functions

Division of Duties:

65% Direct leadership of all day-to-day operations
20% - Property Management
10% - Leadership role in the Annual Impact Fund
5% - Staff development of direct reports

Priorities

Supervise all the day-to-day operations of the assigned location.
Develop, manage, and achieve the budget expectations with an emphasis on licensed childcare programs, Events and Rentals, Sports and Aquatic programming, Community Relations, and Fundraising.
Assist with all fundraising efforts with an emphasis on staff and community giving.
Support board development by assisting the Executive Director in recruiting three new board members annually and leading a board subcommittee.
Oversee property management, ensuring the upkeep of all grounds and facilities.
Foster relationship development with key home office leaders, including VPs of various product lines.

Budget and Financial Performance

Develop, manage, and monitor operating budgets to meet or exceed targets.
Initiate adjustments to operations to ensure a balanced budget.
Ensure completion of monthly variance reports and forecasting.

Program Development and Membership Engagement

Implements Association childcare strategies that support recruitment of new participants and retention of existing participants. Creates a member-focused culture and models relationship-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA “listen first” skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants and interests of participants. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure participant satisfaction
Develops long-range plans for the expansion of programs and services in harmony with overall YMCA objectives.
Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
Represents and promotes the YMCA in the local community by developing positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities
Ensures safety, cleanliness, and function of all related facilities and equipment

Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals

Development and supervision of the Family Center operations
Recruits, hires, trains, develops, and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates staff performance.
Develops strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for supervision of exempt and non exempt employees
Ensures all program operations are consistent with association procedures, including emergency, insurance, accident, purchasing, personnel, accounting and other administrative systems

Fundraising

Provides leadership and is accountable for achieving annual impact fund campaign

Professional Development

Partner with another executive to develop and master the skills needed to move into an executive role. These include leading up, financial analysis and troubleshooting, complex problem solving, and developing a positive team environment and culture.
Assists in all areas as assigned by supervisor

Communication & Influence
Fiscal Management
Engaging Community

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
BE PART OF SOMETHING GREAT

Job Description

The YMCA of Greater Louisville is seeking an experienced, community-focused leader to serve as Executive Director of a full-service YMCA branch with approximately $2.5 million in annual operations

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall leadership and performance of the branch, including financial management, membership and program growth, staff development, fundraising, community partnerships, facility operations, and safety. This position leads a multidisciplinary team and works closely with volunteers, donors, community partners, and the Branch Advisory Board to advance the YMCA’s mission.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, nonprofit management, recreation, public administration, human services, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
At least five years of progressively responsible leadership experience.
Experience managing a significant operating budget and leading managers or multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated success in financial management, staff development, program or membership growth, and community engagement.
Strong communication, decision-making, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work a flexible schedule, including occasional evenings, weekends, and community events.

Preferred Qualifications

YMCA or nonprofit leadership experience.
Experience managing an operation with annual revenue of $2 million or more.
Experience overseeing an indoor aquatic facility.
Experience with fundraising, donor development, grants, or sponsorships.
Experience working with a volunteer board.

Essential Functions

Key Responsibilities

Lead daily branch operations and implement annual goals aligned with the YMCA’s strategic priorities.
Develop and manage an annual operating budget of approximately $2.7 million.
Monitor revenue, expenses, membership, program participation, staffing, and overall branch performance.
Recruit, supervise, coach, and develop branch leadership and staff.
Drive membership growth, retention, engagement, and customer service.
Ensure high-quality programs that respond to community needs.
Provide executive oversight of one indoor swimming pool and aquatics operations.
Ensure compliance with health, safety, child-protection, risk-management, and YMCA standards.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Lead where you love to live—Western NC’s mountain beauty, eclectic vibe, and vibrant culture. Build your career at the Reuter Family YMCA.

Job Description

The Executive Director is a key member of the YMCA of Western North Carolina’s leadership team. They oversee the development and engagement of staff and volunteers, maintain a quality Y experience and positive culture within their center and play a crucial role in raising financial contributions that support the Y’s mission by managing a substantial donor portfolio. This role is responsible for helping manage critical collaborations with other community-based organizations that align with strategic objectives to advance the Y’s mission and expand our community impact. They are guided by the Senior Vice President of Operations, YMCA of WNC operating priorities, Association Leadership Norms, and must operate in a manner consistent with our organizational values.

This role will be housed at the Reuter Family YMCA.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree is required. (Extensive related experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.)Master’s degree in related field preferred (human services, social services, business)
Three to five years of successful experience in frontline fundraising, donor relations, or equivalent experience.
Experience managing high-level donor relationships with demonstrated success in closing gifts of $25,000 and above.
Preference is given to candidates with experience closing six and seven-figure gifts.
Bachelor's degree in human services, social services, business or equivalent is strongly preferred.
Preferably five or more years of management experience in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Experience must demonstrate strong skills in human relations, budgeting and fiscal management, financial development, program management, volunteer and staff development, and committee and board relations.
Ability to direct complex operations through volunteer development, supervision of staff, development and monitoring of budget, marketing, public relations, and program development.
Ability to relate effectively to diverse groups of people from all social and economic segments of the community and manage and maintain collaborations with other community-based organizations.

Essential Functions

Manages a portfolio of high-capacity donors/prospects from throughout Buncombe County, working directly with the Vice President of Development. Plays a key role in achieving financial development benchmarks in annual, capital and endowment campaigns through cultivation, acquisition, stewardship and retention.
Leads recruitment and development of center Advisory Committee and provides leadership over each meeting. Ensures the highest quality of member/program participant satisfaction by continuously observing program and member service areas. Identifies and resolves issues in collaboration with center leaders while fostering a culture of service throughout operations.
Represents and promotes the YMCA in the local community and develops positive working relationships with other community-based organizations, businesses, and governmental entities, advancing the Y’s impact and position in the community.
Responsible for hiring, coaching, and mentoring all direct reports and ensuring compliance with the organization’s personnel policy and HR practices within their team through regular check-ins and annual reviews. Also responsible for indirect leadership, coaching and development of center leadership staff.
Implements a results-based management approach and ensures their center and service line is actively working towards association-level objectives by assessing progress towards identified goals/KPIs, provides ongoing coaching and feedback, and discusses development opportunities.
Partners with peers to ensure budgets align with center operations and ensures that resources are devoted to top priorities and strategic objectives.
Identifies growth opportunities, conducts forecasting regularly and corrects financial deficiencies on a timely basis through monthly variance reports with organizational leaders, and implements action plans to meet budgeted financial targets
Models relationship-building skills in all interactions with staff, members, donors, volunteers, and the community. Prioritize adding value to the Y member experience, ensure programming supports member needs, and aligns with the Association’s strategic & operational priorities throughout assigned service lines.
Ensures that all the policies of the organization are implemented, including Financial, Human Resources, Risk Management/Safety, Member Code of Conduct, and Program Policies.
Supports the Y’s commitment to DEI by upholding policies and practices to ensure underserved communities are welcomed, comfortable and present at the Y.
Serves as a member of Y leadership and supports the overall objectives of the YMCA.
Performs all other duties as assigned

Cause-Driven Leadership Competencies

Mission Advancement: Reinforces the Y’s values within the organization and the community. Effectively communicates the benefits and impact of the YMCA’s efforts for all stakeholders. Implements effective systems to develop volunteers at program, fundraising, and policy leadership levels. Secures resources and support for all philanthropic endeavors.

Collaboration: Develops strategies to ensure staff and volunteers reflect the community. Builds

and nurtures strategic relationships to enhance support for the YMCA. Serves as a community leader

building collaborations based on trust and credibility to advance YMCA mission and goals. Communicates for influence to attain buy-in and support of goals. Provides tools and resources for the development of others.

Operational Effectiveness: Integrates multiple thinking processes to make decisions. Involves members and community in the development of programs and activities. Ensures execution of plans. Institutes sound accounting procedures, investment policies, and financial controls. Assigns clear accountability and ensures continuous improvement.

Personal Growth: Fosters a learning environment embracing diverse abilities and approaches. Creates a sense of urgency and positive tension to support change. Anticipates challenges that can sidetrack or derail growth and personal learning. Has the functional and technical knowledge and skills required to perform well; uses best practices and demonstrates up-to-date knowledge and skills in technology.

Physical Requirements

The role may involve occasional lifting or carrying of items up to 25 pounds, setting up for events, or assisting with minor facility adjustments. Regular walking, standing, or climbing stairs may also be required during site visits, community events, or meetings.

Full-Time Benefits

Full-time employees receive medical, dental and vision insurance, group life insurance and long-term disability paid by the Y; short-term disability, term life insurance and dependent life insurance is available for purchase; generous paid time off, retirement plan with employer contribution of 12% of salary (subject to eligibility requirements), free YMCA membership, free afterschool childcare and summer day camp and program discounts.

The YMCA of Western North Carolina is committed to equal opportunity in terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, faith, gender, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, gender expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law, except where a bona fide occupational qualification applies.

jobs.title: Executive Director, RWD Strategic Accounts
jobs.description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.

Labcorp is seeking a remote Executive Director, RWD Strategic Accounts
to join our team!

Location
: Remote

Work Schedule:
This is a full‑time, exempt (salaried) position assigned to a First Shift schedule, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST.

Business needs may occasionally require flexibility in work hours, including earlier, later, or additional hours, with reasonable notice provided when possible.

Job Responsibilities

Strategy and Leadership:
Partner with Global Head of Client Engagement to define the vision, strategy, and go-to-market plan for the RWD business. Leads all aspects of customer growth, from ideation to full commercialization, with a focus on long-term value creation for Labcorp clients and industry stakeholders.

Data Commercialization:
Identify and implement strategies to commercialize Labcorp's proprietary data alone and in integrated with other data sources, while adhering to the highest standards of data privacy, compliance, and ethical use.

Strategic Partnerships and Business Development:
Identify, negotiate, and secure strategic partnerships with key players in the healthcare ecosystem, including technology firms, research organizations, financial institutions, payer and provider organizations, marketing and advertising companies, consultancies and government agencies.

Industry Expertise:
Serve as a subject matter expert on the healthcare data landscape. Maintain an in-depth understanding of market trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory changes to guide strategic decisions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10 or more years experience in data commercialization, pricing strategies, commercialization models, and business development.
10 or more years experience with healthcare data regulations, including HIPAA, GDPR, and other healthcare frameworks.
5 or more years experience with RWD.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree

Additional Job Standards

Proven track record of building and scaling high-performing, diverse global sales teams and mentoring executives at all levels.
Demonstrated success in commercializing Real-World Data (RWD) products and driving revenue growth in healthcare, payer, provider, financial services, media and advertising and government sectors.
Strong ability to influence stakeholders, lead customer engagement teams, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed, high-growth environment.
Experience selling to, payors, providers, financial services, consultancies, government agencies, marketing/media and advertising organizations, life sciences organizations, and other healthcare ecosystem stakeholders.
Established industry presence with experience presenting RWD topics and executive leadership roles in sales-driven organizations (e.g., IQVIA, Optum, Datavant).
Expertise in scaling RWD product portfolios and developing strategic partnerships or data ecosystems.
Ability to deliver internal sales training, market intelligence, and actionable reporting to leadership.
Skilled in developing partnership models and account-level go-to-market strategies based on customer needs, market dynamics, and competitive landscape.
Strong business development and relationship management skills, including engagement with C-suite executives.
Entrepreneurial mindset with a history of leading innovative business initiatives and achieving year-over-year commercialization targets.
Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
Remote option with up to 35 % US travel
Regularly work with a computer for approximately 6-8 hours a day
Must be able to read and understand complex directions in a professional corporate environment

About The Role

The Executive Director, RWD Strategic Accounts is responsible for driving growth of Labcorp’s Real-World Data (RWD) business by leveraging Labcorp’s unique data assets, multi-modal solutions, and clinical expertise. The position leads the development and execution of commercialization strategies, builds and manages a high-performing sales team, and develops strategic partnerships to expand market presence. The ideal candidate is a proven leader with deep experience in the payer, provider, financial services, media and advertising, life sciences and government sectors with a track record of scaling RWD sales organizations.

Application Window: 8/15/2026

Pay Range: $180-200k

All job offers will be based on a candidate’s skills and prior relevant experience, applicable degrees/certifications, as well as internal equity and market data. The position is also eligible for bonus and/or commissions under the applicable variable compensation plan. Bonus/commissions are earned based on achievement of performance metrics under the plan.

Benefits:
Employees regularly scheduled to work 20 or more hours per week are eligible for comprehensive benefits including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, STD/LTD, 401(k), Paid Time Off (PTO) or Flexible Time Off (FTO), Tuition Reimbursement and Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Employees regularly scheduled to work less than 20 hours, Casual, Intern, and Temporary employees are only eligible to participate in the 401(k) Plan. For more detailed information, please click here.

Labcorp Is Proud To Be An Equal Opportunity Employer

Labcorp strives for inclusion and belonging in the workforce and does not tolerate harassment or discrimination of any kind. We make employment decisions based on the needs of our business and the qualifications and merit of the individual. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), family or parental status, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, personal appearance, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristic. Additionally, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable law.

We encourage all to apply

If you are an individual with a disability who needs assistance using our online tools to search and apply for jobs, or needs an accommodation, please visit our accessibility site or contact us at Labcorp Accessibility. jobs.title: CO DMV Deputy Program Director of Service Delivery.
jobs.description:
Department Information

The mission of the Colorado Department of Revenue (CDOR) is to become a trusted partner to every Coloradan to help them navigate the complexities of government so they can thrive. We are driven by our values of service, teamwork, accountability, integrity, and respect.

The vision of the department is to empower businesses and individuals through quality customer service, innovation, and collaboration. We celebrate diversity and support an equitable and inclusive culture. We embrace our differences because we believe this brings innovation to our work. For more exciting information about the Department of Revenue, please enjoy this brief video !

Helpful Tips For Applying

Applying for a Job with the State of Colorado .

What Happens After You Apply.

Description Of Job

The Colorado Department of Revenue (CDOR)
impacts every citizen in the state. Within CDOR
, the Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
manages identity security, legal driver credentialing, and vehicle enforcement infrastructure across Colorado.

The Driver Services Program (DSP) Service Delivery Unit
is the primary public-facing arm of the DMV
. Accountable for serving millions of residents annually, this unit directs public operations across 35 physical field office branches, the state's mobile operations fleet (DMV2GO), and high-volume, consolidated communication call centers. We are dedicated to providing secure, efficient, and accessible services while adhering strictly to state and federal statutory frameworks, including the Colorado Revised Statutes (C.R.S.) and the federal REAL ID Act.

Position Overview

The DMV
is seeking an innovative, strategically-minded executive to serve as the permanent DSP Deputy Director of Service Delivery
. This critical role provides master strategic direction, policy formulation, and structural operational command for the state's entire public-facing motorist services footprint.

As a senior executive, you will oversee an indirect organizational footprint of approximately 365 FTE, commanding field networks and phone support systems through subordinate District Managers and Operations Managers. Your mission is to assist in the definition and execution of long-term program objectives, standardize service baselines, eliminate operational waste, and optimize multi-channel transaction flow. This role holds final administrative accountability for the state’s field office branches, the consolidated Driver Services Call Center, and the integrated facilities management function.

Primary Responsibilities & Scope

Structural Strategy & Programmatic Optimization (40%): Formulate, evaluate, and permanently approve state-level programmatic policies, transaction standards, and operational frameworks across all front-line channels. Establish long-term strategic plans for wait-time lean goals, statewide throughput cadence tempos, and identity verification compliance. Independently dictate resource allocations and personal services funding between physical and digital transaction channels to address shifting public needs.
Executive Human Capital Command (30%): Direct multiple statewide organizational units through the direct supervision of senior subordinate managers (including District Managers, the Call Center Operations Manager, and the Facilities Lead). Establish cascading performance management systems, continuous professional development plans, and operational metrics for a workforce of ~365 FTE. Serve as final authority for human resource actions, including regional structural alignments and advanced personnel updates.
Infrastructure & Asset Management (20%): Exercise executive command over the DSP Facilities Management Office (FMO) to manage the long-term lifecycle, spatial configuration, and security posture of the state's public infrastructure footprint. Analyze facility utilization metrics, security vendor allocations, and commercial lease constraints to ensure safe, optimized, and productive brick-and-mortar operations.
Public Administration & Legislative Liaison (10%): Serve as the principal service delivery technical expert to program and division executive leadership. Act as the high-level operational liaison with state lawmakers, county authorities, federal compliance overseers, and public stakeholder groups. Formulate data-driven strategic public administration reports and present agency infrastructure plans during legislative hearings and cross-departmental initiatives.

Remote Work Information

This position is designated as remote within the State of Colorado but may be required to work from a department office building location based on business needs.
Employees are responsible to provide and maintain a home office or other suitable remote work location as well as Internet and a secure Wi-Fi connection.
All performance expectations, productivity, and policy adherence requirements apply to remote work from home in the same manner as those assigned to an office.

Check out our DMV video: https://youtu.be/9isQWl9grYc

Relocation compensation may be available if an out-of-state candidate is selected.

Residency Requirement

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

This posting is open to current and non-current residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application. However, if you are selected and accept the position, you will be required to establish residence in the State of Colorado within 60 days of accepting the offer.

Class Code & Classification Description

H6G8XX Management

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

Ten (10) years of relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned to this position, two (2) of which must have included experience with public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, as well as developing and managing a budget to achieve program goals and objectives

Or

Education And Experience

A combination of related education (Business or Public Administration preferred) and/or relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to ten (10) years, two (2) of which must have included experience with public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, as well as developing and managing a budget to achieve program goals and objectives

Document this experience in your application IN DETAIL, as your experience will not be inferred or assumed.

Preferred Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess a proven record of executive leadership within a modern public administration or high-volume enterprise retail environment, displaying specific competencies in:

Previous Experience in the Motor Vehicle Space: The preferred candidate will have significant experience and demonstrated success within a motor vehicle division performing similar work.
Change Management Expertise: Documented experience leading large-scale organizational transformations or administrative modernizations. Holding a Prosci Certified Change Management Practitioner credential is highly desirable.
Continuous Improvement & Operational Efficiency: Demonstrated success identifying operational bottlenecks, establishing throughput cadence metrics, and applying Lean principles to public transaction windows. Possessing a Lean Green Belt (or higher) or a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is strongly preferred.
Advanced Multi-Channel Operations Management: Extensive experience directing geographically dispersed operations that integrate in-person storefronts, remote/virtual transaction systems, and large-scale call center infrastructures (such as managing 200+ FTE multi-tier reporting lines).
Enterprise Technology Acumen: Familiarity or hands-on experience navigating and optimizing workflows within complex modern enterprise architectures or driver licensing platform environments, e.g. FAST Enterprises DS/VS, Amazon Web Services - Connect, and Customer Queuing Technologies. .
De-escalation & Culture Building Leadership: Formal training or credentialing in Verbal De-escalation, Stakeholder Influence, or Conflict Resolution, with a history of cultivating psychologically safe, resilient, and customer-centric front-line work environments.
Public Infrastructure Strategy: Experience collaborating with facilities management teams, managing complex commercial lease arrangements, or evaluating building utilization data for public-facing service centers.

DOR Required Skills and Competencies
: Competencies required for all DOR positions include good communications skills, interpersonal and people management skills, the ability to multitask, the ability to work with confidential information, the ability to work in high-stress environments, and the demonstrated ability to assist customers.

Conditions Of Employment With The CDOR

Residency: Must become a resident of the State of Colorado. The relocation timeframe depends on DOR needs and is typically 30 to 60 days after an offer is accepted.

Employees are in a position of public trust in the performance of their job duties and must operate in a manner that maintains the highest standards of honesty, integrity, and public confidence.

As a condition of employment with the CDOR , all personnel must file all necessary Colorado Individual Income Tax (CIIT) returns and pay tax obligations, therefore all employees must undergo a pre-employment evaluation of their tax records/accounts to ensure compliance with this policy. Final candidates must also complete a successful nationwide background investigation and reference check prior to appointment. Certain positions based on duties may require scheduled background investigations.

Pursuant to the Universal Driving Standards Policy
,
any worker who will be expected to drive a State-owned vehicle is responsible for maintaining a safe driving record and a valid Colorado driver license prior to driving any State-owned vehicle.

To Be Compliant With The New Fleet Vehicle Policy, Motor Vehicle Records (MVRs) Will Be Pulled For Review For Workers Who

Have an assigned State fleet vehicle
Are required to operate a vehicle as part of the position
Utilize a State fleet vehicle as a pool vehicle

Minimum Qualification Screening

A Human Resources Analyst will only review the work experience/job duties sections of the online job application, to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for the position for which you are applying. Only complete applications submitted before the closing date of this announcement will be reviewed.

Cover letters and resumes are encouraged to be attached to applications, however they WILL NOT be accepted in lieu of the official State of Colorado online application. CDOR does not review attachments of any kind during the application process.
Part-time work experience will be prorated.
Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications to continue in the selection process for this position. Do not use "see resume" or "see attached" statements on your application.
List your employment history starting with the most recent job, including part-time, temporary, and volunteer jobs. If more than one job was held with a given organization, list each job held as a separate period of employment.
Information must be accurate, including dates of employment. If it is found that information provided is falsified, you will not be considered for a job with the State of Colorado and/or may be removed from a job after hire.
The eligible list established from this posting may be used to fill additional vacancies.

Email Address

All correspondence regarding your status in the selection/examination process will be conducted via email. Please set up your e-mail to accept messages from "state.co.us" and "info@governmentjobs.com" addresses. It is your responsibility to ensure that your email will accept these notices and/or review your junk mail and spam filtered email.

Appeal Rights

As an applicant who has been removed fro

jobs.title: President and CEO
jobs.description:
In partnership with an engaged Board of Directors and a dedicated staff team, the CEO will translate vision into action.

Job Description

The YMCA of Douglas County

POSITION:
President and CEO

Application Deadline:
August 3, 2026

1151 NW Stewart Parkway

Roseburg, OR 97471

https://www.ymcaofdouglascounty.org/

The YMCA of Douglas County is an equal opportunity employer. We work to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to reach their full potential with dignity.

THE OPPORTUNITY AT THE YMCA OF DOUGLAS COUNTY

The YMCA of Douglas County stands at an exciting point in its history, building on a 75-year legacy as a trusted community anchor while positioning itself for continued growth and deeper impact. Rooted in a close-knit and engaged community, the YMCA has long delivered programs that strengthen youth development, promote healthy living, and advance community well-being. The next Chief Executive Officer will build on this strong foundation while shaping a clear and forward-looking vision for the organization’s future.

This role is ideal for a leader who is both strategic and hands-on, someone who values relationships, thrives in a collaborative environment, and is energized by the opportunity to expand the YMCA’s reach and relevance. In close partnership with an engaged Board of Directors and a dedicated staff team, the CEO will translate vision into action by aligning strategy, operations, and community partnerships to meet evolving needs across Douglas County.

The CEO will advance key priorities by strengthening partnerships, developing staff leadership, and broadening the YMCA’s presence throughout the community. This leader will elevate organizational visibility, ensure long-term financial sustainability, and guide the YMCA into its next phase of growth, impact, and community leadership.

Qualifications

Criteria for Candidates:

Accredited four-year college degree and/or equivalent work experience.
Fiscally sound business management approach with a proven track record of budgetary and fiscal management of $3 million or more annually.
Minimum of seven years of prior experience in a senior management role with a YMCA or related experience at a comparable organization, including direct supervision of multiple levels of staff and employees.
Ability to develop and strengthen community relationships.
Ability to develop innovative programs and review and enhance programs being offered or considered for both economic sustainability and effectiveness in broadening engagement in the communities served.
Strategic planning and fundraising experience, including annual campaigns and securing grants.
Strong communication and public engagement skills, with the ability to serve as a visible and credible ambassador for the YMCA’s mission.
Proven record of accomplishment in progressive budgetary leadership and advanced fiscal management practices.
YMCA Organizational Leader Certification or ability to achieve certification within three years.

Essential Functions

KEY SKILLS AND ABILITIES OF OUR NEXT CEO

Role

The board believes its new CEO should be an experienced leader who has the background and qualities that will permit him or her to achieve excellence in the following roles:

Develop and Implement a Strategic Plan

Work effectively with volunteers, community leaders, and key staff to create and develop a strategic plan that addresses the needs of the communities served by the Y and includes defined organizational strategies, a clear implementation plan with deliverables, and measurable goals.

Key Competencies: Change Leadership, Communication & Influence, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Program/Project Management

Improve Operating Performance

Position Purpose  


The Executive Director of Tribal Administration (EDTA) oversees and manages the day\-to\-day operations of the Tribal Office. The EDTA provides leadership to tribal government staff and ensures effective and efficient management of governmental functions and programs. The EDTA reports to the Tribal Council and implements Tribal Council’s initiatives, programs, policies, and projects.  


  


Essential Duties, Functions \& Responsibilities  


* Oversee the day\-to\-day administration and management of the Tribal Office and provision of services to Tribal Citizens and Clients.

* Ensures the cooperative and efficient operation of the Tribal Office.
* Develops long\-range organizational goals and annual operational objectives and advises Tribal Council regarding emerging opportunities, risks, organizational priorities and departmental outcomes and establishes leadership expectations and accountability standards.
* Supervises and provides leadership and guidance to Tribal staff and Tribal government departments to ensure fulfilment of Tribal and departmental objectives.
* Responsible for developing plans, policies, goals, and programs to implement decisions and initiatives of the Tribal Council.

* Responsible for maintaining standards of service to Tribal Citizens.

* Responsible for risk management and protection of tribal resources and assets, and oversees enterprise risk management, emergency preparedness, business continuity planning, and organizational resilience

A top 10 public school, according to U.S. News \& World Report, SUNY Purchase, part of the State University of New York (SUNY) system, is a dynamic campus that combines conservatory training in the visual and performing arts with programs in the liberal arts and sciences, in order to inspire an appreciation for both intellectual and artistic talents in all students. SUNY Purchase is a community of students, faculty, and friends where open\-minded engagement with the creative process leads to a lifetime of intellectual growth and professional opportunity. For more information about the college, visit SUNY Purchase .  

  

**Benefits:**
* Health, dental, and vision benefits are available to eligible employees after a 28\-day waiting period. More information regarding other benefits such as generous paid time off, tuition assistance, and retirement systems can be found on **SUNY’s Benefit Summaries website**.
* SUNY Purchase is a qualifying government employer allowing eligible employees to participate in the **Public Service Loan Forgiveness** program.
* Access to the NAEYC\-accredited, on\-campus child care at The Children’s Center.
* Discounted access to the world\-class Performing Arts Center, free admission to the Neuberger Museum of Art, and free access to the athletic facilities.
* Other benefits include business\-casual dress and an opportunity to **telecommute** (dependent on job function and operational need). For detailed information on some of the College’s employee benefits, visit the College’s **Human Resources/Benefits website**.

**How to Apply**  

The search committee for SUNY Purchase’s next Vice President for Institutional Advancement/Executive Director is being assisted by Academic Search. To apply, applicants should visit the following link: **https://www.academicsearch.org/SUNYPurchaseVPIAApply**.  

  

Applications should consist of a substantive cover letter addressing the qualifications and expectations in the position profile and a curriculum vitae, both submitted as PDFs. A list of professional references will be required later in the process. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled; however, those received by September 17, 2026, can be assured full consideration. Nominations and expressions of interest can be submitted in confidence to SUNYPurchaseVPIA@academicsearch.org.  

  

To learn more about this opportunity and discuss your qualifications and interest, potential applicants are encouraged to send a copy of their curriculum vitae to SUNYPurchaseVPIA@academicsearch.

jobs.title: Managing Director, The Charleston Place
jobs.description:
The **Managing Director of The Charleston Place** is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, financial performance, operational excellence, and cultural stewardship of The Charleston Place and The Riviera Theatre. This executive role oversees all aspects of the hotel, including Rooms, Food \& Beverage, Sales \& Marketing, Finance, People \& Culture, Engineering, Spa, Retail, and guest experience, while also providing leadership oversight for The Riviera Theatre as a key BHC entertainment venue. The ideal candidate is a visionary, results\-driven luxury hospitality leader with a proven ability to inspire high\-performing teams, deliver exceptional financial outcomes, and consistently operate at a Forbes Five\-Star level. The Managing Director will also directly facilitate and coordinate a full\-scale hotel renovation, ensuring seamless alignment among ownership, design and construction partners, operational leaders, and colleagues while continuing to deliver an uncompromising five\-star guest and colleague experience throughout the transformation.

**DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Strategic Leadership** **\& Ownership Alignment**

* Set and execute the strategic vision for The Charleston Place, ensuring alignment with ownership priorities, BHC’s values, long\-term business objectives, and the hotel’s luxury positioning.
* Lead the Executive Committee and senior leadership team in developing and implementing short\- and long\-term strategies that drive service excellence, financial performance, colleague engagement, and operational discipline.
* Foster a high\-performance culture rooted in excellence, accountability, collaboration, and grace, ensuring every department reflects the hotel’s standards and service philosophy.
* Maintain visible, hands\-on leadership throughout the property, setting expectations for flawless daily execution, luxury service delivery, colleague professionalism, cleanliness, safety, and brand consistency.
* Conduct performance appraisals for Executive Committee members according to BHC standards and ensure leaders consistently develop, coach, and evaluate their teams.

**Renovation Leadership \& Five\-Star Operational Continuity:**

* Directly facilitate, coordinate, and support the execution of a full\-scale hotel renovation, serving as the primary operational leader between ownership, project management, design, construction, consultants, and hotel leadership.
* Ensure renovation planning and execution are fully integrated with daily hotel operations, minimizing disruption to guests, colleagues, revenue generation, and service delivery.
* Lead cross\-functional communication and decision\-making related to phasing, guest impact, colleague readiness, operational contingencies, safety, signage, service recovery, and brand presentation throughout the renovation.
* Protect and elevate the guest experience during periods of construction by maintaining Forbes Five\-Star service standards, proactive communication, luxury touchpoints, and thoughtful recovery strategies when needed.
* Partner with ownership and senior leaders to ensure renovation investments support the long\-term vision, market positioning, financial performance, and operational functionality of the hotel.

**BHC Brand Standards, Re\-Introduction \& Signature Food and Beverage:**

* Lead the implementation and ongoing refinement of BHC brand standards across all hotel departments, ensuring The Charleston Place consistently reflects the values, service philosophy, design intent, and luxury positioning of the collection.
* Guide the future re\-introduction of The Charleston Place to the market, ensuring the property’s renewed identity, guest experience, colleague culture, and operational execution are aligned with BHC’s long\-term vision.
* Place a strong emphasis on Food and Beverage as a defining pillar of the brand, developing and supporting signature offerings, destination restaurant and bar experiences, culinary programming, and memorable touchpoints that distinguish The Charleston Place within the luxury market.
* Partner closely with Food and Beverage, Culinary, Marketing, Sales, and Operations leaders to ensure signature offerings are commercially successful, operationally executable, locally relevant, and reflective of the hotel’s elevated service standards.
* Ensure every brand expression—from arrival experience and guest communications to dining, amenities, events, and colleague interactions—supports the re\-introduction of The Charleston Place as one of the South’s leading luxury hospitality destinations.

**Charleston Community Partnerships \& Brand Positioning:**

* Create and cultivate strategic partnerships within the Charleston community that enhance The Charleston Place’s brand name, reputation, visibility, and positioning as a landmark luxury destination.
* Develop relationships with cultural institutions, civic organizations, culinary leaders, artisans, luxury retailers, nonprofit partners, business leaders, and local tastemakers to strengthen the hotel’s connection to Charleston.
* Identify partnership opportunities that drive meaningful guest experiences, distinctive programming, public relations value, community goodwill, and revenue growth.
* Represent the hotel and BHC with professionalism and grace at community, civic, charitable, cultural, and industry events, serving as a visible ambassador for the brand.
* Ensure partnerships are aligned with the hotel’s values, luxury positioning, commercial priorities, and long\-term goal of deepening The Charleston Place’s role as an essential part of Charleston’s hospitality, culinary, and cultural landscape.

**Guest Experience \& Service Excellence:**

* Regularly review guest satisfaction scores and feedback, implementing strategies to exceed expectations and resolve any issues promptly, with the goal of transforming challenges into opportunities for improvement.
* Uphold and champion the highest standards of gues

jobs.title: Executive Director - Non-Profit
jobs.description:
**Executive Director**

Life Stories Child \& Family Advocacy in Greeley, Colorado is actively seeking an experienced leader as the Executive Director to lead and grow their thriving nonprofit. The Executive Director is ultimately responsible for the overall management of the agency in planning and administering programs, and staff that provide crucial services to abused and neglected children through the Child Advocacy Center and CASA Programs of Weld County. The Executive Director is responsible for leadership and management of the agency’s operational, strategic, programmatic, and fiscal goals and achievements. Operates under the general direction of the agency’s Board of Directors.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

Leadership \& Management:

* Maintaining consistent quality of non\-profit finance and administration, fundraising, communications, and systems; recommend timelines and resources needed to achieve the strategic goals.
* Recommends policies to the Board and/or assists the Board in developing specific written, long, and short\-range plans for the development of agency programs and services.
* Provides overall leadership and direction for the organization’s staff and operations.
* Support of DEI practices into becoming systemic in the agency culture.
* Strong commitment to both the National CASA and National Children’s Alliance Standards of Excellence.
* Ensure effective systems to measure successes ensuring programmatic excellence, rigorous program evaluation and measurement of success.
* Support, coach, and develop Life Stories senior management team.
* Partners with and supports the board of directors; serve as ex\-officio of each committee.
* Organizational risk management including but not limited to legal, and regulatory compliance, community, industry reputation, and financial risks.

**Financial and Fund Development:**

* Oversight of all financial operations of agency.
* Maintain and expand revenue generating and fundraising activities to support existing program operations while simultaneously maintaining healthy reserves.
* Use external presence and relationships to garner new opportunities for partnerships, sponsors, and volunteer recruitment and outreach.
* Completion, implementation, and monitoring of all grants and contracts current and new.
* Prepares with support of consultant, all agency budgets and long\-term funding plans for approval by the Board.

**Communications:**

* Deepen and refine all aspects of communications—from web and social media presence to external relations with the goal of maintaining a strong brand.

**Community:**

* Represents and interprets the mission, goals, and function of the agency to the community through direct involvement and through public relations programs.
* Maintains active representation and participation in the Colorado Children’s Alliance (CCA)

**Advocacy Centers and Colorado CASA.**

* Builds collaborative community relationships with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.
* Continues to build awareness of child well \-being and reducing and preventing child abuse and neglect.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree required, with at least 3 years of senior management experience; master’s degree preferred.
* Passion, integrity, positive attitude, mission\-driven, and self\-directed.
* Effective leadership of an outcomes\-based organization with the ability to coach staff and manage and develop high\-performance teams.
* Excellence in organizational management including budgeting and finance.
* Strong marketing, public relations, and fundraising experience with the ability to engage a wide range of stakeholders and cultures.
* Strong written and public speaking communication skills.
* Experience in leading the agency through the strategic planning process by setting and achieving strategic objectives. Ability to take an organization to the next stage of growth.
* Knowledge of the child welfare system, court system and volunteer management.
* Fund development, including grant writing, management, and resource development experience.
* Excellent human relations skills including problem\-solving, diplomacy and conflict resolution.
* Past success working with a board of directors with the ability to cultivate existing board member relationships.

Life Stories Child \& Family Advocacy offers a benefits package including paid holidays and PTO and professional development opportunities. Benefits include partial employer\-supported health insurance, life insurance, short\- and long\-term disability coverage and a 3% contribution to a Simple IRA.

**Annual Salary Range\- $85,000 \- $120,000, contingent upon education and experience.**

**This is an incredible opportunity to take a great organization with a sound reputation to the next level.**

Please submit a cover letter and resume to the attention of: **recruitment@lifestoriesweld.org**

*Life Stories Child \& Family Advocacy is an equal opportunity employer. The agency policy is to afford equal employment opportunities to all persons regardless of race, creed, color, religion, gender, national, social, or ethnic origin, age, physical condition, marital status, disability, veteran status, or sexual orientation. Our employees and applicants will not be subject to sexual, racial, religious, or any other form of unlawful harassment or discrimination.*

Pay: $85,000\.00 \- $120,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Assistant Development Director
jobs.description:
Since 1952, **Light of Life Rescue Mission** has been a safe refuge for homeless and hurting people in the Pittsburgh area. Our organization recently completed two major building projects and continues to grow in expanded services to serve the community.


Currently we seek an **Assistant Development Director** to provided leadership for the MarketingCommunications function and translates the fundraising, volunteer engagement, and organizational priorities established by the Director of Development into integrated marketing strategies and measurable campaigns.

**SUMMARY OF POSITION:**


The **Assistant Development Director** is responsible for leading people, systems, and projects rather than serving as the primary content producer. The Assistant Director is accountable for marketing strategy, brand stewardship, departmental operations, project management, team leadership, and performance while empowering the Communications Specialist, Digital MarketingContent Coordinator, and future staff to execute day\-to\-day marketing activities.




**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Lead the organization's marketing and communications strategy to increase brand awareness, donor engagement, volunteer engagement, church partnerships, and community support.
* Serve as the primary marketing advisor to the Director of Development by translating fundraising priorities into integrated marketing and communications strategies.
* Provide strategic oversight of all marketing projects by managing workflows, editorial calendars, campaign schedules, priorities, and cross\-functional coordination.
* Provide leadership, coaching, performance management, and professional development for the MarketingCommunications team.
* Direct creative strategy and approve major communications, ensuring consistency with organizational brand standards and messaging.
* Oversee marketing support for fundraising campaigns, donor engagement initiatives, volunteer recruitment, organizational events, and public awareness campaigns.
* Lead brand management, messaging frameworks, communications planning, crisis communications, and executive messaging.
* Lead marketing operations including technology, digital asset management, marketing systems, workflow processes, and continuous process improvement.
* Develop and manage the marketing budget; oversee agencies, photographers, videographers, designers, printers, and media partners.
* Establish marketing KPIs and dashboards; analyze campaign performance and recommend strategic improvements.
* Partner with leaders across Development, Programs, Operations, Volunteer Services, and Executive Leadership to communicate mission impact while protecting brand integrity.
* Responsible for representing and presenting Light of Life at events, churches, businesses, and other organizations throughout the city.
* Shared responsibility for representing Light of Life to the media.
* Make a persuasive verbal and written case for supporting key programs and projects effectively matching the interests of prospects to specific Mission needs.
* Maintain strong lines of communication with colleagues in Programs and Administration to ensure synergy in achieving fundraising goals and objectives.




*Due to the interface with the clients, all jobs at Light of Life require employees to:*

* Participate in the ministry of Light of Life Rescue Mission and walk alongside clients sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ with them through actions and words.
* Resolve all issues in ways that promote the principles of Light of Life while following the processes described in the Light of Life staff handbook.
* Practice Christlike stewardship of all resources.
* Subscribe to and embrace Light of Life's Statement of Faith, Values, and Principles.




**Education/Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Business, or related field.
* 5–7 years of progressive leadership experience.
* Exceptional project management and organizational skills.
* Experience leading integrated marketing campaigns and supervising staff.
* Experience with nonprofit fundraising communications preferred; Virtuous experience desirable.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**Director of Major Gifts**  
**Location:** Rochester, NY \| Onsite, 5 days/week

**Salary:** $75K\-$90K  
**Employment Type:** Full\-Time

Relay Recruiting is proud to partner with a well\-established nonprofit senior care and human services organization in the Rochester community, seeking a Director of Major Gifts to lead major and planned gift fundraising and deepen relationships with a loyal, multi\-generational donor base.

**The Opportunity**

The Director of Development will step into a well\-established portfolio of roughly 130–160 major gift and planned giving relationships, including several multi\-generational family foundations, with warm introductions ready to go from day one. Reporting directly to the Foundation's Executive Director and working as part of the senior leadership team, this person will cultivate, solicit, and steward donors while also self\-generating new prospects, particularly outside the organization's traditional donor community. Success in this role means blending relationship\-driven stewardship with a disciplined process: building trust with donors and families who are often navigating long\-term care, rehab, or memory care, while steadily growing gift size and building toward transformational giving. This is a role for a self\-starter who thrives on process, enjoys working with a close\-knit donor community, and wants a seat at the leadership table for a mission worth showing up for every day.

**About the Company**

This is a large, multi\-service nonprofit serving older adults across independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and memory care, with roughly 1,000 employees across its campus and programs. It's deeply rooted in community and tradition, with a culture that takes care of its employees, residents and their families. The foundation team is investing in its future, launching new signature fundraising events, growing its focus on donor cultivation beyond its traditional base, and renewing its push to engage the next generation of philanthropists. And with a supportive senior leadership team and strong internal relationships, it's a collaborative environment for someone ready to make a visible impact.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and grow a well\-established portfolio of major gift and planned giving donors, including numerous family foundations, picking up warm relationships from day one.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward major and planned gifts, building toward five\- and six\-figure asks with an eye toward transformational giving over time.
* Proactively identify, research, and engage new major gift prospects, including donors outside the organization's traditional community, to diversify and grow the base.
* Partner with the Executive Director to build and execute an annual major gift and planned giving work plan, including budgets, goals, and strategy.
* Build relationships with estate and financial planning professionals, and guide donors and their advisors toward planned giving vehicles that meet shared goals.
* Maintain current knowledge of gift and estate tax law and planned giving best practices.
* Support grant writing and funder identification alongside the Executive Director, contributing to an annual portfolio of roughly a dozen grants.
* Visit with donors and their families in long\-term care, rehab, and memory care settings, communicating the Foundation's role with warmth and steadiness.
* Represent the Foundation at community and donor events, including an annual golf tournament and emerging young\-leader engagement efforts.
* Deliver regular reporting and analysis on giving activity to the Foundation team and Board of Directors.

**What We're Looking For**

* 5\+ years of progressive fundraising experience, with proven success in major gift and planned giving work.
* A genuine self\-starter who's comfortable building and working a prospect pipeline.
* Bachelor's degree required.
* Excellent relationship\-building and stewardship instincts.
* Comfort and compassion navigating conversations with families in long\-term care, rehab, or memory care settings.
* Experience with donor management systems (Raiser's Edge preferred).
* Strong strategic planning, budgeting, and project management skills.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

**Bonus Points If You Have:**

* Grant writing or funder research experience.
* A track record of growing a donor base into new or non\-traditional communities.
* Experience or interest in engaging next\-generation or young donor audiences.

**Compensation and benefits**

* Base salary $75K\-$90K, commensurate with experience
* Generous PTO package

**Relay Recruiting is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status under applicable law.**

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $90,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* Fundraising: 5 years (Required)

Location:

* Rochester, NY 14602 (Required)

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Associate Executive Director
jobs.description:
Description:
**WHY WORK FOR THE YMCA OF SOUTH HAMPTON ROADS?**


Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads as an Executive Director. The historical attractions of Richmond and the resort city of Outer Banks, NC are only a short drive away.


The YMCA of South Hampton Roads association is recognized as a cutting\-edge leader in the YMCA movement. The association serves the communities of: Chesapeake, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Suffolk, Virginia Beach, Eastern Shore of Virginia, Outer Banks, and Elizabeth City, North Carolina at its 26 locations.


Excellent benefits package includes leadership development opportunities and training to secure a promising future for our employees and our association.

**Core benefits include:**

* Health, Long\-term disability and life insurance
* Generous Paid Time Off
* Employer contributions to 401A retirement (based on qualified hours)
* 403B retirement plan (employee contributions)
* Free YMCA membership at all locations \+ 24\-hour access
* 50% discount on YMCA child care and camp programs
* Discounts at partner organizations and businesses
* Mobile service providers
* Event tickets
* Educational Institutions and more
* Employee Resource Groups
* Membership in the YMCA Professional Network
* Employee Assistance Program
* Continued development and certification

**OUR CULTURE:**


Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. In the Y, we strive to live our cause of strengthening communities with purpose and intentionality every day. We are welcoming: we are open to all. We are a place where you can belong and become. We are genuine: we value you and embrace your individuality. We are hopeful: we believe in you and your potential to become a catalyst in the world. We are nurturing: we support you in your journey to develop your full potential. We are determined: above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger beginning with you.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**


Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Associate Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the daily operations. This position provides cause\-driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal oversight, financial development, program administration, facility and equipment stewardship, community relations, and personal and professional development.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Division of Duties**

* 65% Direct leadership of all day\-to\-day operations
* 20% \- Property Management
* 10% \- Leadership role in the Annual Impact Fund
* 5% \- Staff development of direct reports

**Priorities**

* Supervise all the day\-to\-day operations of the assigned location.
* Develop, manage, and achieve the budget expectations with an emphasis on licensed childcare programs, Events and Rentals, Sports and Aquatic programming, Community Relations, and Fundraising.
* Assist with all fundraising efforts with an emphasis on staff and community giving.
* Support board development by assisting the Executive Director in recruiting three new board members annually and leading a board subcommittee.
* Oversee property management, ensuring the upkeep of all grounds and facilities.
* Foster relationship development with key home office leaders, including VPs of various product lines.

**Budget and Financial Performance**

* Develop, manage, and monitor operating budgets to meet or exceed targets.
* Initiate adjustments to operations to ensure a balanced budget.
* Ensure completion of monthly variance reports and forecasting.

**Program Development and Membership Engagement**

* Implements Association childcare strategies that support recruitment of new participants and retention of existing participants. Creates a member\-focused culture and models relationship\-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA “listen first” skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants and interests of participants. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure participant satisfaction
* Develops long\-range plans for the expansion of programs and services in harmony with overall YMCA objectives. Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
* Represents and promotes the YMCA in the local community by developing positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities
* Ensures safety, cleanliness, and function of all related facilities and equipment
* Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals

**Development and supervision of the Family Center operations**

* Recruits, hires, trains, develops, and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates staff performance. Develops strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for supervision of exempt and non\-exempt employees
* Ensures all program operations are consistent with association procedures, including emergency, insurance, accident, purchasing, personnel, accounting, and other administrative systems

**Fundraising**

* Provides leadership and is accountable for achieving annual impact fund campaign

**Professional Development**

* Partner with another executive to develop and master the skills needed to move into an executive role. These include leading up, financial analysis and troubleshooting, complex problem solving, and developing a positive team environment and culture.
* Assists in all areas as assigned by supervisor

**YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES (Multi\-Team Leader)**

* Communication \& Influence
* Fiscal Management
* Engaging Community


Requirements:
**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Strong business operations background with a proven track record for producing growth, annual giving and strong financial management
* A Bachelor's Degree in a child\-related field or Sports Management/ Recreation/Health Sciences is preferred, or

jobs.description:
Description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**


Under the general direction of the Vice President of Operations, the District Executive Director manages the overall operations of multiple Family Centers, including staff and programs. The District Executive Director supervises, develops and implements a full range of services including Membership, Wellness, Aquatics, Sports and Family Programs, Facilities Management, Scholarship and Board Development.

**OUR CULTURE**


Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. In the Y, we strive to live our cause of strengthening communities with purpose and intentionality every day. **We are welcoming:** we are open to all. We are a place where you can belong and become. **We are genuine**: we value you and embrace your individuality. **We are hopeful**: we believe in you and your potential to become a catalyst in the world. **We are nurturing**: we support you in your journey to develop your full potential. **We are determined:** above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger beginning with you. **We are the Y.**

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**LEAD MULTIPLE FAMILY CENTERS**

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for assigned Family Centers, ensuring alignment with the YMCA of Central Florida's mission, strategic priorities, and operational standards.
* Partner with Executive Directors, Associate Executive Directors, Operations Directors, and department leaders to drive operational excellence, leadership consistency, and achievement of key performance indicators across assigned Family Centers.

**FINANCIAL LEADERSHIP**

* Oversee the financial performance of assigned Family Centers by building, managing and forecasting operating budgets, monitoring financial results, identifying opportunities for growth, and ensuring responsible stewardship of organizational resources.

**TALENT LEADERSHIP**

* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high\-performing leadership teams. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, engagement, succession planning and continuous professional development while supporting leadership succession planning.
* Provide ongoing coaching, performance management, and leadership development for direct reports and center leadership to strengthen organizational effectiveness and talent readiness.

**OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE**

* Drive consistent execution of operational standards, policies, and best practices across assigned Family Centers to ensure high\-quality member experiences and operational efficiency.
* Partner with Association support departments to implement organizational initiatives, improve operational processes, leverage technology, and promote continuous improvement.

**MEMBERSHIP \& PROGRAM GROWTH**

* Lead strategies that strengthen membership growth, member retention, program participation, and overall member engagement across assigned Family Centers.
* Ensure programs, services, and schedules reflect community needs while maintaining consistent quality, operational excellence, and alignment with YMCA standards.

**RISK MANAGEMENT \& FACILITY OPERATIONS**

* Promote a culture of safety, compliance, and accountability by partnering with center leadership to proactively identify and address operational, safety, and risk management priorities while maintaining YMCA standards and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure assigned Family Centers maintain safe, clean, welcoming, and well\-maintained facilities that support exceptional member experiences.
* Report all accidents/incidents to your s and follow the Association’s employee and member injury reporting procedures.

**COMMUNITY \& VOLUNTEER LEADERSHIP**
