jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Operations

Ready to build and scale the operational backbone for a global pioneer in power quality and energy monitoring? As our North American expansion accelerates, we are hiring a strategic, hands\-on **Director of Operations** to drive delivery, optimize processes, and build a world\-class execution engine.

Reporting directly to the **Chief Operating Officer**, you will lead our **Project \& Program Management, Business Analysis, and Field Services** teams. Working across Sales, Engineering, Finance, and Product, you will turn rapid growth into scalable operation, leveraging data to streamline customer project delivery and on\-site field execution.

If you are an operational leader who excels at bridging high\-level strategy with hands\-on field execution, this role was built for you.

**Location:** Remote (hybrid preferred if local to Northern Virginia)

**Schedule:** Eastern Standard Time

**Compensation:** $160,000 \- $200,000 base with a 20% target annual bonus

**Responsibilities**

**Operational Strategy \& Team Leadership**

* **Strategic Execution:** Develop and execute an operational strategy aligned with core business goals, building scalable processes to manage growth and mitigate operational risk.
* **Team Development \& Succession:** Lead, coach, and develop multidisciplinary teams across Project Management, Program Management, and Field Services—fostering high accountability and building leadership depth for organizational resiliency and future executive succession.
* **Workforce \& Performance Alignment:** Partner with executive leadership on workforce planning, resource allocation, and continuous improvement initiatives that elevate team productivity and customer satisfaction.

**Project Management Office (PMO)**

* **Standardization \& Governance:** Lead the Project Management team driving customer implementations and internal strategic initiatives, establishing standardized methodologies, governance, documentation, and executive reporting.
* **On\-Time, In\-Scope Delivery:** Improve project visibility through milestone tracking and resource planning to ensure initiatives are delivered on time, within scope, and on budget.
* **Cross\-Functional Handoffs:** Partner with Sales and Engineering to streamline project handoffs and customer onboarding.

**Business Process Improvement \& Automation**

* **Process Excellence \& Automation:** Oversee the Business Analysis function to evaluate workflows, champion Lean/continuous improvement methodologies, and eliminate manual effort through smart automation.
* **Systems Optimization:** Maximize the performance and utilization of enterprise systems (ERP, CRM) to increase efficiency and elevate the customer experience.

**Data Analytics \& Performance Management**

* **Executive Dashboards \& Forecasting:** Build operational dashboards and leverage business analytics to refine forecasting and drive data\-backed decision\-making.
* **KPI Tracking:** Monitor, manage, and present key operational metrics to executive leadership—including project completion rates, customer satisfaction, process efficiency, and supplier performance.

**Global \& Cross\-Functional Alignment**

* **Unified Execution:** Partner seamlessly across Sales, Engineering, Finance, Customer Support, Logistics/Warehouse, Executive Leadership, and global headquarters to ensure tight organizational alignment.

**Requirements**

**Baseline Requirements**

* **Education \& Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related field, backed by 8–12 years of progressive operations leadership experience—including 5\+ years directly leading cross\-functional teams and managing multiple operational functions simultaneously.
* **PMO \& Process Excellence:** Strong working knowledge of project management methodologies with a proven track record of leading organizational process improvements.
* **Systems \& Analytics:** Hands\-on experience with ERP systems, CRM platforms, and operational reporting, supported by strong analytical and financial acumen.
* **Leadership \& Executive Presence:** Excellent communication and executive presentation skills with a history of building and coaching high\-performing teams.
* **Travel Flexibility:** Willingness to travel up to 35% (including visits to Ashburn, VA, and global headquarters).

**What Will Make You Stand Out**

* **Domain \& Technical Context:** Experience within manufacturing, industrial technology, electrical equipment, automation, or energy management industries, with direct exposure to supporting technical product organizations.
* **Certifications:** PMP certification.
* **Global Exposure:** Prior experience working with international organizations.

**How We Measure Success**

In your first 12–18 months, success in this role means:

* **PMO Standardization:** You have standardized project management processes, governance, and reporting across all customer implementations and internal initiatives.
* **Delivery Performance:** You have measurably increased on\-time project delivery and operational execution.
* **Executive Visibility:** You have developed and implemented executive operational KPI dashboards that drive data\-backed decision\-making.
* **Process Automation:** You have identified and executed high\-impact business process automation opportunities that eliminate manual effort and increase efficiency.
* **Cross\-Functional Alignment:** You have strengthened operational integration and collaboration across Sales, Engineering, Operations, and Finance.
* **Scalable Operations:** You have built a resilient, scalable operational structure fully equipped to support our continued expansion.

**Company** **Benefits:**

Health, Vision, Dental – Client covers 80% of employee premium, 401K with 4% match, PTO, All Federal Holidays, Annual Bonus, Professional Development Opportunities. No wait on any benefits, enroll day 1\.

Pay: $160,000\.00 \- $200,000\.00

**Job Title: Chief Operating Officer**


**Location****:** 1900 Silver Lake Rd, New Brighton, MN 55112



**Working Model:** Hybrid



**Employee Type:** Full Time

  



At Sagent Behavioral Health, we believe profound change is possible. As one of the largest behavioral health organizations in the Midwest—with 2,000\+ team members across 80\+ locations in five states—we offer the stability and resources to help you thrive.  

  

Backed by more than 100 years of combined behavioral health experience, Sagent brings together the trusted legacies of Ellie Mental Health, LifeWorks, Nystrom \& Associates, Psychiatric Associates, Sandhill Counseling \& Consultation, and Vantage Point.  

  

Here, you'll find a supportive, inclusive culture where you can hone your skills, collaborate with a fantastic team, and build a rewarding career focused on what matters most: helping others find hope. Guided by our HOPE values—Humility, Optimism, People\-Centered, and Ethical Practice—we provide manageable caseloads, flexible schedules, and compensation options that work for you.  


The Chief Operating Officer (COO), along with the senior leadership team, will help define and lead the company’s strategy and operations to ensure organizational alignment and disciplined execution against the organizational goals. The ideal COO will bring a track record of leading successful multi\-site healthcare businesses through growth, operational improvement, and measurable performance gains. This executive will use data, analytics, and consistent operating metrics to identify opportunities, prioritize resources, monitor execution, and drive accountability across the enterprise. The COO will provide leadership and serve as a unifying force within the organization, maintaining a mission\-driven culture of clinical quality, operational excellence, patient satisfaction, and continuous improvement.  


**Full\-Time Benefits:**



* Medical, Dental, Vision


* 401k, Long Term Disability, Short Term Disability and Life Insurance


* Comfortable offices and clinic environment
  



**Responsibilities:**


* Oversee company operations to ensure that people, systems, processes, and performance data are in place for the business to scale, while not sacrificing superior patient care.
* Recruit, retain, and develop talent at all levels; use data, performance metrics, and regular operating reviews to coach, mentor, and develop leaders who can drive consistent results across the organization.
* Continue to build a culture and environment that embraces growth, operational improvement, patient service excellence, compliance, measurable performance improvement, and accountability for results.
* Provide day\-to\-day operational leadership and P\&L management of the company across all functions, using dashboards, KPIs, and analytics to identify trends, prioritize action, improve execution, and support near\- and long\-term value creation.
* Lead the strategy of the business, working closely with the chief executive officer (CEO) and senior management; provide oversight of the business across all functions.
* Provide regular, data\-informed updates to the CEO and board of directors on business performance, opportunities, risks, key operating metrics, and progress against strategic priorities.
* Develop and foster strong relationships with regional operations leaders and clinical leaders to review financial, operational, clinical, and patient\-experience performance; use analytics to benchmark best practices, identify leadership development needs, and support the effective roll\-out and management of clinical initiatives.

  


**Requirements:**


* 10\+ years of senior leadership experience in multi\-site healthcare or healthcare services; for\-profit experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading scalable operations across multiple locations while maintaining high standards for clinical quality and patient care.
* Proven P\&L ownership and ability to improve financial, operational, clinical, and patient\-experience performance.
* Experience using KPIs, dashboards, analytics, and operating reviews to drive execution, accountability, and measurable results.
* Track record of recruiting, retaining, developing, and coaching leaders capable of delivering consistent enterprise\-wide outcomes.
* Experience supporting organic and inorganic growth, including evaluation, affiliation, integration, or expansion of healthcare businesses.
* Ability to build collaborative relationships with clinical, regional operations, executive, and board\-level stakeholders.
* Demonstrated commitment to patient service excellence, compliance, continuous improvement, and operational discipline.
* Experience translating strategy into clear priorities, action plans, resource allocation, and sustained performance improvement.
* Behavioral health experience preferred but not required.
  


**Compensation:** $250,000\-$350,000 plus bonus/incentives.


* Actual compensation may be determined by various factors such as education, experience, skillset, internal equity, schedule and/or location.
  


*Sagent* *Behavioral Health is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.*

**Position Description:**

The Center for Precision Behavioral Health Research \& Innovation at the University of Louisville is seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to provide strategic and operational leadership for a high\-impact behavioral health center integrating clinical research, basic research, digital innovation, community outreach, and philanthropy. In close partnership with the Center Director, the COO ensures that the Center's scientific vision is translated into efficient, scalable, and sustainable research programs that improve behavioral health outcomes and expand access to care.


This role oversees all operational domains, including program execution, research operations, financial management, compliance, and infrastructure, while building systems that support growth across grant\-funded and revenue\-generating activities. The COO plays a critical role in scaling digital health tools, managing complex research portfolios, and ensuring seamless coordination across interdisciplinary teams. **This position is supported by one\-time funding designated for the development of the Center. As with all positions supported by limited\-term funding sources, continuation of the position is subject to the availability of funding and institutional priorities.**

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**  

Duties include leading day\-to\-day operations and translating strategic priorities into actionable plans with clear metrics, timelines, and accountability; collaborating with the Center Director and Principal Investigators to ensure efficient coordination of research initiatives, including randomized controlled trials, digital interventions, longitudinal research, and multiple complex research trials; managing budgets across grants, contracts, and other revenue streams; supporting forecasting, sustainability planning, and growth scenarios; building and expanding operations for innovative behavioral health programs, including technology\-enabled interventions; recruiting, supervising, and mentoring interdisciplinary staff; providing administrative and HR oversight of research managers, research assistants, and other staff; ensuring adherence to HIPAA, IRB processes, federal and state regulations, and other relevant compliance standards; implementing quality assurance systems; developing and maintaining relationships with institutional leadership, funders, community partners, and industry collaborators; and designing and implementing operational systems, workflows, and data infrastructure to support scale, efficiency, and evaluation.


**Preferred Qualifications**  

Master's degree (e.g., MPH, MHA, MBA, MS) with substantial leadership experience, or PhD in a relevant field such as clinical psychology, public health, health services research, or a related discipline.


Demonstrated experience in operations, program leadership, or center management in behavioral health, healthcare, or research settings. Strong financial management and grant portfolio oversight experience. Experience working with or scaling clinical research programs, particularly clinical trial research studies, or digital health and AI\-based interventions. Knowledge of regulatory and compliance frameworks, including HIPAA and IRB processes. Exceptional organizational, leadership, and communication skills.


Experience managing large, multi\-site, or federally funded research programs. Background in implementation science or translating research into practice. jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
7 Flags Car Wash is a community-focused car care provider offering full-service, self-service, detailing, express washing, and an express lube center in Fairfield, California. The company is deeply committed to giving back through programs such as “Helping Hands,” which supports local non-profit fundraising, and partnerships with organizations including Grace for Vets, Susan G. Komen, and The Leaven. 7 Flags honors military members and veterans with special discounts and free car washes on Veterans Day, and promotes environmental stewardship through Earth Day clean-up activities and complimentary washes for hybrid and electric vehicles. Rooted in family and community values, 7 Flags Car Wash emphasizes long-term growth, service excellence, and strong relationships with customers and community partners.

Position Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as the senior operational leader of the organization and is responsible for translating the company's vision into consistent operational execution across all locations.
This is a highly engaged, field-oriented executive leadership role. The COO maintains a visible presence throughout the organization, working alongside operational leaders to develop leaders, strengthen systems, remove organizational barriers, and ensure operational excellence. The COO builds organizational capability by improving decision-making, strengthening accountability, and designing systems that enable the organization to perform consistently without unnecessary executive intervention.
Working in close partnership with the President/CEO and executive leadership team, the COO ensures the organization's people, systems, and operational performance support the company's long-term growth while preserving its culture and values.

Essential Responsibilities

Leadership & Talent Development

Provide executive leadership, coaching, and mentorship to operational leaders throughout the organization.
Establish clear leadership expectations, decision authority, and performance standards that promote consistency across all locations.
Strengthen leadership capability and business acumen throughout the organization by developing managerial judgment, accountability, coaching effectiveness, critical thinking and leadership succession.

Operational Excellence

Assume overall responsibility for operational performance across all company locations.
Maintain a visible and engaged presence throughout company operations ensuring operational execution remains aligned with the company's strategic objectives.
Translate strategic priorities into consistent execution through clear ownership, disciplined follow-through, and defined decision authority.
Ensure consistent execution of company standards, operating procedures, safety expectations, regulatory compliance, financial objectives, and guest experience initiatives.
Promote cross-functional collaboration to achieve shared organizational objectives.
Partner with operational leaders to optimize labor, operating expenses, resource allocation, and site performance while maintaining exceptional guest experience.
Ensure significant operational incidents, customer damage claims, and corrective actions are resolved consistently and effectively.

Organizational Capability

Continuously refine leading indicators, key performance indicators (KPIs), and forecasting processes to anticipate business needs, improve resource planning, and enable proactive operational decision-making.
Design, implement, and strengthen operating systems, workflows, management disciplines, and organizational practices that improve consistency, increase organizational capacity, and support long-term scalability.
Establish operating rhythms, performance review processes, and management systems that enable leaders to identify, address, and resolve issues before executive intervention becomes necessary.
Leverage operational metrics, reporting, and performance data to strengthen decision-making and improve organizational performance.

Strategic Execution

Lead strategic initiatives that strengthen organizational capability while reinforcing organizational principles.
Partner with the President/CEO and executive leadership team to establish priorities, allocate resources, and execute the company's long-term strategic objectives.
Provide the President/CEO and executive leadership team with timely assessments of operational performance, organizational risks, and emerging business needs to support strategic decision-making.
Partner with the President/CEO and executive leadership team to achieve operational and financial objectives through disciplined execution, sound resource allocation, and continuous improvement.
Evaluate organizational performance to identify opportunities that improve efficiency, consistency, safety, financial results, guest experience, and long-term growth.

Financial Performance

Assume responsibility for operational P&L performance across the organization.
Improve profitability through disciplined management of labor, operating expenses, and operational efficiency.
Utilize operational and financial data to identify trends, prioritize improvements, and support informed business decisions.
Develop and execute strategies that improve EBITDA, membership growth, retention, customer lifetime value, and overall profitability.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive multi-site operational leadership experience, including responsibility for multiple locations and large, geographically dispersed teams.
Proven ability to develop leaders and build high-performing management teams.
Strong operational, financial, and strategic business acumen.
Exceptional coaching, communication, and leadership skills.
Demonstrated ability to build systems, improve processes, and create organizational scalability.
Experience leading organizational change and driving continuous improvement initiatives.
Ability to analyze operational and financial data to support sound business decisions.
Strong understanding of regulatory compliance, workplace safety, and operational risk management.
Ability to build trust and credibility at every level of the organization through visible, hands-on leadership.
Demonstrated ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution.

Leadership Expectations

The successful COO consistently demonstrates the ability to:
Maintain a visible presence throughout the organization.
Develop leaders before solving problems personally.
Make timely decisions despite incomplete information.
Hold leaders accountable while providing coaching and support.
Use data to inform judgment rather than replace it.
Build trust through consistency, transparency, and follow-through.
Preserve the company's culture while raising organizational performance.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
About the Organization

The National Center for Family Philanthropy (NCFP) activates a diverse community of philanthropic families to embrace bold vision and realize their greatest giving potential. We do this by sharing proven practices, working through common challenges, and learning together — strengthening our collective ability to drive meaningful change. We serve family philanthropy decision-makers through convenings, virtual and asynchronous learning, peer cohorts, and individualized support. NCFP is growing, and we're looking for a thoughtful, proactive Executive Assistant (EA) to manage the CEO’s office and support the three-person executive team.

Position Overview

The Executive Assistant (EA) to the CEO plays a critical role in ensuring the effectiveness and efficiency of the executive office, with a primary focus on supporting the Chief Executive Officer. This position partners closely with a small executive leadership team and serves as a key coordinator of priorities, information flow, and administrative operations.
The EA manages complex scheduling, prepares leaders for meetings and engagements, supports communication workflows, and ensures seamless day-to-day operations. This role requires strong judgment, discretion, and the ability to anticipate needs in a fast-paced, relationship-driven environment.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and prioritize the CEO’s calendar, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and proactively identifying potential conflicts or constraints
Serve as a primary point of contact for the executive office, managing inbound communications and facilitating timely, thoughtful responses
Prepare briefing materials and ensure the CEO is fully prepared for meetings, events, and external engagements
Track action items and follow-ups to support accountability and continuity across the executive team
Maintain accurate notes and records of meetings in alignment with organizational systems
Coordinate travel arrangements and logistical details for executive engagements

jobs.description:
As a thought-leader and best-in-class provider in education, wellness, youth development, and community-building, The YMCA of Metro Atlanta is one of the oldest and most essential non-profits serving in Atlanta. Today, we’re looking for you to join us as we carry out our mission to positively impact lives and communities across the state.

At the Y, we’re an association of like-minded people (staff, volunteers, and members), on the forefront of a movement to ensure that everyone -- especially children -- experience an equal opportunity to reach their full potential. In the course of a year, we provide more than 3,000 children, ages 6 weeks through Pre-K with high-quality literacy and STEAM-infused learning; give 58,000 youth and teens access to sports, aquatics, day and resident camps, teen leadership development programs, and employment opportunities; provide over 200,000 members with programs, services, and facilities to enjoy connection and maintain wellness regardless of age; and engage over 25,000 volunteers and donors from across Atlanta to share in the gift of supporting their communities.

Nature And Scope

The YMCA of Metro Atlanta is seeking a passionate and forward-thinking executive director with a proven, successful track record of developing a strong branch board, increasing annual giving, engaging community through increasing membership and programs while advancing the Y’s impact in the community.

This highly motivated leader who is impact focused and entrepreneurial by nature will report directly to the Group Vice President and will have primary responsibility for day-to-day operations. Experience in and a demonstrated track record of the areas of staff supervision, membership and program development, fiscal management, fundraising, volunteer cultivation, and community engagement are required. The continued development and coaching of an experienced staff team to new levels of service will be key to achieving full potential.

RESPONSIBILITIES (including, But Not Limited To)

Establish a culture of quality and service to meet and exceed the goals and objectives set forth in the strategic plan and standards established by the Board of Directors.
Represents and promotes the Y in the local community by developing strategic, positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities.
Develop, manage, and monitor a balanced operating budget to meet or exceed budgeted targets.
Develop and direct high quality, relationship-based member engagement strategies.
Provide metrics to measure program/membership impact, staff, and program and membership satisfaction.
Maintain branch and association certifications in CPR, Multimedia First Aid, Blood-borne Pathogens, Metro Atlanta YMCA new staff orientation, branch orientation and branch emergency procedures.
Manage delivery of related programs to exceed YMCA standards and program objectives.
Participate in branch and Association-wide activities and initiatives.
Act as the LEAD campaigner for Why It Matters Annual Giving Campaign including but not limited to volunteer recruitment, training and support, and lead as an integral member of the management team committed to reaching stated fund-raising goals.
Serve on the Executive Cabinet, liaison with appropriate professional groups in the community and serve on Metro Task Forces.
Effective board development including recruitment of board members who represent the branch community and developing a strong board committee structure.
Ensures revenue growth through a climate of innovation to develop member-focused programs which support the Y mission, goals, and strategies.
Effectively mentor, supervise, and develop branch staff and volunteers and build an exceptional culture to motivate them to achieve their personal and professional goals.
Responsible for facility management and maintenance to ensure high quality facilities, grounds, and equipment. A culture of risk management and safety is maintained at the branch. Maintains required safety and training certifications, Emergency Action Plans, SDS Manuals, etc.

Requirements

Bachelor's Degree and 8+ years overall leadership experience or high school diploma and 12+ years of directly relevant experience with the Y or closely related non-profit
2+ years of successful experience managing large teams in an executive level/senior management position
Business management skills and demonstrated ability to lead people
Proven ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organization, corporations, and government agencies
Strong attention to detail
Passionate commitment to the YMCA mission, values, and purpose
CPR and First Aid certifications required within 30 days of hire

Preferred Requirements

Bachelor's degree in human services, social services, business or equivalent
Experience in directing total operations through volunteer development, supervision of staff, development and monitoring of branch budget, marketing and public relations, and program development
Hands on experience working with a diverse population in a YMCA strongly preferred
12+ years of directly relevant experience with the YMCA or closely related non-profit
4+ years of management experience, strategic vision and relationship building preferably in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency

Employment and Benefits package for this job posting is offered through the YMCA of Metropolitan Atlanta, Inc.

Job Summary

The Career Development Center is seeking an Executive Director
of Career Development
. This is a full-time (1.00 FTE), 12-month, professional faculty position.

The Executive Director of Career Development provides university-wide leadership for career development at Oregon State University, advancing a comprehensive, coordinated and student-centered career ecosystem that serves undergraduate and graduate students across Corvallis, OSU-Cascades in Bend, and Ecampus. The Executive Director leads the strategy, programs, partnerships, operations and assessment efforts that help students explore purpose, build career readiness and advancement, connect academic learning to future pathways, engage with employers and alumni, and transition successfully to meaningful work, graduate education, service, entrepreneurship and other post-graduation opportunities.

This position is responsible for building upon Oregon State University’s ecosystem of career development and the vision of Beyond OSU: a university-wide commitment to integrating career development across the student experience so that every student has access to timely, relevant and inclusive career learning, experiences and connections. The Executive Director works collaboratively across the institution, including academic colleges, Student Affairs, Academic Affairs, OSU-Cascades, Ecampus, graduate education, advising, experiential learning, alumni engagement, employer relations, industry partnerships, student employment/University Human Resources, faculty and staff networks, and other university partners to strengthen career readiness as a shared institutional priority.

The Executive Director provides strategic leadership for the Career Development Center and related career development initiatives, including career education, career integration, employer and alumni engagement, experiential learning, technology, data, assessment, staff development, resource stewardship, and university-wide partnerships. This role develops and evaluates short- and long-range plans, sets standards for high-quality and equitable career development practices, and leads efforts to ensure that career development is intentionally embedded within curricular and co-curricular experiences for students across modalities, campuses and academic levels.

The Executive Director reports to the Associate Vice President of Student Affairs and serves as a member of the Associate Vice President’s leadership team. In this capacity, the Executive Director contributes to Student Affairs priorities, collaborates with peer leaders across the division, and helps align career development strategy with broader divisional and university goals for student success, engagement, belonging, well-being and post-graduation outcomes.

Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with senior leaders, campus partners, employers, alumni, students and community stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience in building partnerships and relationships with stakeholders, including ability to navigate conflict and find solutions to shared challenges.
Demonstrated ability to use data, assessment and evidence-based practices to inform decision-making, evaluate outcomes and guide continuous improvement.
Experience managing budgets, resources, projects, technology systems or operational processes.
Ability to exercise independent judgment, diplomacy, discretion and confidentiality in a complex and highly collaborative environment.

At Tidewater Tech

As a leading educational provider in the trade industry, our programs, designed in collaboration with industry leaders, ensure that students are well-prepared for today’s workplace. With high academic standards and hands-on training, we create a learning environment that supports student success. At Tidewater Tech, we’re dedicated to shaping the next generation of skilled professionals.

CAMPUS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

Tidewater Tech — Two Campus Locations

Lead the Campus. Drive the Mission. Deliver Results.

Business Purpose

The Campus Executive Director is responsible for the overall success and long-term performance of two Tidewater Tech campuses. As the senior executive leader for both locations, this role drives operational excellence, financial performance, academic quality, regulatory compliance, and student outcomes while ensuring each campus delivers on the institution's mission to prepare students for successful careers in the skilled trades.

Through strategic leadership, sound financial stewardship, data-driven decision making, and the development of high-performing leadership teams, the Campus Executive Director creates an environment where students, employees, and the institution thrive. Success is measured through sustainable enrollment growth, student retention and graduation, career placement outcomes, employee engagement, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and the overall health and culture of each campus.

Key Competencies

Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute long-term business strategies that drive sustainable enrollment growth, operational excellence, and financial performance across both campuses.
Academic & Student Experience Leadership: Champion academic quality and the overall student experience by ensuring instructional excellence, student engagement, persistence, graduation, and career readiness.
High-Level Stakeholder Management: Build and maintain relationships with key industry partners, accrediting bodies, and community organizations to foster collaboration and support campus initiatives.
Broader Accountability: Lead the financial strategy for the campus, ensuring sustainable growth and efficient resource allocation to support long-term goals.
Decision-Making & Influence: Lead campus hiring decisions, shaping the organizational structure to meet strategic objectives, and ensuring staff performance aligns with campus goals.
Enhance Outcome Focus: Drive measurable improvements in student outcomes and operational efficiency, with accountability for key performance indicators such as graduation rates, job placement success, and campus financial performance.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic, Operational & Financial Leadership

Own overall business performance for both campuses, including P&L accountability, revenue growth, budgeting, forecasting, operational efficiency, and long-term financial sustainability.
Develop and execute strategic growth plans aligned with organizational priorities.
Develop enrollment forecasts and operational plans that align staffing, instructional capacity, and financial performance.
Lead campus leadership teams to achieve enrollment, retention, graduation, placement, and financial performance goals.
Drive operational excellence through continuous process improvement and effective resource allocation.
Oversee campus facilities, capital planning, and operational investments while evaluating future expansion opportunities.
Identify and mitigate operational, financial, regulatory, and reputational risks impacting campus performance

Academic Quality & Regulatory Compliance

Directly manage the Director of Education at each campus while maintaining accountability for academic quality, instructional excellence, and student learning outcomes.
Champion a student-centered learning environment that promotes engagement, persistence, graduation, and career readiness.
Ensure compliance with accrediting agencies, state regulators, Title IV, Title IX, and all institutional policies.
Lead accreditation visits, audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory reporting.
Partner with academic leadership to ensure curriculum, instructional delivery, and academic resources remain aligned with employer and student needs.

Directly lead, coach, and develop the campus leadership team across Academics, Admissions, Student Financial Services, Student & Career Success, and Compliance.
Build and sustain a high-performing, mission-driven culture centered on accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and exceptional student service.
Recruit, develop, and retain campus leaders while building a strong succession pipeline for critical leadership positions.
Establish clear performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and hold leaders accountable for achieving campus and organizational objectives.
Partner effectively with Corporate functional leaders through a matrix leadership structure to ensure alignment with institutional standards, initiatives, and best practices.
Lead organizational change initiatives while fostering employee engagement, adaptability, and operational excellence.

Community, Industry & Stakeholder Engagement

Represent both campuses as the senior executive leader within the community.
Develop strategic partnerships with employers, workforce agencies, military organizations, secondary schools, community leaders, and advisory boards.
Strengthen employer relationships to support graduate placement, curriculum relevance, and workforce development initiatives.
Promote Tidewater Tech's mission and reputation throughout the communities served

Data-Driven Performance Management

Leverage dashboards, KPIs, and operational reporting to evaluate campus performance and identify improvement opportunities.
Translate business insights into actionable strategies that improve enrollment, student outcomes, employee performance, and financial results.
Monitor organizational health across both campuses and proactively address emerging trends and challenges.
Regularly communicate campus performance, strategic initiatives, and business results to executive leadership.

Bachelor’s Degree
Must have at least five (5) years of management experience in post-secondary education, preferably in private, for-profit, career-focused, or trade/technical settings
Experience directly managing leaders across Admissions, Financial Aid, Student & Career Success, Compliance, and Education/Academics
Demonstrated ownership of academic quality and the overall student academic experience

Demonstrated history of improving student outcomes (retention, graduation, placement)

Ability to manage two campus locations, including regular travel between sites

jobs.title: Associate Director of Development
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Associate Director of Development (ADoD) works closely with the development team to implement and coordinate effective multi-year strategies and plans for gift prospects, including individual, corporate, and/or foundation donors.

The Associate Director of Development is responsible for increasing the major and principal gift donor pipeline and managing a portfolio of qualified donors and developing relationships. They understand and apply the principles of developing donor strategies that fulfil the donor’s interests and align with the organization’s conservation funding needs. They are knowledgeable and can navigate conversations regarding gifts of assets and other non-cash gifts, such as planned gifts and real estate. The ADoD provides opportunities for donors to receive recognition and increase future giving. They are extraordinarily collaborative involving appropriate partners in the field and Global Development staff, keeping them apprised of interactions, issues or concerns, and direct questions as appropriate. They may be responsible for volunteer engagement within formal and/or informal networks. The ADoD will be required to use TNC’s donor database and will participate in the development of proposals. Given the geographic size of Tennessee, they will travel frequently and on short notice, work long and flexible hours as needed. The work environment may involve infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.

We’re Looking For You

The ADoD will work closely with the Development Team, State Director, Board of Trustees, and Conservation program leaders to plan, implement, and coordinate effective multi-year strategies and plans for gift prospects, including individual donors, foundations and corporations to support the conservation goals of the Nature Conservancy’s Tennessee Business Unit.

The ADoD is responsible for building and maintaining a portfolio of qualified donors and developing donor relationships. They will:

Increase and manage the major and principal gift donor pipeline so it is adequately populated with quality donor prospects.
Build and manage a portfolio of 75 - 100 individual/corporate/foundation donors with the capacity to give over $100,000.
Responsible for approximately 225-300 qualified moves annually.
Meet or exceed annual fundraising goal of $500,000 and continue to grow from there.
Meet or exceed fundraising goals for TNC in TN and additional TNC priority projects/programs.
Understand project budgets; may build proposal budgets utilizing this knowledge.
Develop personalized written proposals and submit grant proposals as needed.

Have you ever asked yourself, “How can I make a difference?”, but you don’t know where to go or have the time to do it? Welcome to The Nature Conservancy.

You have found the solution and now you can pointedly make a difference every day! By joining our Tennessee team, you will become part of a group that is a force for nature and people. Our team consists of a dedicated group who are leading the conservation effort on multiple fronts and who expertly bring strategy and action together. We’re looking for an individual with fundraising or business development experience who wants to make a difference. The Conservancy is a global conservation leader and one of the top fundraising charities in the United States.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree and 5 years related experience or an equivalent combination.
Experience building and maintaining long-term relationships with fundraising constituents.
Experience in asking for and closing gifts of $25,000 or more.
Experience in managing and tracking multiple prospects and donors.
Experience working with cross-functional teams.
Experience, coursework, or other training in fundraising principles and practices.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program
. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

The Associate Director of Development (ADoD) works closely with the development team to implement and coordinate effective multi-year strategies and plans for gift prospects, including individual, corporate, and/or foundation donors.

Meet or exceed annual fundraising goal of $500,000 and continue to grow from there.

Company Description

The Chief Executive Officer/President serves as the organization's senior leader and is ultimately responsible for the overall management, strategic direction, financial health, and operational success of Sheffield Place. The CEO works closely with the Board of Directors, staff, donors, volunteers, and community partners to advance the organization's mission and ensure high-quality services for clients.

Leadership & Strategy

Provide vision, leadership, and strategic direction for the organization.
Articulate and champion Sheffield Place's mission, values, and goals.
Foster a positive, mission-driven organizational culture.
Engage stakeholders in decision-making while ensuring effective leadership and accountability.

Operations & Program Oversight

Direct organizational operations and major projects.
Supervise daily activities and ensure effective service delivery.
Ensure staff have the training, technology, supplies, and support needed to perform their roles.
Stay informed of trends and innovations in the nonprofit and human services sectors.

Financial Management

Oversee budgeting, cash-flow management, and financial planning.
Maintain financial accountability, transparency, and strong internal controls.
Assist with audits, compliance requirements, and understanding of IRS Form 990 reporting.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and risk-management practices.

Lead fundraising strategy and execution.
Cultivate relationships with donors, funders, volunteers, and community partners.

Board Relations & Governance

Provide timely communication regarding organizational goals, opportunities, and challenges.
Support board operations, planning, committee work, and policy compliance.

Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, teamwork, and excellence.

Demonstrated nonprofit fundraising experience.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Public speaking and community engagement experience.
Experience managing budgets and organizational finances.

Company Description:

Farmers Insurance District 04, a President's Council district
, supports more than 30 established agencies across the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area and ranks in the top 1% of districts nationwide. The district focuses on helping agency owners grow their businesses while recruiting and mentoring new entrepreneurs who want to build their own agencies. Its leaders are recognized for best-in-class customer service, strong business performance, and commitment to Farmers Insurance’s values and long-term goals. With almost 100 years of experience and 19 million customers, Farmers Insurance is a trusted provider of Auto, Home, Business, and Life Insurance. District 04 offers tools, training, and ongoing support to help agents deliver exceptional service and protection to their clients.

Role Description

The CEO / Build Your Business role is a full-time on-site position based in Fort Worth, TX, focused on launching and growing a Farmers Insurance agency. This opportunity is not for everyone. It is a challenging opportunity for proven sales leaders, executives, and entrepreneurs who have had or are having a successful career and are looking to build something for themselves.

Day-to-day responsibilities include developing and executing sales strategies, building and leading a team, nurturing client relationships, and expanding the agency’s presence in the local market. The role also involves creating and implementing marketing and community engagement initiatives to drive new business and retain existing customers. The individual will collaborate closely with District 04 leadership to leverage available tools, training, and mentorship to build a sustainable, high-performing agency.

Qualifications

Demonstrated ability in Finance and Business Planning to manage budgets, revenue targets, and long-term growth strategies.
Have an
Enterprise Mindset:
you invest in marketing; you purchase quality consumer leads; you recruit exceptional producers; you leverage technology and data to your advantage as well as develop strong, symbiotic relationships with other leaders in their communities such as: Mortgage professionals; Realtors; Banking professionals; Financial advisors; Commercial lenders; CPAs; Attorneys; Chamber of Commerce organizations; Local business owners; Other Centers of Influence in the community.
Proven track record in Sales,
including developing pipelines, closing deals, and maintaining strong client relationships. This is a leadership role, but it all begins with sales.

Strong leadership, people management, and coaching skills to recruit, develop, and retain team members. A Servant Leader who cares about their customers and every member of their team.
Entrepreneurial mindset with a high level of initiative, accountability, and comfort with business ownership responsibilities.
The Capital and belief system to understand that to invest in competitive compensation for the best salespeople is critical to success as well as the business acumen to grasp that quality data/ lead generation is the Oxygen of the Agency.
Knowledge of or interest in the insurance industry; prior experience in insurance, financial services, or related fields is beneficial, but not required. The most successful agency owners don't think like insurance agents—they think like CEOs
. They recruit top talent, build systems, invest in growth, develop leaders, and create organizations that can thrive without relying solely on their own production.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Management, or a related discipline preferred, or equivalent professional experience.

Successful agency owners often come from:

Executive Leadership
Medical Device Sales
Technology & SaaS
Financial Services
Commercial Banking
Commercial Real Estate
Business Ownership
Automotive Sales Leadership
Recruiting & Staffing
B2B Sales

Is This Right for You?

This opportunity is ideal for someone who wants to build something meaningful. You will own your book of business here and could sell it at a multiple when you retire. This isn't for someone looking for a guaranteed paycheck or a traditional 9-to-5 role.
Let's Have a Conversation
We are not looking to convince someone to become an agency owner.
We are looking to meet experienced professionals who are exploring what's next and want to understand whether Agency ownership could be the right move.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
A LITTLE BIT ABOUT Boldr

Boldr is the first global B-Corp dedicated to delivering world-class Client experiences while creating access to dignified, meaningful work in communities around the world
We are a global team, united by our desire to connect diverse people with common values for boldr impact. 
We employ just over a thousand team members across five countries and we want to employ over 5,000 people by 2027, if not sooner

LET'S START WITH OUR VALUES

Meaningful connections start with AUTHENTICITY
We do our best work by being CURIOUS
We grow by remaining DYNAMIC
Our success combines AMBITIOUS VISION with OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE 
At the heart of great partnerships we'll always find EMPATHY

WHAT IS YOUR ROLE

The Chief Operating Officer is the operational, commercial, and systems spine of Boldr. You translate the CEO's vision into day-to-day delivery across five geographies, the critical support functions, and a workforce of 1,000+.
You work in close partnership with the CEO, CFO and CRO, turning commercial ambition into operating reality, and ensuring the systems, technology, and financial discipline are in place to deliver it. You hold direct ownership of Boldr's operating infrastructure and a defined share of its financial performance.
This is not a coordination role. It is an ownership role. You hold the operating P&L. You own the systems that run the business. You set the operating tempo and ensure every function is pulling in the same direction, at pace, without drifting from mission.

WHY DO WE WANT YOU

We are scaling a mission-driven business in a demanding industry and we need a leader who has done this before. Someone who has built operational infrastructure that doesn't break under growth, who understands the commercial levers without losing sight of purpose, and who can lead senior leaders across cultures, time zones, and geographies.
You bring more than operational expertise. You bring the kind of judgement and breadth that makes organisations more resilient, more legible, and more capable of delivering on ambitious commitments.

WHAT WILL YOU DO

Decision-making and operating cadence

Own how decisions get made at Boldr: who sets the bar, who owns the call, who carries it out. Keep decision rights clear so the business moves without stalling or reopening settled calls
Build the operating cadence that keeps every function aligned: the reviews, the metrics, and the rhythm that turn strategy into delivery
Make sure big commercial and operational decisions get real cross-functional scrutiny before they are committed, so no single function carries a decision alone

Commercial partnership and revenue growth (with the CRO)

Partner directly with the CRO to ensure revenue targets are funded by operational and financial reality, not aspiration
Hold a clear understanding of key client relationships and the health of the revenue pipeline
Ensure commercial commitments are operationally and technically deliverable before they are made, closing the gap between what is sold and what is built
Identify and act on growth opportunities that align with Boldr's mission, margin, and systems capacity

Systems, technology, and data

Own Boldr's operating technology stack; the platforms, tools, and integrations that run People, Finance, and Delivery across five geographies
Set the systems roadmap: prioritise, sequence, and resource implementations (HRIS, workforce, and operations platforms) so they land and get adopted, not just bought
Build the data infrastructure that gives the CEO and leadership a single, trusted view of performance: operational, commercial, and financial
Drive automation and responsible AI adoption across the operation to lift productivity, quality, and margin
Make systems readiness a precondition for scale: security, integration, and resilience built in, not bolted on

Financial ownership and stewardship

Hold direct ownership of the operating P&L and budget. Make the resource and cost decisions inside operations that balance growth with responsible stewardship
Own cost discipline and operating forecasts across the operating functions. Partner with the CFO on company-level planning, capital allocation, and reporting
Give the CEO clear, candid financial visibility on operating performance, risks, and outlook
Treat financial discipline as a standard, not a constraint, and make the operating numbers legible through better systems and data

Client delivery excellence

Through VP CX, own Boldr's delivery standard. Define what "great" looks like at scale and hold the organisation accountable to it
Ensure client NPS, retention, and service metrics are managed proactively, not reactively; instrumented through reliable systems and data
Act as the executive escalation point for high-stakes client issues, and ensure the system learns from every escalation
Drive the continuous improvement of Boldr's CX practice as a competitive differentiator

Operational scaling across geographies

Build and maintain the operating infrastructure that supports growth without breaking culture or quality
Own cross-geo execution: process discipline, systems readiness, and accountability frameworks across PH, ZA, MX, CA, and US
Identify and resolve structural constraints before they become crises
Ensure every geography feels resourced, connected, and clear on how it contributes to the whole

Leadership, culture, and talent

Lead a high-performing senior team. Set the standard for how Boldr's leaders lead
Model Boldr's values in how you operate: with accountability, candour, curiosity, and care
Make the culture feel real in operations, not aspirational in documents
Lead change well. Boldr is scaling fast, so this role owns transformation and change management: bringing people with you, not just rolling out new systems and structures

Governance and reporting

Keep the CEO informed, not surprised; clear, timely reporting on performance, risks, and material decisions, backed by reliable data
Represent operations at executive level when required; present with clarity and confidence
Ensure regulatory and governance compliance across all operating geographies
Maintain the integrity of Boldr's B-Corp certification in how operations are structured and run

WHAT WE'LL LIKE ABOUT YOU

 You are

A builder who has scaled complex, multi-geo operations and a systems thinker who knows which technology investments hold and which break
Commercially sharp, you understand revenue and financial mechanics, not just operational delivery
A leader people trust: clear, direct, fair, and present
Mission-aligned, you see Boldr's B-Corp identity not as a constraint to manage, but a reason you are here
Broad enough to hold the whole business: commercial, finance, systems, delivery, people, governance
High EQ. You lead through influence and get results through other people, not through title or pressure

You have

12+ years of senior executive leadership, including direct accountability for financial performance and operating systems
Proven experience leading multi-geo operations across different cultures and jurisdictions, ideally including emerging markets
Direct P&L or budget ownership at meaningful scale in a services, tech-enabled services, or high-growth environment
A track record of selecting, implementing, and scaling core operating systems (HRIS, ERP, workforce, or operations platforms) and getting them adopted
Strong financial acumen, you can read a balance sheet, challenge assumptions, and translate numbers into decisions
Fluency with data, automation, and AI as levers for productivity and margin
Experience working in close partnership with a CEO, CFO and commercial leadership (CRO or equivalent)
Experience operating within a mission-driven, B-Corp, or ESG-aligned organisation (preferred)
A reputation for delivery: results are not a side effect of your strategy, they are the point

jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz

Department: Office of Advancement

Job Title:

Director of Development

Position #: 00725102 – Requisition #:
40689

Job Summary:

The Director of Development is a strategic leader responsible for cultivating and strengthening philanthropic relationships to advance the organization's mission. This position will focus on the College of Nursing. This person will be a thought partner for the Dean of the College for all fundraising. This person will work with faculty, staff, alumni, board members, community leaders, and third-party organizations to create experiences that will cultivate annual, major, and principal gifts.

Supervision:

Received: Reports to 00669735 - Executive Strategist of Institutional Engagement
Exercised: No direct reports

Key Responsibilities:

Philanthropic Strategy: 30%

In partnership with the Executive Strategist for Institutional Engagement:
Develop and implement strategic plans for engaging the community and stakeholders in philanthropic support of the College of Nursing, including strategy on individual donor cultivation, expanding the College’s donor base, foundation relations, and corporate partnerships.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Dean of the College of Nursing in developing a robust community of potential supporters.
Serve as a partner to faculty to increase philanthropic support to the programs and centers of the College.
Develop a multi-year fundraising operating plan to establish fundraising goals built on portfolio projections, historical fundraising, and prospective donor analysis.
Develop and maintain a deep understanding of institutional priorities, academic programs, and centers of excellence in order to translate these assets into compelling funding.

Fundraising: 50%

Major and Principal Gift Fundraising: 30%

Lead all major and principal gifts, working closely with organizational leadership to ensure a positive philanthropic experience for current and potential benefactors. Cultivate and maintain relationships with key philanthropic partners, ensuring their alignment with the organization’s vision.
Direct the development of event concepts, messaging, and marketing strategies to maximize attendance and donor engagement.
Engage high-profile individuals and community leaders to serve as event hosts, chairs, and ambassadors, leveraging their networks for fundraising success.
Analyze event outcomes and campaign performance, using insights to inform future strategies and initiatives.
Facilitate productive relationships between benefactors and ColoradoSPH administrators, faculty and staff to ensure effectiveness of outreach and alignment with the College’s needs and priorities.

Annual Giving Fundraising: 20%

Maximize annual giving donations to the College and support effective pathways of the future of major and principal gifts to the College.
Direct the development of annual giving campaigns, including messaging, and marketing strategies to maximize attendance and donor engagement.
Analyze the effectiveness of annual giving efforts.

Development Operations: 20%

Expand upon and maintain expertise on philanthropic opportunities at the College of Nursing.
Serve as a solutions oriented main point of contact between the College of Nursing and the Office of Advancement, providing a high level of customer service to the College on development related inquiries.
Manage process and issues around accurate reporting, gift stewardship, faculty support on development efforts.
Manage projects from conception to completion, including continuous evaluation and improvement of strategies.
Monitor and analyze fundraising data to identify areas of improvement and to support strategy development.
Work closely with and support generalist gift officers on opportunities within the College.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

Philanthropy brings people together; it’s a driving force in accelerating the pace of discovery, attracting and retaining excellent students and faculty, and delivering world-class prevention and care.

At the Office of Advancement at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, we put our passions to work.

We have the privilege to collaborate with people who want to make a difference in the world – people who want to make an impact on humanity that may be felt long after they have passed. Our office exists to ensure stakeholders within and outside the university know, value, and support the important work being done on this academic medical campus.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options
Additional Insurance: Disability, Life, Vision
Retirement 401(a) Plan: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay
Paid Time Off: Accruals over the year
Vacation Days: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)
Sick Days: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)
Holiday Days: 15/year
Tuition Benefit: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses
ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university
Minimum of 3 years of professional fundraising experience or experience in related fields like nonprofit administration, public affairs, or business development, including managing funding relationships with individuals, corporations or foundations.
A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year for year basis.

Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

4 years of leadership experience in community engagement, development, or a related field, with a proven track record in board development, strategic partnerships, and major and principal fundraising success.
Minimum of 5 years of successful professional fundraising experience, or experience in related fields like nonprofit administration, public affairs, or business development.
Master’s degree in business administration, public relations, management, communications, or similar fields.

Conditions of Employment:

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.
National travel may be required for partnership development, fundraising events, and conferences.
This position requires flexibility in hours, including evenings and weekends for events and meetings.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.
Outstanding customer service skills.
Demonstrated experience in fostering a community that values a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
Project Management: Personal computer proficiency required, especially as related to Microsoft Office Products; MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; and donor tracking software.
Exceptional leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and mobilize diverse groups towards common goals.
Strategic thinker with strong analytical skills and the ability to envision and implement high-impact engagement strategies.
Excellent negotiation and presentation skills, with experience in high-level partnership development.
Knowledge of the latest trends in community engagement, fundraising, and non-profit management.
Strong development skills including comfort with cold calling, leading effective one-on-one visits, and utilizing multiple modes of communication to achieve results.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to be both proactive and responsive in a metrics driven environment.
Ability to handle sensitive information discreetly and maintain confidentiality.
Solid ability to organize and manage multiple projects/tasks simultaneously; must have ability to work independently and collaboratively and adapt to changing priorities.
Flexibility and adaptability to evolve in an emerging and changing environment.
Proven ability to foster and build relationships internally and externally.

How to Apply:

For full consideration, please submit the following document(s):

A letter of interest describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position (only use if a cover letter is necessary)
Curriculum vitae / Resume
Three to five professional references, including name, address, phone number (mobile number if appropriate), and email address

Questions should be directed to: Shannon Palombi – Shannon.Palombi@cuanschutz.edu

Screening of Applications Begins:

Applications will be accepted until finalists are identified, but preference will be given to complete applications received by August 14, 2026.

The starting salary range ( or hiring range ) for this position has been established as $103,497 - $108,000

The above salary range ( or hiring range ) represents the University’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. This position may be eligible for overtime compensation, depending on the level.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Colorado provides generous leave, health plans and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

jobs.title: Corporate Development Director
jobs.description:
The next part of your journey is right around the corner — with The Standard.

A genuine desire to make a difference in the lives of others is the foundation for everything we do. With a customer-first mindset and an intentional focus on building strong teams, we’ve been able to uphold our legacy of financial stability while investing in new, innovative technologies that support the needs of our customers. Our high-performance culture focused on operational excellence thrives thanks to remarkable people united by compassion and a customer-first commitment. Are you ready to make a difference?

Job Summary

The Corporate Development Director supports the execution of The Standard’s growth initiatives, including mergers, acquisitions, partnerships, and strategic investments, as directed by the CEO and corporate development leadership. This role evaluates potential opportunities, supports transaction execution, and helps advance corporate development projects that align with the company’s long-term strategic objectives.

The position is actively involved across the transaction lifecycle, including strategic assessment, valuation, due diligence, and transaction execution. The Corporate Development Director works closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including senior leaders and officers across finance, actuarial, legal, HR, IT, and operations, and partners with external advisors to support thorough evaluation and efficient execution of transactions.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Planning and Deal Evaluation:

Support the execution of corporate development initiatives by evaluating potential acquisitions, partnerships, and investment opportunities. Research market trends, industry developments, and competitive dynamics, and perform financial and strategic analyses to assess strategic fit, risks, and value creation potential.

Due Diligence and Transaction Execution:

Coordinate and manage assigned diligence workstreams across cross-functional partners, track progress, and surface key risks, issues, and decision points. Work closely with external advisors and internal stakeholders to keep diligence activities on track, elevate issues, and provide recommendations to corporate development leadership in support of transaction structuring, negotiation, signing, and closing.

Analysis, Communication, and Strategic Storytelling:

Prepare analyses, presentations, and communication materials to support internal discussions and inform decision-making related to corporate development initiatives. Contribute to the development of the strategic rationale for transactions, including supporting preparation of board-level materials.

Process Improvement and Operational Effectiveness:

Maintain and enhance corporate development tools, templates, and processes to support consistent and efficient deal execution. Establish effective ways of working with external advisors and internal stakeholders to improve coordination, communication, and overall transaction effectiveness.

Skills And Background You’ll Need

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Actuarial Science, Economics, or a related field.
5+ years of experience in investment banking, investor relations, private equity, corporate development, corporate finance, actuarial, consulting, or a related field.
Strong financial acumen, including the ability to understand and analyze financial statements, valuation analyses, and key deal economics in the context of mergers, acquisitions, and strategic initiatives.
Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize financial, legal, operational, and market information to evaluate strategic alternatives, identify risks, and develop recommendations for senior leadership.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders at all levels.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and drive projects to completion.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, demanding, and often ambiguous environment.

Key Behaviors of a Successful Candidate

Driving Success:

Demonstrates energy and persistence when tackling complex challenges and views difficult problems as opportunities to create value.

Adaptability:

Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs, remains effective in ambiguous situations, and takes ownership for delivering results.

Winning Together:

Builds trust and strong working relationships across teams, values diverse perspectives, and fosters collaboration to achieve shared objectives.

Strategic Visioning:

Considers future scenarios, opportunities, and risks to develop thoughtful recommendations that align with the company's long-term strategic objectives.

Why Join The Standard?

We have built an enduring legacy of stability, financial strength and exceptional customer service through the contributions of the service-oriented people who choose to work at The Standard. To ensure we can attract and retain the best talent, when you join The Standard you can expect:

A rich benefits package including medical, dental, vision and a 401(k) plan with matching company contributions
An annual incentive bonus plan
Generous paid time off including 11 holidays, 2 wellness days, and 8 volunteer hours annually — PTO increases with tenure
A supportive, responsive management approach and opportunities for career growth and advancement
Paid parental leave and adoption/surrogacy assistance
An employee giving program that double matches your donations to eligible nonprofits and schools

In addition to the competitive salary range below, our employee-focused benefits support work-life balance. Learn more about working at The Standard.

Eligibility to participate in an incentive program is subject to the rules governing the program and plan. Any award depends on a variety of factors including individual and organizational performance.

The actual compensation for this role will be based on a combination of education and experience, knowledge and skills, position budget, internal equity, and market data.

Salary Range:

$137,000.00 - $200,750.00

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability or veteran status or any other condition protected by federal, state or local law. Description

Who We Are:

Neighborhood Health Center is a non-profit organization local to Portland, OR serving underserved patients in the areas of primary care, internal medicine, dental services and more. Our patient-centered approach to care honors the unique needs and circumstances of each individual patient. NHC sees people, not problems, and recognizes that the time spent as a patient in a doctors office is only one factor in a persons overall health. Our leading edge, integrated clinical teams work in partnership with patients, their families, and the communities we serve to provide whole-person care, prevention, and ongoing support.

NHC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate differences in the workplace and do not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, gender (sex), national origin, age, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law.

Why work with us?

We are a non-profit organization, passionate about providing the underserved population with medical and dental services across the greater Portland area, committed to making a difference daily.
We offer our employees a competitive compensation and benefits package which includes 20 days of PTO (based on full time employment), 9 paid holidays, health/dental/vision insurance, quarterly wellness reimbursements, generous 401k retirement plan with employer match, employer paid disability insurance, EAP and life insurance.
Our employees voted NHC a Top Workplace in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025!

Director of Communications

Administrative

Reports To:
Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
