jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Lead the operational heartbeat of a global mission-driven organization, where strategy meets impact, teams thrive, and growth has purpose

Position Overview

As the Chief Operating Officer at Sigma Nursing, you will lead the organization’s operations, translating strategic priorities into scalable systems, operational excellence, financial stewardship, and sustainable growth across multiple departments. Working closely with the Chief Executive Officer, Executive Leadership Team, Board of Directors, and departmental leaders, you will align operations, technology, finance, human resources, and strategic initiatives to advance organizational priorities and strengthen enterprise performance.

You will lead organization-wide operational planning, designing frameworks that strengthen efficiency, accountability, and alignment across every department. That includes establishing, monitoring, and evaluating KPIs across Marketplace, Membership, Information Technology, Events, Finance, Publications, and other operational areas, and using what you learn to guide long-range planning for organizational growth, staffing, infrastructure, and resource capacity.

You will also help drive revenue growth and operational performance, partnering with executive and departmental leaders to develop strategies across e-commerce, publishing, events, and other business lines. That means evaluating new business opportunities, pricing strategies, and cost-saving initiatives, and ensuring organizational offerings stay aligned with member needs, market conditions, and long-term strategic objectives.

You will provide strategic leadership, coaching, and performance oversight for the leaders of Marketplace, Information Technology, People & Culture, Finance, Strategic Initiatives, and other operational functions, building a high-performing leadership culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement, with clear performance expectations, ongoing coaching, and a real investment in succession planning.

Financial stewardship and risk management sit close to the center of this role. You will partner with the Controller and executive leadership to oversee operational budgets, revenue forecasting, and resource allocation; ensure compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, and governance standards; and develop the contingency planning and risk mitigation strategies that protect the organization’s assets and long-term sustainability.

You will provide executive oversight of Information Technology, partnering with IT leadership to strengthen digital infrastructure, enterprise systems, cybersecurity, and technology-enabled operations, while championing a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and data-informed decision-making across the organization.

Success in this role looks like an organization that operates efficiently, leaders with clear visibility into performance, strengthened cross-functional collaboration, optimized resources, effectively managed risk, and strategic initiatives executed in step with our mission. Through operational leadership and organizational stewardship, you will help Sigma expand its global impact, strengthen the value it delivers to members, and advance our mission through sustainable, mission-driven operations.

Location, Travel & Compensation

This is a hybrid and remote-friendly role, open to U.S.-based professionals nationwide.

Domestic and international travel to organizational events and in-person gatherings is expected approximately 5 – 6 times per year.

The salary range for this position is $145,000 - $175,000; offers are made within this range to ensure equity, consistency, and fiscal responsibility.

A Week in the Life

Monday often starts with a look across the organization’s KPI dashboards, covering Marketplace, Membership, IT, Events, Finance, and Publications, checking for anything that needs attention before the week gets moving, and setting priorities with your team accordingly.

Throughout the week, you are in regular conversation with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, translating strategic priorities into coordinated operational execution and making sure resources, workflows, and priorities stay aligned as business needs shift.

You spend meaningful time with the leaders who report to you, including the heads of Marketplace, IT, People & Culture, Finance, and Strategic Initiatives, coaching them, working through performance questions, and thinking together about succession and capability building. One week that might mean a deep dive with IT on a cybersecurity investment; another week it might mean sitting with the Marketplace lead to evaluate a new pricing strategy or with the events team on conference pricing.

You partner closely with the Controller on budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation, and you’re regularly reviewing operational controls, compliance, and governance practices, refining a business continuity plan, or thinking through the operational implications of a new regulation, always working to safeguard the organization’s assets and long-term sustainability.

Technology and innovation show up often, too. You partner with IT leadership on enterprise systems, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and process modernization, and you’re a steady advocate for automation and data-informed decision-making across departments that might not think of themselves as technical. Periodically, you also prepare materials or updates for the Board of Directors, translating operational performance and strategic initiatives into a story that helps board members understand where the organization stands and what’s ahead.

No two weeks look exactly the same, but the throughline is constant: turning strategy into systems, and systems into results, while building a leadership culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

You Would Thrive in This Position If

You bring 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in operations, including at least 5 years in a senior or executive role, and you’ve used that experience to manage complex projects and cross-functional teams inside a mission-driven organization.
You’ve overseen enterprise operations across multiple functional areas, including IT, HR, Finance, Strategic Initiatives, or e-commerce, and you know how to translate strategic plans into operational systems, KPIs, and measurable outcomes.
You partner naturally with Finance leadership. You’re comfortable in budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation conversations, and you bring the financial acumen to make sound, sustainable operational decisions.
You’ve supervised senior leaders and built high-performing, accountable teams by coaching people, setting clear expectations, and investing in succession planning along the way.
You’ve led organizational change, operational improvements, or systems modernization initiatives, and you’re comfortable overseeing digital platforms, enterprise systems, or technology-enabled operations.
You understand data governance, cybersecurity, or digital risk mitigation practices, and you’ve developed or overseen compliance, risk management, or contingency planning frameworks.
You hold sound business judgment and systems thinking, able to zoom out to strategy and zoom in to execution in the same week. An MBA or equivalent advanced degree, a Certified Association Executive (CAE) designation, or experience in a nonprofit and/or individual membership-based organization is a valued plus, though not a requirement.

Who We Are

Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing (also known as Sigma Nursing or Sigma) is a global nursing organization with more than 100 years of impact, but what really sets us apart is how we support people—both the nurses we serve and the team members who make our work possible. We’re a community-oriented group of approximately 40 employees based in Indianapolis, Indiana, working in a remote-friendly environment. At Sigma, you’ll find a culture that values accountability, growth, and purpose. We offer strong health and retirement benefits, support professional development, and encourage open communication and collaboration across teams. If you’re looking for a place where your work matters and your growth is supported, you’ll feel right at home here.

We recognize that diversity and inclusion are essential to our success and are committed to creating a workplace that reflects the global nursing community we serve. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Ready to Join Us?

Apply today and help drive Sigma’s mission forward—building a stronger, more connected global nursing community.

jobs.description:
**Overview**

The Director of Advocacy and Outreach facilitates the strategic direction and continued growth of CRPA's statewide grassroots programs. This role executes program priorities and standards, builds the organizational structures that allow chapters, volunteers, and business affiliates programs to grow, and directs the staff and resources needed to execute on them. The A \& O Director serves as CRPA's senior oversight staff with chapter leadership, members, and business affiliates, and is accountable to organizational leadership for the program's growth, performance, and impact.

This position reports directly to the Operations Director and partners closely with the Legislative, Training, and Development Directors on initiatives where grassroots organizing, coalition building, and fundraising intersect. This position is expected to keep measurable outcomes for program activities and report to the Board of Directors and board committees on a regular basis. This position oversees other department personnel.

**Duties**

* Develop and execute comprehensive advocacy strategies aligned with organizational goals.
* Execute the strategic direction for chapter growth statewide, establishing the onboarding standards, leadership structures, and communication cadence that allow the chapter network to expand and mature.
* Program\-level reporting on chapter health: membership trends, meeting participation, and grassroots calls to action, translating field data into direction for the department and updates for organizational leadership.
* Conduct policy research and analysis to inform advocacy campaigns and program goals as directed by operations personnel and the board of directors.
* Build and nurture coalitions by collaborating with community groups, industry leaders, and other stakeholders.
* Oversee the operating model for the Business Affiliates program, driving Affiliate participation and CRPA Membership recruitment. Work with affiliates to bolster membership in the organization.
* Execute local engagement strategy: prioritizing which local issues warrant member mobilization, set the framework for talking points and alerts, and oversee volunteer coordination on letter\-writing and meeting attendance.
* Draft regular articles from the Advocation and Outreach Department perspective for publication in company
* Coordinate cross\-functional collaboration across departments such as communications, legal, marketing, and fundraising to ensure unified messaging.
* Develop and evolve the volunteer incentive program to strengthen long\-term engagement and retention.
* Build organizational capacity for chapter and volunteer presence at gun shows and other public\-facing events, delegating execution to field staff. And when necessary work weekend events and get materials to volunteers and help set up for events.
* Manage and develop department staff, including schedules, field routes, workload distribution, and professional growth.
* Represent CRPA at speaking engagements on the Second Amendment and CRPA's mission, including in\-state travel as required. (Candidate must have reliable vehicle, be able to travel when needed, and be able to fly is necessary)
* Ensure warehouse and field material needs are ordered and resourced, directing staff responsible for inventory and logistics.
* Monitor the broader political and advocacy landscape, benchmark against peer organizations, and drive continuous improvement and innovation in program reach and effectiveness.

● Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications and Required Skills**

● Strong commitment to the Second Amendment and constitutional rights, with the ability to speak knowledgeably and represent CRPA on 2A issues, candidates, hunting, shooting sports, and organizational mission.

● Demonstrated leadership and staff management experience, with a track record of building or scaling a program rather than solely executing day\-to\-day tasks.

● Excellent public speaking and writing skills.

● Strong strategic and organizational skills, with the ability to synthesize data from multiple sources into direction and recommendations for other departments and leadership.

● Demonstrated ability to produce clear, actionable reports communicating departmental performance, growth, and outcomes.

● Superior project and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and oversee multiple direct reports across a statewide program.

\*Strong computer, analytical, and public speaking skills are a must.

\*We are looking for a "can do" person with energy and a desire to further our mission in California. This is not the job for a 8\-5 mindset. We want a go\-getter who believes in the mission.

\*Travel in and out of state when needed is a must and there will be non\-standard hours. This is a salary position for a state\-wide nonprofit so it is expected that this position will help to cover this territory.

Pay: $65,000\.00 \- $85,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Family leave
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid parental leave
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.description:
***The World Science Festival seeks a creative and visionary Chief Development Officer to build a bold new chapter in its fundraising strategy***

  


### **About the World Science Festival**

The World Science Festival (WSF) is a multimedia organization producing original content straddling science, the arts, journalism and education. Founded in 2008, WSF is viewed by many as the premier platform bringing the most transformative ideas at the forefront of discovery to mainstream audiences. With formats spanning innovative works of theatre, film, dance, and music, immersive live and virtual experiences, as well as riveting discussions and debates, WSF is lauded globally for its groundbreaking live and digital content featuring world\-renowned scientists, artists, and intellectuals, shifting science to the cultural center. Based in New York City, WSF is distinctive in its commitment to the highest of editorial standards and production excellence, providing worldwide audiences an exciting and impactful view of the near and far future.



You can find more information about the organization at https://www.worldsciencefestival.com/


### **Position Overview**



The Chief Development Officer (CDO) will lead the design and execution of a comprehensive fundraising strategy for WSF, diversifying and expanding its funding base while stewarding a loyal core of long\-standing supporters. Reporting to the Co\-Founder and CEO, with a dotted line to the President, this person will help grow the organization's philanthropic revenue to support its mission and goals. This role offers a creative, transformational fundraising leader the chance to elevate WSF's fundraising program, deepen its impact, and expand its reach.



The CDO will develop infrastructure, processes, and manage a team while working in close partnership with organizational leadership and an engaged, accomplished board. The ideal candidate will be comfortable in high\-level, creative strategy conversations and in the hands\-on work of identifying, cultivating, and closing new philanthropic relationships. This person will represent WSF externally with confidence to funders, partners, and the broader philanthropic community.


### **Core Responsibilities**


#### ***Strategy***

* Design and lead a multi\-year comprehensive fundraising strategy that diversifies WSF's funding base while setting the stage for year\-over\-year philanthropic growth
* Collaborate with senior leadership to shape organizational priorities into high\-impact funding strategies
* Identify and prioritize funding opportunities across WSF's core program areas, including all live and digital content and educational initiatives
* Set clear revenue goals, performance benchmarks, and accountability structures across the department

#### ***Fundraising \& Relationship Management***


* Directly cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of major funders that include individuals, foundations, and corporations.
* Identify and pursue new funders with a specific focus on bringing in new individual, foundation, and corporate donors while also exploring innovative funding streams outside of traditional philanthropy
* Support the Founders and Board with donor cultivation, solicitation strategy, and stewardship, helping them to prepare, position, and follow through on solicitations

#### ***Team Leadership \& Management***


* Lead, inspire, and mentor a talented team of fundraising professionals while fostering a high\-performance, accountable team environment
* Assess and build out the development team's organizational structure, including hiring for current vacancies, defining role scope, and identifying gaps in capacity
* Set clear performance expectations, establish and maintain strong KPI practices, provide consistent feedback, and build professional development pathways that attract and retain top talent

 #### ***Cross\-Functional Collaboration***

* Serve as a visible and trusted leader across the organization, helping to build a culture of philanthropy where staff at all levels understand and support fundraising goals
* Align fundraising priorities with programmatic and creative teams

### **Qualifications**


* 10\+ years of progressive experience in nonprofit fundraising, with a minimum of 5 years of senior leadership experience overseeing a development program
* Track record of fundraising success and measurable revenue growth in organizations of similar size and scope, including direct solicitation and closing of individual major gifts and corporate partnerships at the 6\-figure level and above
* Proven success leading, coaching, and mentoring teams, including building culture and managing performance
* Experience diversifying a funding base and cultivating new and non\-traditional philanthropic relationships
* Commitment to leading by example, including demonstrating and fostering a strong sense of urgency, accountability, and sound decision\-making to achieve goals
* Exceptional interpersonal skills and high emotional intelligence, with the ability to build genuine relationships with a sophisticated, generous, and busy board, as well as donors and colleagues at all levels
* A data\-informed mindset with comfort using KPIs and performance data to drive accountability and decision\-making
* Collaborative, flexible, team\-oriented, and positive approach to work
* Authentic and deep interest in the mission and work of the WSF
* Familiarity with the NYC philanthropic community and funders is a plus but not required

### **Location \& Work Environment**



This role is based in New York City with a full\-time in\-office schedule.


### **Compensation \& Benefits**



The salary range for this position is $190,000 \- $220,000 annually. WSF offers a comprehensive package of benefits.

With 50 locations and 100 programs in NYC’s most under\-served communities, our 1,000\+ results\-oriented professionals make a difference for more than 40,000 children and their families each year.
  
  

The Senior Program Director (SPD) is responsible for supervising multiple program directors and overseeing all facets of these multiple programs including finances; staff development; program advocacy and compliance; and the overall strategic planning. The SPD builds key relationships with all significant stakeholders (internal \& external) including funders; licensing agents; school and community leaders; participants and families; program directors and support staff; and other relevant individuals and entities critical to the successful running of programs, division, and/or agency.
  
  

**Essential Functions:**  

* Provide consistent supervision, coaching and feedback to site leadership and teams.
* Oversee and continually strategize all operations of the program(s) to ensure the enrollment, participation, and program goals are achieved.
* Ensure the cost\-effective delivery of high\-quality services to the families served by the program(s) and the smooth operation of the program(s).
* Prepares for audits and meets with auditors from various regulatory agencies. Develops and implements response and/or change of policies/procedures to meet regulatory requirements.
* Meet performance expectations/metrics, as defined for the position within the assigned program.
* Communicate program aspects throughout the agency and oversee community engagement and outreach efforts.
* Design, secure, and/or facilitate professional development experiences including core divisional trainings. Help ensure skills are transferred to program operations and systems via consistent coaching, feedback, supervisory, and accountability efforts.
* Other duties as assigned.


**Supervisory Responsibilities:**  

Manages several Program Directors responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of their respective Programs. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the agency policies and applicable laws. Deep understanding and knowledge of Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) where applicable. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, planning, assigning, directing work, rewarding, disciplining employees, performance reviews, and addressing complaints and resolving problems.
  
  

**Minimum Qualifications:**  

* Bachelors’s Degree in Education, Social Work, Public Administration or related field.
* Certification may be required.
* 5 years’ experience in a similar role, minimum of 2 years’ supervising staff.
* Demonstrated competence in youth development, supervision, training facilitation, and working knowledge of community program administration and planning.
* Bilingual in one or more of the following: Spanish, Mandarin, Cantonese, Bengali and others, may be required depending on client needs.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
* Ability to plan and carry out assignments independently.
* Ability to prioritize, adhere to timelines and multi\-task.


**Qualifications Preferred:**  

* Master's Degree in Education or Social Work with SIFI certification.

**Chief Program Officer**



Bonneville Environmental Foundation (BEF) is an entrepreneurial nonprofit working on environmental solutions at the intersection of renewable energy and freshwater. Partnerships are key to our success. We build long\-term relationships with our corporate, utility, non\-profit, and philanthropic partners by understanding their goals and needs and providing solutions that achieve those goals while delivering real, measurable environmental benefits.


**Who are we looking for?**



BEF is seeking an experienced, mission\-driven executive to serve as its first Chief Program Officer (CPO). Reporting to the CEO and serving alongside the CFO and Chief of Staff, the CPO will provide integrated leadership across BEF's full portfolio of water, carbon, and energy programs. This is a newly created role that reflects BEF's ambitions for expanded impact and the increasing complexity of its program work. The CPO will contribute to and hold center on program performance; drive and manage strategic growth in emerging program areas (for example water and energy stewardship for the data center sector); expand BEF's client base and revenue streams to reduce revenue concentration risk; and support meaningful program partnerships that support priorities of Tribal Nations. The ideal candidate brings deep experience managing (and directly supporting the success of) complex program portfolios in a mission\-driven organization; a rigorous approach to performance management; and a genuine commitment to equity, partnership, and impact.

Partnership: We believe we can accomplish more by working together.



Adaptability: We evolve, adapt, and apply what we learn to improve our approaches and outcomes.



Knowledge: We seek out and value diverse perspectives, embrace new ideas, and advance new approaches.



Innovation: We recognize that the scope and pace of the change we need demands innovation, drawing on knowledge from the past and new information and tools.

jobs.description:
**Executive Director**  

*Full\-Time, Remote Position*

 **Lead the nation's premier nonprofit supporting ranked choice voting implementation.**

  

The Ranked Choice Voting Resource Center is a national, nonpartisan 501(c)(3\) organization dedicated to making ranked choice voting elections successful. We provide research, education, technical tools, and practical support to election administrators, policymakers, advocates, media, and the public. We currently support our partners across the country with a remote, distributed team of seven full\-time staff members and a $1M annual budget.

  

The incoming Executive Director will lead the Center’s next phase of growth — expanding our team and revenue base while maintaining the credible, high\-caliber service that has earned the trust of partners nationwide. In the process, you'll help shape the delivery and public perception of election innovation in the United States.

 **Responsibilities**  

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the Center’s chief executive officer – leading our strategy, fundraising, and external affairs while maintaining operational excellence and managing our talented, dedicated staff. Responsibilities include:

  

*Strategy*


* strategic planning — setting priorities for our next growth phase and aligning programming and personnel with those goals
* monitoring developments in election administration and related policy fields that affect our work
* identifying opportunities to expand the Center’s reach and impact
  


*Fundraising*


* stewarding existing foundation relationships, ensuring renewal of the six\-figure grants that anchor our budget
* cultivating new grant support from institutional funders
* growing our individual donor base, with a focus on five\-figure and recurring major gifts to diversify our funding
* developing the Center’s emerging fee\-for\-service revenue stream
  


*External Relations*


* serving as the Center’s primary spokesperson at conferences, meetings, and other public events
* building and maintaining relationships with partners in election administration, civic engagement, philanthropy, academia, and the media
  


*Operations*

  

* recruiting, developing, and retaining a high\-performing, mission\-driven, all\-remote team
* overseeing day\-to\-day operations and financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, and contracts, with support from the Center’s operations staff
* ensuring compliance with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and ethical standards, in partnership with the Center’s general counsel
  


*Governance*


* serving as the primary liaison between the Board and staff
* planning and facilitating board meetings with reporting on program milestones and finances
* collaborating with the Board to strengthen governance, including Board recruitment and leadership development

  


**Qualifications**  

*Required*

  

* Bachelor's degree in public administration, public policy, nonprofit management, finance, or a related field – or comparable professional experience
* 5\-10 years of senior leadership experience managing teams and budgets (in any sector), including at least three years managing in a nonprofit organization
* demonstrated ability to set strategic priorities and translate them into actionable plans in a shifting landscape
* a track record of cultivating new foundation grants and renewing existing grants
* experience building an individual donor base, including five\-figure and recurring gifts
* strong financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, and reporting
* excellent communication skills for conveying the Center’s mission and impact to partners and donors
* strong project and program management skills
* experience leading teams in a largely remote work environment
* proven success developing and collaborating with a Board of Directors to achieve strategic goals
* demonstrated ability to maintain professional neutrality and nonpartisan credibility with a wide range of stakeholders
  


*Preferred*


* graduate degree in public administration, public policy, law, nonprofit management, finance, or related field – or equivalent professional experience
* experience working in election administration, election policy, democracy reform, or civic engagement
* experience leading an all\-remote, nationally distributed team
* expertise in nonprofit financial planning, impact evaluation, and organizational development
* a nonprofit management certification from an accredited university or the willingness to obtain one within one year of hire
  


**Compensation and Benefits**


* starting salary: $140,000 \- $175,000
* employer\-matched SIMPLE IRA
* paid parental leave
* unlimited PTO
* 11 organization\-wide holidays
* two organization\-wide vacation weeks – one in July and one in December
  


**How to Apply**



Please complete the application on the Center’s website at rcvresources.org/careers. Applications submitted by email or through third\-party job sites will not be reviewed.
  

  

Qualified applicants will be interviewed on a rolling basis. We aim to extend an offer in early October with a target start date for the new Executive Director in December.

  

RCVRC is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. To request an accommodation, please write Rosemary Blizzard at rosemary.blizzard@rcvresources.org.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Executive Director — Villa Terrace Museum \& Gardens**



Villa Terrace Museum \& Gardens seeks an experienced, mission\-driven Executive Director to lead the organization’s artistic, operational, and financial future. Housed in a landmark Mediterranean\-style villa overlooking Lake Michigan, Villa Terrace combines historic house museum stewardship, decorative arts collections and exhibitions, formal gardens, and public programming. The Executive Director serves as the organization’s chief executive, reporting to and working closely with the Board of Directors.


**Key Responsibilities**


* **Strategic leadership: Partner with the Board to set and execute the organization’s vision, strategic plan, and annual goals.**
	+ Translate strategic priorities into operating plans, staff assignments, and measurable outcomes.
* **Fundraising \& development: Lead all fundraising activities, including individual giving, major gifts, grants, sponsorships, and special events.**
	+ Cultivate and steward donor and funder relationships personally,
	+ Identify and pursue grant opportunities (state and federal historic preservation, arts council, foundation).
* **Financial management: Own the annual budget, monthly financial monitoring, and long\-range financial planning.**
	+ Work with the Treasurer/Finance Committee and outside accountant on budgeting, cash flow, and audit/990 preparation.
	+ Ensure sound internal controls and compliance with nonprofit financial reporting requirements.
* **Board relations \& governance: Serve as primary staff liaison to the Board and its committees.**
	+ Support board recruitment, orientation, and engagement; prepare board materials and reporting.
* **Collections, exhibitions \& programming: Oversee curatorial direction, exhibition planning, and educational/public programming.**
	+ Ensure appropriate collections care, historic preservation standards, and interpretive quality.
* **Operations \& facilities: Oversee day\-to\-day operations, visitor experience, retail/rental revenue, vendor management, and the historic building and gardens.**
* **Staff leadership:** Develop and enhance organization chart, hire, supervise, and develop staff and volunteers; set a positive, accountable organizational culture.
* **Community \& external relations:** Represent Villa Terrace to donors, members, civic and cultural partners, and the television, online, and print media.


**Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree arts/nonprofit administration, museum studies, history, or a related field preferred.
* Proven experience in facility administration, operation, and vendor relationship management.
* Minimum 5–7 years of senior nonprofit leadership experience, ideally in a museum, historic site, or arts/cultural organization.
* Demonstrated fundraising success, including major gift cultivation and grant management.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, financial statement literacy, and board financial reporting.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfort as a public\-facing spokesperson.
* Track record of effective board partnership and staff management.
* Experience with historic preservation, collections stewardship, or historic building museum operations is a plus.


**Compensation \& Benefits**



Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications, range: $100,000–$110,000\. The Board anticipates an additional performance\-based incentive tied to fund\-raising milestones, the organization’s operational success and/or the active capital improvement projects; structure to be finalized with the selected candidate. Benefits include health insurance, retirement plan participation, paid time off, and professional development support.


  
**To Apply**



Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and three professional references to Thomas Roepsch thomasroepsch@tfroepschcpa.com. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis; priority given to applications received within the first three weeks of posting.

This one doesn’t.

JnD Services is offering the right leader the opportunity to earn significant ownership in an established, growing company—without investing their own money.

We’ve already done the hard part:

* Built a respected local brand
* Earned hundreds of positive customer relationships
* Purchased professional trucks and equipment
* Established proven marketing channels
* Created consistent revenue
* Built a reputation for quality and integrity

Now it’s time to build something much bigger.

I’m looking for a true business partner.

About Me

I’m the founder of JnD Services.

My strengths are:

* Sales
* Marketing
* Building relationships
* Estimating projects
* Networking
* Growing the brand
* Creating opportunities

What I need is someone who loves running the business.

Someone who enjoys:

* Building systems
* Leading people
* Improving operations
* Financial management
* Hiring and developing great employees
* Holding teams accountable
* Scaling companies

Together, I believe we can build a company far larger than either of us could alone.

What You’ll Help Build

This isn’t simply an operations role.

You’ll help lead nearly every aspect of the company:

* Daily operations
* Hiring, training, and leadership
* Building scalable systems and processes
* Financial reporting and budgeting
* Pricing strategy and profitability
* Customer experience
* Business development
* Strategic planning
* Expansion into new markets and services

You’ll have real influence—not just responsibility.

Ownership Without Writing a Check

This is what makes this opportunity unique.

The right candidate will not be asked to invest capital into the business.

Instead, ownership is earned through performance and long\-term commitment.

You can earn up to 40% ownership through a four\-year vesting schedule based on mutually agreed\-upon business milestones.

Example Vesting Schedule

* 10% after Year 1
* 20% after Year 2
* 30% after Year 3
* 40% after Year 4

If either of us determines the partnership isn’t the right fit before equity is fully vested, any unvested ownership simply remains with the company.

The goal is simple:

Earn ownership by helping create value.

Who I’m Looking For

Ideally, you’ve already:

* Owned or operated a successful business
* Built teams and systems
* Managed financial performance
* Improved operational efficiency
* Held people accountable
* Helped grow revenue and profitability

Experience in construction, demolition, restoration, home services, or other service\-based businesses is a major advantage—but strong operators from other industries are encouraged to apply.

Why This Opportunity Is Different

This isn’t another management position.

It’s a chance to become a true partner in building a company with significant long\-term potential.

You won’t be starting from scratch.

You won’t need investors.

You won’t need to purchase equipment.

You won’t need to build a brand.

Instead, you’ll step into an established business with the opportunity to help shape its future—and earn meaningful ownership along the way.

If you’re the kind of entrepreneur who wants to build something lasting instead of simply collecting a paycheck, I’d love to meet you.

Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world. Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.

**The Opportunity**:


Advancement \& Partnerships’ Development team is hiring for multiple Associate Directors of Development to support fundraising efforts for the College of Sciences and the College of Engineering and Computer Science. These frontline fundraising roles are responsible for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and securing major gifts of $25,000 and above. The selected candidates will manage and grow a portfolio of prospects, build meaningful donor and alumni relationships, and contribute to special initiatives that advance college, unit, and UCF priorities.


These roles are ideal for proactive, relationship\-driven fundraisers who are energized by building connections, opening doors, and moving donor relationships forward. The strongest candidates will bring demonstrated experience closing major gifts, strong communication and listening skills, and the resilience to build and grow a portfolio in a dynamic advancement environment. If you are a self\-driven gift officer who is motivated by mission\-driven work and ready to help shape philanthropic support for UCF’s future, we want to hear from you.


The positions will support the following colleges:

* The **College of Sciences** helps lead the way with a focus on transformative industry partnerships and student success that enhance social mobility in the Central Florida community and beyond. Private support is essential to sustaining that momentum, and the Associate Director of Development plays a central role in building the relationships that make it possible.
* UCF’s **College of Engineering and Computer Science** is one of the largest and most dynamic engineering colleges in the nation, preparing the next generation of innovators, problem\-solvers, and technology leaders. Private support is essential to sustaining that momentum, and the Associate Director of Development plays a central role in building the relationships that make it possible.


UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional vacancies in this department.

**Responsibilities:**

* Build and strategically manage a portfolio of major gift prospects through all stages of the fundraising cycle. Conduct face\-to\-face visits with current and prospective donors, including individuals, foundations, and corporations, with the goal of bringing major gift solicitations to a successful close.
* Develop and present compelling major gift proposals tailored to the interests and priorities of each donor. Acknowledge and recognize gifts in ways that are meaningful to donors and consistent with the values and mission of the college unit and UCF's Advancement \& Partnerships division.
* Maintain thorough and accurate records using UCF's prospect management tools and fundraising database, including contact reports, research summaries, and gift documentation. Ensure consistent adherence to best practices in record\-keeping and data integrity.
* Contribute to special fundraising initiatives as needed to advance college and university priorities, in coordination with development leadership and unit partners.

**Minimum Qualifications**:


Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4\+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112\.219(6\).

**Preferred Qualifications**:

* Demonstrated success identifying, cultivating, and closing major gifts of $25,000 or more from individual donors, foundations, or corporations
* Experience as a frontline fundraiser, gift officer, nonprofit development professional, or similar relationship\-driven revenue generation role.
* Experience in higher education advancement, nonprofit fundraising, healthcare philanthropy, alumni engagement, or a related fundraising environment.
* Experience building and managing donor, prospect, client, or partner relationships through a portfolio\-based engagement cycle.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Moran Company is pleased to partner with Friends of the Children - Stockton to recruit the organization's next Executive Director.

Friends of the Children is a nationally recognized nonprofit organization with a powerful mission to impact generational change by empowering youth who face the greatest obstacles through relationships with paid professional mentors—12+ years, no matter what. For more than three decades, the Friends of the Children model has produced measurable outcomes for children and families across the country. Friends of the Children’s impact is evident - a longitudinal study by the Harvard Business School Association of Oregon confirmed that for every $1 invested in Friends of the Children, the community benefits over $7 in saved social costs.

Established in 2024, Friends of the Children - Stockton has been building the infrastructure, partnerships, and organizational capacity to support sustainable growth in its mission. The chapter has a strong foundation in place, including strong seed funding (approximately $1.7 million in fundraising revenue last year), a dedicated and mission-driven staff team of five, an engaged seven-member Board of Directors, and the collaborative support of a proven national network, including operational, financial, programmatic, and leadership resources. The chapter is poised to accelerate its visibility, expand its impact, and strengthen its position as a leading force for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The Executive Director role is an incredible opportunity to build upon this momentum, helping establish Friends of the Children - Stockton as one of the region's most visible, trusted, and influential organizations serving children and families through its two-generation approach.

Friends of the Children – Stockton seeks a highly relational, entrepreneurial, and community-centered Executive Director to guide the organization through its next phase of start-up growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors and partnering with Friends of the Children National, the Executive Director will serve as the organization’s chief executive, fundraiser, strategist, ambassador, and culture-builder. This leader will focus on expanding visibility, increasing philanthropic investment, strengthening community partnerships, building organizational capacity, and advancing long-term outcomes for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The successful candidate will be a compelling advocate and storyteller who can build authentic relationships with donors, community leaders, partners, staff, families, and other stakeholders. This is an ideal opportunity for an accomplished nonprofit executive who combines strategic vision, entrepreneurial business acumen, and hands-on leadership with a deep commitment to mission.

The Executive Director will provide strategic, mission-centered leadership while serving as the organization’s lead fundraiser, spokesperson, ambassador, and advocate. This leader will partner closely with the Board, National leadership, staff, and peer Executive Directors to strengthen governance, support collaboration, and ensure fidelity to the Friends of the Children model. They will lead fundraising and community relations efforts by cultivating donors, foundations, corporations, public officials, and nonprofit partners to build a diversified and sustainable funding base. The Executive Director will oversee strategic planning, annual operations, budgeting, growth initiatives, performance monitoring, and risk management to advance long-term organizational goals. They will also ensure high-quality program delivery, sound financial stewardship, strong administrative systems, and a supportive team culture that promotes staff development, accountability, morale, and retention.

The ideal candidate will have a bachelor’s degree, with an advanced degree preferred, and 10 or more years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience in nonprofit or related environments. They should bring demonstrated success in fundraising, operations, finance, strategy, people leadership, organizational growth, and major gift development, along with strong executive presence and credibility with donors, board members, community leaders, and public stakeholders. The successful candidate will be a strategic, collaborative, culturally competent, and approachable leader with excellent communication, storytelling, decision-making, and supervisory skills, as well as a strong commitment to child development, youth outcomes, and long-term mentoring models.

The salary range for this position is $145,000–$165,000 including incentive compensation, depending on qualifications and experience. Friends of the Children offers a comprehensive benefits package and a culture that values collaboration, belonging, professional growth, and work-life harmony.

The search for the Friends of the Children - Stockton Executive Director is being conducted by The Moran Company. Questions about the position can be directed to Angie Heer, The Moran Company: angie (at) morancompany.com.

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to Angie Heer at The Moran Company via the secure online portal. The resume should include all professional education and experience, examples of nonprofit leadership accomplishments, dates of employment (month and year), position/title, and organization names. The cover letter should highlight your relevant experience, passion for Friends of the Children Stockton’s mission, and your approach to building and scaling an organization. Applications should be submitted by July 19.

Location:
Santa Barbara, California
Organization Type:
Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation (501c3)

Board of Directors
Position Type:
Full-time, Exempt

Sarah House Santa Barbara provides end-of-life care with extraordinary kindness
to people with low incomes and individuals living with HIV/AIDS. Our 8-bed residential home offers social model hospice care in a compassionate, dignified environment during life's final chapter.

For over three decades, Sarah House has been a sanctuary for our community's most vulnerable residents, ensuring that no one faces death alone or without comfort. We work in partnership with hospice providers, community organizations, and dedicated volunteers to deliver person-centered care grounded in respect, warmth, and humanity.

Position Overview

Sarah House seeks a passionate, skillful, strategic, mission-driven leader to serve as Executive Director / Development Director. The ideal candidate will bring proven nonprofit management experience, fundraising expertise, and a deep commitment to serving those experiencing homelessness, serious illness, and end-of-life transitions.

The Executive Director / Development Director, reports to and works with the Board of Directors, providing overall leadership, strategic planning, legal compliance, and operational supervision for the organization, in accordance with all Federal, State, Local and Licensing Regulations and Company Policy and Procedures. This role requires extensive fundraising and development work with financial oversight, board relations, community engagement, and staff supervision—all while keeping Sarah House's mission of extraordinary kindness at the center of every decision.

Key Responsibilities

Fund Development & Community Relations

- Lead individual donor identification and cultivation, stewardship, and major gift solicitation programs
- Manage Planned Giving and Endowment Fund programs and development
- Write and manage grant proposals and reports for government, foundation, and

corporate funders
- Plan and execute all special fundraising development events and marketing activities per

Fund Development Plans
- Build and maintain partnerships with community organizations, hospice providers,

stakeholders, donors and volunteers
- Represent Sarah House publicly through speaking engagements, media relations, and

advocacy, direct mailings and special events and as active community liaison

Financial & Operational Management

- Oversee annual budget development and financial planning in partnership with Executive Committee
- Monitor cash flow, financial performance, and operational sustainability per Budget guidelines

- Ensure compliance with nonprofit regulations, tax filings (Form 990, welfare exemption), and grant requirements with records maintenance and management
- Manage Resident Care via House Manager and staff supervision; coordinate with contracted bookkeeping services, Hospice agencies and Human Resources / Legal services

Board Governance & Leadership

- Support Board of Directors with meeting preparation, strategic planning, and governance activities
- Provide regular financial and programmatic reports to Board and committees
- Cultivate board engagement and help identify prospective board members
- Implement Board-approved strategic initiatives
- Perform all other reasonable and suitable duties and responsibilities as assigned by the

Board of Directors

Data & Systems Management

- Maintain donor database (DonorPerfect) and ensure accurate gift processing and acknowledgment
- Oversee QuickBooks accounting system and financial record-keeping
- Manage email communications, donor appeals, and digital outreach (Mailchimp)
- Manage Web site, proficient in Word, Excel, Power Point and Social Media Systems

Qualifications

Required

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, or related field
- Minimum 3 years of nonprofit leadership experience, including fundraising and budget management
- Demonstrated success in donor cultivation, grant writing, and revenue diversification
- Strong financial acumen with experience in budget development, financial reporting, and

audit processes
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Proficiency with nonprofit financial and donor management systems (QuickBooks,

DonorPerfect or similar)
- Commitment to serving people experiencing serious illness, and end of life care with

dignity and compassion
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple competing priorities
- Valid California driver's license and reliable transportation
- Pass CA DSS Background Check

Preferred

- Knowledge of hospice care, HIV/AIDS services, or homeless services sectors
- Experience with government grants and contracts (city, county, state)
- Familiarity with Santa Barbara nonprofit landscape and community resources
- Bilingual (English/Spanish) a plus
- CA RCFE certification desired, funding for initial certification available

Personal Attributes

- Mission-driven with a servant leadership approach
- Comfortable working with people facing death and dying
- Ability to build authentic relationships across diverse communities
- Calm under pressure with strong problem-solving skills
- Detail-oriented with excellent organizational and time management abilities
- Collaborative team player who can also work autonomously
- Integrity, transparency, and accountability in all aspects of work

Compensation & Benefits

- $110,000 base salary commensurate with experience and nonprofit sector standards
- Health insurance contribution
- IRA retirement plan with employer contribution
- Paid time off (vacation, sick leave, holidays)
- Flexible schedule with occasional evening/weekend responsibilities for events and board meetings

Work Environment

The Executive Director / Development Director works primarily from a home office or on site working space, with regular visits to Sarah House facility, community meetings, donor visits, and external appointments. jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Moran Company is pleased to partner with Friends of the Children-San Diego to recruit the organization's first Executive Director.

Friends of the Children is a nationally recognized nonprofit organization with a powerful mission to impact generational change by empowering youth who face the greatest obstacles through relationships with paid professional mentors—12+ years, no matter what. For more than three decades, the Friends of the Children model has produced measurable outcomes for children and families across the country. Friends of the Children’s impact is evident - a longitudinal study by the Harvard Business School Association of Oregon confirmed that for every $1 invested in Friends of the Children, the community benefits over $7 in saved social costs. Now, Friends of the Children is bringing its proven model to San Diego.

Friends of the Children–San Diego is launching with extraordinary momentum. Rather than building from scratch, the organization's first Executive Director will inherit a remarkable opportunity to accelerate an already well-established vision. Over the past 18 months, Friends of the Children National and local community leaders have worked together to establish a strong foundation for the organization's long-term success. Multi-year seed capital has already been secured, relationships have been cultivated with philanthropic, civic, and nonprofit leaders throughout the region, and the model has been enthusiastically welcomed into collaborative efforts, such as the United 4 Youth Collaborative.

Friends of the Children–San Diego will intentionally enroll children ages 4 to 6 and their caregivers who face the greatest challenges to long-term stability and well-being, with an initial focus on former foster youth who are parenting and families most at risk of child welfare involvement. The chapter will launch as an independent 501(c)(3) supported by Friends of the Children National, benefiting from a nationally proven operating model, extensive leadership resources, and a network of successful Executive Directors across the country.

Friends of the Children–San Diego seeks a highly relational, entrepreneurial, and community-centered Executive Director to lead the successful launch and long-term growth of this new chapter. As the organization’s chief executive, chief fundraiser, strategic leader, and primary ambassador, the Executive Director will build trusted relationships across San Diego County, expand philanthropic investment, hire and support the founding staff team, and work closely with the founding Board of Directors and Friends of the Children National. The Executive Director will ensure excellence and fidelity to the Friends of the Children model while strengthening the visibility, capacity, and sustainable funding needed for the program and the children and families it serves to thrive. This opportunity is ideal for an accomplished nonprofit executive or senior advancement leader with strong fundraising success, entrepreneurial business acumen, and a deep commitment to building a high-impact organization in a new market.

The Executive Director will provide enthusiastic leadership, strategic direction, and long-term vision while serving as Friends of the Children–San Diego’s lead fundraising champion, spokesperson, ambassador, and advocate. They will build trust across staff, board members, community partners, families, donors, and Friends of the Children National, while recruiting and developing a high-performing team and fostering a collaborative, children-first culture. The Executive Director will lead all fundraising and resource development efforts, personally cultivate major donors, foundations, corporations, and public funding opportunities, and strengthen the organization’s visibility throughout San Diego’s philanthropic, civic, business, and nonprofit communities. They will develop and execute strategic plans, annual operating plans, budgets, growth initiatives, and risk management strategies in partnership with the Board and National leadership. The Executive Director will ensure fidelity to the Friends of the Children model, support excellent program delivery and outcomes, provide sound financial and administrative stewardship, and build the organizational capacity needed for long-term sustainability.

The ideal candidate will have a bachelor’s degree, with an advanced degree preferred, and ten or more years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience in nonprofit or related environments. They will bring a deep appreciation for child development, youth outcomes, and long-term mentoring models, along with significant fundraising experience and a demonstrated ability to secure major gifts and diversify revenue streams. Strong candidates will offer executive presence, credibility with donors and community stakeholders, and either established relationships within San Diego County or a proven ability to quickly build trusted relationships with philanthropic, business, civic, and community leaders. The successful candidate will be a strategic, collaborative, and empowering leader with experience building and scaling organizations, leading across fundraising, operations, finance, strategy, and people, and motivating teams with cultural competence, sound judgment, accountability, and strong communication skills.

The salary range for this position is $145,000–$165,000, including incentive compensation, depending on qualifications and experience. Friends of the Children offers a benefits package and a culture that values collaboration, belonging, professional growth, and work-life harmony.

The search for the Friends of the Children-San Diego Executive Director is being conducted by The Moran Company. Questions about the position can be directed to Angie Heer, The Moran Company: angie (at) morancompany.com. Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to Angie Heer, The Moran Company. The resume should include all professional education and experience, examples of nonprofit leadership and fundraising accomplishments, dates of employment (month and year), position/title, and organization names. The cover letter should highlight your relevant experience, passion for Friends of the Children-San Diego’s mission, fundraising experience, and your approach to building and scaling an organization. Applications should be submitted by July 31.

Under the artistic direction of Tamara Rojo and executive leadership of Branislav Henselmann, SF Ballet is leading boldly into a new era, where artistic vision, organizational momentum, and civic energy converge to create a genuinely rare moment of opportunity. The company is reimagining what ballet can be, and making the case that its most compelling chapter is still ahead.

Direct content creation and storytelling that deepens audience connection, advances institutional priorities, and provides the narrative foundation for revenue-driving campaigns across all channels.

About San Diego Health Connect

San Diego Health Connect (SDHC) is a nonprofit Health Information Exchange (HIE) and designated California Qualified Health Information Organization (QHIO) serving San Diego and Imperial Counties. As a subsidiary of 211 San Diego, SDHC serves as a trusted bridge between healthcare, public health, emergency medical services, behavioral health, and community-based organizations, enabling secure, real-time exchange of health information to improve care coordination and advance whole-person care. Processing more than 50 million clinical messages each month and maintaining a patient index of 4.8 million individuals, SDHC connects hospitals, health systems, federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), physician groups, EMS agencies, public health departments, managed care organizations, pharmacies, and community partners throughout the region. Through leadership in interoperability, health information exchange, and healthcare innovation, SDHC supports improved health outcomes while advancing California's vision for integrated health and social care.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the President & CEO of 211 San Diego, the Executive Director (ED) provides strategic, operational, financial, and technical leadership for San Diego Health Connect. As the organization's senior executive, the ED is responsible for advancing SDHC's mission while ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, financial sustainability, and continued growth as one of California's premier Health Information Exchanges.

Responsibilities

Develop and execute SDHC's strategic plan, business model, and long-term financial sustainability roadmap.
Translate organizational vision into measurable operational objectives, ensuring successful execution across all areas of the organization.
Identify opportunities to leverage SDHC's relationship with 211 San Diego to expand partnerships, strengthen interoperability, and increase organizational impact throughout the healthcare and social care ecosystem.
Drive organizational growth through strategic partnerships, innovation, service expansion, and continuous improvement.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, service excellence, and mission-driven leadership.
Serve as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, providing strategic guidance, organizational performance updates, and recommendations that support informed governance and long-term sustainability.
Represent SDHC in local, regional, state, and national healthcare interoperability initiatives and policy discussions.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with healthcare executives, elected officials, state agencies, industry associations, and community leaders.
Monitor, interpret, and synthesize healthcare legislation, public policy, and regulatory developments affecting health information exchange, interoperability, healthcare technology, and data sharing.
Guide organizational strategy related to California's Data Exchange Framework (DxF), TEFCA, Qualified Health Information Organization (QHIO) requirements, CMS regulations, HIPAA, HITECH, and emerging interoperability standards.
Provide executive oversight of all organizational operations, ensuring high-quality, efficient, and compliant delivery of HIE services.
Oversee budgeting, procurement, contract management, operational planning, and organizational performance measurement.
Provide strategic leadership over SDHC's technical infrastructure.
Ensure operational excellence while maintaining the flexibility to pivot quickly in response to evolving healthcare priorities, regulatory changes, funding opportunities, and technological advancements.
Build, strengthen, and sustain trusted executive-level partnerships with various stakeholders.
Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable federal, state, and industry regulations.
Develop and oversee the organization's annual operating budget and long-term financial plans.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of approximately 10–15 professionals across operations, technology, data services, and administration.

Qualifications

Master's degree in Healthcare Administration, Public Health, Business Administration, Health Informatics, Information Systems, Public Administration, Information Management, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of seven years of progressive executive leadership experience in a healthcare system, Health Information Exchange (HIE), health information technology organization, public health agency, healthcare technology company, or similarly complex healthcare environment.
Demonstrated success leading organizational strategy, operational excellence, financial management, and enterprise growth.
Experience working with hospitals, health systems, physician organizations, clinics, managed care organizations, government agencies, and community partners.
Experience operating in politically complex environments requiring diplomacy, executive presence, consensus-building, and strategic relationship management.

Required Skills

Strong knowledge of healthcare delivery systems and healthcare operations.
Electronic Health Records (EHRs) and Health Information Exchanges (HIE).
Healthcare interoperability standards HL7, FHIR, and clinical messaging.
Master Patient Index (MPI) and Master Data Management (MDM).
Healthcare analytics and data governance.
Population health and care coordination.
Social Determinants of Health (SDoH).
Healthcare privacy, cybersecurity, and data security.
Enterprise risk management.
Healthcare regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements.
Visionary and strategic thinker with exceptional execution skills.
Strong political acumen and executive presence.
Outstanding networking, relationship-building, and partnership development abilities.
Deep understanding of healthcare industry terminology, policy, and regulatory environments.
Proven ability to synthesize complex policy, regulatory, and technical information into actionable organizational strategy.
Exceptional communication, negotiation, and consensus-building skills.
Strong financial and business acumen.
Adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced, evolving healthcare environment.
Ability to balance strategic leadership with operational execution while leading through change and organizational growth.

jobs.description:
Atlas Assistance Dogs envisions a world where anyone who could benefit from a service dog can have one, and where people with disabilities and their dogs thrive together.

Our mission is to support people with disabilities to train their own service dogs, educate ethical trainers, strengthen the human-canine bond, and promote a more inclusive society. We are a relational, volunteer-rich, mission-driven organization committed to disability inclusion, accessibility, client-centered service, positive reinforcement, force-free training, and the well-being of both people and dogs.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Atlas is entering an important next stage of growth. We have a strong foundation built by founders, board members, staff, contractors, volunteers, trainers, clients, and community supporters. We are seeking an Executive Director who can help us build on that foundation with greater clarity, sustainability, and shared purpose.

We are looking for someone who can help Atlas grow in a thoughtful and realistic way. The Executive Director’s first priority will be fund development and financial sustainability. The second priority will be organizational coordination. The third priority will be broader community messaging, partnership building, and outreach.

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL FOCUS ON

1. Fund development and financial sustainability
The Executive Director will help build the financial foundation Atlas needs for long-term impact. This includes:
Leading a practical fund development plan.
Building relationships with donors, funders, sponsors, and community partners.
Leading donor cultivation, grant strategy and writing, fundraising campaigns, and stewardship.
Partnering with the board to strengthen fundraising and community ambassadorship.

2. Organizational coordination
The Executive Director will help the organization work together with clearer roles, priorities, communication, and decision-making. This includes:
Serving as the executive leader accountable for whole-organization output, viewing the organization holistically to ensure integration, compliance, and performance across programs, fundraising, operations, communications, finance, and board communication.
Helping clarify who owns what, where questions go, and how decisions are made.
Supporting staff, contractors, and key volunteers with clear coordination and follow-through.
Strengthening systems that reduce over-dependence on informal knowledge or any one person.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Moran Company is pleased to partner with Munchausen Support to recruit the organization's Executive Director.

Munchausen by Proxy (MBP) is a serious, complex, and widely misunderstood form of medical child abuse. It leaves a wide swath of destruction and trauma for everyone involved, often resulting in lifelong devastation for survivors.

Founded in 2021 in collaboration with some of the world’s top experts on MBP, the Munchausen Support Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to providing science- and fact-based resources. The Foundation offers critical support for family members in crisis, survivors seeking treatment, and professionals navigating active cases.

Today, the organization offers structured 10-week survivor support groups alongside specialized cohorts, including dedicated groups for fathers and grandparents. In addition to direct peer support, the Munchausen Support Foundation focuses on pioneering research, education for healthcare providers on how to recognize medical abuse, and professional training for proper evaluation and support delivery.

As the Foundation approaches its 5-year milestone, the Board of Directors is seeking a high-caliber, experienced, and visionary leader with a growth mindset to serve as its inaugural Executive Director. This pivotal role is designed for a strategic builder who will guide the organization through its next phase of expansion to deliver deeper, wider support to those impacted by Munchausen by Proxy. The Executive Director will oversee programs, financial growth, fundraising strategy, remote operations, consultants, and volunteer engagement to strengthen and expand the Foundation’s impact.

The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors to develop and execute strategic and operational plans that expand the Foundation’s reach, impact, and organizational capacity. This leader will supervise volunteers, board members, and paid consultants while ensuring strong daily operations and full legal, ethical, and regulatory compliance. The Executive Director will support founders and board members as public representatives of the organization, strengthen brand awareness through multimedia and digital communications, deepen relationships with partners, donors, healthcare professionals, and institutional stakeholders, and oversee peer support groups, research initiatives, and specialized committees. This role will also lead annual fundraising strategy, manage the Foundation’s budget, support long-term financial sustainability, and partner with the Board Treasurer to provide clear financial reporting to the Board and key stakeholders.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong commitment to the mission of the Munchausen Support Foundation, exceptional emotional intelligence, trauma-informed sensitivity, and the ability to communicate complex medical and social issues with clarity to diverse audiences. This leader should have a proven ability to build trust with survivors, families, peer facilitators, medical and academic professionals, while also demonstrating success in donor cultivation, fundraising, grant writing, financial management, budgeting, governance, and strategic planning. A bachelor’s degree and at least three to five years of senior-level nonprofit management experience are required, along with the initiative to thrive in a fully remote environment and the flexibility to travel for conferences, Foundation-related meetings, and donor engagement.

The salary range is $100,000–$105,000, commensurate with experience, with standard benefits including PTO, flexible scheduling, retirement, and healthcare.

The executive search for the Munchausen Support Foundation is being conducted by The Moran Company. Questions regarding this position may be directed to Jane Lampo at jlampo (at) morancompany.com. To apply, please submit a tailored cover letter and comprehensive resume via our secure online portal.

Resume requirements: Must include all professional education, employment dates (month and year), specific titles, and organization names.

Cover letter requirements: Should explicitly articulate your relevant experience, alignment with the Foundation's mission, and fit for this leadership role.
