jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
About the job

CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

SPY is looking for a leader who can guide an established youth homelessness organization through its next stage of scale, sustainability, housing growth, public advocacy, and strategic planning. The next leader must have an unwavering commitment to championing SPY's mission and the young people it serves; the ability to adaptively support and develop SPY staff; effectively lead a robust fundraising, external relations, and finance management strategy; and the experience to oversee a complex $15M organization operating 24 hour programs.

ABOUT SAFE PLACE FOR YOUTH

Safe Place for Youth is a leading youth homelessness organization serving young people ages 12 to 25 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Los Angeles. SPY’s mission is to prevent and end youth homelessness through supportive services, sustainable housing opportunities, community collaboration, and advocacy, with a vision of a socially just and equitable world where all young people are empowered to thrive in self-directed lives and have a safe place to call home.

SPY provides a continuum of youth-centered services that includes street outreach, a drop-in center, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, community garden, pregnant and parenting support, shelter, social enterprise, family reunification, housing, and advocacy. In 2025, SPY served more than 1,200 youth, helped 315 young people move into housing, and connected hundreds more to mental health counseling, case management, workforce training, creative arts, street outreach, and other critical supports.

SPY has entered a new stage of organizational complexity and opportunity. The organization now operates 10 sites across the County, including multiple housing programs across shelter, transitional housing, and permanent housing, providing 224 housing resources on any given night. SPY also provides robust supportive services through a field-based model and out of our drop-in center in Venice, including basic needs resources, case management, mental health, substance use counseling, education and employment, pregnant and parenting, healing arts and more.       

The next leader will be called upon to sustain operational excellence across housing and services programs, actively lead a robust fundraising strategy, ensure strong financial oversight, continue SPY’s leadership in advocacy, maintain strong community collaboration, support strong recruitment, retention and development of staff, while keeping the dignity and wellbeing of youth at the center of all of SPY’s work.     

POSITION OVERVIEW

SPY seeks a Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization into its next phase of impact, sustainability, and public leadership.

The next leader will inherit a respected, mission-driven organization with a strong community identity, a seasoned senior team, an engaged Board, a growing housing portfolio, a newly redeveloped drop-in center, a planned capital campaign, and an urgent opportunity to shape the future of youth homelessness policy and practice in Los Angeles. The role requires a leader who can hold multiple responsibilities at once: stewarding a complex nonprofit enterprise, strengthening internal systems, serving as an external advocate and fundraiser, leading through a new strategic plan, and ensuring that SPY remains deeply connected to the young people and communities it serves.

The successful candidate will be a values-driven, emotionally intelligent, operationally capable, and externally credible leader who can balance ambition with sustainability. They will bring the strategic judgment to decide where SPY should grow, where it should consolidate, where it should advocate, and where it should say no. They will be equally comfortable with youth, staff, donors, elected officials, public agency leaders, community partners, and the Board.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute strategic plans in alignment with the organization’s mission, vision, and values. Lead the organization in identifying trends, funding environment, challenges, and future growth opportunities in the housing environment.
Advocacy and Policy Engagement: Serve as an external champion, advocate, and coalition builder for SPY. Build and maintain strong relationships with elected officials, public agencies, funders, community stakeholders, peer organizations, housing partners, researchers, advocates, neighborhood leaders, and media. Advocate for youth-specific homelessness funding, policy, housing resources, and service models.
Program and Housing Leadership: Oversee the continued development of SPY’s continuum of care, including outreach, drop-in services, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, pregnant and parenting supports, advocacy, shelter, transitional housing, permanent housing, and housing navigation.
Fundraising and Resource Development:

Lead fundraising efforts to secure financial support from diverse sources, including grants, donations, and corporate giving, and other forms of sponsorships.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with donors, foundations, and corporate partners to expand and diversify the organization's funding base and ensure financial sustainability.
Design expansion and business planning for program expansion. Build partnerships in new areas, establishing relationship with funders and political and community leaders for expansion sites.
Financial Management and Enterprise Sustainability: Oversee SPY’s financial health in partnership with the CFO, Board Treasurer, Finance Committee, and senior leadership. Ensure strong budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, reserves planning, audit readiness, internal controls, contract compliance, and financial reporting.
Staff Leadership and Culture: Provide effective leadership and management of staff, volunteers, and consultants that fosters a collaborative and inclusive work environment while still maintaining accountability.
Board Relations and Governance: Work closely with the Board of Directors to ensure effective board operations, governance, accountability, and transparency. Provide regular updates, reports, and recommendations to the Board to facilitate informed decision-making and strategic planning.
Other duties as assigned to support the mission of the organization.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE YOU’LL NEED:
At least 5 years of executive leadership experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree or relevant professional training preferred
Significant senior leadership experience in a nonprofit, public agency, housing, social services, youth-serving, advocacy, or mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated commitment to racial equity, social justice, LGBTQ+ inclusion, trauma-informed practice, and youth voice.
Ability to embody SPY’s values of care, community, inclusivity, innovation, integrity, and sustainability.
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage complexity, and build organizational infrastructure.
Experience with fundraising, external relations, public funding, and     institutional partnerships.
Strong financial literacy and experience managing or overseeing budgets, audits, contracts, and organizational risk.
Demonstrated adaptive and situational leadership, and experience mentoring and developing teams. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Past success working with a Board of Directors with the ability to cultivate board member relationships

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Hybrid work environment, such as shared office space and/or remote work, with meaningful engagement at SPY sites.
Physical effort/lifting, up to 15-20 pounds at times.

SPECIAL CONDITIONS:

Mandated Reporting Requirements: The person holding this position is considered a ‘mandated reporter’ under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements as a condition of employment.

Safe Place for Youth offers a competitive benefit package including comprehensive health coverage, 403b with agency contribution, and vacation/sick time. We also offer unique perks including weekly meditation/mindfulness and professional development opportunities that are tailored to your individual career growth. 

COMPENSATION:

All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. Safe Place for Youth does not discriminate on the basis of any protected status under federal, state, or local law. 

Safe Place for Youth is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. jobs.description:
Reports to
: Assistant Superintendent of College, Career & Life Readiness

Location:
BPS Office of Secondary Schools, Bolling Building, 2300 Washington St. Roxbury, MA

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Executive Director of School Counseling Services resides in the Office of College, Career, and Life Readiness (CCLR) within the Academic & Professional Learning Division of Boston Public Schools, reporting to the Assistant Superintendent of CCLR. The Executive Director of School Counseling Services is responsible for creating a vision and establishing a district-wide comprehensive school counseling program plan to equitably support the needs of every student across Boston Public Schools. In alignment with the district’s mission, the Executive Director of School Counseling Services will develop, implement, evaluate, and improve city-wide systems of school counseling functions; work collaboratively with counselors, site-based administrators, district staff, and community partners to ensure every child receives support in their journey towards academic achievement, social and emotional well-being, and postsecondary readiness; and serve as an advocate and modern visionary for the profession and current school counselors.

RESPONSIBILITIES
:

Comprehensive School Counseling Leadership

Collaborate with various stakeholders including (but not limited to) school counselors, special education professionals, Multilingual lLearner (MLL) professionals, and other student support partners to design, implement, monitor, and evaluate a comprehensive, data-driven district plan for equitable school counseling services that support every student’s academic achievement, social-emotional well-being, and post-secondary readiness.
Oversee the creation of district metrics and tools for monitoring successful outcomes of comprehensive school counseling program implementation.
Provide leadership and direction for implementing Mass Core Graduation Requirements and related policies.
Lead creation of Registrar Handbook to clearly articulate accurate processes for scheduling and transcript maintenance.
Train and Support Registrars and Welcome Center, and REC., to ensure that all registrars appropriately code student coursework
Analyze critical needs in counseling across BPS and work collaboratively to design, implement, refine, and evaluate programs and services in order to continuously improve.
Ensure that the school counselor voice is represented in the development of district policies, procedures, and initiatives.
Oversee the development and training of districtwide counseling curriculum and interventions to support student success.
Prepare and present school board documents highlighting comprehensive, equitable, data-driven counseling services across BPS.
Support the recruitment, hiring, placement, retention, and continuous development of highly qualified, diverse counseling team members across BPS.
Implement measurement tools to ensure that all state requirements for counseling are met by counselors and students.
Prepare annual operating budget recommendations for the department, alongside implementing and monitoring assigned budgets.
Seek ways to promote and advocate for equitable counseling services across BPS.

Team Management and Leadership

Oversee the growth and development of districtwide comprehensive school counseling services, including directly supervising and evaluating district team members and indirectly supporting site-based counselors.
Provide leadership and administrative direction to assigned staff for the operations, financial, and personnel resources to effectively support counseling and district goals.
Facilitate communication and collaboration among assigned departmental personnel and school and district administrators to enhance program development, service delivery, and student/family engagement.
Participate on a cross-functional team, including internal and external partners, to advance the districts’ vision of a graduate and aligned college, career, and life readiness strategies.
Lead a central office counseling team consisting of the Director of Guidance and Staff Assistant.

Professional Growth and Development

Support the creation and delivery of a professional development scope and sequence, differentiated by school level, that increases counseling staff effectiveness and improves student outcomes.
Utilize tools to assess counselor skill levels, knowledge of the needs of adult learners, and characteristics of effective professional development.
Provide professional learning to site- and district-based administrators to support the appropriate use of counseling staff in alignment with site-based goals.
Support school leaders to provide effective supervision and evaluative feedback to school counselors
Increase the quality and scope of the district’s counseling program by staying current in best practices and pedagogy at the state and national levels.
Work with the district’s Postsecondary team to design and execute annual My Career & Academic Plan (MyCAP) professional learning for school counselors.

Partnership Support

Build relationships with university pre-service counseling programs to attract, onboard and support graduate student interns across all BPS schools and diploma granting programs.
Build and support relationships with transition support services such as STRIVE, Massachusetts Rehabilitation Commission, and Easter Seals College Navigator.
In partnership with district colleagues, support counselors’ roles in MTSS.
Participate on internal and external cross-functional teams to drive the district’s college and career readiness strategies, including New Skills Boston, Success Boston and others.

QUALIFICATIONS - REQUIRED
:

Master’s degree in counseling, education, or a related field.
MA DESE School Counselor or School Adjustment Counselor license.
Minimum five to seven (5-7) years working as a school/school adjustment counselor and/or counseling director (or another form of counseling leadership).
Evidence of commitment to equity-focused work and support for the role of comprehensive counseling services to close opportunity gaps and eliminate inequitable student outcomes.
Knowledge of K-12 school counseling best practices related to academic advising, social-emotional well-being, and postsecondary planning and evidence of a commitment to stay current on relevant research.
Evidence of a strong understanding of MassCore, the American School Counselor Association (ASCA) National Model, MA Model 3.0 (MASCA), data-driven school counseling, and MyCAP.
Knowledge and experience with systems-level work and antiracist school counseling practices.
Understanding of data-driven school counseling practices.
Evidence of exceptional leadership and collaboration skills - ability to hold multiple perspectives and make connections between ideas and concepts.
Current authorization to work in the United States
An understanding of and commitment to gaining a greater understanding of what is necessary for an urban school system to enjoy a continuous improvement in an increasingly complex and competitive environment.
A deeply held and unyielding belief in the overarching mission of public education.

QUALIFICATIONS - PREFERRED
:

Master’s degree in School Counseling and/or School Adjustment Counseling
Familiarity with Boston and Boston Public Schools

TERMS:
Managerial, D71.

jobs.title: General Manager/ COO
jobs.description:
About Sarasota Polo Club

Sarasota Polo Club is a distinctive sports, entertainment, and event destination located in Sarasota, Florida. Set on more than 170 acres, the property is home to an established seasonal polo program that attracts thousands of spectators, members, players, sponsors, and guests throughout the season.

While polo remains central to the identity and heritage of the Club, Sarasota Polo Club has significant opportunity to expand the use of its property, facilities, audience, and brand beyond traditional polo operations. Ownership’s vision is to develop the Club into a broader year-round destination for sports, entertainment, hospitality, corporate, community, and special events while preserving the character and quality that make the property unique.

We are seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial leader who can operate today’s business while helping build what Sarasota Polo Club can become.

The Role

The General Manager / Chief Operating Officer will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day business and operations of Sarasota Polo Club and will work directly with ownership to execute the Club’s long-term strategy.

This is not simply a club management position. We are looking for a hands-on business leader who combines strong operational discipline with commercial instincts and an ability to identify and develop new revenue opportunities.

The successful candidate will oversee club operations, events, facilities, personnel, budgets, vendor relationships, guest experience, and coordination of the seasonal polo program. Equally important, this individual will help expand the Club’s commercial potential through non-polo events, partnerships, sponsorships, hospitality programs, facility utilization, and other revenue-producing opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead the overall day-to-day operation of Sarasota Polo Club, with accountability for operating performance, service standards, staffing, and execution.
* Develop annual operating plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures, and financial controls.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team responsible for events, facilities, grounds, hospitality, polo operations, marketing, and administration.
* Oversee the planning and execution of polo matches, major events, private functions, and other activities held on the property.
* Identify and develop opportunities to increase revenue and year-round utilization of the Club’s property and facilities.
* Build relationships with event producers, promoters, sponsors, corporate partners, vendors, community organizations, and other potential business partners.
* Evaluate new events and commercial opportunities based on revenue potential, operational requirements, brand fit, and profitability.
* Negotiate and manage vendor, tenant, promoter, and partner relationships.
* Maintain high standards for facilities, grounds, safety, security, regulatory compliance, and guest experience.
* Establish operating systems, reporting, accountability, and processes appropriate for a growing organization.
* Work closely with ownership on strategic initiatives, capital improvements, property development, and the long-term evolution of Sarasota Polo Club.

Candidate Profile

We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully managed complex venues or businesses where operations, events, hospitality, and revenue generation intersect.

Relevant backgrounds may include sports and entertainment venues, major event facilities, destination attractions, equestrian facilities, private clubs, hospitality businesses, festivals, fairgrounds, convention or event centers, or other multi-use properties.

Polo experience is not required.

The strongest candidates will demonstrate:

* Significant leadership experience with responsibility for people, operations, budgets, and financial results.
* A track record of improving business performance and developing new revenue opportunities.
* Experience managing events, venues, hospitality operations, or businesses with significant guest attendance.
* Strong financial and business judgment, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control, and P&L accountability.
* Experience recruiting, leading, developing, and holding teams accountable.
* Ability to manage multiple departments, vendors, partners, and stakeholders simultaneously.
* Strong commercial instincts and the ability to turn ideas, facilities, audiences, and partnerships into profitable business opportunities.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
* A practical, hands-on leadership style and willingness to be highly visible throughout the operation.
* Comfort working in an event-driven environment that includes weekends and holidays during the polo season.

A bachelor’s degree in business, hospitality, sports management, or a related discipline is preferred, although substantial relevant leadership experience may substitute for formal education.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to lead an established Sarasota institution through its next stage of development.

The successful candidate will inherit a substantial operating platform, recognized brand, established polo program, significant physical property, and loyal audience—but will also have the opportunity to help shape a much larger business.

We are looking for someone who sees a polo club today and can envision—and build—the sports, entertainment, hospitality, and event destination it can become.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non\-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions\-driven, passionate change\-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world\-wide for a better future.


We are committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. We are a dedicated advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Job Overview:**  

As the Development Director you will oversee the design, implementation, and monitoring of resource mobilization efforts in support of our mission. The specific areas of responsibility and oversight include: donor relations and reporting, collaboration with colleagues at IRC headquarters on a new collaborative fundraising structure for individual donors, outreach and prospecting to local corporate and private foundation donors, special events planning and oversight. As a member our region's senior leadership team, you will share responsibilities with other Directors for providing effective oversight over regional operations and good stewardship of resources. This is a full\-time exempt position, reporting to the Executive Director of the Sacramento/Turlock region.

**Major Responsibilities:**  

The Development Director works in close coordination with the Executive Director and local leadership to achieve the following goals:

* Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan with specific and measurable goals and objectives for development of restricted and unrestricted funds.
* Develop strategy for and execute special, restricted fundraising campaigns through digital and traditional channels, in partnership with HQ Mass Markets teams.
* Cultivate national partnerships from companies and foundations based in the Sacramento/Central Valley region, in coordination with HQ\-based Institutional Philanthropy \& Partnerships team.
* Support local high\-value donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship in close collaboration with USA Philanthropy team.
* Oversee the preparation of letters of inquiry, proposals, budgets and reports to local foundations and other potential donors in coordination with the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team, office leadership and HQ counterparts.
* Oversee joint initiatives with local programming to identify funding needs and create strategic plans to seek funding support for these needs.
* Organize annual fundraisers and other special events as applicable.
* Ensure development of strong corporate donor engagement opportunities that are aligned with program need and donor interest for national and local donors.
* Serve as focal point and liaison for Sacramento\-Turlock to HQ fundraising teams.
* Provide high level oversight for the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team.
* Coordinate with Resource \& Development Coordinators across the region to ensure consistency between volunteer and financial / in\-kind support.
* Assist in raising awareness about the IRC and representing the office at meetings, seminars, and forums.
* Recruit, hire, train and supervise development\-related interns and volunteers, when appropriate.
* Maintain ongoing communication on status of resource development initiatives and provide timely reports on management issues and concerns.
* Participate actively on Sacramento\-Turlock’s Leadership Team and collaborate closely with management team to ensure efficient collaboration with all offices in the delivery of quality services
* Work with Executive Director on opportunities to highlight the local and global work of IRC.
* Other tasks as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

* University degree (BA/BS) required; graduate degree in Development, Nonprofit Management or Business Management, or International Relations preferred
* Minimum of five (5\) years prior experience with leading fundraising, communications, public relations, and other development duties in the non\-profit sector required
* Impeccable attention to detail
* Experience with Salesforce strongly preferred
* Strong writing skills required
* Strong donor network in the Sacramento/Central Valley region preferred
* Demonstrated record of foundation and donor relations with successful development of private foundation grant proposals
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically with donors, volunteers, partner agencies, government officials, multi\-cultural clients and colleagues on all levels. Demonstrated ability to work successfully in a multi\-cultural environment.
* Experience coordinating multiple partners and consensus building toward common goal.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (especially Word, Excel, Outlook) and internet research
* Strong organizational, leadership and team\-building skills with ability to promote productivity and efficiency

**Working Environment:**


Hybrid work with minimum 3x/week in office. Standard office environment. Some travel to other regional offices required as well as to various venues for events and for meeting with donors. Availability for non\-traditional hours including weeknights and weekends on a limited basis required.  

  

**Compensation:** ($109,416 \- $117,354\). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Executive Director – Temple Sinai (Stamford, CT)**

Temple Sinai is a warm, inclusive Reform Jewish community of 400\+ households in the greater Stamford, CT area (including Darien, Greenwich, New Canaan, and Pound Ridge), where creating a genuine sense of belonging is a guiding principle. Rooted in enduring Jewish values, we blend tradition with innovation to support and uplift our congregants. We live our mission through lifelong learning, spiritual exploration, and a shared commitment to purposeful service and repairing the world. We welcome people from all backgrounds who share our dedication to community, compassion, and meaningful impact.

At Temple Sinai (“TS”), every congregant plays a vital role—whether they engage through learning, worship, volunteering, or simply by adding their presence to our shared community. We provide a warm, spiritual home where people can find meaning. Growth Happens Here.

**About the Role**

We are seeking an Executive Director to serve as the “Chief Operating Officer” for the congregation, accountable for overseeing TS’s daily business operations and executing the temple's strategic vision. In this role you will provide operational and tactical leadership, effective financial management, and continuous organizational improvement to ensure TS’s mission and goals are effectively achieved. You will work collaboratively with the Board of Trustees, clergy, staff and volunteers to foster a dynamic and thriving community. You are a dynamic leader with strong organizational, analytical, communication and technical skills, financial acumen and the ability to engage with a diverse congregation. You will manage staff, TS’s daily and long\-term operations, finances, technology, HR and facilities.This is a hands\-on position, acting as an individual contributor as well as a manager.

**Who You Are**

You are a forward‑thinking, highly effective, empathetic leader and doer who thrives in a mission‑driven environment. You have a history of success with hands‑on operational management. You enjoy supporting and developing staff and creating welcoming experiences for a diverse community. You anticipate challenges, identify opportunities, and bring professionalism and heart to your work.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operations \& People Management**

* You will drive incremental value through strong leadership, optimizing processes, and championing the adoption of modern technology.
* You will lead, supervise, and support staff to foster high performance and a collaborative team culture, with a strong emphasis on capability building and professional development.
* You will oversee daily operations and administration, programming and resource utilization, including the Synagogue and our Early Childhood Education Center..
* You have management responsibility over TS’s technology, infrastructure and security.
* You ensure TS data is maintained and secured.

**Financial Management**

* You will work in collaboration with the VP of Finance, senior staff and the Board of Trustees to develop the annual budget, and have primary responsibility for expense management and budget achievement.
* You have oversight over financial operations, including bookkeeping, payroll, and internal reporting.
* You will provide administrative support for large fundraising efforts.

**Additional Responsibilities**

**Facility Management and Security**

* You will oversee the strategic direction, vendor management, capital expenditures, maintenance and operations of TS’s facilities and grounds.
* You are accountable for TS security protocols, policies and training, and overseeing contracted security personnel, liaising with enforcement agencies and security firms.

**Congregational and Community Relations**

* You will cultivate relationships with lay leaders, Board of Trustees, key volunteers, and community partners.
* Your role oversees and implements mission\-aligned programs and events, in collaboration with staff, enhancing congregant involvement and engagement.

**Communication and Public Relations**

* You develop communication strategies to promote activities, events and initiatives.
* Your role ensures consistent and transparent communications with the Board of Trustees.
* You oversee TS’s marketing, website, social media and public relations efforts.

**Professional Development \& Best Practices**

* You will connect with peer institutions and professional networks (e.g., NATA, Executive Director roundtables) to bring best practices to TS.

**Knowledge and Skills**

* You are highly effective at managing staff, vendors, operations, and finances.
* You have a professional temperament and interpersonal skills to effectively interface across diverse membership (generations, perspectives, and traditions).
* You are an independent self\-starter who can balance multiple priorities.
* You have a proven ability to work with leadership, staff, and volunteers in managing large events (e.g., annual fundraising and high\-attendance events), contributing to and optimizing event/program resourcing, and evaluating and optimizing event portfolios.
* You have excellent written and oral communication skills; effective organizational skills.

jobs.description:
**About Break Through Tech**  

Break Through Tech transforms how tech talent is discovered, developed, and connected to opportunity in the age of AI. Working across higher education and industry, Break Through Tech delivers programs nationwide and integrates technical training, work\-based learning, mentorship, and career readiness with deep employer partnerships to create more effective and scalable routes into early tech careers. Break Through Tech is actively shaping the field of early tech talent development by identifying what works, translating those insights into replicable models, and helping define more consistent approaches to how talent is prepared, assessed, and hired across institutions and employers.  

  

At a moment when AI is reshaping every aspect of work and society, Break Through Tech’s mission is urgent: to ensure that the people who build what comes next — and who are in the room where the most consequential technology decisions of our time get made — look like the world they will shape. Learn more about our work at www.breakthroughtech.org/.  

  

**Position Summary**  

We’re looking for a strategic and collaborative Director of Development to join our team. Reporting to the Senior Director, Strategy and External Relations, this full\-time, exempt role is responsible for managing a portfolio of high\-value prospects and securing major gifts to support Break Through Tech’s mission. This role leads the development and execution of cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies, with a focus on successfully closing individual, corporate, and foundation gifts. The Director of Development collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to align fundraising activities with organizational priorities, supports annual revenue goals, and contributes to the advancement of diversity and gender equity in technology.  

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**  

The essential duties of this role are grouped into four categories, with the approximate percentage of time spent on each category indicated below  

  

*Portfolio Management and Leadership* *(35%)*  

Leads the development of proposals for major gifts, coordinating with internal stakeholders to ensure alignment with organizational priorities and own a portfolio of 15\-25 top\-tier prospects (Tier 1 \& Tier 2\), maintaining deep relationships and tracking engagement.  

  

*Cultivation Strategy* *(20%)*  

Designs and implements strategic cultivation plans, including events, thought leadership opportunities, ensure timely acknowledgment and ongoing engagement of major donors and personalized outreach to advance prospects toward a meaningful engagement.  

  

*Stakeholder Engagement* *(25%)*  

Prepares regular internal reports and dashboard updates on portfolio activity, pipeline health, revenue forecasting, and major gift progress for senior leadership and cross\-functional planning utilizing our CRM or fundraising databases.  

  

*Internal Reporting \& Pipeline Management* *(15%)*  

Partners with leadership, program teams, and external advisors to present compelling cases for support and maintain alignment with strategic objectives.  

  

*Development Operations \& Financial Coordination* *(5%)*  

Works collaboratively with Finance to ensure timely and accurate recording of gifts and alignment on funding with and without donor restrictions.  

  

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities*** Proven track record of closing major gifts in the $250K\-$1M\+ range.
* Skilled at managing ambiguity and navigating complex stakeholder environments.
* Exceptional relationship\-building, communication, and project management skills.
* Experience in leading cross\-functional teams to advance high\-value opportunities.

**Education and/or Experience*** Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in nonprofit management, business, or related field preferred.
* Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in fundraising, with at least 3 years focused on major gifts or principal gifts.
* Demonstrated success in securing individual gifts of $250K or more.
* Experience managing a portfolio of high\-net\-worth donors and leading cross\-functional fundraising initiatives.

**Work Model/Location**  

This role is available as a remote or hybrid work arrangement, although hybrid is preferred. If hybrid, you are expected to work on\-site in New York City at least 1 day per week on Wednesday, based on Break Through Tech and team needs. If remote, periodic in\-person attendance is required for all\-staff meetings, trainings, retreats, or similar Break Through Tech events.  

  

**Compensation**  

The annual salary range is $135,000 \- $150,000, depending on experience.  

  

**Benefits**  

At Break Through Tech, we care deeply about supporting our employees and their families. We offer a competitive, thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports health, financial wellbeing, and work\-life balance. Eligible employees have access to day\-one medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with tax\-advantaged HSA and FSA options, mental health resources, wellness offerings, commuter benefits, and convenient prescription support. We also provide employer\-paid life insurance, short\- and long\-term disability coverage, and a generous 401(k) benefit with a 10% employer contribution, regardless of employee participation. Additional voluntary benefits and wellbeing programs help support employees and their families both at work and beyond.

Position Summary



Reporting to the Executive Director of the National Synthesis Center for Organismal Resilience (NSCORE), the Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for a federally funded research center by directing all aspects of administration, including financial management, grant administration, human resources, operations, communications, academic governance, and institutional partnerships. Reporting to the Executive Director, the incumbent oversees a $2–5\+ million annual operating budget, supervises administrative staff, ensures compliance with federal and University policies, supports executive leadership and governance activities, and leads special initiatives that advance the Center’s research, education, outreach, and broader impact objectives. The Director serves as the primary administrative liaison among faculty, University offices, funding agencies, and external partners, ensuring effective resource coordination, operational excellence, and successful execution of the Center’s strategic priorities.



Based at Columbia University, NSCORE will inspire, unite, and train organismal biologists and computer scientists in a collaborative effort to leverage vast amounts of real\-world data utilizing advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques to address the growing challenges in understanding and predicting organismal resilience. In collaboration with academic and research institutions across the greater New York City area, North America, Europe, Asia, and beyond, NSCORE will facilitate interdisciplinary synthesis through working groups and conferences that bring together experts and students. Central to NSCORE’s mission is the education and training of the next generation of computational organismal biologists, to be achieved through a hybrid interdisciplinary education program for students and educators, from K\-12 through university. By integrating across diverse disciplines, NSCORE will transform how scientists study and predict organismal responses to change and make recommendations to improve resilience. About Baruch Senior Ministries:  


Baruch Senior Ministries is a faith\-based, nonprofit organization dedicated to honoring God by serving people as they age. If you share our commitment to honoring God through our work and delivering quality care to all our residents, then we invite you to join our team.

The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors, Loan Review Committee, community stakeholders, borrowers, and funding partners to ensure strong portfolio performance and organizational growth.

● Market GIF’s business and housing loan funds and respond to borrower and partner inquiries

● Monitor and service the loan portfolio, including scheduling site visits and housing inspections

● Prepare reports on borrower inquiries, lending activity, and loan repayment schedules

● Lead capitalization efforts for lending pools, including grant solicitation, compliance, and investor relations

● Develop and maintain marketing materials to promote GIF programs and impact

● Represent GIF within the service area and strengthen partnerships with communities and stakeholders

● Complete additional assignments as directed by the Board of Directors

● A strong commitment to housing and economic development

● Demonstrated leadership and organizational management skills

● Strong marketing and relationship\-building abilities

● Experience working with a diverse range of borrowers and community partners

● Excellent written and verbal communication skills

● High initiative and the ability to manage multiple projects effectively

● Strong attention to detail

● Ability to work independently and collaboratively Required:

**About Grow Iowa Foundation** 

Grow Iowa Foundation, Inc. (GIF) is a 501(c)(3\) organization dedicated to strengthening communities across southwest Iowa. jobs.description:
Interim Executive Director (Volunteer)

**North Alabama Zoological Society (NALZS)**

**Location:** North Alabama (Hybrid/Flexible)  
**Position Type:** Volunteer \| Interim (12–18 months)  
**Compensation:** Volunteer (Unpaid)  
**Reports To:** Board of Directors

Help Build the North Alabama Zoo

The North Alabama Zoological Society (NALZS) is seeking an exceptional community leader to serve as our **Interim Executive Director**. NALZS is a volunteer led organization.

This is more than an administrative role. It is an opportunity to help lead one of North Alabama's most exciting community initiatives—bringing a world\-class zoological park to our region.

During a planned executive sabbatical, the Interim Executive Director will become the primary leader responsible for advancing the organization's mission, growing its community presence, strengthening strategic partnerships, expanding fundraising efforts, and helping move the North Alabama Zoo from vision to reality.

Position Summary

The Interim Executive Director serves as the chief operating executive of NALZS and is responsible for leading the organization's daily operations while continuing to grow the organization and build public support for the future North Alabama Zoo.

Working closely with the Board of Directors, the Interim Executive Director will execute the organization's strategic vision, strengthen community partnerships, expand fundraising efforts, and represent NALZS throughout North Alabama.

The President \& CEO will remain available as a strategic advisor and resource but will step away from day\-to\-day leadership, allowing the Interim Executive Director to lead the organization with confidence and authority.

Primary ResponsibilitiesOrganizational Leadership

* Lead the day\-to\-day operations of NALZS.
* Execute the strategic direction established by the Board of Directors.
* Build and develop the executive leadership team and volunteers.
* Ensure the organization continues to grow in capability, professionalism, and effectiveness.
* Provide regular updates and recommendations to the Board of Directors.

Community \& Civic Leadership

* Serve as the public face of NALZS throughout North Alabama.
* Build relationships with local, county, and state elected officials.
* Strengthen partnerships with civic organizations, chambers of commerce, educational institutions, conservation organizations, and community leaders.
* Represent NALZS at public meetings, community events, speaking engagements, and networking opportunities.
* Continue building public awareness and support for the North Alabama Zoo.

Fundraising \& Development

* Cultivate relationships with donors, sponsors, and philanthropic partners.
* Lead fundraising initiatives and sponsorship opportunities.
* Support grant development and donor stewardship.
* Expand the organization's network of supporters, advocates, and corporate partners.

Strategic Growth

* Continue advancing the vision for the North Alabama Zoo.
* Identify opportunities to grow membership, volunteers, partnerships, and organizational influence.
* Help position NALZS for future land acquisition, capital fundraising, and long\-term organizational success.

Time Commitment

This is a volunteer executive leadership position requiring an active, hands\-on commitment.

Candidates should expect to dedicate **20–30 hours per week**, depending on organizational priorities, events, and ongoing initiatives. Work is flexible and self\-directed but will include:

* Daytime meetings with community leaders, donors, elected officials, and partner organizations.
* Evening meetings with the Board of Directors, committees, volunteers, and community groups.
* Weekend attendance at fundraising events, outreach activities, and other organizational functions as needed.
* Regular communication with volunteers, sponsors, and stakeholders throughout the week.

Because much of NALZS's work involves community engagement and relationship building, flexibility in scheduling is essential. Candidates should expect a combination of daytime, evening, and occasional weekend commitments.

Desired Qualifications

* Executive or senior leadership experience in nonprofit, business, government, military, education, or community organizations.
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams, volunteers, and organizational initiatives.
* Strong relationship\-building and networking skills.
* Experience working with boards of directors and volunteers.
* Success in fundraising, business development, public affairs, government relations, or community leadership.
* Financial stewardship and organizational management experience.
* Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills.
* Passion for conservation, education, community development, and building organizations.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who:

* Is a servant leader with integrity and vision.
* Has the flexibility and availability to actively represent NALZS throughout the community.
* Enjoys building relationships with civic leaders, elected officials, businesses, donors, and volunteers.
* Is comfortable speaking publicly and serving as the face of the organization.
* Can organize people, build momentum, and accomplish strategic goals.
* Is collaborative, self\-motivated, and mission\-driven.
* Believes in leaving a lasting legacy for North Alabama.

Why Volunteer?

This is a unique opportunity to help shape one of North Alabama's most ambitious community projects.

As Interim Executive Director, you will help expand an organization dedicated to creating a destination that will educate future generations, inspire wildlife conservation, strengthen tourism, enhance economic development, and improve the quality of life throughout our region.

Your leadership will directly influence the future of the North Alabama Zoo and help turn a shared community vision into reality.

To Apply

Interested candidates should submit:

* A résumé highlighting leadership experience

This is a unique YMCA leadership opportunity. Unlike a traditional branch focused primarily on fitness, aquatics or youth programming, the Binghamton Branch is centered on housing, supportive services, facility operations, and community impact. The YMCA is preparing for a significant housing expansion, and this role will help lead the systems, staffing, partnerships, and operations needed to support that growth.


The Binghamton Branch Executive Director will provide daily leadership and operational oversight for the branch, working closely with the CEO to strengthen housing operations, service delivery, fund development, facility coordination, and community partnerships.

The successful candidate will work closely with the CEO and executive leadership team and may be considered for future advancement opportunities, including long\-term executive succession planning, based on performance, organizational needs, and Board approval.


Qualifications
The ideal candidate will bring:


* A bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, human services, business administration, public administration or a related field; equivalent leadership experience may be considered
* At least five years of progressive leadership or management experience
* Experience in nonprofit organizations, housing, human services, community development or facility\-based operations
* A proven ability to lead staff, manage daily operations and maintain accountability across multiple departments

* Experience developing and maintaining community partnerships

* Oversee the branch’s housing services, gymnasium, fitness center, group exercise offerings and sports leagues, ensuring programs and services are well managed and responsive to community needs.
* Coordinate closely with Finance, Maintenance, Human Resources and Executive Leadership to monitor branch performance, staffing, service delivery, budgets and facility needs.

Balances competing priorities, responds calmly to challenges and makes timely, sound decisions.

We recruit, prepare, and support Black men to enter and thrive in the classroom, strengthening schools and transforming communities in the process. At BMT, we’re reimagining what it means to teach, lead, and belong. Our team is bold, innovative, and deeply rooted in purpose. **Job Summary**
===============


The Manager supports the Office of the Chief Development Officer (CDO), managing workflow, projects, scheduling, and travel planning, and ensuring that internal and external stakeholders receive the information and decisions they need to keep projects on schedule. Working closely with staff across the Development Division, the Manager supports the National Trust’s principal giving donors; organizes Division meetings, retreats, and Board of Trustees materials; supports strategic planning and budgeting; and completes special projects as assigned. This is a support role that requires a level of proactivity as well as excellent communication, data management, interpersonal, and computing skills.**Duties**
==========

***Office of the Chief Development Officer***
---------------------------------------------

* Manages the CDO’s calendar, travel schedule, and daily workflow; helps prioritize tasks based on Division and organizational needs; and coordinates the strategy and logistics of fundraising visits.
* Ensures that communications from the CDO are timely, clear, and responsive, and that stakeholders across the National Trust receive the information and decisions needed to move projects forward.

Description:

Gulfstream Goodwill Industries is a powerful force for transformation in our community. Through housing and shelter options, a career academy, and skill\-based and workforce development programs, Gulfstream Goodwill helps individuals facing disabilities, economic hardship, homelessness, and other significant barriers build meaningful, self\-sufficient lives. Every day, the organization changes the trajectory of lives equipping people with the skills, confidence, and opportunity to thrive as contributing members of our community. Joining the Gulfstream Goodwill team means joining a mission of dignity, second chances, and lasting impact.


The Director of Development will plan, develop, and execute a comprehensive fundraising program for Gulfstream Goodwill Industries aligned with the organization's strategic priorities. With a current fundraising portfolio of $1\.2 million and a five\-year goal of growing philanthropic revenue to $3 million, this position will place primary emphasis on major gift development while building and implementing a multi\-faceted development plan in partnership with organizational leadership and staff. The Director will establish and strengthen relationship management systems for existing and prospective major donors, deepen stewardship practices at all giving levels, and actively identify and cultivate new major donor prospects within a rapidly growing and increasingly philanthropically engaged community.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising plan aligned with the strategic plan and organizational priorities:**


Develop a multi\-year fundraising plan grounded in Gulfstream Goodwill's strategic priorities, with clear annual milestones.


In partnership with the President/CEO and leadership team, set and achieve annual fundraising revenue and activity goals that advance the organization toward a $3 million fundraising goal within five years.


Collaborate and coordinate with organizational leaders and essential staff to implement the fundraising plan.


Oversee a donor database and consistently track current and prospective funder information, engagement history, and key touchpoints.


Produce regular fundraising reports for the President/CEO and Board of Directors.

**Lead major gift development as the primary focus of the fundraising program:**


Personally manage a portfolio of major donor prospects and active donors.


Design and execute individualized strategies for identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of each donor in the portfolio.


Serve as the primary staff partner supporting the President/CEO's donor engagement and portfolio management.


Leverage the organization's growing community to identify philanthropically capable individuals new to the area and expand the major donor pipeline.


Foster relationships with board members, community leaders, business partners, and other organizational contacts to open doors and make meaningful introductions to prospective major donors.


Strategize, prepare for, and participate in gift solicitations at the major gift, leadership gift, and planned giving levels.

**Build and implement robust donor relationship management processes:**


Establish clear protocols for donor outreach, moves management, and timely follow\-up to ensure every relationship is actively cultivated.


Develop and maintain a systematic approach to managing both existing major donors and prospective major donors.


Ensure no relationship falls through the cracks by building accountability structures into the development operation.

**Champion a culture of donor stewardship at all giving levels:**


Design and execute meaningful stewardship strategies that acknowledge, recognize, and engage donors at every level of giving.


Deepen donors' connection to the mission of Gulfstream Goodwill through personalized, mission\-rich communications and experiences.


Ensure donors at all levels feel valued and connected to the organization's impact.

**Build event strategies that lead to new donor development:**


Collaborate with event staff to identify and prioritize major donor prospects attending organizational events.


Develop strategies to engage event participants as prospective donors and deepen relationships with existing donors through event experiences.


Ensure meaningful, timely follow\-up with event attendees to convert engagement into lasting philanthropic relationships.


Coordinate with the board to maximize their role in cultivating donor relationships through and beyond special events.

**Activate and support board members as philanthropic ambassadors:**


Help cultivate a vibrant culture of philanthropy among Goodwill board members and organizational leadership.


Provide training, tools, and strategies to help board members open doors to their networks and make personal asks on behalf of the organization.


Work closely with board members to identify prospects within their spheres of influence and develop strategies for engagement.

**Develop a planned giving program to create opportunities for legacy giving:**


Create and maintain a legacy giving society.


Develop a marketing plan to promote planned giving opportunities to donors, board members, and prospects.


Integrate planned giving conversations in major gift development.


Facilitate personalized stewardship for planned giving donors.

**Collaborate with staff to execute a comprehensive, multi\-channel annual giving program:**


Partner with organizational staff to implement annual giving campaigns utilizing direct mail, online giving, and other donor communications.


Support foundation and corporate grant strategies in collaboration with relevant staff and leadership.


Develop and coordinate planned giving efforts as part of a comprehensive development strategy.

**Develop a compelling Case for Support:**


Create a Case for Support that clearly articulates the mission, impact, and vision of Gulfs

**Job Title:** Chief Executive Officer

 **Tier:** 5

 **Type of Position:** Full\-Time, Regular

 **Schedule:** (TBD by Supervisor)

 **Location:** Anchorage, AK

 **Travel Requirements:** Frequent travel required

 **FLSA Classification:** Exempt

Job OVERVIEW


The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the senior executive leader of Gana\-A'Yoo Limited and is responsible for leading the organization's strategic direction, financial performance, operational effectiveness, and long\-term sustainability. Reporting directly to the Boad of Directors, the CEO works closely with the Board to advance the Corporation's mission, drive growth, and create lasting value for Alaska Native shareholders.


The CEO is responsible for balancing growth and profitability with the Corporation's mission to create lasting value for its Alaska Native shareholders and communities. This executive will build and lead a high\-performing leadership team, foster a culture of accountability and integrity, and ensure the Corporation and its subsidiaries operate in a manner consistent with its values, strategic priorities, and fiduciary responsibilities.


The ideal candidate is an experienced executive with a proven track record of leading complex organizations, driving sustainable growth, managing diverse stakeholder relationships, and navigating the unique opportunities and responsibilities associated with an Alaska Native Corporation.


Job specific competencies

* Strategic Leadership – Ability to develop and execute a long\-term vision that drives sustainable growth, profitability, and organizational success while aligning with shareholder and Board objectives.
* Financial Stewardship – Demonstrates strong financial acumen and accountability in managing corporate assets, budgets, investments, and resources to ensure long\-term financial health and shareholder value.
* Corporate Governance – Understands and supports effective governance practices by working collaboratively with the Board of Directors, ensuring transparency, compliance, and adherence to corporate policies.
* Organizational Development – Builds and leads high\-performing teams by fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, employee engagement, and continuous professional growth.
* Change Management – Effectively leads organizations through growth, transformation, and evolving business environments while maintaining focus on strategic priorities and operational effectiveness.
* Stakeholder Engagement – Develops and maintains productive relationships with shareholders, board members, employees, business partners, community leaders, government agencies, and other key stakeholders.
* Cultural Awareness and Stewardship – Demonstrates respect for and commitment to Alaska Native values, traditions, and culture while balancing business objectives with shareholder and community interests.
* Ethical Leadership – Leads with integrity, honesty, and accountability, fostering trust and ensuring decisions are made in the best interests of the Corporation and its shareholders.
* Communication and Influence – Communicates effectively with diverse audiences, builds consensus, and influences decision\-making through clear, transparent, and persuasive leadership.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**Board and Shareholder Relations**

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors and corporate management.
* Keep the Board informed of the Corporation's performance, opportunities, risks, and strategic initiatives requiring attention or action.
* Provide timely, transparent, and solution\-oriented communication regarding risks, opportunities, and organizational performance.
* Collaborate with the Board to develop and execute the Corporation's strategic goals and objectives.
* Foster positive relationships with shareholders and promote initiatives that support long\-term shareholder value.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Develop and implement the Corporation's long\-term strategic vision to ensure sustainable growth and profitability.
* Identify and pursue opportunities that strengthen the Corporation's portfolio and competitive position.
* Lead organizational planning and change initiatives that align business operations with Board directives and shareholder interests.
* Promote a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Model ethical leadership and demonstrate a commitment to Gana\-A'Yoo Limited's mission, vision, and Alaska Native heritage.

**Operational and Financial Management**

* Provide leadership and oversight for all corporate operations and subsidiary activities.
* Directly supervise senior leadership, including the CFO, COO, and other key executives.
* Establish organizational priorities and ensure resources are effectively allocated to achieve strategic objectives.
* Monitor operational and financial performance through measurable goals, reporting, and accountability.
* Develop budgets for Board review and approval.
* Ensure prudent management of corporate assets and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies.

**Decision Making and Governance**

* Analyze and apply financial, operational, and market information to guide sound business decisions.
* Develop recommendations for the Board regarding corporate strategy, policy, investments, and growth opportunities.
* Ensure effective risk management practices are in place to protect Gana\-A'Yoo Limited's assets and reputation.

**External Relations**

* Serve as the Corporation's chief representative and spokesperson.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with business partners, government agencies, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
* Promote a positive public image and increase awareness of the Corporation's accomplishments, mission, and impact.
* Advocate for opportunities that advance the interests of the Corporation and its shareholders.

**Overview**

**ABOUT KAUAI PHILIPPINE CULTURAL CENTER**

The Kauai Philippine Cultural Center (KPCC) is a 501(c)(3\) non\-profit organization whose mission is “to provide, promote and enhance cultural, economic, educational training and social programs as well as cross cultural exchanges in our multi\-ethnic environment.”

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Executive Director (ED) is the chief administrative and operating officer of the KPCC. The ED provides leadership, strategic direction, and day\-to\-day management to ensure the organization fulfills its mission.

The ideal ED will have strong leadership, strategic thinking, financial acumen, fundraising expertise, and exceptional communication skills. The ED will be aligned with achieving KPCC’s mission and have the ability to communicate the mission to donors and customers, build rapport, manage stress in a fast\-paced environment, and navigate through change. Furthermore, the executive director will grow the KPCC’s revenue and expand the number of users, develop a membership program, and maintain a self\-sustaining facility to shift management away from the KPCC’s board of directors and corporate officers.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Organizational Leadership \& Strategy**

* Engage and report to the Board of Directors (Board). Implement the mission, vision, and strategic goals set by the Board
* Set goals and pivot when faced with adversity. Be able to provide timely and confident decision\-making, especially in times of crises.
* Provide leadership in program development and community engagement
* Serve as the public face, spokesperson, representative of KPCC, building partnerships, managing external communications, engaging with the public and officials at events/meetings.
* Create, maintain, and strengthen partnerships with schools, cultural groups, nonprofits, and government agencies
* Develop and implement long\-range goals and annual work plans in collaboration with the Board of Directors.
* Manage day\-to\-day operations, including but not limited to human resources, program delivery, administrative systems, staffing the Center.

**2\. Program \& Event Management**

* Plan, oversee, and coordinate cultural, educational, and social programs including cross\-cultural exchanges, Filipino Cultural Experiences, youth programs, and other relevant events benefiting the Kauai community in collaboration with volunteer committees
* Develop innovative new programs and partnerships. Evaluate and report on program effectiveness.
* Ensure compliance with safety and permitting requirements

**3\. Facility \& Rental Operations**

* Manage the KPCC facility and grounds; coordinate maintenance and vendor services

**4\. Financial Management and Compliance**

* Proficiency in budget development and management. Monitor revenues, expenses, and cash flow

* Increase revenue through facility use, donor cultivation and solicitation, and grant writing.
* Ensure grant budgets/requirements are followed as required in agreements or contracts
* Assist with financial review or audits

**5\. Fundraising \& Development**

* Work in collaboration with Fundraising Committee, Board of Directors, and other volunteers to create and sustain a robust fund development program and meet or exceed fundraising goals
* Lead fundraising efforts and carry out fund development projects and tasks as required

* Research and solicit funders – individual, government, foundation, and corporate – in order to generate required contributed revenue to sustain the organization

**Position Overview**

The Director of Advancement is a visionary relationship builder and strategic fundraising leader responsible for advancing the mission and long\-term sustainability of St. Andrew's Schools through philanthropy, community engagement, and institutional partnerships.

Working closely with the Head of School, Board of Trustees, and Administrative Leadership Team, the Director develops and executes a comprehensive advancement strategy that inspires generosity, deepens constituent engagement, and secures philanthropic support for the school's strategic priorities. This leader cultivates meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, grandparents, foundations, corporations, community leaders, and friends of the school while fostering a vibrant culture of philanthropy grounded in Queen Emma's legacy of compassion, service, and educational opportunity.

Above all, the Director of Advancement understands that philanthropy is about people, purpose, and relationships. Successful fundraising begins with listening, building trust, and helping donors connect their passions with opportunities to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students.

This leader will help ensure that the generosity of today's donors creates life\-changing opportunities for tomorrow's students, strengthening the school for generations to come.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**Director of Development**

**Behind Every Door \| Dallas, TX**

Behind Every Door is a mission driven nonprofit dedicated to bringing hope, opportunity and community transformation to children, teens and families in Dallas. We create spaces where people can thrive through relationship based programs, supportive services and meaningful partnerships.

**Help Build What's Next**

Behind Every Door is looking for a strategic, relationship\-driven leader to help build the next chapter of our Development Department.

The Director of Development serves as the **execution leader and integrator** of the Development Department, translating strategy into action while cultivating meaningful relationships that inspire long\-term investment in Behind Every Door's mission.

Working alongside the Vice President of Development, this role helps transform vision into measurable results by building fundraising strategies, strengthening donor relationships, leading campaign execution, and establishing the systems and structure that will support the organization's next season of growth.

This is a unique opportunity for someone who enjoys building, thinking creatively, and leading with both strategy and execution. If you're energized by creating meaningful donor experiences, growing philanthropic partnerships, and helping shape a high\-performing development department, we'd love to meet you.

**What You'll BuildRevenue Strategies That Grow the Mission**

Lead the execution of fundraising strategies that strengthen and grow each of Behind Every Door's philanthropic revenue streams, including individual giving, major gifts, grants and foundations, corporate partnerships, church partnerships, annual campaigns, and special fundraising initiatives. Working closely with the Vice President of Development, you'll help turn strategy into measurable results.

**Meaningful Donor Relationships**

Cultivate and steward a portfolio of donor and partner relationships while creating intentional opportunities for people to engage more deeply with the mission. You'll help design thoughtful donor journeys through stewardship, tours, cultivation experiences, and personalized engagement that inspires long\-term partnership.

**Execution That Moves the Department Forward**

Serve as the integrator of the Development Department by creating accountability, managing priorities, and ensuring fundraising initiatives move forward with consistency and excellence. You'll help establish the rhythms, systems, and structure that allow a growing department to thrive.

**Collaboration That Strengthens the Mission**

Partner closely with the Vice President of Development, Director of Communications, program leaders, Finance, and our contract grant writer to align fundraising strategy, storytelling, donor communications, grant efforts, and campaign execution. Success in this role depends on strong collaboration and a shared commitment to excellence.

**Building the Future**

Help lay the foundation for a scalable Development Department by refining processes, strengthening fundraising systems, and preparing the department for future growth. As the organization grows, you'll play a key role in mentoring future team members and helping shape a collaborative, relationship\-centered culture.

**What We're Looking For**

We're looking for someone who enjoys building as much as leading. You are a relationship\-builder, a strategic thinker, and a strong executor who naturally brings organization, momentum, and follow\-through to every initiative.

You likely bring:

* Five or more years of nonprofit development or fundraising leadership experience.
* Success managing multiple fundraising strategies and revenue streams.
* Experience cultivating donor, corporate, church, and foundation relationships.
* Strong project management and organizational skills.
* Experience with donor CRM systems and using data to guide decision\-making.
* Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across departments.
* A proactive, creative, and solution\-oriented leadership style.
* A passion for building teams, systems, and meaningful donor relationships.
* Alignment with the Christ\-centered mission, Statement of Faith, and core values of Behind Every Door, with the ability to authentically communicate how faith shapes our work and relationships.

**What Success Looks Like**

In this role, success means:

* Fundraising campaigns are executed with excellence and achieve annual revenue goals.
* Donor engagement, stewardship, and retention continue to grow.
* Relationships with donors, corporations, churches, and foundations become deeper and more strategic.
* Fundraising strategies are strengthened across every philanthropic revenue stream.
* The Development Department becomes increasingly organized, scalable, and prepared for future growth.
* The Vice President of Development is empowered to focus on transformational relationships, board engagement, and long\-term philanthropic strategy.

**Why This Role Matters**

At Behind Every Door, we believe relationships are our greatest resource. Every campaign, every conversation, and every act of stewardship is an opportunity to invite others into God's work of bringing hope, belonging, and transformation to the Cedar Crest community.

The Director of Development is more than a fundraiser—they are a builder. This role helps create the leadership capacity, fundraising infrastructure, and relationship strategies that position Behind Every Door for its next season of growth.

In two years, success won't simply be measured by dollars raised. It will be reflected in a stronger development department, deeper partnerships, healthier fundraising systems, and a growing community of people who are committed to investing in lasting transformation through Behind Every Door.

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Sabbatical
* Vision insurance

Pay: $70,0
