Who We Are

Founded in 1991, Sunnyside Foundation is an education and community foundation built by graduates of Sunnyside Unified School District (SUSD). The Sunnyside Foundation champions Tucson's southside by investing in education, community support, and partnerships that uplift students, strengthen families, and help neighbors thrive together.

Our vision is a community where every southside family has the capacity to cultivate their own learning opportunities throughout their lifetime. We focus on enriching our community by making resources available year-round that bring knowledge, opportunity, and insight to those who volunteer, donate, or receive any type of assistance.

We are uniquely positioned at the intersection of education, community, and policy, and we're growing. With a new strategic plan on the horizon, this is an extraordinary moment to step into leadership at Sunnyside Foundation.

The Opportunity

The Sunnyside Foundation is seeking its next Chief Executive Officer to build on a strong foundation and lead the organization into its next chapter of impact.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a beloved, mission-driven organization with deep community roots, a growing portfolio of programs and partnerships, a news strategic plan, and real momentum continuing to expand our footprint in the community. This momentum includes the Juntos Fund, a landmark $1 million scholarship endowment and an expanding partnership with the University of Arizona.

The incoming CEO will inherit a financially healthy organization with an annual operating budget of approximately $1.3 million and three priority funds: Excellence in Education, Emergency Relief, and Community Investment. Sunnyside Foundation has a committed board, a talented team, and a community that has shown up year after year. This role calls for a leader who will honor that legacy, deepen those roots, and grow boldly from them.

Vision for the CEO

The incoming CEO should be passionate about working with our southside partners, leveraging the broader Tucson community, and optimizing internal infrastructure to grow education and community funds that are equitable and transformative.

We are looking for a leader who leads from within the community, someone who understands the southside not as a geography, but as a people. A leader who brings urgency and care in equal measure, who can cultivate donors and hold space for families receiving food assistance, who can navigate a board meeting and roll up their sleeves at a community cleanup. Someone who sees the new strategic plan as their first major act of co-creation with the community.

Our Programs & Partnerships

The CEO will oversee and grow three core funding areas and a rich network of community partnerships:

Excellence in Education Fund

This Fund invests in students and educators at every stage of the educational journey, from scholarships for graduating seniors and dual enrollment students to Career and Technical Education investments and the Tri-School Partnership, which strengthens pathways to college. It also supports educators through classroom mini-grants and professional development via Sunnyside CommunityShare. A scholarship endowment secured in FY25 anchors the Fund for generations to come.

Emergency Relief Fund

This Fund meets families' most essential needs through monthly food distributions, utility assistance, and direct cash support for households in crisis. Through the Juntos Fund, we provide assistance to undocumented and mixed-status households for legal fees, emergency expenses, education, and mental health support.

Community Investment Fund

This Fund supports community-led improvement across Tucson's southside through partnerships with FUGA, Regeneración, the Gabe Gallegos Memorial Foundation, and the University of Arizona Southside Engagements program. In FY 26, through From our Families for our Futures, funded by the City of Tucson, 3,100 residents came together for youth programming, bike rides, cleanups, and neighborhood reinvestment events, building a lasting sense of belonging and connection.

Gives Week

Annual community fundraising campaign, Gives Week 2025 raised $126,103 with 286 Burrito Run participants, 500 Health & Wellness Fair attendees, 116 volunteers, and 350 guests at the Block Party. A cornerstone of our donor community and organizational culture.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategic Planning
Lead the development and execution of a new multi-year, community-centered strategic plan in partnership with the Board, staff, and community stakeholders
Provide visionary, values-aligned leadership that advances Sunnyside Foundation's mission across education, emergency relief, and community investment priority funding areas
Serve as the Foundation's primary spokesperson, engaging public, civic, and donor partners on behalf of its mission and the people it serves.
Continue to grow a culture of learning, accountability, and belonging within the organization
Fundraising & Development
Lead and grow the Foundation's community-centered fundraising strategy, including Gives Week, individual donor cultivation, corporate partnerships, and grants
Steward and grow existing donor relationships; cultivate new donors in alignment with the Foundation's values and community-first approach
Collaboratively write grants and raise dollars with partner organizations for students, teachers, and families on Tucson's southside
Oversee and continue expanding the $1 million scholarship endowment and other legacy giving opportunities
Create fundraising events that are accessible, community-celebrating, and fun, in the spirit of Gives Week
Fiscal Management
Oversee the full organizational P&L; ensure budget is met or exceeded annually
Manage expenses within budget; work directly with CPAs on annual reviews and accounting needs
Report monthly financial progress to the Board of Directors
Ensure long-term fiscal sustainability through diversified revenue streams and responsible stewardship of the endowment
Community Relationships & Partnerships
Build and maintain deep relationships with SUSD leadership, community-based organizations, policymakers, philanthropic partners, civic leaders and stakeholders
Ensure Sunnyside Foundation maintains its accessible, warm, and encouraging brand; show up at events large and small
Grow and deepen strategic partnerships, including FUGA, Regeneración, Gabe Gallegos Memorial Foundation, the University of Arizona Southside Engagements, and others
Seek and cultivate media, marketing, and co-sponsorship opportunities that amplify the Foundation's presence and reach in partnership with SF's Communications Manager
Work closely with SUSD leadership to develop collaborative programs and funds for teachers, students, and families
Team Management & Culture
Directly supervise the Director of Operations and Communications & Outreach Manager
Foster a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging; maintain high staff morale and retention
Set clear organizational goals and support staff in achieving them; conduct meaningful annual performance conversations
Board Relations & Governance
Partner closely with the Board of Directors to advance the strategic vision; provide monthly updates on progress toward objectives and budget
Support board recruitment and cultivation; ensure the board has the information and engagement needed to govern effectively
Respond to board inquiries with transparency and timeliness
Compliance & Risk Management
Ensure the Foundation maintains good standing and complies with all applicable local, state, and federal laws
Maintain appropriate organizational protections and policies to mitigate risk
Oversee proper administration of the scholarship endowment, Juntos Fund, and all restricted funds

Reports to:
Board of Directors

Staff Size:
SF team is composed of 4.75 FTE staff, including a CEO, Program Manager, Communications & Outreach Manager, Operations & Administrative Coordinator, and a Director of Operations. Accounting services are provided through an external contractor.

Location:
Sunnyside Foundation is headquartered at the SUSD Los Ranchitos Office, currently working remotely half the week.

Employment Type:
Full-time, exempt

Compensation:
Pay Range: $90,000- $110,000; commensurate with experience.

Benefits:

100% employer-covered health care insurance for individual employee; dependent coverage available at employee cost

Voluntary vision and dental plans available

Simple IRA plan with a 2% employer contribution

18 paid holidays

Paid time off: up to 80 hours annually, with incremental increases depending on years of service. PTO is accrued each pay period.

Sick leave: up to 24 hours annually. Hours are accrued each pay period.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Sunnyside Foundation is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity in our workplace and we hire the most qualified candidates without regard for age, ethnicity, gender, gender identity or expression, language differences, nationality or national origin, family or marital status, physical, mental, and developmental abilities (or the perception of a disability), genetic information, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, skin color, social or economic class, education, work and behavioral styles, political affiliation, military service, caste, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will be a dynamic, strategic, collaborative leader, committed to the vision and mission of Sunnyside Foundation, with demonstrated leadership and fundraising experience in the non-profit sector. The following will generally define the ideal candidate:

Community-Focused: the ability to lead the organization from behind and from within the community. Experience working in coalitions, grassroots organizations, committees, and other collaborative settings.
We especially welcome bilingual candidates with authentic ties to Tucson’s southside, those who have lived here, served here, or have family in our geographic serving area.

Creative Problem Solver: the ability to simultaneously think big, lead with urgency and aspirations, and understand reality and the bold moves needed to strengthen pathways that bring funding into our community.
Demonstrated racial equity and inclusion competencies: ability to manage a growing team, stakeholders, and partners with a racial equity and inclusive lens.
Fundraising: Proven fundraising ability with corporate, foundation, and individual donors coupled with a skill set to think long-term sustainability. Experience writing grants and/or overseeing grant writing staff or consultants.
Authentic Communicator: A skilled listener and storyteller who communicates with clarity, warmth, and conviction to diverse internal and external audiences including board and staff members, business, policymakers, philanthropic partners, and social sector leaders.

How to apply

For the highest level of consideration, please submit your cover letter and resume to: recruiting@xmarksthespotconsulting.com by Wednesday August 12, 2026

jobs.description:
**Organization Overview**


GreenLight Fund is a national nonprofit with a local focus that partners with communities to create opportunities for inclusive prosperity.  

  

We facilitate a community\-driven process that matches the local needs of individuals and families not met by existing programs, to organizations with track records of success elsewhere. Working with communities, we identify, invite in and launch proven organizations, providing collaborative support so they can quickly take root and deliver change. Everything we do is designed to remove barriers to inclusive prosperity all too often rooted in racial inequities. Our impact increases exponentially as we address one specific, community\-identified need each year, in each GreenLight site.  

  

To date, we have brought 63 evidence\-based portfolio organizations across 14 sites, invested $41M, and attracted an additional $364M from other funding sources, reaching nearly 1\.3M individuals and families this past year alone.

  

To learn more about the GreenLight Fund, please visit www.greenlightfund.org.

**Position Overview**


The Manager, Office of the CEO will help strengthen the effectiveness of GreenLight’s Office of the CEO by supporting planning, coordination, communication, and follow\-through on key organizational priorities. This role works closely with the Chief of Staff and CEO to help move important work forward across the Board of Directors, National Advisory Council, Executive Team, Leadership Team, annual planning, and cross\-functional projects.


This is a strong fit for someone who is highly organized, thoughtful, proactive, and able to turn ideas and conversations into clear plans, strong materials, and next steps. The Manager will help ensure that the Office of the CEO is operating with clarity, alignment, and follow\-through as GreenLight continues to grow. The Manager reports directly to the Chief of Staff.

**Key Areas of Responsibility**

### *Strategic Planning and Project Support*

* Support the Chief of Staff in moving key Office of the CEO priorities from idea to execution.
* Create project plans, timelines, trackers, meeting agendas, and follow\-up systems.
* Help coordinate cross\-functional work by clarifying next steps, owners, deadlines, and dependencies.
* Track progress against key priorities and surface risks, gaps, or decisions that need attention.
* Support annual planning, organizational goal\-setting, progress reviews, and related follow\-up.

### *Executive Communications and Materials*

* Develop clear, polished presentations, reports, memos, briefings, and meeting materials for internal and external audiences.

* Help prepare the CEO and Chief of Staff for important meetings and conversations.
* Ensure materials are accurate, well\-organized, and aligned with GreenLight’s priorities and voice.

### *Board, National Advisory Council, and External Stakeholder Support*

* Support planning and coordination for Board of Directors, National Advisory Council, and external stakeholder meetings.
* Manage timelines for agendas, pre\-read materials, meeting preparation, follow\-up, and documentation.
* Coordinate with internal team members to gather content and prepare high\-quality materials.
* Support onboarding, engagement, and follow\-up processes for Board and National Advisory Council members.
* Partner with the Office of the CEO Coordinator on scheduling, logistics, materials distribution, and meeting support.

### *Executive Team and Leadership Team Support*

* Support the planning and follow\-up for Executive Team and Leadership Team meetings.
* Help develop agendas, organize materials, track decisions, and monitor follow\-up items.
* Help ensure leadership team meetings are connected to organizational priorities and key decisions.
* Help identify themes, questions, or issues that need additional attention from the Chief of Staff or CEO.

### *Office of the CEO Operations and Collaboration*

* Help improve Office of the CEO systems, templates, trackers, and recurring workflows.
* Partner closely with the Office of the CEO Coordinator to ensure strong coordination between strategic priorities and operational execution.
* Build strong working relationships across GreenLight to support collaboration, clarity, and timely follow\-through.
* Take on special projects as assigned by the Chief of Staff.

jobs.title: Chief Communications Officer
jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, US
jobs.description:
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory invites visionary, accomplished communications leaders to apply for the role of **Chief Communications Officer** (CCO)—a rare opportunity to shape the voice and reputation of one of the world's premier scientific research institutions. The CCO will lead Berkeley Lab's strategic communications function and help advance the Laboratory's mission of delivering science solutions to the world's greatest challenges.

  



Reporting directly to the Laboratory Director and serving as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief Communications Officer is a trusted strategic advisor who partners closely with senior leaders to advance Berkeley Lab's scientific, operational, fiscal, cultural, and reputational goals. Leading the 17\-person Strategic Communications Office, the CCO will develop and execute a bold, integrated communications strategy that elevates the Laboratory's global profile, strengthens engagement with the U.S. Department of Energy, the University of California, policymakers, scientific collaborators, employees, and surrounding communities, and reinforces Berkeley Lab's position as a world leader in scientific innovation.

  



This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a modern, enterprise\-wide communications organization, inspire a high\-performing team, and shape compelling narratives that showcase groundbreaking research, operational excellence, organizational culture, and public impact. The successful candidate will foster trust across diverse stakeholders, lead through moments of opportunity and complexity, and ensure Berkeley Lab's voice reflects its enduring commitment to scientific excellence, innovation, service, and stewardship.

  



**About Berkeley Lab:**

  



At Berkeley Lab, our collective purpose is to serve humankind through science. A Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), Berkeley Lab is a U.S. Dept. of Energy Office of Science national laboratory managed by the University of California . Founded in 1931 on the belief that the biggest problems are best addressed by teams, Berkeley Lab and its scientists have been recognized with 17 Nobel Prizes to date. We conduct groundbreaking research focused on discovery science and solutions for abundant and reliable energy supplies, performed by teams whose expertise spans materials, chemistry, physics, biology, earth and environmental science, mathematics, and computing. jobs.title: Senior Director / Executive Director, Medical Affairs
jobs.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast\-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with **neffy®**, the first and only FDA\-approved needle\-free epinephrine product. If you're motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.



ARS Pharma is committed to improving patients' lives and building healthier communities. We foster a culture of inclusivity, integrity, and creativity as we pursue solutions for patients and families affected by severe allergic reactions. Our product, neffy™, is a needle\-free, low\-dose intranasal epinephrine nasal spray rescue medication for people with Type 1 severe allergic reactions. Headquartered in San Diego, CA, ARS Pharma invites you to join our team and help make a meaningful difference for millions.


**The Opportunity**



In this role, you will inspire and lead the Medical Affairs function, guiding Medical Science Liaisons and broader teams while fostering trusted scientific relationships with Key Opinion Leaders, healthcare practitioners, medical societies, and other stakeholders. You will oversee medical information, medical education, HEOR, publication planning, lifecycle management, launch strategy, and the development and approval of promotional and non promotional medical materials. Working cross\-functionally, you will be a partner with internal teams, serve on the Promotional Review Committee, and ensure Medical Affairs activities are conducted with scientific rigor, operational excellence, and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and company policies.


**ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES**


* **Medical Affairs Strategy \& Operations**: Develops systems and processes to support an integrated, compliant Medical Affairs function across investigational and marketed products. Ensure compliance with corporate policies and procedures, as well as all related healthcare laws and regulations.
* **Medical Education \& Information**: Builds and executes a cohesive medical education and information strategy, including HEOR models, to support corporate and brand objectives.
* **Team Leadership**: Hires, leads, coaches, and develops a high\-performing Medical Affairs team that promotes excellence, collaboration, and accountability. Assure that the highest quality, ethical \& professional values are demonstrated in all aspects of the team's work.
* **External Scientific Engagement**: Builds trusted scientific partnerships with KOLs, medical societies, and other stakeholders through therapeutic insights and scientific education.
* **Evidence Generation \& Publications**: Provides strategic input into company\-initiated and investigator\-initiated studies, manages the medical education agency, coordinates publication strategy, and reviews manuscripts and abstracts as needed.
* **Educational Materials \& Stakeholder Collaboration**: Partners with internal and external stakeholders to develop and approve medically accurate, appropriate educational materials for providers and patients
* **Budget \& Resource Management**: Manages the Medical Affairs budget and ensures effective allocation of resources.


**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**:


* **Medical Affairs Leadership:** Proven ability to build a Medical Affairs function with strong strategic and operational capabilities, including experience overseeing product launches and lifecycle management activities.
* **Scientific and Therapeutic Expertise**: Knowledge of Type 1 severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, is a plus. Broad understanding of product development, clinical trial design, regulatory requirements, payer landscape, pharmaceutical development, and healthcare environment.
* **Strategic Execution**: Excellent strategic thinking skills, with the ability to develop plans, translate ideas into action, manage multiple priorities, identify resource needs, drive work to completion, prepare reports, and evaluate results.
* **Relationship Building**: Partner with Legal and Compliance to ensure Medical Affairs activities are conducted according to company policies and procedures, and in a manner compliant with all external laws and regulations. Demonstrated ability to develop credible peer\-to\-peer relationships with medical experts, decision makers, and key customer stakeholders.
* **Communication and Presentation**: Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex scientific concepts, deliver and tailor presentations to the audience, engage participants, and adapt to last\-minute changes.
* **Scientific Communication**: Experience with scientific presentations, medical writing, and biostatistics.
* **Work Style**: Self\-directed, hands\-on, and able to work independently with urgency in a fast\-paced, entrepreneurial environment.


**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**:


* Will consider a MD, PhD, or PharmD, or other relevant advanced degree in life sciences, medicine, or a related field required; equivalent experience, including academia experience, may be considered in lieu of degree requirements.
* At least 10 years of experience in medical affairs or clinical research.
* At least 8 years of progressive experience leading a Medical Affairs function in biotechnology or pharmaceuticals with no less than 6 years directly managing teams and people.
* Experience in the U.S. health care marketplace required.
* Deep expertise in scientific communications, external expert engagement, medical strategy, and cross functional collaboration.
* Strong understanding of Medical Affairs compliance and best practices.
* Must be available outside normal business hours (8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.) during the workweek and occasionally on weekends. Field engagement, through travel or virtual meetings, is required up to 50% of the time.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality and operate with the highest ethical standards and professionalism.

jobs.title: Executive Director of Facilities
jobs.description:
Responsible for overseeing the operation, maintenance, and managerial oversight of multiple buildings (operational (open 24/7/365\) and residential); implementing policies, procedures, and programs that will assure well\-managed, well\-maintained buildings and equipment; leading staff in a positive service response to the concerns and needs of employees and tenants; providing assurance of safety concerns, quality programs, NYC code compliance and policy compliance, in coordination and conjunction with the company goals. This position serves as an exemplary leader and develops and maintains excellent working relationships with AMC employees/tenants, the community, and regulatory and city and state agencies. The ED assumes financial accountability, people management of direct reports, manages key performance indicators, and executes the strategic directives of AMC.


### **Key Responsibilities**


* Maintains complete responsibility and oversight of day\-to\-day operations of hospital and other facilities, ensuring that all services are effectively delivered and building needs are met including, custodial, life\-safety, housing, security, risk management, engineering, and general and preventative maintenance (including medical equipment); ensures that staff implements and provides these services in a manner consistent with the policies, goals, and objectives.
* Provides leadership in programming, budgeting, and full oversight of campus capital program instantiates annually.
* In collaboration with Finance identify campus utilities reduction opportunities and operational efficiency.
* Directly oversees campus asset NYC code compliance and regulatory compliance to NYC Local Laws.
* Provide exemplary leadership to management team including prioritization, direction, development, and assessment.
* Implementing policies, procedures and programs that will assure well\-managed, well\-maintained buildings and equipment
* Lead staff in a positive service response to the concerns and needs of employees and tenants
* Provide assurance of safety concerns, quality programs, NYC code compliance and policy compliance, in coordination and conjunction with the organization's goals.
* Lead, develop, maintain an excellent working relationships with employees, tenants, the community, and regulatory and city and state agencies.
* Assumes financial accountability, people management of direct reports, manages key performance indicators and executes the strategic directives of the organization.
* Oversee the planning and operation of facilities in emergency response situations, disaster preparedness, and emergency notification programs.
* Advises C\-Suite leadership on operational improvement goals and activities.
* Develop and maintain strong rapport with employees and tenants to elicit feedback for continuous improvement ensuring organizational effectiveness.
* Assure organization\-wide compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws, ordinances, and codes relating to the operation and safety of facilities and staff; assures mandated inspections and repairs of fire safety/suppression systems and other such systems are completed, as required.
* Develop and maintain a house\-wide preventative maintenance program.
* Oversee Biomedical vendor and annual assessment of in\-house feasibility.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
--------------------------------


* Oversees all Building Operations (5 FTEs), Environmental Services (15 FTEs), and Housing (3 FTEs).
	+ 510 east 62nd Street – Main Hospital – 75,000 square feet.
	+ 320 East 53rd Street – Resident\\Intern Housing – 60,000 square feet.
	+ 425 East 61st Street – Leased Office\\Administrative Space – 5,000 square feet.
	+ 425 East 61st Street – Leased Storage Space – 1,000 square feet.
	+ 1113 York Avenue – Leased Veterinary Care Space – 2,500 square feet

**Required Skills/Abilities**
-----------------------------


* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Excellent interpersonal and conflict resolution skills.
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills in qualitative and quantitative research.
* Proficient in Excel, Microsoft office, and other certifications as required by the Schwarzman Animal Medical Center.
* On\-call; after\-hours and emergency response availability when needed.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------


* BA degree in Business Management, Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or Facility Management from an accredited college or university.
* Ten (10\) years of management level work experience that has demonstrated effective leadership, technical knowledge, communication, and interpersonal skills, including understanding of and experience in budgeting, staff supervision, construction \& facility management, procurement, OSHA, ADA codes \& regulations, program development and project management at a multi\-building organization.
* Hospital and/or healthcare facility management (preferred).

**Physical Requirements:**
--------------------------


* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, and taste or smell.
* Employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

**Benefits Package Includes**
-----------------------------


* Competitive salary
* Generous paid time off
* 50% discount on veterinary care
* Continuing education funds with rollover options
* 403(b) matching
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
* You may be eligible for The Public Loan Service Forgiveness Program as we are a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit employer

jobs.title: Executive Director - Mukti Mission US
jobs.description:
Executive Director \- Mukti Mission US
The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Mukti Mission US is the public face of MMUS, and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission, strengthening donor and ministry partnerships, overseeing operations, and providing leadership for fundraising, communications, and organizational development. The Executive Director reports directly to the US Board of Directors and works collaboratively with donors, churches, volunteers, ministry partners, and Mukti Mission leadership in India.  

  

  



**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**  

**Leadership and Administration**

* Provide leadership for the day\-to\-day operations of Mukti Mission US.
* Recruit, train, supervise, coordinate, and support paid staff.
* Responsible for staff culture, performance management, and leadership development.
* Create annual goals, plans, and priorities consistent with the mission and direction established by the Board. Responsible for strategic planning and execution with measurable goals.
* Ensure effective administrative systems, policies, and procedures.

**Fundraising and Donor Development**

* Develop and implement strategies to increase financial support for Mukti Mission.
* Cultivate and maintain relationships with individual donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and ministry partners, with a focus on expanding the donor base and strengthening long\-term giving. Also, responsible for spearheading fundraising campaigns.
* Encourage engagement through prayer, giving, advocacy, and volunteer service.
* Manage CRM database \& integrate donation platform to website for funding campaigns.

**Partnership and International Relations**

* Serve as the primary liaison between Mukti Mission US and Mukti Mission in India, and facilitate communication and partnership while respecting the governance and leadership structures of Mukti Mission in India.
* Maintain current knowledge of ministry activities, projects, and priorities in India.
* Foster collaborative relationships with international councils and/or Executive Directors.

**Volunteer and Mission Team Coordination**

* Recruit, train, and coordinate volunteers and local ambassadors serving Mukti Mission US.
* Facilitate short\-term service opportunities and ministry\-related travel to India, when appropriate, in partnership with Mukti India.
* Represent Mukti Mission US at international Council meetings (once every 3 years), along with at least one annual site visit, and any other key events as requested by the Board.

**Communications, Events, and Ministry Promotion**

* Oversee the development and distribution of publications, prayer updates, newsletters, electronic communications, annual donor giving statements, sponsorship letters, and promotional materials. Promote awareness of Mukti's ministry, impact, and needs.
* Ensure effective use of digital platforms, including website and social media channels.
* Represent Mukti Mission US through speaking engagements and tables at relevant meetings, conferences, etc. Also responsible for hosting the annual Muk\-Tea event.

**Board Relations and Governance**

* Support the Board of Directors in fulfilling its governance responsibilities.
* Prepare materials and reports for Board meetings in consultation with the Executive Committee, and provide regular monthly updates regarding ministry activities, finances, and organizational performance to the board. Assist in the implementation of Board\-approved initiatives.
* Regularly engage with the Board Executive Committee on key issues facing the ministry.

**Financial Oversight and Compliance**

* Oversee accurate financial records, budget development, cash\-flow, internal controls, and risk management. Monitor ministry\-sponsored projects and donor\-designated funds.
* Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
* Maintain compliance with applicable legal, financial, and accountability standards, including IRS, State \& Federal 501(c)3 regulations and registrations, ECFA, and Candid requirements.
* Work with Board Treasurer and External Auditor on reporting and accountability.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Genuine commitment to evangelical Christianity, and the mission and vision of Mukti Mission U.S.
* 8\-10 years of experience in nonprofit ministry leadership, cross\-cultural ministry, nonprofit financial management, and fundraising.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, and excellent interpersonal skills.
* Demonstrated experience building relationships with donors, churches, volunteers, and community partners.
* Demonstrated technical proficiency with digital communication tools, CRM database management, website management, etc.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including periodic travel to India.
* Bachelor's degree in relevant field required; master’s degree preferred.

  

All candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S.; no visa sponsorships are offered.


This position is currently based in our New Jersey office, though we are open to a fully remote arrangement for the right candidate. Regardless of location, candidates should expect to travel domestically and internationally.


Applicants should submit their cover letter, resume, relevant work samples, and a list of 4 references (pastoral, supervisor, direct report, peer)

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer - Heathcare
jobs.description:
The Bedford\-Stuyvesant Family Health Center (BSFHC) is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that serves all of the primary health care needs of families in the heart of North and Central Brooklyn for over 40 years. Our mission is to provide the most professional, courteous and highest quality health care, with dignity, to those we serve, especially the undeserved population, without regard for ability to pay.
  
  

**SUMMARY:**  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a Cross\-Enterprise Leader that provides leadership and strategic direction for operating units at BSFHC, including Operational Improvement, Network Management, Provider Operations, and Sales \& Marketing. The COO will partner with BSFHC’s President and executive leaders, directors and managers to develop strategies that shape BSFHC’s overall direction, achieve the organization’s performance goals, and deliver outstanding value for BSFHC’s customers.
  
  

The COO is a leader and innovator of new ideas, ventures and progressive initiatives and will consider the best interests and strategic direction of the entire organization when evaluating department decisions. Enterprise leaders will use their influence to work collaboratively across the organization to initiate and maintain relationships and resolve conflicts. Enterprise leaders will be comfortable dealing with ambiguity, uncertainty, complexity and time pressures, while leveraging these relationships.
  
  

**Duties and Responsibilities include but not limited to:**  

* Accept delegated areas of administration. Responsible for efficient practices and maximize productivity in all areas as defined by the CEO.
* Provides operational oversight and creates mechanisms to monitor infrastructure, processes and standards to achieve desired outcomes as part of corporate business plan and strategic initiatives.
* Collaborates with Leadership to set goals, clearly define operations, and develop appropriate performance standards, metrics and reporting tools.
* Develops, implements and manages the operations budget ensuring effective stewardship of resources, and achievement of Strategic Operating Plan (SOP) goals and annual corporate goals.
* Sets vision and leads operational departments by directing and coordinating activities consistent with established goals, compliance and quality requirements, objectives and policies and procedures.
* Develops short and long term strategies and tactics to assure operational and programmatic excellence, management and control.
* Develops and implements strategies to deliver superior Customer Service, Enrollment and Claims Administration to members and providers.
* Initiates, implements and monitors improvement activities aimed at reducing costs, increasing accuracy and efficiency and both internal and external customer satisfaction in each operational area.
* Analyze systems and procedures and recommend changes to improve workflow and efficiency.
* Prepare assigned areas for Joint Commission, DOH and HRSA Surveys
* Responsible for Emergency Preparedness, Fire Drills and PCEPN
* Interpret clinic policies, objectives and operational procedures to department heads.
* Resolve problems relating to utilization of facilities, equipment and supplies.
* Represent the Center at public and professional meetings and conferences as requested.
* Responsible for MIS system personnel and equipment placements
* Maintain professional affiliations and enhance professional development to keep pace with the trends in health care administration.
* Assist the Chief Executive Officer with planning, directing and coordinating facility activities to ensure full patient care based on clinic policies.


**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:**  

* Bachelors Degree required
* Masters, MBA, MPH or related post\-graduate degree preferred
* Three years experience in health administration including two years experience in a clinic environment.
* 10\+ years of senior management experience, with a minimum of 5 years leading one or more of the following functions: Customer Service, Claims, Enrollment, Operational Improvement, Value\-Based Contracting, or Sales \& Marketing
* 10\+ years of experience in a managed care/health care environment or a related government program
* Demonstrated experience successfully planning, organizing, managing and implementing Executive level projects


**Related Skills/Experience and requirements:**  

* Experience with government programs and their regulations, guidelines, and standards
* Exceptional executive leadership, strategic and day\-to\-day project and task management
* Demonstrated abilities in: Inductive Reasoning, Data Analytics, Employee Engagement, Conflict Resolution, Marketing Management and Provider Relationships
* Strong organizational and project management skills
* Excellent judgment and creative problem solving skills
* Solid understanding of physician practice operations including charge capture and clinical documentation;
* Outstanding listening and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively work and communicate with providers and practice staff;
* Time management skills and attention to detail;


**Benefits Overview:** We offer attractive compensation with comprehensive benefits including: Medical, 401k Retirement Plan with discretionary Match, Free Life Insurance and Long\-Term Disability, Transportation Plan, Generous Paid Vacations and Holidays.
  
  

**Salary:** 100k and based on experience
  
  

BSFHC IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

jobs.title: CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION:**

The Chief Operations Officer reports to the Chief Executive Officer with primary responsibility for the oversight of the organizations line operations. The role provides leadership and strategic vision to the organization and is vital to driving results for the organization. Oversee the day\-to\-day operations including Residential, Day Habilitation, Community Habilitation, Respite, Employment Services, and Clinical Operations (Nursing, Psychology, Crisis) with a focus on optimizing performance, processes and policies as well as setting up and monitoring KPI’s for the organization.



Pay: 190K\-210K


**QUALIFICATIONS:**


* Master’s Degree in a related field
* Five years of profound experience in operations oversight, leadership development, data analytics and building relationships with business and government partners.
* Experience with OPWDD and Justice Center compliance regulations and regulatory policy
* Program leadership experience at the Director level of a non\-profit organizations and vulnerable needs populations
* Exhibit core abilities including relationship building, communication, problem\-solving, time\-management, leadership, emotional intelligence, decision making, prioritization and delegation
* Intermediate MS Teams and practical experience with databases
* Valid NYS driver’s license \& ability to travel as needed

EBC Program Director


The Police Athletic League (PAL) of New York City is an independent youth development nonprofit organization and has been a vibrant and vital institution, serving as an effective, critical bridge between police and communities across all five boroughs of the City since 1914\. PAL operates diverse programs for children as young as 2 years old to young adults. Programs include Head Start, after\-school programs and summer day camps for elementary, middle and high school youth, and summer Playstreets. PAL also runs evening teen centers and college readiness programs, youth employment, and juvenile justice programs. Staying true to PAL’s roots, a cornerstone of our youth development strategy includes offering competitive and recreational sports for children of all ages. At PAL, we’re devoted to empowering communities and building the best places to work, and that goes for our own teams too.


In its 110th year, PAL continues to reimagine the agency’s leadership structure to ensure the next 110 years are nimble, strategic, responsive, and efficient. We are looking for SONYC School Program Directors to elevate our out\-of\-school programming embedded within a New York City public school or PAL Center. Locations may serve Elementary through High School youth through SEL, STEM, Literacy, Sports, Arts, Mental Health, and College and Career Access Programming.


This position reports to the Borough Lead.


The EBC Program Director is a key on\-site supervisor managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Directors must be creative programmers, skilled supervisors, and skilled talent developers. Familiarity with SACC regulations and DYCD funding requirements is a plus. Directors will partner with the NYPD, DOH, NYCHA, DYCD, NYCPS, and local community organizations. * Candidates must be able to support programming that happens during the evenings, and weekends.

* Demonstrated skills in program planning, implementation, and evaluation.
* Open to learning and growing. All staff will be learning mental health, SEL, and special needs inclusion skills and expected to integrate them into programming.

***Join our vibrant community...***

  



Brethren Village is seeking an innovative and proactive executive to serve as our Chief Operating Officer (COO).

  




The successful applicant will possess: experience and success managing large\-scale projects, including facilities / land use projects; a record of initiating and implementing process improvements; strong leadership competencies, including the ability to develop and engage staff, form productive partnerships, and collaborate across an organization to achieve objectives.

  



Brethren Village, a non\-profit Life Plan Community, is home to 1,200 Residents and employs 480 dedicated Team Members. Brethren Village is located in Lititz, PA, a vibrant small city with an active downtown area, rural areas, and top\-quality schools and healthcare organizations. Lititz is within easy driving distance, or train ride, of Philadelphia, Baltimore, New York City, and Washington D.C. Interested individuals are invited to visit www.bv.org to learn more about Brethren Village, and https://landinlancasterpa.com/ to learn more about the Lititz and Lancaster County areas.

  



Brethren Village's Chief Operating Officer will identify and advance strategic priorities; work collaboratively across the organization to drive innovation; help enhance service, efficiency, and effectiveness; help foster a positive and supportive workplace culture and a vibrant living community.

  



In conjunction with the President and other executives, the Chief Operating Officer will provide effective leadership and oversight for operations and staff; proactively identify opportunities, define priorities, and develop and implement short and long\-range plans aligned with the mission of the organization; help ensure sound fiscal management throughout the organization.

  


Primary responsibilities of the Chief Operating Officer include:  



* Participating in long and short\-range planning, and proactively identifying opportunities and challenges. In conjunction with the President, providing leadership for the development of the organization’s strategic plans; establishing priorities and specific objectives; ensuring plans are effectively implemented by managers.
* Fostering the highest standards of excellence with respect to the organization’s healthcare services, customer service / hospitality, safety and risk management, fiscal management, and other operations. In conjunction with the executive management team, overseeing and evaluating all services provided to Residents, on an ongoing basis.
* Establishing, tracking, and regularly reviewing relevant performance measures and benchmarks. Monitoring key financial and other performance indicators relevant to areas of responsibility; making decisions and taking action based on data / factual information.
* Proactively identifying opportunities to enhance service, increase efficiency, increase revenue, and control costs. Working collaboratively with managers to develop, implement, and complete specific process improvement projects.
* In conjunction with department managers, overseeing significant campus projects to help ensure such projects remain on\-budget and that quality, efficiency, and service objectives are achieved.
* Exploring and facilitating opportunities for collaboration / partnerships with external organizations and agencies to enhance services and/or manage costs.
* Working with the Vice President, Facilities, helping to determine optimal, future use of land and campus facilities.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer (CDO)
jobs.description:
**Startup Foundation \| U.S.\-Based**

Position Summary

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is a key executive leader responsible for building the Foundation's financial sustainability and long\-term growth. As a startup organization, the CDO's primary mission is to generate revenue that enables the Foundation to expand its programs, increase its impact, and achieve its strategic goals.

This role is responsible for creating and executing comprehensive fundraising and revenue\-generation strategies, developing strategic partnerships, securing grants, cultivating major donors, identifying new funding opportunities, and establishing systems that support sustainable growth. The CDO will work closely with the Founder, Executive Leadership Team, and Board of Directors to build a diversified funding portfolio and position the Foundation for long\-term success.

Key ResponsibilitiesRevenue Generation \& Growth

* Develop and execute a comprehensive revenue\-generation strategy aligned with the Foundation's mission and strategic objectives.
* Build multiple revenue streams, including individual giving, corporate sponsorships, grants, major gifts, planned giving, events, and earned\-income opportunities where appropriate.
* Establish annual fundraising goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
* Continuously identify innovative funding opportunities to increase financial sustainability.

Fundraising Strategy

* Design and lead annual fundraising campaigns.
* Develop donor acquisition, engagement, and retention strategies.
* Create donor stewardship programs that encourage long\-term giving.
* Monitor fundraising performance and adjust strategies to maximize results.

Major Gifts \& Donor Relations

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors and philanthropic partners.
* Build relationships with high\-net\-worth individuals, family foundations, and community leaders.
* Prepare compelling proposals and presentations for prospective donors.
* Ensure exceptional donor experience and recognition.

Grants \& Institutional Funding

* Identify local, state, federal, and private grant opportunities.
* Lead grant strategy, proposal development, submission, and reporting.
* Ensure compliance with grant requirements and funding agreements.

Corporate Partnerships

* Develop strategic partnerships with corporations and businesses.
* Secure sponsorships for Foundation programs and events.
* Create mutually beneficial partnership opportunities that support both community impact and organizational growth.

Business Development \& Strategic Partnerships

* Identify opportunities that generate sustainable income for the Foundation.
* Develop collaborations with nonprofits, government agencies, educational institutions, and private organizations.
* Explore innovative revenue\-generating initiatives consistent with the Foundation's mission.

Marketing \& Brand Development

* Collaborate with Marketing and Communications to strengthen the Foundation's visibility.
* Support campaigns that increase donor engagement and public awareness.
* Represent the Foundation at networking events, conferences, and community functions.

Leadership \& Organizational Development

* Build and lead the Foundation's Development Department.
* Develop fundraising policies, procedures, and best practices.
* Recruit, mentor, and manage development staff as the organization grows.
* Present fundraising performance, forecasts, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and the Board.

Financial Stewardship

* Develop annual development budgets and revenue forecasts.
* Track fundraising performance through key performance indicators (KPIs).
* Ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance with all fundraising regulations and ethical standards.

Startup Expectations

As an early\-stage Foundation, the Chief Development Officer is expected to be a hands\-on leader who can both develop strategy and execute it. This role requires creativity, entrepreneurial thinking, and a willingness to build systems, relationships, and fundraising programs from the ground up.

The CDO will play a critical role in transforming the Foundation from a startup organization into a financially sustainable nonprofit with diversified revenue sources and long\-term community impact.

QualificationsEducation

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Communications, Marketing, or a related field.
* Master's degree preferred.

Experience

* 8–10\+ years of progressive experience in fundraising, development, business development, or nonprofit leadership.
* Proven track record of securing major gifts, grants, corporate sponsorships, and strategic partnerships.
* Experience building fundraising programs for growing or startup organizations is highly preferred.
* Experience working with executive leadership and Boards of Directors.

Preferred Skills

* Fundraising strategy
* Revenue generation
* Business development
* Grant writing and management
* Corporate partnership development
* Major gift solicitation
* Strategic planning
* Financial forecasting
* Public speaking and presentations
* Relationship management
* Leadership and team development
* CRM and donor management systems

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

* Annual fundraising revenue achieved
* Total unrestricted funds raised
* Major gifts secured
* Grant funding awarded
* Corporate sponsorship revenue
* Number of strategic partnerships established
* Donor acquisition and retention rates
* Revenue diversification
* Return on fundraising investment (ROI)
* Growth in the Foundation's annual operating budget
* Progress toward long\-term financial sustainability

Send CV/Resume to: cabangan@wendellman.org

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Remote

**CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER**

**The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential (FCAP)**

**Organization**

The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential (FCAP)

**Position**

Chief Operating Officer

**Reports To**

Chairman, Board of Directors

**Classification**

Full\-Time, Exempt

**Location**

Crozet, VA — Hybrid; regular travel to partner university sites

**Salary Range**

$100,000 – $150,000, commensurate with experience

**ABOUT FCAP**

The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit operating at the intersection of **healthcare education, disability inclusion, and preventive fitness.** Since 2016, FCAP has trained more than **100 undergraduate UVA student interns** — nearly all of whom have gone on to careers in healthcare — while delivering supervised, evidence\-based exercise interventions to clients with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) and the general population.

Two clinics are currently operational, generating approximately **300 client visits per week.** FCAP is entering an ambitious expansion phase, with new university partner clinics planned at **Virginia Commonwealth University and William \& Mary**, and a long\-term goal of **15 university\-based programs nationally by 2035\.**

This is a rare opportunity to join a mission\-driven organization at an inflection point – one with a proven model, a unique and compelling story, a talented team, and the organizational will to grow.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Chief Operating Officer will build the business infrastructure to support FCAP’s expansion. This is a ground\-floor leadership role — part systems builder, part revenue strategist, and part chief of staff. The COO will design and oversee the business side of the organization: financial management, operations, university partnership agreements, communications, board operations, and operational scaffolding for each new clinic site.

The role is built to complement FCAP’s clinical leadership and to anchor its fundraising. Led by the Founding Clinical Director/President, the clinical team oversees the FCAP method, designs the curriculum, and ensures quality across sites. On the business side, the COO will implement FCAP’s revenue strategy, secure institutional commitments, and — in collaboration with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director/President, and Board — cultivates and stewards major\-gift relationships.

The role requires close collaboration and consultation with the Founding Clinical Director to align FCAP’s clinical and operational functions, ensuring that business operations continually serve the nonprofit clinical mission. The COO will hire a Development Manager, who will run day\-to\-day fundraising execution, building the systems and pipeline for fundraising success.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Operations and Financial Infrastructure**

▪ Design and implement the administrative systems that let FCAP operate across multiple university sites: budgeting, payroll, HR, compliance, insurance, and data management.

▪ Establish financial controls, manage cash flow, track spending against budget, and produce regular financial reporting for the board.

▪ Build and maintain the operational playbook for launching each new clinic, coordinating logistics across clinical, university, and FCAP central stakeholders.

▪ Select and implement FCAP’s donor management platform and core development systems, which the Development Manager will then run day to day.

**University Partnerships and Agreements**

▪ Negotiate, document, and maintain partnership agreements and MOUs with university partners, vendors, and service providers.

▪ Structure each site’s financial partnership on FCAP’s cost\-share model and hold partners to a minimum five\-year commitment.

▪ Serve as the operational point of contact for university administrators throughout each clinic’s launch and ongoing operation.

**Revenue Strategy and Sustainability**

▪ Set FCAP’s overall revenue strategy and diversification plan, in close collaboration with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director, and board.

▪ Oversee earned and institutional revenue — university contributions, fee\-based programming, CKC System sales, and corporate partnerships — and steward long\-term, endowment\-building goals that give each clinic and FCAP central durable footing.

▪ Lead FCAP’s development function and collaborate with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director, and Board to oversee major\-gift cultivation and solicitation.

▪ Hire and manage the Development Manager to run day\-to\-day fundraising execution.

▪ Lead FCAP’s grant strategy, collaborating with the clinical team and Development Manager to identify grant opportunities, write and secure grants, complete necessary grant reports, and build relationships with grantmakers as needed.

**Communications and External Relations**

▪ Oversee FCAP’s communications strategy, including website management, digital presence, social media, branding, and public relations.

▪ Build and manage a student intern team that produces FCAP’s social media — giving students hands\-on experience while extending the organization’s reach.

▪ Work with the Founding Clinical Director and clinical team to translate program impact into clear narratives for funders, partners, and the public.

▪ Support FCAP’s professional certification and credentialing initiative as the model establishes a recognized professional pathway.

▪ Represent FCAP operationally with university administrators, community organizations, and external stakeholders.

**Board Operations and Governance**

▪ Collaborate with the Chairman to bring the current working board to the level of a strategic board.

▪ Manage board operations: prepare meeting materials, coordinate committee work, track action items, and support board recruitment and onboarding.

▪ Ensure compliance with nonprofit governance standards, IRS requirements, and state regulations.

jobs.description:
**Department**


Harris School Sit\-D **About the Department**


Policy with real impact doesn’t evolve from ideology or intuition, or even experience. At the University of Chicago Harris School of Public Policy, developing effective public policy is a science, based on data and measurable impact. Addressing today’s interconnected challenges requires rigorous inquiry. It also requires innovative people who will face the facts, gather data, and understand why current policies exist to improve them. For more than 30 years, the University of Chicago Harris School of Public Policy has been steadfastly committed to serving society by advancing analysis\- and evidence\-informed policy. Guided by this exacting mission, our community of faculty, students, and alumni from the public, private, and nonprofit sectors are taking on the world’s most important problems by using the latest tools of social science. **Job Summary**


The Harris School seeks to hire a Program Director for the Situational Decision\-making (Sit\-D) Training.  

  

Sit\-D is an innovative police training program developed at the University of Chicago that integrates cutting\-edge behavioral science with immersive simulation technology to strengthen officer decision\-making in high\-stakes encounters.  

  

The Program Director will work directly with Professor Oeindrila Dube, who helped create the Sit\-D training. This work is supported by the Harris School Bike Shop@UChicago, a research center where economists and computer scientists build "bicycles for the mind"—algorithms that enhance human capacity rather than replace it. The Program Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for a portfolio of projects supporting the replication, evaluation, and expansion of Sit\-D—including incubating AI\-enhanced versions of the training. Working in close partnership with Professor Dube, the Program Director will guide these projects from early engagement with law enforcement partners through implementation and evaluation readiness, exercising substantial day\-to\-day leadership. The Program Director will also represent the initiative with external partners and funders and help secure the resources, relationships, and visibility needed to position Sit\-D for broader expansion across agencies and jurisdictions.  

  

The role calls for two core capabilities. The Program Director must be able to build and sustain high\-level relationships with senior law enforcement officials and institutional partners, bringing the energy and drive to generate momentum across a complex, multi\-site initiative. Equally important is a sophisticated understanding of program evaluation — including study design, randomization, and outcome measurement — that enables productive engagement with research teams and partner agencies in working through evaluation parameters and implementation feasibility.**Responsibilities**

* Leads and directs the operational development, incubation, replication, and scale\-up of Sit\-D training initiatives, guiding a portfolio of projects from early engagement with law enforcement partners through implementation and evaluation readiness, in close partnership with Professor Dube.
* Conducts strategic outreach and engagement with senior officials in state government and law enforcement leadership to build partnerships and advance opportunities for Sit\-D implementation and evaluation.
* Advises on strategic decisions regarding which states and jurisdictions to prioritize for Sit\-D expansion and replication.
* Assesses opportunities to integrate emerging technologies, including AI\-assisted tools, into Sit\-D training and scaling; oversees law enforcement consultants retained to refine and adapt training curricula for new jurisdictions and emerging technology applications, considering both technological feasibility and institutional constraints.
* Leads study design discussions and early\-stage evaluation planning, working with research staff and partner agencies to establish feasible approaches to randomization, sample size, outcome measurement, and implementation.
* Oversees the groundwork required to launch evaluations, including coordinating data use agreements, facilitating data transfers, and securing access to administrative data, training records, and other relevant data sources.
* Oversees and coordinates University of Chicago IRB processes, maintaining confidentiality of participant and agency data.
* Manages implementation and evaluation teams as projects advance from incubation to replication and scale\-up, including project managers, research staff, external collaborators, and trainer teams responsible for delivering train\-the\-trainer programs across participating agencies.
* Identifies funding opportunities and leads the development of grant proposals.
* Prepares written summaries, memos, and presentations for academic researchers, funders, policymakers, and practitioner audiences describing project progress, feasibility findings, and plans for replication and evaluation.
* Works independently to develop detailed work plans, schedules, project estimates, resource plans, and status reports. Assembles and leads a project team, assigns individual responsibilities, identifies appropriate resources needed, and develops schedules to ensure timely completion of projects.
* Tracks progress, conducts analysis, as well as prepares for and facilitates project meetings. Ensures adherence to quality standards and reviews project deliverables.
* Performs other related work as needed.

A best\-in\-class city that attracts best\-in\-class talent, Philadelphia is an incredible place to build a career. From our thriving arts scene and rich history to our culture of passion and grit, there are countless reasons to love living and working here. With a workforce of over 30,000 people, and more than 1,000 different job categories, the City of Philadelphia offers boundless opportunities to make an impact.


As an employer, the City of Philadelphia values inclusion, integrity, innovation, empowerment, and hard work above all else. We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

***What we offer***

* **Impact** \- The work you do here matters to millions.
* **Growth** \- Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
* **Diversity \& Inclusion** \- Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
* **Benefits** \- We care about your well\-being.

***Agency Description***


The Office of Prison Oversight is a newly established agency within the City of Philadelphia, created to strengthen accountability and transparency in the Philadelphia Department of Prisons (PDP) within the Office of the Inspector General.


The Office is charged with promoting the safety, health, and well\-being of incarcerated individuals through independent oversight, policy review, investigations, and public reporting. Working in close partnership with the Philadelphia Prison Community Oversight Board, the Office will conduct inspections, access prison records and data, engage directly with staff and incarcerated individuals, and provide recommendations to improve conditions and operations within Philadelphia’s correctional system.

 **Job Description** **Position Summary**


The Executive Director is responsible for building and leading the newly established Philadelphia Office of Prison Oversight. This role develops policy and practice, sets vision in consultation with the Prison Oversight Board, and leads oversight of the City’s four correctional facilities.


The Executive Director will direct independent reviews of the Philadelphia Department of Prisons, respond to sentinel events (including deaths in custody), and issue public reports with findings and recommendations.

**Essential Functions**

* Provide visionary leadership, establishing strategic goals and objectives aligned with the Office’s mission and the City’s priorities.
* Collaborate with the Philadelphia Prison Community Oversight Board to identify and address emerging prison\-related concerns.
* Lead recruitment, hiring, and training of staff for the Office of Prison Oversight.
* Manage the Office’s annual budget (approximately $1\.4 million for FY26\).
* Develop and maintain relationships with the Prison Oversight Board, Department of Prisons, Office of the Mayor, and City Council.
* Represent the Office at public meetings, forums, and conferences.
* Conduct scheduled and unscheduled inspections of Philadelphia’s correctional facilities to examine and document conditions and interview incarcerated individuals.
* Respond to sentinel events, including investigating every death in custody.
* Oversee the review of prison data, inmate grievances, and follow\-up investigations.
* Review and evaluate regulations, policies, and procedures of the Department of Prisons.
* Identify systemic issues and provide recommendations to the Department of Prisons and the Oversight Board.
* Access department of Prisons staff and incarcerated individuals, facilities, databases, and documents, including grievances filed against the department.
* Monitor compliance with statewide and nationwide best practices in corrections and oversight.
* Establish and maintain data collection and reporting systems.
* Prepare and submit periodic reports to the Oversight Board and City Council summarizing Office activities.
* Report on conditions of confinement including use of force, infrastructure, out\-of\-cell time, access to services, food and nutrition, due process, and access to programming.
* Develop and implement community education programs to increase public understanding of prison conditions and oversight efforts.
* And other duties as assigned.

* Knowledge of the Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) and related regulations.
* Legal standards for investigating complaints, conducting hearings, and issuing recommendations.

The Department of Labor includes the Office of Employee Relations, the Office of Labor Relations, the Office of Worker Protections, the Office of Labor Standards, and the Living Wage Working Group.

 **Job Description** **Position Summary**


The Deputy Director of Worker Protections is a member of the executive leadership team within the Department of Labor, and is responsible for the setting strategic vision setting, operations, and performance of the Office of Worker Protection.


This role is responsible for the management of all enforcement activities related to worker protection ordinances assigned to the Office of Worker Protection. To do this, the Deputy will set ambitious performance goals for all office staff, ensure that worker complaints and inquiries are responded to in a consistent and timely manner, and deliver results to the citizens of Philadelphia.


Externally, the Deputy is responsible for successfully engaging with, and communicating across a wide variety of stakeholders, and serves as the first point of contact for City Council, the advocacy community, and the business community for concerns related to worker protection ordinances.


This role reports to the Chief of Staff for the Department of Labor, and directs through subordinate Worker Protections Staff which includes the Assistant Compliance Director and Labor Protection Supervisors.

**Essential Functions**
