jobs.title: Director of Development (0462U), Berkeley Law #87795
jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and providing space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

The Law School’s Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) team engages alumni philanthropically and in programming and initiatives that strengthen the school and the student experience. The mission of the Development arm is to secure financial support for core operations and special initiatives that advance the law school’s mission.

Position Overview

The position involves designing, developing, delivering, and administering fundraising programs. Develops and implements strategies for cultivating, soliciting and stewarding major gifts prospects with the capacity for a major gift of $25k to $1M and above; identifies new donor prospects through researching background information on potential donors and developing materials, creating marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; cultivates, stewards, and solicits donor prospects for gifts ranging from $25K to $1M and above; prepares and negotiates gift instruments ranging from moderate to high complexity; works with the Dean, Assistant Dean and faculty as necessary to solicit the largest gifts; manages a portfolio of principal gift prospects assigned to the Dean. Directs the research and preparation of the Dean’s briefings materials, creates talking points and meeting strategies for the Dean and briefs the Dean on these strategies. As appropriate, staffs the Dean on principal gifts visits and directs the tracking and implementation of all follow-up; manages the activities of the campaign cabinet and their meetings; collaborates with the Director of Financial Aid and the Director of Career Services to ensure proper stewardship of financial aid donors.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is: August 12, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

Responsibilities

Fundraising

Plans, organizes, and directs large-scale fundraising campaigns for Berkeley Law.
Participates in short- and long-range strategic planning. This includes annual stewardship for existing donors, long-term planning for prospect cultivation, foundation research and strategy, and campaign planning related to Berkeley Law endowment funds and long-term fundraising initiatives.
Identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards major gift prospects and donors, using established metrics (currently CADS) to track activity and report outcomes. Utilizes a return-on-investment approach in managing a donor portfolio.
Responsible for major gifts, corporate and foundation fundraising, and direct marketing efforts that generate philanthropic support for Berkeley Law. Manages a portfolio of donors with the capacity to give between $25,000 and $1,000,000 or more.
Writes complex proposals for individual, corporate, and foundation prospects.
Travels to meet with donors and represent Berkeley Law. Designs, organizes, and attends functions, meetings, and conferences as a representative of Berkeley Law. May serve on internal and external committees as a campus or Berkeley Law representative.
May participate in cross-campus, multi-unit fundraising campaigns in partnership with UDAR.
Ensures fundraising goals are achieved and raises at least $1 million annually by:
Managing a portfolio of 75–100 major gift and corporate/foundation prospects with the capacity to give $25,000–$1,000,000+.
Making 15–20 substantive donor contacts per month that advance relationships.
Conducting 80–120 donor visits annually.
Leading the planning and evaluation of fund development and annual solicitation programs, including financial feasibility studies, market research, and recommendations for program improvements.
Closing at least $1 million in new gift commitments or outright gifts.

Volunteer Engagement

May recruit, train, and support key volunteers who assist in advancement and fundraising efforts.

Program Leadership & Administration

May oversee the work of professional and support staff involved in implementing multi-component fundraising programs.
Uses key fundraising applications and databases to support fundraising strategies, goals, and objectives.

Professional Development & Other Duties

Engages in professional development and training opportunities as appropriate.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Advanced knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including relevant issues affecting the campus and higher education.
Advanced knowledge of UC Berkeley and Berkeley Law, including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements, and organizational infrastructure.
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, regulations, and institutional policies related to gift acceptance, prospect management, and philanthropic fundraising.
Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the political acumen to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
Advanced skill in developing persuasive and compelling presentations that effectively communicate campus priorities and secure philanthropic support.
Advanced ability to achieve established goals and objectives through effective program and project planning, organization, execution, and evaluation.
Demonstrated commitment to and understanding of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB), with the ability to integrate DEIB principles into daily work and interactions.
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds represented within the UC Berkeley community.
Commitment to fostering an equitable, inclusive, and welcoming environment where students, faculty, staff, alumni, and donors of all backgrounds feel respected, supported, and valued.
Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to make sound decisions, identify and resolve complex issues, and develop creative solutions.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Advanced project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint, as well as UDAR fundraising systems and the ability to quickly learn new technologies.
Experience working with alumni, donors, volunteers, and other constituent groups, with the ability to cultivate and maintain positive, productive relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment.
Ability to travel and work evenings, approximately twice per month, as needed.
Demonstrated ability to meet or exceed fundraising goals and performance objectives.

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

Preferred Qualifications

Juris Doctor (JD) degree and/or experience in legal environments.
Membership in Council Advancement Secondary Education (CASE) and/or Association of Fundraising Professionals.

Salary & Benefits

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $126,800.00 - $158,500.00.

This is an exempt, monthly-paid position.
This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position eligible for UC benefits.

Other Information

This position is eligible for up to 20% remote work. Exact arrangements are determined in partnership with your supervisor to meet role responsibilities and department needs and are subject to change.
This is not a visa opportunity. This position does not include sponsorship of a new consular H-1B visa petition that would require payment of the $100,000 supplemental fee.

How to Apply

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

Conviction History Background

This is a designated position requiring fingerprinting and a background check due to the nature of the job responsibilities. Berkeley does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities. The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Misconduct Disclosure

As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts a conditional offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; received notice of any allegations or are currently the subject of any administrative or disciplinary proceedings involving misconduct; have left a position after receiving notice of allegations or while under investigation in an administrative or disciplinary proceeding involving misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of misconduct with a previous employer.

“Misconduct” Means Any Violation Of The Policies Or Laws Governing Conduct At The Applicant’s Previous Place Of Employment, Including, But Not Limited To, Violations Of Policies Or Laws Prohibiting Sexual Harassment, Sexual Assault, Or Other Forms Of Harassment, Discrimination, Dishonesty, Or Unethical Conduct, As Defined By The Employer. Abusive Conduct in the Workplace

The University of California is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, or other protected status under state or federal law.

jobs.description:
Location:
New York, NY
Classification:
Full-Time
Reports To:
President & CEO

Position Overview

The CEO Fundraising Sr. Specialist will play a pivotal role in advancing fundraising efforts led by the President and CEO, recognized as Women's World Banking's most effective fundraising asset. In this role, you will work in direct partnership with the CEO to identify, develop, and advance a strong pipeline and portfolio of prospective supporters, helping create opportunities that contribute to the organization's long-term fundraising goals.

A significant element of this work involves supporting the implementation of the CEO’s fundraising strategy and the development of a principal gifts pipeline under her leadership. You will be responsible for building and advancing a robust pipeline of prospective supporters, creating a disciplined cultivation process that generates a steady flow of new and engaged donors. This work supports the CEO's fundraising objectives, which include securing $10 million annually, representing approximately half of the organization's overall fundraising target, with at least half of that funding being unrestricted. While the organization's broader fundraising strategy is developed by senior leadership, the CEO defines the fundraising strategy and priorities needed to achieve her fundraising goals within that framework. This role is responsible for helping to bring that strategy to life through generating opportunities, advancing prospects, and contributing to fundraising objectives.

Success in this role requires a combination of strong research and analytical skills, sound judgment, persistence, and a sales-minded approach to relationship development. The ideal candidate is energized by opening doors, connecting the dots across networks, creating momentum, and helping move relationships from prospect to partner. While not a front-line fundraising role, this position requires the same discipline, urgency, organization, and initiative to build the systems and partnerships that drive fundraising success.

Collaboration with Board members, senior leadership, Development colleagues, and other members of the CEO's front office team will be essential to identifying, cultivating, and advancing opportunities. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging with high-level stakeholders, exercising discretion and sound judgment, and representing Women's World Banking with professionalism and credibility in a variety of external settings.

Key Responsibilities

Prospect Development and Pipeline Management

Steward and advance a pipeline of prospective individual donors, family offices, philanthropic advisors, foundations, corporate leaders, and other high-potential supporters, ensuring the CEO's engagement is well-sequenced and well-prepared at every stage
Develop prospect engagement plans and recommend priorities, outreach approaches, and next steps in support of the CEO's fundraising strategy and priorities.
Conduct prospect research and due diligence, developing profiles that assess alignment, capacity, interests, networks, and potential pathways to engagement.
Generate new opportunities through relationship mapping, market intelligence, networking, and creative prospecting.
Maintain accurate pipeline activity, engagement plans, and prospect records in Salesforce and other fundraising systems.

Relationship Development and CEO Engagement

Manage and advance a portfolio of CEO-priority prospects, driving outreach and cultivation efforts through introductions, correspondence, meeting requests, follow-up, and engagement strategies.
Identify and cultivate pathways to introductions through Board members, donors, advisors, partners, and other stakeholders.
Generate opportunities for CEO engagement and help maintain a consistent cadence of qualified prospect and donor meetings.
Work with the CEO to develop the Leaders Circle into a strategic engagement platform for the organization’s most committed donors, prospects, and friends. Optimize the potential for the Leaders Circle to deepen affiliation, increase giving, expand influence, and create a pipeline for future leadership.
Partner with the CEO and Executive Assistant to coordinate meetings and cultivation activities while maintaining ownership of prospect progression, engagement plans, and next steps.
Regularly assess prospect activity and recommend actions that will strengthen relationships and move opportunities forward.

Donor Engagement and Relationship Advancement

Prepare briefing materials, prospect profiles, talking points, and recommendations for CEO meetings and external engagements.
Draft and manage donor-facing correspondence and stewardship communications on behalf of the CEO.
Track relationship activity, commitments, action items, and engagement outcomes, ensuring timely execution and follow-through.
Capture donor insights and communications in Salesforce and share relevant information with the broader fundraising team.
Coordinate with Development colleagues to ensure opportunities are appropriately advanced, cultivated, or transitioned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum 7-9 years of direct experience in fundraising, principal and major gifts, donor engagement, philanthropic partnerships, business development, private wealth, or a closely related external-facing relationship development role, with demonstrated success identifying prospects, building pipelines, and advancing high-value relationships.
Demonstrated ability to operate with a strong sense of urgency, take initiative, and independently drive opportunities forward in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment.
Strong relationship-building instincts and a demonstrated ability to leverage networks, social platforms, and market intelligence to identify prospects, uncover connection pathways, and generate new engagement opportunities.
Experience working with senior executives, organizational leaders, Board members, or other high-level stakeholders.
Strong research and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize information into actionable recommendations and engagement plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience using Salesforce or similar CRM platforms.
Highly organized, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities with minimal oversight.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting CEO-, President-, C-suite-, or Board-led fundraising, partnership development, or external engagement efforts.
Experience working within principal and major gifts, executive fundraising, business development, philanthropy, or private wealth functions.
Existing professional networks aligned with Women's World Banking's prospective donor base.
Knowledge of international development, social impact, financial inclusion, or women's economic empowerment.

Measures of Success

Within the First 75 Days

Develop a strong understanding of the CEO's fundraising priorities, relationship network, and expectations for donor and prospect engagement.
Develop an understanding of Women's World Banking's mission, strategic priorities, programs, impact, and value proposition.
Build productive working relationships with the CEO, Executive Assistant, Development leadership, Board members, and other colleagues involved in donor cultivation and stewardship.
Assess existing CEO-linked donor and prospect activity and establish a prioritized prospect pipeline with clear engagement strategies and introduction pathways.
Demonstrate early success in generating and advancing opportunities through prospect research, outreach, relationship development, and CEO engagement support.

jobs.title: Program Director - Edward Byrne Center
jobs.description:
EBC Program Director

The Police Athletic League (PAL) of New York City is an independent youth development nonprofit organization and has been a vibrant and vital institution, serving as an effective, critical bridge between police and communities across all five boroughs of the City since 1914. PAL operates diverse programs for children as young as 2 years old to young adults. Programs include Head Start, after-school programs and summer day camps for elementary, middle and high school youth, and summer Playstreets. PAL also runs evening teen centers and college readiness programs, youth employment, and juvenile justice programs. Staying true to PAL’s roots, a cornerstone of our youth development strategy includes offering competitive and recreational sports for children of all ages. At PAL, we’re devoted to empowering communities and building the best places to work, and that goes for our own teams too.

In its 110th year, PAL continues to reimagine the agency’s leadership structure to ensure the next 110 years are nimble, strategic, responsive, and efficient. We are looking for SONYC School Program Directors to elevate our out-of-school programming embedded within a New York City public school or PAL Center. Locations may serve Elementary through High School youth through SEL, STEM, Literacy, Sports, Arts, Mental Health, and College and Career Access Programming.

This position reports to the Borough Lead.

Requirements

The EBC Program Director is a key on-site supervisor managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Directors must be creative programmers, skilled supervisors, and skilled talent developers. Familiarity with SACC regulations and DYCD funding requirements is a plus. Directors will partner with the NYPD, DOH, NYCHA, DYCD, NYCPS, and local community organizations. We are looking for individuals who can listen, problem solve and build bridges to partnerships that expand opportunities for NYC’s youth. As such:

Candidates must be dedicated to learning and implementing Best Practices in the field of youth development.
Candidates must be able to support programming that happens during the evenings, and weekends.
Candidates must support the ideas and opportunities of the youth, staff, and community.
Candidates must possess excellent communication and listening skills.
Candidates must work together as a team to support PAL’s programming throughout the entire City.

Major Duties & Responsibilities

Foster social and emotional competencies and mental and physical well-being in a safe, welcoming, inclusive, and nurturing environment.
Manage all aspects of PAL Teen Afterschool Programming including overseeing the implementation of mental health support and inclusion coordination. Use identified resources to support youth with special needs and/or mental health needs, complete mental health referrals, and/or activate inclusion resources.
Recruit, hire, and provide excellent supervision and support to all part-time Group Leaders and Activity Specialists, Outreach Coordinators, and Content Specialists.
Ensure the program is aligned to strategic objectives of PAL, policies and procedures, agency programming calendar, SACC regulations, and the contractual obligations of government and private funding sources including fire safety certification.
Develops a strong Youth Development culture within the Center ensuring voice, growth, and advancement for all youth and staff. Train, conduct observations, and coach across all programs ensuring SEL, mental health, and inclusion policies are being implemented as designed.
Coordinates with the Principal, Director, Regional Director, SYEP Director, and Head Quarters staff to grow creative programming opportunities unique to the Site.
Collects program data, analyzes and drives PAL forward with data driven recommendations.
Ensure strong reciprocal partnerships with NYPD, NYCPS school partner, DYCD, DOH and other Community partners aligned with PAL’s mission.
Plans and coordinates various citywide programs, activities, and special events.
Assists in the development of future funding grants and requests for proposals.
Provides mediation and troubleshooting for on-site issues.
Respond appropriately when time-sensitive mental health services are needed such as suicide prevention, grief, and loss due to death or incarceration of a family member.

Qualifications

What You Bring:

An associate's in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13 OR a NYS Children’s Program Administrator Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR a SACC Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR two years in college with 18 credits in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13.
A minimum of 4 years of demonstrated successful experience in a supervisory position providing services to youth that includes program management and staff supervision with at least three years in a leadership capacity.
Demonstrated skills in program planning, implementation, and evaluation.
Open to learning and growing. All staff will be learning mental health, SEL, and special needs inclusion skills and expected to integrate them into programming.
Knowledge of DYCD Connect preferred. Microsoft office skills are required.
Strong verbal and written communication skills and ability to work collaboratively. Bi-lingual in Spanish, French, or Chinese preferred.
Able to travel to any PAL location in the 5 Boroughs for training.
Work Schedule: Tuesday to Saturday, 1:00-9:00pm with additional days as needed.

Compensation:
The salary for this role is $68,000-70,000 annually.

Benefits:
PAL offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes health insurance, flexible spending account options, an employee assistance program, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, life insurance, retirement savings options, a generous paid time off policy, training and more!

Location: Edward Byrne Center - Queens, NY

Start Date:
August 10th, 2026

Director of Development (Full-Time/Exempt)

About this Opportunity

Queens Botanical Garden seeks an experienced and passionate leader to be our next Director of Development. The Director of Development is responsible for annually raising approximately $4.5M from public and private sources and helps secure additional funds to support critical capital projects spanning the Garden’s 39-acre campus. Working with the Executive Director, Board of Trustees, and key staff leaders, the Director of Development devises and executes fundraising strategies to advance the ambitious ideas articulated in the Strategic and Master Plans and annual operating budget. The Director of Development leads the Development and Marketing/ Comms team to success in meeting fundraising goals through institutional giving, individual giving, special events, and membership support. In addition to providing leadership and strategy, the Director is also an active front-line fundraiser who directly contributes to institutional and individual fundraising efforts, including grant writing, ongoing stewardship, and major gift solicitation. They are a passionate advocate for the Garden’s work to engage the public through inspiring gardens, innovative educational programs, and real-world applications of environmental stewardship. The ideal candidate will thrive in a fast-paced fundraising environment which demands exceptional written and oral communications skills and enthusiastically collaborate with other organizational leaders to generate and execute new programmatic and capital initiatives.
The Director of Development is part of the Senior Staff leadership team, reports to the Executive Director, and supervises the Institutional Giving Manager, Senior Manager for Communications and Marketing, and Development Assistant.
Key Responsibilities: 

Fundraising Leadership & Strategy

Refresh and implement an ambitious fundraising plan designed to grow the organization’s annual operating budget, diversify funding streams, and grow unrestricted revenue and major gifts, including naming opportunities.
Activate the Board of Trustees as ambassadors for fundraising through strategy sessions, committee work, and training, as needed, to develop a culture of philanthropy.
Closely track fundraising projections and strategize with Senior Staff to accordingly expand or alter planned activities; generate fundraising reports for the Board of Trustees.
Work with Executive Director and Senior Manager for Communications & Marketing to develop strategies for maximizing revenues.
Collaborate with fundraising and marketing consultants and partners as needed.

Institutional Giving

Strengthen relationships with existing institutional funders, including the City of New York, elected officials, and major foundation and corporate partners, with a focus on increasing support and securing multi-year commitments.
Liaise with leaders in Education/Programs, Visitor Services, Horticulture, Marketing, and other departments to identify fundable projects in accordance with QBG’s new strategic plan; oversee ongoing work with Finance Department to ensure appropriate grant-tracking activities and accurate reporting.
Take the lead on proposal development for major funders and new prospects; work with Institutional Giving Manager and Development Assistant to ensure accurate and compelling proposals and reports for all institutional donors.
Lead the Garden’s Corporate Sponsorship and collaborate as needed on Membership programs; collaborate with Marketing, Visitor Services, Education/Programs, Operations, and other departments to implement sponsorship and activation benefits.

Individual Giving & Special Events

Lead the Garden’s existing Individual Giving programs, including the Adopt-a-Bench, Adopt-A-Tree, and Adopt-A-Garden initiatives.
Develop and execute compelling new individual giving campaigns using the Garden’s communications channels and cultivation events with the Executive Director.
Establish relationships with current and potential major donors; create custom support and sponsorship packages based on donor interest.
Strategize to grow Membership revenue with Membership Coordinator and key staff.
Lead planning and execution of Rambling Rose Gala, the organization’s annual fundraising gala, including devising strategies for revenue growth, and work with the Board Development Committee to implement such strategies; lead ideation for new special events, as needed.

Marketing and Communications 

Oversee the work of the Senior Communications and Marketing Manager who manages all comms and marketing.
Work with Executive Director and Senior Communications and Marketing Manager to devise a marketing and comms plan aligned with 5-year strategic plan goals, and to develop strategies for maximizing revenues.
Ensure completion of Annual Report, printed materials, and other assets with clear brand fidelity and messaging.

Development Operations

Identify opportunities to streamline and strengthen development operations.
Oversee Department expense budgets; approve purchases in accordance with budgets.
Harness data from fundraising database (DonorPerfect) to develop moves management strategies for existing donors

Qualifications:

At least seven (7) years of progressively increasing responsibility, experience, and success in fundraising for a non-profit organization, preferably at cultural, educational, and/or environmental institutions
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; Master’s degree and fundraising credentials preferred
Supervisory experience required; passion for fostering collaboration and excellence while promoting professional development of staff
Strong relationship manager; enthusiasm for collaborating with internal and external partners
Familiarity with donor management software (DonorPerfect a plus); ease with using technology, including the Microsoft Office Suite
Superb verbal and written communication skills
Knowledge of the New York City fundraising landscape; enthusiasm for sustainability, environmental organizations and cultural institutions
Creativity, marketing savvy, and business development acumen; awareness of fundraising and marketing trends
Occasional evening and weekend work required for special and public events

Schedule & Benefits

This is a full-time, exempt position with weekly on-site work, and some flexibility to work remotely. Benefits offered include excellent medical, vision, dental and life insurance, generous PTO, paid holidays, employee discounts, access to the Museums Council pass, which grants free admission to various museums and cultural institutions, pension and other retirement savings plans. Schedule is generally Monday through Friday, with occasional evening and weekend work.

Salary Range:
$110,000 – 120,000

For consideration, please submit your resume, cover letter, and any relevant documents via our Career Center.

If you encounter difficulties with uploading documents to the portal, please send via email to Human Resources at hr@queensbotanical.org.

jobs.description:
Program Director

Division: Youth Development

Reports To: Senior Program Director

Effective Date: November 2025

FLSA: Exempt

Summary

The Program Director (PD) is responsible for leading, managing, and implementing all aspects of assigned programs to ensure excellence, safety, and alignment with The Child Center of NY’s mission and contractual expectations. The PD ensures program goals are met, budgets are monitored, and all compliance, data, and reporting requirements are fulfilled. The PD also serves as the site’s Mental Health Lead, overseeing implementation of mental health supports in coordination with the host school, The Child Center’s Behavioral Health Division, and external partners.

Essential Functions

Program Leadership and Operations

Lead the development, implementation, and monitoring of all program components to ensure goals align with agency mission and community needs.
Maintain an active presence throughout program hours to ensure consistent safety, quality, and alignment with agency standards.
Supervise, coach, and evaluate staff to promote strong performance, professional growth, and adherence to agency expectations.
Oversee program documentation, reporting, and fiscal management to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and contract compliance.

Mental Health Role and Supports

Oversee implementation of all Mental Health Supports as required by DYCD, including ensuring all staff complete the one-hour DYCD Mental Health training and completing the two-hour DYCD training on the mental health spectrum, crisis response, and crisis navigation planning.
Work with agency leadership to promote hiring of staff with the New York State Youth Peer Advocate Credential or support eligible staff in obtaining it.
Develop and maintain a Mental Health Referral Plan in collaboration with the host school, The Child Center’s Behavioral Health Division (as the key Behavioral Health Partner), and any external partners. Update and share the plan with staff annually.
Communicate and coordinate with NYCPS social workers, school mental health staff, and community providers to ensure comprehensive participant support.
Facilitate referrals to mental health services using The Child Center’s QR code referral system and track and report de-identified, aggregate referral data to DYCD as required.
Create and implement a Crisis Navigation Plan for the site using the DYCD template, developed jointly with school-based and community mental health staff.
Ensure all staff understand and follow the Referral and Crisis Navigation Plans, responding appropriately when mental health needs are identified.

Partnerships and Program Quality

Collaborate with school leadership, families, and community organizations to maintain strong partnerships and shared accountability for participant outcomes.
Promote youth and family engagement through consistent communication, events, and inclusive practices.
Stay informed about trends and best practices in youth development, education, and mental health to ensure services remain relevant and effective.
Identify and maintain community partnerships that enhance program access and impact.

Training and Professional Development

Participate in all required DYCD and agency trainings, ensuring personal completion and staff compliance.
Support and document ongoing professional development for all site staff.
Foster a learning culture that integrates youth development, trauma-informed practice, and social-emotional learning.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Manages the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of program operations.
Supervises Assistant Program Directors, Group Leaders, Activity Specialists, and other staff as assigned.
Ensures adherence to agency policies, collective bargaining agreements, and all applicable laws and standards.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Education, Child Development, Public Administration, or related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in youth development or education, including 2 years in a supervisory role.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and strong administrative skills.
Ability to plan independently, meet deadlines, and manage multiple priorities.
Satisfactory background check, fingerprint clearance, and health screening.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Education, Public Administration, Social Work, or related field.
Bilingual in Spanish, Mandarin, Cantonese, Bengali, Haitian Creole, or other languages relevant to the community.

Job Behavioral Expectations

Maintain consistent professional attendance, punctuality, and conduct.
Communicate effectively with staff, partners, and families.
Use data and feedback to inform improvement.
Uphold confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA and all agency policies.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

This role requires regular movement between classrooms, offices, and outdoor spaces during program hours. The employee may lift up to 20 pounds and must be able to supervise active youth settings. Work occurs primarily in school environments with standard conditions.

jobs.title: Executive Director - Dallas Community Land Trust
jobs.description:
Executive Director - Dallas Community Land Trust (DCLT)

About Dallas Community Land Trust

The Dallas Community Land Trust (DCLT) is a newly established nonprofit organization dedicated to acquiring, developing and stewarding land for the purpose of creating and preserving permanently affordable housing opportunities in the City of Dallas for low-to-moderate income families while helping to build and preserve equitable, inclusive, and culturally sustainable neighborhoods and communities in Dallas.

The DCLT is a registered charitable organization in accordance with IRC

501(c)(3). The DCLT has an independent Board that is made up of community leaders in housing development and two intermediaries (The Real Estate Council and Communities Foundation of Texas). The Board is in the process of expanding to include additional members who enhance the organization’s prospects for success. Eventually, one-third of the seats will be filled with DCLT homeowners and leaseholders.

To ensure the sustainability of the organization during its startup phase, Communities Foundation of Texas (CFT) has agreed to serve as an incubator for the organization . For a period of up to 5 years, CFT will provide the organization with in-kind back-office support, which includes hiring the Executive Director as a member of its staf f and providing resources to allow the Executive Director to add a team member.

The Opportunity

The DCLT Is Seeking An Executive Director (ED) To Lead The Organization In Its Mission To Acquire And Steward Land For The Benefit Of Developing And Preserving Permanently Affordable Housing In Dallas , And Build Trust In An Approach That Is Largely Unfamiliar To Local Stakeholders . The Organization’s Primary Objective Will Be To Provide Homeownership Opportunities For Low-income Households Earning 60-80% Of The Area Median Income, And Secondarily, To Steward Non-residential Community Assets, And /or Provide Affordable Rental Housing. The D CLT Expects To Pursue Multiple Strategies To Grow Its Portfolio Of Homes Including

New construction in partnership with developers,
Renovation of existing homes(single and multifamily),
Acquisition of existing single family rental homeproperties.

The portfolio and strategy will evolve over time as the DCLT strengthens its partnerships and funding pipeline.

The ED is ultimately responsible for the overall direction, execution, and effectiveness of the entire organization. The ED will oversee all aspects of the organization’s operations including strategic planning, partnerships, marketing, real estate development, community engagement, fiscal management, fundraising, and board relations. The ED will be the public face of the DCLT and must be a dynamic, visionary and culturally competent leader with a strong entrepreneurial spirit, committed to increasing access to homeownership through a community-driven approach. This is a unique opportunity to build a high-impact organization from the ground up with the advantage of strong backing from established organizations.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership& Strategy:
Continue todevelop andexecute a comprehensive strategic plan aligned with DCLT's mission and vision.
Foster an effective and collaborative relationship with the Board of Directorsand committees.
Represent DCLT in the community to promote its mission and enhance its public profile.
Create a clear performance evaluation process in collaboration with Board membersincluding goals, metrics, and outcomes reporting.
Operational Management:
Develop and implement operational plans for property acquisition, real estate development (through partnerships with developers), property management, community outreach, and homeowner support.
Oversee the execution and tracking of operational plans and report results to the Board.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws and regulationspertaining toCommunity Land Trusts and affordable housing development organizations.
Oversee the engagement and management of service providers including risk management, human resources, and financial reporting.
Community Engagement & Advocacy:
Serve as a key representative of DCLT in the community and with the City of Dallas, advocating forequitablecommunity development practicesand shared equityhousing models .
Develop andmaintainpartnerships with other organizations, community groups, and agencies to enhance the impact of DCLT’s work.
Engage with residents and community members to build support for and trust in the DCLT model.
Staff & Team Development:
Build and lead a high-performing teamthat is united around mission andcharacterized by strong internal coordination.
Build apositive,collaborative, transparent and ethical organizational culture.
Adhere tohuman resources policies and practices.
Financial Management & Fundraising:
Oversee all operational and financial reporting activities of the organization.
Work with staff, contracted accounting partners, and the Board to prepare a comprehensive budget, administer the funds according to the approved budget,monitorthe monthly cash flow, and provide regular reports to the Board on the revenues and expenditures of the organization.
Work with the Board to create short -term and 5-year revenue models aligned with programmatic goals to ensure the financial sustainability and solvency of the organization .
Refine andimplement the resource development planin accordance withrevenue models and the projected budget.
Guide and leadallfundraising activities including overseeing the submission of grant proposals and grant reporting.
Ensure compliance with all contract , grant, and regulatory requirements.
Ensure compliance and submission of annual audit, tax, and insurance filings/policies.

Develop and implement strategies for real estate development and property management.

Role Summary

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief administrative and operational leader of Temple B’nai Or. Reporting to the Board of Trustees, the ED is responsible for executing the board’s strategic priorities, ensuring strong financial stewardship, overseeing all non-clergy staff, and maintaining the operational, cultural, and organizational health of the Temple. The ED creates and implements systems with accountability measures, leading to operational excellence across all functions. The ED partners closely with clergy and lay leaders to support a thriving congregational community.

This role requires seasoned leadership, sound judgment, emotional intelligence, executive functioning, disciplined management, and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Core Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Governance Execution
Lead day-to-day administration and ensure alignment with the Board of Trustees’ strategic goals.
Advise the Board proactively on operational issues, risk management, staffing, finance, and facilities.
Implement policies, systems, and procedures that strengthen efficiency, accountability, and consistency across the organization.
Oversee senior staff meetings, drive cross-functional coordination, and ensure timely follow-through.
Financial Stewardship & Risk Management
Lead the budgeting process, financial planning, and ongoing financial management of the Temple.
Oversee finance professionals and ensure timely, accurate reporting and compliance with all regulatory requirements.
Present monthly and periodic financial statements to the Board and relevant committees, highlighting risks, variances, and recommended actions.
Maintain appropriate internal controls, cash-flow management, insurance coverage, and financial policies.
Partner with fundraising leadership to support resource development strategies and donor stewardship.
Staff Leadership, Human Resources & Culture
Supervise all non-clergy staff, establishing clear performance expectations, accountability systems, and professional development pathways.
Lead hiring, performance review, discipline, and dismissal of reporting staff.
Foster a professional, collaborative, and solutions-oriented work culture.
Ensure compliance with federal and state employment laws, HR policies, and best practices.
Operations, Facilities & Compliance
Ensure all facilities are safe, well-maintained, and operated efficiently, meeting regulatory and security standards.
Oversee major maintenance, capital projects, and vendor relationships.
Strengthen operational systems including IT, cybersecurity, software platforms, member data, and administrative workflows.
Ensure compliance with all relevant legal, educational, financial, and safety requirements.
Communications, Membership & Community Engagement
Oversee communications staff responsible for internal and external messaging, website, newsletters, and social media.
Provide leadership for membership engagement strategy to create an inclusive, welcoming, and connected congregational experience.
Partner with clergy and lay leadership to support programming, community-building, and lifecycle events.
Preschool Oversight
Supervise the Director of the Preschool ensuring strong educational operations, financial sustainability, and regulatory compliance.

Required Skills And Qualifications

Leadership & Management:Proven senior management experience with a track record of building effective teams, managing conflict, creating accountability systems, solving complex organizational problems, and leading through change.
Financial Acumen:Demonstrated experience managing budgets, overseeing financial operations, and ensuring compliance and risk management.
Communication:Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal skills; able to engage with staff, board members, congregants, donors, and external partners with clarity and professionalism.
Organizational Mastery:Strong planning, prioritization, and execution skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and respond quickly to shifting needs.
Technical Proficiency:Experience with organizational software systems (database, CRM/membership systems, financial software, communication platforms, and IT/cybersecurity basics).
Knowledge of Jewish Community Life:Understanding and respect for Reform Jewish values, traditions, and congregational dynamics.
Strategic Thinking:Ability to translate board vision into operational plans, anticipate future needs, and build systems that support long-term growth and stability.

Job Summary

The Director of Operations and Outreach (DOO) leads the strategic business management and tactical operation of the Chemistry of Life Process Institute. The DOO innovates, implements and continually enhances the Institute’s programs and plans to ensure excellence at all levels. Proactively interfacing with Institute senior management, executive committee and advisory board, the DOO manages current initiatives and long-term planning in support of the Institute’s education, research and outreach mission. The DOO fosters the collaborative spirit of the institute with alliances both internal and external to the University.

This position will support the Faculty Director, as described above. The mission of The Chemistry of Life Processes is three-fold: 1) To lead the world in a proteomics revolution that will catalyze a new wave of innovation in protein chemistry and biology, 2) To converge powerful proteomics and chemical biology platforms with clinical insights to precisely define high value protein targets that will accelerate drug discovery and translation for cancer and neurodegenerative diseases and 3) To train the next generation of scientific leaders at the interface of chemistry and biology. Staff within the Institute support this mission and are an integral part of the Institute’s success.

Specific responsibilities include: multidisciplinary research institute development, strategic and operations planning, staff hiring and cross-functional team development, oversight of research administration, budget and financial operations, research and interdisciplinary program development and implementation, fund raising collaboration, public-private sector partnership development (with the university’s central offices, including global alliances), executive and board-level engagement, communications and marketing team management; creative/proactive ideas and strategy input and support.

Specific Responsibilities

Management of Operations

Develops the vision, mission and operating principles of institute.
Creates and maintains the infrastructure operating plan and process to enable efficient operations and compliance with University and funding agency policy.
Orchestrates and coordinates activities of many people in various departments to provide seamless support for the Institute’s operations and research programs.
Determines the staff organization structure and supervises the recruitment, hiring, training and performance management of any new administrative staff.Continually stays abreast of external regulations.
Manages capital and operating budget planning, purchasing and payroll expenditures, and regular reconciliation and reporting to ensure sound financial/fiscal management.
Manages administrative aspects of space planning and other resource deployment.
Coordinates with other budgeting units within the University.

Internal and External Relations

Works with the Director and leadership team to support the Institute’s growth, development, and expand internal and external relationships

Supervisory

Bachelor’s in business, accounting or a related field with 5 or more years’ experience in administrative or supervisory capacity with exposure to a combination of budgets, finance, grant administration, facilities, staff supervision, &/or human resources.
5+ year’s management experience with progressively larger responsibilities.
Interest in the business of higher education and research.
Knowledge of Word, Excel and PowerPoint or similar packages; familiarity with web development.

Minimum Competencies: (Skills, knowledge, and abilities.)

Proven communication, interpersonal and analytic skills.
Adept at project management.Ability to work under pressure, prioritize and meet deadlines.
Demonstrated competency in organization management and financial stewardship.
Proactive, energetic, innovative.
Ability to work independently and yet is an accomplished team player.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledgeable on proteomics or related field as applies to Center mission
Previous management experience in a university environment.

Responsible for quality, safety, workforce, and patient experience outcomes. Develops, monitors, and ensures achievement of short- and long-range goals.

Posted Job Title

Executive Director, Strategic Communications

Job Profile Title

Executive Director A, Business and Finance

Job Description Summary

The Executive Director (ED) of Communications is the senior communications leader for the Office of the Executive Vice President (EVP) and its nine divisions. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, the ED is responsible for designing, building, and leading a newly integrated communications organization that supports the University's administrative enterprise. The Executive Director develops and executes a comprehensive communications strategy aligned with the organization's strategic priorities, brand, and stakeholder needs while leading a high-performing communications team.

Serving as the principal communications advisor to the Executive Vice President and Vice Presidents across administrative divisions, the Executive Director leads the strategic communications function, shaping executive messaging, media relations, reputation management, marketing, and change communications in support of divisional and institutional priorities. The role develops and executes an integrated communications strategy that strengthens stakeholder trust, advances strategic initiatives, and elevates the visibility and impact of the University's administrative enterprise. The Executive Director partners closely with University Communications and leaders across the institution to ensure coordinated, consistent messaging and alignment and provide trusted counsel on high-profile institution-wide initiatives, emerging issues, and reputational matters.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

Organizational Leadership

Build and operationalize a newly integrated communications organization serving the EVP Office and its divisions, establishing the vision, governance, operating model, and communications standards for the function.
Align communications resources, processes, and priorities to deliver integrated, strategic communications that support the organization's goals and stakeholders.
Establish service delivery models that balance enterprise initiatives with divisional needs across the EVP organization.

Strategy and Executive Communications

Develop and execute a comprehensive communications strategy that advances the organization's strategic priorities, strengthens its brand, engages key stakeholders, and ensures consistent internal and external messaging across the administrative enterprise.
Advise the Executive Vice President and divisional leaders on executive communications, strategic messaging, reputation management, organizational change, and emerging issues.
Oversee executive communications, including speeches, presentations, talking points, leadership messaging, and thought leadership.
Coordinate communications across the EVP divisions and partner closely with University Communications and other key stakeholders on media relations and issues requiring a coordinated approach.

Media Relations, Marketing, and Content Strategy

Lead proactive and reactive media relations and crisis communications for the organization.
Advance the organization’s visibility, reputation, and impact through strategic communications, marketing, and issues management.
Oversee integrated storytelling and content strategy across websites, newsletters, executive communications, intranet/extranet, social media, video, print, and other digital channels.
Identify and implement emerging communications tools, technologies, and practices that strengthen organizational effectiveness.

Team Leadership and Operations

Lead, mentor, and develop the communications team, supporting nine divisions across all communications functions.
Foster a collaborative, service-oriented culture focused on innovation, accountability, continuous improvement, and effective change management.
Manage the communications budget, vendors, and major communications initiatives.
Establish performance metrics and use data to evaluate impact and continuously improve communications strategy, channels, and outcomes.

Qualifications

Master's degree plus 7 – 10 years of progressively responsible communications leadership experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated success advising senior executives and leading strategic, executive, media, crisis, digital, and change communications.
Experience building and leading teams, managing budgets, and overseeing vendor relationships.
Exceptional writing, editing, project management, and interpersonal communication skills.
Demonstrated judgment, professionalism, and experience navigating complex organizational environments and advising senior leaders.

Skills and Competencies

Organizational design and change management, with experience standing up or restructuring an organization or function.
Sound judgment in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
Executive presence and the ability to counsel senior leaders under pressure or on sensitive issues.
Crisis and issues management.
Talent development and team building across disciplines.
Data-informed decision making and use of metrics to guide strategy.
Vendor management.

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

The Office of the Executive Vice President provides strategic leadership and oversight for the University's business, financial, operational, and administrative functions through nine divisions: Audit, Compliance and Privacy; Budget Planning and Analysis; Business Services; Facilities and Real Estate Services; Finance; Human Resources; Information Systems and Computing; Investments; and Public Safety.

The EVP portfolio encompasses diverse communications needs, including executive and Board communications, regulatory reporting, employee engagement, organizational change, operation communications, media relations, marketing, public affairs, and student-facing communications. Supporting this breadth requires the Executive Director to build a flexible, integrated communications function capable of tailoring strategies to the unique needs of each division while ensuring consistent messaging across the University’s administrative enterprise.

# CEO Wanted — Equity-Only Partnership

**Location:** Remote / Flexible
**Compensation:** 100% Equity (No Salary)
**Commitment:** Full-Time
**Travel: ** 50% of the time

---

## The Opportunity

We've built a new AI based software product and are looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial CEO to take the reins, bring it to market, and scale it into a major player in the space. This is not a traditional executive hire — it's a partnership. You won't be drawing a salary; instead, you'll earn a significant equity stake and share directly in the value you help create.

If you've led a company through go-to-market, scaled a product from early traction to real revenue, and want to build something you own a piece of, we want you.

---

## What You'll Be In Charge Of

- **Fundraising** — Your initial primary objective will be to represent the company to investors and lead funding rounds
- **Go-to-Market Strategy** — Over time you will also define positioning, pricing, and the launch plan that gets this product in front of the right customers
- **Revenue & Growth** — Continue to build the sales, marketing, and customer acquisition plan from the ground up

---

## What We're Looking For

- Proven experience as a CEO or a senior executive who has taken a product to market successfully
- A track record of driving revenue growth, ideally in B2B software
- Strong understanding of marketing, sales, and customer acquisition strategy in the biotech industry
- Hunger to build something from the ground up

---

## Required Qualifications

Master's degree or equivalent professional experience
Minimum 3–4 years of experience in a management role or equivalent
Held a major leadership role in a start-up environment

---

## Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of relevant work experience in the biotech industry
A track record of bringing start-ups to market and successfully exiting them

---

## Compensation Structure

This role is **100% equity-based** — there is no base salary. Specific equity terms will be discussed directly with qualified candidates.

---

## How to Apply

Send us:
1. A brief note on your relevant CEO/executive experience and what you've taken to market before and why this opportunity excites you
2. Your resume or CV

We're looking for the right long-term partner, not just a hire — so tell us why that's you.

---

*Note: Because this role offers no cash salary, this opportunity is best suited for someone who can operate without salary income.*

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
High Museum of Art is pleased to partner with DRG to conduct this search.

Background

Located in the heart of Atlanta, the High Museum of Art is acclaimed for its extensive and diverse programming, and its commitment to accessibility and engagement. With more than 300,000 square feet of light-filled spaces designed by noted architects Richard Meier and Renzo Piano, and a growing collection that exceeds 19,000 items, the High Museum is widely recognized as the Southeast’s leading art museum. As the High approaches its 100th anniversary in October 2026, the Museum continues to gain national and global recognition.

Guided by Director Rand Suffolk and an exceptional team and Board of Directors, the High strives to provide exhibitions and educational programs that challenge and inspire the Museum’s diverse audience of regional and global visitors.

To support the Museum as it continues to strive for excellence, the High seeks a Chief Operating Officer (COO) with strong operational, logistic, and partnership building skills to help guide the impact of the leading cultural institution of the American South. The COO will operationalize the Museum’s commitment to providing access to dynamic and compelling visual art and programming for all.

About the High Museum of Art

The Museum has been intentional about listening to feedback from the Atlanta community while seeking to captivate both the High’s local and global audiences. Since 2018, the Museum leadership has added nearly five thousand objects to the permanent collection, intentionally acquiring works that reflect the High’s current and prospective audiences.

The organizational values of Inclusivity, Collaboration, Connectivity, and Growth inform the High’s engagement with patrons, the thoughtfulness of its exhibitions, and its internal culture. This framework is grounded in a commitment to Atlanta’s diverse community.

Working closely with the Director and other senior leaders, the COO will be charged with developing the systems that support the work of the High Museum, allowing the High to fully engage in its purpose and commitments to Atlanta and beyond.

The Opportunity

The COO will be a leader of integrity, entrusted with overarching operational responsibilities. Strategic and tactical, fluent in data and trends, the COO will play a significant role in the High’s growth and scaling. The COO will be the thought leader in organizational matters, leading efforts for process improvements. The Chief Operating Officer will be a skilled communicator and convener, facilitating collaboration that supports the Museum’s path forward.

Key Responsibilities

Develop a strong, effective partnership with the Director that ensures strategic, anticipatory management of the Museum and its programs.
In consultation with the Director, forge and implement the museum’s long and short-range strategic planning efforts to develop multi-year budgets, evaluate progress of museum activity against established goals and relevant benchmarks, and ensure plans are revised and updated as necessary to respond to market conditions.
Seek out and bring best practices of museum strategic operations to ensure the continual improvement of the High.
In tandem with the Director and CFO, institute rigorous, best-in-class processes in budgeting and financial planning and analysis, cost management, program improvement metrics and/or policy changes. Create strong integration and collection of data and lead a cross-departmental team to understand how data can be used strategically to meet revenue and programmatic goals.
Optimize technology across the organization to enhance and streamline museum-wide workflow and identify technological solutions to automate and/or improve finance and accounting functions.
Guide senior leadership in designing and integrating strategic, multi-year planning and goal setting to achieve desired results and support the High’s objectives.
Provide proactive, creative and effective leadership around increased earned revenue, ensuring the maximum financial contribution of all revenue-generating activities of the High including the store, rental activities, admissions, membership and parking operations while reflecting the institution’s mission and high standards.
Serve as a strategic partner to the Chief Financial Officer to interpret budget strategies and short and long-term goals into operation and program expenditure budgets as well as collaborate on reforecasting and refining multi-year philanthropic revenue projections.
Lead the Director of People Success to support and enhance human capital management efforts around staffing, training and overall organizational culture.
Ensure that all operational aspects of the High are aligned with overall objectives and reflect the institution’s core artistic and educational values; uphold high standards for integrity, accuracy, productivity, professionalism and cooperation in the workplace.
Implement and streamline process optimization and role definition, positioning the museum more appropriately for sustainable growth.
Expand applied data to introduce management analytics at all levels.

The ideal candidate possesses the following professional and personal qualities, skills and characteristics:
Professional Experience: The COO will have at least 10 years as a senior operations or administrative leader in an organization of similar size and budget.
Operational Acumen: The COO will be a tactical visionary and creative finance leader with strong quantitative and analytical skills. The COO will transition seamlessly between the “big picture” and minutiae. This leader will bring a high level of intellectual enterprise with a collaborative, creative and service-oriented mindset.
Organizational Efficiency: The COO will proactively bring innovative ideas to the Director around identifying and implementing new earned revenue opportunities that fit within the mission. The COO must have proven experience in budgeting, strategic forecasting and planning, and in overseeing the risk management of a complex organization. The COO will be skilled at presenting information in a clear, confident fashion to a range of constituents with varying levels of expertise.
Building Relationships and Leading Through Influence: The COO will have strong executive presence, engender confidence and lead with authority. The COO will be skilled at quickly establishing rapport and cultivating relationships across all levels of the organization and with Board members. Highly articulate and a deft communicator, the COO will easily convey the High’s successes and opportunities with passion and intensity in written and verbal formats in both formal and informal situations.
Trusted Partner: The COO will foster trust and collaboration among team members and possess the ability to manage through change with flexibility and poise. This leader is an individual with unquestioned integrity, ethics and values; someone who can be trusted with highly confidential and sensitive information.
Results-oriented: The COO will have the skills to provide leadership for a new institutional chapter following a period of significant growth. As the key strategic partner to the Director, the COO will be a sound problem solver with excellent reasoning skills, able to conceptualize and analyze problems and solutions in a proactive, constructive, creative manner that will result in improved performance across the organization.
Passion for the Mission: The COO will bring a passion for the work of the High. This is a leader who understands, and embraces, how the financial and operations functions of the High align to support the museum’s mission.

How We Work

Organizational Structure

The Chief Operating Officer reports to the Director of the High Museum of Art. The COO is part of the senior leadership team which includes the Deputy Director of Philanthropy, the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Communications Officer, Chief Curator, Deputy Director of Collections and Exhibitions, and the Eleanor McDonald Storza Deputy Director for Learning and Civic Engagement. The COO maintains strong collaborative relationships across the Woodruff Arts Center and works closely with the High Museum’s Board of Directors.

The COO oversees the engineering and security teams for The Woodruff Arts Center campus.

Work Environment

The COO role will be expected to work on-site at the High Museum in midtown Atlanta. The team can work remotely one day a week, either Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday.

Salary

$275,000 - $300,000 based on experience.

Benefits

The High Museum of Art offers a competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance, including:
Generous paid time off, including holidays, vacation, personal days, and sick days.
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
Life insurance, short- and long-term disability,
Employee Assistance Program 403(b) retirement

Timeline and Next Steps

If you are interested in this position, please click apply to submit a resume and cover letter. All applicants will receive an email confirming receipt of their application.

Pinnacle Fertility is a leader in physician-centric fertility care, supporting high-performing fertility clinics and comprehensive service providers nationwide. Guided by our mission of fulfilling dreams by building families, Pinnacle offers compassionate care, innovative technology, and comprehensive fertility treatment services to provide patients with a seamless and personalized journey to parenthood. Learn more at www.pinnaclefertility.com.
About the Role

The Chief Operating Officer/Executive Vice President of Operations (COO/EVP)
serves as the executive leader responsible for driving operational excellence across Pinnacle Fertility's national network of fertility clinics, embryology laboratories, and ambulatory surgery centers. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, this leader oversees enterprise operations, practice integration, market expansion, physician partnerships, and operational strategy to ensure consistent performance, exceptional patient experiences, and scalable growth across the organization.  
The ideal candidate is a visionary healthcare executive with extensive experience leading multi-site healthcare operations, building and developing high-performing leadership teams, partnering collaboratively with physicians and executive leaders, and driving large-scale operational transformation. This individual has a proven track record of improving organizational performance, implementing scalable systems and processes, leading integrations and change initiatives, and fostering a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement within a complex, growth-oriented healthcare environment.
Key Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for Pinnacle’s fertility clinics, laboratories, surgery centers, and related patient care operations.
Establish clear operating priorities, performance expectations, and accountability across the network.
Lead and develop executive directors and local operational teams.
Partner with physicians and clinical leaders to improve patient access, workflow, capacity, productivity, and practice performance.
Work with the CEO, CFO, and executive team to achieve financial, growth, and strategic objectives.
Develop meaningful operational metrics and lead regular market and practice performance reviews.
Identify performance gaps and ensure that effective improvement plans are developed and implemented.
Lead the operational integration of acquired and affiliated practices.
Support de novo clinics, service expansion, facility growth, and new market development.
Champion a compassionate, responsive, and consistent patient experience.
Partner with Human Resources to strengthen organizational design, leadership development, workforce planning, engagement, and succession.
Collaborate with technology, quality, compliance, legal, finance, marketing, and revenue cycle leaders to improve enterprise performance.
Lead or contribute to additional initiatives and special projects as assigned.

Position Requirements

Education:
A bachelor’s degree is required. A master’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, or a related field is preferred.
Experience:
At least 10 years of progressive healthcare operations experience.  
Experience in fertility care, women’s health, physician practice management, ambulatory surgery, laboratory operations, private equity-backed healthcare, or an MSO environment is strongly preferred.

Significant senior leadership experience within a complex, multi-site healthcare organization.
Demonstrated responsibility for operational performance, financial results, workforce planning, and organizational growth.
A successful history of partnering with physicians and clinical leaders.
Experience leading change, improving underperforming operations, and developing strong operational leaders.
Experience supporting acquisitions, practice integrations, de novo locations, or rapid organizational growth.  

Skills:
Strong financial, operational, analytical, and strategic capabilities.
The ability to build trust and lead effectively across a geographically dispersed organization.
Excellent judgment, communication skills, emotional intelligence, and executive presence.

Compensation & Benefits

Annual Salary:
Final offers based on experience, skills, and qualifications.
Benefits:
Comprehensive healthcare, dental, life, and vision insurance. Additional benefits include generous paid time off (PTO), paid holidays, and a retirement savings program. Further details regarding salary and benefits will be provided during the interview process.

jobs.description:
In partnership with Lindauer, the University of Louisville Foundation seeks an accomplished Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer to lead at a pivotal moment in the University's future.

In this executive leadership role, the successful candidate will provide strategic direction for finance, investments, governance, operations, and real estate while overseeing the stewardship of approximately $1.6 billion in assets
that support scholarships, faculty excellence, research, and the University's long-term success.

Key Responsibilities

Provide leadership for all financial, business, and administrative operations of ULF with responsibility for the custodianship and investment of all ULF assets.
Oversee ULF’s process for valuing and unitizing its investment portfolio, administer the investment committee’s process, manage ULF’s outsourced Chief Investment Officer (CIO) and evaluate CIO reports and recommendations, and prepare periodic reports, data, and presentations for the ULF Board and the Board of Trustees of the University regarding holdings and investment results.
Steward donations received for the University and ensure adherence with donor intent and fiduciary responsibilities through an ongoing and formal annual compliance review process.
Provide executive oversight of non-endowed assets of ULF to safeguard the assets and invest as appropriate to realize long-term returns for the University.
Develop and administer appropriate gift policies for existing and proposed gifts held under ULF’s fiduciary custody including appropriate acceptance, investment management, distribution, risk management, fee structures, and reporting.
Manage personnel for financial, investment, information technology, technical, and support functions.
Oversee ULF’s operating budget, including submitting an annual budget to the Board for approval.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum of 15 years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience, with at least 10 years leading complex financial, operational, administrative, or business functions and teams.
Experience working in complex mission-driven organizations is desired; experience in higher education or foundations is a plus. Candidates from the private sector with relevant executive leadership experience are also encouraged to apply.
Demonstrated success leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, with experience fostering collaboration, accountability, and organizational excellence.
Significant experience overseeing financial operations, budgeting, investments, treasury, audit, risk management, governance, and strategic planning.
Experience managing or overseeing complex real estate assets, commercial properties, development projects, investment portfolios, or affiliated business entities is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience partnering with governing boards, executive leadership, legal counsel, external advisors, and key institutional stakeholders.
An MBA, Juris Doctor (JD), Master of Finance, Master of Accounting, or other relevant graduate degree is highly desirable.

Lindauer, a national search and talent firm, has been retained to conduct this search on behalf of the University of Louisville Foundation. To apply or nominate a candidate for this role, please visit the Lindauer website at https://www.lindauerglobal.com/.
