jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
The COO Position

Working alongside the President & CEO, the COO will provide senior operational leadership across the Aquarium, ensuring that day-to-day operations, guest experience, staff experience, infrastructure, technology, financial stewardship, and cross-functional execution are aligned in service of the Aquarium’s mission and strategic priorities.

The COO will lead a portfolio of operational functions directly and will work across the executive team to ensure strong coordination among departments, including areas that may not report directly to the COO. As the Aquarium continues to evolve, the COO’s direct reporting structure may shift to best support organizational needs. Currently, the Acting COO supports a team of five, including the Vice President of Marketing, Communications & Experience, the Vice President of Facilities & Operations, the Senior Director of Capital Projects, the Senior Director of Technology and the Sr. Manager for Dive Operations. The COO also works closely with the Board of Directors, President & CEO and executive team, and represents the Aquarium externally with our government and business partners to advance our operational relationships.

As the aquarium evolves its conservation role and vision, the COO’s strategic leadership and integration will be crucial to bringing all aspects of our conservation model together and ensuring optimal delivery of our services

Essential Functions:

While no two days will look alike, we anticipate the COO will devote their time and attention to the following key priorities:

Strategic Leadership & Execution

Partner with the Board of Directors, President & CEO, and executive team to help shape organizational goals, centering the Aquarium’s mission, values, strategic priorities, and collaborative ways of working.
Translate strategic priorities into clear operating plans, milestones, resourcing decisions, accountability structures, and communication rhythms.
Lead ongoing business review and communication of initiatives, report status on implementation progress, and reduce barriers for operational success and accountability.
Model through daily work how to strategize and lead in manner that integrates and advances our inclusion, and regenerative practices in alignment with our S.A.L.I.S.H. Values.

Operational Leadership

Oversee day-to-day operations of the Aquarium with the executive team, ensuring a high-quality guest experience and staff wellbeing.
Implement and advance sustainable/regenerative and equity-centered practices within the Aquarium and advocate for regenerative and equity-centered marine conservation practices beyond our walls.
Prioritize and integrate collaborative relationships and initiatives with Tribes, local government, and our community partners with Aquarium operations and programs.

Financial Management

Support the development, growth, and management of the Aquarium’s overall budget. Help ensure the Seattle Aquarium values, priorities and needs are represented appropriately in the various budgets.
Identify revenue-generating opportunities and manage expenses in close collaboration with the VP of Finance to ensure the Aquarium meets or exceeds its financial objectives.
Identify opportunities to strengthen operational efficiency, resource stewardship, and organizational sustainability through thoughtful prioritization, technology, process improvement, and cross-functional planning.

Team & Organizational Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of collaboration, clear communication, staff wellbeing, and accountable management.
Lead with curiosity and empathy while developing the skillsets of direct reports, building on their strengths and holding them accountable to their decisions and actions.
Provide mentorship and coaching to executive leaders through change, growth, and development processes while fostering a positive, inclusive, and values-aligned culture.
Partner with the President & CEO and executive team to strengthen leadership practices across the Aquarium, supporting clarity, accountability, collaboration, and staff wellbeing at all levels.
Foster innovation, learning, community engagement, and openness to new, creative, intercultural, and collaborative ideas.
Model the Aquarium’s leadership expectations
Build connections among staff, volunteers, and partners, and actively seek to understand the experiences of members of the Seattle Aquarium community with our institution.
Represent the Aquarium at local, regional, Tribal, and international conferences and events, with the press and media, and through boards, coalitions, and committees.
Serve as a key thought partner to the President & CEO by providing insight rooted in thoughtful analysis of the organization’s operations, finances, and culture, surfacing risks and opportunities early, and offering candid perspective that strengthens decision-making.
To work and engage others in line with the Aquarium’s Mission, D.E.I and S.A.L.I.S.H values.

What You Bring:

Delivering on our bold, urgent mission takes people from every background. The Seattle Aquarium is committed to building a workforce and community rich in diverse identities, languages, cultures, and life experiences. Candidates will be evaluated on the full range of their lived and learned experience and core competencies, including:

Passion for the Aquarium’s mission, of Inspiring Conservation of our Marine Environment and commitment to advancing the Aquarium’s SALISH values .
10+ years of proven senior leadership experience in a complex, mission-driven, and/or visitor-serving organization, ideally including nonprofit, aquarium, zoo, museum, cultural institution, conservation, or public-facing operations experience, with a successful track record of creating operational excellence.
Proven ability to create operational excellence while leading through change, growth, ambiguity, adaptive challenges and evolving organizational priorities in a way that maintains trust, clarity, engagement, and accountability.
Ability to translate organizational strategy into clear operating plans, milestones, resource decisions, accountability structures, and communication rhythms.
Strong operational execution and process discipline, including the ability to design, implement, and improve systems, workflows, SOPs, and decision-making structures that support both consistency and adaptability.
Strong financial and business acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, revenue opportunities, expense management, resource stewardship, risk assessment, and operational tradeoffs.
Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop senior leaders while building trust, accountability, collaboration, and healthy communication across diverse teams.
Ability to use data, financial information, guest insights, operational indicators, and staff feedback to assess organizational health, identify issues early, and make informed decisions.
Strong relationship-building and communication skills, and experience working effectively with executive teams, boards, staff, external partners, Tribal partners, community partners, government partners, funders, and other key stakeholders.
Commitment to values-based leadership rooted in equity and regenerative/sustainability practices, with the ability to embed those commitments into operational decisions, budgets, systems, and team culture.
Understanding of, or strong curiosity about, marine conservation, sustainability, regenerative practices, public education, or mission-based visitor-serving organizations. Direct experience in conservation, aquarium, zoo, museum, cultural, or environmental organizations is a plus.
Ability to identify operational, legal, financial, and reputational risks early and to develop and implement effective mitigation strategies.
Excellent verbal, writing, and editing communication skills. Preference for Multilingual or English speakers with comfort and practice communicating across cultural and language differences

A degree, advanced degree, or specific professional certification is not required. Relevant leadership experience, sound judgment, operational depth, and alignment with the Aquarium’s mission and values are the most important qualifications.

jobs.title: Director of Development - College of Arts & Sciences
jobs.description:
Brief Description

Director of Development – College of Arts & Sciences

The Director of Development for the College of Arts & Sciences serves as a strategic fundraising leader advancing the Texas A&M Foundation’s philanthropic mission in support of the college’s academic, research, and student success priorities. This position works closely with college leadership, department heads, faculty, alumni, donors, and Foundation colleagues to identify and pursue transformational philanthropic opportunities that strengthen the College of Arts & Sciences and its impact on Texas A&M University.

This position is based on site in College Station, fostering strong collaboration with campus partners while supporting donor engagement throughout Texas and beyond. The Director of Development is responsible for managing a portfolio of major and principal gift prospects, building meaningful relationships that result in philanthropic investments supporting scholarships, faculty excellence, research initiatives, student experiences, and other strategic priorities across the College of Arts & Sciences.

We are passionate about Texas A&M University and the transformative impact of the College of Arts & Sciences. As the university's largest and most academically diverse college, Arts & Sciences drives discovery, innovation, and education across disciplines that shape our understanding of the world and prepare future leaders. At the Texas A&M Foundation, we strive to be the most trusted philanthropic partner to our university, our donors, and our team. Are you ready to connect passions with purpose and make a meaningful impact?

What you'll do...

Role

As the Director of Development – College of Arts & Sciences
, you will serve as an ambassador of the Texas A&M Foundation and the College of Arts & Sciences by connecting donor interests with institutional priorities. In this role, you will:

Develop and execute strategic fundraising plans aligned with the College of Arts & Sciences' priorities and advancement goals.
Build and manage a portfolio of major and principal gift donors and prospects through strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities.
Secure philanthropic support for scholarships, faculty excellence, research programs, student success initiatives, capital projects, and other strategic opportunities.
Partner closely with college leadership, department heads, faculty, and Foundation colleagues to identify and advance fundraising opportunities.
Conduct donor visits and meaningful engagement activities designed to strengthen relationships and increase philanthropic investment.
Prepare donor correspondence, gift proposals, stewardship reports, and presentations that communicate impact and opportunities for support.
Lead stewardship efforts to ensure donors remain informed, engaged, and connected to the outcomes of their philanthropy.
Represent the Texas A&M Foundation and the College of Arts & Sciences at donor meetings, university events, and regional engagement activities.
Maintain accurate donor records and activity reporting while utilizing Foundation systems to support fundraising efforts and strategic planning.

What we have to offer...

Purpose:
Help advance student success, groundbreaking research, faculty excellence, and academic innovation within the College of Arts & Sciences.

Competitive total compensation package with performance-based incentives.
Comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, life insurance, identity protection, and more available at no cost to you.
Retirement planning with a 17% employer contribution toward your retirement.
Opportunities for professional growth and development within a mission-driven organization.
Collaboration with a passionate team dedicated to supporting Texas A&M University's future.

What we require...

Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of 3+ years of fundraising experience, including major gift solicitation, or equivalent experience in sales, business development, or relationship management with demonstrated success.
Proven ability to build and maintain productive relationships with diverse stakeholders.

jobs.title: Director of Development, Department of Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
jobs.description:
The Director of Development will direct the overall strategy and fundraising operation on behalf of Johns Hopkins University and for a smaller development office (DOFF), department, area or division. The Director will play a significant role in department or DOFF operations, which includes serving as a member of its senior administrative team, and providing substantial input into the strategy and management of its philanthropic priorities and stewardship including major gift cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, annual giving, and constituent engagement and may include oversight of other portfolios such as corporate and foundation giving, alumni relations, stewardship and events. The Director will manage and set goals for a team in support of Johns Hopkins’ ambitious fundraising goals.

The Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery currently raises $1M-$2M annually in philanthropic support but is poised for significant growth as it expands its faculty, clinical programs, research enterprise, educational initiatives, and global reach. This role will be responsible for building a proactive and sophisticated fundraising program capable of identifying, cultivating, and securing support from major donors, grateful patients, foundations, alumni, and other philanthropic partners.

The Director of Development will serve as the department’s chief fundraising strategist and build and manage a comprehensive major and principal gifts program. Working in close partnership with Dr. St. John, faculty leaders, grateful patients, alumni, and institutional partners, the Director of Development will develop and execute fundraising strategies that secure critical support for research, education, and patient care, and strategic initiatives.

Founded in 1914, the Johns Hopkins Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery has over a century of history in clinical excellence and research innovation. It pioneered American sinus surgery, established the first US temporal bone lab, and is a global leader in cancer care. Today, the department is directed by renowned surgeon and physician-scientist Dr. Maie St. John, MD, PhD, Andelot Professor of Laryngology and Otology.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Lead a complex team of professional and support staff, including directing personnel actions such as hiring, performance appraisals, promotions and transfers, and vacations schedules, among others. Direct reports will typically include at least two fundraising professionals, and will include an additional area such as communications, finance or data.
Implement fundraising strategies and priorities for a complex division or department(s). Evaluate and update strategies as needed to meet long- and short-range goals and objectives to ensure the successful completion of individual and cumulative team solicitation and fundraising goals. Oversee the strategy and execution of all stewardship efforts for specific department(s) and/or division(s).
Create and implement strategies for pipeline building through data analytics and outreach.
Oversee, mentor, and motivate team members by assigning tasks, monitoring performance, resolving conflicts and ensuring compliance with JHU policies to achieve organizational goals. Ensure that the team is well-supported to reach its goals and is engaged in activities that support development in various parts of the organization.
Align team activities towards building, strengthening, and sustaining relationships with key stakeholders to advance departmental and organizational priorities.
Cultivate and maintain an active portfolio of major and principal gift level donors and prospects, engage directly in the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individuals, foundations, and/or corporations. Individual fundraising goals should consistently be $1M or greater.
Develop and execute personalized cultivation strategies to engage and build relationships with prospects.
Build and maintain strong relationships with faculty and administrative leaders and fundraise to support and execute their vision for the particular unit. Work with the leader to maximize the appeal and giving potential for donors by shaping and refining the philanthropic strategy for the assigned unit. Create strong working relationships with the various divisions and departments across the university.
Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of school/divisional/departmental mission, history, teaching, research, and/or clinical programs to effectively communicate funding opportunities. Stay abreast of school/divisional/departmental collaborative partnerships, priorities, and shared goals. Train and debrief internal colleagues on current priorities and cases for support.
Lead the recruitment and management of the department’s volunteers and advisory board, leveraging volunteerism toward giving.
Ensure compliance with all relevant regulations and ethical standards. Advocate and ensure donor intent is honored in funds distribution and utilization. Represent the department(s) and/or division at public events and speaking engagements.
May manage personnel and operating budgets directly or at the direction of a senior leader.
Collaborate with DAR leadership on high-priority, high-visibility tasks.
Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties described above, the Director of Development will:

Collaborate directly and autonomously with the Chief Administrator and Chief Financial Officer to advance department-wide strategic priorities and fundraising initiatives, including budget planning, revenue projections, and philanthropic forecasting. Ensure clear, consistent communication and alignment with the Department Chair and Chief Administrator.
Oversee the development team’s operations, including gift processing, donor acknowledgments, and stewardship, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and full compliance with donor intent and organizational standards.
Partner effectively and transparently with development colleagues across JHM, particularly within the National Capital Region-affiliated hospitals and practices, to advanced shared fundraising priorities, support the needs of faculty and patient care teams, and ensure philanthropic opportunities are aligned with both departmental objectives and the strategic goals of partner institutions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree.
Seven years professional level related experience, including one year of supervisory/management experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.description:
**About the Position**

The Director of Development is Fight For The Forgotten's first full\-time fundraising hire and chief architect of the organization's development program. This is a builder's role: part strategist, part implementer, fully invested in FFTF's mission to end slavery, violence, and preventable death among the world's most forgotten people. The Director will design and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy that manages and deepens existing donor relationships, professionalizes CEO\-led donor engagement and follow\-up, expands institutional giving, and builds the systems, processes, and infrastructure needed for FFTF to scale its philanthropic revenue over the long term.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the Director of Development is both a hands\-on fundraiser and a strategic partner, working closely with the CEO to manage his donor relationships and correspondence, ensure timely and thoughtful follow\-up, and translate his vision and frontline credibility into a compelling case for giving. This role is ideal for a seasoned frontline fundraiser ready to build a development function from the ground up, or an experienced development manager ready to take full ownership of an organization's fundraising program.

**About Fight for the Forgotten**

Fight for the Forgotten (FFTF) is a nonprofit on a mission to defeat hate with love. Founded by MMA fighter Justin Wren, FFTF partners with the Batwa Pygmy people of Uganda and Eastern Congo to restore dignity and build lasting, self\-sufficient futures through land ownership, clean water, health care, education, and livelihood opportunities.

**Core ResponsibilitiesFundraising Strategy \& Execution**

* Design and implement a comprehensive annual development plan with clear revenue goals, strategies, and timelines across all contributed revenue streams.
* Manage a personal major gifts portfolio, typically 40–75 donors and prospects, with responsibility for cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* Oversee and personally contribute to grant prospecting, writing, and reporting for foundation and government funders.
* Lead annual fund strategy, including direct mail, digital giving, and mid\-level donor programs.
* Plan and execute fundraising events and donor cultivation activities.
* Set and monitor monthly revenue targets; provide regular pipeline reporting to the CEO and board.

**Donor Relations \& Communications**

* Build and maintain high\-trust relationships with individual, corporate, and foundation donors.
* Ensure consistent, timely, and meaningful donor acknowledgment and recognition.

**Infrastructure \& Operations**

* Maintain and improve CRM data integrity; establish consistent processes for donor tracking, moves management, and reporting.
* Develop and document fundraising policies, procedures, and systems that scale with organizational growth.
* Manage the development budget with attention to cost\-effectiveness and return on investment.

**Board \& Leadership Partnership**

* Partner with the CEO to begin engaging board members as ambassadors, connectors, and solicitors.
* Provide regular reporting and data\-driven analysis to inform organizational decision\-making.

**QualificationsYou Might Be the Right Fit If...**

* You have 5–7 years of progressive fundraising experience, with demonstrated success in major gifts.
* You are a skilled relationship\-builder who leads with curiosity and genuine interest in donors as partners.
* You thrive in organizations where you wear many hats and your fingerprints are on the work.
* You understand how to motivate and manage up, creating trust and momentum with the CEO and board.
* You are a clear, compelling writer and comfortable with both data analysis and storytelling.
* You bring an entrepreneurial spirit and a track record of building or significantly growing a fundraising program.
* You hold yourself and others to high standards — and you know how to make the work enjoyable along the way.

**Preferred Experience**

* Proficiency with fundraising CRM platforms (Salesforce, Bloomerang, or similar).
* Experience fundraising for international NGOs.
* Experience fundraising alongside a celebrity, public figure, or high\-profile founder/spokesperson.

**Position Details**

**Reports To**

Founder \& CEO

**Location**

Austin, TX

**Hours**

Full\-time, exempt; some evening and weekend availability required

**Compensation**

$115,000 \- $130,000 commensurate with experience

**Travel**

This role requires up to 50% travel including:

* Domestic: Donor visits, staffing CEO speaking engagements, and conferences (40%)
* International: Potential for international travel to Uganda and Eastern Congo to visit program sites \& build donor stewardship content (10%)

*Fight for the Forgotten is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive team. Candidates from underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply.*

Pay: $115,000\.00 \- $130,000\.00 per year

The Director of Development is YWCA St. Paul’s senior fundraising leader, responsible for growing contributed revenue through a disciplined fundraising strategy, strong donor relationships and reliable development systems. The role leads major gifts and individual giving, donor stewardship, fundraising data and performance management, while providing strategic guidance to the Grants Manager.

This position is intentionally focused on fundraising. Marketing, communications and broader community engagement are led by other staff or contractors; the Director works with those partners to develop effective donor\-facing messages and materials.

**Essential Responsibilities \& Approximate Time Allocation**

*Time allocations are approximate and may shift based on campaigns, deadlines and organizational priorities.*

**Fundraising Strategy, Major Gifts \& Leadership — 55%**

* Develop and lead an annual fundraising plan with clear revenue goals, strategies, timelines, ownership and performance measures.
* Build, qualify and actively manage a portfolio of current and prospective major donors.
* Lead donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, closing and follow\-up, with tailored strategies based on donor interests, capacity and connection to the mission.
* Strengthen annual, recurring, reactivation and donor\-upgrade strategies; develop planned giving opportunities as capacity grows.
* Maintain a diversified funding strategy and translate organizational priorities, program outcomes and capital needs into compelling cases for support.
* Monitor fundraising performance, pipeline health, risks and opportunities; provide regular forecasts and recommendations to the CEO, finance leadership and Board.
* Prepare the CEO, Board members and other ambassadors for donor meetings and solicitations.
* Lead philanthropy staff and resources as assigned, establishing clear expectations, accountability and ethical fundraising practices.

**Donor Stewardship \& Engagement — 20%**

* Implement a consistent, personalized stewardship approach that strengthens donor retention, engagement and lifetime value.
* Ensure timely gift acknowledgments, recognition, impact reporting and follow\-up on donor commitments and restrictions.
* Create meaningful donor touchpoints and mission experiences in partnership with program staff.
* Collaborate with marketing and communications staff or contractors on donor stories, appeals, campaigns and impact materials.
* Support institutional funder stewardship and represent YWCA St. Paul at select donor and fundraising events.

**Development Operations, Data \& Grants Coordination — 25%**

* Ensure the donor database is accurate, complete and consistently used for relationship management, reporting and forecasting.
* Establish sound workflows for gift entry, acknowledgments, contact reports, prospect stages, pledge tracking and data hygiene.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including revenue, retention, acquisition, upgrades, portfolio activity and pipeline value.
* Partner with finance to reconcile contributed revenue, track restrictions and maintain consistent reporting across systems.
* Provide strategic guidance and prioritization to the Grants Manager so grant activity aligns with organizational strategy, capacity and revenue goals.
* Maintain visibility into the grants pipeline, calendar, probability, reporting obligations and results without serving as the primary grant writer.
* Help shape institutional funding strategies and cases for support, coordinating with program and finance leaders as needed.

**Qualifications/Required**

* At least five years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including demonstrated success with individual giving and major gifts.
* A record of developing fundraising strategies, personally soliciting significant gifts and producing measurable revenue growth.
* Strong knowledge of donor stewardship, moves management, prospect development and fundraising performance measurement.
* Experience using a donor database or CRM to manage portfolios, maintain clean data and produce useful reports and forecasts.
* Ability to turn organizational priorities and program impact into compelling cases for support.
* Excellent relationship\-building, communication, judgment, organization and follow\-through.
* Experience working effectively with executive leaders, staff and nonprofit Board members.
* Commitment to YWCA St. Paul’s mission to eliminate racism, empower women, and promote peace, justice, freedom and dignity for all.
* Equivalent combinations of education, professional experience and demonstrated results will be considered; a four\-year degree is not required.

**Preferred**

* Seven or more years of fundraising experience, including leadership of a development or philanthropy function.
* Experience in a multi\-program human services, health, housing, workforce or social justice organization.
* Experience guiding grant strategy and collaborating with dedicated grant staff.
* Experience with capital campaigns, planned giving or corporate partnerships; CFRE or relevant professional development.

**Working Conditions**

This role requires regular computer use, local travel for donor meetings and events, and occasional evening or weekend work. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Equal Opportunity**

YWCA St. Paul is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in the E\-Verify program.

Pay: $110,000\.00 \- $120,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

**Chief Operating Officer**

**The Opportunity**

Everest Franchise Brands, LLC is a founder\-led, multi\-brand franchisor headquartered in Miami, operating and launching fitness and wellness franchise concepts. Our current portfolio includes StretchMed (35 locations, assisted\-stretching) and Get In Shape For Women (16 locations, small\-group personal training with a newly relaunched model), with four new concepts in the launch pipeline: GOLF 100 (a members\-capped indoor golf studio concept, next to launch in one of franchising's fastest\-growing categories), FIT28, CLUB150, and a new Pilates brand. We intend to keep adding brands to the platform, and we are building for the long game: our intention is to take our parent company, Everest Global Brands, Inc., public once all brands are scaling — and keep building from there. This is not a build\-to\-flip platform.

We are hiring our first Chief Operating Officer — the true \#2 to the founder. This is not a caretaker role, and the mandate is deliberately phased. Your first mission is focused: stabilize and strengthen StretchMed and Get In Shape For Women — franchisee success, unit economics, support quality, and a disciplined operating cadence across 51\+ locations. The founder will personally lead the initial launches of GOLF 100, FIT28, CLUB150, and the new Pilates concept; as the core brands become solid under your leadership, each new brand transitions into your operating system and your scope grows with the platform. The founder is the Visionary: deal flow, brand creation, launches, franchise development, big relationships. You are the Integrator: everything else.

If you are a proven franchise operations leader — currently a VP or senior Director at a larger system — who is one seat away from running your own platform, this is that seat.

**What You Will Own**

The operating system of the company. You will install and run a disciplined daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly operating cadence — initially across StretchMed and GISFW: brand scorecards, KPI reviews, priority\-setting, and issue resolution. When operational priorities conflict, you decide — the founder is no longer the tiebreaker for daily operations. The cadence you build becomes the template every future brand plugs into.

Franchisee success and unit economics. You own franchisee support, validation, and retention across StretchMed and Get In Shape For Women — including support workflows, field coaching, compliance (e.g., ensuring every StretchMed location maintains its required dedicated full\-time, non\-stretching manager), and the health of unit\-level P\&Ls across 51\+ locations.

Brand\-level EBITDA and margin. This is the scoreboard. Your bonus is anchored to the EBITDA of the core brands because healthy margin is what funds everything this platform does next — new brand development, the growth of the team, and the path to a public offering. You will own the cost structure, royalty collection health, support efficiency, and margin discipline of the operating business, and you will report EBITDA against plan monthly.

The path to a multi\-brand platform. GOLF 100 launches next, followed by FIT28, CLUB150, and the new Pilates brand — all under the founder's personal leadership. Your job in year one is to make the core brands so solid that absorbing the new ones is straightforward. As each new brand validates, you will onboard it into your operating system — scorecards, support, playbooks — and codify what the founder learned in launch into repeatable process. Protecting the core business while the founder builds the new is the whole point of this seat.

A distributed team of approximately 15\. Direct reports will include a Director of Training (a hire you will help select), a Franchise Business Coach covering StretchMed and GISFW, and a talented shared\-services organization spanning marketing and creative, real estate and buildout, legal and admin, and franchisee support. You will organize, develop, and hold this team accountable.

Org design and key hires. Within your first 90 days you will deliver an organizational assessment and own subsequent hiring, restructuring, and performance decisions for the operations organization. A critical secondary benefit of this role: by owning the core brands completely, you free the founder to focus exclusively on new\-brand launches without the existing business losing altitude.

**Who You Are**

You are a systems builder with operator's speed. You have spent your career turning founders' ideas into playbooks, and playbooks into consistent multi\-unit execution. You are energized — not exhausted — by a founder who moves fast and changes direction, because you know how to catch what they launch and make it stick.

The experience profile we are looking for:

**7\+ years of multi\-unit or franchise operations leadership, with at least 3 years at Director/VP level inside a franchisor (fitness, wellness, boutique retail, or service brands strongly preferred).**

**Demonstrated franchisee\-facing experience: you have owned validation scores, support functions, or field coaching, and franchisees would vouch for you by name.**

**Turnaround or stabilization experience: you have taken over a brand or region facing headwinds and restored franchisee confidence, validation scores, and unit economics. (New\-market or new\-concept launch experience is a plus for the platform's future, but stabilization is the first job.)**

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
The Peoria Riverfront Museum—**the only multidisciplinary museum of its kind in the nation**—is seeking a bold, strategic, and creative leader to serve as our next **Director of Marketing and Communications**.

This is not simply a marketing role. It is an opportunity to shape the voice and visibility of a dynamic cultural institution that seamlessly integrates **art, science, history, achievement, and cinema** under one roof. The Director will champion our brand, energize our audiences, and position the Museum as an essential cultural destination locally, regionally, and nationally.

If you are a visionary storyteller who thrives at the intersection of strategy, creativity, and leadership—this is your stage.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads the development and execution of the Museum’s comprehensive external marketing and communications strategy. This role drives brand awareness, audience engagement, attendance growth, media visibility, and revenue support.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director oversees media relations, advertising, digital strategy, website management, social media, graphic design, and all external communications. The role also leads the marketing team, manages budgets, evaluates campaign performance, and ensures that every public\-facing message reflects the excellence and innovation of the Museum.

**Strategic Leadership**

**Brand and Content Excellence**

* Lead the creation and curation of compelling content across print, digital, video, and social platforms.
* Oversee production of brochures, publications, website content, social campaigns, signage, photography, and multimedia assets.
* Ensure brand consistency and high visual standards across all channels.
* Ensure marketing materials meet accessibility standards and reflect the Museum's commitment to serving diverse audiences.

**Digital and Media Presence**

* Manage the Museum’s website strategy, design, and maintenance to ensure a dynamic and user\-friendly experience.
* Drive social media engagement and digital storytelling initiatives.
* Cultivate strong relationships with local, regional, and national media to secure impactful coverage.

**Advertising and Vendor Management**

* Strategically purchase and manage advertising across traditional and digital platforms.
* Oversee relationships with creative agencies, designers, printers, and other vendors.

**Measurement and Impact**

* Implement evaluation tools to measure marketing effectiveness.
* Analyze data, interpret campaign results, and adjust strategy for maximum impact.
* Align marketing performance with institutional goals for attendance, membership, and revenue.

**Team and Department Leadership**

* Lead a highly performing team and oversee day\-to\-day operations of the Marketing and Communications Department.
* Lead budgeting, planning, staff supervision, and professional development.
* Oversee departmental hiring, performance management, coaching, disciplinary action and annual evaluations.
* Collaborate with the COO and Director of Finance to develop and manage the annual marketing budget.

**Who You Are**

You are both strategist and storyteller. You understand how to translate mission into message and ideas into action. You thrive in fast\-paced, creative environments and bring energy, organization, and leadership to everything you do.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required (Journalism, Communications, Marketing, or related field preferred).
* Minimum five years of experience writing and editing across print and digital platforms.
* Demonstrated success developing and implementing marketing strategies with measurable results.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills.
* Strong knowledge of local, regional, and national media landscapes.
* Experience managing advertising and vendor relationships.
* Ability to evaluate and integrate innovative media technologies.
* Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Collaborative leadership style with supervisory experience preferred.
* Nonprofit experience preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and standard business applications.

**Work Environment and Physical Requirements**

* Ability to work in a standard office environment using computers and other office equipment for extended periods.
* Visual acuity for reviewing detailed creative work.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and in writing.
* Ability to move throughout the Museum and event spaces to attend meetings and support programs and special events.
* Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds.
* Ability to work evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed to support Museum operations and events.
* Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, conferences, and professional development.

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

*The Peoria Riverfront Museum is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.*

**Why Join the Peoria Riverfront Museum?**

The Peoria Riverfront Museum is a cultural catalyst creating transformative experiences for our community. As the only museum in the country to unite art, science, history, and achievement in a single institution of its scale, we are redefining what a museum can be.

As Director of Marketing and Communications, you will not just promote programs—you will help shape the cultural narrative of an entire region.

If you are ready to lead boldly, think creatively, and make measurable impact, we invite you to apply.

jobs.title: Vice President of Development
jobs.description:
Salary: $105,000 to $120,000

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President of Development leads Catholic Charities San Bernardino & Riverside Counties' fundraising, donor engagement, marketing, grants, and volunteer engagement strategies. The Vice President is responsible for significantly expanding philanthropic support through individual giving, major gifts, planned giving, institutional funding, strategic partnerships, and community engagement while building the systems, team, and culture necessary for sustained long-term growth. This leader serves as a member of the executive leadership team and works closely with the CEO and Board of Directors to advance the organization's mission and financial sustainability.

The successful candidate will combine strategic discipline with authentic relationship building, strong follow-through, sound judgment, and a commitment to Catholic Charities’ mission and culture of continuous improvement. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, continuous learning, and mission-driven service. Promote data-informed decision-making, continuous improvement, and professional growth while cultivating a positive and high-performing team environment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

To successfully fulfill this role, the individual must perform the following duties to a satisfactory standard:

Leadership and Organizational Collaboration

Serve as a member of the organizational leadership team.
Participate in strategic planning, organizational growth initiatives, and long-term sustainability planning.
Collaborate closely with the Chief Executive Officer, Board of Directors, and the Finance, Programs, Development, Marketing and Communications, Community Relations, and Parish Engagement departments.
Assist in developing organization-wide fundraising and visibility strategies.
Support long-term donor engagement and revenue diversification planning.
Participate in Board meetings, committee meetings, and community presentations as needed.

Fundraising Leadership

Develop, execute, and regularly improve a comprehensive annual development plan with clear revenue goals, strategies, timelines, ownership, and performance measures.
Make growing individual giving the central priority, including annual giving, recurring gifts, major gifts, planned gifts, donor upgrades, and donor reactivation.
Personally manage a portfolio of major and planned-gift prospects and lead their identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Build and maintain a disciplined major-gifts pipeline and moves-management process with clear next steps and accountability.
Develop donor acquisition, retention, stewardship, and upgrade strategies that strengthen donor loyalty and lifetime value.
Establish fundraising KPIs, dashboards, forecasts, and regular performance reviews to drive accountability and continuous improvement.
Ensure the donor database, prospect research, gift records, portfolios, acknowledgments, and fundraising reports are accurate, timely, and actionable.
Establish and grow a planned-giving and legacy-giving program, including prospect education, professional-advisor relationships, policies, stewardship, and documented gift intentions.
Evaluate fundraising performance and recommend strategic improvements.

Grants & Institutional Funding

Oversee the Grants Writer and the organization’s institutional funding strategy, including prospecting, proposal development, reporting, compliance, and renewal planning.
Set clear goals and performance expectations for grant writing and evaluate results, deadlines, quality, and return on investment.
Collaborate with program leadership to align grant opportunities with program outcomes and organizational priorities.
Develop long-term internal grant infrastructure.
Identify and pursue capacity-building funding opportunities.
Assist in identifying sustainable funding opportunities aligned with organizational growth goals.

Marketing & Communications

Direct the marketing consultant and align branding, communications, storytelling, and donor messaging with fundraising priorities.
Increase visibility throughout the Inland Empire region.
Develop an annual communications calendar that supports donor acquisition, cultivation, stewardship, planned giving, grants, volunteer engagement, and special events.
Oversee digital marketing, social media, newsletters, donor communications, website updates, and organizational campaigns.
Collaborate with leadership to ensure messaging aligns with organizational mission and priorities.
Support public relations and media engagement opportunities.

Parish & Community Engagement

Develop strong relationships with parishes and diocesan stakeholders throughout the Inland Empire.
Increase parish engagement in organizational programs and initiatives.
Build community partnerships and donor engagement opportunities.
Collaborate with the Community Relations and Parish Engagement departments to strengthen regional outreach efforts.
Serve as a point of contact for donors, community stakeholders, foundations, healthcare partners, and parish leaders.

Volunteer & Community Engagement

Supervise the volunteer manager and integrate volunteer recruitment, engagement, recognition, and conversion into the broader development strategy.
Develop volunteer-to-donor engagement pathways.
Lead the strategy, revenue goals, sponsorships, donor engagement, execution, and post-event evaluation for two annual special events.
Support regional visibility and partnership development.

Strategic Growth & Organizational Sustainability

Assist in positioning CCSBRIV for long-term sustainable growth.
Support strategic growth initiatives related to: donor expansion, healthcare partnerships, housing and homeless initiatives, parish engagement, regional expansion, and technology modernization
Collaborate with leadership to identify emerging funding opportunities and long-term sustainability strategies.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide direct supervision, coaching, accountability, and performance evaluation for:
Individual Giving Manager
Grant Writer
Marketing Consultant
Volunteer Manager
Other development consultants or personnel assigned to the department
Ensure the team works from coordinated plans, shared priorities, clear goals, and measurable outcomes.

Additional comparable duties may be assigned as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

A B.A./B.S. degree from an accredited university in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Philanthropy, Organizational Leadership, or a related field.
CFRE Certification preferred

Experience:

Minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising and development experience, including demonstrated success growing individual giving and securing major gifts
Minimum of five (5) years of successful supervisory or team-leadership experience
Experience in donor development, major gifts, planned giving, annual campaigns, nonprofit leadership, strategic communications, community engagement, and organizational growth preferred.

Skills and Abilities:

General knowledge of nonprofit organizational practices and fundraising systems.
Strong leadership presence and professional demeanor.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
Strong strategic planning capability.
Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and presentation skills.
Ability to build relationships with donors, clergy, organizational leaders, and community leaders.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Strong customer service and relationship management skills.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Experience with donor CRM systems and fundraising analytics.
Strong understanding of marketing and communications strategy.
Commitment to mission-driven leadership, ethical fundraising, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

YEAR ONE EXPECTATIONS

Complete and begin executing a comprehensive development plan centered on measurable individual-giving growth
Grow the qualified individual-donor and major-gift prospect pipeline
Increase recurring donors and recurring-gift revenue
Improve donor retention, upgrades, reactivation, and stewardship
Launch a planned-giving and legacy-giving program
Personally cultivate and solicit a defined portfolio of major and planned-gift prospects
Implement accurate donor reporting, dashboards, forecasting, and moves management
Successfully lead two annual special events with defined revenue, engagement, and return-on-investment goals
Set and evaluate performance goals for grants, marketing, volunteer engagement, and external consultants
Strengthen development systems, team performance, collaboration, and continuous-improvement practices

LONG-TERM PERFORMANCE METRICS

Individual-giving revenue growth
Donor retention percentage
Monthly donor growth
Major-gift and planned-gift pipeline growth
Planned-gift commitments and documented legacy intentions
Grant revenue, renewal rate, compliance, and on-time reporting
Donor acquisition cost, campaign response, and marketing conversion metrics
Volunteer growth, retention, and donor-conversion measures
Special-event net revenue, sponsorship growth, and donor conversion
Long-term donor lifetime value

PHYSICAL, MENTAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to travel throughout San Bernardino and Riverside Counties as needed.
Work in diverse settings, including office environments, community events, donor meetings, parish meetings, and organizational functions.
Occasionally lift and carry items weighing up to 30 pounds.
Flexibility to work evenings and weekends as required.

To apply, please submit a cover letter and resume outlining your fundraising leadership experience, accomplishments, and interest in serving as Vice President of Development with Catholic Charities San Bernardino & Riverside Counties. Applications submitted without both documents may not be considered.

jobs.title: Contra Costa County Program Director
jobs.description:
Patients’ Right Program Director (Contra Costa County)

Department:
Directorate Team

Reports To:
Deputy Director

FLSA Status:
Full time, Exempt

Work Location:
In Office; 1350 Arnold Dr, Suite 200, Martinez, CA 94553; Contra Costa County Office.

Schedule:
Full-time, typically Monday- Friday; 37.5 hours per week. Additional hours as required to meet hearing coverage, reporting deadlines and contract requirements.

Position Summary

The Patients' Rights Program Director is accountable for protecting and advancing the statutory and constitutional rights of behavioral health clients served under the Contra Costa County Office of Patients' Rights contract. This role leads program strategy, staff performance, contract compliance, reporting, and stakeholder engagement. The Director ensures advocacy is timely, client-directed, and fully compliant with Welfare and Institutions Code, California Code of Regulations, and County policies.

Leadership Expectations

Set the standard for advocacy quality, responsiveness, and professionalism across the program.
Run a disciplined compliance calendar and hold staff accountable to deadlines.
Build strong county and facility relationships without compromising program independence.
Operate as a risk manager: identify issues early and drive corrective action fast.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure program compliance with all applicable Welfare and Institutions Code requirements, California Code of Regulations, and County policies related to patients' rights advocacy.
Lead and supervise supervisors and advocates, including hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, and performance management.
Ensure timely access standards are met for clients contacting the program directly and through facility referrals.
Oversee advocacy work including Certification Review hearings and other legal proceedings; ensure advocates represent clients' expressed interests.
Oversee investigation and resolution of patients' rights complaints at the lowest level possible and in a timely manner; ensure escalations follow policy.
Ensure completion of monthly and quarterly reports and submission of required attachments to the County, including staff rosters as required.
Ensure Adverse Incident Reports and other reportable event documentation are submitted within 24 hours when required and that corrective actions are tracked.
Lead required outreach activities, including providing patients' rights advocacy training at ED, acute, sub-acute, and residential settings at least twice annually, and annual board and care visits with maintained findings database.
Conduct quarterly input sessions with clients, families, direct care staff, and community partners; provide summary and follow-up plan to the County each quarter.
Represent SWS at County provider meetings and workgroups; ensure program remains current on updates issued through those forums.
Oversee data integrity and equity-focused quality improvement, including analysis to ensure outcomes are not driven by protected characteristics.
Ensure compliance with County requirements related to GenAI technology use and reporting, including notification and discontinuation if directed by the County.
Serve as program spokesperson as assigned; manage stakeholder relationships with hospitals, EDs, and community partners.
Coordinate with leadership on budget, staffing plans, and risk management.
Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5 years experience in patients' rights advocacy, mental health law, healthcare compliance, or a closely related field, including at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Strong working knowledge of LPS processes, hearings, and patients' rights statutory framework.
Proven staff leadership skills, including coaching, corrective action, and building a high-performance culture.
Ability to produce clear written reports and maintain audit-ready documentation.
Strong judgment, discretion, and ability to manage confidential information.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn required county systems and reporting tools.
Valid California driver license and proof of auto insurance; ability to travel to facilities across the county.
Successful completion of DOJ background check.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in a relevant field (law, public health, healthcare administration) or equivalent experience.
Experience working with County behavioral health systems and contract monitoring.

Work Environment

This is primarily an in-person position.
Regular in-person attendance is required at assigned program locations, facilities, community meetings, trainings, and other work-related sites.
With supervisory approval, the employee may work from an approved home office for up to two days per week.
Home-office days are intended primarily for administrative duties, including:
Documentation
Reporting
Scheduling
Correspondence
Other related administrative tasks
The employee must remain available and responsive during all scheduled work hours.
On-site attendance may be required on a scheduled home-office day due to:
Meetings
Staffing needs
Training
Facility matters
Emergencies
Other operational priorities
The home-office arrangement is not guaranteed and may be modified or discontinued based on program or organizational needs.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit for extended periods, travel, and perform facility walk-throughs; ability to lift up to 25 pounds.

Compliance and Performance Expectations

Protect the client’s voice and client choice, while remaining within legal and role boundaries.
Maintain strict confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and county privacy requirements.
Meet all reporting deadlines; late reporting is a compliance risk and will be addressed as performance.
Follow SWS Employee Handbook policies on conduct, attendance, technology use, and safety.
Use only approved technology to store, transmit, or process client information.

jobs.description:
At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms—so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure.

Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users.

Our platform is trusted by over 6 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $257M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive—designed for the speed of modern AI development.

We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you.

Applying to Render

We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team.

We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed.

Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time.

About The Role

We are looking for an Executive Business Partner to support our CEO, VP of Finance, and VP of People. You’ll be a force multiplier across the executive team: managing complex calendars, driving critical follow-through, and, above all, representing these leaders’ voices in writing and in person with precision and polish. Because you’ll routinely draft, edit, and speak on behalf of executives across the company, this role calls for a very high bar for written and verbal communication:
clear, correct, well-organized, and appropriately toned for the audience, every time.

This role is a great fit for someone who embodies Render’s Operating Principles, particularly Own impact and outcomes
(you anticipate needs before being asked), Raise the quality bar
(you take real pride in the quality of every email, deck, and invite that carries a leader’s name), Reason clearly; execute quickly
(you triage and act fast, even with incomplete information), and Build together
(you build trust quickly with a wide range of stakeholders across the company).

What You’ll Do

Own and proactively manage complex, fast-changing calendars across three executives, resolving conflicts and prioritizing time against what matters most
Approach AI as a core productivity partner and proactively use AI to automate scheduling and streamline communications, research, and other daily workflows rather than defaulting to manual processes out of habit or hesitation
Draft, edit, and proofread executive communications including calendar invites, Slack messages, memos, and decks to a consistently high bar for clarity, correctness, and tone, since these often represent the leader’s voice directly

Location: Santa Monica, California (On-site)

Employment Type: Full-Time

Position Summary

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for leading the company's day-to-day operations and executing strategic initiatives to drive operational excellence, productivity, quality, and profitability. The COO will oversee all aspects of plastic fabrication operations, including manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, procurement, quality assurance, maintenance, logistics, environmental health and safety (EHS), and continuous improvement.

Working closely with the CEO and executive leadership team, the COO will develop and implement operational strategies that support business growth, optimize manufacturing processes, improve customer satisfaction, and strengthen the company's competitive position within the plastic fabrication industry.

Essential Responsibilities

Operational Leadership
Manufacturing Excellence
Supply Chain & Procurement
Quality & Compliance
Financial & Business Management
Leadership & Talent Development
Customer & Strategic Partnership
Lead all manufacturing and plastic fabrication operations to ensure safe, efficient, and cost-effective production.
Develop and execute operational strategies aligned with corporate goals and growth objectives.
Oversee production planning, scheduling, inventory management, logistics, warehousing, and distribution.
Monitor plant performance using key performance indicators (KPIs) and implement corrective actions as needed.
Ensure optimal utilization of labor, equipment, and manufacturing resources.
Drive Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Improve manufacturing efficiency, throughput, scrap reduction, yield, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).
Optimize fabrication processes, including cutting, CNC machining, thermoforming, welding, bonding, assembly, and finishing.
Support implementation of automation, robotics, and Industry 4.0 technologies where applicable.
Oversee procurement, sourcing, supplier performance, inventory control, and logistics operations.
Develop strategic supplier relationships to ensure quality, cost efficiency, and on-time delivery.
Improve inventory turnover and working capital performance.
Ensure compliance with ISO 9001, OSHA, EPA, and all applicable environmental, health, and safety regulations.
Lead quality assurance programs to improve product consistency and customer satisfaction.
Drive corrective and preventive action (CAPA) initiatives and continuous quality improvement.
Partner with the CFO to develop operational budgets, forecasts, and capital expenditure plans.
Manage operational costs while maintaining high standards of quality and customer service.
Identify cost-saving opportunities and improve operational profitability.
Support capital investment decisions for equipment, facility expansion, and process improvements.
Build, mentor, and develop high-performing manufacturing and operations teams.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.
Lead workforce planning, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
Promote employee engagement and operational excellence across all departments.
Collaborate with Sales, Engineering, and Customer Service teams to ensure timely delivery and customer satisfaction.
Support new product introductions, product launches, and custom fabrication projects.
Participate in strategic planning, acquisitions, and operational due diligence activities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
MBA or Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 15 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
At least 7 years in an executive operations leadership role such as COO, Vice President of Operations, Director of Manufacturing, or Plant Director.
Extensive experience in plastic fabrication, plastic manufacturing, custom fabrication, industrial manufacturing, or related industries.
Strong knowledge of plastic fabrication processes, including CNC machining, thermoforming, routing, welding, bonding, assembly, and finishing.
Proven experience managing multi-site manufacturing operations.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing operational budgets and P&L performance.
Excellent leadership, communication, and decision-making skills.

Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. The Managing Director of Intelligence is a senior security leader responsible for developing and leading security intelligence efforts to protect the company’s people, assets, operations, and reputation. Reporting to the Chief Security Officer, this role oversees intelligence collection, analysis, reporting, and stakeholder engagement across the business.

Responsibilities:

Intelligence Program Leadership

Design, build, and lead a global intelligence and threat assessment function for the firm.
Develop security intelligence strategies, operating procedures, and reporting frameworks.
Establish intelligence collection, analysis, dissemination, and escalation protocols aligned with business priorities and risk considerations.
Create scalable intelligence capabilities supporting corporate offices, executive protection, employee travel, portfolio companies, and investment opportunities.
Build a high-performing intelligence team with expertise in geopolitical analysis, protective intelligence, investigations, and threat management.

Threat Intelligence & Monitoring

Lead proactive analysis of geopolitical, criminal, terrorism, civil unrest, insider, reputational, and targeted violence threats impacting the firm and its investments.
Deliver strategic intelligence assessments to executive leadership and investment stakeholders.
Establish regional and global threat monitoring capabilities with actionable alerting and escalation processes.

Oversee travel risk intelligence, event security intelligence, and crisis monitoring for global employee deployments.

jobs.title: Senior Managing Director, Healthcare Disputes & Economics, Payer/Provider
jobs.description:
Ankura is a team of excellence founded on innovation and growth.

Practice Overview

Ankura’s Health Care team is a recognized leader in health care and life sciences disputes, compliance, and investigations. The team combines clinical, technical, operational, financial, economic, and analytic expertise to help clients and counsel resolve complex matters involving payers, providers, pharmacies, and law firms.

This role is specifically focused on expanding Ankura’s payer/provider disputes platform: matters where commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, exchange, and other health plan arrangements require rigorous data analytics and defensible damages analysis.

Role Overview

The Senior Managing Director will be an executive-level, self-sustaining rainmaker who originates, sells, leads, and testifies in complex healthcare commercial disputes. The role requires a credible marketplace presence with health plans, law firms, and healthcare-focused private equity or strategic stakeholders.

Primary focus: payer/provider contract, payment, reimbursement, claims, coding, utilization, medical policy, network, and financial disputes.
Core technical differentiator: ability to direct large-scale data analytics teams and translate complex healthcare datasets into clear, supportable damages opinions.
Expected revenue impact: proven, tangible business development record with the ability to produce at least $3M in revenue and a target opportunity to generate $3M to $5M+ annually.
Expert role: serve as a consulting expert or testifying expert, including report development, deposition preparation, arbitration or trial testimony, and expert rebuttal work.

Target Candidate Profile

Market position: Recognized rainmaker in healthcare disputes with established relationships among payer/provider counsel, managed care executives, provider finance leaders, and litigation decision-makers.
Dispute focus: Deep experience in payer/provider commercial disputes, including underpayment, overpayment, contract interpretation, rate methodology, coding, claim adjudication, stop-loss, risk adjustment, value-based care, network adequacy, medical necessity, utilization, denial, recoupment, and reimbursement disputes.
Data analytics leadership: Can lead multidisciplinary teams analyzing large claims, eligibility, encounter, remittance, contract, provider, authorization, utilization, coding, clinical, and financial datasets using scalable, quality-controlled analytics.
Damages expertise: Can develop defensible models for lost revenue, underpayment, overpayment, offsets, recoupments, interest, damages scenarios, counterfactuals, and sensitivity analyses.
Expert witness credibility: Has authored expert reports and provided deposition, arbitration, trial, or hearing testimony in healthcare disputes.

Responsibilities

Business Development and Market Leadership

Originate and expand relationships with national and regional law firms, health plans, pharmacy organizations, and healthcare investors that routinely face payer/provider reimbursement and damages disputes.
Develop a go-to-market plan focused on payer/provider disputes where Ankura can combine healthcare industry expertise, advanced analytics, damages modeling, and expert testimony.
Build a visible marketplace presence through panels, publications, law firm briefings, client training, and industry events focused on managed care litigation, reimbursement disputes, and claims analytics.
Convert marketplace relationships into consulting expert, testifying expert, privileged advisory, and complex analytics engagements.

Technical and Disputes Expertise

Lead matters involving contract breaches, payment disputes, underpayment or overpayment claims, reimbursement methodology, fee schedules, DRG/APC/APG or other payment logic, risk corridors, value-based payment, capitation, shared savings, risk adjustment, denials, recoupments, and claims adjudication issues.
Apply knowledge of commercial, Medicare Advantage, Part D, Medicaid managed care, ACA exchange, pharmacy, and provider reimbursement operations when developing case strategy and damages approaches.
Assess liability and damages theories in collaboration with counsel while preserving attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, and expert independence where applicable.
Prepare expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, deposition testimony, arbitration testimony, trial testimony, and demonstratives that explain complex analytics in plain English.

Large-Scale Data Analytics and Damages

Direct data teams analyzing high-volume healthcare datasets, including claims, encounters, eligibility, premium, membership, remittance, EOB/EOP, authorization, denial, utilization, coding, provider contract, fee schedule, capitation, risk adjustment, and financial data.
Design repeatable analytic workplans that include data intake, normalization, validation, completeness testing, reconciliation, exception handling, sampling or extrapolation where appropriate, quality control, and audit trails.
Develop damages models that quantify alleged underpayments, overpayments, lost revenue, leakage, offsets, recoupment exposure, reasonable value, contract-based damages, and alternative damages scenarios.
Translate analytic findings into counsel-ready narratives, executive presentations, settlement support, mediation materials, expert reports, and trial or arbitration demonstratives.
Partner with data scientists, statisticians, coding experts, clinicians, economists, forensic accountants, and operations professionals to ensure analytic conclusions are technically sound and legally defensible.

Client Delivery and Team Leadership

Serve as the accountable executive on complex, multi-workstream matters with law firm, payer, provider, and board-level stakeholders.
Scope and price engagements, staff teams, manage budgets, review work product, ensure quality, and deliver concise insights under litigation deadlines.
Mentor directors, managing directors, analytics professionals, clinicians, coders, and operational specialists, with a focus on developing future testifying experts and client-facing leaders.
Collaborate across Ankura practices, including Health Economics, Data Analytics including AI, Strategy and Performance, Forensic Accounting, Investigations, and other dispute capabilities.

Relevant Matter Experience

Payer/provider contract disputes involving alleged underpayment, denial, repricing, reimbursement methodology, rate implementation, or recoupment issues.
Managed care disputes involving Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, ACA exchange, commercial group, self-funded, pharmacy, or delegated-risk arrangements.
Large-scale claims and encounter analytics supporting affirmative damages, rebuttal damages, settlement valuation, mediation, arbitration, or trial.
Hospital, physician, ancillary, pharmacy, behavioral health, and specialty provider reimbursement disputes.
Matters requiring expert reports, rebuttal analyses, deposition testimony, arbitration testimony, or trial testimony.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in business, finance, accounting, economics, data analytics, health care operations, health policy, clinical discipline, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of litigation, disputes, forensic, damages, payer/provider reimbursement, managed care, healthcare analytics, or consulting experience; senior consulting leadership experience strongly preferred.
Proven and tangible business development record with a portable book of relationships and revenue generation of at least $3M; demonstrated ability to grow toward $3M to $5M+ annually.
Specific experience originating and leading payer/provider commercial disputes, reimbursement disputes, managed care litigation, claims analytics, damages quantification, or expert witness engagements.
Demonstrated ability to direct large project teams analyzing complex healthcare datasets and producing quality-controlled analytic outputs for counsel, executives, and triers of fact.
Experience authoring expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, affidavits, or damages analyses; prior deposition, arbitration, trial, or hearing testimony strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of healthcare legal, regulatory, reimbursement, and operational issues affecting payers, providers, pharmacies, and government program participants.
Exceptional executive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical, analytic, reimbursement, and damages issues to boards, C-suite clients, law firms, regulators, mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries.
Demonstrated commitment to privilege, confidentiality, work-product discipline, expert independence, collaboration, quality, and team development.
Ability and willingness to travel; must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship now or in the future.
