jobs.description:
ESW is striving to have a measurable impact on 100 communities a year (and 500 a year by 2035) and your role is crucial in creating industry awareness, building relationships, and advancing our fundraising programs in support of our growth sustainability goals.

The  Executive Director
 (ED) serves as Engineers for a Sustainable World’s (ESW) most significant fundraiser and prominent external spokesperson. The ideal candidate will be passionate about sustainability and dedicated to embedding it within engineering. Candidates should be able to articulate a vision for ESW’s role in a rapidly changing world to stakeholders including members, potential and current donors, corporations, and foundations. As an equal member of the Executive Committee, the Executive Director is responsible for helping to grow the organization’s resources to more effectively tackle large problems, supporting a large decentralized team of staff and mostly volunteers in the implementation of our strategic plan, and developing a stronger network of business, nonprofit, and academic partners. This position offers the opportunity to help put sustainability into the education and practice of the next generation of technical students and professionals.

Responsibilities

The Executive Director is a non-compensated position responsible for:

Lead fundraising strategy and obtain dedicated and secure resources for successful operation and program management (60% of the time):
Work with the Development Team to collectively design and execute fundraising activities
Identify and help secure funding from corporations and philanthropists for programs and operating expenses
Guide the planning and implementation of individual fundraising campaigns
Assist with proposal writing to governmental agencies or foundations to fund programs
Develop partnerships for shared resources in the form of in-kind donations and professional expertise 

Build the ESW brand in the form of public and organizational recognition and key partnerships (30%)
Provide representation for ESW at public events and in the media
Identify potential for collaboration and develop connections between ESW and: faculty and staff at institutions of higher education in order to build ESW’s presence on college campuses; engineering and or sustainability-related companies; and existing non-profit networks
Coordinate creation of an Annual Report for public distribution

Support the Organizational Effectiveness and the Achievement of our Strategic Plans (10%)
Act as a strategic partner to the Chief Operating Officer on all internal initiatives and operational improvements
Provide vision and perspective to the team, bringing new ideas for expansion and growth opportunities
Work with the Board of Directors and Leadership Team on strategic planning for both short and long term horizons

Desired Skills and Qualifications

Experience with nonprofit administration
Knowledge or experience in engineering or sustainability is a plus.
Superb verbal and excellent written communication skills and confidence communicating to a wide variety of audiences 
Demonstrated experience meeting funding goals from government and foundation sources and individual fundraising
Experience dealing with a range of organizational stakeholders, including university faculty, non-profit leaders, and businesses
Demonstrated ability to help create, share, and act on a large-scale vision
Management experience a plus
Experience creating and/or managing multi-stakeholder projects and programs Project management
Passion for a sustainable future

About Engineers for a Sustainable World

Engineers for a Sustainable World (ESW) is an international nonprofit network of students & professionals united by their shared passion for technical sustainability. We are dedicated to empowering engineers to tackle sustainability challenges. We believe that engineers, and anyone who loves to solve problems, are key to solving today's biggest sustainability challenges. Founded in 2002, ESW is an international network of over 1,750 members and more than 45 collegiate chapters working to build a more sustainable world through technical hands-on projects. Since its founding, ESW has supported over 500 chapter-led projects in 12 countries and 23 states and Canadian provinces.

Our goals: 
Design:
Work with ESW members or on your own to design, build, and implement sustainability solutions in your community.
Educate:
By working with ESW, our members are gaining both the technical and professional skills to tackle the world's biggest problems
Unite:
Our community is here for you, whether you are looking to get feedback on a design or nerd out about sustainability.

At Cannon School, relationships are at the heart of our community. This individual will help foster a strong sense of belonging, inspire advocacy and philanthropy, and ensure members of the Cannon community feel heard, valued, and connected.

They thrive on connecting with people, navigating conversations with care, and creating experiences that strengthen community. Working closely with the Advancement team, Alumni Board, Parents at Cannon (PAC), and colleagues across campus, this position plays an important role in advancing Cannon's mission and strategic vision while helping build a vibrant culture of lifelong engagement.

If you are passionate about people, community, and making a lasting impact through authentic relationships, we invite you to explore this opportunity to join Cannon School.

Cannon School is a JrK through Grade 12 independent school located in the greater Charlotte area. In the twenty years that we have been at our present location, the physical campus has grown to include new facilities for performing arts, athletics, language labs and makerspaces. Cannon recently adopted a new strategic design with five commitments centered around community and belongingness; students; educators; wellness; and sustainability. In the teaching and learning process, we hold a philosophical commitment to autonomy, inquiry, and mastery among other habits known as Adaptive Expertise. Director of Operations

About Us

Reframe Systems is a Physical AI and robotics company on a mission to make high-performance housing attainable and abundant in the communities where people want to live. Through our vertically integrated delivery model and highly automated microfactories, we deliver climate-resilient homes and buildings with greater speed and predictability than traditional construction.

Our volumetric modular buildings are produced in our Andover, MA microfactory, with a growing pipeline across North America and a new 100,000 sq. ft. microfactory on the way in Billerica, MA. We are building a system that balances repeatability with site-responsive design, enabling homes that are adaptable to each site, community, and customer's needs. Our cross-disciplinary team brings together architecture, robotics, design engineering, software, factory operations, and field delivery to change how housing gets delivered.

We’re reimagining the future of housing through a smarter and more sustainable system that empowers people to live better. Build it with us.

What We're Looking For

We’re looking for a Head of Operations to join the Reframe executive team and lead the scaling of our manufacturing and field operations. Reporting directly to the CEO and working alongside leaders in Design, Technology, Field Construction, and Revenue, you will own the transition from single-site prototype operations to a high-volume, multi-facility scaling model.

As Head of Operations, you are a proven operational leader who thrives at the intersection of physical systems, automation software, and high-velocity teams. We are not managing a steady-state operation—we are building the infrastructure, culture, and playbook to scale from one factory to many. We need a technology-forward leader who brings deep rigor, systems thinking, and execution discipline to a genuinely novel manufacturing challenge.

Key Responsibilities

Factory Operations & Multi-Site Scaling
Launch & Facility Transition: Lead the transition and launch from our Andover prototype facility (FAB0) to our new 100,000 sq. ft. production facility in Billerica, MA (FAB1)—from floor layout, work cell design, and equipment commissioning through full production capacity.
P&L & Target Ownership: Own factory P&L, throughput targets, labor efficiency, quality metrics, and unit cost reductions.
The "1 → 2 → N" Playbook: Build the organizational playbook, standard operating procedures, and management infrastructure to scale from our current team to a multi-facility production network.
Plant Leadership & Floor Operations Management
Direct Management of Plant Leadership: Oversee the Plant Manager (who owns daily huddles, floor takt time, and direct shop supervision) to ensure production plans reliably translate into finished, high-quality homes.
Workforce Scaling: Build the supervision structure required as direct labor scales from ~20 to 80+ builders, technicians, and area leads across multiple shifts.
Operational Rhythms: Institutionalize durable daily/weekly management infrastructure (S&OP, tiered huddles, visual management boards, and standardized KPI dashboards).
Operational Excellence, Quality & Safety Systems
Continuous Improvement (CI): Establish a data-driven CI function that systematically eliminates bottlenecks, improves cycle times, and enhances labor efficiency.
Quality & Safety Systems: Implement robust QA/QC gates, in-process line checks, standardized problem-solving, and closed-loop CAPA processes. Build scalable safety programs designed to protect a growing hourly workforce.
Supply Chain, Procurement & Cost Accounting
Supply Chain Resilience: Own materials procurement, inventory management, vendor relationships, and logistics to eliminate supply chain fragility as throughput accelerates.
Real-Time Margin Tracking: Partner with Finance to establish real-time cost accounting by work cell and project, providing full visibility into unit economics.
Technology & Data Integration
Software Collaboration: Serve as a strategic power user and sponsor for our factory floor software, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), design-to-manufacturing pipelines, and operational data tools.
Product Feedback: Translate shop-floor realities into actionable priorities for software, robotics, and design engineering teams.

Qualifications

10+ years of operations leadership, including direct ownership of at least one large-scale facility launch or ramp in advanced manufacturing, fulfillment, or industrial environments.
Track record of managing plant leadership: Experience hiring, coaching, and managing Plant Managers, Shift Supervisors, and functional operations leads through rapid workforce expansion.
Proven scaling track record: Demonstrated ability to build operational infrastructure from scratch, stand up work cells, design org structures, and scale teams through rapid growth.
Tech-Enabled Operations: Deep experience operating in environments where software, automation, MES tools, and physical assembly are tightly integrated.
Data-Driven Mindset: High analytical rigor with a track record of building metrics systems that directly inform executive decision-making ("If it isn't measured, it isn't managed").
Executive Presence: Strong communication and leadership skills; comfortable representing operational strategy to investors, board members, and floor operators alike.

NICE TO HAVE

Experience navigating the “prototype facility to production factory” transition (low-rate to high-volume) and managing the edge cases that arise during facility moves.
Background in high-velocity advanced manufacturing, volumetric modular construction, automotive, aerospace, or industrial logistics.
Practical application of Lean, TWI, or Six Sigma methodologies within a venture-backed startup or high-growth environment.
Comfort operating in an environment where product design and production playbooks are actively evolving.

First-Year Outcomes & Roadmap

First 30 Days (Assessment, Alignment & Floor Integration)

Build trust and operating rhythm with executive peers (CEO, Product, Field, Finance) and on-the-floor plant leadership (Plant Manager and Area Leads).
Audit current-state performance at Andover (throughput, labor efficiency, quality escapes, safety, schedule reliability, unit cost) and identify the top 3 bottlenecks holding back the build plan.
Align on 3–5 core operational KPIs with the CEO that define company success for the year.
Produce the initial Factory Scaling & Move Plan for the Billerica launch, including hiring ramp assumptions, facility readiness, and risk mitigation strategies.
Baseline the operational excellence and quality system (QA/QC gates, defect taxonomy, corrective action loops).

First 90 Days (Systemization & Billerica Readiness)

Institutionalize the core operating system: weekly S&OP processes, daily shop-floor management rhythms, visual management, and standardized KPI dashboards.
Deliver measurable performance lifts at Andover against primary constraints using systematic CI mechanisms.
Stand up the integrated Billerica Launch Program with Plant Management (facility layout, staffing/hiring, training, commissioning sequence, quality, safety, and supply chain readiness) with formal go/no-go gates.
Implement production-ready safety, compliance, and closed-loop CAPA quality systems across active production cells.

First Year (Scale, Launch & Repeatability)

Successfully lead the production team through the Billerica launch and ramp to stable output (40–50+ homes annually) with predictable throughput, quality, and labor efficiency.
Scale direct labor from ~20 to 80+ with a robust supervision structure and strong leadership bench that holds under load.
Document and finalize the repeatable "1 → 2 → N" Operational Playbook for rapid multi-site replication.
Drive a step-change improvement in unit economics (material/labor cost per unit down, on-time delivery up, defect escapes down).
Establish end-to-end supply chain visibility and work-cell level cost accounting for precise project margin control.

Reframe Systems is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you believe you have the skills to thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. At this time, we are only considering candidates who are authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

NYC Department of Finance (DOF) is responsible for administering the tax revenue laws of the city fairly, efficiently, and transparently to instill public confidence and encourage compliance while providing exceptional customer service.
  

  

DOF’s Treasury and Payment Services Division is responsible for overseeing all City payment websites, the payment processing of tax returns, property recording forms, parking violation programs, and the collection of delinquent accounts, and oversees the agency’s management of the City’s cash balances and its relationships with banking institutions. Treasury and Payment Services is also responsible for collecting outstanding violations issued by City agencies and adjudicated by the Environmental Control Board.
  

  

Payments, Billing, and Refunds is responsible for processing payments for property taxes and property\-related charges, business and excise taxes, and parking and camera violations. The division is responsible for communicating amounts due, maintaining the quality of departmental records, and providing customer service to individuals seeking information on making payments or receiving refunds. jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
**Managing Director (Chief Operating Officer)**

Lead one of the country's most innovative animal welfare organizations. Help redefine what an animal shelter can be.

At Friends For Life, we don't simply rescue animals—we redesign systems.

We pioneered Houston's first no\-kill shelter, developed nationally recognized programs that keep pets with the families who love them, mentor shelters across the country, and continually ask a simple question:

How can we save more lives tomorrow than we saved today?

We're looking for an exceptional leader who thrives in fast\-moving environments, loves solving difficult problems, and believes compassion and accountability belong together.

This position isn't about maintaining the status quo. It's about helping build the future of animal welfare.

As Managing Director, you'll serve as the organization's operational leader, translating vision into execution while ensuring every department has what it needs to succeed. Working closely with the Executive Director, you'll oversee day\-to\-day operations, strengthen organizational systems, remove obstacles for department leaders, and ensure Friends For Life continues to innovate while remaining financially strong.

If you enjoy building teams, improving systems, making difficult decisions, and helping great people do their best work, we would love to meet you.

**What You'll Lead**

You'll directly supervise Friends For Life's Senior Leadership Team and other key staff members, including:

* Animal Pathways Director
* Animal Welfare Director
* Behavior \& Training Director
* Development Director
* Full\-Charge Bookkeeper
* Office Manager
* Volunteer Manager

**What You'll Do**

**Lead People**

Great organizations are built by great teams.

You will coach, mentor, and develop department leaders while creating a culture of trust, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You will facilitate leadership meetings, conduct performance reviews, resolve conflict, and help every leader grow into the strongest version of themselves.

**Turn Vision Into Reality**

Ideas matter. Execution matters more.

Working alongside the Executive Director, you will translate organizational vision into measurable goals, priorities, and action plans. You will help departments establish meaningful metrics, monitor progress, and ensure every initiative moves Friends For Life closer to its mission.

**Build Better Systems**

You are energized by making organizations work better.

You will identify inefficiencies, remove barriers, improve workflows, and help create systems that allow our staff to spend less time fighting processes and more time saving lives.

You will cultivate a culture where problems are solved—not simply discussed.

**Protect Financial Health**

Mission success requires sustainability.

Working with the Executive Director, you'll oversee budgeting, financial planning, and organizational performance. You will participate in monthly financial reviews, analyze trends, monitor key metrics, and help ensure Friends For Life remains financially healthy while continuing to grow its impact.

**Drive Strategic Initiatives**

Some projects don't fit neatly inside one department.

You will lead cross\-functional initiatives, oversee strategic projects, coordinate implementation across teams, and ensure major organizational priorities are completed successfully and on time.

**Strengthen Communication**

Healthy organizations communicate well.

You will help ensure staff understand where the organization is headed, why decisions are made, and how every department contributes to our mission. You will facilitate quarterly State of the Organization meetings and foster an environment built on transparency, collaboration, and shared purpose.

**Keep Us Looking Forward**

Animal welfare continues to evolve.

So do we.

You will stay informed about emerging trends, encourage thoughtful innovation, evaluate new ideas using data, and help Friends For Life remain one of the industry's leading innovators.

**What Makes You Successful**

We're less interested in where you've worked than in how you lead.

You are someone who:

* Naturally develops leaders rather than simply managing employees.
* Makes thoughtful decisions, even when information is incomplete.
* Balances compassion with accountability.
* Loves solving complex operational problems.
* Thinks strategically while paying attention to details.
* Communicates with clarity, honesty, and empathy.
* Can juggle multiple priorities without losing sight of the mission.
* Builds trust quickly across teams.
* Remains calm under pressure.
* Enjoys continuous improvement and is not satisfied with "good enough."

**Qualifications**

Preferred qualifications include:

* Bachelor's degree in business administration, Nonprofit Management, or a related field.
* Significant leadership experience, preferably within nonprofit organizations or animal welfare.
* Experience overseeing budgets, financial planning, and organizational performance.
* Strong project management and organizational skills.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication abilities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change and build high\-performing teams.
* Creative, strategic thinking combined with strong execution.
* Passion for animal welfare and alignment with Friends For Life's mission.
* Knowledge of shelter operations, canine and feline behavior, or the animal welfare field is a plus.

**Working at Friends For Life**

Shelter work is meaningful, challenging, and sometimes unpredictable.

Everyone here is expected to pitch in wherever needed. While you'll have defined responsibilities, you will occasionally find yourself helping outside your department because that is what serving animals requires.

Some weekends and holidays are required.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

Salary: $75,000 annually

Benefits include:

* Paid time off
* Medical stipend
* Pet benefits
* The opportunity to help shape

Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.
Job Description
Under the direction of Operations, the Senior Executive Director is responsible for the day\-to\-day operations and supervision of the assigned primary and secondary locations. This position provides Cause\-Driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal management, financial development, membership and program administration, facility \& equipment stewardship, community relations and personal\-professional development. Directly responsible for growing, managing and leading change of the budget and unit membership of their assigned locations.


Qualifications
* Strong business operations background with a proven track record of producing growth and strong financial management
* Bachelor's degree in Human Services, Business Management, Business Administration, or equivalent
* Ten or more years of successful management experience, preferably in YMCA or other nonprofit agency in health and wellness field
* Must have previous experience working with diverse populations
* Supervision of full and part\-time employees with accountability of annual budgets
* Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
* Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision
* Development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
* YMCA Multi Team Leader certification, preferred
**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* This role requires daily onsite work and occasional after\-hours response; therefore, candidates must be able to reliably commute to the assigned location and reside within approximately 30 miles or 45 minutes of the worksite by their start date to meet operational needs.
* Requires a person of maturity and good judgement, who can operate with a minimum of guidance from the supervisor
* Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgement and make non\-routine decisions regarding day\-to\-day operational issues
* Requires effective team building and leadership skills
* Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
* Must maintain a positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals and values
* Must have the ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management with on\-site presence managing major operational issues
* Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors and community leaders
* Ability to perform the duties of direct reports as needed

**ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to:


* Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
* Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multitasking
* Physically able to successfully complete required certifications
Essential Functions
**Priorities:**

* Achieve budget expectations annually
* Meet quarterly and annual outcomes and expectations of the Association Strategic Plan
* Attain the Annual Campaign financial expectations
* Develop and grow the District programs and services in quality and quantity
* Supervision and maintenance (through partnership with Property Team) of two YMCA locations
* The development and leadership of exempt staff leaders

**Budget and Financial Performance**

* Develops, manages, and monitors center operating budgets to meet or exceed targets. Initiates and manages adjustments to the budget to assure a balanced operation and submits reports on current operations
**Program Development and Membership Engagement**

* Implements Association membership strategies that support the recruitment of new members and retention of existing members. Creates a member\-focused culture and models relationship\-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA "listen first" skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants, and interests of members. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure member satisfaction
* Develops long\-range plans for the expansion of programs and services, in harmony with overall YMCA objectives. Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
* Ensures safety, cleanliness and function of all related facilities and equipment
**Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals**

* Ensures all program operations are consistent with association procedures, including emergency, insurance, accident, purchasing, personnel, accounting and other administrative systems
* Recruits, hires, trains, develops and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates performance.
* Develop strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for exempt staff and non\-exempt employees
**Fundraising**

* Provides leadership and is accountable for achieving the Annual Giving Campaign
Cause\-Driven Leadership Competencies
* Communication and Influence
* Fiscal Management
* Engaging Community

jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly driven, hands\-on Chief Operating Officer to take command of daily operations, build a high\-performance organization, and aggressively drive the company’s next stage of growth.

We are not looking for someone to maintain the current operation. We need a proven trucking executive who will challenge under\-performance, create urgency, develop leaders, strengthen every department, and turn company goals into measurable results.

The right candidate will be a builder and executor—someone who sees growth opportunities, develops a clear operating plan, assigns ownership, establishes deadlines, and pushes the organization forward until results are achieved.

The COO will report directly to the CEO and oversee all departments including dispatch, recruiting, safety, compliance, fleet operations, maintenance coordination, accounting support, driver relations, and office personnel.

**Location Requirement**

This position requires the COO to be based in Florida, preferably within reasonable driving distance of the Tampa Bay area.

Although some employees and departments operate remotely, the COO must be available for regular in\-person meetings for:

* Strategic planning
* Growth initiatives
* Operational reviews
* Leadership meetings

* Financial and performance reviews

This is not a fully remote position. Candidates outside Florida must be willing to relocate.

* Develop, implement, and enforce a company\-wide preventive maintenance and roadside inspection compliance program designed to reduce recurring maintenance\-related DOT violations, out\-of\-service events, breakdowns, and repair costs. Track all reported defects through documented repair completion, analyze inspection trends, strengthen pre\-trip and post\-trip accountability, and hold drivers, owner\-operators, staff, and maintenance vendors responsible for timely corrective action.

* Consistently challenge under\-performance and require department leaders to produce measurable results.

* Develop the management structure, staffing plan, and operating systems required for significant company expansion.
* Improve recruiting production, onboarding speed, driver engagement, and owner\-operator retention.
* Strengthen coordination between dispatch, recruiting, safety, fleet management, maintenance, accounting, and compliance.
* Monitor fleet utilization, revenue performance, operating margins, driver retention, downtime, claims, service failures, and operating costs.
* Identify operational bottlenecks and eliminate problems that restrict company growth.
* Recruit, train, develop, evaluate, and hold office personnel accountable.
* Make strong personnel and operational decisions when performance standards are not being met.
* Reduce preventable mistakes, unnecessary expenses, equipment downtime, compliance exposure, and unresolved operational issues.
* Lead weekly performance meetings focused on results, accountability, corrective actions, and upcoming priorities.
* Provide the CEO with clear weekly reporting on company performance, growth initiatives, departmental results, risks, and required decisions.
* Build an organization that can expand rapidly without losing financial control, service quality, safety, or compliance.
* Take command of routine operating decisions so the CEO can focus on capital, equipment, financing, strategic partnerships, and long\-term company direction.

* Significant executive or senior operational leadership experience with an asset\-based trucking company.

jobs.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

  

  

**This position is open to current Colorado residents only.** **\*\*This is a Term Limited position\*\*** **Colorado Benefits Enrollment and Eligibility Systems (CoBEES)**  


The Colorado Benefits Eligibility and Enrollment Systems team (CoBEES) manages the portfolio of technology solutions that is used to deliver access to critical health and human services programs for the people of Colorado, including food, cash, and medical assistance benefits. Colorado is state\-supervised, county\-administered, with 64 counties responsible for connecting people to programs. The current portfolio includes the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS) used by counties and medical assistance sites for integrated eligibility and enrollment to process applications, changes, and renewals; the Program Eligibility and Application Kit (PEAK) public\-facing website and PEAKPro assister tool; and the Joint Agency Interoperability Program (JAI) connecting case systems and counties. CoBEES is also embarking on an ambitious effort to reimagine and replace its legacy systems to deliver a more integrated experience: streamlined workflows that reduce duplicative data entry, coordinated cross\-program service delivery, and “whole family” support that simultaneously serves children and the adults in their lives. Colorado has a long history of being a leader in the innovative use of technology to provide support services to those in need.  


**Description of Job**
----------------------

  

  

**This position is currently hybrid.****Remote with up to two (2\) days in the office per week****The role may involve travel within the state for meetings and community engagement activities**
Please note: These working arrangements are subject to change. **What you will be doing:**
The Deputy Director serves as the Chief Product Officer's second\-in\-command, providing executive leadership for the day\-to\-day operations, administration, and strategic program coordination needed to deliver the CoBEES product portfolio during a multi year technology modernization effort. Working across CDHS, the Department of Health Care Policy \& Financing (HCPF), Colorado Department for Early Childhood (CDEC), the Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT), counties, and other partners, this role ensures people, resources, processes, and governance are aligned to support successful product delivery, organizational priorities, and better outcomes for Coloradans. The Deputy Director oversees operational planning, program coordination, organizational development, and communications.

  

Additionally, as a member of the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) extended executive management team (E\-EMT), the Deputy plays a key role in the leadership and direction of CoBEES and acts as a strategic advisor to the Chief Product Officer to achieve the team’s mission. Acting with delegated authority from the Chief Product Officer, the Deputy Director represents CoBEES as needed in executive, legislative, and interagency settings.

  

This role is term\-limited due to the type of funding available and will be made into a permanent position before the term is over.

 **Primary Job Duties:****Office Operations and Administration** \- Provides executive oversight of the administrative and operational functions of the organization to ensure resources, processes, and organizational capabilities support strategic objectives, in partnership with CDHS, HCPF, and OIT offices. This includes organization\-wide planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and workforce planning activities; procurement and contract management; and performance management.

**Product Portfolio Alignment and Strategic Coordination** \- Leads enterprise coordination efforts to advance the product strategy established by the Chief Product Officer and ensure product investments, priorities, and execution across programs are aligned with organizational goals and customer needs.

**Cross\-Agency Stakeholder Engagement and Communications** \- Leads the organization's stakeholder engagement and communications strategy to strengthen alignment, transparency, and collaboration with program leadership, county leadership, partner organizations, business units, and external entities.

**Product Enablement and Shared Services** \- Provides executive oversight and strategic direction for shared services that support product delivery and customer success for our county workers, medical assistance sites, and clients/residents, including customer support, training, communications, change management, customer feedback, and product analytics.

**Other Duties As Assigned** \- Acts on behalf of the Chief Product Officer in that person's absence, including meeting coverage and decision\-making.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Description

About Business For Good San Diego

Business For Good (BFG) San Diego is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that activates the San Diego business community around social impact, policy advocacy, and community investment. We sit at the intersection of commerce and conscience — convening business leaders, shaping policy, and driving meaningful change across our region.

After six months of volunteer board leadership and a period of organizational reflection, BFG is ready for its next chapter. We are creating this Chief Executive Officer (CEO) role to establish dedicated executive leadership for the first time since 2018 — bringing on a visionary, entrepreneurial leader to stabilize our financial foundation, deepen our community partnerships, and scale our impact across San Diego.

The Opportunity

This is a rare chance to shape a growing, mission-driven organization from the inside out, and contribute to its long-term stability . The incoming CEO will step into an organization with strong mission clarity, an engaged board, and defined goals — and will have the mandate to build on that foundation with purpose and ambition.

The right candidate will be equally at home in a boardroom and at a community event, equally comfortable building a fundraising pipeline and crafting a compelling public narrative. This is a hands-on, relationship-intensive role for a leader who thrives at the intersection of business and social good.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Vision & Organizational Leadership

Partner with the Board of Directors to develop and execute BFG's strategic plan, ensuring alignment between mission, programs, and resources

Serve as the primary driver of organizational growth, identifying opportunities to deepen impact, create and expand programs, and position BFG as an indispensable voice in the San Diego business community

Establish organizational infrastructure, policies, and systems that support a high-performing, mission-aligned team

Provide regular, transparent reporting to the Board on organizational health, progress, and emerging challenges, with minimum frequency of reporting determined by the Board

Fundraising & Financial Sustainability

Lead BFG's fundraising strategy, diversifying revenue across membership dues, corporate sponsorships, grants, events, and earned income, ensuring a balanced budget

Personally cultivate and steward relationships with major donors, funders, and corporate partners

Develop and manage annual operating budgets in partnership with the Treasurer and Board, ensuring fiscal responsibility and long-term sustainability

Pursue and secure new grant opportunities, including government, foundation, and philanthropic sources

Design and execute an earned revenue strategy that reduces dependency on any single funding stream

Community & Business Partnership Building

Serve as BFG's primary relationship holder with San Diego's business, civic, philanthropic, and government communities

Grow and retain BFG's membership base, deepening value for existing members and attracting new ones

Build and sustain partnerships with chambers of commerce, trade associations, CDFIs, and other mission-aligned organizations

Represent BFG at community events, coalitions, convenings, and public forums

Advocacy & Policy

In partnership with the Advocacy Committee, advance BFG's policy priorities at the local, regional, and state levels

Build relationships with elected officials, city and county staff, and other decision-makers

Position BFG as a trusted, credible voice on issues at the intersection of business community and social impact

Communications & Public Presence

Serve as BFG's primary spokesperson and public face, communicating its mission and impact with clarity and conviction

Oversee BFG's communications strategy across all channels — digital, media, events, and stakeholder outreach

Cultivate media relationships and ensure BFG's story is told compellingly and consistently

Develop and distribute annual impact reports, bi-monthly member communications, and donor stewardship materials as requested by the board

Team & Operations Leadership

Lead, develop, and inspire a small, defined team — setting a culture of accountability, collaboration, and mission alignment

Oversee day-to-day operations, including use of platforms for membership management, communications, budget operations, and more

Ensure compliance with all 501(c)(3) regulatory requirements, financial controls, and governance best practices

Coordinate closely with board committees including Advocacy, Finance/Treasurer, Communications, and Operations

Ensure grant deliverables are accurately and timely met

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications & Skills

8+ years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit, association, chamber of commerce, social enterprise, or mission-driven organization

Demonstrated success in fundraising, revenue diversification, and donor or sponsor relationship management

Ability to use digital screens and platforms uninterrupted for prolonged periods of time

Strong financial acumen, including experience managing budgets, preparing Annual Reports, and reporting to a Board of Directors

Proven ability to build and sustain authentic relationships with diverse stakeholders — business leaders, community members, elected officials, and funders

Track record of building partnerships, creating tangible value for multiple stakeholders

5+ years of experience managing direct reports, part-time employees, and/or contractors

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Team-oriented and highly collaborative personality, open to receiving and acting on constructive feedback to drive organizational improvement.

Ability to quickly learn new tech platforms and familiarity with office programs including Google, Slack, Canva, Quickbooks, and more

Commitment to continuous learning and dedication to personal and professional growth

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with San Diego's business, social impact, civic, and philanthropic landscape

Experience leading or working within a 501(c)(3) membership organization or chamber of commerce

Background in public policy, advocacy, or government relations

Experience with membership management and/or customer relationship management platforms (GrowthZone or similar)

Track record of scaling a small organization — growing revenue, staff, and community presence

Confident and compelling public speaker

Who Thrives In This Role

An entrepreneurial self-starter who can build systems while also rolling up their sleeves

A connector who genuinely enjoys relationship-building across sectors and communities

A strategic thinker who can hold the big picture while managing real operational complexity

Someone who believes deeply that business can and should be a force for good in the world

A communicator who can inspire members, motivate a team, and move funders to invest

Compensation & Work Environment

Business For Good San Diego offers a competitive compensation package commensurate with experience. Salary range is $90,000-$110,000, and benefits details will be shared with qualified candidates during the hiring process.

This is a full-time, remote position based in San Diego, CA. The CEO should expect regular in-person presence for events, member engagement, and community representation. Some evening and weekend availability is required.

The Director also serves as a key liaison to parent volunteers and TPA leadership, helping align parent engagement, event leadership, volunteer systems, and community-building efforts with Trinity’s mission and development goals.

Essential Responsibilities

Development Strategy and Fundraising

Lead Trinity’s development strategy in alignment with the school’s mission, strategic priorities, financial sustainability, and purposefully small preschool through Grade 5 model.
Develop, implement, and evaluate an annual development plan that includes fundraising, donor engagement, stewardship, communications, volunteer participation, and event goals.
Lead the annual giving program, including strategy, messaging, segmentation, volunteer engagement, solicitation, follow-up, reporting, and stewardship.
Partner with the Head of School and Board leadership to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors in support of annual giving, campaign priorities, special projects, and long-term institutional needs.
Identify and develop new sources of philanthropic support, including alumni families, grandparents, friends of the school, corporate partners, foundations, and other mission-aligned prospects.

Donor Relations, Stewardship, and Events

Build and maintain meaningful relationships with current families, alumni families, grandparents, trustees, former trustees, employees, friends of the school, and community partners.
Design and implement stewardship practices that ensure donors are thanked promptly, recognized appropriately, and shown the impact of their giving.
Lead or coordinate major fundraising events, including the gala and other advancement events, with responsibility for fundraising strategy, volunteer coordination, donor engagement, sponsorship opportunities, event messaging, and follow-up.
Support donor cultivation by preparing materials, tracking outreach, coordinating next steps, and partnering with the Head of School and trustees on relationship-centered donor engagement.
Support long-term philanthropic opportunities, including endowment growth, through donor education, stewardship, messaging, and coordinated development planning.

Advancement Operations and Data

Oversee advancement operations, including donor database management, gift processing, acknowledgments, pledge tracking, donor records, reporting, and confidential donor information.
Maintain accurate gift tracking and recording systems for gifts, pledges, donor restrictions, acknowledgments, campaign data, event revenue, and stewardship notes.
Partner with the Business Office to support accurate gift processing, reconciliation, fund tracking, pledge reporting, financial reporting, and responsible management of the development budget.
Use donor data, giving trends, communications analytics, and constituent feedback to inform fundraising strategy, stewardship, reporting, and continuous improvement.

Communications, Marketing, and Storytelling

Coordinate Trinity’s communications and marketing strategy in partnership with the Head of School and administrative colleagues, ensuring messaging is clear, warm, accurate, inclusive, mission-aligned, and consistent.
Steward Trinity’s institutional voice, visual identity, brand consistency, public presence, and reputation across communications for current families, prospective families, alumni families, donors, trustees, employees, and external audiences.
Oversee the strategy, content, accuracy, and effectiveness of Trinity’s publications, website, social media, email communications, and print and digital materials.
Develop messaging that showcases Trinity’s preschool through Grade 5 program, Episcopal identity, student experience, academic life, faculty excellence, community traditions, commitment to belonging, and the impact of philanthropic support.
Partner with Enrollment on outreach collateral, admission materials, prospective-family storytelling, and enrollment-facing communications.

Parent Partnership and Volunteer Engagement

Collaborate with the Head of Elementary, who serves as the primary administrative liaison to TPA, as well as TPA leadership and school administrators, to help ensure parent-led events and volunteer activities are well-coordinated, mission-aligned, inclusive, and manageable for staff and volunteers.
Provide guidance and support to parent volunteer leaders, event chairs, and committee leads, particularly in areas related to fundraising, advancement, alumni engagement, grandparent engagement, communications, and community-building efforts.
Recruit, support, and steward volunteers involved in fundraising, development events, communications, alumni engagement, grandparent engagement, and other advancement-related community initiatives.

Leadership and Collaboration

Serve as a trusted partner to the Head of School and Board of Trustees by preparing donor materials, supporting donor outreach, contributing to development committee work, and accompanying donor conversations when appropriate.
Collaborate across departments to ensure development, communications, marketing, enrollment, events, and community engagement efforts are coordinated, accurate, and mission-aligned.
Manage consultants, contractors, vendors, designers, writers, photographers, videographers, printers, or support staff working in service of development and communications goals.
Communicate proactively with colleagues about fundraising timelines, parent volunteer needs, event expectations, communications deadlines, and cross-departmental dependencies.
Maintain confidentiality, sound judgment, professionalism, warmth, and follow-through in all school, donor, family, employee, and volunteer relationships.

Working Conditions

Must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.
Must be able to work in an active school environment with frequent interruptions, changing priorities, multiple deadlines, seasonal fundraising cycles, event preparation, parent volunteer needs, and high-volume communications needs.
Must be able to move throughout campus for events, meetings, tours, photography, storytelling, volunteer support, and community engagement.
Must be comfortable interacting regularly with students, families, employees, trustees, donors, volunteers, vendors, consultants, alumni families, grandparents, parent leaders, and external partners.
Must be able to work occasionally during evenings or weekends for fundraising, admissions, communications, community engagement, parent volunteer, TPA, or school events.

Qualifications And Experience

Bachelor’s degree required, or equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience; degree in development, marketing, communications, nonprofit management, education, or related field preferred.
Significant experience in fundraising, development, donor relations, communications, marketing, nonprofit management, or related relationship-centered work.
Experience in an independent school, elementary school, nonprofit, Episcopal, or mission-driven organization strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to develop and implement fundraising, donor engagement, communications, marketing, stewardship, and volunteer strategies.
Experience with annual giving, donor cultivation, campaign support, advancement operations, Board or volunteer support, and fundraising events.
Experience with donor databases, gift tracking, pledge tracking, stewardship systems, event tracking, advancement reporting, and confidential constituent records.
Excellent writing, editing, verbal communication, presentation, storytelling, and audience-specific messaging skills.
Strong relationship-building skills with donors, families, trustees, volunteers, employees, alumni families, community partners, parent leaders, and external audiences.
Strong organizational, project management, documentation, communication, and follow-through skills.
Technologically adept and able to learn and manage donor databases, communications platforms, email tools, content management systems, spreadsheets, reports, digital media, and basic analytics.
Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging, and respectful engagement across differences.
High level of confidentiality, judgment, flexibility, creativity, resilience, optimism, and service orientation.

About Trinity School

Trinity School is a small, connected learning community serving students from age two through Grade 5 across two campuses in Menlo Park. Grounded in curiosity, belonging, and joyful learning, Trinity prepares children to thrive academically and personally in an environment that values integrity, empathy, and growth. With an annual operating budget of approximately $7 million, ample reserves, and 40 employees, Trinity is entering a new phase of organizational maturity–building on its strong systems foundation and preparing to launch a strategic plan that will shape the school’s next decade.

jobs.description:
The Banker Team Leader SAFE Act manages senior Banker UHNW & HNW professionals. The job requires a broad and comprehensive understanding of the different systems, theories and practices relevant to a function as well as practical experience of multiple business cycles. In-depth knowledge of the industry and direct competitors' products/services is also necessary in order to contribute to the commercial objectives of the business. Requires thorough understanding of strategic direction of the function within the business, combined with a solid conceptual/practical grounding in both the function and/ or area of expertise. Excellent communication skills required in order to influence a wide range of audiences. The job is likely to be involved in both internal and external negotiations which will have a major impact on the area managed, and possibly on other related areas and organization as a whole.

Responsibilities:

The position entails growing the existing client business, along with an acquisition strategy for UHNW & HNW target names. Thus thorough knowledge of the relevant market is critical and a track record evidencing the ability to grow such business through a focused and high quality team.
In addition to the role of Private Banker, the Team Leader will also have the following Responsibilities:
Accountable for driving revenue and be responsible for their entire team’s revenue goals.
Works closely with the Market Executive to lead the activities for the team.
Coach and guide team members and help them develop and share sales ideas across their and the wider team.
Co-ordinate client calling and prospecting amongst team members and sharing best practice.
Work with the Market Executive to achieve overall team revenues and growth objectives.
Take the lead in developing and implementing marketing and client events for the team.
Help team members in executing their account plans by providing guidance and support on specific deals and clients.
Provide ongoing feedback to team members on their performance as well as the formal mid-year & year-end reviews.
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of clients’ businesses and sources of wealth generation.
Anticipate events in a client’s life and business, which have significant financial implications.
Serve as a trusted advisor to clients who frequently seek strategic advice regarding financial matters.
Build relationships with client families that cross generations to establish long-term connections to the Citi Private Bank.
Effectively manage client expectations regarding what can and cannot be executed on their behalf.
Maintain a comprehensive understanding of client goals and risk tolerance to ensure that financial strategies are appropriate.
Uncover needs that are not articulated or clearly expressed by the client.
Bring together the appropriate product experts to develop long-term solutions that strengthen client relationships with the firm.
Help clients achieve broad financial & investment goals related to the creation, management, and transfer of wealth.
Develop tailored solutions that address clients' unique investment, risk management, and financing/ liquidity needs.
Regularly monitor progress against goals and make adjustments to achieve objectives.
Plan and prioritize daily, weekly and monthly activities to maximize revenue growth and client satisfaction.
Transfer or eliminate non-productive accounts in order to focus on clients who fit within the business strategy.
Establish a referral network and gain introductions to potential clients which generate new sales.
Close the deal, making concessions that are appropriate and in line with the fundamental interests of the Private Bank.
Help team members acquire the experience to establish credibility with clients and intermediaries.
Demonstrate strong commitment to team success and place team goals above personal achievement.
Encourage team members to work collaboratively and with the entire business to deepen client relationships and exceed sales goals.
Align complementary experiences and skill sets of team members to maximize client effectiveness.
Develop strong relationships and partners with support functions across the Citi Private Bank to maintain control, find solutions and resolve issues.
Ensure compliance on regulatory requirements and minimizes any potential liability for Citi.
Ensure strong controls and effective operational and administrative services.
Partner with colleagues across the Citigroup network to leverage capabilities and share expertise.
Advocate for the client, negotiating on their behalf with members of the Private Bank and Citi.
Ensure clients are presented with seamless execution of internal processes and Citi services.
Prioritize issues that need to be escalated, getting the appropriate people involved to expedite resolution.
Understand and communicate the risk involved with various investment strategies.
Establish credibility and trust with all Citi Private Bank colleagues, maintaining the highest standards of personal and professional integrity.
Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency, as well as effectively supervise the activity of others and create accountability with those who fail to maintain these standards.

15+ years of experience
Extensive and proven experience in Private Banking having covered the UHNW market / Extensive experience in working with and/or leading client teams and transactions / Demonstrated track record in relationship selling /
Have an in-depth knowledge of the Citi Private Bank internal policies to be compliant with serving the UHNW market / Demonstrates extensive knowledge of all Citi Private Bank banking and product systems, platforms, tools and capabilities.

jobs.description:
The Executive Director
(ED) provides overall strategic, operational, and financial leadership for HFH7RM, working in close partnership with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, and community partners. The ED advances the mission through effective program oversight, innovative fundraising, careful financial stewardship, and enthusiastic community engagement.

The successful candidate will embody Habitat’s core values of integrity, respect, compassion, and accountability, and will lead with creativity, collaboration, and a commitment to organizational, financial, and environmental sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Administration
Provide day-to-day leadership and management of HFH7RM operations in alignment with Board-approved policies and strategic priorities.
Hire, supervise, mentor, and evaluate staff; foster a positive, inclusive, and mission-driven workplace culture.
Oversee staff responsible for volunteer recruitment, engagement, and training.
Ensure compliance with Habitat for Humanity International standards, affiliate requirements, and all applicable laws and regulations.
Represent the affiliate at conferences and professional development opportunities.

Finance & Resource Development

Provide overall financial leadership, including budget oversight, financial planning, and long-term fiscal sustainability.
Lead the development and implementation of new major donor campaigns and planned giving initiatives as well as support current fundraising strategies and grant writing.
Work with staff and the Board of Directors to develop, monitor, and report on annual budgets.
Authorize expenditures within Board-approved guidelines.
Serve as lead contact for outside auditing agency every year.
Monitor and maintain appropriate insurance coverage.

Board Partnership & Governance Support

Work collaboratively with the Board of Directors, attending all Board meetings and supporting committee work as needed.
Support Board development, including orientation and ongoing training of Board members.
Provide timely, accurate, and relevant reports on organizational performance, finances, and strategic initiatives.
Assist the Board with strategic planning, goal setting, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Programs & ReStore Oversight

Provide executive oversight of all affiliate programs, including new home construction, weatherization, and critical home repair.
Collaborate with staff, committees, and volunteers to ensure program quality, consistency, safety, and funding alignment.
Work with partners and committees to identify and secure suitable building sites.
Support the ReStore Manager in pursuing operational excellence and revenue growth.
Encourage retail best practices to maximize mission-aligned income generation.
Maintain appropriate engagement with Habitat for Humanity International and ASO–Habitat of Maine program teams to strengthen and expand affiliate programming.

Community Engagement & Public Relations

Serve as the primary spokesperson for HFH7RM within the community.
Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, faith partners, businesses, civic organizations, and local government.
Support visibility and awareness of HFH7RM through public speaking, outreach, and media engagement.
Collaborate with staff on communications, marketing, and social media to strengthen the organization’s public presence.

Facilities & Property Management

Oversee maintenance of the office and ReStore facilities.
Manage relationships with property owners and facility management partners.
Oversee maintenance of trucks, vans, and trailers used by the Restore and the Critical Home Repair teams.
Support annual facilities budgeting and long-term maintenance planning.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; an equivalent combination of education and significant relevant experience may be considered.
Minimum of five years of leadership experience in nonprofit management, marketing/public relations, construction, housing, or community development.
Experience with fundraising, donor relations, and/or resource development.
Ability to supervise, mentor, and lead staff and volunteers effectively.
Experience with budgeting, financial oversight, and organizational management.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to build productive partnerships with community and governmental organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Habitat for Humanity’s mission, values, and affiliate structure.
Knowledge of residential construction or building science.
Experience with nonprofit retail operations (such as a ReStore or similar enterprise).

Additional Requirements

Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.
Ability to travel throughout the service area.
Ability to lift boxes up to 45 pounds.
Successful completion of criminal background, motor vehicle, and sex offender registry checks.

What We Offer

HFH7RM offers a competitive salary between $65,000 and $85,000, depending on experience, as well as a comprehensive benefits package, flexibility in work schedule, and a strong commitment to professional development. You’ll join a collaborative staff team, a supportive Board of Directors, and a welcoming community in Maine’s beautiful Midcoast region.

Job Description

LCS is seeking an experienced Executive Director in the senior housing industry to oversee the daily operations at Brandon Wilde. Brandon Wilde provides a full continuum of care located on a 73-acre wooded campus minutes away from all the conveniences of Augusta, Atlanta, and Charlotte.

Thinking about future growth? LCS is the third-largest senior living operator in the Nation and has opportunities to expand your career through multiple avenues and we are dedicated to employee development at every level of your career. With over 140 communities, there is a seemingly infinite opportunity to take your next step in your career.

Experience is Everything;

At LCS, experience is everything. We provide you the opportunity to use your talents in a progressive, growing organization that makes a positive difference in the lives of the seniors we serve. If you are seeking an organization that gives back, you’ll love working here. Our principles and hospitality promises define our company culture. LCS employees can be found participating in volunteer activities, getting involved in our committees or collaborating with team members in our innovative work space. You’ll find several opportunities to grow as a professional, serve the community, and enhance the lives of the seniors.

The Role

Actively participate in and provide leadership for the community and its staff. Supervise directly/indirectly all staff in the community.
Direct the management team to ensure the success of the Community including accountability for all areas of operations meeting all financial and budgetary objectives.
Participate and be accountable for oversight of all marketing and sales activities and results.
Operate the Community in accordance with the Company's policies and procedures and ensure the safety and security of residents and staff.

Qualifications

The technical knowledge required is best obtained through a BS or MS degree in business, health care, or a closely related area.
Five or more years of experience in a leadership capacity in the senior living industry.
A background in financial management, including budget preparation, cash flow management, and analysis of financial reports.
Ability to work effectively and diplomatically with a variety of publics, including residents, ownership groups, community groups, government agencies.

Why LCS?

Industry leader.
The Nation’s third-largest senior living operator, ranked number one in customer satisfaction among senior living communities.

Inclusive and collaborative culture.
We’re dedicated to diversity, equity, and inclusion and have an engaged Diversity and Inclusion Council focused on creating awareness and educating employees on inclusivity. In addition, LCS creates a collaborative culture that provides an exceptional experience for every employee.

Top Workplace USA:
LCS has earned the Top Workplaces USA award for several consecutive years and is recognized for our strong company culture and engaged workforce.In addition, LCS earned ten culture excellence awards in areas such as DE&I practices, top managers, professional development and clued-in leaders, to name a few.

Top Workplace Iowa:
LCS employees truly believe we are an employer choice. This recognition, for 4 years running, is in large part due to the culture of excellence that our employees help deliver every single day.

Competitive pay, great benefits and vacation time.
We are an equal opportunity employer with benefits including medical, dental, life insurance, disability, 401(k) with company match and paid parental leave.

Charity and community involvement.
We are recognized as a national team for the Alzheimer’s Association and consistently a top contributor to United Way. We also support our employee’s individual community contributions and provide opportunities to get involved at our corporate locations and in our communities.

Outstanding advancement opportunities.
LCS is growing and we think you should too. Our company growth allows for internal growth opportunities across all of our business lines.

Ongoing career development.
Onsite education opportunities, education assistance, and continuing education credits allow LCS employees to keep their knowledge of current industry changes relevant.

LCS creates living experiences that enhance the lives of seniors. You’ll see this commitment in our people. They’re talented, dedicated professionals who truly care about residents, with each conducting his or her work with integrity, honesty and transparency according to the principles of LCS. We strive to help every community succeed—strengthening available resources, establishing proven practices that lead to long-term growth and creating lasting value for those living in, working for and affiliated with the community. Check us out on our website: www.lcsnet.com

Travel Frequency:
Occasional

$160,000 - $190,000

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
Helioustin.io is a global B2B strategic alliances and management consulting firm focused on helping organizations achieve sustainable growth through intelligent partnerships and research-driven insights. Through its Three-Tier Enterprise Membership Program, the firm offers scalable access to strategic consulting, market intelligence, AI-powered research, digital transformation, operational optimization, and alliance development for businesses at different growth stages. Helioustin.io specializes in designing and executing cross-sector collaborations, joint ventures, technology partnerships, distribution networks, institutional alliances, and investor relationships that align strategy with execution. By combining business intelligence, competitive research, ecosystem mapping, and implementation support, the company helps clients reduce inefficiencies, expand markets, strengthen competitive positioning, and build long-term enterprise value. Helioustin.io operates as a strategic implementation partner, engineering collaborative ecosystems that turn opportunities into measurable business outcomes.
Role Description
The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide overall strategic leadership for Helioustin.io, setting vision, priorities, and long-term goals in line with the company’s mission as a global B2B strategic alliances and consulting firm. This full-time remote role includes overseeing enterprise membership programs, guiding alliance development, and driving client-facing initiatives that support research, consulting, and digital transformation services. The CEO will manage financial performance, lead operational planning, and ensure that cross-functional teams are aligned to deliver high-quality research, strategic partnerships, and implementation support. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading executive decision-making, nurturing key client and partner relationships, representing the company in high-level negotiations, and identifying new markets and strategic opportunities. The CEO will also build and mentor a diverse leadership team, reinforce a culture of collaboration and accountability, and ensure compliance with ethical and professional standards.

Strong background in Finance, including budgeting, forecasting, and oversight of revenue and investment strategies.
Proficiency in Operations Management and Business Planning to design scalable processes, drive efficiency, and support enterprise growth.
Demonstrated experience in Sales and Strategic Planning to expand market presence, develop alliances, and achieve business objectives.
Proven leadership experience in executive roles within consulting, B2B partnerships, or technology-driven organizations.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills in diverse, global business environments.
Ability to operate effectively in a remote, high-growth setting, with strong decision-making and problem-solving capabilities.
Track record of building and leading cross-functional teams and fostering an inclusive, performance-oriented culture.
Advanced degree in Business, Finance, Management, or a related field preferred; equivalent executive experience strongly considered.

jobs.description:
RS&H is seeking a Senior Project Director to join our Innovative Program Advisory Service Group!

The Company

Employee-owned, RS&H is one of the nation’s leading architecture, engineering, and consulting firms, with associates who work hard every day to create tomorrow together. We offer an exceptional journey from start to future. Our integrated teams translate experience into insight, turn challenges into opportunities, and build relationships that are as strong as the buildings and infrastructure we deliver together. We attribute our success to our unwavering commitment to our core values: integrity, accountability, curiosity, and teamwork.

Job Summary

This position will support the Innovative Program Advisory team on various alternative delivery programs and projects across the country utilizing more progressive delivery methods such as design-build, progressive design-build, CMGC/CMAR, and P3 (DBF/DBFOM). Typical client engagements include program management tasks ranging from the development of implementation manuals and program guidelines, template documents and forms, internal and external stakeholder education; and project management tasks which include drafting and development of RFI, RFQ and RFP documents, evaluation manuals, project management plans, and deliverables to assist clients in meeting FHWA major project requirements (PMP, CSRA, IFP, etc.).
The successful candidate will have experience performing diverse and complex work tasks associated with development, delivery and/or oversight of large infrastructure projects procured using a variety of alternative delivery methods. The candidate will have an understanding and proficiency in drafting performance based technical requirements, ITPs and responses to bidder RFIs during procurements. As a project manager, the candidate should have experience working within defined timelines and budgets to develop deliverables and be able to manage a team of technical discipline experts who will contribute to the development of various project and program documents.

Essential Functions

Support experienced nationally recognized experts in alternative delivery
Serve in a meaningful technical role on current alternative delivery engagements with various state DOT’s including Maryland, Virginia, Georgia, Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Texas, North Carolina, among others
Help grow a high performing Innovative Program Advisory group that believes in accountability, communication, ethics, teamwork, and a performance-rewarding culture
Serve as a Project Manager for project pursuits that provide the best opportunity for selection by the client in such a role

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited program or equivalent combination of education and experience
Minimum 15 years of experience with alternative delivery including:
Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, and/or CM/GC
P3 (DBF, DBFO/M)
Minimum 10 years of direct project management experience
Experience in task management on complex and large transportation projects
Experience working on alternative delivery projects as a consultant to or employee of a state department(s) of transportation
Ability to market and maintain positive and trusted relationships with clients, staff, and subconsultant partners
Excellent organizational skills with attention to detail along with overall quality control and schedule management
Ability to track individual project tasks and financial management of individual and overall project tasks

Preferred Qualifications

Active, good-standing Professional Engineering license, American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP), Design Build Certified Practitioner (DBIA), or Project Management Professional (PMP)

Please note: no agency representation or submissions will be recognized for this vacancy. Candidates should apply directly to this role to be considered.
