jobs.title: Youth Program Director
jobs.description:
An exciting opportunity to join the team of a progressive YMCA located in vibrant Somerset County, New Jersey.

Job Description

An exciting opportunity to join the team of a progressive YMCA located in vibrant Somerset County, New Jersey. The YMCA is one of the nation’s leading nonprofit organizations dedicated to strengthening communities through youth development, healthy living and social responsibility. With a 150-year-old history, Greater Somerset County YMCA (GSCY) is a pillar of the community and has seven locations across three counties, which collectively serve upwards of 30,000 individuals. GSCY has 100 full-time and 950 part-time employees along with operating revenues to $22+ million.

The Y empowers everyone—no matter who they are or where they are from. To fulfill our purpose of strengthening community for all, GSCY is committed to being an inclusive organization and leveraging our collective impact to address social inequities. To learn more about GSCY, visit our website: http://gscymca.org

Position Summary

Under the direction of the Senior Program Director, the Youth Program Director is responsible for managing activities associated with our School Age Child Care, Summer Camp, and Youth Enrichment Programs. This includes the administration of these programs to ensure that they create opportunities for youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility.

This job is fully on-site without opportunities for remote work.

Qualifications

A Bachelor’s Degree in a related field preferred or equivalent experience

2-3 Years Experience working with Youth in a School aged childcare background

Supervisory Experience Preferred

Proficiency with Microsoft Suite

Availability to work evenings and weekends as required by program schedules.

Current CPR/AED and First Aid certification or obtain within 30 days of hire.

Bloodborne Pathogens, Child Abuse Prevention, Sexual Harassment, and other program-specific courses.

Essential Functions

Provide leadership, supervision, and performance management for SACC, camp, and youth staff, including hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, coaching, payroll review, and ongoing professional development.
Oversee and support School Age Child Care (SACC), Summer Camp, Early Education Center (EEC), Youth Sports, and other Youth Programs, ensuring high-quality, safe, educational, and engaging experiences that align with YMCA standards and core values.
Plan, organize, implement, and evaluate program curricula, activities, special events, field trips, and seasonal programming to support participant growth and program success.
Manage program enrollment, registration, attendance, waitlists, billing, parent communication systems, and related software platforms to ensure effective administration and customer service.
Develop and manage program budgets, monitor revenue and expenses, authorize program purchases, and ensure responsible stewardship of YMCA resources.
Coordinate staffing, facility usage, transportation, equipment, supplies, and program logistics to support efficient operations and participant safety.
Build and maintain positive relationships with participants, families, staff, volunteers, and community partners by providing exceptional customer service and timely resolution of questions or concerns.
Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, licensing requirements, risk management practices, and regulatory standards, including safety inspections, incident reporting, and staff accountability.
Lead program marketing, member engagement, and growth initiatives through promotions, community outreach, social media, website content, and other communication channels.
Support YMCA fundraising efforts by actively participating in the Annual Campaign, meeting campaign goals, recruiting and coordinating volunteers, and assisting with fundraising events and activities.
Collaborate with branch and association leadership on strategic initiatives, staff training, special events, and organization-wide projects while promoting the YMCA mission and core values of caring, honesty, respect, and responsibility.
Perform other duties as assigned in support of branch operations and organizational objectives.

Cause-Driven Leadership Competencies

Mission Advancement: Models and teaches the Ys values. Ensures a high level of service with a commitment to changing lives. Provides volunteers with orientation, training, development, and recognition. Cultivates relationships to support fundraising.

Collaboration: Champions inclusion activities, strategies, and initiatives. Builds relationships to create small communities. Empathetically listens and communicates for understanding when negotiating and dealing with conflict. Effectively tailors' communications to the appropriate audience. Provides staff with feedback, coaching, guidance and support.

Operational Effectiveness: Provides others with frameworks for making decisions. Conducts prototypes to support the launching of programs and activities. Develops plans and manages best practices through engagement of team. Effectively creates and manages budgets. Holds staff accountable for high-quality results using a formal process to measure progress.

Personal Growth: Shares new insights. Facilitates change, models adaptability and an awareness of the impact of change. Utilizes non-threatening methods to address sensitive issues and inappropriate behavior or performance. Has the functional and technical knowledge and skills required to perform well; uses best practices and demonstrates up-to-date knowledge and skills in technology.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Sufficient strength, agility and mobility to perform essential functions of position and to supervise program activities.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use a computer for extended periods of time and be able to communicate using a computer and phone/smart device.

The employee frequently is required to sit and reach and must be able to move around the work environment.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, with occasional noise levels associated with working with school-aged children.

This position is fully in-person without remote work opportunities.

Benefits Of Working Full-time At GSC YMCA Include

FREE family membership to Greater Somerset County YMCA, including full access to all of our branch facilities including Bridgewater YMCA, Hillsborough YMCA, Princeton YMCA, Somerset Hills YMCA, and Somerville YMCA.

FREE nationwide membership with access to over 2,500 YMCA locations across the country

Discounted program fees

Paid sick leave and short-term disability insurance

Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Generous 12% retirement contribution to the YMCA Retirement Fund after eligibility period (no employee contribution required)

Medical and dental insurance with prescription coverage

Vision insurance

Flexible Spending Account for medical and/or dependent care

100% contribution towards life insurance and long-term disability

Optional additional life insurance and dependent life insurance available at low rates

403(b) Smart Savings Plan

Generous paid time off policy

7 paid holidays

Greater Somerset County YMCA is a drug free work environment. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, protected veteran or disabled status, or genetic information who share our values of Caring, Honesty, Respect and Responsibility.

jobs.title: Senior Executive Director
jobs.description:
Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.

Job Description

Under the direction of Operations, the Senior Executive Director is responsible for the day-to-day operations and supervision of the assigned primary and secondary locations. This position provides Cause-Driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal management, financial development, membership and program administration, facility & equipment stewardship, community relations and personal-professional development. Directly responsible for growing, managing and leading change of the budget and unit membership of their assigned locations.

Qualifications

Strong business operations background with a proven track record of producing growth and strong financial management
Bachelor's degree in Human Services, Business Management, Business Administration, or equivalent
Ten or more years of successful management experience, preferably in YMCA or other nonprofit agency in health and wellness field
Must have previous experience working with diverse populations
Supervision of full and part-time employees with accountability of annual budgets
Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision
Development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
YMCA Multi Team Leader certification, preferred

Working Conditions

This role requires daily onsite work and occasional after-hours response; therefore, candidates must be able to reliably commute to the assigned location and reside within approximately 30 miles or 45 minutes of the worksite by their start date to meet operational needs.
Requires a person of maturity and good judgement, who can operate with a minimum of guidance from the supervisor
Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgement and make non-routine decisions regarding day-to-day operational issues
Requires effective team building and leadership skills
Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
Must maintain a positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals and values
Must have the ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management with on-site presence managing major operational issues
Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors and community leaders
Ability to perform the duties of direct reports as needed

Environmental Factors, Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to:

Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multitasking
Physically able to successfully complete required certifications

Priorities

Essential Functions

Achieve budget expectations annually
Meet quarterly and annual outcomes and expectations of the Association Strategic Plan
Attain the Annual Campaign financial expectations
Develop and grow the District programs and services in quality and quantity
Supervision and maintenance (through partnership with Property Team) of two YMCA locations
The development and leadership of exempt staff leaders

Budget and Financial Performance

Develops, manages, and monitors center operating budgets to meet or exceed targets. Initiates and manages adjustments to the budget to assure a balanced operation and submits reports on current operations

Program Development and Membership Engagement

Implements Association membership strategies that support the recruitment of new members and retention of existing members. Creates a member-focused culture and models relationship-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA "listen first" skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants, and interests of members. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure member satisfaction
Develops long-range plans for the expansion of programs and services, in harmony with overall YMCA objectives. Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
Ensures safety, cleanliness and function of all related facilities and equipment

Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals

Ensures all program operations are consistent with association procedures, including emergency, insurance, accident, purchasing, personnel, accounting and other administrative systems
Recruits, hires, trains, develops and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates performance. Develop strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for exempt staff and non-exempt employees

Fundraising

Provides leadership and is accountable for achieving the Annual Giving Campaign

Cause-Driven Leadership Competencies

Communication and Influence
Fiscal Management
Engaging Community

**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**


**ABOUT STEAM:CODERS**



STEAM:CODERS expands access to high\-quality science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics education for young people from diverse backgrounds. Based in Pasadena, the organization provides hands\-on coding, robotics, engineering, AI and technology programs that help underserved K\-12 students build technical skills, confidence, and pathways to future academic and career opportunities. Through small classes, project\-based learning, and partnerships with schools and community organizations, STEAM:CODERS offers after\-school programs, workshops, summer camps, and other educational experiences. As STEAM:CODERS enters its next chapter, the organization seeks an entrepreneurial Executive Director who can build on its strong reputation and programming while expanding fundraising, strengthening organizational systems, and deepening community partnerships.


**ABOUT THE POSITION**



Reporting to the Advisory Board, the Executive Director serves as STEAM:CODERS' chief executive and public ambassador. The Executive Director will lead organizational strategy, fundraising, community engagement, and program oversight while guiding the organization through sustainable growth. Key priorities include establishing a vision for the organization's future, diversifying revenue, cultivating corporate and individual donors, strengthening infrastructure, and increasing STEAM:CODERS' visibility in Pasadena and beyond.


**ROLES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**


**Organizational Leadership \& Strategy**


* Serve as the day\-to\-day leadership of STEAM:CODERS, establishing organizational priorities, goals, and systems that position the organization for long\-term sustainability.
* Support Board development, committee engagement, and strategic planning efforts that reflect the organization's mission, values, and aspirations for growth.
* Build organizational infrastructure, processes, and operational systems appropriate for a small and growing nonprofit.
* Keep the Board informed of organizational performance, emerging opportunities, and potential challenges.


**Fund Development \& Financial Sustainability**


* Develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy that includes foundations, corporations, major donors, individual giving, and special events.
* Cultivate, steward, and expand relationships with current and prospective donors, funders, and community investors.
* Partner with Community Initiatives and Board leadership on annual budgeting, financial planning, and financial reporting.
* Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources and maintain strong financial oversight.


**Community Engagement \& External Relations**


* Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for STEAM:CODERS throughout the community.
* Build meaningful partnerships with school districts, colleges, technology companies, nonprofits, civic organizations, and community leaders.
* Increase community awareness of STEAM:CODERS through networking, presentations, public events, and strategic communications.
* Cultivate relationships that create new opportunities for students, volunteers, and supporters.


**Program \& Organizational Management**


* Provide strategic oversight of all STEAM:CODERS programs, ensuring continued excellence, innovation, and measurable impact.
* Support staff in delivering engaging, equitable, and high\-quality educational experiences.
* Monitor program outcomes and use data to inform continuous improvement.
* Recruit, develop, and retain talented staff and volunteers who are passionate about the organization's mission.
* Cultivate organizational and leadership skills for staff in support of workforce development.
* Ensure organizational policies, systems, and practices support effective program delivery.


**QUALIFICATIONS**



The ideal candidate will bring many of the following qualifications:


* Demonstrated success in nonprofit leadership positions for a minimum of five (5\) years, preferably during a period of organizational growth or transition.
* Proven fundraising success across multiple revenue streams, including grants, major gifts, corporate partnerships, and individual giving.
* Exceptional relationship\-building skills with donors, community leaders, public agencies, and strategic partners.
* Experience developing and implementing organizational or strategic plans.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting and organizational financial oversight.
* Experience supervising and developing staff while fostering a collaborative organizational culture.
* Outstanding written, verbal, and public speaking skills. Spanish language skills are a plus.
* Passion for educational equity, youth development, and expanding opportunity for historically underserved communities.
* Familiarity with STEAM, education, or youth\-serving organizations is preferred.
* Knowledge of Pasadena, Altadena, and the greater Los Angeles philanthropic and nonprofit community is an advantage.


**WHY JOIN STEAM:CODERS?**



This is an opportunity to shape the future of a respected organization at an exciting point in its evolution. With a planned hand\-off from a committed founder, the next Executive Director will inherit a strong programmatic foundation, a highly engaged Board, powerful community relationships, and a mission that changes the trajectory of young people's lives through tech education. STEAM:CODERS is in a strong financial position and is fiscally sponsored by Community Initiatives, which provides administrative support, allowing the Executive Director to focus primarily on leadership, fund development, partnerships, strategic planning, and organizational growth. Tech education for underserved youth is one of our most timely issues, given the rapid changes in the tech sector, the adoption of AI, and the growing need to equip our youth for future challenges.

The salary range for this position is $140,000–$16

One of the most active property investors in the world for over three decades, MSREI employs a patient, disciplined approach through global value\-add / opportunistic and regional core / core\-plus real estate investment strategies.

**Position**: Executive Director

**Position Length/Type**: Full\-time (40hrs/week)

**Compensation:** $57,000–$62,000 annually, depending on qualifications and experience.Monthly bonus to supplement healthcare costs. Vacation, wellness, and paid holiday leave.

**Start Date:** September 21, 2026

**Background**

The Nisqually Reach Nature Center (NRNC) is a non\-profit organization whose mission is to promote the understanding, appreciation, and conservation of the Nisqually Estuary through education, interpretation, and community science. NRNC is located on Luhr Beach – a destination for thousands of visitors a year who have access to one of the finest estuaries in Puget Sound. For over forty years we have offered a variety of environmental education and community science programs.

**Position Description**

The Executive Director provides strategic, operational, and financial leadership for the Nisqually Reach Nature Center while working closely with the Board of Directors to advance the organization's mission and long\-term sustainability. This position is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the organization, including staff supervision, financial oversight, fundraising, community partnerships, communications, and day\-to\-day operations.

The successful candidate will foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, mutual respect, and shared purpose while serving as the organization's primary spokesperson and community leader. This is an exciting opportunity for a dynamic leader who is passionate about the environment, community engagement, and nonprofit leadership.

**Core Responsibilities Include**

* Provide strategic leadership and implement organizational priorities in partnership with the Board of Directors.
* Oversee daily operations, administration, facilities, technology, and organizational systems.
* Supervise, mentor, and support staff, resident caretakers, volunteers, and interns.
* Develop and manage the annual budget while ensuring financial accountability and sustainability.
* Lead fundraising efforts, including grant writing, donor cultivation, sponsorships, membership growth, and fundraising events.
* Build and strengthen partnerships with community organizations, agencies, schools, funders, and stakeholders.
* Represent NRNC at community events, public meetings, and with media and government partners.
* Oversee marketing, public relations, social media, and organizational communications.
* Ensure compliance with organizational policies and applicable legal, financial, and ethical standards.

**Other**

Nisqually Reach Nature Center employees are flexible and may be asked to take on additional duties according to organizational needs and individual skills. Because we are a nonprofit serving the community, this position occasionally requires evening and weekend work for Board meetings, fundraising events, community programs, and other organizational activities.

**Required Qualifications \- NOTE: Experience may have been gained concurrently.**

* Bachelor's degree in business, public administration, nonprofit management, environmental studies, or a related field.
* Minimum of two years of senior leadership or management experience in a nonprofit or mission\-driven organization.
* Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
* Strong financial management, budgeting, and reporting experience.
* Demonstrated fundraising success, including grant writing and donor development.
* Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills.
* Proven ability to build collaborative relationships with staff, volunteers, partners, funders, and community members.
* Strong organizational, leadership, and strategic planning skills.
* Demonstrated integrity, sound judgment, and commitment to ethical leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in business, public administration, nonprofit management, environmental studies, or a related field.
* Five or more years of senior nonprofit leadership experience.

**To Apply**

Submit a cover letter describing how you meet the qualifications and why you are interested in this position, a current resume, and three (3\) or more professional references, which include at least one supervisor, to . Applications will be reviewed beginning August 5, 2026\.

A satisfactory background check will be a contingency of any hire offer. Recruitment remains open until filled; first applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Nisqually Reach Nature Center is an Equal Opportunity employer. We strive to create a working environment that is inclusive and respectful. We prohibit discrimination based on race/ethnicity/color, creed, sex, pregnancy, age, religion, national origin, marital status, the presence or perception of a disability, veteran’s status, military status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender expression, or gender identity.

By submitting materials, you indicate that all information is true and correct. Nisqually Reach Nature Center has the right to verify the information. Any untruthful or misleading information is cause for removal from the applicant pool or dismissal if employed.

**Executive Director\- Holy Ground PBC**

Are you a visionary, compassionate, and results\-driven leader with a passion for empowering young mothers and breaking cycles of poverty? **Holy Ground PBC** is seeking an inspiring **Executive Director** to lead our organization into its next chapter of growth, impact, and community engagement.

Located in Palm Beach County, Florida, Holy Ground PBC provides shelter, mentoring, life skills, and comprehensive supportive services to homeless, pregnant, or parenting young women and their children. Over the past decade, we have grown from supporting a single mother to empowering 12 families across two campuses.

As Executive Director, you will serve as the chief brand ambassador, strategic leader, and primary driver of our fundraising and donor engagement strategies. If you are a collaborative servant leader who thrives on building meaningful donor relationships and expanding community support, we invite you to lead our mission.

**Our Mission \& Vision**

* **Mission:** To shelter and mentor homeless, pregnant, or parenting young women and their children living in Palm Beach County who are willing to make positive changes in their lives.
* **Vision:** To empower and transform the lives of young women and their children by fostering generational change that contributes toward breaking the cycle of homelessness, poverty, and teen pregnancy.

**Key Responsibilities\- Fundraising \& Revenue Development (Primary Focus)**

* **Lead Philanthropic Growth:** Drive all fundraising strategies, including major gifts, individual donor cultivation, corporate sponsorships, capital campaigns, and foundation grant opportunities.
* **Donor \& Funder Engagement:** Cultivate, steward, and maintain strong relationships with individual donors, grantmakers, and community partners. Organize site visits and donor campaigns to increase engagement and retention.
* **Events \& External Communications:** Partner with the Development Director and Board to plan and execute annual fundraising benefits and signature events. Oversee marketing collateral, social media, newsletters, and digital presence.
* **Diversify Funding:** Expand existing funding streams while proactively identifying new revenue opportunities to ensure long\-term financial sustainability.

**Strategic Leadership \& Community Representation**

* Serve as the main spokesperson and public face of Holy Ground, elevating our visibility and brand across Palm Beach County through public speaking, networking, and media relations.
* Establish strategic partnerships with local organizations, corporate partners, and programs such as College Internship Programs and Leadership Palm Beach County.
* Set and execute organizational strategy in close collaboration with the Board of Directors.

**Operational, Financial \& Board Governance**

* Partner with the Board Treasurer, Accountant, and Bookkeeper to manage the annual budget, ensure financial health, and maintain audit\-ready financial and bookkeeping records.
* Keep the Board of Directors fully informed through detailed monthly reports, financial updates, grant reports, and active participation in board meetings and annual retreats.
* Ensure strict adherence to local, state, and national compliance regulations.

**Team Leadership \& Program Oversight**

* Inspire, mentor, and build a high\-performing staff culture grounded in accountability, empathy, and mission dedication.
* Oversee recruitment, onboarding, and staff development, ensuring effective operational structures.
* Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator to support quality volunteer programming.
* Ensure overall program quality and alignment with key outcomes while delegating day\-to\-day service delivery to program staff.

**Required Qualifications \& Skills**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration (MBA), or Social Work (MSW) preferred.
* **Experience:** Minimum of 2–3 years in senior nonprofit management or executive leadership.
* **Fundraising Excellence:** Proven, documented track record in fundraising, donor stewardship, major gift acquisition, and grant oversight.
* **Board Relations:** Demonstrated success reporting to and collaborating with a Board of Directors.
* **Financial Acumen:** Solid understanding of nonprofit budgeting, financial reporting, and audit preparedness.
* **Communication Skills:** Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills; highly comfortable with public speaking and media interactions.
* **Technical Proficiency:** Proficiency in MS Office Suite (advanced Excel), virtual platforms (Zoom, MS Teams, Google Meet), CRM/donor databases, and basic accounting software.

**Salary \& Benefits**

* **Position Type:** Full\-Time, Exempt (In\-Person position in Riviera Beach, FL)
* **Salary Range:** $70,000 – $80,000 per year, commensurate with experience
* **Benefits Include:**
* Health insurance contribution/stipend (negotiable upon offer)
* Paid Vacation Time
* 12 Paid Holidays
* Personal Time / PTO

**How to Apply**

**To be considered, candidates must submit:**

* A tailored **Cover Letter** detailing your connection to Holy Ground’s mission and highlighting your specific fundraising achievements.
* Your current **Resume/CV**.

*This search is conducted by Executive Service Corps\- Florida on behalf of Holy Ground PBC.*

* senior management: 2 years (Required)

**ECHO Community Health Care, Incorporated (ECHC)** is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) located in Evansville, Indiana.


The health center is an established FQHC, with roots back to the 1980’s. ECHC serves the Evansville community and beyond.

“We provide quality healthcare to all members of our community, including the uninsured, underinsured and homeless. Our comprehensive services are Affordable, Accessible and Appropriate. Our team of professionals is here to care for you and to advocate on your behalf.”

Enlace Chicago convenes, organizes, and strengthens the capacity of stakeholders across Little Village to confront systemic inequities and expand access to economic and social opportunity. For more than 35 years, Enlace has served as a trusted community anchor, championing opportunity, improving lives, and building partnerships that drive lasting change.


Through our work, we advance community health, protect human rights, empower futures, promote safety, and foster resilience for families throughout Little Village. Our core departments of Education, Community Safety, Mental Health, Community Health, and Immigration \& Advocacy—deliver critical, culturally responsive services that uplift and support the strength and dignity of our community

**Position Overview:**


The Director of Development is responsible for strengthening and growing Enlace Chicago’s fundraising infrastructure, with a primary focus on increasing individual giving, building a strong major gifts pipeline, and advancing campaign strategies that deepen donor engagement and diversify revenue. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Institutional Advancement, this position will help lead the implementation of a comprehensive fundraising strategy that includes individual donors, major gifts, monthly giving, corporate campaigns, foundation support, public funding, special events, and donor stewardship.


The Director of Development will oversee the work connected to Enlace’s public and private fundraising portfolios, ensuring strong systems, timely execution, clear accountability, and alignment with organizational priorities. This position will work closely with the Deputy Director of Institutional Advancement, Executive Director, program leadership, finance team, Board of Directors, and development staff to identify funding opportunities, cultivate donor relationships, support grant strategy, and grow sustainable revenue for Enlace Chicago’s programs and operations.


This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced fundraising professional who is relationship\-driven, systems\-minded, and committed to advancing community\-based work rooted in equity, justice, and opportunity for Little Village.

jobs.description:
The **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)** serves as the strategic and operational leader of Charles Settlement House (CSH) and The Community Place of Greater Rochester (CPGR), two affiliated nonprofit organizations operating under a shared services model and a joint Board of Directors, while maintaining separate legal identities.  

  

The CEO is responsible for advancing a unified vision, ensuring mission alignment, and maximizing collective impact while maintaining compliance with each organization’s independent fiduciary, legal, and governance obligations.  

  

This role requires a highly collaborative executive capable of navigating dual\-entity leadership, optimizing shared services, and building strong relationships with volunteer Board members, staff, funders, government, and the broader community.  

  

This is a unique opportunity to lead two mission\-driven organizations with deep community roots and significant potential for greater collective impact. The CEO will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of an innovative shared services model while strengthening services for the Rochester community.  

  

**About Us**  

CSH and CPGR are settlement houses with roots well over 100 years in Rochester. Settlement Houses are place\-based human service providers with programs that are focused on neighborhood needs and serve people of all ages.  

  

CSH serves as the parent entity, while CPGR operates with a larger programmatic footprint, revenue base, and asset portfolio.
  

**Essential Job Duties**  

*Strategic Leadership \& Vision:*
* Lead long\-term planning across both organizations, including long\-term and annual growth, sustainability, and program innovation.
* Develop and execute a cohesive strategic vision that aligns the missions of CPGR and CSH while respecting their distinct identities. Identifying opportunities to deepen integration, improve efficiency, and expand community impact through shared services.


  

*Governance \& Board Relations:*
* Serve as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, ensuring transparency, trust, and effective communication.
* Support the Board in fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities, including governance, compliance, and strategic oversight.
* Navigate the parent–affiliate relationship, ensuring appropriate authority, accountability, and decision\-making structures.
* Serve as a member of CSH subsidiary Boards related to the Stadium Estates affordable housing project, co\-developed by CSH.


  

*Operational \& Financial Oversight:*
* Oversee all operational functions across all entities, including programs, finance, HR, facilities, and shared administrative services.
* Ensure financial sustainability of both organizations, including budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation.
* Maintain clear financial separation and compliance with each organization’s EIN and regulatory requirements.
* Optimize shared service functions to improve efficiency while maintaining appropriate internal controls.


  

*Fundraising \& External Relations:*
* Lead comprehensive fundraising strategies across both organizations, including major gifts, grants, government funding, and partnerships.
* Serve as the primary external ambassador, strengthening relationships with funders, community leaders, and stakeholders.
* Elevate the visibility and reputation of both CSH and CPGR locally and regionally.


  

*Program Leadership \& Impact:*
* Ensure high\-quality, mission\-driven programming that meets community needs and delivers measurable outcomes.
* Foster collaboration across programs and sites to maximize impact and reduce duplication.
* Promote data\-driven decision\-making and continuous improvement.


  

*Organizational Culture \& Talent:*
* Build and sustain a unified, inclusive organizational culture across both entities.
* Recruit, develop, and retain a high\-performing leadership team.
* Support staff alignment and clarity within a shared services structure.


  

*Key Leadership Challenges:*
* Balancing dual\-entity leadership with differing governance structures and organizational scale.

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy
jobs.description:
**About Us**  

The Just One Project's mission is to increase access to food, resources, and supportive services to build a stronger, healthier, and more connected community. The Just One Project has a culture of attracting the most passionate and talented people to represent The Just One Project by reinforcing strong values, work\-life balance, and diversity. We know that our company culture ultimately affects client experience. Every program is designed with our clients in mind; we are "client\-centric."  

  

**What You'll Do**  

As Director of Philanthropy, you will lead and execute strategies that grow philanthropic revenue and strengthen long\-term donor relationships by:

* Leading the organization's fundraising strategy and achieving annual philanthropic revenue goals.
* Building and managing a strong pipeline of individual donors, major gift prospects, corporate partners, and sponsors.
* Cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major gifts while expanding unrestricted funding.
* Developing new donor acquisition strategies while strengthening engagement with existing supporters.
* Planning and overseeing fundraising events that generate revenue and deepen donor relationships.
* Partnering closely with the CEO and senior leadership to execute strategic fundraising initiatives.
* Tracking fundraising performance through CRM reporting, revenue forecasting, and pipeline management.
* Collaborating with marketing to create compelling donor communications, campaigns, and storytelling.
* Building systems and processes that support accountability, sustainability, and long\-term fundraising success.

**What We're Looking For**  

The ideal candidate is an experienced fundraising professional who combines strategic thinking with disciplined execution and exceptional relationship building.  

  

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Public Relations, Nonprofit Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Seven or more years of progressive nonprofit fundraising, development, donor relations, or partnership management experience.
* Demonstrated success securing major gifts of $25,000 or more.
* Proven experience managing fundraising events, corporate partnerships, and major donor portfolios.
* Demonstrated history of generating at least $500,000 in annual fundraising revenue.
* Experience working directly with executive leadership on fundraising strategy.
* Strong relationship building, communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.
* Experience using donor CRM systems to manage fundraising pipelines and reporting.
* Financial acumen with the ability to forecast revenue, monitor budgets, and measure fundraising performance.

**Preferred Qualifications**  

Candidates with experience generating more than $1 million annually in philanthropic revenue and securing six figure gifts are strongly encouraged to apply.  

  

**Why You'll Love This Role**  

You'll have the opportunity to:

* Shape the future of philanthropy at a growing nonprofit.
* Build meaningful relationships that directly impact thousands of individuals and families.
* Work alongside a collaborative and mission driven executive leadership team.
* Develop innovative fundraising strategies that create lasting community impact.
* Help expand programs that address food insecurity, housing stability, workforce development, and supportive services throughout Southern Nevada.

**Our Commitment**  

The Just One Project is more than a workplace. We are a team united by compassion, innovation, accountability, and service.  

  

As part of our culture, all team members support organization wide initiatives that strengthen our mission, including participation in up to six **Pop\-Up and Give** community events each year. These events are typically held on the third Saturday of the month and provide opportunities for our entire team to serve the community together.  

  

**Work Schedule**  

This is a full time exempt position. Evening and weekend work is required as needed to support donor meetings, fundraising events, and organizational initiatives.  

  

Local travel throughout Southern Nevada is required. A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and the ability to meet the organization's insurability requirements are required.  

  

**Join Our Team**  

If you're passionate about building relationships, securing transformational gifts, and helping create lasting change in our community, we'd love to hear from you.  

  

Apply today and help us create a stronger Southern Nevada\-one family, one partnership, and one act of generosity at a time.  

  

**Equal Opportunity Employer**  

The Just One Project is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.  

  

**Don't Meet Every Qualification?**  

Research shows that many qualified candidates, particularly those from historically underrepresented communities, hesitate to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. If you're excited about this opportunity and believe you can make an impact, we encourage you to apply. We'd love the opportunity to learn more about you.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the Founder/CEO
jobs.description:
**About The Center for Mind\-Body Medicine** 

The Center for Mind\-Body Medicine (CMBM) is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization whose mission is to help communities around the world heal from population\-wide trauma. Whether impacted by war and other forms of violence, climate\-related disaster, public health crises, poverty and racism, or other conditions and circumstances that can affect population\-wide mental health, CMBM partners with community leaders to deploy a trauma relief model that combines evidence\-based methodologies for self\-care with the wisdom and cultural values of that community. CMBM has trained more than 8,000 individuals thus far in mind\-body healing techniques throughout the world.

**About Dr. Gordon** 

James S. Gordon, M.D., is the Founder and CEO of The Center for Mind\-Body Medicine. A Harvard\-educated psychiatrist, he is also a Clinical Professor at Georgetown Medical School and was Chairman (under Presidents Clinton and G.W. Bush) of the White House Commission on Complementary and Alternative Medicine Policy. He is a noted author and essayist, authoring or editing ten books and publishing over 150 articles in professional journals and the popular press. He has also been featured on news and television programs such as CBS 60 Minutes, Good Morning America, The Today Show, CBS Sunday Morning, and on channels such as CNN and FOX News. Dr. Gordon’s most recent book is *Transforming Trauma: The Path to Hope and Healing*.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Assistant (EA) supports Dr. James S. Gordon, who has led efforts to relieve population\-wide psychological trauma for more than 30 years.

The EA will provide comprehensive administrative support to Dr. Gordon in all his activities, including speaking engagements, stakeholder communications, meetings with partners, donors, faculty and staff, and scheduling appointments. They will manage Dr Gordon’s busy and fluid schedule by balancing priorities, safeguarding his time and anticipating needs and demands placed on him. The EA’s responsibilities include but are not limited to: managing and prioritizing Dr. Gordon’s complex calendar; arranging national and international travel; preparing agendas, correspondence, reports, and presentations; including providing layout and graphics; and coordinating event logistics and communication across departments.

The EA serves as a key liaison between Dr. Gordon and internal and external stakeholders, provides technical support for Zoom and phone meetings, facilitates outreach to other organizations and media, and ensures that Dr. Gordon stays focused on high\-priority tasks. The EA reports directly to Dr. Gordon, and works in partnership with members of the CMBM team.

Dr. Gordon is an original thinker and charismatic leader. Both as CEO and as an essayist, he has many ideas and interests, and he needs an Executive Assistant who can navigate the complexities of responding quickly to events in the world around us.

The ideal candidate is detail\-oriented, adaptable, compassionate, and committed to excellence, a thoughtful writer and creative designer; she/he must be open\-minded and good humored, and is deeply interested in—or at least curious about—mind\-body medicine.The EA may be given additional responsibilities as needed and/or assigned. This is a hybrid position, with some travel to the DC office and to Dr. Gordon’s home office approximately once or twice a week.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Administration**

* Oversee Dr. Gordon’s busy and fluid schedule, including balancing priorities, safeguarding his time, anticipating and resolving conflicts, and ensuring he is prepared for calls, appointments, meetings, and events
* Manage Dr. Gordon’s calendar, including scheduling appointments, sending invitations, arranging Zoom meetings, and coordinating seamless transitions between activities
* Serve as a liaison between Dr. Gordon and CMBM staff, partners, and other stakeholders. Coordinate communications, track follow\-up items, and ensure he has the background information and materials needed for meetings and engagements
* Handle and report official expenses and reimbursements from tracking expenditures, maintaining receipts and supporting documentation, preparing and submitting expense reports, to following up for timely reimbursement
* Make appointments on Dr. Gordon’s behalf and coordinate and oversee some household tasks
* Manage incoming and outgoing mail, such as opening, sorting, and routing correspondence; preparing and mailing packages; and fulfilling and shipping requests for Dr. Gordon’s books
* Screen Dr. Gordon’s email, telephone, and social media correspondence, determine the appropriate response or follow\-up, and escalate urgent or sensitive matters, as needed
* Organize and maintain physical and digital files, including reports, research, correspondence, works in progress, and other relevant materials
* Support the recruitment, onboarding, and supervision of interns in collaboration with the Human Resources Manager
* Participate in CMBM’s weekly staff meetings, Dr. Gordon’s weekly research meetings, and other meetings, as appropriate

**Communications, Writing, and Research Support**

* Transcribe correspondence dictated by Dr. Gordon, including researching and inserting relevant links, gathering attachments
* Transcribe, edit, format, and organize drafts of articles, books, essays, blog posts, proposals, and other written materials
* Assist with formatting and pitching essays and op\-ed pieces to major publications, including *The New York Times*, *The Washington Post*, among others
* Draft, schedule and publish Substack and social media posts
* Prepare and format PowerPoint presentations, background materials, reports, and executive summaries for meetings, interviews, speaking engagements, trainings, and events
* Conduct online research, evaluating and synthesizing information from credible sources to support Dr. Gordon’s writing, presentations,

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Executive Director serves as the primary leader, advocate, and public representative of Allied Arts of Whatcom County. This role focuses on strengthening the organization’s role as a central connector and champion for the arts through partnerships, fundraising, and strategic leadership.

The Executive Director works closely with the Board of Directors to guide the organization’s vision and sustainability while supporting staff responsible for program implementation. Much of the role involves relationship building across the arts community, civic organizations, and local institutions.

The Executive Director also leads the organization’s fundraising efforts, including grant writing, donor development, and sponsorship cultivation.

**Key Responsibilities** 

Community Leadership \& Advocacy

Serve as the primary ambassador for Allied Arts within the community.

Responsibilities include:

* Building relationships with artists, arts organizations, and community partners
* Representing Allied Arts in regional conversations about arts and culture
* Advocating for the role of the arts in the community
* Participating in civic and cultural leadership forums
* Working toward Allied Arts having a leadership role in initiatives such as the proposed Whatcom County Arts and Culture Committee

Partnerships \& Community Engagement

Develop strategic partnerships that strengthen the regional arts ecosystem.

Responsibilities include:

* Building collaborations with local arts organizations, schools, and community groups
* Supporting initiatives that elevate emerging artists
* Identifying opportunities for shared programs and community impact
* Strengthening Allied Arts’ role as a connector within the arts community

Fundraising \& Grant Development

Lead the organization’s fundraising strategy.

Responsibilities include:

* Researching and writing grant applications
* Managing grant reporting and compliance
* Cultivating donor relationships
* Identifying sponsorship opportunities
* Working with the board to support fundraising initiatives

Organizational Leadership

Provide strategic leadership and ensure the organization operates effectively.

Responsibilities include:

* Working with the Board of Directors to guide strategic planning
* Monitoring organizational goals and priorities
* Supporting staff and ensuring projects move forward
* Managing organizational operations and systems
* Ensuring compliance with nonprofit regulations

Financial Oversight

Work with the bookkeeper and board treasurer to maintain financial health.

Responsibilities include:

* Creating and monitoring organizational budgets
* Supporting responsible use of grant funding
* Reviewing financial reports and guiding financial decisions
* Supporting long\-term financial sustainability

Staff \& Organizational Leadership

Provide leadership and oversight for all staff and organizational functions.

Responsibilities include:

* Supervising and supporting all staff positions across programs, marketing, and finance
* Providing clear direction and priorities aligned with the organization’s strategic goals
* Ensuring staff projects and programs are progressing on schedule and within budget
* Facilitating regular staff communication and coordination across departments
* Supporting staff problem\-solving and decision\-making when challenges arise
* Encouraging a collaborative, efficient, and mission\-focused team culture
* Monitoring staff workload and helping prioritize organizational efforts when capacity is limited

The Executive Director focuses on organizational leadership and oversight, while staff managers lead the day\-to\-day implementation of programs and operations.

**Desired Skills \& Experience**

* Leadership experience in nonprofit, arts, or community organizations
* Strong relationship\-building and partnership development skills
* Experience with grant writing and fundraising
* Ability to represent the organization publicly and build trust across sectors
* Strategic thinking and organizational leadership
* Passion for arts education and supporting creative communities

Pay: $68,500\.00 \- $70,800\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Work Location: In person

**Director of Philanthropy and Community Engagement****Job Title:** Director of Philanthropy \& Community Engagement**Status:** Regular, Full Time**Reports To:** Executive Director**Compensation:** $90,000 \-$120,000 DOE**Department:** Philanthropy/Development**Classification:** Exempt**Home Office:** Seattle/Hybrid: Required in the office 3 days a week \& 2 days remote.**Office hours:** 8:30 a.m. \-4:30 p.m. Relationship\-building is central to this role; occasional evening and weekend participation in fundraising events, donor gatherings, board activities, and community events is required.  

**Application Requirements:**
To be considered, applicants must apply online: **https://mockingbirdsociety.org/about/careers)** and include a resume and a letter of interest that includes a statement regarding the applicant’s commitment to racial equity.  

**ABOUT THE MOCKINGBIRD SOCIETY**
The Mockingbird Society (TMS) is a non\-partisan advocacy organization focused on transforming foster care and ending youth homelessness. We do this by creating, supporting, and advocating for racially equitable, healthy environments that develop youth and young adults at risk of or experiencing foster care or homelessness.  

**POSITION SUMMARY**
The Director of Philanthropy \& Community Engagement leads The Mockingbird Society's fundraising strategy, revenue generation, donor and community relationships, sponsorships, board engagement, and philanthropic growth. As Mockingbird's lead fundraiser and ambassador, this role builds authentic partnerships that advance youth\-led systems change.  


As a member of the Leadership Team, the Director works closely with the Executive Director, Communications Director, Board of Directors, program leaders, and youth and young adults to build meaningful relationships that strengthen support for Mockingbird's mission. Together, they help tell the story of Mockingbird's impact, deepen connections with supporters and community partners, and create opportunities for people to meaningfully invest in systems change for young people.  


Grounded in Community\-Centric Fundraising principles, the Director cultivates a culture where philanthropy is rooted in relationships, shared values, and collective responsibility. The role ensures fundraising, donor engagement, storytelling, and community events are ethical, youth\-centered, and aligned with Mockingbird's commitment to racial equity and meaningful youth leadership.  

**WHAT YOU’LL BRING**
You are a relationship\-builder who believes philanthropy is rooted in community, trust, and shared responsibility. You enjoy connecting people to a meaningful mission and creating opportunities for supporters, partners, and community members to invest in lasting change for young people.  


You bring a balance of strategy and heart to your work. You are collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable working across teams while building authentic relationships with donors, board members, youth, and community partners. You are committed to racial equity, youth leadership, and community\-centered approaches to fundraising and engagement.  


Most importantly, you lead with authenticity, curiosity, humility, and a sense of humor. You take the mission seriously while helping create a workplace where people feel connected, supported, and inspired.

jobs.title: Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager - Executive Director
jobs.description:
Morgan Stanley Community Development Finance is seeking a senior-level Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager to lead the end-to-end management of the Firm’s affordable housing private equity investment portfolio. The role will oversee the full investment lifecycle—from sourcing and origination through underwriting, transaction approval, closing, portfolio and asset management, governance, risk monitoring, performance reporting, and investment exits.

This individual will serve as a senior product owner and relationship manager for affordable housing private equity strategies, working closely with internal stakeholders, fund managers, sponsors, legal counsel, risk partners, and other control functions to ensure disciplined execution, strong portfolio performance, and alignment with Morgan Stanley’s community development, risk management, and business objectives.

Note: Location is open within the the U.S.

Responsibilities

Oversee the affordable housing private equity product strategy and portfolio management framework, including origination priorities, investment guidelines, portfolio objectives, performance targets, and exit planning.
Lead sourcing and originations for new affordable housing private equity investment opportunities, including evaluation of fund managers, sponsors, markets, investment structures, projected returns, community development impact, and strategic fit.
Oversee due diligence, underwriting, financial analysis, market review, sponsor and guarantor assessment, legal documentation, and transaction approval materials for new investments and follow-on commitments.
Present investment opportunities, portfolio updates, risk matters, and strategic recommendations to transaction council, senior management, credit partners, and other internal governance forums.
Serve as the primary relationship manager for affordable housing private equity fund managers, developers, sponsors, and other external partners, ensuring strong communication, accountability, and execution.
Manage post-closing portfolio oversight, periodic asset reviews, compliance monitoring, operating performance analysis, capital account tracking, distribution forecasting, valuation support, and watchlist management.
Monitor fund and underlying asset performance against underwriting expectations, investment agreements, regulatory requirements, and CRA objectives.
Represent Morgan Stanley on fund advisory boards, investor committees, and other governance bodies, providing guidance on consents, amendments, waivers, workouts, dispositions, and other material portfolio matters.
Partner with internal risk stake holders to ensure appropriate controls, approvals, reporting, and issue resolution.
Lead, mentor, and develop staff supporting affordable housing private equity products, promoting strong execution standards, analytical rigor, and consistent portfolio management practices.

Skills Required

Deep understanding of affordable housing finance, private equity fund structures, LIHTC investments, multi-family real estate underwriting, asset management, and portfolio risk management.
Strong financial modeling, valuation, credit analysis, cash flow forecasting, and investment performance assessment skills.
Proven ability to evaluate complex transactions, identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and make sound investment recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex investment, risk, and portfolio matters clearly to senior management and governance committees.
Strong relationship management and negotiation skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively with fund managers, developers, sponsors, legal counsel, and internal control partners.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities, transactions, portfolio matters, and deadlines in a complex institutional environment.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with portfolio reporting systems, investment databases, and data visualization tools preferred.

Experience

15+ years of relevant experience in affordable housing finance, private equity, multi-family real estate investment, asset management, credit, or portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience managing investments across the full lifecycle, including origination, underwriting, approval, closing, construction or stabilization monitoring, ongoing asset management, workouts or restructurings, and exits.
Experience with public sector financing sources and regulatory frameworks, including Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HUD/FHA programs, tax-exempt bonds, state and local housing programs, and other community development tools.
Established relationships with affordable housing developers, fund managers, lenders, investors, public agencies, and other industry participants preferred.
Prior experience leading teams, managing senior stakeholder relationships, and operating within a regulated financial institution or similarly complex investment platform strongly preferred.

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

New York

However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs.

This individual will serve as a senior product owner and relationship manager for affordable housing private equity strategies, working closely with internal stakeholders, fund managers, sponsors, legal counsel, risk partners, and other control functions to ensure disciplined execution, strong portfolio performance, and alignment with Morgan Stanley’s community development, risk management, and business objectives.

Responsibilities

Oversee the affordable housing private equity product strategy and portfolio management framework, including origination priorities, investment guidelines, portfolio objectives, performance targets, and exit planning.
Lead sourcing and originations for new affordable housing private equity investment opportunities, including evaluation of fund managers, sponsors, markets, investment structures, projected returns, community development impact, and strategic fit.
Oversee due diligence, underwriting, financial analysis, market review, sponsor and guarantor assessment, legal documentation, and transaction approval materials for new investments and follow-on commitments.
Present investment opportunities, portfolio updates, risk matters, and strategic recommendations to transaction council, senior management, credit partners, and other internal governance forums.
Serve as the primary relationship manager for affordable housing private equity fund managers, developers, sponsors, and other external partners, ensuring strong communication, accountability, and execution.

Lead, mentor, and develop staff supporting affordable housing private equity products, promoting strong execution standards, analytical rigor, and consistent portfolio management practices.

Deep understanding of affordable housing finance, private equity fund structures, LIHTC investments, multi-family real estate underwriting, asset management, and portfolio risk management.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex investment, risk, and portfolio matters clearly to senior management and governance committees.
Strong relationship management and negotiation skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively with fund managers, developers, sponsors, legal counsel, and internal control partners.

Experience with public sector financing sources and regulatory frameworks, including Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HUD/FHA programs, tax-exempt bonds, state and local housing programs, and other community development tools.
Established relationships with affordable housing developers, fund managers, lenders, investors, public agencies, and other industry participants preferred.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
TITLE:
Beacon Program Director

DEPARTMENT:
Youth and Community Development Services

PROGRAM:
DYCD Beacon Initiative

Work Schedule

School Year: Monday-Friday, 11 a.m. - 7 p.m., alternating Saturdays. PD is required to work and alternate a 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. shift with the Assistant Director twice a week.

Summer: Monday-Friday, 9:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. as an exempt employee; working hours will include non-standard hours

SALARY RANGE:
$80,000-82,000 annually

REPORTS TO:
Manhattan Deputy Director of Youth Programs

DATE:
July, 2026

Job Summary

The Beacon Program Director provides strategic leadership and overall management of Grand Street Settlement's Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) Beacon Community Center, serving as the agency's primary liaison within the school and surrounding community. The Director is responsible for planning, implementing, and overseeing a comprehensive, year-round community center that provides high-quality, innovative programming and services for elementary and middle school youth, high school youth, adults, and older adults. In partnership with school leadership, community organizations, and agency staff, the Director fosters a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment that promotes academic achievement, positive youth development, family engagement, wellness, leadership, and community connection. The Director provides leadership in program development, staff supervision, partnership cultivation, fiscal and operational management, and continuous quality improvement while ensuring compliance with DYCD performance standards and advancing Grand Street Settlement's mission of strengthening individuals, families, and communities.

Education, Experience And Skill Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree required
Supervision of multiple budgets and programs
Proven track record of successfully working with multiple school leadership teams and accompanying stakeholders
At least three (3) years of experience working in a community center or school-based after-school program; at least two years of which were in a supervisory capacity.
Required to obtain a SACC Program Director's (30-hour) credentials.
Ability to work independently, assess priorities, and take initiative.
Effective oral, written, and collaborative skills.
Experience in lesson planning, curriculum development, and implementation of structured programming for students in school settings.
Familiarity with Program Budgeting, fiscal management a plus.
Familiarity with DYCD Connect and database management is a plus.
Ability to maintain State Central Registry (SCR) clearance- $25 nonrefundable fee required and fingerprint clearance throughout the duration of employment.
Experience working with students in urban school and/or community-based settings
Must be computer literate.
Capacity to thrive under pressure while working on multiple tasks and projects
Must be able to build and maintain a productive working relationship with the school’s administration & personnel.
Knowledge of the public education system and positive youth development best practices.
Strong public speaking, writing, and organizational skills.
Must demonstrate knowledge of New York State Learning Standards.
Knowledge in STEM, Health & Sexuality, Careers & Life Planning, Sports & Adventure, and Academic Enrichment highly desirable.
Must Be CPR/First Aid Certified
Bilingual (Spanish or Chinese preferred) a plus

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Develop and implement comprehensive outreach, recruitment, enrollment, and retention strategies to maintain full enrollment in accordance with DYCD Beacon contract requirements, including 100 school-age participants (75 elementary and 25 middle school youth), 100 high school participants, and 100 adult participants.
Monitor enrollment, attendance, retention, and participation data using DYCD Connect and agency reporting systems to ensure the program consistently meets or exceeds DYCD Results-Oriented Performance (ROP) standards, including maintaining a minimum 85% participant retention rate, and implement corrective action plans when needed.
Provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of the DYCD Beacon Community Center, ensuring high-quality, inclusive programming that advances Grand Street Settlement's mission and meets all DYCD contractual, fiscal, and programmatic requirements.
Provide leadership and coordination for all Grand Street Settlement programs operating within the school building, including the DYCD Beacon, COMPASS, SONYC, 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC), Summer Rising, holiday programming, and other agency initiatives, fostering collaboration, integrated service delivery, shared resources, and a seamless experience for participants and families.
Serve as Grand Street Settlement's primary liaison to the school community by cultivating strong relationships with school leadership, teachers, support staff, parents, students, community organizations, funding partners, and other key stakeholders.
Partner with school administration to align Beacon programming with school priorities, student success initiatives, and community needs while strengthening the connection between school-day and out-of-school-time learning.
Develop, implement, and oversee high-quality programming that promotes academic success, STEM, arts enrichment, leadership development, physical wellness, workforce readiness, family engagement, and positive youth development for children, youth, adults, and older adults.
Recruit, hire, supervise, coach, mentor, and evaluate full-time, part-time, seasonal, and volunteer staff while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, equity, and continuous professional growth.
Provide leadership and support to site management teams by establishing clear expectations, conducting regular supervision and performance evaluations, and ensuring staff completes all required agency, DYCD, DOHMH/SACC, and regulatory trainings and certifications.
Foster collaboration among all Grand Street Settlement programs housed within the school by coordinating services, sharing resources, jointly planning initiatives, and creating seamless pathways of support for children, youth, families, adults, and older adults.
Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with schools, community-based organizations, higher education institutions, businesses, healthcare providers, government agencies, and other stakeholders to expand resources and opportunities for participants and families.
Secure a minimum of three (3) new strategic community partnerships annually that enhance programming and address identified community needs.
Plan, implement, and evaluate at least four (4) major non-holiday community events annually that respond to community needs while promoting family engagement, community partnerships, and participant achievement.
Conduct ongoing community needs assessments using participant feedback, stakeholder input, surveys, and program data to guide program planning and continuous improvement.
Represent Grand Street Settlement at school leadership meetings, School Leadership Team meetings, Building Council meetings, DYCD convenings, community coalitions, and other stakeholder meetings.
Develop and manage program budgets, monitor expenditures, and ensure responsible fiscal stewardship while supporting grant development, reporting, and resource development efforts.
Ensure accurate enrollment, attendance, participant records, reporting, and documentation in compliance with DYCD, DOE, DOHMH/SACC, and agency requirements.
Oversee the School Foods Program, educational field trips, participant showcases, and special events, ensuring compliance with agency policies and contractual expectations.
Maintain a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment by collaborating with school personnel to address facility, maintenance, and safety concerns.
Prepare for and successfully participate in DYCD, DOE, DOHMH, and internal monitoring visits, audits, and quality assurance reviews.
Perform other duties as assigned to support the mission and strategic priorities of Grand Street Settlement.

Administrative

Ensure accurate enrollment, attendance, participant records, and data entry in DYCD Connect and other agency systems to maintain compliance with contractual requirements.
Oversee program budgets, monitor expenditures, and ensure timely purchasing and fiscal accountability in accordance with agency and funder guidelines.
Prepare monthly program calendars, reports, schedules, and documentation to support effective program operations and communication.
Ensure compliance with all DYCD, DOE, DOHMH School-Aged Child Care (SACC), Summer Day Camp, and Grand Street Settlement policies, procedures, and licensing requirements, including quarterly internal compliance reviews.
Oversee the administration of the School Foods Program, ensuring compliance with all documentation, reporting, and food safety requirements.
Coordinate major program events, participant showcases, and agency-wide initiatives in collaboration with Grand Street Settlement leadership and Program Directors.
Maintain regular communication with DYCD, DOE, school leadership, funding partners, and agency departments while representing the program at required meetings and trainings.
Collaborate with agency leadership on strategic planning, cross-site initiatives, quality improvement efforts, and organizational priorities.

Facility Management

Ensure the Beacon Center maintains a safe, clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment for participants, families, staff, and community partners.
Work collaboratively with school administration and custodial staff to address facility, maintenance, safety, and operational needs in a timely manner.
Conduct routine facility inspections and ensure all program spaces meet health, safety, and licensing standards.
Support emergency preparedness procedures and ensure compliance with agency and school safety protocols.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned in support of Grand Street Settlement's mission and operational needs.

How To Apply

Please submit a resume and thoughtful cover letter, outlining how your skills and experience meet the qualifications of the position you are applying for. If selected, we ask that you also provide us with three (3) professional references that we can contact (at least one (1) professional reference should be from a former supervisor). Please click on the link provided below, or use the link in a search bar, and apply online through our career center.

https://workforcenow.adp.com/jobs/apply/posting.html?client=grandst&ccId=19000101_000001&type=MP&lang=en_US

No phone calls, please!

Please be advised that job offers can only be made once your clearances come through!
