About Mpta

Created through North Carolina's landmark Projects for Advancing Vehicle-Infrastructure Enhancements (PAVE) Act, the Metropolitan Public Transportation Authority (MPTA) has been entrusted with delivering a bold vision for mobility, economic opportunity, accessibility, and regional connectivity throughout Mecklenburg County and the greater Charlotte region. It is worth noting that voters were asked to approve the tax, not specific transportation plans.

The voter-approved initiative provides a projected $19.4 billion transportation investment program for transit over the next 30 years that will expand mobility options, modernize transit infrastructure, strengthen regional connectivity, provide greater access to transit-dependent riders, and support continued economic growth for decades to come. As a newly established independent regional transit authority, separated from the City of Charlotte, the MPTA will guide one of the most ambitious transportation programs in the Southeast while helping shape the future of mobility for generations of residents, businesses, and visitors.

The MPTA is governed by a 27-member Board of Directors representing communities and stakeholders from across Mecklenburg County and the state. The Board includes transit riders, small business leaders, and professionals with expertise in finance, engineering, planning, law, real estate development, and related disciplines. Through its Executive, Operations and Safety, Planning and Capital Project Delivery, and Finance and Audit Committees, the Board provides strategic direction and oversight for one of the region's most important public transportation investment organizations.

The MPTA builds upon nearly five decades of public transportation service in the Charlotte region. Charlotte Transit began operating bus service as a department of the City of Charlotte in 1976, and the Charlotte Area Transit System (CATS) was established in 2000 to lead the region's transit within the City of Charlotte. Today, that system includes an extensive multimodal network of bus, light rail, streetcar, paratransit, vanpool, and microtransit services and serves as the largest public transportation system between Atlanta and Washington, D.C.

The process has begun to transfer employees and assets from the City of Charlotte to the MPTA, which will oversee the delivery of bus, rail, paratransit, microtransit, and other mobility services throughout Mecklenburg County and eventually the Charlotte region. Current public transportation services operated by CATS are provided through a combination of employees employed directly by CATS and a nonprofit corporation known as Transit Management of Charlotte (TMOC). Bus operators, specifically, are contracted and employed by TMOC and represented by SMART Transportation Division Local 1715, the exclusive collective bargaining unit for bus operators. rail, paratransit, maintenance, administrative, and other transit personnel operate under separate employment and management structures and are employed directly by CATS.

As the region transitions from the City of Charlotte to the newly created MPTA, the Authority's leadership will be responsible for maintaining strong relationships with employees, labor representatives, contractors, and operating partners while ensuring the continued delivery of safe, reliable, customer-focused transit services.

The creation of the MPTA marks the next chapter in that evolution of transit for the Charlotte region. By transitioning from a city-operated department to an independent regional authority, the MPTA will build upon a strong operational foundation while striving to become the nation’s premier transit authority, pushing the region to cultivate educational and training institutions focused on innovative transit solutions that will foster generations of talent focused on public transit services designed to meet the needs of one of America's fastest-growing metropolitan regions.

Mpta Transition Mission Statement

Through safety, reliability, transparency, and accountability, MPTA earns the confidence of the region it serves. We connect people to opportunity, strengthen regional prosperity, and build a transit system that the region will trust, value, and support.

About The Region

Located within Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, the City of Charlotte has emerged as one of the nation's most dynamic and desirable metropolitan areas in the nation. Home to nearly one million residents and located within a metropolitan region approaching three million people, Charlotte continues to attract new residents, employers, and investment at an exceptional pace.

The region offers an exceptional quality of life, combining economic opportunity, affordability, and outstanding community amenities. Charlotte's economy is powered by nationally recognized employers in finance, healthcare, energy, technology, manufacturing, and logistics. Residents benefit from excellent public and private schools, respected higher education institutions including the University of North Carolina at Charlotte, Davidson College, Johnson C Smith University, Central Piedmont Community College, Johnson and Wales University Charlotte and Queens University of Charlotte, and a cost of living that remains attractive relative to many peer metropolitan areas.

Beyond its economic strengths, Charlotte offers a vibrant lifestyle that appeals to individuals and families alike. Residents enjoy major and minor professional sports, including the Carolina Panthers, Charlotte Hornets, Charlotte FC, Charlotte Knights, and Charlotte Checkers, a thriving arts and cultural scene, diverse dining and entertainment options, and extensive outdoor recreation opportunities. Hundreds of miles of greenways, walking and biking trails, nearby lakes, and convenient access to the Blue Ridge Mountains contribute to a quality of life that consistently ranks among the best in the Southeast.

Position Summary

Reporting directly to and at the direction of the MPTA Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the Authority’s chief strategic leader and principal public representative. The CEO is responsible for all aspects of organizational leadership, including operations, safety, capital program delivery, administration, financial stewardship, workforce and business development, risk management and regulatory compliance, stakeholder engagement, innovation, and long-range strategic planning.

The CEO will work closely with the board, municipalities, local, state, and federal government officials, community organizations, business stakeholders, riders, employees, and regional partners to advance a shared vision for transportation and regional prosperity. The successful candidate must be equally comfortable serving as a strategist, coalition builder, diplomat, communicator, innovator, and, most importantly, an operational executive. Through the delivery of safe, reliable, accessible, affordable, and timely transit operations, the next CEO will help shape economic development patterns, improve access to opportunity, support workforce mobility, advance transit-oriented development, and enhance quality of life throughout the region.

Scope And Responsibilities

The inaugural CEO will be expected to:

Establish the identity, credibility, and culture of the newly created Authority.
Build trust among the Board, municipalities, riders, employees, elected officials, business leaders, and community stakeholders.
Deliver safe, reliable, and customer-focused transit services while advancing transformational investments.
Build trusting relationships and provide support, mentorship, training and leadership to the Authority’s employees during this period of transition to ensure that they are empowered to deliver the highest quality of services possible.
Strengthen relationships with regional, state, and federal partners.
Create and manage a high-performing leadership team capable of executing a generational transportation vision.
Position Charlotte and Mecklenburg County as a national leader in mobility, transportation innovation, and transit-oriented economic development.
Demonstrate that transportation investments can improve access to opportunity, support economic growth, and enhance quality of life for all residents.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities Include

Provide visionary leadership for the Authority and establish MPTA as a premier national mobility organization that offers safe, secure, reliable, customer-focused, timely, affordable, and accessible transit services to its customers.
Partner closely with the board to translate policy direction into measurable outcomes that positively impact and enhance the quality of life in the region.
Direct the day-to-day operations of the MPTA in accordance with established board policy and applicable laws.
Develop, execute, and deliver transit services through strategic initiatives that advance mobility, economic development, and long-term regional growth while constantly considering new technologies, and cost-effective alternative service delivery options consistent with the organizations mission.
Build and promote a culture of operational excellence, accountability, transparency, inclusion, innovation and continuous improvement.
Strengthen public confidence through exceptional service delivery and responsive leadership.
Oversee planning, financing, and implementation of one of the nation’s most significant transportation investment programs while continuing to deliver high- quality transit services to customers.
Demonstrated ability to establish and oversee enterprise-wide risk management, safety, security, and compliance programs ensuring adherence to applicable federal, state, and local regulations while proactively identifying, mitigating, and monitoring operational, financial, legal, and reputational risks.
Advance major mobility initiatives including the Gold Line Streetcar Program, the Better Bus Program, Red Line, Silver Line, and future multimodal investments.
Ensure projects are delivered responsibly, efficiently, and in alignment with board priorities.
Build productive relationships with elected and local leaders at the local, state, and federal level.
Navigate a complex governance environment involving multiple jurisdictions, municipalities, and stakeholder groups.
Serve as a trusted ambassador and advocate for the Authority in the media and in public settings.
Develop and submit for board approval an annual budget that meets the organizational needs of MPTA.
Serve as the lead champion of the MPTA and its successes at a local, state and national level to obtain support, funding and other services needed to build a world-class organization and transit system.
Foster innovation while maintaining operational discipline and fiscal responsibility.
Recruit, develop, and retain a high-performing executive leadership team and workforce.
Develop organizational capacity and succession strength for long-term success.

In this senior leadership position, you will own the product vision and multi\-year roadmap for a next\-generation, real\-time fraud intelligence platform that protects millions of customers across digital banking, payments, and financial ecosystems.
Leverage your expertise in transformer\-based ML, graph intelligence, continuous learning, and modern MLOps, you will build capabilities to detect fraud rings, coordinated attacks, and multi\-step fraud schemes. You will drive innovation in dynamic feature engineering, graph\-based risk detection, sequence modeling, and experimentation frameworks to rapidly deliver governed fraud models that protect customers. Partnering with Fraud Operations, Data Science, Engineering, Product, and Model Risk Management, you will deliver measurable fraud\-loss reduction while preserving an excellent customer experience. You will also communicate platform strategy, experiment outcomes, and capability roadmaps to senior leaders to inform decisions and continuously improve fraud prevention.  

**Job responsibilities*** Oversees the product roadmap, vision, development, execution, risk management, and business growth targets
* Leads the entire product life cycle through planning, execution, and future development by continuously adapting, developing new products and methodologies, managing risks, and achieving business targets like cost, features, reusability, and reliability to support growth
* Coaches and mentors the product team on best practices, such as solution generation, market research, storyboarding, mind\-mapping, prototyping methods, product adoption strategies, and product delivery, enabling them to effectively deliver on objectives
* Owns product performance and is accountable for investing in enhancements to achieve business objectives
* Monitors market trends, conducts competitive analysis, and identifies opportunities for product differentiation
* Own the multi\-year platform strategy and roadmap for fraud models, dynamic feature infrastructure (incl. streaming \+ feature store), graph intelligence, and MLOps across CCB payment and banking products.
* Lead experimentation and delivery with clear success criteria/lift metrics, converting validated POCs into production capabilities that reduce fraud loss and improve customer experience.
* Productize graph intelligence for fraud rings (entity schema, graph features/embeddings, freshness/latency SLAs, and explainability requirements).
* Establish end\-to\-end model lifecycle standards (model CI/CD, evaluation gates, monitoring, drift detection, automated retraining, and rollback) to ensure safe, reliable deployment.
* Embed governance by design including explainability, bias/fairness checks, and Model Risk documentation to meet regulatory expectations.
* Build strong partnerships and team capability by developing a high\-performing product org, collaborating cross\-functionally (Product, Engineering, Data Science, Fraud Ops, MRM), staying ahead of industry trends, and translating technical topics for executives.
**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills*** 8\+ years of experience or equivalent expertise delivering products, projects, or technology applications
* Extensive knowledge of the product development life cycle, technical design, and data analytics
* Proven ability to influence the adoption of key product life cycle activities including discovery, ideation, strategic development, requirements definition, and value management
* Experience driving change within organizations and managing stakeholders across multiple functions
* Bachelor's degree
* 5\+ years building or owning ML\-enabled products such as feature platforms, model platforms, or fraud decisioning systems in production environments.
* Deep expertise in fraud, payments risk, trust and safety, cybersecurity, or similarly adversarial domains where models face adaptive threats.
* Strong technical fluency across applied machine learning, data systems, and production constraints including latency, reliability, monitoring, and scale.
* Proven track record of leading cross\-functional execution with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Operations, and Model Risk Management teams.
* Exceptional communication and executive presence; comfortable translating technical capabilities into business value for senior leadership.
* Strong analytical skills and ability to define success metrics, evaluate experimentation results, and make data\-driven platform decisions.
**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills*** Recognized thought leader within a related field
* Advanced degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or related quantitative field
* Hands\-on experience building and scaling transformer\-based or other large\-scale sequence models in production, using high\-volume event data (e.g., fraud, security, behavioral analytics, risk).
* Experience productizing graph features/embeddings or graph ML for fraud ring detection, network analysis, or risk assessment.
* Proven RL system design in live environments (optimization/control/fraud decisioning), including reward design, online/offline evaluation, and safe deployment in adversarial settings.
* Experience designing feature stores and maintaining online/offline parity at scale for real\-time decisioning systems.
* Strong representation learning/embeddings and long\-horizon temporal modeling skills, familiarity with financial services model governance, and demonstrated thought leadership (papers, patents, talks, or open source).

**Position Title: Director of Communications**

**Job Purpose**

Exodus World Service seeks an experienced, talented communications professional to join our energetic and supportive team. The ideal candidate will thrive in a fast\-paced and collaborative environment, value excellence, and produce content that motivates others to take action. If this sounds like you, keep reading!

As Director of Communications, you’ll serve as a strategist, content creator, project manager, and team leader. Your goal is to drive deeper and wider engagement in our mission of mobilizing the Christian community to serve resettled refugees in Chicagoland and displaced refugees overseas.

If you are experienced in nonprofit communications, excel at driving multifaceted initiatives from concept to reality, and motivated by a mission that helps refugees locally and globally, this position may be for you.

**About Exodus World Service**

Founded in 1988, Exodus World Service mobilizes the Christian community to welcome, serve, and befriend refugees. Through education, church partnerships, and volunteer engagement, Exodus equips individuals and congregations to build meaningful relationships with refugees across Chicagoland and beyond, and empowers people to become champions for refugees.

In addition to its long\-standing local ministry initiatives, the organization is expanding global partnerships, strengthening advocacy efforts, and developing new community\-centered programs to meet evolving refugee needs in the United States and internationally.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

1\. In collaboration with the Executive Director, develop communications plans and strategies.

2\. Create and implement campaigns that achieve specific program, fundraising, and event goals.

3\. Conceive of and produce compelling content across mediums, including web, email, social, video, and print. Ensure integration across platforms.

4\. Direct others in content creation, providing substantive editing and copyediting. Proofread materials with a high attention to detail.

5\. Work closely with fund development, mobilization, education, and program teams to produce support materials on a regular basis.

6\. Manage the Communications Team, supporting their continued professional growth and development.

7\. Oversee all communications projects, set priorities, and ensure that deadlines are met.

8\. Ensure that high\-quality content (written and visual) is produced that aligns with the brand story, editorial, and graphic standards. Ensure consistent look, style, and feel for communications across the organization.

9\. Provide creative direction and manage relationships with contractors, including graphic designers, photographers, videographers, printers, etc. Includes understanding print and mail house production needs and scheduling.

10\. Oversee key performance indicator reports and keep up with industry trends to ensure effective marketing communications.

11\. Generate new and innovative ideas to increase engagement and grow target audiences.

12\. Other duties as assigned.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

1\. Commitment to Exodus World Service’s Christian mission and values.

2\. Desire to inspire and empower the Christian community to serve refugees.

3\. Exceptional ability to write compelling content and to edit others’ content.

4\. Experience with a variety of communications channels, including email, web, social, video, print, and direct mail.

5\. Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple workflows with numerous details in a fast\-paced environment.

6\. Strong copyediting and proofreading skills; familiarity with AP Style a plus.

7\. Excellent relational and interpersonal skills, including a positive attitude and a customer service approach toward working with team members.

8\. Ability to work well independently and as part of a highly collaborative team.

9\. High level of organization, attention to detail, and time management skills.

10\. Experience relating to diverse groups of people. Knowledge of refugee and cross\-cultural concerns a plus.

11\. Experience supervising staff and/or freelance creative individuals.

12\. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite. Experience with Adobe Creative Suite a plus.

**Education and Experience**

Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, journalism, English, or related field. At least 5\-7 years’ experience in marketing communications, copy writing, or other content production. Must have portfolio to demonstrate capabilities.

**Job Classification**

Full\-time exempt. Work generally conducted Monday – Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Occasional evening and weekend availability required.

**Compensation and Benefits**

Annual salary of $75,000\-$80,000, commensurate with experience. Eligible for paid time off; health, dental, and vision insurance; short\-term disability insurance; and retirement benefits.

**Location**

Exodus World Service office in Park Ridge, IL, with ability for remote work on occasion as appropriate.

**About Exodus World Service**

Founded in 1988, Exodus World Service mobilizes the Christian community to welcome and befriend refugees. We do this by educating churches about the plight of refugees, connecting volunteers with refugees through practical service projects, and empowering people to be champions for resettled refugees in Chicagoland and refugees overseas.

Please submit cover letter and resume to hr@exodusworldservice.org.

**Position Summary:** The Executive Director provides visionary leadership and strategic oversight for the Mount Mary University Institute for the Advancement of Women and Children. The Institute advances the University's longstanding commitment to gender equity and empowerment by equipping women and children with the tools, resources, and support necessary to thrive personally, academically, and professionally. Reporting directly to the President and working in close partnership with the Institute's Executive Committee, the Executive Director is responsible for advancing the Institute's mission through program development, resource cultivation, partnership building, and operational leadership. The ideal candidate has a record of success in securing competitive external funding, leading large\-scale events, and cultivating strategic partnerships with leaders in healthcare, technology, and philanthropic community organizations.

 **Primary Responsibilities:**

* Strategic Leadership and Vision: The Executive Director leads the overall direction and growth of the Institute, ensuring alignment with Mount Mary University's mission and strategic priorities. This includes developing and implementing a comprehensive strategic plan that advances the Institute's four Centers of Excellence: Women in Technology; Women and Children's Rights; Women's Health and Wellness; and Women's Leadership.
* Program Development and Impact: The Executive Director oversees the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs and initiatives that support leadership development, career readiness, and holistic well\-being for women and children. The role includes establishing grantmaking processes, such as funding academic and community\-based projects that demonstrate measurable impact and alignment with Institute goals.
* Governance and Institutional Engagement: Serving as an ex officio member of the Executive Committee, the Executive Director partners closely with University leadership and advisory bodies to guide Institute strategy and operations. The Executive Director convenes committee meetings, supports shared governance, and ensures effective collaboration between faculty, staff, students, and external partners.
* Advancement and Resource Development: In collaboration with University Advancement, the Executive Director leads efforts to secure philanthropic support, grants, and sponsorships that sustain and grow the Institute. The role includes cultivating relationships with donors, foundations, and corporate partners to expand programmatic reach and community impact.
* Partnership and Community Engagement: The Executive Director serves as the primary external ambassador for the Institute, building strategic partnerships with industry, nonprofit, and community organizations. These partnerships enhance experiential learning opportunities, expand access to resources, and deepen the Institute's regional and national impact.
* Operational and Financial Management: The Executive Director oversees the Institute's day\-to\-day operations, including budgeting, staffing, program administration, and assessment. This includes managing internal grant processes, reviewing proposals, and ensuring accountability for outcomes and resource utilization.
* Assessment and Continuous Improvement: The Executive Director establishes measurable outcomes and evaluation frameworks to assess the effectiveness of programs and initiatives, ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with institutional goals.
* Perform other duties, responsibilities, or special projects as assigned

 **Skills and Experience:**

* Knowledge of issues related to gender equity, leadership development, and community\-based programming.

 **Qualifications:**

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Lead the Pack: Executive Director at Zoo New York!** 

**Location:** Watertown, NY (Historic Thompson Park)

**Organization:** Thompson Park Conservancy (d.b.a. Zoo New York)

**Reports To:** Board of Directors

**About Us**

Are you ready to lead an organization with a wild purpose? The Thompson Park Conservancy is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit responsible for running **Zoo New York**. As the *only* zoo dedicated entirely to New York State’s native wildlife, our mission is to spark conservation through science\-based natural and cultural experiences. We serve as a vibrant hub for education, tourism, and family recreation in the Northern New York community.

We are looking for a visionary, business\-minded leader to step into the role of **Executive Director** and become the primary architect of our future success. If you are passionate about community impact, fiscal strategy, and wildlife conservation, we want to hear from you!

**The Role: What You’ll Do**

As our Executive Director, you will wear many hats—from strategic mastermind to community champion. You will secure the vital resources that drive our mission forward while keeping our operations running smoothly and efficiently.

Your core focus areas will include:

* **Strategic \& Financial Architecture:** Develop long\-term plans for financial health, explore new revenue streams (like corporate partnerships and earned income), and drive a data\-driven culture of business efficiency.
* **Fundraising \& Advocacy Leadership:** Spearhead capital campaigns, major gifts, and annual appeals. You will write and manage grants while cultivating strong relationships with municipal partners (like the City of Watertown and Jefferson County).
* **Community Engagement:** Act as the proud "face" and voice of the Conservancy to the media, government officials, and the public, expanding our reach across the gorgeous Thousand Islands region.
* **Team \& Board Collaboration:** Provide executive oversight of administration, visitor services, and facilities. Provide oversight and support of the Animal Curator, who handles zoological care and welfare. You will also partner closely with our Board of Directors.

**What You Bring to the Habitat**

We are looking for a proven leader who balances business acumen with diplomacy and heart.

**Required Qualifications:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, or a related field (Master’s preferred) OR if you have an equivalent combination of formal education and professional experience, we strongly encourage you to apply. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered and evaluated by the Board of Directors.
* **Experience:** 5–7 years of senior leadership experience in either the nonprofit or for\-profit sector.
* **Financial Savvy:** A proven track record in budgeting, P\&L oversight, and ideally, transforming or stabilizing organizational finances.
* **Fundraising Power:** Demonstrated success securing major gifts, grants, and sponsorships.

**Bonus Points If You Have:**

* Prior experience as an Executive Director or senior manager at a zoo, cultural institution, or tourism/destination management organization.
* Familiarity with municipal government processes and grant writing.

**Core Competencies We Value:** Strategic vision, decisive leadership, political savvy, and excellent public speaking skills.

**Salary:** Commensurate with experience with an expected range of $75,000 \- $90,000\.

**Ready to Apply?**

If you are a decisive leader ready to champion regional tourism, conservation education, and community growth, we would love to connect!

*Please submit your resume and cover letter detailing your experience by email to Kenneth A. Mix, Board of Directors Chair (boardchair@zoonewyork.org). Applications will be evaluated as they are received.*

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $90,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Health insurance
* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

**Position Summary**

The Director of Philanthropy is a strategic and hands\-on fundraising leader responsible for advancing the High Line Canal Conservancy’s philanthropic goals and ensuring the long\-term financial sustainability of a dynamic nonprofit organization with an annual operating budget of approximately $2\.5 million.

This frontline fundraising role manages a portfolio of major donors and prospects while leading all aspects of the organization's fundraising strategy including annual giving, major giving, planned giving, donor cultivation and stewardship. The Director of Philanthropy partners closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and Leadership Team to promote a strong culture of philanthropy and achieve ambitious fundraising goals.

**High Line Canal Conservancy**

With over a decade of organizational growth and impact, the High Line Canal Conservancy is accelerating progress on the community’s vision for the High Line Canal’s 71 meandering miles by preserving and enhancing this cherished greenway that connects people to nature and binds communities together from the foothills to the plains.

This is an exciting time to join the Conservancy as it builds on the success of its recently completed $33 million capital campaign and enters a new phase of organizational growth and impact. Over the past decade, the Conservancy has established itself as a trusted partner, convener, and catalyst for advancing the vision of the High Line Canal through a unique public\-private partnership.

While the organization continues to mature, it remains driven by the creativity, ambition, and entrepreneurial spirit that have fueled its success from the beginning. As a regional advocate and member of the Leadership Team, the Director of Philanthropy will play a pivotal role in securing the required resources, relationships and community investment to continue to transform the Canal into a 71\-mile linear park.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**Fundraising Strategy and Organizational Leadership** 

· Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy that maximizes revenue, envisions strategic growth in all areas, and successfully advances organizational programs.

· Serve as a member of the organization's Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, annual budgeting, cross\-departmental planning, and long\-term growth initiatives.

· Lead philanthropy program including major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, foundation grants, planned giving, donor stewardship, and special events.

· Establish annual revenue goals, fundraising benchmarks, and key performance indicators across all fundraising programs in partnership with Leadership Team.

· Manage Philanthropy Department staff of two and ensure performance metrics are met.

· Oversee departmental systems, workflows, and fundraising operations to ensure efficiency and excellent donor service.

· Oversee grant prospecting, application, and reporting pipeline.

· Partner with the CEO on Board engagement, fundraising strategy, and organizational priorities.

· Ensure accurate revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and fundraising reporting.

· Meet annual fundraising goals through structured moves management process.

· Develop and implement a new legacy giving program to support long\-term sustainability.

**Major Gifts Fundraising** 

· Personally manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 75–125 major donor and prospect relationships, foundations, and institutional funders, developing tailored cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for each.

· Conduct regular donor visits and qualification meetings.

· Guide and partner with the CEO and board of directors on major gift strategies and solicitations.

· Prepare compelling proposals, gift agreements, impact reports, and stewardship communication that align donor and foundation interests with organizational priorities.

**Special Events Fundraising** 

· Provide strategic leadership for the organization's two annual fundraising events, including a signature gala and community 5K race.

· Establish fundraising goals, sponsorship strategies, and donor engagement plans that maximize philanthropic revenue and community participation.

· Collaborate with staff, volunteers, sponsors, and volunteer committees to cultivate sponsorships, in\-kind donations, and leverage events to deepen donor relationships.

**Qualifications**

· Six years or more years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, including major gift fundraising.

· Demonstrated success personally soliciting and closing five\- and six\-figure gifts.

· Experience developing comprehensive organizational fundraising strategy.

· Experience managing donor portfolios using moves management principles.

· Experience supervising and developing fundraising staff.

· Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

· Experience using donor database/CRM systems and fundraising analytics. Raiser’s Edge experience preferred.

**Application Instructions** 

Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply by sending a resume with a cover letter addressing the applicant’s interest and qualifications for the position. Send both documents as one PDF attachment to employment@highlinecanal.org. No phone calls, please. The position will remain open until filled with a preferred application deadline of August 9 and preferred start date in mid\-September 2026\. All High Line Canal Conservancy employees are required to undergo a background check. This is an at\-will position.

Pay: $105,000\.00 \- $125,000\.00 per year

* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

* Major Gifts Fundraising: 6 years (Required)

The Frederick Gunn School, founded in 1850, is a co\-ed boarding and day school for students in grades 9\-12, as well as a post\-graduate year. Mr. Gunn had a deep appreciation for the natural world, believing that in nature students understand themselves as humans and their place in the world. He took a principled stand against slavery and spurred students (and the town at large) to examine their beliefs. In addition to the habits and skills students will need in college and life beyond, we teach them to follow Mr. Gunn’s example: to cultivate wisdom, to be trailblazers, to act with conviction, and to value character as highly as intellect and achievement.



Our continuous focus on moral character development intentionally engages all members of our school in the work of creating an inclusive and equitable living and learning ecosystem. Community and citizenship are at the heart of our aspiration to both social justice and academic excellence, with individual diversity integral to the strength of that community. When we embrace difference and pursue school life with respect, equity, and compassion, we build a foundation for engaged citizens.



In keeping with the tenets of our founder Frederick Gunn, who was himself a prominent abolitionist and progressive educator, The Frederick Gunn School seeks to provide a pluralistic learning environment for all inclusive of (but not limited to): culture, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, national origin, learning differences, physical difference, political affiliation, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, and socioeconomic differences.

* Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, or a related field.

Not simply to manage a law firm. But to help continue building one of the most innovative family law firms in the country.

This is a true executive leadership position. You will serve as my strategic partner in shaping the future of the firm while leading our operations, people, technology, and long-term growth. About Jetty Extracts:

Jetty Extracts is a premier cannabis extraction company that produces innovative products and world-class cannabis oils, headquartered in Oakland, CA. In 2013, Jetty Extracts began producing extracts and concentrates in San Diego, CA. Jetty is now one of the top extracts and concentrates brands in California.

Starting with a few individuals committed to creating clean, refined cannabis concentrates by the beach, Jetty has evolved into a group of passionate professionals committed to becoming one of the world’s most respected cannabis brands.

While the last several years have seen Jetty grow exponentially, we continue to be committed to craft, working with small farmers, producing the cleanest and tastiest products, and contributing to our communities. As we do so, we continue to support the Shelter Project, the company’s in-house compassion program that has been providing free cannabis oil to cancer patients since 2014.

About the Role:

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is the executive leader responsible for Jetty's manufacturing, supply chain, and operational strategy, ensuring the company has the capabilities, systems, and leadership required to achieve its long-term business objectives.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the COO provides strategic leadership across Jetty's manufacturing network, including production facilities in Oakland, CA and Albany, NY, as well as the company's third-party manufacturing partner in Denver, CO.

The COO is accountable for ensuring the organization's operational capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure, innovation engine, and supply chain network support Jetty's long-term growth, profitability, product quality, and customer commitments. This leader establishes the operational vision, develops organizational capability, and drives enterprise-wide initiatives that improve manufacturing performance, supply chain resilience, capital efficiency, and execution across the network.

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO partners with the CEO and executive leaders to shape company strategy, advise on operational investments, and ensure manufacturing capabilities support Jetty's long-term business objectives.

Drive enterprise-wide operational excellence initiatives that improve efficiency, quality, service, and profitability.

Buildout and Relocation of CA Headquarters: lead the planned relocation of Jetty’s headquarters within California:

Innovation, R&D & Scale-Up: Build and institutionalize a scalable innovation, research & development, and commercialization engine that supports Jetty's long-term growth, product leadership, and market expansion.

Build the systems, talent, and capabilities required to support new product development, formulation innovation, process improvement, and technology evaluation.
Develop and manage capital and operating plans required to scale manufacturing capabilities in support of future market expansion.
Work with internal teams and external partners to design, develop, test, and implement new equipment, technologies, and production processes.
Ensure successful scale-up and commercialization of new products and processes from concept through full production while maintaining quality, compliance, and operational efficiency.
Establish innovation and R&D performance metrics, resource planning, and prioritization frameworks that maximize return on investment.
Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and continuous improvement that strengthens Jetty's competitive advantage and supports future market expansion.

Supply Chain & Network Optimization: Develop a resilient, efficient manufacturing network that delivers consistent execution and supports long-term business growth.

Provide executive oversight of production planning, procurement, inventory strategy, logistics, and manufacturing partnerships.
Optimize manufacturing capacity, network utilization, and supply chain performance across all operating locations.
Develop long-term capacity and capital planning strategies to support future growth.
Strengthen strategic relationships with key suppliers and manufacturing partners to improve operational resilience.

Financial Stewardship: Drive operational performance that strengthens profitability and creates long-term enterprise value.

Establish operational performance metrics that provide executive visibility into business health and manufacturing effectiveness.

Maintain the highest standards of quality, compliance, product safety, and regulatory adherence.
Establish enterprise-wide operating standards and accountability for operational performance.
Proactively identify operational risks and implement strategies that strengthen business continuity.

Executive Leadership & Organizational Development: Build an operational organization capable of sustaining high performance and long-term growth.

JK Executive Strategies is proud to partner with the Board of Directors of Jordan Health in search of its next President & CEO. Founded in 1904, Jordan Health is one of the nation's oldest Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and a recognized leader in providing comprehensive, community-based healthcare services throughout the Greater Rochester region. The organization delivers primary care, dental, behavioral health, women’s health, pediatrics, pharmacy, urgent care, and specialty services to nearly 30,000 patients annually.

The President & CEO serves as the strategic and operational leader of Jordan Health, responsible for advancing the organization’s mission while ensuring clinical excellence, financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, workforce engagement, and organizational effectiveness. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO provides vision, leadership, and accountability for all aspects of organizational performance.

Jordan Health seeks a transformational executive to lead the organization through a critical period of financial stabilization, operational improvement, and strategic growth. The successful candidate will bring executive leadership experience within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly complex healthcare environment. This leader will possess expertise in healthcare reimbursement, regulatory compliance, operational excellence, workforce development, and community-centered care.
The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record of improving financial performance, strengthening revenue cycle operations, building high-performing teams, and leading organizations through significant change while fostering a culture of accountability, transparency, and service excellence.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Strategic Leadership & Governance

• Partner with the Board of Directors to establish organizational strategy, priorities, and long-term sustainability plans.
• Lead organizational transformation efforts that strengthen financial performance, operational effectiveness, workforce engagement, and patient outcomes.
• Assess emerging risks, opportunities, and community needs to guide strategic decision-making and service expansion.
• Provide the Board with timely and transparent information regarding organizational performance, financial results, compliance, quality outcomes, and strategic initiatives.
• Represent Jordan Health with healthcare partners, government agencies, advocacy organizations, funders, and community stakeholders.
Financial Stewardship & Sustainability

• Provide leadership and oversight for budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and resource allocation.
• Lead financial stabilization initiatives and ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
• Oversee Medicaid, Medicare, managed care reimbursement, revenue cycle performance, grant funding, payer strategy, and value-based care initiatives.
• Monitor key financial indicators and implement strategies that improve financial performance while maintaining mission alignment.
• Ensure strong financial controls, audit readiness, and compliance with grant and funding requirements.
Operational Excellence & Compliance

• Ensure delivery of high-quality, accessible, patient-centered services that meet community needs and FQHC requirements.
• Promote continuous improvement through quality initiatives, operational efficiencies, and performance management systems.
• Oversee organizational infrastructure, facilities, technology, and resources necessary to support current operations and future growth.
• Ensure compliance with HRSA requirements, FQHC regulations, federal and state laws, accreditation standards, and reporting requirements.
• Oversee enterprise risk management activities that promote organizational integrity, accountability, and regulatory compliance.
Leadership & Workforce Development

• Build, develop, and retain a high-performing executive leadership team aligned around accountability, collaboration, and service excellence.
• Foster a culture of trust, transparency, inclusion, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.
• Lead workforce recruitment, retention, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
• Recruit and retain high-quality providers, clinical staff, and operational leaders while developing future organizational leaders.
Community Leadership

• Serve as a visible and trusted leader within the Rochester community and broader healthcare ecosystem.
• Engage patients, employees, community partners, funders, and elected officials in advancing organizational priorities and health equity.
• Ensure community and patient voices are incorporated into organizational planning and decision-making.
• Support fundraising, grant development, marketing, communications, and community outreach efforts that strengthen organizational sustainability and reputation.
CORE COMPETENCIES

• FQHC Leadership
• Financial Turnaround & Stabilization
• Healthcare Reimbursement & Revenue Cycle Strategy
• HRSA Compliance & Governance
• Organizational Transformation & Change Management
• Workforce Development & Retention
• Board Relations & Community Engagement
• Health Equity & Risk Management

• Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive executive leadership experience, including substantial leadership responsibility within an FQHC, community health center, safety-net healthcare organization, or similarly regulated healthcare environment. Direct FQHC experience strongly preferred.
• Demonstrated success leading organizational transformation, financial stabilization, operational improvement, workforce development, revenue cycle enhancement, and strategic growth initiatives.

• Experience with HRSA requirements, FQHC regulations, federal grant administration, audits, quality improvement programs, risk management, and reporting requirements preferred.
• Proven success building high-performing teams and leading organizations through significant change.

Job Opening: Executive Director

About Philo Ridge Farm:

Philo Ridge Farm (PRF) is a certified organic 500-acre farm located in Charlotte, Vermont, a vibrant agricultural community in the Champlain Valley, just south of Burlington. As a diversified farm with a decade of production experience, PRF aims to create a new model for small-scale farmers, one that will allow both the land and the farmer to prosper while also serving the community. PRF works with the University of Vermont, the Vermont Land Trust, and others to help monitor and evaluate its impacts on soil health, crop and pasture productivity, water quality, carbon sequestration, and wildlife populations, with the goal of inspiring others who are interested in understanding and supporting regenerative agriculture.

Creating and sharing good food has always been a part of PRF’s work and spirit—as established by the founders Peter Swift, Diana McCargo, and Grant McCargo—who bought the property with the dream of preserving the farm’s agricultural legacy. PRF’s livestock program grazes over 300 acres of perennial pasture and includes ewes, lambs, pigs, chickens, and 100 Belted Galloway cattle. Its garden program grows two acres of organic produce and flowers using farming practices that build soil health, produce a variety of nutrient-dense foods, reduce the use of fossil fuels, and support the local agricultural community. Everything harvested is processed at PRF and sold in the dining facilities and Market which are inspired by a closed-loop nutrient system and serve as year-round gathering places for the community.

After a decade of learning the land, growing with the community, and envisioning the future of farming, the founders have established PRF as a nonprofit foundation so that the farm continues to operate as a community asset for generations to come. PRF believes a key part of this future is to keep working lands working, which is why it will always remain a working farm. Today, PRF is driven to restore the connection between humans and land, valuing curiosity, empathy, honesty, humility, and conversation.

Who We’re Looking For:

Philo Ridge Farm is looking for an outstanding and inspiring leader to be our Executive Director. The Executive Director will be the top senior leadership position on the farm, which operates year-round with a high season from May to October, and will oversee all aspects of day-to-day operations. This person will be an enthusiastic, entrepreneurial, creative, and hands-on leader of all parts of this diverse and innovative farm, including land-based agriculture teams, the market and events space, food service and hospitality teams, and the produce and meat processing facilities. The Executive Director will oversee all business operations, financial tracking and management, leadership development, internal communication, outward-facing marketing, human resources, and administration. In addition, this person will be the key ambassador for PRF’s core values, mission, and story to the local community as well as to the broader food and agriculture community.

The Executive Director must share PRF’s passion for land conservation, growing produce, raising animals, and how they intersect with food and hospitality. They will provide operational excellence through inspiring leadership, strategic thinking, team development, and a willingness to roll up their sleeves and participate in the hands-on work of the farm when needed, all while providing experienced financial and operational management of the business. Strong candidates will be equally comfortable managing Excel spreadsheets as they are hosing off their muck boots, all while creating a welcoming, community atmosphere across all aspects of the farm. In this role, the Executive Director will be a facilitator, an active listener, a clear communicator, a mentor, a coach, a mediator, and a source of positive inspiration for the entire team at PRF and someone who can motivate and hold staff members accountable to the foundations ethos and goals. The Executive Director will report to the Philo Ridge Farm Foundation Board, will work daily at PRF, and will need to live locally.

Responsibilities:

Strategic Management
Lead the design and development of annual strategic goals and a five-year strategic plan in collaboration with the Board
Adapt and align organizational structures and ways of working as needed to ensure that PRF’s departments, staffing, and budget are aligned with the strategic goals
Lead the development, implementation, and continual refinement of organizational metrics
Maintain regular communication with the Board regarding farm operations and performance
Serve as a steward and model of the farm’s mission, vision, and values
Provide strategic leadership for current and future entities under the PRF Foundation’s umbrella, including Vermont Livestock Slaughter & Processing

Team Management
Effectively recruit, train, coach, and develop managers and staff across departments
Create a positive, inspired team-oriented culture rooted in communication and collaboration
Ensure accountability by actively demonstrating and teaching exceptional professionalism
Support individual managers to facilitate staff learning and development
Hold individual managers accountable to address staff incidents and interpersonal issues
Support Board in the development and implementation of new business units and teams

Operations Management
Oversee all aspects of PRF’s day-to-day operations and property management
Lead daily coordination between all PRF managers, teams, owners, vendors, and providers

Lewiston & Portland

Salaried, Full-Time position with Health, Dental, IRA match and paid vacation and sick time

The Root Cellar Board of Trustees is seeking a Kingdom minded leader to steward a thriving ministry that has faithfully served the neighborhoods of Lewiston and Portland for more than 40 years.

This is not simply an opportunity to lead a nonprofit organization. It is an opportunity to join a story that God has been writing through churches, volunteers, neighbors, staff members, and community partners for generations.

The Root Cellar exists to engage neighbors and volunteers to cultivate social, economic, and spiritual wholeness as part of God’s Kingdom. Through youth mentoring, workforce development, English language learning, food access initiatives, trauma healing, and community engagement, thousands of individuals are impacted each year.

While deeply rooted in neighborhood ministry, The Root Cellar's influence extends far beyond the blocks surrounding its buildings. The organization has become a trusted presence in Lewiston and Portland, serving as a bridge between churches, schools, businesses, government agencies, and families from around the world. The work begins in neighborhoods, but increasingly contributes to the flourishing of entire cities.

The next Executive Director will provide spiritual, strategic, and organizational stewardship while helping guide a healthy and growing ministry. This leader will build upon a strong foundation, support an exceptional staff team, strengthen partnerships throughout Maine, and help discern how God is calling The Root Cellar to serve its communities in the years ahead.

In addition to its ministry and programmatic work, The Root Cellar is actively investing in the long-term flourishing of its neighborhood through strategic community development initiatives. The organization currently owns two residential apartment buildings and adjacent property in downtown Lewiston, creating opportunities for affordable housing, community investment, and future expansion. The next Executive Director will play an important role in stewarding these assets and helping shape a long-term vision for neighborhood transformation.

Most importantly, we are not looking for someone to bring their own vision for Lewiston and Portland. We are seeking a leader who can prayerfully discern, faithfully steward, and courageously pursue God's vision for these communities alongside our staff, volunteers, supporters, and neighbors.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
Summary
The Development Director serves as a key member of the Senior Leadership Team and provides strategic leadership for New Life Center's fundraising, donor and volunteer engagement, and community partnership efforts. Reporting to the Executive Director, this role is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive fundraising and engagement strategy that generates contributed revenue, deepens supporter engagement, and expands opportunities for individuals, churches, and community partners to engage in the Mission through giving, serving, and prayer.

The Development Director serves as the organization’s chief relationship builder and external ambassador, cultivating connections with major donors, churches, businesses, community leaders, and strategic partners. This role provides leadership and oversight for fundraising initiatives, donor and volunteer engagement strategies, donor and volunteer relationship management systems, and contributed revenue goals. The Development Director leads and develops the development team, coaches fundraising staff, and maintains a select portfolio of major donor relationships. Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, and Marketing Director, the Development Director ensures fundraising efforts, supporter engagement, and community partnerships effectively advance the organization’s mission and strategic priorities.

The Development Director serves as both a ministry leader and fundraising professional, helping supporters understand and experience the transformational impact of New Life Center’s ministry. Through authentic relationships, compelling vision casting, prayer, and faithful stewardship, this role invites supporters into deeper involvement in the life-transforming work of Jesus Christ among those experiencing homelessness and hardship. The Development Director models Christ-centered leadership while advancing the mission, sustainability, and long-term impact of New Life Center.

Our work is rooted in our Christian faith and driven by our mission to guide people experiencing homelessness or addiction toward holistic transformation through the love of Jesus. Every role contributes to this ministry and advances our shared vision. Our team members are followers of Jesus Christ, affirm our Statement of Faith, and demonstrate our BEACON values.

Essential Functions
Essential Function 1:  Department Leadership
Lead: Provide clear vision, direction, and alignment for the development team and volunteers, modeling New Life Center's core values, fostering a healthy, high-performing culture, and demonstrating a willingness and ability to lead teams in prayer. 
Manage: Ensure the right people are in the right roles, set clear expectations, develop team members through coaching and mentorship, and consistently monitor performance through effective communication, problem-solving, and ongoing support. 
Hold Accountable: Drive results by holding self and others accountable to goals, priorities, fundraising activity, donor engagement expectations, and measurable outcomes, ensuring follow-through and continuous improvement.

Essential Function 2:  Fundraising Strategy and Revenue Leadership
Create, implement, and continuously refine a comprehensive fundraising strategy with clear objectives, goals, and initiatives designed to achieve annual and long-term contributed revenue targets. 
Maintain accountability for all contributed revenue goals, including major gifts, annual giving, corporate giving, planned giving, events, digital fundraising, and other fundraising initiatives. 
Cultivate meaningful, long-term relationships with an assigned portfolio of existing and prospective donors with the capacity to make significant annual and transformational gifts, inviting them into deeper engagement through giving, prayer, and service. 
Provide strategic oversight for donor programs, including individual, corporate, and planned giving, ensuring effective cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and long-term donor engagement. 
Lead and coach fundraising staff to strengthen relationship-building, donor engagement, stewardship, and fundraising effectiveness. 
Partner closely with the Marketing Director to align fundraising strategy, donor communications, campaigns, events, volunteer engagement initiatives, and community outreach efforts with revenue and relationship-building objectives. 
Review donor data, giving trends, and fundraising performance metrics to inform strategy, identify growth opportunities, and strengthen long-term revenue sustainability and diversification.

Essential Function 3:  Relationship Development, Volunteer Engagement, and Community Partnerships
Develop and strengthen meaningful relationships with donors, churches, businesses, community partners, and other key supporters to advance New Life Center's mission and strategic priorities. 
Cultivate and manage a select portfolio of major donor relationships, focusing on individuals with the capacity to make significant annual and transformational gifts. 
Oversee volunteer engagement strategy and experiences, ensuring volunteers are meaningfully connected, well-supported, and aligned with organizational priorities. 
Ensure a meaningful and consistent supporter experience that helps donors, volunteers, and partners clearly understand the impact of their involvement and encourages long-term engagement. 
Represent and periodically speak on behalf of New Life Center at community meetings, partner gatherings, churches, donor events, and public forums to strengthen awareness, trust, and support.

Essential Function 4:  Operations, Systems, and Administrative Oversight
Oversee donor and volunteer relationship management systems, including CRM administration, donor records, gift processing, receipting, and stewardship practices, ensuring accuracy, integrity, and alignment with financial controls. 
Monitor and report on fundraising, donor engagement, volunteer engagement, and revenue performance, providing regular updates to the Executive Director and Board of Directors. 
Provide financial oversight of the development function, including budgeting, forecasting, and expense management. 
Evaluate and improve development systems, processes, reporting, and operational workflows to increase effectiveness, scalability, and organizational stewardship. 
Other duties as assigned.

Position Reports to Rob Swiers, Executive Director
This job description identifies the major responsibilities of this job. It does not include all aspects of the position such as the potential additional duties assigned by the Executive Director, the requirement for flexibility in helping others, or the highly valued team-oriented approach used for the overall benefit and success of New Life Center.

Qualifications

Personal:
Must be engaged in a local church and exhibit a personal, evident, growing relationship with Jesus Christ.  
Compassionate heart for those in need. 
Willingness to serve others. 
Desire to see the lost transformed through the love of Christ. 

Required/Preferred Education and Experience:
Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, or related field.
Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in fundraising, development, or related field, including leadership or management experience.
Demonstrated experience in major donor fundraising, relationship management, and executing successful fundraising strategies.
Experience working with donor databases/CRM systems and analyzing giving data to inform strategy.
Experience engaging and equipping volunteers, boards, or stakeholders in fundraising efforts preferred.

Additional Eligibility Requirements:
Ability to pass a pre-employment drug test and background check.
Must possess a valid driver's license, maintain an acceptable driving record in accordance with the organization's insurance carrier requirements, and provide proof of insurance, as required for the performance of job duties.

Skills:
Passion for mission-driven, ministry-focused work with the ability to invite others into giving, serving, and engagement.
Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage donors, partners, and community stakeholders.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking and donor-facing communication.
Proven leadership ability, including coaching, developing, and motivating staff, volunteers, and stakeholders.
Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to translate vision into actionable fundraising plans.
Demonstrated ability to analyze data, track performance metrics, and adjust strategies accordingly.
High level of organization, attention to detail, and follow-through.
Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise discretion, and demonstrate personal integrity.
Proficiency with CRM systems, donor management tools, and cloud-based and traditional software applications.
Adaptability and ability to lead through change in a dynamic environment.
Willingness and ability to work flexible schedules, including occasional evenings and weekends.

Work Environment
Primarily office-based with regular local travel for donor engagement, community meetings, speaking engagements, and events.
Fast-paced and dynamic environment requiring the ability to manage multiple priorities in support of fundraising, engagement, and organizational goals.
Regular use of office technology, including computers, phones, CRM systems, and cloud-based platforms.
Physical requirements include periods of sitting, standing, walking, and occasional travel for meetings, events, or donor and partner engagement.
Full-time position with a flexible schedule that may include evenings, weekends, and occasional travel.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.

Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.

With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.

At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts.

Code for America is looking for a talented Program Director
who will own delivery and strategic direction across a portfolio of high-impact programs. In this role, you will manage a team of Associate Program Directors and program staff, setting the conditions for excellent execution while maintaining the external relationships and policy fluency that government work requires. You will ensure that Code for America's programs not only deliver for clients and partners today, but build the organizational learning, government trust, and policy foundations that enable systemic, lasting change.

About the role:

Code for America's Program Directors lead portfolios of work that sit at the intersection of technology, policy, and government service delivery. At the core of this role is the belief that government services can and should work better for the people who depend on them most — and that achieving that requires sustained, expert leadership over complex, multi-stakeholder programs.

As a Program Director at Code for America, you will own a portfolio of approximately four to six projects and the teams that deliver them. Your portfolio may include work across areas such as Safety Net benefits access (including multi-benefit enrollment and Medicaid and SNAP delivery), Tax programs, or Criminal Justice initiatives, depending on organizational need and your area of expertise.

You will be externally facing, building and sustaining relationships with federal agencies, state-level leadership, county partners, and/or community-based organizations, while supporting your direct reports in doing the same. You will also work closely with other delivery colleagues to ensure our projects achieve their intended impact and that your portfolio is aligned with Code for America's strategy.

This role will report to the Senior Director of Safety Net
and is expected to travel no more than 15%-25% of the time.

Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position.

In this position you will:

Portfolio Oversight
Own partnership escalation and/or strategic direction across a portfolio of approximately four to six projects, ensuring each project meets its commitments to government partners, funders, and clients, and outputs are high-quality and delivered on time and within budget.
Collaborate with the Partnerships team to ensure efficient scoping and smooth handoffs, including clear kickoff processes and well-defined responsibilities during project kickoffs and transitions.
Ensure programs staff apply consistent delivery management practices, focused on setting clear project timelines and goals, clarifying roles, and running appropriate meeting cadences, leveraging Code for America's standard best practices, tools, and processes.
Ensure ongoing project-level direction & strategy aligns with organizational strategy, ensuring your portfolio advances mission priorities and contributes to measurable client outcomes.
Work with programs team members, programs leadership, and discipline leads to ensure each project has a clear, realistic plan for success aligned with organizational goals, partner expectations, client outcomes, and/or philanthropic commitments, and that programs staff understand how to drive aligned progress.
Anticipate risks, staffing needs, and resource constraints across your portfolio; serve as the primary escalation point for APDs and programs staff , escalating to programs leadership when the decision has implications beyond your purview.
Support APDs in driving clear, frequent communication internally and with external stakeholders to maintain alignment on program progress, scope changes, risks, and emerging opportunities.
Partner with programs and resource management leadership to ensure project teams are staffed appropriately from a programs perspective; contribute to headcount recommendations and support recruitment and onboarding of new team members.
Ensure APDs serving as Project Sponsors surface staffing needs across delivery disciplines early and escalate when tradeoffs or reprioritization are required. Proactively flag when teams need resource adjustments to ensure strong delivery across multiple teams.

People Management
Directly manage Associate Program Directors (APDs) and, where applicable, other Program ICs within your portfolio; provide coaching, feedback, and development support that builds their effectiveness as program leaders.
Coach and develop people managers on the team, supporting them in managing their own direct reports effectively.
Lead goal setting, performance reviews, and regular check-ins to support team performance, professional growth, and team culture.
Model Code for America's values and ways of working across your team, setting expectations for how program staff use best practices and tools, engage with partners, clients, and each other, to ensure strong and efficient program delivery across your portfolio

Strategy & Operations
Surface insights from projects and partners to inform organizational priorities, strategy, and emerging opportunities, as well as to identify possibilities for policy and systems change.
Participate in optional cross-functional working groups addressing organizational priorities, emerging program practices, and the role of technology and artificial intelligence in government service delivery, as relevant.
Ensure lessons learned inform other projects across your portfolio and the broader delivery area.

External Relationships & Communications
Build and sustain relationships with federal agency leads, state-level government partners, county agencies, and mission-aligned community-based organizations across your portfolio.
Travel to partner sites, government offices, and program locations as needed to maintain trust, assess project health, and identify opportunities for deeper engagement.
Serve as a credible, knowledgeable voice for Code for America for work within your purview, representing the organization's work you oversee and approach with government and funder audiences.
Contribute to cultivation efforts within your portfolio area, including opportunity spotting, advising on statements of work, project scoping, and pitch materials in partnership with the Growth and Partnerships team.
Ensure reporting across projects is purposeful, consistent, and aligned with funder and partner requirements, surfacing the right insights and signals for internal organizational leadership. This may include drafting, reviewing, and/or approving grant reports for projects in your portfolio.

Other duties as assigned
Engage in ad hoc projects and initiatives as required by the organization's evolving needs.

About you:

8+ years of experience in program development, policy, or government service delivery, with demonstrated progression of responsibility; some experience working within or directly alongside government required.
Familiarity with agile or iterative program delivery approaches, and experience collaborating with product and engineering teams.
3+ years of experience managing teams, including direct management of at least one people manager.
Proven track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder program delivery — from strategy through execution — in a government, civic tech, or social sector context.
Deep familiarity with at least one of Code for America's program areas: Safety Net benefits access (including SNAP, Medicaid, or multi-benefit enrollment), Tax programs, or Criminal Justice; ability to credibly represent Code for America's approach with government partners in that area.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with federal and state agency leadership, county partners, and community-based organizations across political and institutional differences.
Strong understanding of government service delivery structures, including the social safety net, and the policy landscape shaping program implementation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex program and policy information clearly & concisely to government partners, funders, and internal leadership.
Ability to manage multiple programs simultaneously, maintaining clarity and accountability across a portfolio with competing priorities.
Willingness to travel 15–25% of the time to partner sites, government offices, and program locations.
Curiosity about emerging AI tools and a commitment to using them responsibly and effectively
A deep commitment to Code for America's mission of making government services work well for the people who need them most

It’s a bonus if you have:

Experience contributing to cultivation or business development work, including advising on scopes of work, writing funding reports, and sharing program learnings with funders and partners.
Experience working in or alongside civic tech organizations or technology-forward government reform initiatives.
Experience with AI tools or technology-assisted service delivery in a government or social sector context.
Proficiency in languages other than English.
Experience managing philanthropic grant requirements, including reporting, learning documentation, and funder communication.

What You’ll Get -

Salary:

Code for America’s salary bands are transparent as a part of our commitment to transparency and fairness. As part of our hiring practices, we aim to target the midpoint of the 2nd quartile of the range for all new hires.

Offer targets vary based on market / geographic location. The offer targets for this role range from $121,869 to $149,188
, annually. Your Recruiter will discuss compensation in more detail & answer any related questions, during the initial Recruiter phone screen.

Benefits and perks:

This role includes a comprehensive benefits package including the following:

Values:
Leadership and teammates who share a strong work ethic and values, and who respect and care for one another
A collaborative, cross-functional, hardworking, and joyful environment

Employee Enablement Support:
Laptop provided
A one-time $700 payment for remote environment setup; $200 stipend (in first paycheck) and up to $500 reimbursement, in accordance with our equipment policy
Cell phone and/or internet reimbursement of $50 per month

Professional Development:
$500 annual (per calendar year) stipend towards professional development; prorated at time of hire
Up to $500 of professional development funds can be rolled over each year, up to a maximum of $1000
Training / guidance for staff required to utilize AI as part of their role, plus opportunities for employees to gain AI-related skills to support job and career growth

Retirement & 401k Plans:
Employees receive a 100% employer match on the first 3% of contributions.
Employees with 3+ years of service receive an additional 5
