Director of Development

Farmers Alley Theatre, Kalamazoo, MI

About The Position

This position is responsible for the management and execution of the overall development program. The Director of Development reports to the Executive Director and provides staff support for the Development Committee of the Board of Directors. Annually, this person will establish, with the Development Committee, a plan to secure adequate resources to meet the theatre’s immediate and long-term needs.

Working Conditions

This is a full-time, at-will position, working collaboratively with a small staff in Kalamazoo, Michigan. The position requires work involving irregular shifts, including some evenings and weekends. 

Job Duties

Areas of responsibility include development strategy; relationships with foundations; grants; major gifts; corporate sponsorships; annual campaigns; special events; planned giving; donor recognition; overseeing database management and record keeping; budgeting; and special projects as assigned by the Executive Director. Capital campaign experience a plus. This individual works cooperatively with board and staff members to ensure development interests are represented in the community. 

Requirements

The selected individual will have a proven track record in meeting/exceeding fundraising goals, including securing large gifts; writing successful grants; and cultivating authentic relationships. Experience should include a strategic approach to all aspects of fundraising and grant writing. Excellent verbal and written communication skills are expected in the ideal candidate. 

Salary

$60,000, plus medical, dental, vision insurance coverage for themselves and their family through the group insurance plans offered by Farmers Alley Theatre. Farmers Alley Theatre currently covers most of the cost of these plans.

How to Apply

Send a cover letter and résumé, with three references, to blaine@farmersalleytheatre.com

Application Deadline
-- August 14, 2026

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. Job Summary

The Director, Philanthropic Relations plays an integral role in strengthening the Mass Eye and Ear and Mass General Brigham philanthropic program. Working in close collaboration with colleagues, physicians and other faculty, the Director is an individual contributor responsible for the strategic identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of prospects and donors for assigned fundraising areas.

The Director will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors and meet annual fundraising and performance metrics as established by the department.

Build and actively manage a portfolio of prospects and donors

jobs.description:
The Commercial team at EyePoint focuses on bringing innovative therapies to patients by ensuring healthcare providers, partners, and communities have access to treatment, reimbursement, and are able to use the product appropriately. This team uses data-driven insights, market access strategies, and a patient-centric approach to improve awareness, access, and adoption of EyePoint’s therapies to help improve vision outcomes for people with serious retinal diseases.

The Executive Director, Field Marketing will architect and lead the KOL engagement and advocacy strategy for EyePoint Pharmaceuticals' retina franchise. This leader is responsible for building deep, strategic relationships with national, regional, and emerging retina opinion leaders; cultivating advocacy networks across academic and community settings; driving KOL-led scientific content and digital advocacy; and serving as the strategic liaison between the retina KOL community and EyePoint's commercial and medical organizations. This position will lead a team of remote, field-based, Field Marketing Managers to engage directly with thought leaders in retina.

EyePoint is building its commercial infrastructure to support the anticipated launch of DURAVYU for wet AMD. As the TKI class emerges in retina, physician education, advocacy, and opinion leader engagement will be critical to establishing DURAVYU's scientific credibility, differentiated positioning, and adoption among retina specialists. This role is distinct from peer-to-peer marketing (which focuses on speaker programs and promotional P2P) — the Head of Field Marketing focuses on strategic relationship development, advocacy cultivation, and ensuring EyePoint is deeply embedded in the retina community.

Reporting to the SVP, Marketing and Strategy, this role will partner closely with Medical Affairs, Peer-to-Peer Marketing, HCP Marketing, Sales, and the broader Commercial Leadership Team.

Key Responsibilities

KOL Engagement & Advocacy Strategy

Design and execute a strategic, tiered KOL development plan that deepens relationships with national, regional, and emerging retina opinion leaders.
Develop a comprehensive engagement framework spanning advisory boards, 1:1 executive engagements, informal dinners, scientific forums, and collaborative partnerships.
Identify and cultivate relationships with high-influence retina specialists across academic medical centers, community retina practices, and centers of excellence.
Establish tiered KOL segmentation aligned with commercial priorities, scientific influence, and advocacy potential.
Drive clinical conviction and scientific credibility for DURAVYU among the retina community.

Field-Based Team Leadership

Recruit, hire and lead field-based Field Marketing Manager team. Represent EyePoint to the retina thought leader community.
Partner with Medical Affairs on field-based insight development.
Work closely with Marketing Operations and Analysis to provide strategic insights to inform marketing decisions.

Retina Advocacy Network Development

Build and manage a nationwide retina advocacy network across academic and community settings.
Identify and engage next-generation retina leaders, fellowship directors, and rising KOLs.
Foster strong relationships for advisory, scientific content, speaker, and advocacy roles.
Coordinate with Medical Affairs to ensure seamless transitions between scientific and commercial engagement.
Leverage EyePoint's senior leadership for high-value KOL interactions and relationship building.
Create memorable, meaningful KOL interactions that balance scientific depth with authenticity — reinforcing EyePoint's retina identity.

KOL-Led Content, Podium Presence & Digital Advocacy

Partner with KOLs to develop scientific communications, podium presentations, and peer-influence content for key retina congresses.
Drive KOL-led social media engagement and digital advocacy initiatives.
Develop disease-awareness content featuring KOL voices across trade journals, podcasts and digital platforms.
Ensure KOL-led content amplifies DURAVYU's differentiated positioning

Strategic KOL-Commercial Liaison

Serve as the primary strategic liaison between the retina KOL community and EyePoint's commercial organizations.
Integrate KOL insights into brand strategy, competitive positioning, launch planning, and messaging development.
Coordinate closely with Peer-to-Peer Marketing, HCP Marketing, and Medical Affairs to ensure advocacy efforts are aligned across scientific and promotional engagement.
Gather and relay field intelligence from KOL interactions to inform ongoing strategy refinement.
Participate in competitive intelligence gathering at congresses and scientific meetings.

Required Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Experience

12+ years of pharmaceutical or biotechnology commercial experience with significant focus on KOL engagement, physician advocacy, or field-based marketing.
Demonstrated success building and managing physician opinion leader networks and advocacy programs.
Experience designing and executing KOL engagement strategies in specialty therapeutic areas.
Strong cross-functional collaboration experience with Medical Affairs, Sales, and Marketing teams.
Experience working in a pre-launch or emerging commercial organization.
Proven ability to build relationships with academic and community physicians at all levels.

Knowledge & Capabilities

Deep understanding of the retina disease space, retina practice dynamics, and physician engagement models.
Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical compliance requirements for KOL interactions and advocacy programs.
Exceptional relationship management, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Strategic thinking combined with hands-on execution capability.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-growing biotechnology environment.

Preferred Experience

Ophthalmology or retinal disease market experience.
Experience with retina congresses and retina KOL networks.
Biotechnology launch experience within a pre-commercial or emerging-growth organization.
Digital and social media advocacy experience.

Success Measures

KOL engagement depth, breadth, and advocacy activation.
Retina advocacy network size, quality, and engagement metrics.
KOL-led content output, podium placements, and digital advocacy reach.
KOL insights captured and integrated into commercial strategy.
Cross-functional collaboration effectiveness with Medical Affairs, P2P, and HCP Marketing.

==================================================

**Job Description:**

Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.


**Where Your Career is a Force for Good!**

The American Red Cross is seeking a **Chief Development Officer** to support the California Gold Country Region. This region supports 31 counties in Northern California. This is a hybrid position. Incumbents will spend several days a week in the office and the remainder of their time in the field or in a home office.


**WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW:**

In this role, you will lead a team of professional fundraisers to strengthen and grow the region’s donor base to meet its assigned financial target of more than $10M. The Chief Development Officer will provide leadership to the staff and volunteers in planning, managing, and implementing fundraising development strategies for the assigned segment(s) of giving. They will also assist in cultivating donors and sponsors to meet monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue targets while maintaining their own portfolios. The Director is responsible for managing an assigned team, including hiring, training, coaching, evaluating, and managing performance. This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.


**WHERE YOUR CAREER IS A FORCE GOOD:**

* Manage a portfolio of high\-level donors and prospects within the assigned segment to achieve the annual revenue target, including both renewable gifts and new incremental revenue.
* Develop and implement a plan for revenue growth from donors at the $5,000\+ level with an emphasis on maximizing revenue for the American Red Cross. The individual segment will collaborate with the Gift Planning team to strategically grow planned giving revenue across major donor\-managed accounts for individuals and families. The corporate and foundation segments’ strategic growth plan could include (but are not limited to) engagement and growth of giving societies such as the Tiffany Circle, serving as a staff liaison to the Board's Philanthropy Committee and developing and implementing strategies for board giving and influence for the region, growing cause marketing and overall corporate revenue by assisting corporations in achieving their goals to strengthen their brand, marketing, and employee engagement, leading the region's special events program, or leading a strategy to identify, cultivate, and engage foundations to grow their support for the American Red Cross.

* Collaborate with national headquarters development team members to maximize fundraising opportunities and implement policies and procedures to ensure the success of the region's fundraising efforts.
* Oversee the implementation of organizational campaigns in the region.
* Serve as a senior leader in the Region and proactively drive the implementation of strategic decisions for the organization. Ensure that the Region meets all reporting requirements related to fundraising, including ensuring up\-to\-date donor records in Salesforce.
* Provide strong leadership, develop, and set individual and team performance goals and manage/drive change.
* Hire, manage, train, and evaluate staff and volunteers to ensure fundraising results and that all team members meet or exceed national/regional fundraising metrics.
* Lead and execute disaster relief fundraising efforts as appropriate.

***WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED:***

**About Redwood Community Services**
------------------------------------


Redwood Community Services (RCS) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening individuals, families, and communities through behavioral health, child welfare, youth development, housing, and support services. Our work changes lives every day, and our employees make that possible.


We are seeking an experienced, strategic, and collaborative Director of Lake County Programs to provide leadership and oversight for a diverse portfolio of behavioral health, child welfare, youth development, and community\-based services throughout Lake County. The ideal candidate is a mission\-driven leader with strong clinical knowledge, operational expertise, and a passion for supporting children, youth, families, and communities. This role requires the ability to balance program quality, fiscal stewardship, staff development, community partnerships, and innovative service delivery while ensuring excellence in care and outcomes.

**What You'll Do**


Key responsibilities include:


* Provide overall leadership, direction, and oversight for Lake County programs, ensuring high\-quality services across behavioral health, rehabilitation, substance use disorder treatment, foster care, wraparound, residential, and school\-based programs.
* Oversee clinical and program operations while promoting effective coordination of services for children, youth, families, and individuals with complex behavioral health and social service needs.
* Monitor program performance, revenue, and expenditures to ensure fiscal responsibility, sustainability, and alignment with organizational goals.
* Participate in strategic planning, program development, and implementation of new services that respond to emerging community needs and funding opportunities.
* Collaborate with clinical leadership to support treatment planning, program reviews, quality improvement activities, and resolution of reportable incidents and service concerns.
* Provide leadership in budget planning, review financial performance, and authorize expenditures consistent with approved budgets and organizational priorities.
* Recruit, interview, hire, supervise, mentor, and develop program managers, supervisors, clinicians, rehabilitation specialists, and support staff.
* Foster a positive, collaborative culture through staff development, training, coaching, performance management, and succession planning efforts.
* Work closely with leadership teams across RCS to ensure seamless coordination among programs and alignment with the agency's mission, values, and strategic objectives.
* Establish and maintain productive partnerships with county agencies, schools, child welfare organizations, behavioral health providers, regional centers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
* Represent RCS within community collaboratives, public meetings, and professional organizations to strengthen partnerships and advance services for vulnerable populations.
* Ensure compliance with licensing requirements, contractual obligations, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory standards while promoting continuous quality improvement.
* Prepare and review program reports, operational data, and outcome measures to support informed decision\-making and effective communication with executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Respond to complex operational issues, critical incidents, and crisis situations while maintaining a focus on safety, service quality, and positive outcomes.
* Support community engagement, public relations, fundraising, special projects, and organizational initiatives as assigned.

* A master's degree in Behavioral Science, Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or a related field.
* California BBS licensure (or eligibility consistent with program requirements).
* Significant leadership and supervisory experience in behavioral health, child welfare, youth services, or related community\-based programs.
* Experience managing complex programs, budgets, contracts, and multidisciplinary teams.

* Excellent communication, relationship\-building, and community partnership abilities.
* A commitment to trauma\-informed, culturally responsive, family\-centered, and strengths\-based services.

At RCS, you'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful programs that improve the lives of children, youth, and families while working alongside dedicated professionals who share a commitment to service, innovation, and community impact. You'll play a key role in shaping programs, developing staff, strengthening partnerships, and helping advance our mission of building healthier and stronger communities throughout Lake County.

**We offer:**

* Meaningful work with a respected nonprofit organization
* Collaborative and supportive team environment
* Opportunities for professional development
* Stable, mission\-focused employment
* Comprehensive benefits package (for eligible employees)
* The opportunity to make a real impact every day

Not simply to manage a law firm. **But to help continue building one of the most innovative family law firms in the country.**

Our matters frequently involve complex financial issues, executive compensation, founder equity, private equity, closely held businesses, international issues, and high\-conflict custody litigation.

Over the past thirteen years, we have built one of California's fastest\-growing family law firms. Our gross revenue has increased by approximately 25% to 50% year over year for thirteen consecutive years.

Why? Because we are relentless in our pursuit of excellence. We strive to provide the highest level of legal representation and client service in family law in California. We invest in exceptional people, embrace innovation, continually refine our systems, and refuse to become complacent. We believe that when you build an extraordinary team and deliver an extraordinary client experience, sustained growth naturally follows.

Just as importantly, we believe extraordinary results should never come at the expense of extraordinary people.

**We're looking for an exceptional Chief Operating Officer who is energized by the opportunity to continue building one of the most innovative family law firms in the country.**

**Executive Director**

**Supervisor:** Board of Directors

**Type:** Full\-time, 40 hours/week, FMLA\-exempt

**To apply** 

Send your resume or CV and a one\-page cover letter to hiring@sonorandesert.org with the subject line “CSDP Executive Director Application."

Please attach the resume/CV and cover letter as one PDF document. References requested upon interview selection. If you need any special accommodations for the application process, please contact us at (520\) 388\-9925\. Applications will be accepted until August 16, 2026\.

\*Applications received through Indeed will not be accepted.\*

**About the Coalition for Sonoran Desert Protection**

The Coalition’s mission is to protect the biodiversity of the Sonoran Desert in Southern Arizona through science\-based advocacy, education, and collaboration. We are an alliance of conservation and community organizations that formed in February 1998\. Through our Coalition, we work towards a common vision of a community in the Sonoran Desert where ecosystems are healthy, valued, and protected, with benefits for current and future generations.

**Position description**

The Executive Director provides strategic leadership and day\-to\-day management, ensuring CSDP advances its mission, remains financially sustainable, and operates effectively. As the leader of a small, collaborative team, the Executive Director is both a strategic leader and a working manager, setting organizational direction while remaining actively engaged in programs, advocacy, fundraising, communications, and operations.

The Executive Director serves as the public face of CSDP, building strong relationships with the Board of Directors, staff, coalition members, elected officials, government agencies, land managers, developers, communities, supporters, major donors, and more. Success in this role requires exceptional leadership, sound judgment, strong communication skills, and the ability to navigate complex conservation, land\-use, and local government issues while bringing diverse interests together around a shared vision.

CSDP’s current annual budget is just under $500,000, with anticipated growth in the years ahead. The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and is responsible for the leadership and management of CSDP’s staff.

***Core tasks and areas of responsibility***

**Organizational leadership**

* Manage staff and contractors, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, and professional development.
* Maintain and update internal and external policies and procedures, including CSDP’s Employee Handbook.
* Oversee CSDP’s coalition structure and members, including relationships, agreements and contracts, communications, and other elements necessary to maintain a healthy coalition.
* Communicate effectively with the Board.
* Support the Board with organizing meetings, and prepare Board meeting materials.
* Acknowledge and dismantle inequities within CSDP policies, systems, programs, and strategies, while reflecting on lessons learned.
* Foster an organizational culture that embodies CSDP’s core values: collaborative, inclusive, responsible, committed, knowledge\-based, results\-focused, and inspired.

**Financial management**

* Develop and manage CSDP’s annual budget.
* Develop and oversee delivery on CSDP’s fundraising strategy, to include related events and communications.
* Develop and lead CSDP’s foundation and major donor relations.
* Monitor and manage CSDP’s organizational finances, including monthly financial statements.
* Oversee banking, accounting, tax compliance, insurance, payroll, benefits, contracts, and regulatory compliance processes and tasks.

**Policy, planning, and programs**

jobs.title: Senior Director of Operations
jobs.description:
**About Journey Found:**  

Headquartered in Manchester, CT, and established in 2013, Journey Found (JF) is a proven leader in providing behavioral, residential, and many other support services to Connecticut individuals with Pervasive Developmental Disorders and Intellectual Disabilities, enabling them to become all they are capable of being. Journey Found currently serves 73 adults with intellectual disabilities ranging in age from 21\-82 in small (mostly 3\-person) group homes and apartments, in individualized day support services, and a growing number in their own or their family’s homes. Services are person\-centered, and each person has an individual plan of service that addresses their hopes, wants, and needs in each aspect of their life: home, work, recreation, medical, and sometimes education.  

Journey Found’s annual budget is $19 million, 95% of which comes from contracts with the state of Connecticut. The organization has 292 employees (\~166 FTEs) and is governed by an actively engaged 10\-member board.

 **Opportunity Going Forward:**  

The Senior Director of Operations provides oversight of all the agency's operations and acts as the internal face of the organization. This role is critical in helping fulfill Journey Found’s mission of providing the best person\-centered services to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and to secure its sustainability in service to this mission.  

The Senior Director of Operations is a dynamic leader and creative individual who works to maintain and expand the high\-quality services provided by the organization. The candidate is willing to learn and remains flexible enough to adjust priorities to ensure the organization continues to fulfill its mission as new service trends emerge, and changes in the environment occur. Journey Found’s next Senior Director of Operations will join the team at an exciting time. The field is changing, with innovations in technology presenting new ways to serve the people Journey Found supports. The new Senior Director of Operations will have the opportunity to work with the CEO to explore and realize the impact of new service models that align with Journey Found’s person\-centered culture, leaving an imprint on the organization and the lives it touches. In addition, there is a strong team in place, and the new Senior Director of Operations will be able to partner with team leaders who have been providing high\-quality services to the people JF serves while looking for growth opportunities within the organization.  

The Senior Director of Operations reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer under the general direction of the Board of Directors. The position is based in JF’s Manchester, CT office and is expected to be on\-site for the majority of the Monday\-Friday work week, with the flexibility to work remotely as their schedule and commitments permit. This individual has direct supervisory responsibilities for five professionals in the role of Director of Support Services, the Facilities Manager, and the Director of Clinical Services. This role indirectly supervises the organization’s nursing department and approximately 250 Direct Support Professionals.




**The Senior Director of Operations Key Responsibilities Include:**

 **Management and Administration**  

* Foster a work culture of success, empowerment, team building, and reward organizational effectiveness.
* Effectively resolve conflicts, deal with challenging situations, and make smart decisions.
* Assure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, statutes, licensure, accreditation (where applicable), and agency policy.
* Provide on\-call support to the organization.
* Critically evaluate situations and strategically plan solutions.
* Firmly, promptly, and effectively manage crisis situations.
* Adeptly collect and analyze data to inform decisions that lead to positive outcomes.
**Organizational Engagement**  

* Make strong connections with the staff and people supported.
* Strongly focus on stakeholder engagement.
* Effectively communicate with families of people supported.
* Approach working with teams and mediating positive outcomes in a proactive manner.
**Clinical Oversight**  

* Partner with the Director of Clinical Services to ensure high\-quality services are provided.
* Ensure the Clinical Team completes continuing education to promote learning and best practice approaches to clinical supports.
* Effectuate a Person\-Centered approach using applied behavior analysis (ABA) techniques and strategies.
**Facilities Oversight**  

* Develop and evaluate proactive facilities management plans.
* Ensure all Journey Found homes are maintained to the highest standards, and they reflect positively upon their communities.
* Manage a network of vendors and property managers in support of Journey Found’s mission.
* Negotiate contractual agreements and manage capital improvement projects.
* Maximize the efforts of the Facilities department by triaging work orders.



**Desired Credentials/Profile of the Ideal Candidate:**  

There are innumerable ways to learn, grow, and excel professionally with Journey Found. We respect this when we review applications and take a broad look at the experience of each applicant. We want to get to know you and the unique strengths you will bring to the work. We will most likely be interested in your candidacy if you demonstrate most of the qualifications and attributes listed below:  

* A sincere commitment to Journey Found’s mission of delivering high\-quality, person\-centered services to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
* Five or more years of managerial and administrative responsibilities in a non\-profit organization or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
* At least three years of experience working with the CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS).
* An established track record of fostering a successful and effective team\-base

jobs.description:
**Job Posting Title:**


Director of Development, Major Gifts**\-**

**Hiring Department:**


Texas Memorial Museum**\-**

**Position Open To:**


All Applicants**\-**

**Weekly Scheduled Hours:**


40**\-**

Exempt from FLSA**\-**

Aug 01, 2026**\-**

Expected to Continue**\-**

**Location:**


UT MAIN CAMPUS**\-**

**Job Details:**

**General Notes**
-----------------


Texas Science \& Natural History Museum is developing new exhibits, programs, and experiences that spark curiosity, promote belonging, and tell stories about Texas science and natural history. Since reopening in September 2023, the reimagined institution blends its historic building and world\-class collections with engaging, modern exhibits focused on science education. The museum has welcomed more than 200,000 visitors from all 50 states and 28 countries while supporting preK–12 education through field trips and outreach and presenting an active schedule of public programs. The museum continues to evolve as a vibrant educational and cultural hub with a strong path toward long\-term sustainability.

**Purpose**
-----------


To serve as the Director of Development, Major Gifts, on the museum’s development team. The museum seeks a seasoned fundraising professional to identify and cultivate new donor prospects with a capacity of $100,000\+. Reporting to the Director of Development, the position holds a critical role advancing Texas Science \& Natural Museum’s strategic priorities through fundraising.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Build and carry an active portfolio of 40\-60 well\-qualified prospective donors with a capacity of $100,000\+ and solicit gifts to support operations, capital projects, education programs, and endowments through pledged and planned monetary gifts. Engage in strategy, identification, qualification, cultivation, relationship building, and closing of major gifts to support the museum’s priorities.
* Participate in goal setting, proposal preparation, strategy development, and stewardship as required for donors in the managed portfolio and as requested.
* Successfully and consistently deliver funding proposals with a focus on engaging new donors and building contributed revenue that is available within the fiscal year as well as building endowment funding.
* Maintain an understanding of the museum’s priorities, vision, and mission. Effectively work with, communicate with, and collaborate with leadership and other staff to develop funding opportunities to reach annual budgetary and long\-term goals. Work collaboratively, proactively, and in a professional, service\-oriented manner with all departments and development staff to further goals and mission of the museum.
* Utilize fundraising databases and prospecting tools. Maintain appropriate electronic documentation on a timely basis, including engagement activities, proposal tracking, contact reports, donor strategies, and forecasting.
* Work collaboratively and proactively with Texas Development and development colleagues within the College of Natural Sciences to align and advance the museum’s fundraising efforts. Leverage relationships with development officers across the university to explore and/or strengthen fundraising opportunities for the museum. Participate in professional development opportunities to create and nurture a culture of philanthropy within Texas Science \& Natural History Museum and its constituencies.
* Performs related duties as assigned. May work on assigned projects.
**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor’s Degree and minimum of 5\+ years experience in major gift fundraising
* Proven success in developing and executing full\-cycle donor strategies
* Strong emotional intelligence, intellectual curiosity, and strategic thinking
* Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, interpersonal).
* Effective project management and problem\-solving abilities, thrives under pressure
* Collaborative and independent work style; able to engage across teams
* Proficient in CRM platforms such as VIP, Salesforce, or similar applications
* Willingness and ability to travel to engage with prospects and donors
* Demonstrated discretion, integrity, and professionalism in all interactions
* Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate
**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* 10\+ years in major gift fundraising
* Prior experience at UT or in a large, complex academic research university environment
* Background in fundraising within a museum or educational organization
* Graduate degree and/or Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) certification
**Salary Range**
----------------


$115,000\+ depending on qualifications

**Working Conditions**
----------------------


Hybrid position

**Required Materials**
----------------------

* Resume/CV
* 3 work references with their contact information; at least one reference should be from a supervisor
* Letter of interest

**Important** **for applicants who are NOT current university employees or contingent workers:** You will be prompted to submit your resume the first time you apply, then you will be provided an option to upload a new Resume for subsequent applications. Any additional Required Materials (letter of interest, references, etc.) will be uploaded in the Application Questions section; you will be able to multi\-select additional files. Before submitting your online job application, ensure that ALL Required Materials have been uploaded. Once your job application has been submitted, you cannot make changes.

**Important for Current university employees and contingent workers:** As a current university employee or contingent worker, you MUST apply within Workday by searching for Find UT Jobs. If you are a current University employee, log\-in to Workday, navigate to your Worker Profile, click the Career link in the left hand navigation

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy (Immediate Opening)
jobs.description:
**Description**


**Director of Philanthropy**

**Role Mission:** The Director of Philanthropy is a seasoned major\-gifts fundraiser responsible for securing transformational philanthropic investments that advance IDEA Public Schools’ mission. Managing a multi\-region portfolio of high\-capacity donors, the Director drives strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship to grow IDEA’s pipeline of individuals, corporations, and foundations capable of giving $10,000–$250,000\+ annually.  

  

Operating within IDEA’s new Foundation model, the Director applies a disciplined, data\-informed approach to portfolio strategy—executing thoughtful qualification, crafting tailored donor pathways, and aligning every engagement to long\-term revenue growth. The role requires mastery in major gifts, including multi\-year commitments, donor\-advised funds, endowed gifts, and planned giving, and the ability to translate IDEA’s bold ambitions into compelling investment opportunities.  

  

A trusted philanthropic advisor to donors and a strategic thought partner across IDEA’s fundraising and regional leadership, the Director collaborates closely with program leaders, regional executives, Advancement Services, and the Donor Experience team to design high\-impact proposals, stewardship plans, and engagement experiences that deepen trust and strengthen IDEA’s financial sustainability.  

  

Reporting to the Lead Director of Philanthropy, this role bridges strategy and execution—ensuring IDEA’s major gifts work is coordinated, relationship\-centered, metrics\-aligned, and high\-impact. The Director plays a critical frontline role in expanding IDEA’s community of loyal supporters and securing the philanthropic investments needed to serve more students, in more regions, for years to come


**Supervisory Responsibilities:** None

**Location:** This is a full\-time remote position based in Texas, with preference given to candidates who live in Austin, El Paso, Houston, Permian Basin (Midland/Odessa), Rio Grande Valley, San Antonio, and Tarrant County (Fort Worth), or who are willing to relocate.

**Travel Expectations:** This role requires regular in\-person donor meetings across multiple regions, including travel within and outside the Director’s home market. Approximately 30–40% travel annually, with increased volume during peak fundraising periods (e.g., donor solicitations, cultivation events, College Signing Day, and the Annual Gala).

**What You’ll Do – Accountabilities**

**Essential Duties:**


* Manage a multi\-region portfolio of high\-capacity individual, corporate, and foundation donors, leading strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship efforts that secure major gifts of $10,000–$250,000\+ annually.
* Develop and execute individualized donor strategies informed by data, research, and relationship history to advance prospects through the major gifts pipeline toward long\-term philanthropic investment.
* Conduct thoughtful donor qualification and discovery to assess capacity, interest, and readiness, aligning donor priorities with IDEA’s funding needs and strategic initiatives.
* Prepare and deliver compelling proposals and gift solicitations, including multi\-year commitments, donor\-advised fund gifts, endowed gifts, and planned giving opportunities.
* Maintain accurate, timely documentation of donor interactions, strategies, and progress within IDEA’s CRM to support effective portfolio management, forecasting, and collaboration.
* Collaborate with internal partners to design and execute stewardship plans, engagement experiences, and donor communications that demonstrate impact, reinforce trust, and encourage continued investment.

 **Additional Duties and Responsibilities:**


In addition to the essential duties outlined above, the Director of Philanthropy contributes to portfolio planning, forecasting, and continuous improvement efforts related to major gifts fundraising. This role participates in special initiatives, pilots, or campaigns that support the effectiveness and scalability of IDEA’s major gifts program; supports leadership reporting and analysis as needed; and maintains flexibility to adapt strategies in response to donor feedback, regional priorities, and organizational needs.

 **Knowledge and Skills – Competencies**

* **Make Strategic Decisions:** This team member makes informed decisions by gathering reliable information, asking clarifying questions, and evaluating multiple options. They thoughtfully align their choices with team objectives, current responsibilities, and the broader mission of the organization.
* **Manage Work and Teams:** This team member sets clear, measurable goals and regularly reflects on progress, adjusting actions as needed. They prioritize work aligned with their goals using a task management system and consistently meet deadlines through effective time management.
* **Grow Self and Others:** This team member demonstrates self\-awareness by actively seeking and thoughtfully responding to feedback with curiosity and a growth mindset. They identify development areas, implement feedback when appropriate, and pursue opportunities to build their knowledge and skills.
* **Build a Culture of Trust:** This team member proactively builds strong personal and professional relationships with individual stakeholders and regularly seeks feedback to improve their work experience. They create a supportive environment where others feel safe to take risks and learn from mistakes without fear of retribution.
* **Communicate Deliberately:** This team member communicates thoughtfully by anticipating potential misunderstandings and providing necessary context to ensure clarity. They leverage structured communication channels to address challenges, ask meaningful questions, and guide conversations toward solutions, while actively listening to the concerns of others.

  



**Additional Skills:**

* Proven ability to cultivate, solicit, and close gifts of $10,000

jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Managing Director
**Department:** Growth and Development
**Location:** Remote in the San Franciso Bay Area
**Who We Are**
Today’s societal challenges are more complex, interconnected, and urgent than ever. Sunflower Services is comprised of over 240 professionals with deep expertise in the philanthropic sector. We provide support services to fiscal sponsors and intermediaries—and their hundreds of mission\-driven projects—that are creating meaningful change. We welcome jobseekers who are motivated by results and driven by impact. For a list of current job openings at Sunflower, please visit our LinkedIn page.
Sunflower Services is an independent, nonprofit\-owned Public Benefit Corporation dedicated to providing operational excellence to nonprofit and social impact organizations. Sunflower delivers integrated solutions in finance, HR, grants management, compliance, and other administrative areas, helping mission\-driven organizations and changemakers focus on what matters most: their impact.
**Position Overview**Sunflower Services is seeking a bold, relationship\-driven Managing Director of Business Development to help shape the next chapter of the growth of a newly formed ecosystem providing fiscal sponsorship to changemakers tackling today's thorniest problems.
We are a private benefit corporation, wholly owned by three 501c3 public charities: New Venture Fund, Windward Fund, and Hopewell Fund. This is a senior leadership role for someone who combines deep fluency in the social sector with an entrepreneurial mindset and a track record of building high\-value, trust\-based partnerships.
The ideal candidate brings firsthand knowledge of the fiscal sponsorship landscape and understands how philanthropic capital flows, how changemakers and their funders make structural decisions, and how to position this ecosystem, powered by Sunflower’s unparalleled services, as the partner of choice for organizations operating at the frontier of social change. Based in northern California, this leader will influence strategy, develop people, and serve as a credible and inspiring voice in the field.
This role reports to Sunflower’s Chief Relationship Officer and works closely with senior leaders across Sunflower and its affiliated funds, including Hopewell Fund, Windward Fund, New Venture Fund, and Sixteen Thirty Fund.
**What You’ll Do**
Business Development (60%)
* Shape and advance Sunflower’s multi\-year growth strategy, in conjunction with our partners/owners, identifying and closing opportunities aligned with emerging trends in philanthropy and fiscal sponsorship
* Build and manage a pipeline of business aligned with the ecosystem partners’ areas of focus and a set of strong values, resulting in meeting individual and teamwide revenue and impact targets through the full sales cycle—providing leadership from lead generation through close
* Serve as a strategic advisor to prospective funders and project leaders, helping them understand how fiscal sponsorship can unlock new possibilities for their work
* Represent Sunflower and its partners/owners as a thought leader at conferences, in publications, and in high\-value sector forums; author content that positions the ecosystem at the forefront of the field
* Monitor market trends and philanthropic shifts to inform business development strategy and identify new service opportunities
* Cultivate channel partner and referral relationships that expand Sunflower’s reach and reputation


Relationship Stewardship and Client Stewardship (30%)
* Develop and sustain strong, long\-term relationships across the 501(c)3 and 501(c)4 ecosystem, and with a defined portfolio of funders and strategic partners
* Partner closely with the Presidents and senior leadership of multiple and separate nonprofit entities and partners to align priorities, share market intelligence, and identify collaborative opportunities
* Bring a sophisticated understanding of the ecosystem’s full\-service offerings to every client interaction—diagnosing needs, designing solutions, leading fee negotiations, and defining scope
* Collaborate with service teams to ensure excellent client experience that drives retention and referrals
* Proactively deepen existing relationships by anticipating evolving needs and introducing creative and relevant capabilities


Leadership (10%)
* Serve as a senior contributor to strategy, bringing market perspective, sector intelligence, and partner insight to leadership discussions about the ecosystem’s – and specifically, Sunflower’s direction and priorities
* Represent Sunflower and its partners as a credible and inspiring spokesperson for fiscal sponsorship – enhancing the ecosystem’s reputation and relationships across the social sector.
* Provide leadership to internal teams to contribute to organizational learning and sustainability


**What You’ll Bring**
* 10\+ years of progressive experience in business development, strategic partnerships, or client advisory roles within or adjacent to the social sector,
* Experience with fiscal sponsorship \- how it works, who the key players are, and how organizations and campaigns use it as a strategic tool
* A track record of building and closing complex, multi\-stakeholder relationships, ideally in a professional services or consulting context

jobs.title: Strategic Operations Lead, Office of the CEO
jobs.description:
Job Title:
Strategic Operations Lead, Office of the CEO

About Nscale

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development.

Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About The Role

We're looking for a highly analytical, execution-focused operator to work closely with the CEO and Chief of Staff on Nscale's most important priorities. Reporting directly to the Chief of Staff, this role will sit at the center of the business, driving cross-functional initiatives, supporting planning and operating cadence, and ensuring senior leadership has the insight needed to make fast, high-quality decisions.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role — you will move between strategy and execution, turning ambiguity into structured plans, driving accountability across teams, and surfacing insights that shape company direction.

We are looking for someone based in, or willing to relocate to, San Francisco.

What You'll Be Doing

Drive strategic initiatives

Support and lead high-priority, cross-functional projects on behalf of the CEO
Partner with leaders across Product, GTM, Finance, and Operations to drive alignment and execution
Break down ambiguous problems into clear workstreams, milestones, and deliverables
Conduct deep dives and ad hoc analysis on strategic and operational topics

Run operating cadence and planning

Support the company's operating rhythm, including weekly leadership meetings and follow-ups
Assist in quarterly planning cycles, including OKR tracking and alignment across teams
Track progress against company priorities, identifying risks and gaps early
Work across teams to unblock issues and maintain execution momentum

Own reporting and business insights

Own the weekly reporting process, ensuring outputs are accurate, timely, and actionable
Build and maintain core dashboards and tracking frameworks across the business
Identify trends, risks, and performance gaps, escalating insights to the CEO and Chief of Staff

Enable CEO and leadership team

Prepare high-quality briefing materials for leadership meetings, board discussions, and external engagements
Synthesize complex information into clear, concise, and actionable outputs
Act as a thought partner to the Chief of Staff on priorities, focus areas, and execution

About You

5+ years of experience in strategy, operations, consulting, investment banking, or a high-growth startup environment
Strong problem-solving ability with a track record of structuring ambiguous problems into actionable plans
Highly analytical, with experience in building models, dashboards, and synthesizing data into insights
Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and drive alignment across senior leaders
Proven ability to operate in fast-paced, high-growth environments with a high degree of ownership
Strong communication skills, with the ability to distill complex topics into clear narratives
High attention to detail and a bias for action, with a focus on delivering outcomes

What We Can Offer You

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

Highly competitive package (base + equity) with reviews every 12 months 🚀
Join the fastest-growing tech startup — your chance to push boundaries, collaborate with brilliant minds, and make your mark on cutting-edge AI ✨
Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by trying new things, leading, challenging the status quo, and owning your impact
Human-first flexibility — we trust you to shape your day and deliver your best work

The range below reflects the base salary for the position. Actual compensation may vary based on job-related factors such as skill set, experience, education, and location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus, equity, and/or commission programs. Nscale may offer a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, flexible paid time off, parental leave, and retirement plan participation.

Salary Range

$180,000—$280,000 USD

jobs.title: Managing Director, MU Ventures
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron is seeking a visionary, well-connected investor to lead Micron Ventures, the company’s corporate venture capital arm. This is a unique opportunity to shape how Micron engages with the next wave of innovation across AI, semiconductors, compute infrastructure, and adjacent technologies. The role will define Micron Ventures’ investment strategy, sector priorities, and portfolio construction in alignment with Micron’s corporate strategy and technology roadmap.

This leader will own the full venture lifecycle, including thesis development, sourcing, diligence, valuation, structuring, negotiation, and executive-level investment recommendations. The role will also partner closely with Micron business units and technical leaders to turn investments into strategic value through pilots, commercial engagement, product collaboration, and market insight.

Serve as the venture arm’s primary external ambassador across the founder, VC, and research communities, while acting as a trusted advisor to Micron’s executive leadership on technology shifts, competitive dynamics, partnership opportunities, and adjacent M&A themes.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate will bring a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, Business administration, or related field along with 15+ years of experience in venture capital, corporate venture capital, growth investing, or corporate development, including at least 5 years in senior fund leadership roles.

Consistent track record of successful investments and exits with financial and measurable strategic outcomes;
Experience leading or shaping the strategy of a $100M+ venture fund, including portfolio construction, deployment pacing, reserve strategy, and exit planning;
Extensive network across premier venture firms, founders, universities, accelerators, and frontier AI and semiconductor communities;
Proven ability to build and lead high-performing investment teams and focused investment processes;
Deep expertise in AI/ML, semiconductor ecosystems, advanced compute infrastructure, and the evolving hardware-software stack;
Exceptional executive presence, communication skills, and judgment in high-stakes internal and external settings.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Legal Operations
jobs.description:
About GlobalFoundries

GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

Summary Of Role

GlobalFoundries is seeking Senior Manager, Legal Operations that will lead the strategy, governance, and continuous improvement of GlobalFoundries' legal operations capabilities, with a primary focus on contract lifecycle management (CLM), legal technology, workflow automation, and AI-enabled solutions. This role will drive operational excellence across contracting processes while enabling greater efficiency, compliance, scalability, and business partnership throughout the enterprise.

Essential Responsibilities

Own and evolve GlobalFoundries' legal operations technology roadmap, including contract lifecycle management platforms, workflow automation tools, and emerging AI capabilities.
Lead the administration, optimization, and governance of CLM solutions, including templates, workflows, integrations, reporting, and user experience.
Identify, evaluate, and implement AI-enabled solutions that improve contracting efficiency, accelerate legal service delivery, and enhance business support.
Partner closely with Legal, IT, Procurement, Sales, Finance, and other stakeholders to streamline contracting and legal workflows across the enterprise.
Drive adoption of self-service contracting capabilities, automation tools, playbooks, and standardized processes that improve scalability and consistency.
Establish governance frameworks for legal technology and AI solutions, ensuring appropriate controls related to privacy, security, compliance, and risk management.
Oversee operational processes supporting commercial agreements, NDAs, procurement contracts, technology agreements, and other legal transactions.
Develop and monitor key operational metrics, dashboards, and reporting to measure effectiveness, adoption, cycle times, workload trends, and business impact.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing cycle times, improving stakeholder experience, mitigating risk, and increasing operational efficiency.
Create and maintain process documentation, standard operating procedures, training materials, and governance frameworks.
Manage relationships with external legal technology vendors and service providers, including roadmap planning, upgrades, performance reviews, and contract management.
Lead cross-functional projects and change management initiatives that support the modernization and digital transformation of Legal operations.
Serve as a trusted advisor to Legal leadership on technology investments, process optimization opportunities, and operational strategy.

Other Responsibilities

Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements, and programs.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, Legal Studies, Information Systems, Operations, or related field.
8+ years of experience in Legal Operations, Contract Management, Legal Technology, Procurement Operations, or related discipline.
Experience implementing, administering, or optimizing Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platforms.
Demonstrated success leading technology-enabled process transformation initiatives.
Strong program and project management capabilities with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Experience working across Legal, IT, and business organizations to deliver enterprise solutions.
Strong analytical, communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Icertis or other leading CLM platforms.
Experience implementing AI, automation, or digital transformation initiatives.
Semiconductor, manufacturing, or global technology industry experience.
Experience with CRM, ERP, and enterprise system integrations.
Experience developing operational dashboards and business metrics.
Lean Six Sigma, process improvement, or operational excellence certification.
Advanced degree (MBA, JD, or equivalent) preferred.

Expected Salary Range

$161,000.00 - $269,000.00

The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location.

Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

jobs.title: Assistant Director of Major Gifts
jobs.description:
Full-time, Exempt

Reports to Senior Director of Individual Philanthropy

Denver Scholarship Foundation (DSF) is seeking a passionate, driven individual with the desire to learn, grow, and excel in a culture that values every member of the team. DSF was named one of the Denver’s Top Workplaces in 2026 (7 year recipient of Top Workplaces), a testament to our team and to our intentionality in co-creating a positive, inclusive work environment. When you join the DSF team, you will enjoy a supportive, and innovative environment where your work has a profound impact on the lives of students and their families.

As a nonprofit organization, DSF’s mission is to inspire and empower DPS students to enroll in and graduate from postsecondary institutions of higher education, by providing the tools, knowledge, and financial resources essential for success. By embodying the core values of equity, innovation, leadership, learning, relationships, and integrity in everything we do. DSF strives to be a leader within the community, as we constantly seek to improve our services, we build strong relationships with college staff members, partners, students, team members and the broader community. We are committed to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion, believing in the value and ability of all students and team members.

We seek candidates who will model, live, and reinforce DSF’s mission and core values with colleagues, students, families, and the broader community. If you are passionate about the philosophy and mission of DSF, then we invite you to join us and help make college possible for Denver's students.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Major Gifts serves as a frontline fundraising leader and is responsible for executing Denver Scholarship Foundation’s (DSF) individual giving strategy with a focus on soliciting major and midlevel gifts, reporting to the Senior Director of Individual Philanthropy. The Assistant Director leads the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individual donors, with a focus on advancing relationships, increasing giving, and moving donors through the pipeline in alignment with established portfolio standards. This individual manages a portfolio of donors and prospects and prioritizes relationship-driven engagement that balances stewardship with intentional growth strategies.

Working in close partnership with the Senior Director of Individual Philanthropy, this role contributes to revenue goals by executing and ensuring consistent, coordinated engagement across the donor journey. The Assistant Director collaborates across the Growth and Engagement team, including the Chief Growth & Engagement Officer, Director of Corporate Relations, Development Operations, and Marketing & Communications in support of DSF’s overall fundraising strategy.

Job Responsibilities

Portfolio Management

Manage a portfolio of individual donors and prospects, leading all stages of the fundraising cycle from identification through stewardship
Develop and execute individualized cultivation and solicitation strategies aligned with portfolio standards
Implement tailored strategies across major and mid-level donors
Actively manages and grows their portfolio of donors

Strategy Execution and Metrics

Execute DSF’s individual giving strategy in partnership with the Senior Director of Individual Philanthropy
Drive progress toward revenue goals through portfolio management and donor engagement
Maintain accurate pipeline tracking, donor activity, and performance metrics in Salesforce
Regularly assess portfolio performance and adjust strategies to improve giving outcomes

Donor Experience

Partner with the Senior Director, Chief Growth & Engagement Officer, CEO, and volunteers to coordinate donor strategies and engagement
Collaborate inter-departmentally to ensure aligned messaging and a cohesive donor journey
Execute donor acknowledgment, recognition, and stewardship strategies that enhance the overall donor experience
Support strategic engagement for principal, planned, and endowment-level donors as appropriate
Collaborates and coordinates with staff in all departments to maximize donor relationships and philanthropic giving

Pipeline Development

Apply prospect research to identify, qualify, and prioritize new donors
Contribute to broader strategies including annual giving, alumni engagement, events, and campaign efforts
Support the development of a sustainable donor pipeline, with particular attention to mid-level donor growth
Serve as a knowledgeable ambassador for DSF, effectively communicating mission, impact, and funding opportunities

Requirements

Required Skills and Abilities

Ability to build strong relationships with a donor centric approach
Ability to understand the needs and interests of major donors to develop relationships between them and DSF
Dedication to promoting DSF’s fundraising priorities through developing excellent working relationships with DSF staff, board, committees, and other volunteers
Ability to initiate, analyze, monitor, evaluate, and alter strategic development plans
Experience working with all Microsoft Office applications
Excellent oral, written, interpersonal, analytical, and organization skills
Strong attention to detail and ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks
Ability to work independently as well as in a team environment
Ability to deal professionally and courteously with a wide variety of people, both in person and over the phone
Ability to maintain confidentiality
Optimistic attitude and flexibility in a changing work environment
Experience working with culturally diverse and communities with low-income
Commitment to the DSF mission
Hybrid position 3 days onsite and two days remote

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent combination of training and experience
Five or more years of individual major gift fundraising experience
Experience with Salesforce preferred

Benefits

$74,000 to $97,500
401(k) plan with $ for $ match of up to 5%
Group health, dental, and vision insurance, low-cost premium plans offered. DSF pays for 90% of employee only and 70% of dependent plans.
Life Insurance that provides 2 Times Your Annual Salary
Free Annual Eco RTD Bus Pass
Short Term and Long Term Disability Insurance
Short Term Disability Supplement (Based on Years of Service)
Paid holidays (includes Winter Break and Summer 1/2 Fridays in June and July) and 2 Floating holidays each year
Trusted Time Off (unlimited vacation policy following 90 days)
Paid Maternity and Paternity Leave (Based on Years of Service)
ID Theft Protection and Will Preparation Assistance
Reduced cost for Legal Counseling
Free Financial Counseling
Four Professional Wellness Sessions and $300 annual wellness reimbursement
Free Employee Assistance and Confidential Counseling Services

Learn about DSF’s commitment to Equity & Inclusion.

jobs.title: Director of Partnerships and Community Outreach, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
On-site (multiple locations listed in Requirements)
W2 Employee
$200K annually

Families who select Alpha already rely on trusted advisors across every dimension of their lives. This role fills the one advisory relationship they've been lacking.

You will become the person they reach out to when uncertainty arises, when something doesn't feel right, or when they want to share a milestone they know you will appreciate. You'll develop familiarity with each family that allows you to foresee their needs before they articulate them—and you'll possess the judgment and composure to address whatever they bring with discretion, warmth, and ease. Over time, you won't simply represent their child's school. You'll become woven into the fabric of how they navigate this stage of their family's journey.

This level of trust is not built through systems. It emerges from presence—regular, sustained, and unrushed. You'll be accessible during morning arrival and afternoon departure, at significant evening gatherings, and in spontaneous one-on-one exchanges that rarely appear on schedules. You'll cultivate a community that families feel invested in protecting, where belonging is natural and referrals flow from the quality of the experience itself.

Alpha operates differently from conventional schools. Students complete core academics in two hours daily through AI-enabled applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical thinking, and applied projects. No traditional lectures. No unnecessary assignments. Performance in the top 1% nationally. The families who enroll are investing in something they value deeply—but confidence requires ongoing reinforcement.

You'll sustain that dialogue with every family, through every question, for the duration of their enrollment. If the prospect of championing an unconventional approach to discerning skeptics feels daunting, this position is not suitable. If it represents the most compelling work you could pursue, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Take ownership of the relationship with every family at your campus—the evolving, deepening connection that ensures parents feel recognized, not merely attended to
Identify potential concerns in advance and address them with the discretion and interpersonal skill that preserves confidence
Maintain visible presence in family spaces: morning arrival (7–9am), afternoon departure (2–4pm), evening parent gatherings, and select weekend programming
Develop a campus community with authentic depth—events, rituals, and touchpoints that foster a sense of belonging to something families consider worth safeguarding
Nurture parent champions organically, designing experiences of such consistent quality that referrals emerge naturally
Sustain the dialogue about Alpha's AI-driven model with families managing screen time questions, skeptical relatives, and periodic uncertainty—not only during enrollment but throughout their campus experience
Recognize when a family is not aligned and manage that reality with the same care you apply to all interactions—community protection is integral to service
Create the structures and routines this role demands in a setting where established protocols are still emerging

What You Won’t Be Doing

Overseeing enrollment processes—that falls under the Admissions Director; your responsibility begins after families enroll and intensifies over time
Operating from an office—your community presence defines the role
Maintaining standard 9–5 schedules—early mornings, late afternoons, and evening programming are routine components, not occasional requirements
Relying on administrative infrastructure, standardized procedures, or a complete team—you function with significant independence and create what is necessary
Managing family relationships as transactional accounts—this role values authentic engagement over procedural adherence

Director Of Partnerships And Community Outreach Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central trusted relationship in every family's Alpha experience. Maintain their confidence during challenging periods, cultivate a community where belonging feels meaningful, and establish conditions under which satisfied families naturally become outspoken advocates.

Basic Requirements

Currently living within commuting range of one of the following campuses OR prepared to relocate within 60 days (preference given to candidates with established local community ties): Denver, CO; Greenwich, CT; Boca Raton, FL; Tampa, FL; Boston, MA; Bethesda, MD; Charlotte, NC; Las Vegas, NV; Oklahoma City, OK; Tulsa, OK; Nashville, TN; Austin, TX; Dallas (Carrollton), TX; Fort Worth, TX; Houston (The Woodlands), TX; Park City, UT; Burlington, VT; Kirkland, WA; or Jackson Hole, WY
Authorized to work legally in the United States without sponsorship requirements
5+ years in relationship-focused roles serving high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families—private school admissions, luxury hospitality, philanthropic development, or any context where discretion, warmth, and social acuity were equally critical to competence
Proven capacity to preserve relationships through complex situations with sophisticated families and maintain trust throughout
Authentic presence and communication approach that builds confidence rapidly with affluent, high-expectation families—genuine rather than rehearsed
Direct familiarity with independent, private, or alternative education—through professional work or parenting—that provides credible standing when families challenge the model
Authentic conviction in AI-enabled education and capacity to sustain that belief genuinely across years of parent engagement, not merely during initial enrollment
Flexibility for variable hours: early mornings (7–9am), late afternoons (2–4pm), evening events 2–3 times monthly, and occasional weekend activities

Nice-to-have Requirements

Exceptional candidates will possess at least one of these qualities:

Established connections within the local affluent community providing immediate, organic credibility on campus
Private school or independent school background with demonstrated success in family retention and community building—beyond enrollment metrics alone
Experience managing high-stakes family dynamics where your discretion and judgment were instrumental in preserving trust
Natural ability to design experiences—gatherings, moments, settings—where participants feel connected to something they value protecting
Prior startup or early-stage organizational experience where you built from the ground up and maintained composure amid rapid change

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $100 USD/hour, which equates to $200,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly.  **Position Overview:**


Jewish National Fund\-USA is expanding its Tristate fundraising team and adding several new positions to support our growing donor community and organizational impact.

  

We are seeking an experienced Associate Executive Director to oversee fundraising and community engagement in Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens.This role focuses on building and sustaining strong donor relationships, partnering closely with lay leadership, and expanding regional support through strategic cultivation, events, and mission\-based engagement.

  



Reports to: Executive Director, Tristate


Location: New York, NY (on\-site, 5 days)

 **Responsibilities:**


Regional Leadership \& Strategy

* Develop and execute a regional fundraising and engagement strategy aligned with national priorities
* Set and manage revenue goals, performance metrics, and accountability standards
* Serve as a senior representative of JNF\-USA within the regional Jewish community


Fundraising \& Donor Engagement

* Manage and grow a portfolio of major donors and prospects through strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
* Identify and develop new donor relationships to expand the regional pipeline
* Partner with lay leadership and board members to leverage networks and advance fundraising outcomes
* Oversee cultivation initiatives, donor briefings, events, missions, and stewardship activities


Team Leadership \& Collaboration

* Lead, mentor, and develop a high\-performing regional team
* Support hiring, onboarding, coaching, and performance management
* Collaborate with national development, marketing, finance, and program teams


Community Engagement \& Representation

* Build and maintain strong relationships with communal partners and stakeholders
* Recruit and engage participants for missions, conferences, and signature initiatives
* Host visiting Israeli partners and affiliates with appropriate donor alignment and follow\-up


Operations, Data \& Reporting

* Ensure accurate donor activity tracking and reporting in Salesforce
* Use data and analytics to support forecasting, strategy, and performance management
* Oversee regional budgets and responsible resource management

 **Qualifications:**

* Deep passion for Israel and JNF\-USA's mission
* 10\+ years of progressive fundraising, development, or related leadership experience, including major gifts
* Proven ability to develop strategy and drive revenue growth
* Strong executive\-level written and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams
* Strategic, organized, and comfortable operating with autonomy
* Salesforce or CRM preferred
* Familiarity with the regional Jewish community and nonprofit landscape strongly preferred

 **Travel:**

* Regular regional travel within the assigned territory
* Occasional domestic and international travel, including missions to Israel and national conferences

 **Perks:**

* Days off for all work\-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to the secular US holidays
* Generous paid time off
* 3pm close\-of\-business on Fridays
* Top\-notch healthcare (including dental and vision)
* Parental Leave policy
* Employer\-paid life insurance
* Employer\-paid short and long\-term disability
* 403(b) with 10\.5% employer contribution
* Opportunities to travel to Israel
* Occasional domestic and international travel, including missions to Israel and national conferences

 **Compensation:**


$175,000–$210,000

 **Pay Type:**


Salaried

  

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role.

 **WHAT WE DO**


For 125 years, Jewish National Fund\-USA has helped strengthen the land and people of Israel by investing in the communities, infrastructure, and leadership that shape the country's future. Our work is focused on making Israel's North and South places where families can build full, vibrant lives with access to medical care, emergency response, water solutions, parks, playgrounds, jobs, and economic opportunity.
