jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a senior executive who provides strategic leadership and oversees the integration and growth of Veit’s construction operations in line with the company’s 2032 Vision to become the Midwest’s most trusted infrastructure solutions provider. This role develops and implements forward-thinking strategies to ensure safe, reliable project delivery, exceptional client experiences, and innovation. The COO builds scalable teams, enhances leadership and technical skills, and adapts operations to market and client needs.

With a strong background in Heavy Civil construction, the COO turns enterprise strategy into actionable plans, leading operations across all service lines and markets. The COO drives collaboration, breaks down organizational silos, and champions multidivisional initiatives and joint projects.

Additionally, the COO supports team versatility through cross-training, rotational assignments, and robust operational training. By continuously improving standard operating procedures and sharing best practices, the COO enables responsible growth, market differentiation, and long-term value for clients and communities.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Enterprise Operations & Integration

Provide overall leadership and integration of construction operations across all service lines and markets.
Ensure consistent execution of operational standards, project delivery models, and performance expectations.
Drive collaboration and communication across all departments and business units to support enterprise-wide goals.
Own and enforce enterprise go/no-go criteria aligned to Veit’s strategic focus, margin thresholds, and resource capacity.
Ensure operational leaders consistently prioritize negotiated, multi-service, union-friendly projects aligned with Veit’s core markets and strategic clients.
Champion the elimination of organizational silos by encouraging and facilitating multidivisional initiatives and joint project delivery.
Promote cross-training opportunities and rotational assignments to build versatile teams and deepen organizational expertise.
Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of standard operating procedures to ensure best practices are shared and adopted across all regions and service lines.
Develop, support, and oversee comprehensive operational training programs to foster consistency, safety, and excellence throughout the organization.

Scalable Organization & Team Development

Design and lead an operational organization capable of scaling over time while maintaining consistency, accountability, and performance.
Build and evolve leadership structures, spans of control, and role clarity to support growth across regions, service lines, and markets.
Ensure Veit has the right people, in the right roles, with the right capabilities to support current and future work.
Partner with People & Culture to define and implement clear skills and competency frameworks for operational leadership, project management, and field execution.
Champion intentional development of technical, leadership, and business acumen skills at all levels of operations.
Establish succession plans for critical operational roles to ensure continuity and long-term stability.

Strategy & Market Approach

Own operational readiness for Veit’s client and market strategy ensuring growth is pursued only where Veit can deliver the Legendary Client Experience profitably and consistently.
Partner with executive leadership, Business Development, and Market Leaders to identify priority clients, target markets, and strategic opportunities.
Translate client and market insights into operational readiness: staffing plans, equipment strategy, delivery models, and leadership capacity.
Drive differentiated market approaches by aligning Veit’s services, delivery models, and operational strengths with client needs.
Ensure operational teams are prepared to support national, regional, and strategic accounts with consistency and excellence.

Legendary Client Experience & Market Trust

Establish operational expectations and systems that consistently deliver legendary client experiences, not just successful projects.
Ensure project teams understand client goals, success metrics, and long-term relationship objectives.
Embed client experience measures (predictability, communication, responsiveness, outcomes) into operational KPIs.
Partner with Market Leads and Project Executives to proactively strengthen key client relationships and expand repeat business.
Reinforce Veit’s reputation as a trusted partner through disciplined execution and value-driven delivery.
Accountable for Voice of Client outcomes, including predictability, communication quality, relationship depth, and repeat work.
Ensure consistent project closeout processes that reinforce trust, learning, and future opportunity.

People Leadership

Build an environment where the best people proudly do their best work, feel ownership over outcomes, and see a clear future at Veit.
Develop strong operational leaders who can balance safety, performance, people leadership, and client stewardship.
Reinforce leadership behaviors that align with Veit’s values, vision, and long-term strategy.
Support cross-functional collaboration and break down silos between operations, preconstruction, fleet, and support teams.

Innovation & Technology Leadership

Champion a culture of continuous improvement and innovation across all operations, encouraging teams to identify and implement new technologies and process enhancements.
Partner with IT and operational leaders to evaluate, select, and deploy cutting-edge construction technologies to improve project outcomes and efficiency.
Drive digital transformation by integrating technology solutions that streamline workflows, enhance collaboration, and support scalable growth across service lines and regions.
Establish frameworks for piloting and adopting emerging tools, ensuring that Veit remains at the forefront of industry advancements and maintains a competitive edge.
Monitor industry trends and proactively assess opportunities for automation, AI, and other innovations that can reduce risk, improve safety, and enhance client value.
Ensure operational leaders and teams are equipped with the necessary training and support to maximize the benefits of new technologies and foster a mindset of adaptability.
Collaborate with executive leadership to align technology investments with strategic objectives, ensuring measurable impact on operational performance and client experience.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
20+ years of progressive leadership experience in Heavy Civil construction, including multi-market or multi-division operations.
Proven experience building and scaling operational teams and leadership structures in growing or complex organizations.
Demonstrated success developing and executing multi-year market and client strategies tied to operational capability.
Strong understanding of project management, construction operations, and operational risk.
Ability to develop talent, define competencies, and build leadership depth.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong financial acumen with experience overseeing operational performance and margins.
Proven ability to lead, develop, and motivate cross‑functional teams to achieve high performance and operational excellence.
Familiarity with multiple construction types, such as commercial and industrial.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with an executive presence that builds trust and alignment across stakeholders.
Strategic business and financial acumen with strong capability in budgeting, forecasting, cost control, and performance optimization.
Strong client relationship and business development abilities to secure, expand, and sustain partnerships.
Strong ethical judgment and commitment to integrity, accountability, and professional standards in all business practices.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide change in complex, field-based organizations.
Strong decision discipline: able to make clear tradeoffs and hold the line on strategy under pressure.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Experience leading organizations through growth, integration, or operating model transformation.
Demonstrated success strengthening client trust and expanding long-term, strategic client relationships.
Experience supporting national or multi-regional clients.
Familiarity with competency-based leadership development and succession planning.

Supervisory Responsibility

Provides executive-level leadership that influences and sets direction for SVPs and VPs of Service Groups and for VPs of Operations, aligning performance expectations, standard work, and cross-functional delivery across the enterprise.

Additional Job Description

Who Are We?

Veit is one of the country’s leading specialty contractors, with nearly a century of experience and the best people in the industry. We specialize in foundations, earthwork, utilities, marine services, industrial cleaning, cured‑in‑place pipelining, and waste disposal. We pride ourselves on our relentless pursuit to push the construction industry forward and deliver for our customers. Our modern fleet of iron, diverse expertise, and unmatched determination allow us to successfully tackle some of the largest and most complex projects across every sector while also living out our values every day. Our company culture is one where everyone pitches in to get the job done, regardless of job title or seniority. We do everything we can to maintain an atmosphere where family comes first. We want every one of our employees to look forward to each day at work and make it home safe and happy at the end of the day.

Never settle, dig deeper

Our Core Values

Deliberately Safe We believe all safety incidents are avoidable when everyone operates with a deliberate mindset. We are deliberately proactive and thorough in training and job planning. We are deliberately safe in our everyday operations and decision-making.
Build with Intention We build with intention. Whether in the office or the field, we work with grit and determination toward a better future for everyone involved. We leave things better than we found them, and never leave a job until we’re proud to put the Veit name on it.
Leaders Dig First Egos have no place at Veit. We expect everyone on our team to dig in with a leadership mentality. That means being willing to jump in, take ownership, and get mud on our boots — especially when times get challenging.
Real Relationships Like our work, we approach relationships authentically, with a long-term mindset. Whether you’re a client partner, vendor, or team member, we make an effort to build a more meaningful connection with you by communicating with respect and honesty.
Integrity in Everything As part of the Veit family, everything we do and say reflects on this entire company. We act with integrity, which means treating others just as we want to be treated, doing the right thing, and holding ourselves accountable.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

** NOTE A COVER LETTER IS REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION **

In this senior-level strategic role with no direct supervisory responsibilities, the Program Development Director, Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP), leads the development, coordination, and delivery of applied transportation research produced through ACRP. ACRP is sponsored by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and managed by the Transportation Research Board. ACRP undertakes research that directly engages and benefits the airport industry.

Reporting to the Director of the Cooperative Research Programs and working closely with both the Director and Deputy Director, the Program Development Director serves as a primary staff partner to the ACRP Oversight Committee and FAA. The position ensures that the oversight committee’s priorities, decisions, and guidance, together with external stakeholder input, are effectively translated into internal program delivery activities and cohesive research portfolios.

The role exercises substantial independent judgment, manages a portfolio of complex and high-visibility research projects, and engages extensively with senior volunteers, sponsors, and stakeholders across the transportation community.

The Transportation Research Board (TRB), a division of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, provides leadership in transportation innovation through objective, evidence-based research and convenes experts from government, industry, and academia to address complex transportation challenges. Within TRB, the Cooperative Research Programs (CRP) is a group of applied research programs—such as the National Cooperative Highway Research Program (NCHRP), Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP), Transit Cooperative Research Program (TCRP), and Behavioral Traffic Safety Cooperative Research Program (BTSCRP), among others—that develop practical, implementable solutions to current and emerging transportation issues through stakeholder-driven research and collaboration.

Job Description

Responsibilities

Oversight Committee & Program Development

Work in close cooperation with the Director and Deputy Director to support the program oversight committee in identifying, refining, and prioritizing research needs.
Prepare analyses, options, and recommendations to support oversight committee deliberations and approval of research projects.
Contribute substantively to program development by integrating oversight committee guidance, stakeholder input, and operational considerations.
Ensure oversight committee decisions and priorities are clearly communicated and addressed through internal delivery activities.

Oversight Committee Meeting Planning & Support

Lead planning and coordination of oversight committee meetings, including agendas, schedules, materials, and decision frameworks, in cooperation with the Director.
Develop executive-quality briefing materials, background papers, program updates, and decision documents.
Document committee decisions, track action items, and coordinate follow-up to support timely implementation.

Stakeholder Engagement & Environmental Scanning

Independently engage with federal, state, local, and private-sector stakeholders to identify emerging research needs, trends, issues, and concerns.
Conduct environmental scanning of transportation policy, practice, technology, and research developments.
Synthesize stakeholder input and present insights to the Director, Deputy Director, and oversight committee to inform program direction and delivery.

Coordination with TRB Committees & NASEM Offices

Serve as a primary liaison with relevant TRB standing committees, task forces, and panels to inform research needs identification and promote alignment.
Coordinate with other National Academies divisions and offices, as appropriate, to leverage institutional expertise and avoid duplication.
Maintain awareness of related work across CRPs and NASEM to support integrated program delivery.

Program & Portfolio Management

Manage an assigned portfolio of complex research projects approved by the oversight committee.
Manage selected complex or high-profile research projects personally, including contractor oversight and delivery of final products.
Oversee contractor performance, schedules, budgets, and deliverables with minimal supervision.
Identify and resolve project-level issues independently and escalate strategic, fiscal, or reputational risks as appropriate.

Governance, Quality & Compliance Alignment

Ensure adherence to TRB and National Academies policies governing committee operations, peer review, ethics, and conflicts of interest.
Work closely with centralized CRP quality, compliance, contracting, and training functions to ensure projects meet institutional standards.
Support consensus-driven committee processes with objectivity and professionalism.

Communication & Influence

Prepare concise, decision-focused written materials for senior volunteers, sponsors, and leadership.
Communicate clearly and confidently with oversight committee members, stakeholders, contractors, and colleagues.
Influence outcomes through expertise, analysis, and collaboration rather than formal authority.

Requirements

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of cooperative or committee-driven research programs and familiarity with transportation research sponsors and policy environments.
Understanding of the National Academies’ mission, structure, and culture.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage complex portfolios and competing priorities.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage and influence stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to negotiate funding and manage high-risk or complex research initiatives.
Ability to train, develop, and support staff.
Ability to operate with substantial independence, sound judgment, and discretion in a complex organizational environment.
Ability to solve complex problems involving significant variety and to serve as a resource to others in resolving issues.
Ability to work effectively in team-based settings and build and sustain collaborative relationships across departments and stakeholder groups.
Ability to perform effectively in complex, high-impact environments with multiple priorities and demands.

Minimum Education/Training Requirements

Ph.D. in a discipline relevant to transportation, public policy, research management, or a closely related field; or a master’s, or bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline with significant professional experience demonstrating advanced subject matter expertise, leadership in complex projects or programs, and independent research, analysis, or policy development responsibilities.

Minimum Experience

Ten years of related professional experience. Demonstrated impact on the advancement of science or policy through the successful completion of National Academies’ activities or equivalent outside activities and through effective dissemination of these activities.
Significant experience managing applied research projects or programs.
Demonstrated experience supervising and developing professional staff in a complex organization.

Required Licenses, Certification or Registration:
None

Any qualification to be considered equivalent, in lieu of stated minimum, requires the prior approval of the Office of Human Resources.

Preferred Qualifications

Possession of an Accredited Airport Executive (A.A.E.), Certified Manager (C.M.), or International Airport Professional (IAP) designation

Other Details

Supervisory Responsibilities/Controls

Reports to the Division Director. Independently establishes goals and objectives. May supervise staff.

Mental And Physical Capabilities

Ability to be visible on camera for meetings when remote.

Ability to use a computer and applicable hardware/software to perform responsibilities.

Ability to use multiple technology collaboration platforms, including collaboration tools. Examples: Microsoft Teams, Asana.

Ability to Focus/concentrate on tasks and multi-task, when needed

Begin work at the required time, per approved schedule.

Ability to lift/carry laptop and other mobile devices between work and home.

Ability to commute to work.

Ability to travel between National Academies’ facilities and offsite sponsor/partner locations.

Ability to work in different time zones, when travel is outside of current location, e.g., when traveling internationally.

Ability To Perform Work Responsibilities Onsite, Where Required.

Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines.

Ability to use a computer and applicable hardware/software to perform responsibilities.

Work Environment

Hybrid office/telecommute environment; expected onsite percentage 60%. Occasional travel between National Academies’ facilities and to off-site meeting/sponsor locations.

Company Description
Students Engaged In Advancing Texas (SEAT) is a youth-led movement focused on developing transferable skills and elevating youth visibility in policymaking across Texas. In 100+ school districts and colleges statewide, the organization engages young people in hands-on advocacy and educational opportunities that foster civic participation and leadership. These include peer-led fellowship programs, campus-based chapters, an annual Advocacy Day at the Texas Capitol, legal action, creative projects, and public advocacy campaigns. SEAT aims to drive civic transformation by empowering communities to address systemic issues and dismantle oppressive power structures. Team members collaborate in a mission-driven environment that values equity, grassroots engagement, and sustainable social change. Joining SEAT means contributing to a growing movement centered on youth voice, community betterment, and inclusive policy impact.

Role Description
The Development Director is a full-time (40/hours), mostly remote role based in Texas, responsible for leading and executing SEAT’s fundraising and development strategy. This position oversees donor cultivation and stewardship, including individual, corporate, and foundation relationships, while designing and implementing annual and long-term giving plans that align with organizational goals. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing fundraising campaigns, coordinating special events, preparing development-related budgets and financial reports, and ensuring accurate tracking of contributions and donor data. The Development Director collaborates with leadership and program staff to craft compelling cases for support, develop grant proposals, and integrate fundraising messages into communications. This role also involves managing volunteers or interns engaged in development activities and continuously assessing and improving fundraising processes to support SEAT’s mission and growth. Up to 20% of work could include in-person activities such as hosting fundraiser events, meeting with prospective donors, and traveling to conferences.

Qualifications

3+ years of demonstrated expertise in Fundraising and Philanthropy, including cultivating and stewarding diverse donor and partner relationships.
Proven ability to develop and implement comprehensive development plans, including grant writing, event-based fundraising, securing major gifts, and digital engagement.
Track record of securing five-figure or more contributions from individuals, corporations, and foundations.

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment

Partner with product management, engineering, IT, finance, HR, and business leaders to align technology operations with business priorities.
Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives and technology-enabled business growth.
Ensure effective coordination across global technology teams.

VIII. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead high-performing technology operations teams.
Develop leadership capabilities, succession planning, and talent development programs.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Promote employee engagement and collaboration across technology functions.

Education Background

Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related fields.
Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

Typically 18+ years of experience in technology operations, IT management, engineering operations, or related functions, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles.
Proven experience managing large-scale technology organizations, digital transformation programs, and enterprise operations.
Strong background in software development operations, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and technology governance.

**About the Opportunity**

The San Gabriel Valley Economic Partnership (SGVEP) is seeking an experienced, visionary, and collaborative leader to serve as its next President \& Chief Executive Officer. For more than 30 years, the Partnership has served as the leading voice for business and economic development in the San Gabriel Valley, representing 31 cities and nearly two million residents throughout eastern Los Angeles County.

**Position Overview**

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the President \& CEO serves as the chief executive officer of the organization and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, organizational management, fiscal oversight, membership growth, stakeholder engagement, advocacy, and program development.

The successful candidate will be a dynamic relationship\-builder who can effectively work with elected officials, business leaders, educational institutions, workforce partners, and community stakeholders while positioning the Partnership as the premier regional economic development organization in the San Gabriel Valley.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership**

* Lead the implementation and execution of the Partnership's Strategic Plan.
* Collaborate with the Board of Directors to establish organizational priorities, goals, and performance measures.
* Identify emerging economic, workforce, and public policy opportunities affecting the San Gabriel Valley.
* Position the Partnership as a recognized regional leader on issues impacting business competitiveness and economic growth.

* Ensure effective governance support for the Board of Directors and its committees.

**Revenue Development \& Membership Growth**

* Lead membership recruitment, retention, and engagement efforts.
* Develop and implement strategies to diversify and grow organizational revenue.
* Secure sponsorships, grants, partnerships, and other funding opportunities.
* Cultivate relationships with corporate, public\-sector, philanthropic, and community partners.

**Regional Advocacy \& External Relations**

* Serve as the chief spokesperson for the organization.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with elected officials, business executives, city managers, educational leaders, and community stakeholders.
* Represent the Partnership at regional, state, and national meetings and events.
* Advance public policy initiatives that support economic development, workforce development, infrastructure investment, housing, and business growth.

**Program \& Economic Development Leadership**

* Guide the development and implementation of programs and initiatives that support the Partnership's mission.

* Strengthen collaboration among cities, educational institutions, employers, and workforce development partners.

The ideal candidate will possess:

* Strong financial management and budgeting experience.
* Exceptional communication, public speaking, and relationship\-building skills.
* Experience working with boards of directors, elected officials, and diverse stakeholder groups.

**Education Requirements** 

A **bachelor's degree** from an accredited college or university is **required**. A master's degree in public administration, business administration, economic development, or a related field is preferred.

The annual salary range for this position is **$135,000 to $170,000**, depending on qualifications and experience.

Our pioneering public\-private partnership between the San Francisco Recreation \& Parks Department and San Francisco Botanical Garden Society combines the city's expertise in horticulture and facilities with the nonprofit’s strengths in visitor experience, education, philanthropy, membership, marketing, curatorial services, interpretation, and community engagement. jobs.title: Managing Director, Discovery and Insight
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **ABOUT TED**


TED is on a mission to discover and spread ideas that spark imagination, embrace possibility, and catalyze impact. Our organization is devoted to curiosity, reason, wonder, and the pursuit of knowledge — without an agenda. We welcome people from every discipline and culture who seek a deeper understanding of the world and connection with others, and we invite everyone to engage with ideas and activate them in your community.

**ABOUT THE AUDACIOUS PROJECT**


The Audacious Project is a collaborative funding platform that invites visionary changemakers to imagine their boldest ideas to solve the world’s most urgent challenges.


Housed at TED, the nonprofit dedicated to the belief that ideas change everything, Audacious works to surface ideas that are breathtakingly ambitious yet achievable and brings together a community of philanthropists to unlock the funding needed to make them real. Each year, Audacious selects a cohort of extraordinary leaders from around the world — visionaries with proximity to the problems they're solving, and bold plans to shift systems, lift up communities, and contribute to a healthier planet.


Since its launch in 2018, Audacious has helped to catalyze more than $8B for over 70 projects across a range of issue areas. Rooted in TED's belief that ideas can come from anywhere, Audacious focuses on the strength of the idea and the team behind it, not a fixed issue area. Funded projects span science, climate, technology, health, social safety net and justice.

 **Job Description** **Role Description**


The Managing Director, Discovery and Insight leads Audacious's global search for ambitious ideas and changemakers — finding, testing, and building the case for the ideas and leaders most worth backing each funding cycle. This role owns end\-to\-end curation, application, and diligence activities, ultimately leading to recommendations for the cohort of finalists selected annually.


The Managing Director's work is centered on: a strategy informed by continuous learning about systems\-level impact and Audacious' unique role within it; deep collaboration with applicants, donors, and partners nurtured over time; and leadership of a strong team to sustain the work.


Each year, the Discovery and Insight team conducts a global search to identify nonprofit ideas that are:

* Innovative and offer a unique approach to a significant problem with the potential to shift the status quo or the system they operate within
* Proximate \& Community\-Oriented in leadership and decision\-making structure (i.e., led by those who intimately understand the problem/opportunity, incorporating impacted communities in decision\-making, led by someone who has direct experience in/with the community served)
* Approaching an inflection point or needing a significant capital inflow to catalyze a differentiated level of impact that they haven’t received support for yet (rather than support for ongoing operations)
* Thoughtfully ambitious ideas that both inspire and convince — have an exciting, breakthrough vision (‘inspire’), clear outcomes, and evidence that the idea will have a significant and concrete impact (‘convince’)

 **Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Set and evolve the sourcing and curation strategy.**

* Advance sourcing and curation strategy for each cycle, forming a clear point of view on where Audacious should be learning, looking, collaborating, and why, ultimately carrying that strategy forward across cycles
* Develop a “future\-oriented” approach by monitoring and anticipating emerging trends and innovations that Audacious actively engages with or responds to
* Actively capture insights and lessons learned to refine and improve Audacious's sourcing and curation activities annually

 **2\. Lead selection and diligence.**

* Apply the sourcing and curation strategy to identify the ideas most worth Audacious's attention \- deciding what advances into the application stage, and bringing along multiple stakeholders and inputs along that decision\-making process
* Lead diligence on selected organizations, rigorously testing readiness, viability, and fit within Audacious's portfolio
* Build the recommendation — evidence, rationale, and risks included — that carries an idea into finalist selection

 **3\. Cultivate and steward the partners who bring ideas to Audacious.**

* Surface strong ideas by building genuine, ongoing relationships with social sector leaders, including funder and intermediary partners (incl. sourcing networks, collaboratives, and others)
* Steward key partner relationships by developing a deep understanding of each stakeholder’s goals, priorities, and aspirations
* Maintain stakeholder relationships continuously, within and across cycles, to ensure trust and rapport among all actors
* Represent Audacious's point of view in the field, using that standing to draw the most ambitious organizations and ideas toward the platform and to create richer opportunities for sector collaboration

 **4\. Build and nurture a team that explores the frontier of audacious social change.**

* Lead the Discovery and Insight vertical and its resourcing strategically, matching capacity to where the real work sits and bringing in the right technical expertise when needed
* Develop people who can source, diligence, and hold partner relationships credibly in their own right — building a team of strong practitioners so Audacious's discovery capacity grows beyond any single person
* Effectively steward relationships and actively collaborate with key Audacious partners (e.g., The Bridgespan Group) with whom we partner year\-round

 **Qualifications** **Career and Functional Experience**

**Essential**

* A leader who has set strategy in fast\-paced, entrepreneurial environments, and who can hold their own in rooms both with ultra\-high net worth individuals and issue experts and with their own team, making consequential decisions grounded in clear principles

Destination Tomorrow (DT) is a national grassroots LGBTQ\+ organization founded in the Bronx, built on the principle that no individual should have to leave their neighborhood for necessary services. DT's mission is to move clients off the path of emergency care to one where they can grow, learn, and flourish by emphasizing economic, social, and mental empowerment through comprehensive educational, financial, and health programs, as well as housing solutions. As an expanding multi\-site organization, Destination Tomorrow proudly serves the community across The Bronx, New York City; Atlanta, GA; and Washington, D.C.

More than a traditional administrative role, this position acts as the CEO's right hand—managing priorities, driving accountability and decisions, coordinating and improving executive scheduling and operations, streamlining communication, and facilitating follow\-through to keep momentum . This role will function as an extension of the CEO’s office and play a critical role in helping Destination Tomorrow scale effectively while protecting the CEO’s time and attention. The ideal candidate is proactive, solutions\-focused, highly organized, resourceful, and thrives in dynamic environments where no two days are the same.

**Qualifications**

**Director of Operations** 

**Full\-Time \| On\-Site \| Asheville, NC** 

**Help Drive Our Mission Forward** 

At Working Wheels, we believe reliable transportation changes lives. Through our Vehicle Purchase Program and Vehicle Repair Program, we help hardworking individuals and families gain access to safe, dependable vehicles so they can get to work, school, medical appointments, and care for their families.

We're seeking an experienced, mission\-driven Director of Operations to help lead our organization into its next chapter. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys leading people, improving systems, making decisions, and finding practical solutions in a fast\-paced environment.

**About the Role** 

The Director of Operations provides day\-to\-day leadership for Working Wheels' operations, overseeing the office, automotive dealership, in\-house repair shop, and community programs. This role is responsible for the successful operation of the Vehicle Purchase Program, Vehicle Repair Program, and the sale of refurbished vehicles to the public.

The Director of Operations leads and supports a multidisciplinary team, fostering a collaborative, positive workplace culture. Direct reports include the Director of Vehicle Operations, who manages the daily operations of the repair shop; the Vehicle Repair Program Coordinator, who oversees the Vehicle Repair Program; the Vehicle Donation Coordinator, who manages the vehicle donation process; the Administrative Specialist, who provides administrative and operational support; and the HR/Finance Coordinator, who manages human resources and financial administration.

In addition to personnel leadership, the Director of Operations oversees the organization's financial systems, human resources functions, and operational infrastructure. As the primary administrator of the organization's technology platforms and data systems, this role ensures accurate reporting, supports grant compliance and program evaluation, and uses data to inform operational and strategic decision\-making. The Director of Operations also cultivates relationships with community partners to strengthen collaboration and expand the organization's impact.

**We're Looking for Someone Who...** 

● Is passionate about serving the community through nonprofit work.

● Leads with integrity, empathy, and accountability.

● Enjoys leading and developing people.

● Takes initiative and makes thoughtful, strategic decisions

● Looks for opportunities to improve processes and build effective systems.

● Communicates well and builds strong relationships with staff, program participants, volunteers, donors, and community partners.

● Can manage multiple priorities while staying organized.

● Brings a positive, solutions\-focused attitude to every challenge.

**Qualifications**

● Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

● Three or more years of operations management experience.

● Experience supervising and developing employees.

● Experience with budgeting, financial oversight, and organizational planning.

● Experience with SaaS (Software as a Service) for project management (e.g., Asana, monday.com)

● Strong organizational, communication, and problem\-solving skills.

● Experience with Google Workspace.

● Valid driver's license.

*Preferred* 

● Experience with and interest in automobiles.

● Nonprofit leadership experience.

● Experience with grant administration or reporting.

● 16 days of paid time off (PTO) during the first year of employment, increasing with tenure

● Paid Holidays including your birthday

● Retirement plan with a 3% employer contribution

● Short\-term disability coverage

● Access to voluntary dental, vision, critical illness, and accident insurance plans

● Opportunities for professional development and continued growth

**Why Asheville?** 

Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains, Asheville offers an incredible quality of life with endless opportunities for outdoor recreation, live music, local restaurants, and a vibrant arts community. It's a place where you can build a meaningful career while enjoying everything Western North Carolina has to offer.

Email one document containing your cover letter and resume to gillian@workingwheelswnc.org

Reporting to the Dean of the Divinity School, The Program Director provides academic leadership and

first doctoral\-level offering. This person sets the academic vision for the program in partnership with the

agency in Year 2, research methods and colloquy in Year 3, and dissertation research in Year 4\) is

designed for bi\-vocational adult learners.  

Because this is a launch\-phase program, the Director will also help build the infrastructure, faculty
  

bench, and external partnerships (e.g., with AI\-ethics centers and technical institutions) that the degree
  

will depend on for the next several admissions cycles.

* Provide overall academic leadership for the EdD program, including curriculum oversight,

 learning outcomes, and program review in coordination with the Dean and institutional
  

 accreditation requirements.

 relevant to theological education and AI ethics.

FT Faculty, PT\-Adjunct Faculty

 dissertations.

 and discrimination, accountability and transparency standards such as the NIST AI Risk
  

 Management Framework) sufficient to guide curriculum and faculty hiring, or a documented

**Campus Location:** Indianapolis Ed Center North, Indianapolis, IN



**Summary of Position:** The Executive Director of Workforce Engagement provides strategic leadership for the Department of Career Readiness and Workforce Launch within IWU National and Global. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Learner Success and Retention, this role is responsible for the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of a three\-pillar career launch system that transforms career preparation from a passive, transactional service into a lifecycle\-integrated, data\-driven intervention model. The Executive Director ensures that every IWU student graduates with a verified Human Capital Package and an active advocate working on their behalf in the regional labor market.



This position serves as the senior strategic leader for the department, overseeing a lean team of 1\.0 to 6\.0 FTE across three operational pillars: Career Clarity, Professional Development, and Market Advocacy. The Executive Director is the primary institutional liaison for the circular talent ecosystem, connecting employer intelligence from Regional Career Agents back to academic curriculum and enrollment strategy. The role operates at the intersection of student success, workforce development, and institutional advancement, requiring the ability to engage credibly at the C\-suite level with employer partners while maintaining deep alignment with IWU's mission of student flourishing.



This is a foundational leadership role in a newly approved, purpose\-built department. The individual selected will have the opportunity to design the model, build the team, and establish the operational infrastructure — not simply execute a pre\-existing system.  

Christian Commitment Requirement: In accordance with Indiana Wesleyan University's employment policy, all employees must possess a strong Christian commitment and adhere to the standards outlined in the IWU Community Lifestyle Statement.


**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership and Department Vision
	+ Lead the implementation and ongoing refinement of the Career Readiness and Workforce Launch model, ensuring alignment with IWU National and Global's enrollment, retention, and student success goals
	+ Develop and execute a 24\-month implementation roadmap, managing phase transitions from foundation to full\-scale operation with clear milestone accountability
	+ Establish and maintain the department's key performance indicator framework, including placement rates, employer satisfaction scores, Human Capital Package completion rates, and 90\-day graduate retention metrics
	+ Produce a termly Student Success Intelligence Brief that synthesizes workforce outcomes data for VP\-level and Board\-level audiences, translating complex placement and retention data into actionable institutional intelligence
	+ Represent the department in cross\-divisional governance structures, including the Digital Credential Wallet steering committee and the Partnership\-to\-Placement integration with the Enrollment Division
	+ Manage the department budget within approved parameters, applying data\-validated expansion triggers to authorize FTE growth from 4\.0 to 7\.0 as enrollment and caseload thresholds are reached
* Employer Partnership Development and Market Advocacy
	+ Cultivate and manage high\-value employer partnerships at the C\-suite and senior HR level, positioning IWU graduates as verified talent assets through the Human Capital Package framework
	+ Oversee the Regional Career Agent team's employer account portfolio, ensuring consistent relationship management across 15 to 30 active accounts per FTE
	+ Coordinate weekly with the Enrollment Division's Partnership Executive team to align on shared employer account management, relationship ownership protocols, and market intelligence sharing through Salesforce
	+ Provide monthly market intelligence briefs to the Vice President of Learner Success and Retention, summarizing employer workforce needs, hiring trends, and graduate performance data
	+ Lead the institution's participation in regional employer engagement events, workforce development convenings, and industry partnership initiatives across the Indianapolis, Chicago, and Cleveland hub markets
* Team Leadership and Pillar Oversight
	+ Provide direct supervision, coaching, and professional development for all three pillar roles — Career Clarity Specialists, Professional Development Specialists, and Regional Career Agents
	+ Establish and maintain standardized intervention protocols, caseload management practices, and documentation standards across all three pillars
	+ Monitor pillar\-level KPIs on a monthly basis, identifying performance gaps and implementing corrective action plans as needed
	+ Facilitate weekly team coordination meetings and bi\-weekly one\-on\-one supervision sessions with each direct report
	+ Lead the onboarding and training of all new department hires, ensuring alignment with the Human\-First AI philosophy and the Intervention Science framework that underpins the department's operating model
* Technology Infrastructure and AI Augmentation
	+ Oversee the department's AI\-augmented technology stack, including the Student Insights Agent, EdSights early alert integration, and Salesforce CRM workflows, ensuring tools are deployed to maximize human capacity for high\-stakes student interventions
	+ Lead the department's participation in the Digital Credential Wallet initiative, coordinating with Talent Studio, Academics, and Academic Record

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Operations

Brooklyn, New York | Hybrid

Compensation:
$175,000–$200,000, commensurate with experience, plus a performance-based bonus opportunity of up to 20% of base salary tied to agreed-upon individual and Firm performance objectives.

Help Build New York's Premier Boutique Business Litigation Firm

At Alisme Law, we believe exceptional legal service begins with exceptional operations.
We represent businesses, business owners, partners, and shareholders in complex business disputes. Our clients trust us because we make sense of complexity through disciplined systems, thoughtful strategy, and consistent execution.
As our Firm continues to grow, we are intentionally building an organization that is every bit as exceptional operationally as it is legally.
We are seeking an experienced Director of Operations to serve as the operational leader of our Firm. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys building teams, developing leaders, improving systems, and creating an organization where people consistently perform at a high level.
If you are energized by building organizations, not simply managing them, we would love to meet you.

Where We Are Going

Alisme Law has built a strong reputation for helping clients navigate complex business disputes. Our next chapter is focused on building a scalable organization capable of sustained growth while maintaining the personalized service, professionalism, and trust our clients expect.
Over the next several years, we will continue to strengthen our leadership team, refine our operating systems, and invest in our people so the Firm can grow intentionally without sacrificing its culture or client experience.
We are entering an exciting stage of growth. Our Firm has built a strong foundation and is now investing in the leadership, systems, and infrastructure necessary to support our next phase. The Director of Operations will inherit responsibility for leading our administrative team while helping build the management structure, operational processes, and organizational capacity needed for sustained growth.
We are looking for an operational leader who is excited to help build that future.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the Owner, you will lead the Firm's day-to-day business operations by developing people, strengthening accountability, improving systems, and ensuring operational excellence across the organization.
This is not an office manager position. It is a senior leadership role for someone who enjoys coaching people, improving organizations, solving operational challenges, and building high-performing teams.
While the Owner establishes the Firm's strategic direction, the Director of Operations is responsible for leading the execution of that vision through people, systems, and operational discipline.

Your First-Year Priorities

During your first year, your primary focus will be to build the operational foundation for the Firm's next stage of growth.

Build a High-Performing Team

Recruit, onboard, develop, and coach exceptional people. Create a culture where every team member understands expectations, receives regular feedback, and is held accountable to measurable standards.

Build a Scalable Operating Model

Strengthen the Firm's operating systems by documenting and improving core processes, implementing meaningful KPIs, establishing consistent meeting rhythms, and ensuring operational excellence across the organization.

Deliver an Exceptional Client Experience

Improve the operational systems that support the client journey, from intake through matter completion, by creating consistency, responsiveness, and professionalism at every stage.

What You Will Own

To accomplish these priorities, you will lead the Firm's business operations, including:
People Operations
Business Operations
Client Experience
Operational Finance
Technology and Vendor Management

Your success will be measured not by how much work you personally complete, but by how effectively the organization performs under your leadership.

Decision-Making Authority

We believe leadership requires both responsibility and authority.
Within established budgets, policies, and strategic objectives, you will have the authority to:

Lead, coach, evaluate, and hold administrative team members accountable while ensuring firm-wide compliance with the Firm's operational systems, policies, and performance standards.
Recommend hiring, promotions, compensation adjustments, and terminations.
Manage recruiting, onboarding, and performance management.
Improve and implement operational systems, workflows, and standard operating procedures.
Select and manage vendors and recommend technology solutions.
Establish and monitor operational KPIs and management reporting.
Resolve day-to-day operational issues independently.
Lead strategic operational initiatives from planning through implementation.

The Owner retains responsibility for legal strategy, client representation, annual budgeting, pricing, compensation strategy, and other major strategic decisions.

As you develop a deep understanding of the Firm, earn the Owner's trust, and build a strong operational foundation, the Owner intends to progressively delegate responsibility for the Firm's day-to-day operations. The long-term vision is for the Director of Operations to lead the Firm's business operations, allowing the Owner to focus primarily on legal strategy, client relationships, business development, and the Firm's long-term growth.

Operational Financial Leadership

You will oversee the Firm's operational financial processes by ensuring disciplined billing, timekeeping, collections, trust replenishment, operational reporting, and KPI management.
You will partner closely with the Owner and the Firm's outside accounting professionals on budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and business planning. While you will play an important role in supporting the Firm's financial health, responsibility for financial strategy remains with the Owner.

Client Experience

The Director of Operations owns the systems and processes that support an exceptional client experience. This includes intake, onboarding, communication standards, service workflows, billing experience, and client feedback systems.
You will work in partnership with the Owner to continuously improve the client experience while recognizing that legal strategy and attorney-client representation remain the responsibility of the Firm's attorneys.

The Director is responsible for establishing, monitoring, and improving the Firm's operational standards across all personnel. Attorneys remain responsible for legal judgment and client representation, while the Director oversees compliance with the Firm's operational systems and procedures.

What Success Looks Like After 12 Months

A successful first year will include meaningful progress in the following areas:

Leadership & People

A structured recruiting, onboarding, and performance management process is fully implemented.
Every employee has clear expectations, measurable KPIs, and regular coaching.
Leadership capacity is strengthened by developing team members, establishing clear accountability, and ensuring operational issues are addressed at the appropriate level within the organization.

Operations

Core operational workflows are documented, standardized, and consistently followed.
A meaningful operational KPI dashboard is implemented and reviewed regularly.
Weekly leadership meetings and quarterly planning sessions operate with consistency, accountability, and follow-through.
Operational decisions are supported by accurate reporting and meaningful performance data.

Client Experience

Client communication standards are consistently met.
Intake, onboarding, billing, and matter completion processes become more predictable and efficient.
Client feedback is actively measured and used to improve service delivery.

Business Operations

Billing, collections, and operational reporting processes operate consistently and efficiently.
Operational technology supports productivity and continuous improvement.
The Firm's leadership team has greater visibility into performance and operational trends through consistent reporting and accountability.

Compensation & Benefits

We believe exceptional performance should be rewarded. Our compensation package includes:

Competitive base salary of $175,000–$200,000, commensurate with experience.
Performance-based bonus opportunity of up to 20% of base salary, tied to agreed-upon individual and Firm performance objectives.
Hybrid work environment. During onboarding, the Director is expected to work primarily from our Brooklyn office to build relationships, learn the Firm, and understand our operations. Thereafter, we anticipate a flexible hybrid schedule with regular in-office leadership presence, generally one to two days per week, depending on business needs and Firm priorities. Additional in-person time may be expected during key hiring, planning, training, and leadership initiatives.
Paid Time Off and paid holidays.
Professional development opportunities.
The opportunity to help shape the future of a growing law firm.

Our Hiring Process

We hire carefully because our people are our greatest competitive advantage.
To apply please email the following to info@alismelaw.com
:
Your résumé.
A brief email explaining why this opportunity interests you.
A video (no longer than three minutes) answering the following questions:
Why does this opportunity excite you?
Tell us about an operational transformation you personally led that had a measurable impact.

Please include the phrase "Systems Create Freedom" in the subject line of your application.
Because attention to detail, communication, and follow-through are essential to success in this role, applicants who submit complete application materials and follow the requested instructions will receive priority consideration.

Please do not contact the Firm by telephone or visit our office regarding this position.

We proudly serve more than 7,000 residents throughout Florida, offering an active lifestyle paired with a full continuum of exceptional care — including independent living, assisted living, memory support, skilled nursing and rehabilitation, home care, pharmacy services, and affordable housing for low-income seniors. Join a team where you can make life great for residents and team members alike!

Resilient and adaptable under pressure, with the ability to navigate the mental and emotional demands of a dynamic senior living leadership role
Genuine passion for the aging services mission and improving the lived experience of older adults

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to lead with purpose — shaping a community where residents feel valued, supported, and at home, and where staff are equipped to do their best work. Centro de Trabajadores Unidos en Lucha (CTUL) is a worker-led organization where workers organize, educate, and empower each other to fight for a voice in their workplaces and in their communities. CTUL is seeking an experienced Deputy Director to oversee the organization’s organizational development, governance, personnel management and strategic planning. The Deputy Director will be a leader and a change agent in driving best practices in support of the organization’s mission. This role will be an advocate for staff experience, organizational agility and creating a learning culture. The Deputy Director will have deep experience with operational best practices and up-to-date online tools.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a manager with outstanding people skills and a proven track record of leadership and effective change management. They will join a successful mission-driven advocacy organization and help lead it to become even more efficient, impactful and nimble.

This position reports to the Executive Director.

What you’ll do

Strategy, Vision and Leadership:

Contribute to the development of CTUL’s strategic goals and objectives as part of the leadership team, and help guide the overall management of the organization.
In support of the CTUL’s  mission, promote a culture of high performance and continuous improvement that values learning, feedback and a commitment to quality throughout the organization.
Provide analytical support to CTUL management and staff including development of internal reporting capabilities.
Maintain a continuous line of communication with the Executive Director to support strategic decision-making on all critical issues.
Report to the board of directors on organizational performance metrics as needed by the Executive Director.

Team Development and Personnel Management

Oversee staff recruitment and hiring.
Managing leads and staff meeting planning and facilitation
Support the ED in the planning and facilitation of director meetings 
Oversee/Provide guidance on informal coaching conversations, corrective action, and progressive discipline
Support conflict resolution and workplace investigations as needed
Oversee best practices for terminations and approve terminations 
Create, update and execute organizational policies across the organization; and ensure that all systems that support CTUL staff are efficient, easily accessible and transparent.
In support of the CTUL’s mission, promote a culture of growth and continuous improvement that prioritizes learning, feedback and a commitment to innovation throughout the organization.
Oversee staff training and practice to build an inclusive, supportive organizational culture where everyone on the team feels valued and can thrive.
Represent CTUL management with the staff union, and cultivate a collegial, problem-solving relationship with the union based on partnership and trust.

Governance 

Support the Executive Director in maintaining robust organizational governance for CTUL’s member-led board of directors; provide staff leadership to Board committees; ensure compliance with nonprofit governance best practices; and support the Board as needed with training and capacity building.
Act as a key staff liaison to the Board of Directors, translating strategic vision into operational reality while ensuring all programs and fiscal activities remain in compliance with the highest legal and ethical standards.

Legal

Manage legal needs for CTUL, working with outside counsel as required.

Qualifications:

10 years experience in a similar position, or equivalent combination of education and experience
Proven track record of success leading organizational change and development within a growing organization
Superior personnel management ability, with strong mentoring and coaching experience on teams with diverse levels of expertise. Experience managing in organizations with unionized staff preferred.
Strong working knowledge of Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBA) and labor law principles
Excellent judgment and creative problem solving skills including the ability to lead a range of stakeholders in establishing a shared vision and executing it together
Entrepreneurial, flexible team player who can think experimentally and can take a learning approach to our work. 
Organized, detail-oriented and experienced in managing complex projects
Exceptional written, oral, interpersonal, and presentation skills and the ability to effectively interface with management, boards of directors, and staff
Passion for racial justice and for CTUL’s mission
Ability to periodically work on weekends and evenings, as needed.
Confidentiality, integrity, and a sense of humor.

CTUL has a tiered salary range set by the Staff and Board based on the principles of economic justice and inclusion. This salaried position is currently compensated at  $87,550 per year. This full-time position will normally work 80  hours per pay period, including some work on evenings and weekends. Submit a resume and cover letter to karina@ctul.net using the subject line “CTUL
Deputy Director

jobs.description:
Chief Executive Officer

Location: San Antonio, TX (relocation supported) · National travel Reports to: Board of Directors Type: Full-time, executive Compensation: Up to $2,000,000+ base, plus significant equity

The vision

We are building the first national brand in pediatric medical day care — a platform of hundreds of Prescribed Pediatric Extended Care Centers across the United States.

Today there are roughly 180 licensed centers in the entire country, operating in 15 states. Texas alone has the demand to support more than 40. Extrapolated across the states that already have a benefit, the category should be a thousand centers or more. It has stayed small because reimbursement policy suppressed it, not because families didn't need it — and that constraint is now being removed state by state.

Nobody has built the national brand. The category is still single sites and small regional operators — no consistent standard of care, no recognized name, no platform at scale.

That is what we intend to be. Hundreds of centers, one brand, one clinical standard, one operating model — and the real estate underneath all of it.

About the opportunity

A Prescribed Pediatric Extended Care Center (PPECC) is a licensed medical day center for children with complex medical needs — ventilator dependence, tracheostomies, feeding tubes, seizure protocols. Skilled pediatric nursing, on-site therapy, developmental programming and supervised transport, reimbursed by Medicaid. It costs the state less than extended hospitalization and less than round-the-clock home nursing, and it allows a parent who left the workforce to return to it.

Our capital structure, real estate strategy and site pipeline are in place. Our first center is in development in a fully built out building in San Antonio with the potential to build additional centers on the same land. We are hiring the CEO who will open it, prove the model, and scale it nationally.
This is a pre-launch role. No centers are currently operating. The person who takes this seat builds the platform from the first location.
How this is structured — and what we already have

Our board is led by a former Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — direct experience with how federal coverage policy is made, in a category defined by it.

The platform operates as two companies. A property company owns the real estate under every center. An operating company runs the clinical business and leases from it. Both accrue to the same ownership group.
The real estate side is solved. Our partner on the property company manages approximately $500 million in assets under management, with deep development and property management experience directly relevant to this asset class. They handle site acquisition, entitlement, ground-up development, construction management, financing and property management across the portfolio. Not a gap we are hiring against — though if you have this expertise, it's a plus.

The operating side is what we are hiring for. Licensure, clinical leadership, staffing, referral development, revenue cycle, census, quality, and the multi-site playbook that turns one center into hundreds. This role owns it.

A CEO who can operate across both is ideal — someone who understands how site selection drives census, how the lease supports the capital stack, and how the real estate compounds alongside the operating business. But we are hiring for operating depth first. We will not trade clinical and multi-site operating excellence for real estate fluency, because we already have the second.

Must-have skills
Non-negotiable. A candidate strong across these is one we want to speak with, whatever their title.
De novo site opening in a licensed healthcare setting. You have personally taken facilities from licensure application through architectural plan review, life safety inspection and state survey to first patient day. Not overseen a footprint someone else built — opened them. You know where the schedule slips and what it costs.
Clinical workforce building in a shortage market. Pediatric nursing supply is the binding constraint — not capital, not real estate, not demand. You have built a nursing pipeline, hired and retained qualified clinical directors, managed turnover in a competitive labor market, and know your own retention numbers without having to look them up.
Regulatory, licensure and survey command. You have owned the relationship with a state licensing authority. You have been through inspections, received deficiencies, written and executed plans of correction, and built compliance infrastructure that holds up across multiple sites and eventually multiple states.
Government-payer revenue cycle. You have carried a P&L that was predominantly Medicaid or Medicare. You understand managed care contracting, prior authorization, medical necessity documentation, denial management and appeals — and you understand that in this category the denial rate is a leadership metric, not a billing metric.
Census and referral development. You have built demand from zero. You know how to earn the confidence of hospital discharge planners, complex-care physicians and specialty clinics, and you know these relationships are personal, slow to build, and the largest determinant of whether a center reaches breakeven on schedule.
Multi-site scaling — not multi-site management. You have taken an operating model from one location to many and know precisely what breaks between site three and site ten. You have built the centralized layer — billing, EMR, HR, compliance, quality — that makes unit economics improve with scale rather than degrade.
Full P&L ownership and unit economics fluency. You can speak to census ramp curves, contribution margin per patient, breakeven census and the working capital a ramp consumes. You have made the call on when a location is underperforming and what to do about it.
Executive team building. You have hired the people who ran your sites and your functions, and you can name both the hires that worked and the ones that didn't.
Clinical quality and risk in a medically fragile population. These are children on ventilators and feeding tubes. You bring genuine seriousness about clinical governance, incident management and family trust, and you understand that a single serious event can end a brand.

Ideal additions

Not required — what makes a candidate exceptional rather than merely qualified.
Real estate literacy. Site selection against demand and drive-time catchment, lease structuring, an understanding of how an operating tenant's credit supports property financing, and the ability to work as a peer with the property company rather than a tenant of it.
Prior CEO, board or chairman experience — or a clear appetite for it.
Multi-state licensure experience, including entering a state with no prior footprint.
M&A and integration. Acquiring regional operators will be part of the national build.
Pediatric or medically complex population experience.
Policy and payer engagement at state level.

Note on title. Prior CEO experience is not required. Some of the strongest platform builders were the second or third in command — the COO who opened the sites, the CFO whose model made scaling survivable, the commercial leader who filled them. If you did the building and someone else held the title, you are exactly who we want to hear from — and if you held the CEO title, that works too.

Compensation and equity
Base salary — up to $2,000,000+, commensurate with experience and track record. We are prepared to pay at the top of the market for the right operator.
Annual performance bonus of 50–100% of base, tied to centers opened, census performance, survey outcomes and clinical quality.

Significant equity — in both companies. The CEO participates in the operating company and the property company.

Operating company equity. A meaningful founder-level ownership position, not a management-pool allocation.

Property company participation. A direct stake in the real estate portfolio. Every center is owned rather than leased, and across hundreds of locations that portfolio becomes an asset base in its own right. Operating executives are rarely offered a position in the real estate they generate the credit for. This one is.
Stock option grants available in addition to direct equity, with strike set at current valuation ahead of the first center opening.

Vesting over four to five years, milestone-weighted to centers opened and stabilized.
Acceleration on change of control.

Benefits. Full medical, dental and vision · relocation assistance · executive severance · change-of-control protections.

We would rather pay in ownership than in salary — and we are prepared to do both.

What you will do

Phase one — prove it
Take the launch center from licensure application through Life Safety Code survey to first patient day
Recruit and lead the clinical leadership team, including the nursing director required for licensure
Build referral relationships with children's hospitals, discharge planning, complex-care pediatrics and home health agencies
Establish billing, prior authorization and denial management operations with Medicaid managed care organizations
Drive census from opening to stabilization

Phase two — make it repeatable
Convert the launch center into a documented, transferable opening playbook
Open and stabilize centers.
Build the centralized services layer so that unit economics improve rather than degrade with scale
Recruit and lead the executive team

Phase three — build the brand
Lead multi-state expansion, including acquisition of regional operators where that is the faster path
Establish the clinical standard and brand identity that defines the category nationally
Own the full P&L and report to the board

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants receive consideration without regard to any protected characteristic.

KLR Executive Search Group is proud to partner with a premier New England full-service law firm to identify an experienced Chief Operating Officer (COO) to lead daily business operations and administrative functions. Based in New Hampshire, with additional offices across New Hampshire and Massachusetts, the firm has built a strong regional reputation and continues to expand its presence across key markets. The COO will work closely with firm leadership to strengthen operational infrastructure, improve systems and processes, enhance financial reporting and business analytics, support technology implementation, and drive cross-office alignment. This is a key leadership opportunity created by the planned retirement of the firm’s current CEO/Executive Director. Ideal candidates will bring strong operational leadership experience within a law firm, professional services firm, or similarly complex organization, along with the ability to manage change, build consensus, and support continued financial success and growth.

Core Responsibilities
:
Operational Leadership

Oversee firm-wide daily operations across all offices, ensuring coordination, communication, consistency, and alignment across the firm’s New England footprint.
Serve as a strategic partner to firm leadership, practice group leaders, department heads, and administrative teams on operational priorities, staffing, resources, and growth initiatives.
Lead administrative infrastructure across Finance, HR, IT, Facilities, Operations, and related business functions while supporting succession planning, recruiting, retention, compensation, and a collaborative team-first culture.

Technology & Process Innovation

Lead business process optimization initiatives across departments and offices, improving workflows, documentation, internal coordination, service delivery, and overall efficiency.
Support the implementation and optimization of accounting systems, HRIS tools, AI solutions, and other technologies while partnering with IT, Finance, HR, and administrative leaders to strengthen systems integration, data quality, reporting, and best practices.

Financial Management and Resource Allocation

Partner with Finance and firm leadership to strengthen financial reporting, business analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and performance tracking.
Use financial and operational data to support informed decision-making across staffing, systems, infrastructure, real estate, and office planning.
Align resources with short-, mid-, and long-term operational goals while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, manage costs, and support thoughtful investment.

Risk and Compliance

Support firm leadership in maintaining clear policies, consistent procedures, sound administrative practices, and strong internal controls across offices and departments.
Partner with Finance, HR, IT, and other leaders to identify operational risks and implement practical solutions, ensuring new systems and processes are rolled out with appropriate attention to compliance, training, change management, transparency, and accountability.

Qualifications :

Executive operational leadership experience within a complex organization, ideally a law firm, professional services firm, or comparable business environment.
Experience overseeing or partnering with Finance, HR, IT, Facilities, Operations, and other administrative functions.
Proven ability to lead operational improvements, systems implementations, process optimization, change management, financial analysis, and business reporting initiatives.
Strong communication, relationship-building, and leadership skills, with the ability to earn credibility in a consensus-driven, team-first environment.
This role is based in New Hampshire
, with oversight across multiple offices in New Hampshire and Massachusetts. Local or relocation candidates are preferred.
