Position Highlights The University of Arizona seeks a strategic and experienced leader to serve as its Executive Director of the Academic Financial Office. In this pivotal role, you work in close collaboration with the Chief Financial Officer, the Chief Budget \& Fiscal Management Officer, the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Provost, and the Deans, providing financial oversight for all 20 colleges of the University. Your responsibilities directly support the University's core academic mission, initiatives focused on student success, academic affairs, faculty and staff excellence, research, and key strategic objectives.
  
  

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), you will be a vital member of both the CFO and the Provost's administrative leadership teams. Your expertise will be instrumental in developing and implementing financial strategies for the near and long\-term, directly contributing to the University's overall academic and strategic achievements. Success in this role requires a comprehensive understanding of finance, outstanding management capabilities, and a versatile professional background relevant to the nuanced financial landscape of an R1 university's central academic administration.
  
  

As the Executive Director of the Academic Financial Office, you will have significant autonomy in designing and implementing a new model for financial operations of the colleges, which will be aligned with the University’s new budget model (Arizona Forward), eventually building and leading a team of finance professionals. You will foster a collaborative and customer\-focused environment while ensuring financial goals and daily operations are aligned with CFO and Provost's vision for academic excellence and student success.
  
  

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
  
  

Outstanding U of A benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance plans; life insurance and disability programs; paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays; U of A/ASU/NAU tuition reduction for the employee and qualified family members; retirement plans; access to U of A recreation and cultural activities; and more!
  
  

The University of Arizona has been recognized for our innovative work\-life programs.
  
  

Duties \& Responsibilities
  
  

**Academic Financial Team Leadership:**  

Lead the transition from a distributed academic financial model to a new structure that is aligned with the university’s financial structures and strategic imperatives and is managed in the CFO’s office in collaboration with academic leadership.
  
Exercise direct, solid\-line supervisory authority over and performance management of approximately 20 leaders/managers, fostering a culture of accountability, professional growth, and "whole\-university" thinking that transcends individual unit interests.
  
Lead and inspire a distributed workforce of over 200 business and finance professionals by establishing clear standards for operational excellence, transparency, and ethical stewardship across all academic units.
  
Set the cultural tone, model the collaborative behavior needed, and align the technical functions of academic business administration with the university's academic and research mission, ensuring all team members understand how their fiscal roles directly support faculty and staff success and student outcomes.
  
Drive large\-scale cultural change by implementing consistent, equitable practices in hiring, workload distribution, and professional development across the academic portfolio, reducing "silo" behaviors and promoting cross\-unit collaboration.
  
With the support of the Office of Business Affairs and with University Communications, design and execute a comprehensive internal communication strategy \- including "all\-hands" interactions, functional working groups, and digital tool sets \- to ensure all members of the team remain informed, engaged, and aligned with the CFO and Provost's strategic priorities.
  
Continuously assess and adjust leadership roles and team structures to ensure optimal efficiency and effectiveness in achieving the financial and University\-wide goals.
  
  

**Strategic Financial Planning \& Execution:**  

Lead the development of a comprehensive suite of multi\-year financial models for the colleges supporting initiatives related to areas such as academic programs, faculty development, student success, optimization of academic revenue streams and the fiscal impact of enrollment fluctuations. Take a lead role in the change management necessary for success.
  
Partner with the Provost, CHRO, and Deans to model and manage the long\-term fiscal impact of faculty affairs, including the competitive structuring of start\-up packages, retention funding, tenure\-track line allocations, and instructional capacity planning across all 20 colleges.
  
Oversee the execution of innovative operational plans and systems for integrated financial operations and budgeting processes strategically aligning the administration of academics with the University's strategic goals.
  
Facilitate cross\-functional collaboration across the colleges and with other central administrative units to integrate financial efforts related to the CFO's responsibilities.
  
Proactively identify and fix the root causes of financial challenges and opportunities related to academic strategic priorities.
  
  

**Financial Evaluation \& Business Planning:**  

Oversee the preparation of business and operational plans, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of financial viability and strategic alignment.
  
Develop a standardized process for and conduct comprehensive financial due diligence for new programs and initiatives, ensuring a thorough examination of financial considerations.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Under general supervision of the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officer (“COO”) has a crucial role in driving operational excellence, ensuring the delivery of high\-quality healthcare services, and advancing WIHCC’s mission to provide accessible and compassionate care to the communities that WIHCC, Inc. serves. The COO is responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day operations, implementing strategic initiatives, and fostering collaboration among various departments to achieve organizational goals. Directs strategy development, planning, and administrative management of WIHCC, Inc. Establishes and maintains standards focusing on effective translation of strategy into operational objectives and specific, measurable goals and associated deliverables consistent with practice standards and requirements and which align/support overall mission, vision and values of WIHCC, Inc. Serves on the Executive Team. Maintains confidentiality of all privileged and sensitive information. Upholds the principles of WIHCC’s Vision, Mission, and Value Statements. Maintains confidentiality of all privileged information at all times.

*This list of duties and responsibilities is illustrative only of the tasks performed by this position and is not all\-inclusive.*




**Essential Duties \& Responsibilities:**

* Maintains regular attendance and punctuality.
* Collaborates with the CEO and other executive leaders to develop and execute strategic plans into actionable steps for growth and implementation that aligns with the WIHCC, Inc.’s mission and objectives.
* Provides guidance on operational initiatives to enhance efficiency, quality of care, and overall organizational effectiveness.
* Oversees WIHCC’s Inc. operations and employee productivity, building a highly inclusive culture that ensures team members can thrive and the organizational goals are met. ;
* Implements and monitors operational policies, procedures, standards of operations, and protocols to maintain compliance with industry standards and regulations.
* Integrates departments and services ensuring quality, accessible, and safe health care environment for patients and staff.
* Provides strategic leadership and oversight across all clinical and non\-clinical operations by identifying organizational priorities, advising executive leadership on strategic issues and opportunities, planning, implementing, and evaluating organizational goals, policies, and performance. Aligns operations with the organization's mission and strategic priorities while ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, fiscal stewardship, quality outcomes, and the effective management of programs, functions, services, activities, and resources.
* Addresses performance concerns promptly by implementing appropriate corrective actions while ensuring compliance with personnel policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
* Assures that the work environment for all supervised employees is fair, equitable and free of discrimination or harassment and practices and encourages exemplary customer services and cultural sensitivity.
* Provides executive leadership and operational planning with the CFO, CEO, ET, and BOD to develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate organizational budgets, financial forecasts, and resource allocation strategies that support strategic priorities and long\-term sustainability.
* Identifies and implements strategies to enhance organizational financial sustainability through cost optimization, revenue growth, and resource development initiatives while maintaining a strong commitment to high\-quality patient care and mission\-driven outcomes.
* Collaborates with Indian Health Service, P.L.93\-638 organizations, tribal health departments, federal, states, counties and community health and social service agencies to achieve goals and objectives of WIHCC, Inc.; orients and trains staff of such agencies as required.
* Works with CEO to meet goals and objectives established under WIHCC, Inc.’s Strategic Plan and develop, implement criteria/measurable standards to monitor and improve programs, organizational performance and provides consultative suggestions/advisements in line with Joint Commission (JC); to include Critical Access Hospital (CAH), and Centers for Medicare \& Medicaid Services (CMS) references.
* Prepares and presents various reports to Executive Team, Board of Directors, 638 Association and Navajo Nation Oversight Committee, (e.g. HEHSC, RDC, etc.).
* Adheres to JC elements of performance, HIPPA and Privacy Act and organization policy and procedures.
* Requires completion of tasks or duties assigned by a supervisor.
* Upholds all principles of confidentiality and patient care to the fullest extent.
* Adheres to all professional and ethical behavior standards of the healthcare industry.
* Adheres to WIHCC, Inc.’s Personnel Policies and Procedures, departmental policies, rules, and regulations.
* Interacts in an honest, trustworthy and dependable manner with patients, employees, visitors, and vendors.
* Possesses cultural awareness and sensitivity.
* Maintains compliance with all Human Resources requirements.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**


Master’s degree in Business Administration, Health Care Administration, Public Administration, or closely related field. Five or more years of progressive executive leadership experience in a healthcare administration with an executive leadership role including responsibilities for development and implementation of strategic programs, functions, services, activities, policies and practices. In addition, in support of understanding of advanced business planning and regulatory issues covering overall operational mission, goals and objectives. Proven success in leading and implementing strategic initiatives within a healthcare setting.


Bilingual skills in English and Navajo language preferred. Must maintain a valid unrestricted and insurable driver’s license.

jobs.title: Assistant Director of Institutional Giving
jobs.description:
**Assistant Director of Individual Giving**

**Reports to:** Director of Development

 **Functional Area:** Advancement Department

 **FLSA Status:** Exempt

 **Job Location:** Ward 5

 **Employment Type:** Full\-Time

 **Classification:** Manager

 **Direct Reports:** 1 (Individual Giving Specialist)

  



  

**POSITION OVERVIEW**


The Assistant Director of Individual Giving plays a central role in growing and diversifying Academy of Hope's (AoH) revenue base by building a strong, sustainable individual giving program. This role is especially important as AoH strengthens the day\-to\-day systems that support consistent donor engagement and stewardship.


Reporting to the Director of Development, the Assistant Director of Individual Giving will develop and implement AoH's individual giving strategy and annual plan — in partnership with, and subject to approval by, the Director of Development — manage performance against goals, and maintain a disciplined moves\-management and stewardship cadence in Salesforce CRM.


The Assistant Director will directly supervise and coach the Individual Giving Specialist, oversee the Annual Fund strategy and results, and oversee donor engagement event logistics.


This role also partners closely with the Director of Development and Chief Growth Officer — providing donor data, portfolio analysis, and prospect research that inform prioritization decisions and help prepare AoH leadership for high\-impact donor engagements. The ideal candidate brings an entrepreneurial mindset: someone who can build systems and processes that don't yet exist, test and refine approaches, and help AoH grow individual giving in a way that is measurable, repeatable, and sustainable.

**A. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Individual Giving Strategy, Pipeline Growth \& Moves Management** *(35%)*

* Develop and implement AoH's Individual Giving Plan (annual fund through leadership\-level gifts), in partnership with and subject to approval by the Director of Development, aligned with AoH's strategic priorities and revenue\-diversification goals.
* Establish and maintain a practical moves\-management cadence (e.g., weekly next\-step review, monthly portfolio refresh, quarterly pipeline health check) that drives measurable movement and reduces stalled relationships.
* Partner with the Director of Development to identify, qualify, and cultivate high\-capacity prospects, and support portfolio strategy and donor\-movement decisions.
* Track performance and pipeline health using Salesforce dashboards and regular reporting (pipeline value, donor movement, retention, attrition, upgrades, solicitations, and outcomes by segment).
* Maintain consistent processes and data standards in Salesforce so individual giving data is reliable for forecasting, decision\-making, and leadership reporting.
* Manage a personal portfolio of donors and prospects with giving potential up to $25,000, using clear moves management (stages, next steps, timelines) to advance relationships over time.
* Drive AoH's leadership annual giving program (the tier just below major gifts), including segmentation, cultivation, stewardship, and annual targets, in coordination with the Director of Development.
* Participate directly in solicitations for the leadership annual giving and mid\-level tiers, including strategy prep, donor meetings, proposal\-drafting support, follow\-up, and documenting outcomes in Salesforce within agreed\-upon timelines.

**Mid\-Level Giving \& Donor Relationship Management** *(20%)*

* Oversee a portfolio of mid\-level donors ($1,000–$9,999\), partnering with the Individual Giving Specialist on day\-to\-day cultivation and stewardship execution while retaining accountability for strategy, segmentation, and upgrade identification.
* Support the Director of Development in preparing senior leadership and board members for donor engagement and solicitation by developing donor and prospect briefing materials tailored to the meeting purpose (cultivation, stewardship, renewal, upgrade, or ask).
* Build and maintain meeting\-prep toolkits for donor visits (contact history, giving/engagement summary, affinity and interests, proposed talking points, "the ask," roles in the meeting, and next steps).
* In partnership with the Director of Development, develop board toolkits to strengthen annual fund execution and donor stewardship (call scripts, email templates, segmented call lists, talking points, and tracking instructions).
* Ensure donor experiences are consistent, personal, and aligned with AoH's mission and culture.

**Annual Fund Oversight** *(20%)*

* Oversee and manage the Annual Fund program, including strategy, calendar, segmentation, and performance tracking across direct mail, email, digital, and stewardship.
* Ensure campaign execution is consistent and measurable (e.g., Giving Tuesday, end\-of\-year, back\-to\-school, and spring campaign).
* Draft and coordinate annual fund messaging and stewardship communications to ensure alignment, tone, and outcomes\-based storytelling, with final approval from the Director of Development.

**Donor Engagement Events \& Cultivation Moments** *(10%)*

* Oversee donor engagement opportunities that strengthen relationships and move donors toward deeper investment (small cultivation gatherings, site visits, graduation touchpoints, and tailored experiences).
* Partner with internal teams to build authentic engagement moments tied to AoH programs and strategic priorities.
* Ensure every event has a defined fundraising purpose (stewardship, upgrade, prospecting, or cultivation) and a clear follow\-up plan in Salesforce (attendance logged, portfolio routed, next step set within a defined timeframe).

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development - Lewis Katz School of Medicine
jobs.description:
**Temple University's Lewis Katz School of Medicine is searching for a Sr. Director of Development!**

**Salary Range: $125,000\-$135,000**  

A variety of important factors are reviewed by HR when considering salary, including job duties, the applicant’s education and experience, all relevant internal equity considerations, department budget, and funding source.


Become a part of the Temple family and you will have access to the following:  

**Full medical, dental, vision coverage**  

**Paid time off**  

**9 Federally Observed Paid Holidays**  

**3 Personal Days**  

**Tuition remission \- eligible employees and their dependents can obtain a degree TUITION FREE**  

**A generous retirement plan and so much more!**

**Position Summary:**  

The Temple Health Sciences Campus is seeking an entrepreneurial, motivated and results\-driven professional with proven experience in cultivating, securing and stewarding major and principal level gifts to join our high\-achieving team as Sr. Director of Development (SDOD), Lewis Katz School of Medicine (School) at Temple University and working in conjunction with (Podiatry, Pharmacy and Dentistry) to help fundraise towards Temple University’s upcoming capital campaign. This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished major/principal gifts officer to lead and manage a team of frontline fundraisers and partner with School leadership, advancement colleagues and stakeholders across the School, University and Temple University Hospital (TUH) to fuel medical education, scientific research, patient care and service to the community with impactful philanthropy. Come join a vibrant world\-class academic R1 research institution on the ground floor of what will be a historic comprehensive campaign.


The SDOD must be a highly energetic, driven, organized, intellectually curious and enthusiastic individual with a track record of building relationships, establishing trust and facilitating meaningful donor\-centric giving opportunities and partnerships. The successful candidate will work collaboratively and strategically, demonstrate good judgment, and evidence a strong application of principles, ethics and best practices of successful fundraising in a complex organization.


Founded in 1901 as Pennsylvania’s first co\-educational medical school, the Lewis Katz School of Medicine has earned a national reputation for training outstanding clinicians and biomedical scientists, attracting students, faculty, and staff committed to improving lives. The School and TUH, its chief clinical training site, provide care for patients from the region and beyond seeking advanced tertiary\- and quaternary\-level care. TUH also serves the local community, one of the most vulnerable populations in the nation, providing more free and under\-reimbursed care than any other hospital in the state.


The Temple Health Sciences Campus strives to maintain a culture of diversity and inclusion, a collaborative team\-based culture that values innovation and creativity, and a commitment to leadership opportunities, professional development and a healthy work culture.

**Job Details:**  

* This position requires a background check for cash handling responsibilities.
**Required Education and Experience:**  

* Bachelor’s degree and at least 7 years of progressively responsible higher education and/or healthcare fundraising experience with a proven track record of closing six to seven figure gifts. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
**Required Skills and Abilities:**  

* Proven experience and success in strategizing and leading the solicitation of major and principal level gifts
* Knowledge of, and experience with, both the art and science of major gift fundraising
* Demonstrated ability to raise and close major and principal level gifts (including current use, endowed and estate gifts)
* Demonstrated track record of fundraising success in a fast\-paced, large organizational structure
* Must possess the negotiation, interpersonal and networking skills necessary for building relationships with external and internal constituents
* Demonstrated success in collaborating with senior management, school leadership, clinicians, faculty and staff
* Proven ability to engage and interact effectively with diverse constituents and serve as a charismatic ambassador

**MISISON STATEMENT**


The Fiesta® San Antonio Commission Inc. is a nonprofit, volunteer, self\-supporting organization that plans, promotes, coordinates, and preserves Fiesta® San Antonio through support of its Participating Member Organizations in presenting a safe, educational, annual celebration of the diverse heritage, culture and spirit of San Antonio for its residents and visitors.  



**WHAT IS FIESTA® SAN ANTONIO**


Fiesta® San Antonio started in 1891 as a one\-parade event to honor the memory of the heroes of the Alamo and the Battle of San Jacinto. That historic commemoration still takes place, but for more than a century, Fiesta® has grown into a celebration of San Antonio’s rich and diverse cultures and today is one of this nation’s premier festivals with an economic impact of more than $340 million.  



Each year, more than one hundred San Antonio Area Non\-Profit, Fiesta Member Organizations coordinate more than one hundred Official Fiesta® Events to raise funds to provide services to San Antonio citizens throughout the year.



The Fiesta San Antonio Commission’s purpose is to help each of its Member Organizations be as successful as they can be.



The Fiesta San Antonio Commission proudly supports Fiesta Member Organizations that support:


* Higher Education Scholarships and Programs
* Diverse Cultures
* Historical Significance / The Alamo
* Arts / Nature
* Military Programs
* Children’s Events / Programs
* Pets / Animal Welfare
* Inclusive Events / LGBTQ
* Sports / Health and Wellness
* Special Needs Community
* Older Adult Community
* Local Community Building


**POSITION SUMMARY**


The Director of Development leads a comprehensive fundraising strategy in support of Fiesta San Antonio, one of the nation’s premier cultural celebrations. This role is responsible for generating revenue through emerging philanthropic initiatives, major gifts, grants, and corporate sponsorships, while building long\-term sustainability through planned giving and capital campaign development.  



Working closely with the Executive Director, Executive Committee, Board of Directors and the Development Committee, the Director of Development will drive strategies that strengthen revenue, deepen partnerships, and position the Commission for future growth.

* Planned Giving \& Long\-Term Philanthropy


* Develop and launch a planned giving program to support long\-term sustainability
* Create opportunities for legacy and estate giving, including donor education and recognition
* Integrate planned giving into overall donor engagement and stewardship strategies


* Capital Campaign Development


* Support the planning and early development of a capital campaign or major fundraising initiative
* Build a pipeline of leadership\-level donors and prospects
* Partner with leadership and board members to advance campaign strategy and readiness


* Relationship Management


* Manage a portfolio of donors, prospects and sponsors
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward high\-level relationships
* Create customized engagement opportunities aligned with donor and sponsor interests


* Membership Integration \& Growth


* Evaluate how fundraising efforts can support and enhance Membership growth and engagement
* Develop strategies to better integrate fundraising and membership pathways
* Identify opportunities to convert members into donors and sponsors into long\-term partners


* Event \& Community Engagement


* Lead fundraising efforts tied to Fiesta events
* Represent the Commission at events, sponsor activities, and community functions
* Partner with member organizations to align fundraising and engagement opportunities


* Board \& Leadership Collaboration


* Work with the Development Committee Volunteers to create fundraising goals and strategies
* Engage Board members in fundraising strategy, donor introductions, and campaign development

jobs.description:
**Mission Statement**



Regis High School transforms Catholic young men into leaders devoted to Deo et Patriae and lifelong service as Men for Others. Merit based and committed to families with financial need, Regis provides an academically exceptional, tuition\-free Jesuit education within a caring community.


**Position**



Senior Director of Advancement Operations and Strategy will have the extraordinary opportunity to work with approximately 530 exceptional, gifted young men, talented faculty, and committed staff. Located in New York City, Regis High School is a Catholic, Jesuit, college preparatory school and the only Jesuit, full\-scholarship high school in the country. The school was founded in 1914 through the extraordinary generosity of an anonymous woman and her family. Regis now relies on philanthropy of alumni, parents, and friends as its most significant source of financial support. Regis is committed to both academic excellence and fostering a spirit of generosity and service to those in need. Regis seeks to inspire and educate the ethnically diverse young men in its care to become imaginative Catholic leaders committed to promoting justice and exerting leadership in the Church, in their civic community, and in their future chosen profession.


**Position Summary**



Regis High School is investing in the continued growth of its philanthropic program, and the Senior Director of Advancement Operations and Strategy is a newly created role at the center of that investment. Reporting to the Vice President for Advancement and serving as a key member of the Advancement team, the Senior Director acts as the Vice President's principal operating partner, responsible for the systems, processes, and cross\-functional coordination that enable a growing fundraising program to run smoothly and scale effectively.



This is an opportunity for an experienced advancement operations professional to play a foundational, highly visible role in shaping how a respected and growing development program is run, partnering closely with colleagues across Advancement, Communications, and Finance, and helping to prepare the institution for its next growth chapter.



Direct reports include the Associate Director of Alumni Engagement, Director of Communications, Events Manager, Advancement Database \& Gift Coordinator, and Administrative Assistant, along with the department's outsourced database services partner, Blackbaud Managed Services.

* Provide day\-to\-day operational leadership across the Advancement department, partnering closely with colleagues in Development, Communications, and Finance to ensure smooth, coordinated execution of departmental goals.


* Directly supervise the Associate Director of Alumni Engagement, Director of Communications, Events Manager, Advancement Database \& Gift Coordinator, and Administrative Assistant, and oversee the department's relationship with its database services partner.


* Develop and lead onboarding, training, and ongoing professional development programming for Advancement.


**Data Management and Finance Partnership**

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer for Energy, Climate, and Environment #86640
jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom and belonging make it a special place for students, faculty and staff.

As a world-leading institution, Berkeley is known for its academic and research excellence, public mission, diverse student body, and commitment to equity and social justice. Since our founding in 1868, we have driven innovation, creating global intellectual, economic and social value.

We are looking for applicants who reflect California's diversity and want to be part of an inclusive, equity-focused community that views education as a matter of social justice. Please consider whether your values align with our Guiding Values and Principles, Principles of Community, and Strategic Plan.

At UC Berkeley, we believe that learning is a fundamental part of working, and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups (staff organizations). Our goal is for everyone on the Berkeley campus to feel supported and equipped to realize their full potential. We actively support this by providing all of our full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours (10 days) of paid time per year to engage in professional development activities. Find out more about how you can grow your career at UC Berkeley.

Departmental Overview

The University of California, Berkeley is a global leader in fundamental science, influential interdisciplinary research, and fostering technological and policy innovation. With a rich history of discovery and a commitment to creating both short-term and long-term societal benefit, UC Berkeley is uniquely positioned to tackle the most pressing challenges of our time, including the climate crisis and sustainability. Under the leadership of the Associate Provost for Energy, Climate, and Environment (AP-ECE), the Office of the AP-ECE will work collaboratively across campus and with external partners to promote research excellence, curricular innovation, community-engaged scholarship, and sustainable campus operations aligned with the university’s broader strategic goals to provide long-term societal benefit. The Office of the AP-ECE is an entrepreneurial experiment for the Berkeley campus to test the boundaries of what is possible to propel transformative energy, climate and environment scholarship as well as curricular innovation within Berkeley’s ecosystem of excellence.

The Chief Development Officer for the Office of Energy, Climate, and Environment is a senior advancement leader who designs, develops, and delivers fundraising programs that support the university’s broader strategic goals to provide long-term societal benefit. This position reports to the Associate Provost for Energy, Climate, and Environment (AP-ECE) and works across disciplines with academic and fundraising leaders to build relationships with new and existing individual prospects and foundations and create solicitation strategies based on donor capacity and interest.

This is an expert fundraising professional in the area of major and principal gifts. The role maintains a portfolio of donors and prospects and may oversee professional staff if funding allows. The position is expected to raise gift dollar amounts as established annually in collaboration with AP-ECE and University Development and Alumni Relations, at a minimum of $5M annually.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is June 19, 2026.

For the initial consideration period, please submit application materials by July 10, 2026. The position will be open until filled.

Responsibilities

Develop and manage a portfolio of approximately 40-60 prospects with the capacity to give $5 million or greater, and collaborate with colleagues to advance with a particular focus of those who may give $10 million+. Qualify major gift prospects and solicit gifts directly.
Ensure that predetermined fundraising goals are met and raise at least $5M annually through individual and collaborative fundraising once the portfolio is established.
Build effective relationships across and beyond campus.
Serves as an expert development professional in the area of philanthropy and principal gifts, leading strategies that include highly complex gift discussions and interaction with donors capable of making significant contributions to the university.
Lead proactive collaborative efforts to develop effective and coordinated strategies for prospects shared by more than one academic unit; facilitate action plans and monitor implementation of strategies. Create and execute events and activities for cultivation, stewardship, and solicitations to advance gift conversations.
Drive and manage strategic, consistent, personalized engagement with donors, including meaningful interaction with academic leaders, faculty, and lead campus supporters and volunteers.
Prepare and present formal fundraising proposals to major and principal gift donors and prospects; or prepare senior campus leaders to present proposals.
Ensure that proposals are well crafted, drawing on support from in-house communications team and gaining sign-off from relevant academic leaders.
Ensure that gifts are well-stewarded, drawing on campus partners for appropriate, timely, and consistent recognition, and ensure that all appropriate reporting and documentation is undertaken.
Collaborate and partner with the AP-ECE as well as the VCRO, the Rausser College of Natural Resources, College of Engineering, College of Chemistry, the College of Letters & Science, Organized Research Units as well as other stakeholders to ensure forward momentum with this university-wide priority.
Establish annual fundraising goals and priorities and ensure effective strategy, implementation, and reporting of development activities.
Serve as a trusted advisor on prospect strategies and collaborations with faculty.

Required Qualifications

Substantial years (usually 8+) of high-level performance in principal and major gift fundraising.
Expert knowledge of all aspects of fundraising strategies, structuring complex gifts, donor relations, and advancement communications.
Successful track record in building strong professional relationships with major philanthropists, academic leaders, collaborating development professionals, and other key stakeholders (for ex: faculty and staff).
Relevant field experience, project/program management skills, organization, communication and interpersonal skills as well as strong writing skills.

Experience

Experience developing business relationships with C-level executives (CEOs, CFOs, Board of directors, etc.) and referral sources (attorneys, bankers, etc.), required
Prior experience working in professional services direct sales industry or in development role at financial services firms, including but not limited to experience with accounting firms, investment banking or private equity firms, personnel recruiting, business journals sales, financial consulting, business advisory services and/or banking industry, preferred

License/Certifications

N/A

Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Suite, required
Experience with client relationship management (CRM), required
Microsoft Dynamics, preferred

Knowledge in the development, management and execution of sales and BD planning, lead generation, pipeline management, account planning, sales strategy and development
Ability to understand compensation incentive plans and strive to achieve revenue goals
Able to understands Business Development (BD) metrics and strive to achieve them
Ability to thoughtfully and positively influence, lead, and manage change

Excellent project management skills

Excellent verbal and written communication as well as presentation skills
Ability to travel to participate in events or sales calls or attend regional or national meetings, as necessary

jobs.title: Associate Program Director, START
jobs.description:
Easterseals Southern California transforms lives every day. For over a century, Easterseals has championed inclusion and independence—delivering essential services like early childhood programs, autism services, employment and independent living support to more than 29,000 people each year. Through advocacy and education, we break barriers and create opportunities for the one-in-four Americans with disabilities.

Starting Salary: $81,900+/yr

Overview Of Position

Under limited supervision, provides clinical leadership, supervision, and support to the START (Systemic, Therapeutic, Assessment, Resource, and Treatment) team. Collaborates with START leadership to ensure the quality and effectiveness of crisis support services delivered through the START model for individuals at risk of acute crisis, loss of residential placement, or those currently experiencing crisis. Builds and maintains strong relationships with community partners and stakeholders to enhance service coordination and communication.

Essential Functions

Assists in supervising the Clinical Team Lead, START Coordinators, START Therapeutic Coaching Lead, and START Therapeutic Coaches.
Ensures associate responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities are clearly defined and understood; manages and evaluates performance and productivity.
Works with the Director of Consultation Services and Human Resources in the recruitment and selection of new program associates; oversees associates involved in the process as needed.
Provides support to the clinical team as required.
Assists in establishing community linkages and serves as liaison to community network partners.
Represents the START team in the community to strengthen partnerships and collaboration.
Coordinates trainings utilizing expertise of psychologists, psychiatrists, team leaders, and community specialists.
Leads and/or attends staff meetings and daily triage meetings; prepares and delivers specialized training and instructional materials, including staff development training, as assigned by the Director of Consultation Services.
Participates in and completes the START Coordinator Certification training process.
Collaborates with START leadership to monitor service quality and ensure fidelity to the START model.
Shares on-call responsibilities to provide 24/7 crisis response: telephonic within one hour and in-person within 24 hours.
Assists in responding to requests from state agencies for data and program information.
Enters, monitors and assures data entry for all team members in the START Information Reporting System; uses data to inform program decisions.
Attends conferences and trainings to stay current on research, trends, and developments related to intellectual and developmental disabilities, special education, and related fields.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Education

Master’s Degree in social work, psychology, counseling or human service field.
Preferred to have a certificate or license (e.g., BCBA, OT, LMFT, LCSW, etc.).
Must have and maintain current CPR certification card.
Must be a certified START Coordinator within 12 months of employment as team leader.

Experience

5 years of professional experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities and behavioral health needs, in a multi-disciplinary team setting.
2 years of supervisory experience. Typically, experience in managing severe behavior problems such as frequent property destruction, aggression towards others, SIB, PICA, etc.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

Expert knowledge of scientifically-validated methodologies and approaches found to benefit individuals with developmental disabilities and behavioral health needs; familiar with current related research findings.
Strong clinical, administrative, and leadership skills.
Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office Applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.).
Able to interpret and implement policies, procedures, and regulations.
Able to consistently demonstrate good judgment and decision-making skills.
Ability to maintain customer service orientation and professionalism in all interactions.
Ability to communicate effectively, through oral and written skills, and work cooperatively with a variety of individuals and groups. Must relate well to participants and their families and maintain positive affect.
Ability to exercise discretion and maintain a high level of confidentiality to handle sensitive and confidential situations and documentations.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Our Consumer & Community Banking division serves our Chase customers through a range of financial services, including personal banking, credit cards, mortgages, auto financing, investment advice, small business loans and payment processing. In this role, you'll apply strong technical judgment to choose the right approaches (including modern LLM-based
methods where appropriate), evaluate performance with rigorous metrics, and ensure solutions are reliable, secure, and scalable
in real-world environments. You'll also contribute to improving data quality and feedback loops, monitoring models in production, and continuously iterating to reduce agent effort, shorten resolution times, and increase consistency and quality across operational workflows.

As an AI/ML Executive Director
within Consumer & Community Banking (CCB) Recommendations & Personalization

that power customer experiences across CCB digital channels. You'll drive strategy and execution across search/retrieval and NLP signals
, experimentation, measurement, and production ML—leveraging GenAI where it meaningfully improves relevance, efficiency, or customer outcomes (but with recommenders and personalization as the core focus

Job Responsibilities

Own and evolve CCB recommendation & personalization platforms (candidate generation, ranking, re-ranking, retrieval, and real-time decisioning) to improve customer relevance and engagement across journeys and surfaces.
Lead end-to-end ML delivery: problem framing, feature strategy, model development, offline/online evaluation, A/B testing, launch, monitoring, and iteration for production recommender systems.
Develop and operationalize evaluation frameworks for ranking and personalization (e.g., relevance/utility metrics, calibration, novelty/diversity, long-term value, bias/fairness considerations, and guardrails).
Apply NLP and search/retrieval techniques to enrich signals (query/document understanding, embeddings, semantic retrieval, entity/intent extraction) that improve recommendation quality and explainability.

Partner cross-functionally with Product, Design, Data, Risk/Controls, and Engineering to align on goals, prioritize roadmaps, and deliver measurable customer and business impact.
Be a hands-on technical leader: contribute to architecture and critical code paths; guide system design for low-latency services, feature pipelines, training/inference infrastructure, and reliability.
Promote a culture of rigor and learning by introducing modern recommendation methods, experimentation best practices, and strong documentation and knowledge sharing.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

PhD in Computer Science (or equivalent experience) with strong research and industry background in machine learning, with depth in recommender systems, ranking, personalization, or information retrieval.
Proven ability to lead and deliver large-scale production ML systems using big data, including recommenders (collaborative filtering, deep retrieval/ranking, sequence models), classification/regression, and causal/experimental methods.
Strong track record of people leadership (building teams, setting technical direction, mentorship, performance management).
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including influencing senior stakeholders and translating business goals into measurable ML outcomes.
10+ years of hands-on programming and system-building experience (PhD + industry); strong in Python and at least one of Scala/Java; experience with Spark and distributed data processing.
Solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, and databases, and experience building scalable, reliable ML services.

Deep expertise in ranking/retrieval/search (semantic retrieval, ANN/vector search, learning-to-rank), online experimentation, and real-time personalization.
Experience designing feature stores, streaming/real-time pipelines, low-latency inference, and ML observability (data/model drift, performance diagnostics).
Experience applying NLP/LLMs to improve recommendation systems (embeddings, query understanding, content signals, retrieval augmentation) with disciplined evaluation and governance.

Job Description

The Chief Data & Analytics Office (CDAO) at JPMorgan Chase is responsible for accelerating the firm's data and analytics journey. This includes ensuring the quality, integrity, and security of the company's data, as well as leveraging this data to generate insights and drive decision-making. Experience with big data and scalable model training and solid written and spoken communication to effectively communicate technical concepts and results to both technical and business audiences.

Lead the Middle Office function for GMA Operations with primary responsibility for the Customized Bond Portfolio (CBP) fixed income SMA, while also designing and building the Middle Office support model for Tax Smart SMA offerings. These managed account solutions currently represent more than $300B in assets across more than 200,000 accounts and are a key growth focus for Asset Management.

As an Executive Director in the AWM Operations Middle Office, you will balance run-the-business (service delivery, controls, and issue management) with change-the-business leadership (operating model design, capacity build, process redesign, and automation). The role inherits an existing team and will expand capabilities in close partnership with global stakeholders, including key internal partners in India.

Own end-to-end fixed income SMA middle office delivery for CBP, including implementation support, restrictions, portfolio transitions, rebalancing support, exception/break management, and timely resolution of client-impact items.
Define and build the tax-managed SMA middle office capability, including operating model, governance, roles & responsibilities, procedures, controls, and service levels.
Establish a scalable global delivery model across locations/time zones, with clear ownership, handoffs, and performance routines in partnership with internal teams in India.
Create a strong control and risk environment across both fixed income SMA and tax-managed SMA scope: preventive/detective controls, issues remediation, operational risk assessments, and audit/regulatory readiness.

Identify and execute automation/STP and process improvement opportunities to improve cycle time, quality, scalability, and operational resiliency.
Establish and monitor relevant KPIs / KRIs (throughput, timeliness, exception rates, quality, client impact, and control performance) and lead performance management routines.
Build and develop the organization: manage an existing team supporting fixed income SMA while hiring/upskilling for future-state capabilities (controls leadership, analytics, process engineering, and platform expertise); coach leaders and contributors, develop a strong future-ready bench and strengthen succession plans.
Provide clear, executive-level communications on operating health, risks, dependencies, and investment needs across both scopes.

Required Qualifications, Skills, And Capabilities

Significant experience in asset management operations, ideally middle office supporting managed accounts/custom portfolios.
Senior leadership experience managing teams and delivering outcomes in a matrixed environment.
Demonstrated strength in operational risk, controls, governance, and issue management, including audit engagement.
Proven ability to lead complex change (operating model build, process redesign, automation and/or platform modernization).
Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.

Experience supporting fixed income SMA operational workflows (implementation/rebalancing support, restrictions management, transitions, and exception handling).
Experience standing up or scaling support for tax-aware/tax-managed SMA workflows (e.g., tax-loss harvesting, tax-aware rebalancing, transitions, restrictions).
Experience with global operating models, including partnership with teams in India.

jobs.description:
Job Description

We are seeking a dynamic and talented professional to join our Open Banking Strategic Business Unit (SBU) as the Executive Director of Industry Representation & Policy. This role offers the opportunity to lead the industry representation of a new, rapidly growing, revenue-generating business, working closely with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to ensure the highest standards of compliance, transparency, and client service.

As the Executive Director of Industry Representation and Policy within Open Banking, you will lead the strategic interpretation of regulatory, policy, and industry developments and translate them into clear direction and operational execution. You will serve as a senior external representative for JPMorgan Chase in industry forums and working groups and act as a policy-to-execution bridge across first line business execution and second line oversight to reinforce a robust, compliant operating model as the business scales.

The Chase Open Banking team is committed to empowering customers to share their financial data securely, safely, and transparently within the open banking ecosystem. Our mission is to deliver market-leading platforms that enable aggregators and direct connectors to securely access customer-permissioned data, while building out a two-sided business model that benefits both customers and commercial partners. We collaborate closely with partners across billing, invoicing, and are developing a self-service developer portal to streamline integration and access. We support our customers' ability to access their financial data and have full control and visibility in sharing it securely with the apps and companies they choose.

Job Responsibilities

Serve as a senior representative of JP Morgan Chase for the Open Banking team in external industry forums, trade associations, regulatory working groups, and financial infrastructure bodies related to Open Banking, payments, data and financial services innovation.
Own the strategic interpretation of regulatory policy and industry developments, with a particular focus on Open Banking frameworks, data sharing practices, and evolving supervisory expectations.
Translate complex regulatory and industry signals into clear, actionable strategic guidance for senior management and Chase leadership.
Partner closely with the Advocacy, Governance Relations, and Communications teams to ensure a credible, consistent and coordinated external position across regulators, policymakers, industry peers, and public forums.
Function as a trusted senior advisor to leadership on policy driven risks, opportunities, and strategic trade-oofs affecting Chase's Open Banking Strategy.
Provide executive-level oversight of policy positions, consultation responses, and industry submissions, ensuring alignment with firmwide strategy and reputational standards.
Represent JP Morgan in high-stakes, senior level discussions with regulators and industry leaders, exercising sound judgment and discretion.
Create the vision, priorities, and operating model for industry engagement and policy interpretation within the Open Banking domain.
Foster a culture of accountability, engagement, and high performance within the Business Execution and Policy team while promoting diversity and inclusion by valuing the unique capabilities.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

10+ years of experience in financial services, regulatory policy, industry representation, or strategy with a proven track record in engaging with regulators, translating regulations and policy to business functions.
Experienced legal background and CFPB knowledge that can represent Chase's perspective on policy updates at industry forums.
Demonstrate experience engaging with regulators, policymakers, industry bodies, or standard-setting organizations in banking or financial services.
Deep understanding of regulatory frameworks, supervisory processes, and policy development affecting large financial institutions.

Strong executive presence with exceptional written and verbal communication—able to credibly represent JPMorganChase in external forums and craft formal policy positions, executive briefings, and external messaging.
Track record of effective cross-functional leadership and influence across Legal, Risk, Compliance, Technology, and Business teams.
Strong understanding of Open Banking, data access, and related regulatory and industry frameworks.
Sound judgement, discretion, and decision-making consistent with senior leadership accountability.
Strong culture leader with a collaborative mindset, teamwork spirit and strong interpersonal skills
Bachelor's degree required

Experience in policy, and regulatory representation in financial services is preferred

**Location:** Miami, FL (Headquarters)  

**Schedule:** Full\-Time


**FLSA Status:** Exempt  

**Salary:** $85,000–$105,000 annually

 **About Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami**



For more than 65 years, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami has been creating life\-changing mentoring relationships that empower young people to reach their full potential. Through the power of one\-to\-one mentorship, we help children build confidence, achieve greater educational success, and realize brighter futures.

  

We are seeking a strategic and relationship\-driven **Director of Institutional Giving** to lead and grow our foundation, corporate, and government fundraising efforts. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced development professional to play a key leadership role in advancing the mission of one of South Florida's most respected nonprofit organizations.

 **Position Summary**



Reporting to the **Vice President of Development**, the Director of Institutional Giving is responsible for developing and executing strategies that increase and diversify institutional funding. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of foundation, corporate, and government funders while identifying new funding opportunities that support BBBS Miami's strategic priorities.

  

This position manages an annual institutional fundraising portfolio of approximately **$3–4 million** and works closely with executive leadership, program staff, and the Board of Directors to secure transformational investments that expand the organization's impact throughout the community.

 **Primary Responsibilities**


* Develop and implement a comprehensive institutional giving strategy aligned with organizational goals.
* Build, manage, and grow a portfolio of foundation, corporate, and government funding partners.
* Identify, research, cultivate, solicit, and steward prospective and current institutional donors.
* Monitor philanthropic trends and identify emerging funding opportunities at the local, state, and national levels.
* Lead the development of compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, reports, and other institutional fundraising materials.
* Collaborate with program and executive leadership to develop program budgets, funding requests, and organizational case statements.
* Ensure timely submission of grant applications, reports, and all funder deliverables.
* Oversee stewardship activities and donor recognition for institutional supporters.
* Partner with the Vice President of Development to establish fundraising goals and monitor progress throughout the year.
* Collaborate with the CEO, senior leadership team, Board members, and volunteers to cultivate and strengthen institutional relationships.
* Maintain accurate donor records and fundraising activity within Raiser’s Edge (or similar CRM).
* Prepare fundraising reports, pipeline updates, and progress reports for leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Support annual audit activities and other organizational reporting requirements as needed.

  


**Qualifications**



The ideal candidate is a strategic fundraiser, exceptional writer, and collaborative relationship builder who thrives in a mission\-driven environment.


* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional fundraising experience.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, with a demonstrated record of securing institutional funding.
* Experience managing foundation, corporate, and/or government grants from cultivation through stewardship.
* Strong grant writing, proposal development, editing, and presentation skills.
* Experience developing program budgets and funding proposals.
* Knowledge of local, regional, and national philanthropic communities and institutional funding sources.

* Excellent organizational, project management, and time management skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships across diverse stakeholders.
* High level of professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment.

**Why Join BBBS of Miami**



Joining Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami means becoming part of a mission\-driven organization committed to changing the trajectory of young people's lives through mentoring.

  

As a member of our Development team, you will have the opportunity to shape fundraising strategy, build meaningful partnerships with institutional supporters, and directly influence the growth and sustainability of programs that serve youth throughout Miami\-Dade County.

  

We offer a collaborative work environment, opportunities for professional growth, and a comprehensive benefits package for full\-time employees.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**About First Place AZ**

We are a spirited charitable nonprofit organization advancing a new marketplace of inclusive housing, healthcare, employment and lifelong\-learning options for adults with autism, neurodivergences and/or intellectual/developmental disabilities (I/DD). First Place\-Phoenix, our flagship property, serves as a proof point informing our national work, offering a real\-world site for innovation, learning and demonstration.

First Place AZ is an equal opportunity employer.

**The Opportunity**

Philanthropy at First Place is relational, strategic and mission driven. We don’t just raise money—we build lasting relationships with individuals, foundations and corporations who share our vision and want to be part of something that’s working. Our donors are allies in a movement to reimagine what’s possible for adults with disabilities.

This role is for someone who wants to shape a development function at a pivotal moment. You’ll work closely with the CEO and Board to set philanthropic strategy, diversify and grow revenue, and strengthen the systems that support it all. You’ll be a member of the leadership team, not a siloed fundraiser.

We’re looking for ambition, maturity and aspiration. Someone who sees what First Place is building and is committed to taking it further.

**Who You Are**

You are a seasoned development professional who has outgrown transactional fundraising. You know how to secure major gifts, write winning proposals and steward donors—and you are hungry to do that work in service of a mission you believe in and an organization on the rise.

You think strategically about revenue, not just tactically about asks. You value the entire development ecosystem: individual giving, foundations, corporate partnerships, planned giving, events—and you know how to build a diversified, sustainable funding base.

You are a relationship builder and are as comfortable in a one\-on\-one donor or team meeting as you are presenting to a board. You bring people along.

You lead with clarity and accountability. You have supervised and mentored staff, managed budgets and built systems that work. You communicate performance honestly and use data to guide decisions.

You are ready to be part of a leadership team, assume a seat at the table where strategy is shaped and contribute beyond your functional area.

**What You’ll Do**

**Strategic Leadership**

You will develop and execute First Place’s philanthropic strategy in partnership with the CEO, Board of Directors and leadership team. This includes setting annual fundraising goals and long\-term revenue targets, identifying opportunities to diversify funding streams, preparing development budgets and projections, and monitoring trends to keep the organization ahead of the curve. You will establish policies, procedures and practices that strengthen department efficiency and position the organization for continued growth.

**Revenue Development**

You will lead fundraising across all channels—individual giving, foundations, corporations and planned giving.

For individual donors, you will build and manage a comprehensive giving program, develop annual campaigns and stewardship strategies, identify and cultivate major gift prospects, expand recurring giving , and support the CEO’s donor portfolio.

For foundations and grants, you will oversee the full cycle from prospect research through submission and reporting, develop compelling proposals and budgets, manage funder relationships, and maintain compliance calendars and pipelines.

For corporate collaborators, you will cultivate long\-term partnerships, secure sponsorships for the annual events and initiatives, and ensure fulfillment of sponsorship benefits.

For planned giving, you will lead the growth of the First Place Forever legacy program, recruit, support the Planned Giving Advisory Committee and develop donor engagement opportunities.

**Engagement \& Events**

You will provide strategic leadership for fundraising and cultivation events, including the annual Dimensions® symposium, community tours, donor events, educational webinars and special initiatives. You will recruit and engage volunteers, support Board committees and advisory groups, and coordinate volunteer communications. In partnership with communications and marketing staff, you will shape fundraising campaigns, impact reports, donor communications, annual appeals, sponsorship materials, case statements and website content.

**Operations \& Team Leadership**

You will oversee development operations, including Salesforce database integrity, dashboards and reporting, fundraising KPIs, gift acknowledgment processes and coordination with the finance department. You will supervise development staff, interns and volunteers, providing coaching, mentoring and professional development. You will foster a collaborative, mission\-driven team culture.

jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

The Foundation for Food \& Agriculture Research (FFAR) is a nonprofit organization that builds public\-private partnerships to fund audacious research addressing the biggest challenges in food and agriculture. FFAR is committed to providing every person access to affordable, nutritious food grown on thriving farms. The Foundation pioneers scientific and technological innovation by funding research that fills critical research gaps. Ultimately, FFAR’s partnership and results benefit farmers, consumers and the environment.**Position Summary**


The Foundation for Food \& Agriculture Research (FFAR) seeks an entrepreneurial, relationship\-driven Director of Philanthropy to lead the organization's philanthropic fundraising efforts by implementing the newly developed Philanthropy Strategy \& Implementation Plan to advance FFAR's mission and long\-term financial sustainability.  

Reporting to the Vice President of Partnerships \& Development, the Director of Philanthropy will lead fundraising efforts focused on major gifts, family offices, private foundations, corporate philanthropy and other mission\-aligned philanthropic investors. The director will be responsible for implementing a developed robust portfolio of philanthropic prospects, securing significant philanthropic commitments and expanding FFAR's base of unrestricted and flexible funding.  

As FFAR continues to diversify its revenue streams, the director will play a foundational role in building fundraising systems, cultivating strategic donor relationships, supporting executive and board engagement, and positioning FFAR as a premier philanthropic investment opportunity within food and agriculture innovation.  

This position offers a unique opportunity to help shape the future of food and agriculture by securing philanthropic investment in scientific innovation, workforce development and food system transformation. **Duties and Responsibilities**


Philanthropy Strategy \& Revenue Growth (20%)

* Lead implementation of FFAR's philanthropy strategy and annual fundraising plan.
* Set annual revenue and pipeline targets and adjust fundraising tactics based on pipeline performance.
* Contribute to revenue forecasting, fundraising targets and pipeline planning.
* Identify opportunities to diversify philanthropic funding sources and increase unrestricted support.
* Monitor fundraising performance and recommend adjustments to strategies, priorities and resource allocation.


Donor Development \& Major Gifts (35%)

* Manage and actively advance a portfolio of high\-potential philanthropic prospects and donors to meet FFAR’s 2027\-2029 fundraising goals.
* Grow prospects portfolio of philanthropic investors to secure higher donations past 2029\.
* Build and implement individualized solicitation plans for each donor.
* Secure philanthropic commitments ranging from major gifts to transformational investments.
* Manage prospect conversion through all stages of the donor lifecycle, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship and renewal.
* Conduct donor meetings, presentations and engagement activities that strengthen relationships and advance fundraising objectives.


Foundation \& Institutional Giving (20%)

* Develop and manage relationships with private foundations and institutional funders aligned with FFAR's mission and strategic priorities.
* Identify and pursue opportunities for unrestricted, thematic and programmatic funding to meet FFAR’s 2027\-2029 fundraising goals.
* Coordinate proposal development, grant submissions, reporting requirements and stewardship activities in collaboration with internal teams.
* Maintain awareness of philanthropic trends affecting food systems, agriculture and innovation funding.
* Build long\-term relationships that position FFAR as a preferred funding partner.


Executive \& Board Engagement (10%)

* Partner with the Executive Director, Vice President of Partnerships \& Development and board members to strengthen fundraising effectiveness and meet FFAR’s 2027\-2029 fundraising goals.
* Coordinate donor engagement activities involving senior leadership and board members.
* Develop briefing materials, relationship maps, meeting preparation materials and solicitation strategies.
* Support board fundraising engagement and ambassador activities.
* Facilitate introductions and relationship\-building opportunities that expand FFAR's philanthropic network.


Donor Stewardship \& Philanthropic Communications (10%)

* Develop meaningful donor engagement opportunities that deepen relationships and encourage long\-term support.
* Partner with Communications and Scientific Program Directors to translate complex scientific work into compelling stories to drive philanthropic opportunities.
* Support development of donor\-facing materials, impact stories, case statements and fundraising communications.


Fundraising Operations \& Portfolio Management (5%)

* Maintain accurate donor, prospect and engagement information within FFAR's CRM system.
* Monitor portfolio health, prospect conversion, fundraising metrics and pipeline performance.
* Contribute to the development of fundraising procedures, reporting systems, dashboards and performance measures.
* Provide regular updates on fundraising progress, pipeline health metrics and opportunities.
**Qualifications**


Education

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Master's degree preferred.
* Degree in business, communications, nonprofit management, public policy, agriculture, food science or systems, sustainability, life sciences or a related field preferred.


Experience

* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible fundraising, philanthropy, advancement, development or donor relations experience in agriculture, food, sustainability, etc. is required.
* Demonstrated success securing and stewarding major philanthropic commitments, including six\- and seven\-figure gifts.
* Experience managing major donor port

**POSITION ANNOUNCEMENT**

**New Orleans Recreation Development Commission**

**POSITION: Chief Executive Officer, New Orleans Recreation Development**

**COMMISSION FUNCTION:** The mission of the New Orleans Recreation Development Commission (NORDC) is to advance the physical, mental, and social well\-being of New Orleanians by providing safe and welcoming environments for recreational, athletic, and cultural experiences. The Commission plans, supervises, conducts, and coordinates programs for cultural and physical recreation that will be administered by the New Orleans Recreation Development Commission. NORDC provides a wide range of sports, health, aquatics, day care, and fitness programs for residents and visitors of all ages. NORDC manages senior services, therapeutic recreation, youth camps, teen development, and athletic programs in over 160 facilities city\-wide. The Commission promotes cooperative planning with public and private entities concerned with recreation.

**REQUIREMENTS:**

* Minimum five years of supervisory experience in the administration of a parks and recreation department or sports organization.

*Oversight Functions —*

* Review reports submitted by staff members in order to recommend approval or to suggest changes.

*Community Functions —*

* Respond to and resolve difficult and sensitive citizen inquiries and complaints; review and reply to daily correspondence and phone inquiries.
* Build community support of and engagement with NORDC's mission and strategic plan.
* Develop relationships with individuals and organizations in an effort to financially and strategically support NORDC's mission and strategic plan.
* Represent NORDC to outside agencies and the community; coordinate assigned activities with outside agencies and organizations.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

*Knowledge of:*

* National best practices of youth development programming
* Business and management: principles involved in strategic planning, resource allocation, human resources modeling, leadership technique, production methods, and coordination of people and resources.
* Principles and practices of marketing and public relations. This includes marketing strategy and tactics, promotion of services provided, and assessments of current and future value of services provided by NORDC.
* Principles and practices of program development and administ

The Director of Development will cultivate relationships with all stakeholders, especially residents, to encourage and celebrate gift giving to promote Foulkeways’ short\-term and long\-term goals. In addition, the Director of Development will appeal to outside foundations, vendors and the greater community to keep Foulkeways at the forefront of new ideas, technology and projects.

**Responsibilities** of the Director of Development are as follows (these are not inclusive of all job responsibilities):

* Develop philanthropy program, as well as communications plan and supporting materials
* Cultivate positive relationships with company stakeholders
* Develop and maintain lists of potential donors
* Manage the receipt and administration of deferred gifts, such as bequests, gift annuities and trusts
* Report to the Board and Fund Development Committee
* Present Development\-related information to stakeholders through committee participation, group presentations, internals publications, etc.

The Director of Development of Foulkeways will promote the mission and values of Foulkeways and will assist in the creation of a culture that celebrates diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging.

**Qualifications Required:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field required

EBL seeks a Development Director to work closely with the Executive Director, Board, and Fundraising and Marketing Committee to raise $3 million in contributed revenue over the next two fiscal years, and to build the relationships, systems, and philanthropic partnerships that will support EBL’s mission and growth for years to come. This is a remote position open to all U.S. candidates, but San Francisco Bay Area-based preferred, with regular in-person engagement expected with donors, board members, and community partners.

Full Job Description

This highly external-facing role is responsible for building deep, long-term donor relationships and executing a comprehensive, sustainable fundraising strategy that ensures EBL’s long-term financial health.

Success In This Role Includes

Raising $3M in contributed revenue over two fiscal years.

Growing EBL’s major donor pipeline and stewardship program.

Expanding foundation and corporate partnerships.

Building fundraising systems and donor engagement practices that support long-term growth.

Increasing board engagement in fundraising.

Organizational Leadership

Set and align EBL’s long-term fundraising vision and annual revenue goals as part of multi-year, donor-centered fundraising strategy that builds continuity, trust, and sustained community engagement while ensuring that programmatic commitments, legal requirements, and gift-related compliance standards are maintained.

Donor & Portfolio Management

Donor & Major Gifts

Develop and lead EBL’s Major Gifts program, including prospect identification and qualification, personalized cultivation, well-crafted solicitations, and disciplined stewardship.

Maintain and develop portfolio of individual donors and prospects, with emphasis on cultivating mid-level and major donors, supporting the Executive Director in managing and stewarding high-priority donor relationships using nationally and globally connected philanthropic networks to expand prospect strategy.

Board Engagement

Support and guide board members in fundraising and ambassadorship; staff the Board Development Committee, and assist members with their donor relationships by creating talking points and tracking introductions.

Foundation Giving

Oversee the foundation and institutional giving programs, which includes researching new foundation partnerships, maintaining the grants calendar, overseeing strategy, proposal development, deliverables, and budget creation, and cultivating strategic relationships with foundation staff.

Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorships

Build and grow a corporate revenue and sponsorship program from the ground up, identifying aligned partners and developing engagement strategies that boost brand visibility.

Community Representation

Act as a visible ambassador for the organization at Bay Area community events, donor gatherings, and public-facing activities.

Communications & Donor Acquisition

Lead EBL’s efforts to grow its donor base and deepen engagement through compelling communications and targeted acquisition strategies, such as social media channels, direct mail or email campaigns, appeal letters and impact reports.

Lead strategy and execution for fundraising events, ensuring strong ROI and an exceptional donor experience and represent EBL at community and donor events throughout the Bay Area.

Track record of building and maintaining long-term relationships with major donors, foundations, and corporate partners.

Demonstrated success securing foundation and institutional funding.

Comfort working in a small, informal, and/or nonprofit environment.

Valid driver’s license.

Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills; ability to inspire philanthropy through authentic engagement.

Existing relationships with Bay Area foundations or individual donors in the environmental or social justice space.

Familiarity with advanced gift planning concepts and planned giving vehicles.

Experience with digital fundraising, direct mail, and current trends in major gifts solicitation.

Knowledge of nonprofit management best practices.

Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience a plus.

401(k) plan

Remote work with flexible scheduling

Department Overview

UC San Diego Advancement's dynamic team inspires, builds and nurtures relationships with our community — alumni, students, faculty, staff and other members of the Triton family — that increase engagement with and philanthropic support for the university. Together, Advancement’s six units bring together strategy, partnerships and expertise to support UC San Diego’s efforts to unite diverse people and unconventional perspectives to propel limitless impact here in San Diego and far beyond.

UC San Diego Advancement’s University Development department is the frontline fundraising team responsible for supporting General Campus and Scripps Institution of Oceanography leadership in securing philanthropic resources that advance opportunity for their students, faculty and initiatives. We recognize the crucial role development professionals play in identifying, engaging, cultivating and stewarding the philanthropic partners capable of assuring this university’s brightest future. Our leadership works tenaciously to seek out development professionals at all stages of their careers who evince the passion and integrity representative of our university’s character. Once part of the University Development team, colleagues are celebrated for their accomplishments and offered the support necessary to identify and realize ambitious goals. The SDOD prepares written and oral presentations to current and prospective donors and leads and partners on philanthropic strategies and activities as defined by campus policy and procedures; develops gift opportunities consistent with the priorities of Scripps Oceanography and UC San Diego's mission; supervises and mentors direct reports and provides work direction to the team as appropriate; and collaborates with colleagues across Advancement and the campus.
