Unlike Grunley's traditional self-perform model, this program is designed around the use of strong local “super subcontractors” in each region who provide the on-the-ground labor, trade relationships, and market knowledge required to execute effectively in remote and geographically dispersed border locations.

The Program Director will lead Grunley's pursuit and execution of work under the CBP program. This person will build and manage a network of local specialty and general trade subcontractors functioning as “super subs,” develop relationships with CBP/DHS contracting officials, direct the pricing and proposal process for competed task orders, negotiate final contract terms, and oversee delivery of awarded projects across a wide and often remote geography. This role is equal parts business developer, subcontractor network builder, and federal program operator.

Reports to: President

Requirements

Required Education
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management or related fields

Required Experience
This position requires a minimum of ten (10)+ years of construction leadership experience, including significant federal government contracting experience.

Required Qualifications
Direct experience with CBP, DHS, GSA, or other federal agencies delivering infrastructure in remote or border-region environments.
Demonstrated success managing work primarily through subcontractors/local partners rather than self- performing.
Strong track record negotiating both government contracts and subcontractor agreements.
Working knowledge of FAR and federal government construction contracting requirements.

Preferred Experience
Existing relationships with CBP/DHS contracting or program offices.
Existing network of qualified subcontractors along the southern U.S. border.
Experience with security-sensitive, remote, or austere-site construction (military, energy, or infrastructure sectors).
Spanish language proficiency.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to travel extensively and work effectively across multiple, geographically dispersed markets

Summary

Responsibilities/Duties

Market & Relationship Development
Serve as Grunley's primary relationship owner with CBP and DHS contracting, program management, and engineering stakeholders.
Identify, vet, and build long-term relationships with qualified local “super subcontractor” partners across the southern border region.
Understand the distinct local market, labor, security, and logistical conditions in each border sub-region (South Texas, West Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, Southern California).
Engage local officials, agencies, and community stakeholders as needed to support project execution in sensitive border locations.

Pursuit & Preconstruction Management
Track and qualify CBP task order releases against Grunley's win strategy and capacity, in coordination with Chip Scott.
Lead the proposal and pricing process for each pursuit in partnership with Grunley's preconstruction team and local super-sub partners.
Structure teaming and subcontract arrangements that appropriately allocate scope, risk, and pricing responsibility to local partners.
Ensure compliance with FAR, DHS/CBP-specific contracting requirements, and any applicable security or site-access protocols.

Contract Negotiation & Execution
Lead negotiation of final task order value and terms with CBP contracting officers.
Negotiate subcontract terms, pricing, and risk allocation with local super-sub partners.
Hire and assign project management and field supervision staff(Grunley and/or partner-provided) to oversee construction across multiple, often remote, project sites.
Monitor safety, quality, schedule, and financial performance across a geographically dispersed project portfolio.

Organization & Culture
Build a lean, mobile program management structure capable of overseeing widely dispersed projects executed largely through local partners.
Establish consistent Grunley standards for safety, quality, and reporting across all super-sub relationships.
Report program pipeline, subcontractor network health, and financial/risk performance directly to Chip Scott.

Our benefits package is designed to support employee well-being and financial security, including employer-sponsored health and life insurance, paid time off for sick leave, maternity/paternity leave, jury duty, and vacation, and retirement options like 401(k) plans. Other compensation opportunities may include overtime and bonuses. Comprehensive benefits will be discussed during the recruitment process; benefit eligibility is determined by tenure, position and/or plan documents.

If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at hr@grunley.com or by phone at 240-399-6162 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this e-mail address.

This position serves as the statewide authority responsible for the strategic direction, policy leadership, and enterprise-level administration of LADOTD's non-movable asset data, the department's comprehensive Maintenance Management Program, and the newly created Maintenance Quality Assurance (MQA) program. jobs.description:
DESCRIPTION:
The Parkinson's Foundation makes life better for people with Parkinson’s disease by improving care and advancing research toward a cure. In everything we do, we build on the energy, experience, and passion of our global Parkinson's community.

The Advancement Director will lead the Tennessee and Kentucky Chapter (TNKY), responsible for strategically implementing revenue development and mission delivery to advance the Parkinson’s Foundation’s goals. This role involves achieving targeted revenue metrics—such as fundraising events, corporate development, individual giving, and Ambassador/board development—and education & outreach metrics, including volunteer development, community partner engagement, and new outreach opportunities. The Director will also develop, manage, and oversee the Chapter budget and long-term strategy for sustained revenue growth. Additionally, the Director will cultivate community partnerships and alliances to promote growth and awareness. As a key member of the regional team, the Advancement Director will collaborate with the Regional Director and other team members to meet regional standards and expectations. The TNKY Chapter extends its services across both states, offering a significant opportunity to make a tangible difference in the lives of individuals affected by Parkinson's.

RESPONSIBILITIES: Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Revenue Generation and Outreach:
·      Drive revenue and outreach standards, strategies, and growth opportunities for the Chapter.
·      Develop, implement, contribute to, and monitor an annual budget and long-term strategy plan for the Chapter, including management of assigned chapter revenue benchmarks.
·      Formulate and implement strategies and tactics for Chapter fundraising activities to sustain continued growth, including optimizing opportunities in core market areas and identifying opportunities for expansion.
·      Build and execute a strategy for consistent Parkinson’s Foundation presence in remote communities served by the Chapter, including regular in-person travel by team to communities and strategically planned outreach activities.
·      Work with the team to create and implement strategies to meet fundraising goals through Parkinson’s Foundation’s signature Peer-to-Peer fundraising initiatives, including Moving Day events and special events. Provide hands-on support for P2P fundraising initiatives when necessary.

Stakeholder and Community Engagement:
·      Serve as lead relationship manager for key stakeholders both in revenue and mission delivery, including local community partners, corporate partners, allied health partners, and strategic partnerships.
·      Manage a personal portfolio of donors for cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation of increased giving. Sustain focus on increasing Chapter-level individual giving growth and work with revenue collaborators within the organization.
·      Develop and direct the cultivation, solicitation, follow-up, and recognition process for fundraising event participants, corporate partners, and key Chapter stakeholders year-round.
·      Actively seek opportunities to address community needs and positively impact the local community while advancing the mission, goals, and values.
·      Serve as a local representative for Parkinson’s Foundation, acting as spokesperson when necessary and appropriate.

Team and Volunteer Management:
·      Lead, recruit, and retain high-level volunteers and Ambassadors, including leadership of the Chapter Board and annual board giving.
·      Lead and coach Chapter team members to achieve revenue, community outreach, and professional development success.

Operational Efficiency:
·      Maintain accurate records of Chapter activities and utilize the RE NXT database for community, donor, and constituent management.
·      Ensure total team compliance with organizational database tracking standards.
·      Perform all other duties and tasks required to support all new and/or proposed fundraising events, programs, and activities.
·      Stay informed about organization-wide activities and properly utilize available resources.
·      Be knowledgeable about Parkinson’s disease and the Foundation’s strategic plan and operations.
EXPERIENCE/SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:
Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 6 years of fundraising experience, preferably within a healthcare non-profit organization.
Demonstrated track record of successful fundraising experience that includes special events, corporate/foundation giving, donor cultivation and recognition, donor records, and acknowledgment.
Proven and applicable skills in strategic planning, budgeting, and volunteer development.
Outgoing, energetic, organized, and detail-oriented team member who can adhere to timelines and prioritize effectively.
Strong verbal and written communication and presentation skills.
Skilled people developer with a history of managing high-performing teams of 2 or more.
Ability to lead and close high-level solicitations.
Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Strong volunteer recruitment, committee development, and management skills.
Experience securing corporate partnerships is a must.
Self-starter who is also collaborative, a quick learner, and an effective team player.
Excellent active listening, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to effectively multi-task, establish priorities, and work in a fast-paced environment.
Highly efficient in time management and able to meet deadlines under pressure. Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills.
Ability to provide a high level of customer service to external constituents.
Self-motivated, results-oriented leader with strong organizational skills.
Strong computer skills, proficient with the MS Office suite.
Proficiency in Raiser’s Edge NXT is a plus.
Must be able to lift at least 20 lbs. from the ground to waist level with or without reasonable accommodation.

·      Capacity to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, with adherence to core business hours.
·      Ability to travel throughout the Chapter and region up to 30% of the time, with reliable personal transportation and a valid driver’s license.
·      Demonstrates the organizational values of excellence, teamwork, collaboration, integrity, positivity, dedication and responsiveness.

COMPENSATION:
Salary for this position is competitive and depends on prior experience. In addition, a comprehensive benefits package is included. The salary range for this position is $70,000-$80,000

HOW TO APPLY:
Please submit a resume, cover letter, and salary requirement to employment@parkinson.org. Applicant review will continue until the position is filled. Please indicate, “Advancement Director – TNKY Chapter” in the subject line. Resumes without a cover letter and salary requirements will not be considered. No phone calls please.
The Parkinson's Foundation is an equal-opportunity employer.

jobs.title: After-School Program Director, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
On-site at an Alpha campus in New York City, NY; Miami, FL; or San Francisco, CA — we provide relocation support
$200,000 per year
Full-time position

Traditional elementary schools reduce expectations when children face difficulties. Your approach is the opposite. You know that six-year-olds can accomplish far more than conventional classrooms demand, and you have used performance data to demonstrate this repeatedly.

Alpha's model allocates two hours to learning. Adaptive software handles academic instruction during morning sessions, freeing your schedule for the interventions that genuinely transform children: motivation, life skills development, coaching, and accountability structures. You take direct ownership of a K-3 student cohort while also coaching the Guides—Alpha's term for the adults who mentor and inspire students—who drive their day-to-day progress. Your role keeps you actively engaged daily, not directing operations from a separate office.

Your typical day alternates among three core activities. You analyze performance metrics and Coachbot data to identify students and Guides falling behind targets. You conduct coaching sessions that conclude with concrete next actions rather than general encouragement. And you lead workshops for groups of five- to nine-year-olds covering topics like public speaking, sustained attention, or peer feedback skills.

When you identify effective methods, you document them. The frameworks you create establish the standard that all other Guides implement, extending your influence from a single cohort to an entire grade level. Demonstrating your ability to replicate that quality at scale is the pathway to broader leadership responsibilities here.

If reducing expectations seems compassionate to you, this role is not appropriate. If increasing them feels like showing respect, submit your application.

What You Will Be Doing

Using performance data, classroom observation, and direct feedback to coach both Guides and students, then maintaining accountability to quantifiable targets for each group
Leading one-hour live workshops for K-3 students focused on life skills including public speaking, sustained focus, teamwork, resilience, accountability, and peer feedback
Conducting individual and small-group sessions that link each student's personal goals and interests to tangible academic advancement
Creating and iterating on playbooks that convert your most effective practices into repeatable frameworks other Guides can implement reliably
Training Guides on these playbooks and demonstrating facilitation excellence so quality standards persist as the team expands

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching academic content or presenting lectures; adaptive technology handles instruction while you focus on coaching people
Reducing expectations when students encounter challenges
Managing from a distance the way instructional coaches and school administrators typically do; you remain embedded with your cohort every day
Managing the full campus budget, operations infrastructure, and parent communication; a Campus Lead handles those areas so you concentrate on student and Guide performance
Advocating for traditional pedagogical approaches or adhering to standard K-12 curricula

After-School Program Director Key Responsibilities

Fulfill Alpha's three core commitments to every K-3 student: they develop a love of school, achieve learning at twice the standard rate, and cultivate outstanding life skills and self-sufficiency.

Basic Requirements

Available to work on-site at an Alpha campus in New York City, NY; Miami, FL; or San Francisco, CA; we provide relocation support
Bachelor's degree in Education, Psychology, Business, Organizational Leadership, Child Development, or a related discipline
Minimum of 5 years' experience working with elementary-aged children (approximately ages 5 to 9)
Demonstrated team leadership experience with 5 or more direct reports, including hiring and performance-based removal authority
Proven experience building, launching, or substantially scaling a program, team, school, or initiative from inception, rather than managing an established operation
Willingness to work in an educational environment that rejects conventional teaching methodologies
Legal authorization to work in the United States

Nice-to-have Requirements

Master's degree in a relevant discipline
Demonstrated ability using metrics, dashboards, or data analytics to identify issues and produce measurable improvements
History of coaching or managing adults toward quantifiable results, beyond personal execution
Experience in youth development programs, camp leadership, competitive athletics coaching, tutoring, or enrichment settings where motivating participants was essential
Proven ability facilitating sessions or speaking publicly to groups of young children

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $100 USD/hour, which equates to $200,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

The role of the Executive Director
requires a combination of organizational leadership and operational talent as well as strategic expertise. The Executive Director provides the management expertise for achieving the goals and objectives of the program in accordance with the mission of the organization. The Executive Director reports to the Regional Operations Director. Reporting to the Executive Director are various department supervisors and staff.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration or related field; licensed Nursing Home Administrator (NHA) for the state of Colorado; State requirements may dictate supervision and degree type.
Minimum of five (5) years Management experience, preferably in a long-term care healthcare setting; knowledge of long-term healthcare and public health settings; familiarity with Federal and State regulations and requirements for long-term care.
Negotiation skills and ability to carry on several levels of reasoning at once during problem-solving sessions.
High degree of professionalism; ability to deal with extremely confidential information.
Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, e-mail and the Internet.
Excellent communication skills.
Flexibility to work occasional weekends and holidays.
Ability to utilize computers and other electronic devices for tasks such as timekeeping, in-servicing and documentation.

In addition to managing the internal operations of the program, the Executive Director
must also be aware of conditions, events and issues that affect the community in which the program operates. Effective fulfillment of this broad responsibility requires awareness, involvement and insight; functioning as an agent for change; and a willingness to take risks and accept accountability for their outcomes within the context of a sound organizational structure and management processes. The Executive Director should serve as the catalyst, facilitator, coordinator and communicator to ensure that strategies to meet goals and objectives are developed, programs are carried out, quality is monitored and continually improved, and the results are evaluated. The Executive Director is expected to infuse the mission and philosophy of the organization into the program.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The Executive Director’s
responsibilities can be divided into six (6) broad categories: planning; organization; operations/management; financial resources; human resources; and leadership.

Planning
The Executive Director engages in a planning process for the program that determines its goals and objectives in relationship to changes in the environment and the needs of its community, establishes priorities, frames the most appropriate organizational structure to achieve its goals and objectives, and provides benchmarks for evaluating the achievement of its goals and objectives. The results of the planning process should be reflected in a business plan, developed by the Executive Director.
The Executive Director should ensure that the business plan is based on an assessment that reflects an adequate database on the needs of the community, an evaluation of trends, legislative activity, and documentation of demographics, utilization and financial trends. This assessment should be linked with an ongoing assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the program’s services in relation to those of other providers and to the needs of the community.
The business plan is supported by an effective public relations program, developed by the Executive Director that builds community understanding and support of the program and services and those of the national organization.

Organization
The Executive Director should create and monitor the organizational structure of the program to ensure its effectiveness and responsiveness to those being served. The nature of the structure is dynamic and flexible, responsive to needs of the participants. The Executive Director should develop an organizational plan that clearly assigns responsibilities for the program’s services to functional departments and to individuals. The Executive Director should develop, recommend and implement a plan for continuity that ensures ongoing stability of the program. Such a plan should include performance standards that are stated in terms of continuous improvement targets, opportunities for internal and external development, and a system for evaluating the performance levels of all employees, consultants and other service providers.

Operations (Management)
The amount of time that can be allocated to essential activities that call upon the visionary and strategic skills of the Executive Director is dependent upon the effectiveness of the day-to-day operations of the program. The Executive Director must create, sustain and evaluate on an ongoing basis an infrastructure of people who take overall responsibility for implementing the program’s service strategy and for initiating corrections that keep the strategy on course.
The infrastructure should be supported by the organization’s general policies and guidelines, and by program-specific systems and processes that are customer-responsive, efficient and continually improved by collecting and analyzing relevant data. These systems and processes must include mechanisms that ensure compliance with the regulations, standards and criteria of various health, governmental, professional and accrediting agencies.
Ensure the facility completes a facility wide assessment to determine what resources are necessary to care for its residents competently during both day to day operations and emergencies. Facility must review and update the assessment, as necessary and at least annually.
Ensures the facility has developed, implemented, and maintains an effective comprehensive, data drive QAPI program that focuses on indicators of the outcomes of care and quality of life.
The Executive Director serves as permanent chair of the program’s Quality Council, the body charged with overseeing the implementation of the Quality Plan, allocation of resources, initiation of project team solutions and monitoring results.
Ensures the facilities has developed an Antibiotic Stewardship Program that promotes the appropriate use of antibiotics.
The Executive Director serves as the Facility Compliance Officer, responsible for implementation of the corporate compliance program and all compliance procedures related to operations of the facility.

Financial Resource Management
The Executive Director is responsible for the cost effective management of the program’s resources, and for implementing the organizational financial policies. This responsibility requires a commitment to provide the most economical and highest quality services possible in keeping with available resources.
As a not-for-profit provider, the organization’s long-term financial stability and capacity to address the diverse needs of those it serves is dependent upon the financial support of contributors who embrace its mission. The Executive Director is responsible for developing and implementing a program-specific fundraising plan (as part of the business plan) that projects the values of the total organization into the community, and ensures the community’s financial support of the program.

Human Resources
The Executive Director should cultivate and promote a work atmosphere that recognizes the vital importance of human resources to the organization. The work atmosphere should empower employees with the tools and autonomy needed to make key service improvements that are in the best interests of the organization and its customers. The Executive Director is responsible for instituting a plan for recruitment, hiring, retention, and development of effective personnel to attain the objectives and goals of the program. The plan should include strategies that effectively build the level of employee morale and esprit de corps necessary to facilitate problem solving, productivity and service excellence. The Executive Director involves managers in developing specific action plans for improving service that include goal-setting and skill-building.

Leadership
The volatility of the health services environment requires that the Executive Director demonstrate a strong proficiency in the ability to manage and effect change. The Executive Director can best achieve and sustain an influential position of shaping the structure and dynamics of the program by developing sharp communication skills, thinking proactively rather than reactively, networking with diversified community and professional representatives, serving in advisory and board positions, and being active in health-related service organizations.
Serve as enforcer of the Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Age Discrimination Act of 1975.
Attends required in-services and completes assigned online modules.

At Valley Manor Care Center
in Montrose, CO, our aim is to find friendly and compassionate staff who are specially trained to care for patients' needs as individuals, respect their privacy, and help clients maintain as much independence as possible. While providing care to our patients, we want our staff to feel cared for and love their work while maintaining a work-life balance, so offering employees paid-time off benefits is a part of our comprehensive benefits package Our diverse and involved staff members are supported by the commitment to maintain relationships of functional trust with every team member, to always practice solutions-focused problem solving, and to continually affirm each team member’s contribution to the quality of our work.

Volunteers of America National Services has been certified as a Great Place to Work for 7 years running by its employees! Their work has a special meaning: this is not “just a job”.

Take pride in helping others and join us today!

At VOANS
, we celebrate sharing, encouraging and embracing diversity. Equal employment opportunities are available to all without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We believe that blending individual strengths and unique personal differences nurtures and supports our organizations’ shared commitment to our mission and creates an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone feels valued and has the opportunity to do their personal best.

jobs.title: Youth Program Director, Waypoint Academy - $150,000/year USD
jobs.description:
On-site role at Waypoint Academy, Dripping Springs, Texas
$150,000 annual salary as a W2 employee with weekly pay. Health benefits begin day one.
Relocation assistance provided

The greatest support you can offer a young person is to place a challenge in front of them and resist the urge to carry it for them. If that philosophy troubles you, this isn't the right fit. If it resonates, read on.

Waypoint Academy runs core academics through self-paced, AI-driven adaptive platforms that consolidate the school day into a concentrated morning block. There are no traditional lectures. This structure liberates your time for the work that genuinely shifts a student's path. You might start your morning in a one-on-one strategy session with a Guide, analyzing student metrics to identify where a group is faltering. By midday, you're outside facilitating a hands-on workshop that builds teamwork and grit through authentic struggle. Afternoons are dedicated to motivational coaching: meeting individually with students, uncovering what inspires them, and mobilizing a reluctant learner toward meaningful goals. You maintain your own student cohort throughout, ensuring the competencies you develop in others remain grounded in current practice.

You've likely been the outlier in traditional education: too metric-oriented, too outcome-focused, too comfortable taking students outdoors and allowing them to grapple with difficulty. This could be the first environment that truly aligns. You'll mentor other Guides from the outset, and as your results compound, the benchmark you establish influences the entire cohort and your authority within the program expands. The impact is tangible and immediate: a doubtful student who begins to claim their own development, a Guide who sharpens because you offered candid feedback, a young person who emerges from the woods more resilient than when they entered.

Uphold the standard. Lead them outdoors. Apply today.

What You Will Be Doing

Mentor the Guides working with you: analyze performance metrics, observe their interactions with students, and conclude each session with targeted actions that address identified gaps.
Facilitate one-hour outdoor life-skills workshops where students in grades K-12 develop leadership, grit, collaboration, and communication through adventure-based activities.
Conduct motivational coaching sessions informed by student analytics and Coachbot insights to activate every learner toward their objectives and cultivate ownership of their progress.
Maintain your own student cohort while guiding other educators, ensuring your coaching is rooted in present experience rather than past recollection.
Monitor student satisfaction, goal achievement, and Guide effectiveness on a weekly basis to identify and address underperformance early.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Delivering lectures or providing academic tutoring. Students engage with content via self-directed adaptive platforms, frequently without direct adult supervision.
Creating curriculum or lesson plans from the ground up. Established playbooks are in place; success depends on faithful execution and engagement, not innovation.
Training Guides on instructional methods. Since Guides don't lecture, your coaching focuses on motivation, accountability, and relational presence with students.
Compromising standards to preserve comfort. You won't advance a student prematurely or overlook a Guide's lack of performance.
Confining students indoors to desks. A substantial portion of development here occurs outside, through experiential challenge.

Youth Program Director Key Responsibilities

Ensure that every student in your cohort loves school, achieves academic growth, and develops the character and life skills necessary to succeed.

Basic Requirements

Willing to work on-site at Waypoint Academy in Dripping Springs, Texas
Bachelor's degree in education, psychology, business, outdoor education, recreation, youth development, or a related discipline
Minimum of 5 years of experience in education, youth development, coaching, outdoor education, or learning and development (L&D)
Demonstrated history of leading a team of 5 or more adults, including making hiring and performance-based termination decisions
Hands-on experience working with youth ages 5-18 in an educational or developmental capacity
Experience building, launching, or substantially growing a program, team, school, or outdoor initiative from inception, with a concrete and measurable example
Documented use of data and metrics to establish goals and inform decisions, not simply to report outcomes
Legal authorization to work in the United States

Nice-to-have Requirements

Master's degree in a relevant field
Experience coaching athletics, leading wilderness or experiential programs, directing camps, or managing youth programs at a scale requiring cohort management and outcome measurement
Transitioned from classroom teaching to build or manage programs in a different capacity: EdTech, tutoring, youth nonprofits, or school intervention teams
Early-career history of exceptional personal performance—academic, athletic, or professional—prior to entering leadership
Conviction that the conventional education model is fundamentally flawed and personal commitment to its transformation

About Waypoint Academy

Nature-based school that blends rigorous academics with real-world challenges.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Director of Development

Full-Time · On-Site · Philadelphia, PA · $175K–$225K OTE · Partner Track
Design Pro Development is scaling its entitlement pipeline to as many as 30 active projects per year across Philadelphia, Montgomery, Bucks, and Camden County, NJ — including our largest project to date, a 300+ unit residential community, and roughly 10 semi-custom luxury homes ($2MM–$8MM) per year under our Atelier Design + Build division. We're hiring a Director of Development to own that pipeline end to end: every approval, every permit, every township agreement, and every dollar of sitework, on every project.
About Design Pro Development

DPD is a Philadelphia-based real estate development firm with 600+ residential units across ground-up construction, adaptive reuse, and condominium conversion in Philadelphia, Montgomery, Bucks, and southern New Jersey. We specialize in complex sites — off-market acquisitions, historic districts, zoning variances, and challenging entitlements — and move fast without cutting corners.
About the Role

Reporting to the CEO and VP of Capital Markets, you'll be a key decision maker leading projects from inception to stabilization. You'll build a standardized entitlement process — acquisition due diligence through zoning, land development approval, and building permit — and run it across up to 30 simultaneous projects spanning multifamily, condominium conversion, and semi-custom luxury design-build, working independently with no construction administrator for the first 12–24 months. You interrogate every civil, geotechnical, and traffic recommendation, maximize each site's potential while driving down cost, and bring a regional network of zoning attorneys, township solicitors, architects, and engineers. You verify; you don't rubber-stamp.
What You'll Own

Due Diligence Oversight:
Key decision maker over due diligence — site conditions, entitlements, zoning, environmental factors, and financial feasibility before acquisition — coordinating with legal, design, and finance and reporting to the CEO.
Full Entitlement Lifecycle:
Carry up to 30 projects/year from due diligence through zoning relief, land development approval, and building permit across four counties — through construction, marketing/leasing, and stabilization — managing consultants and contractors and hitting KPIs.
Philadelphia Approvals:
L&I permitting, ZBA variances, Civic Design Review, RCO meetings, Historical Commission review, PWD stormwater, and Streets Department coordination.
Suburban Approvals:
Township land development (SALDO), conditional use and special exception hearings, zoning variances, planning commission and board of supervisors presentations, PennDOT HOPs, DEP/NPDES permits, and Act 537 sewer modules in Montgomery and Bucks Counties.
New Jersey Approvals:
Planning board and zoning board of adjustment applications under the NJ Municipal Land Use Law in Camden County — site plan and variance approvals, NJDEP permitting, and soil conservation district review.
Condominium Documents & Association Approvals:
Oversee condominium declarations, plats and plans, and public offering statements with counsel; present renovation plans to associations for board approval and negotiate document amendments.
Development & Utility Agreements:
Negotiate improvement agreements, township escrow and financial security terms, fee-in-lieu arrangements, and traffic/infrastructure contributions; secure service, extension, and tap agreements with water, sewer, and power providers (Aqua PA, PA American Water, PECO, PGW).
Engineering Diligence & Value Engineering:
Rigorously review engineer recommendations on grading, stormwater, utilities, and site layout, and use creative value engineering to optimize budgets and maximize financial success.
Sitework Management & Cost Control:
Manage site design/layout to cut sitework cost across clearing, cul-de-sac construction, utility and infrastructure installation, retaining walls, bridges, and stormwater facilities. Build independent budgets; solicit, level, and negotiate GC/sub bids; challenge unit pricing and quantities; and guard against overpricing, scope gaps, and change-order creep.
AIA Contracts & Document Integrity:
Draft, review, negotiate, and administer AIA agreements (A101/A102/A201, B101) — payment applications, lien-waiver tracking, change orders, and schedule enforcement — verifying the correct drawings, specs, and exhibits are attached so no exclusion shifts cost or risk onto the firm.
Design, Renderings & Sales Support:
Manage interior designers and finish/material selections to hit budgets and out-sales; direct rendering companies for entitlement and marketing visuals; and partner with luxury realtors and sales brokers.
Atelier Design + Build Delivery:
Shepherd ~10 semi-custom luxury design-build projects/year through permitting and contract administration. Build strong relationships with discerning $2MM–$8MM custom-home clients and deliver white-glove execution with financial discipline and on-time delivery.
Budget & Schedule Oversight:
Develop and maintain project budgets and schedules from due diligence through completion — forecasting, cost-saving strategies, and negotiating competitive vendor rates.
AI-Powered Pipeline Tracking:
Build and maintain AI-driven tracking systems (Claude, Asana automations, and related tools) that monitor every approval milestone and flag slipping timelines.
Stakeholder & Cross-Departmental Collaboration:
Build relationships with regulatory agencies, township engineers, and zoning and planning boards; collaborate with the CEO, finance, and VP of Capital Markets; and support strategic research and presentations.

What We're Looking For — Required

Bachelor's degree (Master's preferred) and 10+ years in real estate development or construction management in southeastern PA and/or southern NJ, with a track record across all phases of development.
100+ projects permitted (or 500,000+ sq ft), including 25+ zoning projects and 100+ homesites completed — and the ability to walk us through them.
Minimum 3 years in Montgomery or Bucks County developing homes selling for more than $2MM.
Direct experience entitling large multifamily (200+ units) through PA township land development, and hands-on sitework management on 5+ jobs.
An established regional network of zoning attorneys, township solicitors and engineers, architects, and civil engineers across Philadelphia, Montgomery, Bucks, and Camden Counties.
Working fluency in the PA Municipalities Planning Code, township SALDO and zoning ordinances, the Philadelphia Zoning Code, L&I permitting, and the NJ Municipal Land Use Law — plus a baseline command of construction and zoning law (mechanics' liens, risk allocation, vested rights, appeals).
Condominium creation and governance — PA Uniform Condominium Act and NJ Condominium Act, document drafting and amendment, and negotiating with association boards.
Hands-on experience negotiating development agreements, township escrow and financial security terms, and utility agreements with water, sewer, and power providers.
Owner-side AIA contract experience — drafting, reviewing, and negotiating documents, with expert command of contractor proposals, bid inclusions/exclusions, and complete exhibit packages.
Expert ability reading surveys, civil drawings, construction reports, contracts, and design documents, with the technical depth to independently estimate, qualify, and negotiate sitework costs.
Exceptional project budgeting and value-engineering skill; a creative yet risk-averse problem solver who enacts SOPs and safeguards, with acute attention to detail and a strong sense of urgency.
Strong leadership and communication skills for building relationships with contractors, design professionals, township engineers, and boards.
A masterful command of AI tools, Claude in particular, with real examples of AI for site analysis, cost forecasting, bid evaluation, rendering, estimation, and tracking. Show us what you've built.
Full-time, in-office role; must be able to drive 6–10 hours per week to jobsites.

Preferred

Civil engineering, land planning, construction management, or legal background (PE, JD, or AICP a plus).
Experience standing up entitlement processes and reporting systems at a scaling development firm.

Software Proficiency

Proficient in most of the following (quick to pick up the rest): Claude (AI tracking, follow-up, document review); Asana (multi-project pipeline tracking and automations — our standard); Zapier or Make; Bluebeam Revu (plan review, markups, takeoffs); AutoCAD / Civil 3D; Procore, BuilderTrend, or Autodesk Build; Microsoft Project or Primavera P6; advanced Excel (sitework budgets, bid leveling, proforma); eCLIPSE and Atlas (Philadelphia L&I/records); PennDOT ePermitting (EPS); PA DEP GreenPort and NJDEP; ArcGIS or municipal GIS parcel viewers; PlanSwift/STACK; DocuSign; Adobe Acrobat Pro; and Microsoft Office.
What We Offer

Total compensation of $175,000–$225,000 — a $125,000 base plus quarterly performance and project-based profit-sharing of $50,000–$100,000.
Competitive benefits: medical, short/long-term disability, life insurance, and a 401(k) plan.
Ability to invest in company projects.
A structured pathway to become a Partner after five years.

How to Apply

Email your resume and a Word document with links to photos or project websites to logan@designprodev.com, erica@designprodev.com, and alex@designprodev.com. Include the 10 projects (1–2 sentences each, based on your role) that best exemplify your abilities — the approvals you secured, the timelines you hit, and the sitework dollars you saved — plus at least one AI-powered tracking system or workflow you built and what it caught. Qualified candidates are contacted within three business days.

The families who choose Alpha rely on trusted advisors across every aspect of their lives. This role represents the one they've been waiting for.

You will become the person they reach out to when uncertainty arises, when something doesn't feel quite right, or when they want to share a moment they know you'll appreciate. You'll develop enough familiarity with each family to anticipate their needs before they articulate them—and you'll possess the judgment and composure to address whatever they bring with discretion, warmth, and apparent ease. Over time, your role will extend beyond being part of their child's school. You'll become woven into the fabric of how they experience this chapter of their family journey.

This level of trust isn't built through process. It emerges from presence—daily, steady, unhurried. You'll maintain visibility during morning drop-off and afternoon pick-up, at evening events that hold significance, and in the one-on-one exchanges that never appear on any schedule. You'll cultivate a community that families feel invested in protecting, where belonging feels natural and referrals occur because the experience merits them.

Alpha operates outside traditional school frameworks. Students complete their core academics in two hours daily using AI-powered applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical thinking, and real-world projects. No lectures. No busywork. Top 1% outcomes nationally. The families selecting this model are investing in something they believe in—but belief requires ongoing nurture.

You'll sustain that dialogue with every family, through every moment of uncertainty, throughout their child's enrollment. If defending an unconventional approach to sophisticated skeptics feels burdensome, this position isn't suited to you. What You Will Be Doing

Take ownership of relationships with every family on campus—the continuous, evolving relationships that ensure parents feel recognized, not merely serviced

Serve as the trusted relationship anchor at the heart of every family's Alpha experience. Maintain their confidence through challenging moments, cultivate a community where belonging feels meaningful, and establish the conditions under which satisfied families become active advocates.

Basic Requirements

Personal connection to independent, private, or non-traditional education—through professional experience or as a parent—that provides genuine credibility when families challenge the model
Authentic conviction in AI-powered education and the capacity to sustain that belief credibly across years of parent relationships, not solely during enrollment discussions
Availability for non-standard hours: early mornings (7–9am), late afternoons (2–4pm), evening programming 2–3x monthly, and occasional weekend activities

Established relationships within the local affluent community that would provide immediate, organic integration on campus

Natural ability to design experiences—events, moments, settings—where individuals feel part of something worth safeguarding

**Head Cheerleading Coach \& Program Director**

Location: Yonkers, NY

Position Type: Part\-Time (Year\-Round)  
Approximately 10\-20\+ hours per week depending on season, with opportunity for growth. Starting Pay: $35/hour DOE

Required Schedule: Tuesdays \& Thursdays 5:00\-8:00pm, Saturdays 9:00am\-4:00pm, plus additional remote administrative work and occasional weekend events.

**About New York All Stars**

New York All Stars Fitness \& Performing Arts is one of Westchester County's fastest\-growing youth enrichment organizations. Our mission is to build confident, resilient, and creative young people through competitive cheerleading, performing arts, fitness, leadership, and community.

We're looking for someone who shares that mission.

This is more than a coaching position. We're searching for an inspiring leader who will help shape the future of our cheerleading program while becoming an integral member of our leadership team.

New York All Stars is not a traditional All Star program \- in fact, our programming extends far beyond just cheerleading and includes a multitude of fitness and performing arts opportunities. We've intentionally built a program that blends the athletic excellence of competitive cheerleading with the community, leadership, and inclusive spirit often found in school\-based programs. We believe every athlete deserves high\-quality coaching in an environment that prioritizes teamwork, character, confidence, and belonging as much as competitive success.

**Position Overview**

The Head Cheerleading Coach \& Program Director will oversee our All Star Cheerleading Program, leading practices, preparing teams for competitions, mentoring assistant coaches, and helping families feel welcomed and supported.The ideal candidate believes that success is measured by far more than trophies. They value sportsmanship, teamwork, confidence, accountability, and creating an environment where every athlete can thrive.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead weekly practices for multiple cheer teams, ages 4\-16\.
* Oversee tumbling instructional programs
* Choreograph and clean routines appropriate for each team's level.
* Prepare athletes for competitions throughout the season.
* Teach proper stunt progressions, jumps, tumbling technique, motions, dance, conditioning, and performance skills.
* Mentor, train, and evaluate coaches.
* Foster a positive, encouraging, and disciplined team culture.
* Communicate professionally with families regarding schedules, expectations, and athlete progress.
* Assist with athlete evaluations, placements, and recruiting.
* Coordinate practices, competitions, showcases, and special events.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director to continue growing and improving the program.
* Support fundraising initiatives, community outreach, and promotional events.
* Represent New York All Stars with professionalism both inside and outside the gym.

**Qualifications**

* Cheerleading coaching experience required.
* Strong knowledge of stunting, tumbling progressions, choreography, and safety standards.

Executive Director

The Islamic Center of Wheaton (ICW) seeks an experienced, mission\-driven **Executive Director \& Director of Administrative Affairs** to provide leadership and oversight of the organization’s operations, administration, fundraising, community engagement, educational initiatives, and strategic development.

The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors, committees, staff, volunteers, and community stakeholders to advance ICW’s mission, strengthen organizational effectiveness, support sustainable growth, and foster a welcoming and vibrant Islamic environment.

This position requires a strategic leader with demonstrated experience in nonprofit management, fundraising, financial oversight, team leadership, community development, and organizational administration.

**Key Responsibilities:Organizational Leadership**

* Support and advance ICW’s mission, vision, and strategic objectives.
* Collaborate with the President and Board of Directors to implement organizational priorities.
* Provide regular operational updates, recommendations, and reports to leadership.
* Develop and implement policies, procedures, and operational improvements.
* Promote organizational excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Fundraising \& Development (Critical Function)**

* Lead and support fundraising initiatives to strengthen ICW’s long\-term sustainability.
* Partner with fundraising committees to develop annual fundraising strategies and campaigns.
* Build and maintain relationships with donors, community leaders, sponsors, and supporters.
* Assist in securing grants, sponsorships, endowments (Waqf), major gifts, and planned giving opportunities.

* Develop strategies to diversify revenue sources and strengthen long\-term financial stability.

**Operations Management**

* Oversee day\-to\-day operations of ICW facilities and affiliated educational programs.

* Coordinate vendor relationships and municipal interactions.
* Ensure facility maintenance, safety, and operational readiness.
* Manage organizational records and administrative processes.

**Financial Management**

* Work closely with the Treasurer and Finance Committee on budgeting and financial oversight.
* Assist in maintaining fiscal discipline and responsible resource utilization.
* Support long\-term financial planning and sustainability efforts.
* Monitor operational expenditures and organizational efficiency.

**Human Resources \& Team Leadership**

* Assist with recruitment, hiring, onboarding, supervision, and retention of staff.
* Foster a positive workplace culture and encourage professional development.
* Coordinate staffing plans and operational coverage.
* Support volunteer recruitment, engagement, and recognition efforts.

**Programs \& Community Development**

* Coordinate educational, religious, family, youth, and community programs.
* Support interfaith initiatives and community outreach efforts.
* Work collaboratively with committees to implement organizational programming.

**Youth \& Student Development**

* Develop and support youth mentorship and leadership programs.

The Oregon Boating Foundation, a 501(c)(3) charitable organization located in Newport, Oregon, is looking for an Executive Director with a passion for kayaking, sailing, and outdoor education. The ideal candidate is an experienced leader with excellent verbal and written communication skills that will represent our organization publicly, support a culture of longevity, and grow the capacity of the organization.

This is a unique opportunity for the right person to advance their career, positively impact our organization on a daily basis, and grow our programs.

Job Description

The Executive Director contributes to the Oregon Boating Foundation’s mission of making safe, affordable boating opportunities available to everyone by managing the day-to-day operations of the organization. Additional responsibilities include budgeting, customer service, fundraising, and managing seasonal staff and volunteers. The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors, primarily to the Board President.

Requirements

A passion for non-motorized boating, outdoor education, and getting youth outdoors
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Outdoor Education, Business Management, or similar disciplines
Strong leadership and team-building skills with the ability to manage seasonal employees and volunteers, and work with a Board of Directors

As a proud member of the Feeding America network, Second Harvest of Coastal Georgia is the leading hunger\-relief organization serving 21 counties in our region. With facilities in Savannah and Brunswick, we provide more than 26 million pounds of food each year to over 250 local charitable agencies and programs, including food pantries, shelters, and schools.

Through innovative programs like Kids Cafe, Mobile Food Pantry, and Senior Meals—and in partnership with community organizations and volunteers—Second Harvest is dedicated to nourishing lives, building community resilience, and eliminating food insecurity.

**Position Summary**

Second Harvest of Coastal Georgia is seeking an accomplished and mission\-driven Chief Development Officer to lead the organization’s fundraising, marketing and communications, volunteer engagement, advocacy, and community outreach strategies.

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief Development Officer will provide the strategic vision needed to expand philanthropic support, strengthen community relationships, elevate Second Harvest’s visibility, and ensure long\-term financial sustainability. Reporting directly to the President/CEO and working closely with the Board of Directors, this leader will develop and execute comprehensive annual and multi\-year development plans supporting the organization’s mission and strategic priorities.

The ideal candidate is an experienced fundraising executive, collaborative team leader, compelling communicator, and skilled relationship builder who is energized by the opportunity to make a meaningful difference throughout coastal Georgia.

**Executive Leadership and Strategy**

· Partner with the President/CEO and executive leadership team to establish and advance long\-range organizational goals and strategic priorities.

· Develop annual and multi\-year fundraising and engagement plans with measurable goals and performance indicators.

· Serve as a strategic advisor on philanthropy, communications, volunteer engagement, advocacy, and community relations.

· Monitor philanthropic trends, community needs, economic conditions, and donor behavior to identify opportunities for innovation and sustainable growth.

**Fundraising and Resource Development**

· Lead a comprehensive fundraising program encompassing major gifts, annual giving, direct mail, corporate partnerships, foundation and institutional giving, government grants, planned giving, capital campaigns, special events, and donor stewardship.

· Cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors, corporate sponsors, foundations, and community partners.

· Diversify revenue streams to strengthen organizational sustainability and reduce funding risk.

· Develop compelling cases for support and engagement strategies that improve donor acquisition, retention, and lifetime value.

· Establish effective systems for prospect development, donor recognition, stewardship, and fundraising performance measurement.

· Ensure compliance with applicable legal, ethical, and professional fundraising standards.

**Marketing, Communications, and Brand Leadership**

· Oversee integrated marketing and communications strategies that strengthen Second Harvest’s visibility, reputation, and community impact.

· Direct public relations, digital marketing, social media, storytelling, traditional media, and direct\-response campaigns.

· Guide the development of annual reports, newsletters, impact reports, press releases, campaign materials, and executive communications.

· Serve as an organizational spokesperson and represent Second Harvest at community events, public presentations, stakeholder meetings, and media opportunities.

**Advocacy and Community Engagement**

· Partner with the President/CEO and community leaders to increase awareness of hunger, food insecurity, and related public\-policy issues.

· Build relationships with elected officials, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, corporate partners, civic groups, and advocacy coalitions.

· Develop strategies that educate and engage donors, volunteers, and community stakeholders around hunger\-relief priorities.

· Provide strategic oversight of volunteer services, ensuring meaningful experiences that deepen community involvement and expand organizational capacity.

· Create opportunities for volunteers and community partners to become long\-term supporters, ambassadors, and advocates for Second Harvest’s mission.

**Board and Team Leadership**

· Collaborate with the Board of Directors, Advisory Board, and Development and Communications Committee to advance fundraising and engagement priorities.

· Equip board members with the strategies, information, and tools needed to cultivate relationships and serve as effective organizational ambassadors.

· Lead, mentor, and develop high\-performing development, marketing, communications, and volunteer engagement teams.

· Promote a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and professional growth.

· Establish clear performance expectations and provide employees with ongoing coaching, feedback, and recognition.

**Financial and Operational Management**

· Develop and manage departmental budgets with a strong commitment to responsible stewardship.

· Use fundraising analytics and performance data to evaluate effectiveness, guide decisions, and improve return on investment.

· Identify opportunities to strengthen technology, systems, and operational processes.

**Qualifications, Education, and Experience**

· Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree or Certified Fund Raising Executive designation preferred.

· At least 10 yea

jobs.description:
**Director of Development**  

**Goddard House \| Brookline, Massachusetts**
  

**Position Summary**  

Goddard House, a nonprofit leader in innovative approaches to healthy aging, seeks a dynamic and relationship\-driven Director of Development to lead and grow its philanthropic program. This is a newly created position designed to expand Goddard House’s philanthropic impact and strengthen a culture of philanthropy across the organization.
Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, this role offers a unique opportunity to develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy that supports both the Goddard House assisted living community and the continued expansion of Creative Aging Connections, a Goddard House initiative that advances creative arts engagement and healthy aging for under\-resourced older adults living in Boston and surrounding neighborhoods.
  

The Director of Development will have responsibility for the organization’s fundraising strategy and results, while overseeing key advancement functions that support donor engagement and philanthropic growth. This role is both strategic and hands\-on, requiring the ability to develop long\-term fundraising strategy while actively managing donor relationships and driving near\-term results.
Working closely with the President \& CEO and Board of Trustees, the Director will strengthen relationships with donors and community partners and expand philanthropic investment in Goddard House’s mission to support purpose, autonomy, and choice as we age.
  

**Leadership \& Responsibilities**  

**Strategic Leadership**

* Develop and lead annual fundraising goals and strategies supporting programmatic priorities and capital and facility\-related initiatives.
* Collaborate with senior leadership to articulate compelling opportunities for philanthropic support.

**Fundraising and Donor Engagement**
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, foundations, and corporate partners, building and managing a robust pipeline of prospects.
* Manage a personal portfolio of major donors and prospects, building long\-term relationships and securing significant philanthropic gifts.
* Lead major gift strategy and partner with the CEO and Board of Trustees to cultivate and solicit significant gifts.
* Expand the donor base by developing new opportunities for philanthropic engagement and making targeted asks across all giving levels.
* Represent Goddard House at donor events and community outreach activities.

* Strengthen Goddard House and CAC’s visibility through events, campaigns, partnerships, and public engagement opportunities.
* Collaborate with program and leadership teams to ensure consistent messaging about mission and impact.

**Board Engagement**
* Support the Board of Trustees and Development Committee in advancing fundraising goals.
* Partner with board members to identify, engage and cultivate new donor prospects.
* Provide regular reports on fundraising progress and donor engagement.

**Development Operations \& Infrastructure**
* Oversee donor database management, gift tracking, and development reporting.

* Provide leadership and oversight for staff and external partners, including grant writers and consultants.

**First\-Year Priorities**  

During the first year, the Director of Development will focus on strengthening the organization’s fundraising foundation while beginning to expand philanthropic support.  

**Key priorities include:**
* Developing and implementing a comprehensive fundraising strategy in partnership with the President \& CEO.
* Expanding the donor pipeline and increasing philanthropic support for Creative Aging Connections.
* Cultivating relationships with residents, current and former families, and community supporters.
* Strengthening fundraising infrastructure, systems, and reporting organization\-wide.
* Supporting the Board of Trustees and Development Committee in advancing fundraising engagement.

* 5–7\+ years of progressive nonprofit fundraising experience with demonstrated success meeting revenue goals.
* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or equivalent experience preferred.
* Proven track record cultivating and securing major gifts from individuals, foundations, and corporations.
* Experience managing a personal donor portfolio and building a strong fundraising pipeline aligned to annual revenue targets.
* Experience implementing or contributing to a comprehensive fundraising strategy.
* Strong relationship\-building and communication skills.
* Experience managing donor databases and interpreting fundraising data.
* Highly organized with strong planning and project management abilities.

The CEO Communications Manager opportunity

We’re seeking a high-performing CEO Communications Manager to help amplify the voice and vision of our CEO and drive AI optimization across his communications channels. In this role, you will report to Okta’s Head of CEO Communications and partner closely with the Office of the CEO to support, streamline, and scale the CEO comms platform, spanning internal and external speaking events, media & influencer engagements, and social media. You will also work with the Corporate Communications team and partner with the broader executive bench, cross-functional partners, and our various agencies to develop bylines, blog posts, keynotes, talking points, and thought leadership content.
This is a rare opportunity to sit at the intersection of content, operations, strategy, and execution—all in support of a visionary founder leading a global tech company through transformation and growth. Continuously
apply and explore how AI and agents can securely optimize and automate workflows and content development across the CEO’s communications platform.

Manage inputs, timelines, and deliverables across multiple stakeholders, often coordinating between executives and production/design teams to ensure alignment across all CEO materials.
Operational excellence:
The ideal candidate will thrive in and derive energy from a high-pressure, high-performing environment. Obsessive quality control and meticulous attention to detail are table stakes. You will

jobs.title: Executive Director, CRE Transaction Management and Underwriting
jobs.description:
It Starts Here

Santander is a global leader and innovator in the financial services industry and is evolving from a high-impact brand into a technology-driven organization. Our people are at the heart of this journey and together, we are driving a customer-centric transformation that values bold thinking, innovation, and the courage to challenge what’s possible. This is more than a strategic shift. It’s a chance for driven professionals to grow, learn, and make a real difference.

If you are interested in exploring the possibilities We Want to Talk to You!

The Difference You Make

Santander Corporate & Investment Banking (SCIB) provides a comprehensive suite of financing, advisory, and banking solutions to corporate, financial sponsor, institutional investor, and commercial real estate clients globally. Within SCIB, Commercial Real Estate delivers integrated lending solutions to a diverse client base, including private equity sponsors, institutional investors, developers, REITs, and operating companies.

The Executive Director, Transaction Manager and Underwriter is a senior leader within the Commercial Real Estate platform, responsible for the underwriting, structuring, and overall deal execution of commercial real estate loan transactions across Santander's CMBS Conduit, Single-Asset Single-Borrower (SASB), Balance Sheet, and Warehouse lending platforms. This role serves as a player-coach, combining hands-on transaction leadership with mentorship and development of junior team members. The Executive Director partners closely with the Origination team, Credit Risk, Legal, Middle Office, Operations, and senior management to evaluate opportunities, manage risk, and deliver efficient deal execution from initial screening through loan closing, securitization, syndication, and asset management.

The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in commercial real estate credit, structured finance, and CMBS execution while contributing to the continued growth, profitability, and market presence of Santander's growing Commercial Real Estate platform.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the underwriting, structuring, and execution of CMBS conduit, SASB, Balance Sheet, and Warehouse loan transactions across a broad range of property types and markets throughout the US.
Evaluate borrower submissions, property cash flows, sponsorship, market fundamentals, and third-party due diligence to determine transaction viability and creditworthiness.
Work with the team to structure loan proceeds, pricing, and terms consistent with Santander's risk appetite, credit standards, and profitability objectives.
Prepare and present transaction recommendations to internal credit, investment, and approval committees.
Serve as the primary execution lead throughout the transaction lifecycle, coordinating internal and external stakeholders to ensure timely and successful closings.
Oversee due diligence efforts, including appraisal, engineering, environmental, insurance, legal, and market reviews, both internally and with third-party vendor support relationships.
Coordinate with investors, B-piece buyers, rating agencies, legal counsel, Middle Office, and Operations teams to address transaction-related diligence and closing requirements.
Identify, assess, and mitigate transaction risks while balancing client needs, execution certainty, and portfolio objectives.
Monitor active pipeline activity, closing forecasts, and transaction metrics to support business planning and production goals.
Provide market intelligence and strategic insights regarding commercial real estate fundamentals, lending conditions, and competitive market dynamics.
Act as a player-coach by mentoring, training, and developing junior underwriting and execution professionals.
Contribute to the development and enhancement of underwriting standards, execution processes, and risk management practices.
Maintain current knowledge of commercial real estate market trends, CMBS activity, and industry developments.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Real Estate, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field required.

Experience & Skills

10+ years of commercial real estate lending, CMBS, structured finance, or related experience.
Significant experience underwriting and executing across CMBS conduit/SASB/Balance Sheet transactions.
Strong understanding of CMBS securitization, rating agency methodologies, and institutional investor requirements.
Advanced financial modeling, cash flow analysis, and commercial real estate credit underwriting skills.
Demonstrated leadership experience managing deal teams and mentoring junior professionals.
Proven ability to manage multiple complex transactions in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Strong project management, organizational, and analytical capabilities.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present complex credit matters to senior stakeholders.
Proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive consensus across multiple business functions.
Strong relationship management skills with both internal and external stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience across multiple commercial real estate asset classes, including office, multifamily, industrial, retail, hospitality, and specialty sectors.
Familiarity with loan securitization, warehouse financing, and institutional execution processes.
Established reputation for sound credit judgment and transaction execution within the commercial real estate industry.

What Else You Need To Know

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Company Description
Transcend NYC is a recovery-focused organization offering a recovery residence, a strong alumni program, and comprehensive peer support services. The recovery residence is a luxury five-story brownstone located in New York City’s historic Upper West Side, providing men with safe, supportive housing during their recovery journeys. Clients benefit from individualized peer services, working 1-on-1 with experienced recovery coaches and case managers. These professionals draw on their own recovery experience to help clients navigate resources, build stability, and sustain long-term wellness. Transcend NYC fosters a community-centered environment that emphasizes accountability, compassion, and personal growth.

Role Description The Program Director is a full-time, on-site role at our locatuon on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, responsible for overseeing the daily operations and quality of services within the recovery residence and associated programs. This role manages program staffing, scheduling, and supervision to ensure consistent, client-centered support and adherence to organizational policies and regulatory standards. The Program Director collaborates with recovery coaches, case managers, and other team members to design and refine programming, monitor client progress, and address individual needs. Daily responsibilities include coordinating intakes and discharges, maintaining accurate documentation, and ensuring clear communication with clients, families, and external partners. The position also involves continuous program evaluation, implementing improvements, and supporting a safe, structured environment aligned with Transcend NYC’s mission an
d values. Qualifications

Program management and leadership skills, including experience overseeing residential or behavioral health programs, supervising staff, and coordinating daily operations.
Client services and case management skills, such as conducting assessments, developing support plans, monitoring progress, and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams.
Communication and relationship-building skills, including the ability to communicate clearly with clients, families, staff, and community partners, and to handle sensitive information with discretion.
Crisis management and problem-solving skills, with the capacity to respond calmly to emergencies, resolve conflicts, and make sound decisions in fast-paced environments.
Knowledge of recovery-oriented care, substance use and mental health services, and best practices in peer support and supportive housing.
Strong organizational and documentation skills, including maintaining accurate records, tracking program metrics, and supporting compliance with policies and applicable regulations.
Ability to work on-site in New York, NY, maintain a consistent full-time schedule, and foster a safe, inclusive, and non-judgmental environment for all residents.
Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, counseling, public health, or a related field; an advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., CASAC, peer specialist) are preferred.
Previous experience in recovery services, residential treatment a plus.
