Job Summary

The Director of Development for Campaign Initiatives is a front-line fundraising professional responsible for developing and executing strategies to secure philanthropic support for select campaign priorities, multi-disciplinary projects, and non-college specific initiatives across San José State University. Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Development, the Director will provide strategic direction and vision for key fundraising priorities, develop prospect pipelines, and craft compelling cases for support for a variety of fundraising projects and programs. Campaign initiatives for which the incumbent will have primary fundraising responsibility include, but are not limited to, the preservation of Tower Hall, Speed City Legacy Track, Artificial Intelligence, and campaign initiatives from the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library.

The responsibilities include but are not limited to identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting and stewarding individuals capable of making major and principal gifts to the University. In support of these efforts, the Director maintains and strengthens close working relationships with key academic leaders, campus administrators, various stakeholders and University Advancement colleagues to build consensus around complex funding opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Manage an assigned portfolio of key prospects and individuals whose capacity and interests align with university-wide strategic initiatives and campaign priorities
Coordinate with Advancement Research and Prospect Research to proactively build and qualify a robust prospect pipeline
Develop and execute complex strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit and steward major gift prospects/donors, including joint solicitations on multi-unit projects
Present and regularly review top prospect strategies with immediate supervisor and other key team members as appropriate
Work collaboratively with university administrators, academic leadership and other stakeholders to gain counsel and offer expertise on donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategy
Work collaboratively with peers across all development units (Major Gifts, Annual Giving, Planned Giving, Corporate & Foundation Relations) and serve as a key horizontal partner on multi-unit projects
Work with volunteer leadership of university boards, councils and committees to maximize cultivation and solicitation efforts
Focus on securing funding for designated priorities including but not limited to academic programs, endowed chairs and professorships, scholarships, unrestricted support, facility renovations, new facilities and other specified priorities
Collaborate with donor relations colleagues with stewardship efforts to promote a culture of gratitude among internal and external constituents
Develop comprehensive, persuasive proposals for complex, multi-unit funding opportunities, gathering data and buy-in from various campus stakeholder
Effectively utilize campus data management systems and enter prospect/donor contact reports and their relevant data in a timely fashion
Participate in staff, functional and strategy meetings including prospect review sessions, and attend conferences, seminars and other development training as feasible and appropriate

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Ability to identify donors and close gifts of six and seven figures
Ability to navigate the complexity of a large, dynamic university and establish consensus among varied stakeholders to make the appropriate match for donor interests
Skilled in networking, high-level prospect discovery and opening doors among new donor segments, coupled with the ability to design and implement sophisticated, donor-centric cultivation and solicitation strategies
Superior ability to successfully manage multiple, large-scale projects with evolving priorities on tight deadlines and under pressure in a dynamic, politically complex and open environment
Exceptional skill in defining problems, gathering and synthesizing complex data, establishing facts and drawing valid conclusions
Exceptional verbal communication and persuasive writing skills
High level of initiative, attention to detail, and organization skills
Proficient in Google Suite and Microsoft Office Suite, and ability to utilize fundraising database programs and learn new tech platforms for project management
Ability to communicate with constituents in a professional and respectful manner

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
Minimum of three to five years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising
Experience developing and leading complex solicitation strategies resulting in closing major gifts
Evidence of superior written communication skills; ability to articulate and draft persuasive proposals

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree
Experience in identifying, qualifying, and building strategies for new prospects, particularly those with capacity for seven-figure gifts or higher
Fundraising experience within a comprehensive campaign setting at a research or public institution of higher education, specifically managing non-college or cross-disciplinary campaign priorities
Experience serving as a strategic partner to campus administrators and academic leaders

jobs.description:
About Achievement First

Achievement First (AF) is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization supporting 39 public charter schools across New York, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. For more than 25 years, AF has been recognized as one of the top tuition-free public charter school networks in the country. We are committed to creating schools of academic excellence within nurturing environments — schools that prepare students to be college-ready and to pursue and succeed in whatever paths they choose in life.

The majority of AF students are Black and Latinx children from low-income families, many of whom will be the first in their families to graduate from college. Across our network, we employ more than 2,200 staff members — 64% of whom identify as Black, Indigenous, or People of Color — who collectively educate nearly 15,000 students in Brooklyn and Queens, NY; New Haven, Bridgeport, and Hartford, CT; and Providence and Cranston, RI. Our annual budget across all of our charters is approximately $350 million.

Our mission is to prepare every student to excel in college, career, and life; deepen their understanding of self and community;
and lead lives of purpose. We believe in the limitless potential within our students and their power to shape a more just society. That belief drives our deep commitment to student achievement: we aim to set a high bar for learning and create warm, demanding classrooms where rigorous instruction is paired with the care, encouragement, and consistency every student deserves.

Your Impact

The Managing Director of Budgeting is responsible for creating, balancing, and maintaining all school budgets and forecasts, as well as supporting the creation and maintenance of Network Support team budgets, overseeing a total budget of approximately $350 million. This includes working directly with schools and regional staff to address budget challenges, identifying and escalating issues to senior leadership, preparing Board reports, and completing all required monthly forecasting tasks.

In addition, this role owns the maintenance and operations of the budgeting and forecasting platform, Workday Adaptive Planning, and provides training and support to budget owners on both budgeting processes and technical system use.

Reporting directly to the Associate Chief of Financial Planning & Analysis, you will be responsible for:

Develop and Lead the School Budget Process

Integrate information from team leads across Network Support, including Executive Team members and Regional Executive Directors, to determine expense budget targets
Incorporate grant funding and other diverse and restricted revenue sources into final budgets
Facilitate budget trade-off discussions for decision making by Regional Executive Directors and the Executive Team, as needed to achieve budget balance
Hold budget meetings with budget owners to review process, answer questions, and ensure team is on track to balance budget for Board approvals
Oversee annual Adaptive Planning (ERP system) budget data loading process
Maintain system functionality, reports, and integration with other systems (e.g. Intacct) and data integrity; amend structure of system as required

Design and Manage School Budget Forecasting

Develop and manage forecasting processes for schools; lead change management on these processes
Communicate directly with schools and engage on process
Lead budget/forecast analysis for each school/team for items trending off from budget and communicate with owners on a monthly basis, at minimum
Plan and manage grant revenues and expenditures with school leaders and grants team
Lead detailed, trend- and actuals-based analysis of school-based forecasts and apply centralized adjustments to improve accuracy for end-of-year results
Manage regional budgets by charter and adjust modified budgets as resources are approved for deployment by Regional Executive Directors
Prepare quarterly Board reports analyzing data as needed
Prepare reporting and communication on budget vs. forecast variance for outside teams (KPI, CEO) and internal (CFO, Associate Chief)

Lead Training of Budget Owners

Design and lead training for budget owners to learn about the process and how to use Adaptive Planning; hold recurring office hours during monthly forecasting and annual budgeting processes
Create and maintain budgeting and forecasting training tools and materials, updating on an annual basis or more frequently as required
Develop, implement, and lead recurring high-level budget training for school leaders and budget owners

Lead and Develop the Team

Manage two Senior Associate level direct reports who support budgeting and forecasting work at the organization level
Mentor staff in conducting 1:1 budget meetings and trainings with budget owners
Provide in-person and hands-on support to senior executives on budget
Facilitate upskilling of school-based leaders on budget and forecasting

Skills You’ll Have

All candidates for this position will demonstrate strong financial acumen, systems proficiency, and the ability to lead complex cross-functional processes in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

All candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree (B.A., B.S., etc.); a Finance or Accounting degree is strongly preferred.

An ideal candidate will demonstrate competency in the following areas:

Budgeting, forecasting, and standard accounting practices
Full-cycle budget preparation and management at organizational scale
Workday Adaptive Planning or comparable ERP/budgeting systems
Advanced Excel skills and strong analytical capabilities
KPIs, financial metrics, and variance analysis
Clear and effective written and verbal communication
Training design and facilitation for diverse audiences
Team leadership and staff development

In addition, the following characteristics are required to be successful on this team:

Strong ethics and ability to maintain a high level of confidentiality
Confidence in interacting with and influencing individuals at all levels of the organization
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment; flexible, able to work autonomously as well as take direction as needed
Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and follow-through
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with a proactive communication style
Belief in the Achievement First mission and educational model

Travel Expectations

This is a hybrid role. The expectation is that the person in the role would live in one of our 3 regions and be able to come into the Network Support office (NYC, CT, or RI) at least 3 days a week. There may be additional travel to regions outside of your own on a monthly basis.

Compensation

Achievement First sets salaries are set through a lens of equity, and based on the requisite skills, education, and experience relevant to the role. The salary for this position is 150,331. In order to uphold our commitment to equity, Achievement First does not negotiate pay. Additionally, Achievement First offers to all regular, full-time employees a comprehensive benefits package that includes paid time off, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 403(b) retirement benefit package with match, and paid Family Leave.

Achievement First is an equal opportunity employer and an organization that values diversity. People from all diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Job Description

THE OPPORTUNITY AT THE DECATUR FAMILY YMCA

The Decatur Family YMCA is seeking a mission-driven, community-centered Chief Executive Officer to lead one of Central Illinois’ long-standing community institutions into its next era of impact, growth, and sustainability. For nearly 150 years, the Decatur Family YMCA has been woven into the fabric of Decatur and Macon County, serving as a trusted gathering place where children discover confidence and possibility, families find support, adults pursue health and wellness, and neighbors of all backgrounds experience connection, belonging, and care.

This is a meaningful leadership opportunity for a visible, relational, and strategic executive who understands both the heart and business of the YMCA. The next CEO will step into an organization with a proud legacy, an engaged volunteer Board of Directors, a committed leadership team, valued community partnerships, and a clear strategic direction shaped by the Board and staff leadership in summer 2025. Building from this foundation, the CEO will have the opportunity to elevate the Y’s community presence, strengthen operational performance, expand philanthropic investment, and tell a more powerful story of the Y’s role in improving lives across Decatur and Macon County.

The ideal leader will bring disciplined executive management, authentic relationship-building, and an entrepreneurial spirit to help the Decatur Family YMCA meet the evolving needs of its community. This is a moment for a leader who can honor the Y’s deep roots while bringing fresh energy, focus, and vision to its future.

About The Decatur Family Ymca

For nearly 150 years, the Decatur Family YMCA has stood as one of Decatur and Macon County’s trusted anchors for youth development, healthy living, and community connection. Rooted in Christian principles and committed to building healthy spirit, mind, and body for all, the Y has earned a meaningful place in the lives of generations of children, families, adults, seniors, volunteers, donors, and community partners.

From its home at 220 W. McKinley Avenue, the Decatur Family YMCA serves as far more than a fitness facility. It is a place where children take their first swim lessons, young people find safe and enriching spaces before and after school, families access trusted childcare, adults pursue healthier lifestyles, seniors remain active and connected, and neighbors find encouragement, belonging, and support. Through preschool, school-age care, Camp Sokkia, aquatics and swim safety, health and wellness, senior wellness, personal training, evidence-based health programs, financial assistance, and community outreach, the Y responds to the evolving needs of the community while staying grounded in its mission.

The Y’s 2026 theme, “No Place Like This Place,” captures the spirit of an organization that is deeply personal to the community it serves. At its best, the Decatur Family YMCA is where programs become relationships, where participation becomes belonging, and where everyday experiences create lasting impact. As the organization looks ahead, it is positioned to build on that trust, sharpen its story, strengthen its reach, and continue serving as a vital community partner for Decatur and Macon County.

Our Mission

To put Christian principles into practice through programs that build a healthy spirit, mind, and body for all.

Our Cause & Values

To strengthen the foundations of community and instill the values of caring, honesty, respect, and responsibility.

Our Culture

The Y Experience – The Y Experience is built from our mission and encompasses the values and philosophy by which we serve and operate
Welcoming – We are open to all. We are a place where you can be yourself and find yourself in others.
Genuine – We value you and embrace your individuality.
Hopeful – We believe in you and your potential to do good in the world.
Nurturing – We support you as you become the best-version-of-yourself.
Determined – Above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger, beginning with you

Current Key Strategic Initiatives

Growth - expanding our reach, deepening engagement, and building partnerships to serve more individuals and families. Marketing - elevating the Y’s visibility through consistent messaging and meaningful community connection. Fundraising - ensuring long-term sustainability by strengthening donor relationships and expanding philanthropic support.

About Our Community

Decatur and Macon County offer the next CEO a community defined by pride, partnership, resilience, and possibility. Located in the heart of Central Illinois, Decatur combines the accessibility and affordability of a mid-sized community with the assets, employers, institutions, and civic infrastructure that create meaningful opportunities for impact. The area offers affordable housing, family-friendly neighborhoods, parks and recreation, and convenient proximity to Springfield, Champaign-Urbana, Bloomington-Normal, and key interstate transportation routes.

The region is supported by a diverse economic base that includes agribusiness and food processing, manufacturing, health care, logistics, education, and economic development. Major employers and community assets highlighted in the resource materials include Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), Caterpillar, TCCI, Memorial Health, HSHS St. Mary’s Hospital, Midwest Inland Port, the Economic Development Corporation of Decatur and Macon County, Richland Community College, Millikin University, United Way of Decatur and Mid-Illinois, and a strong network of civic and philanthropic partners.

Life in Decatur is enriched by Lake Decatur, Scovill Zoo, golf courses, parks and trails, arts and civic events, the Devon Lakeshore Amphitheater, local schools and colleges, and a deep tradition of volunteerism and community engagement. For a CEO who wants to be visible, accessible, and meaningfully involved in the life of the community, Decatur offers a powerful setting for leadership. It is a place where relationships are personal, civic pride runs deep, and trusted institutions like the YMCA have an opportunity to bring people together, strengthen families, support health and well-being, and contribute to a stronger future for children, adults, and communities across Macon County.

jobs.title: Co-Founder & Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
About Ukambas
Ukambas is building an AI-powered Business Operating System that transforms fragmented operational information into clear, explainable executive intelligence. Rather than replacing accounting, project-management, CRM, inventory, or field-service platforms, Ukambas is designed to interpret the information generated by those systems and help business leaders understand what requires attention and what decisions should come next.

Our initial market is small and medium-sized HVAC contractors in the United States, including residential, commercial, and service-and-maintenance businesses. The long-term vision is to expand the Operational Intelligence Platform into construction, plumbing, electrical, roofing, manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and professional services.

The Opportunity
We are looking for a driven, resilient, and business-oriented Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer
to join Ukambas during its early stage.

This is not a traditional 9-to-5 position. It is a founding partnership for someone prepared to help shape the company, validate the market, develop operating systems, acquire early customers, and scale the business from the ground up.

You will work directly with the Founder and CEO to turn Ukambas’ product vision into a disciplined, customer-focused, and commercially sustainable company.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic leadership:
Co-develop the company strategy, business model, go-to-market plan, milestones, and operating priorities.

Operations:
Build and lead the company’s operational foundation, including internal processes, pilot programs, customer onboarding, performance measurement, and execution discipline.

Customer discovery:
Develop relationships with HVAC owners and executives, understand their workflows and financial challenges, and translate market feedback into clear business requirements.

Go-to-market execution:
Help define Ukambas’ early-access strategy, pilot structure, pricing approach, partnerships, sales process, and customer-success model.

Fundraising:
Partner with the Founder and CEO to prepare pitch materials, develop financial and operational narratives, meet investors, and pursue appropriate funding opportunities.

Team building:
Recruit, lead, and inspire a high-performing early-stage team as the company grows.

Cross-functional leadership:
Connect customer needs, business outcomes, product priorities, and operational execution.

Culture:
Help establish a culture centered on customer value, ownership, transparency, simplicity, continuous improvement, and long-term thinking.

What We Are Looking For
Entrepreneurial grit:
Experience building a business, department, product, operating model, or customer program from the ground up.

Complementary expertise:
Strong experience in one or more of the following areas:

• B2B SaaS operations
• HVAC or construction-industry operations
• Enterprise or contractor-focused sales
• Customer discovery and pilot management
• Business development and strategic partnerships
• Financial planning and fundraising
• Startup go-to-market execution

Business-first thinking:
You understand that technology is a tool for producing better business outcomes—not the objective itself.

Systems thinking:
You can evaluate how people, processes, technology, and financial outcomes influence one another.

Customer focus:
You are willing to spend significant time understanding customers, workflows, operational pain, financial impact, and expected outcomes before recommending solutions.

Commitment:
Ability and willingness to dedicate full-time attention to the venture.

Resilience:
Comfortable operating with limited resources, incomplete information, changing priorities, and the realities of an early-stage startup.

Communication:
Able to communicate complex business challenges clearly to customers, team members, partners, and investors.

Ethical alignment:
Committed to transparency, explainability, responsible AI, data security, and protecting customer trust.

Leadership Alignment
The successful candidate must strongly align with the principles that guide Ukambas:

• Customer value comes first
• Business before technology
• Decisions over reports
• Simplicity wins
• Data requires context
• Trust is built through transparency
• AI assists; humans decide
• Documentation is part of the product
• Long-term sustainability matters more than short-term convenience

At Ukambas, customers do not simply need another dashboard. They need greater confidence in their decisions. Our purpose is to transform operational complexity into clear, explainable intelligence while keeping business leaders fully accountable and in control.

What We Offer
Co-Founder status:
A meaningful equity stake negotiated according to experience, commitment, responsibilities, vesting terms, and long-term contribution.

Strategic influence:
A direct role in shaping the company, operating model, customer strategy, product priorities, and organizational culture.

Operational ownership:
Authority and responsibility to build the business operations and go-to-market organization from the beginning.

Long-term opportunity:
The opportunity to help develop an ambitious platform intended to serve multiple industries and become a trusted source of executive intelligence.

Mission-driven work:
The chance to help business owners spend less time searching for information and more time making confident decisions.

How to Apply
Please submit:

• Your LinkedIn profile or résumé
• A brief introduction describing why you are interested in joining Ukambas as a co-founder
• Examples of businesses, teams, operations, partnerships, or go-to-market programs you have built
• Your availability and expected level of commitment
• The complementary experience you would bring to the founding team

This opportunity is best suited for someone seeking genuine ownership, responsibility, and long-term partnership—not simply a job title.

jobs.description:
What You'll Be Doing

As the Deputy Director of Budget & Management Services
, you will help shape the County’s direction and guide the work that enables long-term stability and strategic investment. You will work with the Budget Director and senior leadership across the organization, bringing clarity to complex policy and financial issues and strengthening the County’s ability to serve a growing community.

You will lead a talented team of budget managers, performance consultants and budget analysts while cultivating a culture of collaboration, trust, and high performance. This role balances people leadership, strategic financial insight, and the ability to build strong relationships with partners at every level.

In This Role, You Will

Lead major components of the annual budget process and provide analysis that informs the County’s most significant decisions.
Build strong working relationships with department leaders and the County Manager’s Office to align resources with community and operational priorities.
Directly supervise three Budget Managers who each supervise a team of budget analysts and performance consultants.
Mentor direct reports and their respective teams, cultivating a culture of growth, empowerment, accountability, and service.
Champion process improvements and technology enhancements that increase transparency, efficiency, and impact.
Navigate complex issues, develop well-reasoned solutions, and communicate recommendations and alternatives in a way that builds understanding and confidence.
Represent the Director when needed and lead special projects that move the organization forward.

Successful candidates will be strategic thinkers and effective communicators who lead with empathy and resilience. They must understand how to drive system-wide improvements while supporting frontline staff and internal clients.

If you enjoy leading people, solving complex challenges, and working collaboratively to shape a stronger future, this is a role where your leadership will matter every day.

About Our Team

Our work connects people, ideas, and insights across the organization to drive smart decisions and deliver results for residents. You build trust and credibility with executives, peers, and staff through clear communication and a collaborative approach.

jobs.description:
Job Details

Description

The Regal Brands family of companies produces decorative hardware products ranging from vintage interior door handle sets to hinges and cabinet hardware, representing a wide range of styles and décor. Our products are sold through various e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Wayfair, and our own website. We are currently seeking a Director of Operations to lead our warehouse, assembly, shipping, and quality control teams in Denver, Colorado. This position offers an anticipated starting salary of $120,000 - $140,000 annually, plus bonus opportunities, and eligibility for our full benefits package, including health, dental, life, and 401(k).

What You’ll Enjoy

Competitive starting pay

$120,000 - $140,000 per year, salaried, with bonus opportunities.

Comprehensive Benefits Package

Medical, dental, vision, short-term and long-term disability, 401(k), paid holidays, and vacation.

Great work environment

We are a small but established company in the home décor space that invests in the right people. We have enjoyed an established pattern of growth and have no intention of slowing down.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Reporting to the General Manager, the Director of Operations will provide leadership for approximately 40 employees and three managers across our shipping, logistics, receiving, warehousing, assembly, and quality control teams. This position is responsible for leading multiple department managers while driving continuous improvement efforts to keep our already thriving operation moving forward. This position will be the senior leader for the following departments:

Warehouse shipping, receiving, and assembly/packing teams. This team consists of approximately 20 employees and one manager who are responsible for receiving inventory, storing products, assembling customer orders, and shipping complete orders.
Quality Control team. This team consists of one manager and three employees responsible for inspecting products received from overseas suppliers and ensuring they are free of defects and blemishes before being released into inventory.
Individual contributors, including our Buyer, who is responsible for procuring inventory and managing supplier orders, and our Project Manager, who leads process improvement initiatives.

Other areas of responsibility include but are not limited to:

Overall responsibility for day-to-day operations.
Managing departmental budgets.
Leading, coaching, and developing managers and employees.
Driving continuous improvement initiatives, utilizing our project manager.
Identifying risks early and leading mitigation strategies.
Assisting with new product development.
Ensuring compliance with OSHA and safety standards.

Who We Are Seeking

The ideal candidate is a proven operational leader with extensive experience in e-commerce fulfillment, manufacturing, and supply chain operations. This individual has a track record of building high-performing teams, driving continuous improvement, and scaling operations while maintaining exceptional quality and customer service. Required qualifications are as follows:

10 years of senior leadership experience in e-commerce, fulfillment, manufacturing, or a similar area.
Subject matter expertise in LEAN Manufacturing, Six Sigma, continuous improvement, or a similar area.
Experience with e-commerce, ideally with systems such as Shopify.
Experience creating, managing, and updating Gantt charts.
Experience with project management methodologies, including Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, and new product introduction (NPI) processes.

Who We Are

Regal Brands is home to four premium hardware brands, representing a wide range of styles and décor. Our brands include our flagship, Nostalgic Warehouse, in the Vintage Hardware space, Grandeur Hardware, in the premium Transitional genre, Ageless Iron, a Rustic Farmhouse style, and Viaggio Hardware, our newest entry into the contemporary design arena. Products from our companies are made with quality and durability in mind and our business model nurtures relationships with e-commerce channel partners, as well as offering our own e-commerce purchasing experience through our individual brand websites. We also serve a select number of brick-and-mortar showrooms that represent our products. As a premier door hardware manufacturer, every aspect of growth has been tempered with consideration for the business and consumer communities we serve, based on practices that are fair and sustainable.

jobs.title: Program Director Burn
jobs.description:
Summary

Job Summary

The Burn Program Director provides leadership, strategic direction, and administrative oversight of the burn program. This role is responsible for the development, growth, and sustainability of the burn center, ensuring compliance with American Burn Association (ABA) verification standards and alignment with organizational strategic priorities. Serves as the primary liaison between hospital executive leadership and the burn medical director, leading multidisciplinary collaboration across the continuum of care and ensuring clinical quality, operational excellence, financial stewardship, and regulatory compliance. Responsible for education, staff (direct reports and clinical oversight for those who provide burn care), inventory, resources, knowledge management, and multidisciplinary collaboration.

Minimum Job Requirements

Work Experience

Three years in program leadership (burn, trauma, or critical care. Demonstrated experience in program development, accreditation, and performance improvement.

Five years of progressive management clinical and operational experience required.

License/Registration/Certification

Current Texas Registered Nurse (RN) license or Compact RN license required.

Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required.

Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) and Advanced Burn Life Support (ABLS) certifications required; may be obtained within one year of placement in the position.

Certified Burn Registered Nurse (CBRN) certification through the Board of Certification for Emergency Nursing (BCEN) required; may be obtained within two years of placement in the position.

Trauma Nursing Core Course (TNCC) or Advanced Trauma Care for Nurses (ATCN) certification required; may be obtained within one year of placement in the position.

Education and Training

Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) required.

Master’s degree in Nursing, Healthcare Administration, or Business Administration preferred.

Skills

Advanced knowledge of burn care, nursing practice standards, and factors affecting the delivery of patient care services.
Ability to lead organizational changes and strategic initiatives that improve patient care, clinical outcomes, and nursing practice.
Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and verification standards applicable to burn programs and healthcare operations.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to build high-performing teams and promote collaboration, accountability, and shared goals.
Well-developed verbal, written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
Proven ability to negotiate, mediate, and build consensus among physicians, leadership, staff, and external stakeholders.
Strong analytical, numerical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to develop, implement, and evaluate strategic plans, operational initiatives, and program growth opportunities.
Knowledge of performance improvement, quality management, patient safety, and outcome measurement methodologies.
Ability to effectively manage budgets, financial resources, capital planning, and operational performance.
Demonstrated teaching, coaching, mentoring, presentation, and educational program development skills.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, coordinate care across the continuum, and facilitate effective patient progression and discharge planning.
Ability to plan and successfully execute projects and change initiatives of significant scope and complexity.
Ability to cultivate and maintain productive relationships with community agencies, referral sources, professional organizations, and healthcare partners.
Ability to serve as a clinical expert and role model while fostering a culture of excellence, innovation, customer service, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
### **Our Work**



We are an architecture and real estate development social enterprise creating spaces that embody justice, healing, and self\-determination. By designing with communities most impacted by incarceration and disinvestment, we build infrastructure that supports community ownership, redistributes power, and lays the foundation for a world rooted in care, not punishment.



To achieve this mission our team is composed of architects, designers, real estate developers and community members working together to create solutionary spaces and places that bring dignity, well\-being and care to the communities we serve.

**The Role**


**Managing Director ·** **Oakland, CA · Hybrid: 3 days in office · $200,000 – $225,000 · Reports to Executive Director**



The Managing Director is a pivotal executive leadership role at DJDS — a steady, strategic presence who holds the interior so the Executive Director can focus externally. This is a cross\-sectional role for someone who can lead a multidisciplinary team with both rigor and heart, and who understands that building a sustainable, mission\-driven organization is itself an act of transformation.



We're looking for someone whose career began in architecture or real estate development and grew beyond it — into community development, into the relationship\-rich, trust\-dependent work of designing and building with communities, and into the adaptive, solutionary leadership it takes to guide a complex organization through a rapidly changing world. The path could have started anywhere on that spectrum — what matters is the curiosity and conviction that shaped the journey.



This is not a role for someone drawn to the traditional practice model. It's a role for someone whose technical foundation gave them a language for the built environment, and whose career since has been driven by a deeper question: what can that environment do for communities who have long been the architects of their own resilience — and deserve infrastructure that reflects it.



You'll own the day\-to\-day leadership of our real estate and architecture verticals — work that is deeply intersecting with fundraising and day\-to\-day operations. You will be second to the Executive Director, partnering closely with her to steward strategy, culture, and growth.


**What You'll Lead**



***Operations \& Team Leadership***


* Serve as the internal anchor for the organization's professional services work — keeping teams resourced, coordinated, and moving toward shared impact
* Directly manage the Studio Director, Director of Real Estate Development (West Coast and East Coast), and Director of Business Development— with the expectation that the team will grow.
* Set goals, work plans, and KPIs across verticals; hold high standards with care and consistency
* Build systems that support clarity, collaboration, and efficiency — without sacrificing the relational culture that makes this work possible
* Support the COO/CFO and Executive Director on organizational operations, financial sustainability, and strategic planning


***Strategy \& Project Decisions***


* Lead the process of project selection based on strategic alignment, mission fit, capacity, and impact potential
* You'll own the day\-to\-day leadership of our real estate and architecture verticals — work that is deeply intersecting with fundraising and day\-to\-day operations. You will be second to the Executive Director, partnering closely with her to steward strategy, culture, and growth.
* Shape and execute long\-term growth strategy in partnership with the Executive Director and sector leaders
* Identify opportunities to improve processes, efficiencies, and earned income across architecture and development verticals


***Business Development \& External Relationships***


* Partner with the Executive Director and Director of Business Development and Strategic Partnerships to support national business development — identifying mission\-aligned opportunities, pitching, and securing new work
* Engage with external partners, funders, and community stakeholders to raise awareness of DJDS's mission and support fundraising
* Participate in community engagement and design processes with genuine curiosity and care for the communities we serve


***Project Level Work***


* Lead at least one project in the portfolio at all times — this is a working leadership role with direct billability expectations, not a purely supervisory one
* Bring a practiced eye to project selection — helping evaluate which opportunities to pursue, which to decline, and why
* Support business development by contributing to proposals, pitches, and client relationships alongside the Executive Director and sector leaders
* Ensure that the way we work on projects reflects how we believe the world should work — with community, with care, and with rigor


**Who You Are**



Your career has taken you across disciplines and into leadership that most people can't easily categorize — and that's exactly the point. You've been front\-facing on large, complex projects — whether as an owner's representative, a project manager on the architecture side, or in a community\-facing leadership role where the stakes were high and the stakeholders were many. You understand how buildings get made and you're equally interested in what they mean to the people who use them. We know no single person will arrive with all of this — what matters most is the combination of experience, curiosity, and values you bring to the role.


* You have 15\+ years of experience across architecture and real estate development, with significant time in community management or owner\-side project leadership
* You have 10\+ years in organizational leadership, with a track record of growing teams and managing across disciplines
* You bring expertise in at least one field and the curiosity to work fluidly across many others — connecting dots between disciplines, bringing unexpected perspectives

jobs.title: Program Director I
jobs.description:
**This recruitment is being managed by NPAG. For consideration please apply at this link:** https://recruitcrm.io/apply/17793124534500079448GXt


\*\*\*\*Do no apply or submit application materials directly to the State Bar. All information should be sent through the application link above. \*\*\*


The Director of Grants oversees the administration of the legal aid grant portfolio of the largest state bar in the country—approximately $300 million distributed annually across multiple grant programs to more than 110 legal aid nonprofit organizations statewide. The Director leads a grants team of more than 20 staff and is accountable for the integrity, compliance, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the State Bar’s grantmaking operations.


The Director serves as a key staff partner to the Legal Services Trust Fund Commission (LSTFC), helping advance the LSTFC’s 2024–2028 strategic plan, the State Bar’s 2022\-2027 strategic plan, and ensures that every grant program is administered responsibly, equitably, and in alignment with the State Bar’s mission to close the justice gap in California. This is a senior leadership role that blends program strategy, fiscal and compliance oversight, stakeholder engagement, and people management. This role reports directly to the OA\&I Program Director II and functions as a core member of the OA\&I executive leadership team, contributing to strategic direction and organizational leadership. This is, above all, a hands\-on leadership role grounded in day\-to\-day grants management and staff supervision, combined with fiscal and compliance oversight, stakeholder engagement, and program strategy.  

  



**About the Office**

The Office of Access \& Inclusion (OA\&I) works to increase access to legal services and to promote diversity and inclusion in the legal profession. As the state’s largest funder of civil legal aid, OA\&I supports free legal services to indigent Californians and advances initiatives to expand legal access to low\- and moderate\-income communities. OA\&I also works to strengthen the pipeline into the legal profession to better reflect California’s diversity, address disparities in retention and advancement, and advance strategies that support inclusive and equitable practices among legal employers. OA\&I has a staff of approximately 30, including a dedicated grants team of more than 20\. In partnership with the LSTFC — the 24\-member body that oversees grantmaking and access to justice work — and the State Bar's Board of Trustees, OA\&I distributed roughly $300 million in 2026 to 118 nonprofit legal aid organizations serving all 58 California counties. These organizations provide free legal help to low income and underserved Californians on the civil matters that shape people's lives — such as housing and eviction, domestic violence, immigration, consumer debt, and access to public benefits — ensuring that the promise of justice does not depend on the ability to pay.


We are a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where all of our employees and prospective employees experience fairness, dignity, and respect.

jobs.title: Senior Executive Director (0998): Communications Department
jobs.description:
**Job Class:** 0998 Senior Executive Director of Communications

**Salary Range:** $181,221\.80 \- $235,994\.40/annually

**Appointment Type:** Permanent Exempt (what does this mean?)

**Length of Appointment:** Permanent Exempt, Full Time not to exceed three (3\) years. This position is excluded by the Charter from competitive Civil Service examination process and shall serve at the discretion of the appointing officer.

**Calendar:** Full Time / Full Year

  

Who We Are


The San Francisco Unified School District (SFUSD) is the seventh largest school district in California, serving more than 50,000 students who speak more than 44 documented languages across 121 schools in the city of San Francisco every year. We aim for every student who attends SFUSD schools to discover his or her spark, along with a strong sense of self and purpose, and that all students graduate from high school ready for college and career, and equipped with the skills, capacities and dispositions outlined in SFUSD’s Graduate Profile. Every day in our quest to achieve this mission we provide each and every student the quality instruction and equitable support required to thrive in the 21st century.

  

What It Means to Work Here


The SFUSD community is unified by ourCore Values:

* Student\-centered: We put students’ needs first
* Fearless: We persist through challenges
* United: We celebrate and build on each other’s strengths
* Social Justice: We stand with those most vulnerable in our community
* Diversity\-driven: We respect and seek to understand each person

  

We are also inspired by Vision, Values and Guardrails which captures our aspirations and vision for the future of public education in San Francisco. Alongside the District’s strategic plan.SFUSD is reimagining how public education will change over the next decade to meet the dynamic future of San Francisco. As a CORE district, SFUSD is also a leader in critical systems change for more comprehensive school accountability and innovations that help strengthen the instructional core, which is the foundation of our strategic plan and goals.

  

Who We Want


We want talented people from diverse backgrounds and experiences, who are inspired by our mission, steeped in equity, and who are motivated to unleash our children’s potential. We want people who are strong collaborators, skilled communicators, and problem solvers who are comfortable in a community of continuous learning.

  

The **Senior Executive Director of Communications** plays a critical leadership role within SFUSD, building public confidence and leveraging public relations to further the mission of the District. Reporting directly to the Head of Staff, the Senior Executive Director of Communications leads communications, including media relations, crisis communications and oversight of the district’s public radio license, and coordinates marketing and public information efforts.


Essential Duties


The duties specified below are representative of the range of duties assigned to the job code/class and are not intended to be an inclusive or exhaustive list.


As the 0998 Senior Executive Director of Communications, you will:

* **Oversee and provide strategic direction to the Communications Department,** ensuring coherent alignment in service of the District’s priorities and goals across all platforms
* **Advocate for the interests of SFUSD** in public relations.
* **Champion a “one\-team” culture** across the district, promoting connections across divisions and between central office and schools
* **Proactively plan, develop, organize, and administer** all aspects of the school District’s communications strategy, priorities, and day\-to\-day communications issues
* **Ensure essential communications** align with the District’s priorities and bring the District closer to its vision, including correspondence to SFUSD staff and families, proactive media placement, internal communications, websites, and support for the executive messaging

jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
### **Our Work**



We are an architecture and real estate development social enterprise creating spaces that embody justice, healing, and self\-determination. By designing with communities most impacted by incarceration and disinvestment, we build infrastructure that supports community ownership, redistributes power, and lays the foundation for a world rooted in care, not punishment.



To achieve this mission our team is composed of architects, designers, real estate developers and community members working together to create solutionary spaces and places that bring dignity, well\-being and care to the communities we serve.

**The Role**


**Managing Director ·** **Oakland, CA · Hybrid: 3 days in office · $200,000 – $225,000 · Reports to Executive Director**



The Managing Director is a pivotal executive leadership role at DJDS — a steady, strategic presence who holds the interior so the Executive Director can focus externally. This is a cross\-sectional role for someone who can lead a multidisciplinary team with both rigor and heart, and who understands that building a sustainable, mission\-driven organization is itself an act of transformation.



We're looking for someone whose career began in architecture or real estate development and grew beyond it — into community development, into the relationship\-rich, trust\-dependent work of designing and building with communities, and into the adaptive, solutionary leadership it takes to guide a complex organization through a rapidly changing world. The path could have started anywhere on that spectrum — what matters is the curiosity and conviction that shaped the journey.



This is not a role for someone drawn to the traditional practice model. It's a role for someone whose technical foundation gave them a language for the built environment, and whose career since has been driven by a deeper question: what can that environment do for communities who have long been the architects of their own resilience — and deserve infrastructure that reflects it.



You'll own the day\-to\-day leadership of our real estate and architecture verticals — work that is deeply intersecting with fundraising and day\-to\-day operations. You will be second to the Executive Director, partnering closely with her to steward strategy, culture, and growth.


**What You'll Lead**



***Operations \& Team Leadership***


* Serve as the internal anchor for the organization's professional services work — keeping teams resourced, coordinated, and moving toward shared impact
* Directly manage the Studio Director, Director of Real Estate Development (West Coast and East Coast), and Director of Business Development— with the expectation that the team will grow.
* Set goals, work plans, and KPIs across verticals; hold high standards with care and consistency
* Build systems that support clarity, collaboration, and efficiency — without sacrificing the relational culture that makes this work possible
* Support the COO/CFO and Executive Director on organizational operations, financial sustainability, and strategic planning


***Strategy \& Project Decisions***


* Lead the process of project selection based on strategic alignment, mission fit, capacity, and impact potential
* You'll own the day\-to\-day leadership of our real estate and architecture verticals — work that is deeply intersecting with fundraising and day\-to\-day operations. You will be second to the Executive Director, partnering closely with her to steward strategy, culture, and growth.
* Shape and execute long\-term growth strategy in partnership with the Executive Director and sector leaders
* Identify opportunities to improve processes, efficiencies, and earned income across architecture and development verticals


***Business Development \& External Relationships***


* Partner with the Executive Director and Director of Business Development and Strategic Partnerships to support national business development — identifying mission\-aligned opportunities, pitching, and securing new work
* Engage with external partners, funders, and community stakeholders to raise awareness of DJDS's mission and support fundraising
* Participate in community engagement and design processes with genuine curiosity and care for the communities we serve


***Project Level Work***


* Lead at least one project in the portfolio at all times — this is a working leadership role with direct billability expectations, not a purely supervisory one
* Bring a practiced eye to project selection — helping evaluate which opportunities to pursue, which to decline, and why
* Support business development by contributing to proposals, pitches, and client relationships alongside the Executive Director and sector leaders
* Ensure that the way we work on projects reflects how we believe the world should work — with community, with care, and with rigor


**Who You Are**



Your career has taken you across disciplines and into leadership that most people can't easily categorize — and that's exactly the point. You've been front\-facing on large, complex projects — whether as an owner's representative, a project manager on the architecture side, or in a community\-facing leadership role where the stakes were high and the stakeholders were many. You understand how buildings get made and you're equally interested in what they mean to the people who use them. We know no single person will arrive with all of this — what matters most is the combination of experience, curiosity, and values you bring to the role.


* You have 15\+ years of experience across architecture and real estate development, with significant time in community management or owner\-side project leadership
* You have 10\+ years in organizational leadership, with a track record of growing teams and managing across disciplines
* You bring expertise in at least one field and the curiosity to work fluidly across many others — connecting dots between disciplines, bringing unexpected perspectives

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
**MISSION STATEMENT**


Are you ready to give back to the community while pursuing your passion? For over 50 years, Acacia Network and its affiliates have been committed to improving the quality\-of\-life and wellbeing of underserved communities in New York City and beyond. We are one of the leading human services organizations in New York City and the largest Hispanic\-led nonprofit in the State, serving over 150,000 individuals every year. Our programs serve individuals at every age and developmental level, from the very young through our daycare programs to mature adults through our older adults centers. Our extensive array of community\-based services are fully integrated, bilingual and culturally competent.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**


Seedco is an affiliate of The Acacia Network, one of the leading human services organizations in New York City and one of the largest Hispanic\-led nonprofits in the State, providing integrated, culturally\-competent, and trauma\-informed programs in the areas of health, housing, social services, economic development, and cultural revitalization to more than 150,000 individuals annually. Seedco is a national nonprofit organization that advances economic opportunity for people, businesses and communities in need.


The *Recovery Works* program responds to the reality that fewer than one in five individuals exiting treatment maintain long\-term employment. By pairing clinical recovery with training, employment linkages, and retention coaching, the program promotes sustainable economic independence. The Recovery Works program integrates workforce development and recovery support services to help individuals in substance use or behavioral health treatment achieve sustained employment and stability. Services are trauma\-responsive, evidence\-informed, and coordinated through strong partnerships with clinical providers, employers, and community organizations. Building on more than 25 years of Seedco’s workforce and family\-strengthening experience, the program connects job readiness, sector\-based training, and long\-term coaching with recovery services. opportunities.


The Program Director provides strategic and operational leadership for Recovery Works. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Program Director leads a 9\-member multidisciplinary team across intake, case management, employment services, peer recovery, and education/training. The role is accountable for milestone achievement and for sustaining strong partnerships with Acacia\-affiliated treatment providers, employers, and community organizations.

**Position Details: Full\-time (Temporary) 12\- 15 mo****nths engagement. Loc****ation:** **2804 Third Avenue, Bronx, NY 10455\.**

**KEY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

* Program Leadership: Direct day\-to\-day operations across all program stages including Engagement \& Stabilization, Workforce Readiness, Skill Building, Employment Services, Peer Mentoring, and Wrap\-Around Supports. Perform team hiring and onboarding duties.
* Partnership Management: Serve as primary liaison with Acacia\-affiliated treatment partners, employer networks, and community providers to sustain referral pipelines and placement opportunities.
* Team Supervision: Hire, coach, and evaluate the 9\-member program team, including the Lead Case Manager, Lead Employment Specialist, Peer Recovery Coordinator, and Education/Training Coordinator. Coach and build and enhanced team cohesiveness through regular communication and active listening; developing relationships w/each team member.
* Performance Management: Ensure that the program and team are operating toward completion of performance goals and adjust staffing, responsibilities, and activities to meet milestones. Track milestone achievement in Salesforce (250 enrolled, 210 soft\-skill completions, 75 credentials, 149 placements), oversee retention coaching at 30/90/180 days, and lead corrective action to maximize program performance.
* Fiscal Oversight: Manage the program budget, approve OTPS expenditures to remain on budget.
* Quality \& Compliance: Ensure trauma\-responsive, evidence\-informed service delivery and timely funder reporting against contracted outcomes.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.
* Interacts with: Seedco Executive Director, Acacia Leadership, key points of contact as assigned at Acacia Behavioral Health affiliates

**REQUIREMENTS**

* Education: Bachelor’s strongly preferred;
* Experience: Minimum 5 years of progressive leadership in workforce development, behavioral health, or recovery services, including at least 3 years supervising multidisciplinary teams.
* Domain Knowledge: Demonstrated expertise in trauma\-informed, evidence\-based service delivery for individuals in substance use or behavioral health recovery.
* Performance\-Based Contracting: Track record managing milestone\-driven, performance\-based contracts and cost\-reimbursement structures with public or philanthropic funders.
* Technical: Proficiency with Salesforce or a comparable case management/CRM platform for participant tracking and outcomes reporting. Windows 365 preferred.
* Skills: Strong partnership development, fiscal management, staff coaching, and written and verbal communication skills.
* Preferred: Lived or professional experience with recovery communities; familiarity with the Acacia Network and the NYC workforce ecosystem.

**WHY JOIN US?**


Acacia Network provides a comprehensive and competitive benefits package to our employees. In addition to a competitive salary, our benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage. We also offer generous paid time off, including vacation days and paid holidays, to support a healthy work\-life balance. We prioritize the well\-being of our employees both professionally and personally.


As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Description: **\*\*This position supports the Sussex County YMCA \& Fairview Lake Camp in Newton, NJ\*\*** **POSITION SUMMARY:**


The Metropolitan YMCA of the Oranges (Metro Y) seeks a dynamic, relationship\-driven fundraising professional to serve as Director of Development. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer, the Director of Development is responsible for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding a portfolio of individual donors and major gift prospects to advance the Association's mission and philanthropic priorities.


As a frontline fundraiser, the Director of Development will develop meaningful relationships with donors, volunteers, and community leaders to secure leadership and major gifts in support of the Association's annual fundraising initiatives, capital campaigns, endowment, and strategic priorities.


Serving as the primary development partner for assigned YMCA branches, the Director of Development will collaborate with Executive Directors, volunteer leaders, and Association staff to develop and execute fundraising strategies, identify new philanthropic opportunities, and strengthen a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.


The successful candidate will actively manage a portfolio of major gift prospects and donors, maintain accountability for annual fundraising metrics, and consistently achieve established revenue goals.


Metro YMCA branches are located in Livingston, Maplewood, East Orange, New Milford, Hardyston, and Stillwater, New Jersey. Regular travel throughout the Association's service area, along with occasional evening and weekend commitments, is required.


Requirements:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Major Gift \& Annual Campaign Fundraising**

* Develop and implement individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for an assigned portfolio of major gift prospects and donors.
* Build, manage, and grow an active portfolio through all stages of the donor lifecycle, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal.
* Conduct regular face\-to\-face meetings, discovery visits, and stewardship conversations with current and prospective donors.
* Personally solicit leadership and major gifts in support of annual operations, capital campaigns, endowment, and other strategic initiatives.
* Prepare compelling gift proposals, personalized correspondence, impact reports, and other donor communications.
* Maintain a consistent pipeline of qualified prospects while advancing donors toward meaningful philanthropic commitments.
* Maintain accurate and timely records of donor activity within the Association's CRM.
* Utilize wealth screening, prospect research, and donor analytics to identify and prioritize fundraising opportunities.

**Branch Partnership**

* Serve as the lead fundraising partner for assigned YMCA branches.
* Collaborate with Executive Directors and branch leadership to identify philanthropic priorities and develop annual fundraising strategies.
* Provide fundraising guidance and support for branch\-based campaigns and donor engagement opportunities.
* Work collaboratively across the Association to maximize donor relationships and fundraising success.
* Partner with volunteer leaders to strengthen philanthropic engagement within the communities served by the YMCA.
* Provide fundraising training, coaching, and ongoing support to Executive Directors, branch leadership, staff, and volunteer leaders to strengthen donor engagement, solicitation skills, stewardship practices, and overall fundraising effectiveness.
* Partner with branch leadership to develop a culture of philanthropy by equipping staff and volunteers with fundraising tools, best practices, and resources that support annual campaigns, major gifts, special events, and community engagement efforts.

**Stewardship**

* Develop and execute thoughtful stewardship plans that recognize donor generosity and demonstrate philanthropic impact.
* Ensure timely acknowledgements, recognition, reporting, and ongoing engagement that foster long\-term donor relationships.

**Community Engagement**

* Represent the Metropolitan YMCA of the Oranges at community meetings, branch events, fundraising activities, and donor gatherings.
* Build relationships with community leaders, civic organizations, and select local and regional businesses to identify philanthropic partnerships that support the YMCA's mission.

**Other Responsibilities**

* Support Association\-wide fundraising initiatives and special events.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Benefits:** We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, which includes medical, prescription, dental, and vision coverage. We also offer generous paid time off (PTO), paid sick leave, paid holidays, a legal plan, long\-term disability, life insurance, 12% retirement benefits upon eligibility, a 403 (b) plan, an employee assistance program, professional development opportunities, Metro Y program discounts, and complimentary use of YMCA facilities. Full\-time employees may be eligible for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

The **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** serves as the senior executive responsible for the overall operational leadership, integration, and execution of Spectrum for Living's strategic priorities. Reporting directly to the President \& CEO, the COO serves as the CEO's principal operational partner and is entrusted with broad executive authority to translate organizational vision into measurable results while ensuring operational excellence across all areas of the organization.

The COO provides executive oversight of the organization's operational infrastructure, including facilities and maintenance, information technology, transportation and logistics, vendor and contract management, risk management, emergency preparedness, capital projects, organizational infrastructure, business operations, and other administrative functions. The position is responsible for creating efficient, scalable, and sustainable operational systems that support the delivery of exceptional services while maximizing organizational performance and financial stewardship.

In partnership with the President \& CEO, the COO leads the implementation of the Strategic Plan, ensuring that organizational initiatives are effectively executed, performance expectations are achieved, and operational priorities remain aligned with Spectrum for Living's mission, values, and long\-term vision. The COO develops organizational systems, performance metrics, accountability structures, and continuous quality improvement initiatives that promote operational excellence, innovation, and organizational growth.

The COO also provides executive leadership and oversight for the organization's Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Brand Management, and Development functions, ensuring that Spectrum for Living's public image, stakeholder engagement, community partnerships, and philanthropic strategies support the organization's strategic objectives and long\-term sustainability.

As a transformational leader, the COO fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, operational discipline, and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will possess exceptional leadership, strategic thinking, business acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to effectively lead complex organizational initiatives while building strong relationships with employees, vendors, government agencies, community partners, families, donors, and the Board of Trustees. The COO is expected to exercise the highest levels of integrity, professionalism, discretion, and executive presence while serving as a trusted advisor to the President \& CEO and acting on behalf of the CEO when delegated.

***Executive Leadership \& Organizational Strategy***

* Serve as the President \& CEO's principal operational partner and trusted executive advisor, providing strategic counsel, objective analysis, and operational recommendations that support informed executive decision\-making.
* Lead the implementation and execution of the organization's Strategic Plan by translating strategic priorities into measurable operational objectives, implementation plans, timelines, accountability structures, and performance outcomes.
* Participate as a member of the Executive Leadership Team in strategic planning, organizational development, executive decision\-making, policy formation, enterprise risk management, and long\-term business planning.
* Advise the President \& CEO regarding operational performance, infrastructure needs, organizational capacity, emerging risks, regulatory changes, business opportunities, and strategic initiatives.
* Act on behalf of the President \& CEO, when delegated, exercising executive authority while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, and sound judgment.

***Strategic Execution \& Organizational Performance***

* Implements and Manges KPIs as assigned by the President and CEO
* Serve as the executive responsible for ensuring that strategic initiatives approved by the President \& CEO are successfully implemented throughout the organization.
* Develop comprehensive implementation plans that clearly define objectives, milestones, timelines, resource requirements, accountability measures, performance indicators, and measurable outcomes.
* Monitor organizational progress toward strategic goals and provide regular executive reporting to the President \& CEO regarding implementation status, operational performance, organizational risks, and recommended corrective actions.
* Hold executive leaders, directors, managers, and operational teams accountable for achieving established organizational goals, operational priorities, timelines, and performance expectations.
* Identify organizational barriers, operational inefficiencies, and resource constraints that may impede progress and implement timely solutions that maintain organizational momentum.
* Coordinate cross\-functional collaboration among departments to ensure enterprise\-wide initiatives are effectively integrated and aligned with organizational priorities.
* Lead organizational transformation initiatives that strengthen operational performance, improve service delivery, increase efficiency, and build organizational capacity.

**Qualifications \& Experience**

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university required.
* Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Healthcare Administration (MHA), Public Administration (MPA), Organizational Leadership, or a closely related field preferred.
* An MBA is strongly preferred.

**Preferred Schedule:** Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. **In\-office position only**.

**Discretionary Incentive Bonus!**

Join us as we drive operational excellence through innovative leadership and strategic vision!

Pay: $160,000\.00 \- $220,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account

**WHO IS CHI?**


Community Housing Innovations (CHI) is a not\-for\-profit housing and human services organization that aims to support social and economic independence. Our vision is to end generational poverty and foster upward mobility by ensuring that all families and individuals live in quality housing, have a home of their own, and a job to support them. We believe quality, affordable housing is the foundation for prosperity, personal fulfillment, and success.

**WHAT DOES CHI OFFER?**


CHI employs a team of hard\-working, compassionate people who want to give back to others in their community. We are proud to offer:

* Generous Paid time off
* Personal and Sick Days
* Health insurance and health reimbursement account
* Dental and vision plans
* Flexible spending account
* AFLAC supplemental insurance
* Dependent Care Spending Account
* Commuter Transit and Parking Account
* Working Advantage\- Employee Perks
* 401(k) retirement plan
* Life insurance
* Employee Assistance Program
* Monthly trainings and career development plans




**JOB SUMMARY**


The Program Director oversees the management and operations of the facility to ensure residents receive proper and appropriate services that promotes independence, self\-sufficiency, and stabilization in a safe, healthy, and culturally sensitive residential environment; and staff are sufficiently equipped and resourced in a safe and healthy work environment. The Director ensures the facility structure, building conditions and maintenance practices are compliant with all applicable building and housing code and is monitored by 24/7 security; adequate staffing in accordance with DHS and OTDA regulations; and all required documentation and reporting are submitted correctly and on schedule to CHI, government agencies, funders, and other oversite agencies.

**Pay: $95,000 salary**

**This role is exempt and not eligible for overtime.**

**Schedule: Monday\-Friday 8am\-4pm plus on call 24/7\.**

**Location: Sheepshead Bay Brooklyn NY**




### ***JOB\-RELATED DUTIES – ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS***




*These duties are essential and specific to the successful implementation of this position.*

**RESIDENTIAL SERVICES**

* Ensure residents receive quality and appropriate services per organizational principles and program requirements.
* Ensure Social Service unit executes residential services properly and on schedule including intakes and assessments, room inspections, case management sessions, service coordination and advocacy, workshop facilitation, and discharge planning.
* Ensure direct and coordinated residential services comprehensively address health and nutrition, mental health, immigration, and citizenship, legal, education and vocation, employment and income, English language acquisition, cultural adaptation, trauma recovery, and other human issues and social needs.
* Develop and maintain a resource network, inclusive of formal and informal partnerships and service agreements, of external providers and organizations that offer support and direct services.

**PROGRAM MANAGEMENT**

* Ensure compliance with funding contracts, partnership and service agreements, and all applicable city, state, and federal laws, rules, and regulations.
* Ensure program and contractual deliverables are met. Evaluate program performance and productivity outcomes and develop enhancement strategies for underperforming areas. Ensure CHI program KPIs are aligned with metrics and deliverables.
* Update and maintain Policy and Procedure manuals in compliance with DHS shelter operations guidance and CHI policies. Disseminate and enforce policies and procedures to all site staff.
* Assist with procurement and contract administration activities by ensuring accurate scopes of work and program deliverables for the site.
* Ensure proper and timely follow\-up for Priority 1 and 2 incidents with clients, and timely reporting to DHS and CHI.
* Ensure staff are properly trained and certified per OTDA and DHS rules, including one\-time and recurring trainings and certifications.
* Ensure site staff adheres to CHI code of conduct and abide by contractual, city, state, and federal rules and regulations.

**FACILITIES MANAGEMENT**

* Ensure facility is code compliant with HPD, DOB, DHS, DOHMH, and OTDA.
* Ensure facility is staffed per OTDA and DHS rules, including 24/7 on\-site security.
* Ensure a safe, clean, and healthy residential environment for residents; and a safe, clean, and productive environment for staff.
* Ensure facility maintenance practices meets COVID standards and are consistent with OTDA, DHS, DOHMH, and US OMH guidelines.
* Ensure facility is sufficiently equipped, stocked, and staffed for daily meals, daily cleaning, weekly towel and linen services, and issuance of DHS care kits upon request.
* Ensure transportation services for residents are always available for housing and medical appointments and emergency situations through MTA MetroCard or car service.

**SUPERVISION and GENERAL DUTIES**

* Conduct 1 to 1 meetings with members of your team and update the performance goals, accomplishments, notes, and feedback in Paycom on a regular basis (weekly/bi\-weekly).
* Troubleshoot difficult resident cases; intervene and directly assist in special needs cases.
* Document interactions and communications with and on behalf of residents in CARES and AWARDS.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the VP of Housing, Chief Housing Officer or Chief Executive Officer.
