Employment Status: Full\-Time, Exempt  
Reports To: Executive Director  
Location: Escambia County, Florida (local travel required)

**Position Summary: A Key Driver of Fundraising and Faith Partnerships**

The Development Director is a key driver of fundraising success at Family Promise of Escambia, with a primary focus on cultivating and strengthening relationships with faith partners. This role serves as a bridge between the Family Promise mission and congregations, donors, and volunteers who want to support families experiencing homelessness.

The Development Director translates big ideas into meaningful impact by building trust\-based relationships, leading fundraising efforts, and engaging faith communities in both financial support and volunteer service. Working closely with the board members and faith partners, this position ensures the organization has the resources and community support needed for long\-term sustainability.

This role blends strategy, heart, and communication. It is ideal for someone who understands the unique role faith communities play in fundraising, volunteerism, and mission\-driven work.

**Core Responsibilities**

Faith Partner Fundraising \& Engagement

* Lead fundraising strategies centered on faith partners, including congregational giving, special offerings, sponsorships, and partner\-supported campaigns
* Cultivate and steward relationships with clergy, lay leaders, and congregational champions
* Create meaningful opportunities for faith partners to financially invest in the mission of Family Promise of Escambia

Fundraising Strategy \& Campaign Management

* Develop and execute fundraising strategies that support short\- and long\-term organizational goals
* Lead fundraising campaigns from start to finish, including goal\-setting, timelines, execution, and tracking results
* Research and identify grant opportunities, prepare and submit proposals, and manage post\-award tracking, reporting, and compliance requirements
* Identify and implement opportunities to grow recurring giving and strengthen donor retention
* Lead communications strategy in collaboration with the Board of Directors and interns, including oversight of social media, website management, and email communications to donors and volunteers.

Donor Development \& Major Gifts

* Oversee major gift efforts, with an emphasis on individual donors connected to faith communities
* Build and maintain strong, ongoing relationships with key donors
* Share compelling stories that connect donors to impact and outcomes

Volunteer Coordination with Faith Partners

* Coordinate volunteer engagement with faith partners, including hosting, meal support, service projects, and special initiatives
* Serve as a primary point of contact for congregations participating as hosts or volunteers
* Work collaboratively with program staff to align volunteer efforts with organizational needs
* Ensure volunteers feel valued, supported, and connected to the mission

Events \& Community Engagement

* Plan and manage fundraising and engagement events that bring faith partners and the broader community together
* Coordinate logistics, volunteers, and follow\-up activities to maximize engagement and support

Board Engagement \& Collaboration

* Work closely with board members to leverage their faith and community networks
* Support board involvement in fundraising, congregational outreach, and donor cultivation

Donor Systems \& Administration

* Maintain accurate, organized donor and faith partner records in the organization’s database
* Track gifts, volunteer participation, and engagement to ensure timely follow\-up and stewardship

**Qualifications**

Required

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience
* Minimum of 3 years of nonprofit fundraising or development experience
* Demonstrated experience working with faith\-based partners or congregational networks
* Strong relationship\-building, communication, and organizational skills
* Experience using donor databases or fundraising software
* Ability to work occasional evenings or weekends to support faith partner events

Preferred

* Experience coordinating volunteers
* Familiarity with homelessness, housing, or family services
* Experience working with boards of directors
* Knowledge of the faith landscape in Escambia County

Compensation

* Annual salary range: $52,000–$62,000, commensurate with experience
* Benefits may include paid time off, holidays, and other benefits offered by the organization

*Family Promise of Escambia is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity, equity, and inclusion. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply.*

A practicing Catholic in full communion with the Church who embraces and can faithfully represent the Church's teaching on the sanctity of human life, and who wholeheartedly supports our pro\-life mission.


**Required**
  

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience); 3\+ years of progressively responsible leadership, ideally in a nonprofit, ministry, or social\-services setting; fundraising and donor\-relations experience; proven ability to lead staff and volunteers; budget and financial\-management literacy; excellent communication and public speaking; discretion with confidential information; valid driver's license and ability to pass a background check.


**Preferred**
  

Pro\-life ministry, maternity home, social work or crisis\-pregnancy experience; familiarity with the Twin Cities Catholic and pro\-life community; grant\-writing experience.

Salary range: $60,000\-$75,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

jobs.title: Marketing and Development Director
jobs.description:
**Job Overview**

The Marketing and Development Director is responsible for leading the school's marketing, enrollment promotion, fundraising, grant development, and community engagement efforts. This position serves as the primary ambassador for the school, working to increase awareness, strengthen the school's brand, build meaningful partnerships, and secure philanthropic support that advances the school's mission and strategic priorities.

The Director collaborates closely with school leadership, faculty, families, community organizations, businesses, and donors to promote the school's successes and expand opportunities for students.

**Responsibilities**

Marketing and Communications

* Develop and implement a comprehensive annual marketing and communications plan aligned with the school's strategic goals.
* Promote the school to prospective families through print, digital, and community outreach efforts.
* Develop compelling stories that highlight student achievement, teacher excellence, school culture, and academic success.
* Manage the school's website to ensure timely, accurate, and engaging content.
* Create brochures, presentations, videos, advertisements, and promotional materials.
* Coordinate photography and videography to document school events and accomplishments.
* Maintain brand standards across all internal and external communications.
* Serve as a liaison with local media to promote positive news stories and school initiatives.

Enrollment Marketing

* Develop and execute enrollment marketing campaigns that increase student recruitment and retention.
* Coordinate open houses, tours, information sessions, and recruitment events.
* Build relationships with prospective families throughout the enrollment process.
* Analyze enrollment data and marketing effectiveness to improve outreach strategies.
* Represent the school at community events, fairs, and networking opportunities.

Development and Fundraising

* Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan that supports the school's mission and strategic initiatives.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, alumni, businesses, civic organizations, and community partners.
* Coordinate annual giving campaigns, sponsorships, and fundraising events.
* Identify new funding opportunities and donor prospects.
* Maintain donor records and oversee donor stewardship and recognition.
* Prepare fundraising reports and measure return on investment for fundraising initiatives.

Grant Writing and Management

* Research federal, state, local, corporate, and foundation grant opportunities.
* Write compelling grant proposals that align with school priorities.
* Collaborate with school leadership to identify funding needs and project goals.
* Manage grant timelines, reporting requirements, and compliance.
* Track grant outcomes and communicate program impact to funders.

Community and Business Partnerships

* Develop strategic partnerships with local businesses, civic organizations, higher education institutions, and nonprofit organizations.
* Coordinate volunteer opportunities and community engagement initiatives.
* Secure sponsorships for school events, programs, athletics, and student initiatives.
* Represent the school at community meetings and networking events.
* Build relationships that expand educational opportunities for students through internships, mentoring, career exploration, and service learning.

Strategic Leadership

* Collaborate with the Executive Director and leadership team to advance the school's strategic plan.
* Develop annual goals and measurable performance indicators for marketing and development initiatives.
* Monitor marketing analytics, enrollment trends, fundraising performance, and community engagement metrics.
* Prepare reports for school leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Ensure all communications reflect the mission, vision, and values of the school.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

Preferred

* Experience in education, public schools, charter schools, or nonprofit organizations.
* Grant writing experience with a demonstrated history of successful awards.
* Experience planning fundraising campaigns and special events.
* Knowledge of donor management software, CRM systems, and marketing analytics tools.
* Graphic design and photography/video editing experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

* Excellent storytelling and presentation skills.
* Strong networking and relationship\-building abilities.
* Creative and strategic thinker with strong problem\-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines.
* Data\-driven decision maker who uses analytics to evaluate success.
* High level of professionalism, integrity, and confidentiality.
* Passion for public education and the mission of charter schools.

Physical Requirements

* Ability to attend evening and weekend events as needed.
* Ability to travel locally for meetings and community events.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds for event setup and promotional materials.

**Performance Expectations**

Success in this role will be measured by:

* Increased student enrollment and retention.
* Growth in community awareness and engagement.
* Successful grant awards and funding secured.
* Growth in annual fundraising revenue.
* Expansion of business and community partnerships.
* Increased website traffic, social media engagement, and communication effectiveness.
* Positive relationships with families, donors, and community stakeholders.

**Mission Commitment**

The Marketing and Development Director is expected to actively support the school's mission by fostering strong relationships, promoting excellence in education, and securing resources that enhance opportunities for every student. This position plays a critical role in ensuring the long\-term sustainability and visibility of the school within the community.

Pay: $50,000\.00 \- $60,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* 403(b)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance

jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**  
AIRA is seeking an accomplished Business Development Director to lead a transformative initiative that will strengthen the organization’s long\-term sustainability and expand its national impact. Reporting to the Executive Director, with strategic support from AIRA’s Fractional Chief Operating Officer, this role will help shape the organization's next phase of growth, diversifying our revenue portfolio, expanding partnerships, and developing new opportunities that build on our reputation, expertise, and national network.

This newly created role offers a unique opportunity to design and lead AIRA's business development strategy. Working closely with organizational leadership, this individual will identify, cultivate, and advance strategic relationships across public health, healthcare, health technology, philanthropy, government and the private sector.

This is an opportunity for a strategic, relationship\-driven leader who thrives on creating and driving new opportunities from vision to execution. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in business development, exceptional communication and relationship\-building skills, strong business acumen, and the ability to work independently in a dynamic, mission\-driven environment.

**Is This You?**  
If you are energized by building partnerships, creating sustainable growth, and helping a respected national organization expand its impact on public health, we encourage you to apply.

**Responsibilities**

* Establish the infrastructure for a new business development function, including defining roles, workflows, and policies, and establishing scalable systems and procedures to support funding diversification and long\-term organizational growth.
* Conduct a funding landscape analysis; develop and regularly update a comprehensive business development plan.
* Develop and manage a fiscal plan for responsible use of the business development budget.
* Build, manage, and actively cultivate a diversified funding portfolio, including federal and state contracts, cooperative agreements, grants, contracts, member services, and subscription services.
* Lead the funding application process, including researching and prioritizing opportunities, gathering requirements, coordinating with subject matter experts, writing and submitting proposals, and attending relevant events.
* Develop tailored cultivation plans for top funder prospects, maintaining active engagement strategies and tracking all touchpoints.
* Leverage, populate, and maintain existing CRM to organize contacts, deadlines, proposals, and engagement history.
* Support the intentional packaging and promotion of AIRA’s proven service offerings, such as technical assistance, IIS assessments, training, and interoperability initiatives, as marketable products for current and prospective customers/funders.
* Lead contracting and funding negotiations in collaboration with AIRA leadership; support identification of co\-applicants or consortium partners where appropriate.
* Track and prepare regular reports on funding diversification progress for AIRA leadership and external partners; evaluate performance quarterly and refresh the funding pipeline annually.
* Represent AIRA’s mission and service offerings positively and compellingly to current and prospective funders, customers, and stakeholders, nationally and internationally.
* Stay current on developments in the public health and health informatics environment to inform AIRA’s funding diversification strategy.

**Required Skills and Qualifications**

* Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in business, sales, healthcare administration, public health, or a related field, and 8\+ years of experience in business development, client relationship management or account management. * Experience developing market strategies, evaluating new business opportunities, and translating organizational strengths into sustainable revenue.
* Proven sales and negotiating track record.
* Experience using Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to present concepts and proposals compellingly to diverse stakeholders.
* Ability to work independently, manage remote reporting relationships, and collaborate across internal and external teams.
* A remote workspace conducive to professional work, with audio and video conferencing capabilities.
* Ability to travel a minimum of three to five times per year.
* Ability to pass a background and reference check is required.

**Highly Desired Experience**

* Experience working at the national level within public health, healthcare, health information technology, health informatics, or related sectors.
* Established network of relationships within federal agencies, foundations, health technology companies, healthcare organizations, public health organizations, and/or industry associations.
* Experience supporting or leading responses to federal, state, or foundation funding opportunities, including cooperative agreements, grants, and contracts.
* Experience commercializing professional services, technical assistance, educational offerings, software, or membership\-based services.
* Experience working with nonprofit organizations, membership associations, or mission\-driven organizations.
* Familiarity with immunization information systems (IIS), interoperability, health data exchange, public health infrastructure, or related healthcare technology.
* Experience developing go\-to\-market strategies for new programs, services, or products.

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Philanthropy (DoP) serves as a member of Concord Community Music School’s leadership team and is responsible for advancing the organization’s fundraising strategy, donor engagement, and contributed revenue growth. The DoP provides leadership for all philanthropic initiatives, including major gifts, annual giving, foundation and government support, donor stewardship, and future fundraising opportunities.

Working closely with the Executive Director, the Development Committee, and community stakeholders, the DoP helps build and sustain a comprehensive culture of philanthropy that supports CCMS’s mission, strategic priorities, and long\-term sustainability.

CCMS operates primarily in person, with occasional opportunities for hybrid work. The Director of Philanthropy is expected to attend select performances, donor events, and organizational activities throughout the year, including some evenings and weekends.

**Organization Profile**

Founded in 1984, Concord Community Music School (CCMS) is one of New Hampshire’s largest community music schools. Our mission is to cultivate lifelong musical growth and meaningful connections for all. We are guided by the values of inclusivity, collaboration, purpose, creativity, empathy, sustainability, community connection, and a growth mindset.

Located in downtown Concord, New Hampshire, CCMS is a vibrant arts center featuring teaching studios, ensemble and percussion rooms, a recording studio, outdoor performance space, and two signature indoor venues. More than 1,400 students participate in lessons and programs each week, both onsite and throughout the community, ranging in age from six months to over 90 years old.

CCMS offers instruction in a wide variety of instruments, voice, expressive therapies, and digital audio production. More than 40% of students receive financial assistance, with approximately $125,000 awarded annually in tuition aid. In 2026, CCMS adopted a new strategic plan that will guide the organization’s work through five key priorities and position the Music School for continued growth and impact.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Strategic Fundraising Leadership***

● Serve as the organization’s fundraising strategist, helping to shape and execute a comprehensive philanthropy program aligned with institutional goals.

● Partner with the Executive Director and Board Development Committee to establish annual fundraising objectives, revenue targets, and donor engagement strategies.

● Lead fundraising efforts across major gifts, annual giving, foundation and government support, sponsorships, and emerging philanthropic opportunities.

● Build and manage a robust donor portfolio and pipeline, guiding donors and prospects through every stage of the fundraising cycle — identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

● Monitor fundraising performance and recommend strategies to strengthen contributed revenue and donor retention.

● Anticipate and respond to the needs and interests of donors, funders, Board members, and community partners.

● Translate organizational priorities into actionable fundraising strategies while effectively managing multiple projects and deadlines.

***Board and Community Engagement***

● Partner closely with Board leadership to strengthen philanthropic engagement and advance fundraising goals.

● Attend and support Board and Development Committee meetings, providing regular fundraising updates and strategic guidance.

● Coach and support Board members in donor cultivation, relationship\-building, and philanthropic best practices.

● Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, institutional funders, community leaders, and strategic partners.

● Represent CCMS as a visible and enthusiastic ambassador for its mission, programs, and community impact.

***Organizational Leadership***

● Contribute as an active member of the leadership team, supporting organizational planning and cross\-departmental collaboration.

● Foster a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization, encouraging shared responsibility for fundraising and donor stewardship.

● Set ambitious goals, navigate challenges, and consistently deliver measurable outcomes.

● Build trust, inspire shared purpose, and foster productive relationships with colleagues, volunteers, donors, and community partners.

● Stay informed about charitable giving trends, fundraising best practices, tax\-advantaged giving strategies, and developments within the nonprofit sector.

● Support special projects and other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

● Minimum of five years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, preferably in a nonprofit, educational, or arts and culture organization.

● Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree and/or CFRE preferred.

● Demonstrated success developing and implementing fundraising strategies that generate revenue across multiple donor categories, including individual, foundation, corporate, and government support.

● Proven experience cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and prospects.

● Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

● Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

● Experience working with boards, volunteers, and community stakeholders required.

● Familiarity with music, arts education, or the cultural sector is a plus.

● Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and donor database/CRM systems.

**Compensation and Benefits**

CCMS offers a competitive salary ranging from $75,000 to $85,000, commensurate with experience, along with a benefits package that includes health and welfare benefits.

**Applications and Inquiries**

To submit a cover letter and resume with a summary of accomplishments, please email Daniel Acsadi, Executive Director, at dacsadi@ccmusicschool.or

**About Read to Grow**

Now in its 26th year, Read to Grow is a Connecticut\-based early literacy nonprofit working statewide to make sure children and families have access to books, early literacy support, and joyful reading experiences from the very beginning.

Read to Grow’s work is rooted in the belief that families are their children’s first and most important teachers, and that all children deserve books of their own. We partner with hospitals, clinics, schools, libraries, community organizations, volunteers, and families to promote a strong culture of early literacy across Connecticut.

As Read to Grow continues to grow and evolve, we are excited about what comes next and the opportunity to deepen our impact while keeping children, families, and the joy of books at the center of the work.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
The **Development Director** is responsible for leading the implementation and management of all fundraising and development activities for United Way of Ulster County. This role focuses on building and sustaining diverse revenue streams, including individual giving, corporate partnerships, grants, and special events, to support the organization’s mission and long\-term sustainability. The ideal candidate is a relationship\-driven leader with a strong track record in fundraising, donor engagement, and strategic growth, and a passion for advancing equity and community well\-being.

**Key Responsibilities**

*Fundraising Strategy \& Implementation* 

* Develop and execute a comprehensive annual development plan aligned with organizational goals.
* Specifically define impact for raised income as aligned with program work.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, corporate sponsors, and foundation partners.
* Lead annual giving campaigns, including workplace campaigns, major gifts, and online fundraising efforts.
* Oversee grant strategy in collaboration with program staff, including identifying opportunities and ensuring timely submissions.
* Expand and diversify revenue streams to ensure long\-term financial sustainability.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, corporate partners, and community stakeholders.
* Design and implement donor stewardship strategies to increase retention and engagement.
* Coordinate donor recognition and appreciation initiatives.
* Represent United Way of Ulster County at community events, meetings, and public engagements.
* Workplace Campaigns – Annual giving campaigns with local businesses

*Events \& Campaign Management* 

* Plan and execute fundraising events and campaigns, including logistics, sponsorships, and follow\-up. Current events include: 1 community based event, 1 golf event where UWUC serves as the recipient of funds and spokesperson but not as the event organizer, 1 fundraising event
* Collaborate with internal teams to align events with programmatic impact and storytelling.
* Evaluate event performance and implement improvements for future initiatives.

*Data Management \& Reporting* 

* Maintain accurate donor records and reporting through CRM systems.
* Track fundraising progress against goals and provide regular reports to leadership.
* Analyze donor data to inform strategy and improve fundraising outcomes.

*Leadership \& Collaboration* 

* Collaborate with the President \& CEO and team on organizational strategy and growth.
* Support board engagement in fundraising activities, including training and coordination.
* Work with the board to identify giving opportunities and programs for board investment.

* Supervise consultants, interns, and/or volunteers as applicable.

* Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, public administration, social work, education, or a related field.

* Strong organizational, budgeting, and data analysis skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines with professionalism and attention to detail.
* Cultural competence and a demonstrated commitment to equity and inclusion.
* Experience with CRM and grants management platforms.
* Knowledge of Ulster County community needs and resources.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $82,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

We are the only university system based exclusively in the robust Dallas\-Fort Worth region. We are growing with the North Texas region, employing more than 14,000 employees, educating a record 49,000\+ students across our system, and awarding nearly 12,000 degrees each year.

We are one team comprised of individuals who are committed to excellence, curiosity and innovation. We are transforming lives and creating economic opportunity through education. We champion a people\-first values\-based culture where We Care about each other and those we serve. We believe that we are Better Together because we foster an environment of respect, belonging, and access for all. We are encouraged to Be Curious about opportunities for learning, creating, discovering, and innovating, and are encouraged to learn from failure. jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

DCS Asset Maintenance is a family owned and operated business with treating all employees like family at the core of our values. Our employees provide innovative, safe, and high\-quality infrastructure/maintenance contracting services to State DOTs, railroads, and other commercial/residential customers across the entire United States. Employees receive generous compensation packages, employee engagement events \& career development programs, just to name a few of the perks of being part of the DCS family!


To provide quality service, we need top\-of\-the\-line employees. That is why we offer great compensation, awesome benefits, and a work environment worth bragging about!

 **Job Description**  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO), DCS Asset Maintenance, is responsible for the overall strategic, operational, and financial performance of the Asset Maintenance business. The COO serves as the senior executive leader of the business and is accountable for delivering profitability, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, safety performance, and sustainable growth across a portfolio of roadway and infrastructure maintenance contracts throughout the United States.  

  

Working closely with the CEO and executive leadership team, the COO develops and executes business strategies that support geographic expansion, market growth, operational scalability, and long\-term value creation. The COO provides leadership for all regional and project operations while building the organizational capabilities necessary to support continued market leadership.  

  

This role carries full responsibility for the Asset Maintenance business performance and serves as the primary executive accountable for achieving strategic, operational, and financial objectives.


Strategic Planning \& Market Expansion

* Develop and execute the long\-term strategic plan for the business.
* Partner with business development teams to pursue new contracts, strategic partnerships, and growth opportunities.
* Lead operational planning and mobilization efforts for major contract awards and new market entries.
* Develop scalable operational models capable of supporting rapid growth while maintaining service excellence.


Operational Leadership

* Provide executive leadership and oversight of all Asset operations across multiple regions, projects, and customer accounts.
* Establish operational standards that ensure consistency, efficiency, safety, and customer satisfaction throughout the portfolio.
* Create and foster a culture of execution to ensure the operating business delivers on its goals without sacrificing safety or customer contract compliance.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, innovation, safety, contract compliance, operational excellence, and cost optimization.
* Ensure successful project delivery while maintaining compliance with contractual requirements and regulatory standards.
* Build operational infrastructure and processes that support a growing national footprint.


Financial Leadership

* Maintain full profit and loss accountability for the Asset Business.
* Develop annual business plans, operating budgets, and growth forecasts.
* Drive margin improvement, and operational efficiency initiatives.
* Monitor performance against established KPIs and implement corrective actions as necessary.
* Partner with Finance to establish capital investment strategies that support long\-term business objectives.


Leadership Development

* Lead and develop a high\-performing team of regional leaders, project executives, and operational managers.
* Build organizational capability through succession planning, talent management, leadership development, and workforce planning.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure company culture remains strong during periods of growth and organizational change.


Customer \& Stakeholder Leadership

* Serve as the executive sponsor for key client relationships.
* Partner with customers to identify opportunities to expand services and enhance value.
* Promote exceptional customer experiences and long\-term strategic partnerships.
* Represent the organization with industry associations, governmental agencies, and strategic stakeholders.


Safety, Compliance \& Risk Management

* Ensure adherence to all contractual obligations, regulatory requirements, and company policies.
* Lead risk management initiatives that protect the organization while supporting growth objectives.
* Maintain a strong focus on quality, compliance, and operational governance.


Executive Success Measures

* Revenue growth
* EBITDA and operating margin performance to hit financial commitments
* Successful expansion into new states and markets
* New contract mobilization success
* Safety performance
* Customer retention and satisfaction
* Contract compliance performance
* Leadership development and succession readiness
* Employee engagement and retention
* Scalability of operational systems and processes

  

**Qualifications**  

* Safety performance
* Customer retention and satisfaction
* Contract compliance performance
* Leadership development and succession readiness
* Employee engagement and retention
* Scalability of operational systems and processes


Qualifications

* Proven executive leadership experience (minimum 10 years) managing multi\-site infrastructure, transportation, asset management, construction, or maintenance operations. State DOT experience is highly desired. Experience with PBMC is additive.
* Demonstrated success leading organizations through aggressive growth and geographic expansion.
* Strong operational execution expertise with business development mindset combined.
* Experience managing large P\&L responsibilities (100mm\+ required).
* Proven ability to balance strategic thinking with operational discipline.
* Proven ability to select, negotiate and manage subcontractors and

Education Qualifications:+ Bachelor's Degree in related field (Required)
+ Master's Degree in related field (Preferred)


Experience Qualifications:+ 10 years of experience, or combination thereof, in administration, investment planning, not\-for profit fundraising, and/or supervision with instructional leadership responsibilities (Required)
+ Experience at the system level (Preferred)


Skills Qualifications:+ Knowledge of fundraising strategies and management
+ Ability to collaborate with individuals and groups
+ Ability to communicate with a wide variety of audiences internally and externally
+ Ability to plan and organize human and financial resources to implement system\-level initiatives
+ Knowledge of event planning and management
+ Ability to make effective presentations to senior level management, public groups, and/or the Board of Education
+ Ability to develop, lead, and maintain effective fundraising initiatives
+ Ability to determine strategies to move the organization forward and set goals


Primary Responsibilities:  

  

Provide senior leadership and strategic direction to support the organization's vision to be a system of world\-class schools through creative and strategic long\-term development and planned giving initiatives.  

+ Lead, design, implement, and direct all fundraising activities including annual giving, endowment and capital campaigns, special projects, and other school\-related funding solicitations.
	- Lead, develop, and manage all strategies and activities for donor cultivation, solicitation, and relations.
	- Maintain contact with and develop grant proposals for foundations and corporations.
	- Lead, develop, and implement parent and class\-based fundraising programs within the Annual Fund.
	- Lead, develop, and cultivate a comprehensive, long\-range planned\-giving program for the Foundation.

	- Provide guidance and support to the Foundation Board of Trustees and the CEO/Superintendent to develop strategies to initiate and meet aggressive fundraising goals.
	- Lead fundraising training for Foundation trustees and other leadership volunteers.
	- Direct responsibility for all development reports to the Board and other agencies.
	- Plan and attend all Foundation Board meetings.
	- Assist the Foundation trustees with all Board duties and responsibilities.
	- Ensure the implementation of the Foundation and school system policies and practices.

	- Lead office systems to support all development projects and operations.
	- Supervise donor and gift record\-keeping.
	- Coordinate research activities.
	- Oversee the management of databases, records, files, and gift processing.
	- Direct the pledge reminder, acknowledgement, and scholarship programs.
	- Lead, design, and manage the Foundation's research and grant procurement processes.
+ Lead the planning and execution of our annual Gwinnett Sports Hall of Fame event.
	- Conduct committee meeting to elect new members.
	- Coordinate sales efforts with the Foundation team.
	- Conduct meetings with the Foundation Executive and Full Board to discuss the event and get their help to ensure a successful evening.
	- Work directly with the Director of Development as needed.

	- Manage and maintain the employee/retiree database.
	- Lead the employee/retiree giving campaign.
	- Organize and support employee/retiree associations.
	- Organize retiree events, collect news and information about retirees for publication, and maintain accurate records of the school system retirees.

	- Conduct the corporate and community giving campaign.

	- Work with the Chief Financial Officer to develop the Foundation budget and monthly and annual reports.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS

Full\-Time, Exempt  
Location: Cornelius, NC (On\-site)  
Salary Range: $90,000–$105,000, commensurate with experience

ABOUT CAIN CENTER FOR THE ARTS

Cain Center for the Arts is a multidisciplinary arts organization serving the Lake Norman region with a mission to provide exceptional visual arts, performing arts, and community experiences. Cain Center operates a growing multi\-venue campus including Cain Center for the Arts, Goodrum House, and Puckett Pottery House. The organization presents professional performances, offers a wide range of arts education programs, produces visual arts exhibitions, and partners with the community to expand access to the arts. As Cain Center continues to expand, the organization is focused on building strong operational systems, clear leadership alignment, and sustainable infrastructure to support long\-term growth.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Cain Center is seeking a Director of Operations to serve as a senior leader responsible for the overall performance, alignment, and continuous improvement of operations across the organization’s multi\-venue environment. This role is accountable for the success of operations across the organization—not for directly executing the work of individual departments. The Director of Operations leads through a team of experienced managers and directors who are responsible for execution within their areas, ensuring that their work is strategically aligned, well\-coordinated, and consistently delivered at a high level.

The Director of Operations serves as the organization’s central operational integrator, aligning people, systems, and resources to support:

* Performing arts programming
* Education and community programs
* Rentals and external partnerships
* Patron and guest experiences

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of best practices in operating multi\-disciplinary arts organizations and facilities and can apply that knowledge to strengthen systems, improve alignment, and support continued growth.

REPORTING STRUCTURE

Reports to: Executive Director

Direct Reports:

* Facilities Manager (and building services team)
* Technical Director (and production staff)
* Patron Services Manager (and front\-of\-house team)
* Food \& Beverage Manager
* Volunteer Services Manager

LEADERSHIP APPROACH

The Director of Operations leads a team of functional managers responsible for execution across facilities, production, patron services, food \& beverage, and volunteer engagement.

Success in this role requires the ability to:

* Lead through clarity of direction rather than direct execution
* Set goals and expectations that align team performance with organizational priorities
* Develop and support team leaders while holding them accountable for outcomes
* Ensure strong coordination across functions to deliver seamless programs and events
* Reinforce Cain Center’s culture of being hungry, humble, and smart

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Leadership

* Lead the overall operational performance of the organization across all venues
* Set clear priorities, goals, and standards for operational departments

**About Mustard Seed Christian Daycare** 

Mustard Seed Christian Daycare has grown from a small vision into a vibrant ministry serving families throughout Vermilion County and the surrounding area. Located in the former Rossville\-Alvin Grade School in Rossville, Illinois, Mustard Seed provides a nurturing, faith\-based environment where children can learn, grow, and thrive.

We serve over 90 children, offering both childcare and preschool programs. Through a combination of structured learning, creative play, and spiritual development, the daycare supports each child’s physical, emotional, cognitive, and spiritual growth. Daily activities include interactive classroom learning, Bible stories and lessons, arts and crafts, outdoor play, and special events that bring families and the community together.

Rooted in Christian values and committed to excellence, Mustard Seed continues to be a trusted place where seeds of faith, kindness, and knowledge are planted every day.

**Role Summary**

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the strategic and operational leader of Mustard Seed Christian Daycare, a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization. This role is responsible for overseeing daily operations, staff leadership, financial sustainability, compliance, and community engagement, while advancing the mission and long\-term vision of the organization.

The ED works closely with the Board of Directors to ensure the daycare operates with excellence, integrity, and impact for the families and children it serves.

**Marketing \& Enrollment Growth**

* Lead enrollment strategy to maintain full capacity

**About Invest in Our Future**


Invest in Our Future (IOF) is a philanthropic initiative and strategy hub focused on accelerating clean energy deployment and unlocking clean energy benefits for all Americans. IOF brings together the power of philanthropy and partner organizations to unleash the enormous economic potential of clean energy to create good jobs for American workers, generate new investment in American communities, and reduce the pollution that causes climate change. Through our large and diverse portfolio of grantees, we support work to speed siting and permitting of utility\-scale projects; grow the market for community\-serving, commercial\-scale clean energy; expand the clean energy workforce and improve job quality; and build the durable public support needed for faster deployment. We coordinate and work closely with partners to align strategies and focus the field’s resources on the most pressing obstacles holding back clean energy buildout.

**Position Overview**


The Managing Director of Programs will lead and support a high\-performing team of Program Officers and Program Associates to ensure the organization’s grantmaking, convenings, and other programmatic work align with Invest in Our Future’s three\-year strategy. The Managing Director of Programs will oversee the program team’s grantmaking and workplan and will strive toward continuous improvement in systems, project management, and program delivery. The Managing Director of Programs will serve on IOF’s leadership team and report to the Executive Director.


The Managing Director of Programs also will work with the program team to understand the broader clean energy landscape, overcome external challenges to implementing IOF’s strategy, and identify opportunities to build new partnerships and tackle emerging issues in pursuit of expedited clean energy deployment.

jobs.description:
Making every moment matter — Join us in leading compassionate end\-of\-life care across the Adirondacks

Are you a visionary leader passionate about hospice care, community impact, and organizational excellence?

High Peaks Hospice is seeking an exceptional Executive Director to guide our mission of providing exceptional hospice and palliative care with dignity, compassion, and integrity. As our Chief Executive Officer, you will partner with the Board of Directors to shape the future of our organization and ensure high\-quality care for patients and families throughout our region.

**About High Peaks Hospice**

Headquartered in Hudson Falls, NY, with offices in Saranac Lake and Mineville, High Peaks Hospice serves a 5,400\-square\-mile medically underserved rural catchment area across upstate New York with an operating budget of 4\.5 million dollars. We are a mission\-driven nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting individuals and families facing life\-limiting illness. Our team delivers compassionate, patient\-centered care while fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and community connection.

**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director provides strategic, operational, and financial leadership to ensure organizational sustainability, regulatory compliance, and continued growth. This is a high\-impact role for a leader who thrives at the intersection of healthcare operations, fundraising, board governance, and community advocacy.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute a forward\-thinking strategic plan in partnership with the Board and senior leadership.
* Board Relations: Serve as the primary liaison to the Board, supporting effective governance and decision\-making.
* Operational Excellence: Oversee daily operations, clinical quality, and continuous improvement and foster effective and transparent communication among agency employees, board members, volunteers and community organizations.
* Financial Stewardship \& Fundraising: Manage budgets, drive revenue strategies, and cultivate donor relationships.
* Regulatory Compliance: Ensure full adherence to Medicare, NY State DOH, and all hospice standards.
* Team \& Culture: Build and lead a high\-performing, compassionate staff and volunteer team; be passionate about employee support and retention.
* Community Presence: Act as the public face of the organization, strengthening partnerships and advocacy among a diverse community of like\-minded groups.

**Qualifications**

Required:

* Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nonprofit Management, Nursing, or related field.
* 7\+ years of senior leadership experience, with at least 5 years in executive or director\-level roles.
* Proven experience in financial management, board relations, and fundraising.
* Strong knowledge of hospice/palliative care regulations and operations (preferred).

**Preferred:**

* Hospice or healthcare leadership experience.
* CHCE or similar certification.
* Demonstrated success in nonprofit fundraising and grant development.
* Familiarity with the North Country and the Adirondacks or similar experience in a decentralized rural hospice setting

**What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation and benefits package.
* Opportunity to make a profound difference in the lives of patients and families.
* Hybrid work environment with meaningful community engagement.
* A supportive Board and dedicated team committed to our mission.

Ready to lead with heart and vision?

This position reports to the Program Supervisor.

Elementary Afterschool Program Directors are key on-site supervisors managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Recruit, hire, and provide excellent supervision and support to all part time Group Leaders and Activity Specialists, Administrative Assistants, and Content Specialists.
Ensure the program is aligned to strategic objectives of PAL, policies and procedures, agency programming calendar, SACC regulations, and the contractual obligations of government and private funding sources including fire safety certification.

Coordinates with the Principal, Director, Regional Director, SYEP Director, and Head Quarters staff to grow creative programming opportunities unique to the Site.
Collects program data, analyzes and drives PAL forward with data driven recommendations.
Ensure strong reciprocal partnerships with NYPD, NYCPS school partner, DYCD, DOH and other Community partners aligned with PAL’s mission.
Plans and coordinates various citywide programs, activities, and special events.
Assists in the development of future funding grants and requests for proposals.
Provides mediation and troubleshooting for on-site issues.
Respond appropriately when time-sensitive mental health services are needed such as suicide prevention, grief, and loss due to death or incarceration of a family member.

jobs.title: Director of Communications
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

We’re looking for a Director of Communications to own how Relay communicates—externally in earned media, and internally across the company. This is a builder role: you’ll be our first dedicated comms hire, which means you’re starting from a position of real momentum—an active PR agency relationship, a brand campaign in market, and a growing media presence—and your job is to turn that into a durable communications function with the infrastructure, relationships, and editorial discipline to match where Relay is going.

The right candidate is a sharp, opinionated communications leader who has worked in a high-growth environment before, knows how to punch above their weight with limited resources, and brings a genuine point of view on how a brand earns trust in a crowded category. You’ll report directly to the VP of Marketing and partner closely with Brand, PMM, and the executive team to ensure what we say publicly reflects what we believe internally—and lands with the audiences that matter most.

What You'll Be Doing

Own Relay’s earned media presence end-to-end—media strategy, press coverage, executive thought leadership, and reactive comms—translating the brand narrative into stories that land with reporters, editors, and the audiences that matter most.
Lead the relationship with our PR agency, setting the strategic agenda, driving accountability on coverage outcomes, and ensuring the partnership is pulling in the same direction as internal priorities.
Build and manage a proactive media program—expanding relationships with reporters covering fintech, SMB, and entrepreneurship beats, pitching stories before they need to be pitched, and getting Relay into conversations we aren’t currently part of.
Own executive communications for the CEO and leadership team, including speech writing, op-eds, LinkedIn presence, and media prep—helping Relay’s founders show up as credible, recognizable voices in their category.
Drive communications around product launches, brand campaigns, and company milestones, partnering with PMM and Brand to build integrated announcement plans that earn coverage rather than just distribute press releases.
Monitor and protect brand reputation, with a clear-eyed crisis communications playbook and the instincts to know when something needs to move fast.
Measure what matters—share of voice, earned media quality, executive visibility, message pull-through, and internal comms reach—and use that data to sharpen strategy rather than just report it.

Who You Are

You have 8+ years in communications, PR, or corporate affairs roles, with meaningful experience at a high-growth SaaS, fintech, or consumer brand.
You’ve owned a media program before—you have reporter relationships you built yourself, coverage wins you drove personally, and a clear theory of what makes a story land.
You have strong executive communications chops: you’ve written for a CEO, shaped a founder’s public presence, and know how to coach someone who’s brilliant but not naturally a media personality.
You’re a skilled writer with a high editorial bar—you can cut through jargon, write for a small business owner, and tell a financial product story without making it sound like a financial product.
You’ve worked in a regulated or compliance-adjacent environment and know how to get the legal team to yes without losing the headline.
You’re a strategic operator who can build systems and processes, not just campaigns—you know what a mature comms function looks like and can run toward it from scratch.
You’re comfortable being the only one in the room who owns this function, which means you’re low-ego about doing the work while being high-conviction about the strategy.

Bonus Points

You have experience working with brands that serve small business owners or self-employed professionals.
You have a public POV on communications, media, or brand—newsletter, talks, a LinkedIn presence people actually follow.
You’ve navigated a major brand moment under pressure: a funding round, a product controversy, a category-defining campaign.

The Interview Process

Stage 1: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team
Stage 2: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the VP of Marketing
Stage 3: A 60-minute Google Meet Live Scenario with our Marketing team
Stage 4: A 60-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

Our Compensation Approach

We believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.

The annual salary range for this role is $216,000 USD to $264,000 USD.

For candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $240,000 USD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.

We encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub.

Why Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You

You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking "how can this be better?" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.
You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.
You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.
You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.
You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself.
You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.
You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. You actively seek input, sit with hard truths, and use feedback as fuel for improvement.
Small businesses are why we're here: Relay exists to help them thrive -- and that mission has to resonate with you.

Join Us

We're looking for people who are relentless, curious, and care deeply about the work. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description -- your perspective and drive matter more. We welcome diverse backgrounds and people who think critically, challenge the status quo, and want to help small businesses thrive.

If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please reach out to your Talent Partner.

Disclaimer: For compliance reasons, all offers of employment at Relay are conditional upon a successful background check and employment verification through Certn.

jobs.description:
The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
is one of the world’s leading manufacturers, marketers, and sellers of quality skin care, makeup, fragrance, and hair care products, and is a steward of luxury and prestige brands globally. The company’s products are sold in approximately 150 countries and territories under brand names including: Estée Lauder, Aramis, Clinique, Lab Series, Origins, M·A·C, La Mer, Bobbi Brown Cosmetics, Aveda, Jo Malone London, Bumble and bumble, Darphin Paris, TOM FORD, Smashbox, AERIN Beauty, Le Labo, Editions de Parfums Frédéric Malle, GLAMGLOW, KILIAN PARIS, Too Faced, Dr.Jart+, the DECIEM family of brands, including The Ordinary and NIOD, and BALMAIN Beauty.

Description

This role is part of the Office of the Chief of Staff to the Chief Technology Office (CTO) for Technology, Data & Analytics (TD&A). The Executive Director, Transformation Enablement is responsible for enabling enterprise-wide adoption, operational readiness, and organizational effectiveness across major Technology transformation initiatives. This role serves as the connective tissue between strategy and execution by ensuring the organization is prepared, aligned, equipped, and capable of successfully adopting new ways of working, operating models, technologies, and practices.

This role will work horizontally across Technology, Data & Analytics functions, partnering with initiative leaders, portfolio management, HR, communications, finance, and business stakeholders to ensure transformation programs are effectively operationalized and embedded into the organization.

Key Considerations

This role requires a highly collaborative enterprise leader who can work across organizational boundaries to drive alignment, readiness, and adoption of transformational change initiatives.
Must possess deep expertise in organizational transformation, change enablement, operating model evolution, and large-scale technology adoption.
Requires the ability to translate strategic priorities into scalable enablement frameworks, practical change interventions and organizational actions.
Must balance strategic thinking with operational execution and hands-on implementation support.
High emotional intelligence and influencing capability are critical to navigate organizational complexity and varying levels of transformation maturity.
Requires strong executive presence and the ability to engage credibly with senior leadership while also driving execution with working teams.
This role is expected to identify organizational friction points, adoption risks, capability gaps, and execution barriers across initiatives and proactively drive mitigation strategies.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

Technology Transformation Enablement

Lead the development and execution of enterprise-wide enablement strategies supporting Technology, Data & Analytics transformation initiatives.
Partner with strategic initiative leaders and functional executives to ensure organizational readiness and successful adoption of new capabilities, processes, and operating models.
Establish scalable transformation enablement frameworks, methodologies, and approaches across TD&A.
Identify organizational barriers, dependencies, capability gaps, and change impacts that may affect successful transformation execution.
Drive alignment across initiatives to ensure consistent approaches to change adoption, engagement, and operationalization.

Organizational Readiness & Adoption

Develop readiness assessments, adoption metrics, stakeholder engagement strategies, and enablement plans for major transformation programs.
Partner with leadership teams, HR, communications to ensure effective rollout and adoption strategies.
Oversee organizational enablement activities including role clarity, process transition support, governance adoption, and operating model implementation.
Ensure leaders and teams are equipped with the tools, communications, and support needed to execute transformation initiatives effectively.
Monitor organizational adoption and effectiveness metrics and proactively address areas of resistance or execution risk.

Key Roles & Responsibilities (Continued)

Operating Model & Ways of Working Enablement

Support the evolution and operationalization of new technology operating models and cross-functional ways of working.
Drive consistency and discipline in transformation execution practices across TD&A.
Partner with leadership to identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve organizational effectiveness, and accelerate decision-making.
Enable scalable governance and execution models that support enterprise agility and transformation maturity.

Cross-Functional Transformation Leadership

Serve as a trusted advisor and thought partner to TD&A leaders on organizational transformation and enablement strategies.
Connect efforts across multiple transformation initiatives to ensure cohesive execution and minimize organizational disruption.
Support executive leadership in driving cultural and behavioral shifts necessary to achieve transformation objectives.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 12+ years of experience in organizational transformation, technology enablement, operating model transformation, management consulting, or enterprise change leadership roles.
Strong understanding of Technology, Data & Analytics organizations and large-scale enterprise transformation environments.
Proven experience enabling complex, cross-functional technology or operational transformation programs.
Experience working within highly matrixed global organizations and influencing senior executive stakeholders.
Organizational transformation & enablement: deep expertise in driving organizational readiness, adoption, and operationalization of large-scale transformation initiatives.
Strategic execution: ability to translate strategic priorities into actionable enablement frameworks, governance structures, and execution plans.
Change leadership: strong ability to guide organizations through ambiguity, resistance, and organizational change while maintaining alignment and momentum. Experienced use of change frameworks.
Operating model design & optimization: experience enabling new organizational structures, governance frameworks, ways of working.
Executive influence & collaboration: exceptional interpersonal and influencing skills with the ability to build trust and alignment across senior leadership teams.
Problem solving & systems thinking: ability to identify interconnected organizational challenges and develop practical, scalable solutions.
Communication & facilitation: strong communication and facilitation skills with the ability to engage diverse audiences and drive alignment across functions.

Pay Range

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $177,100.00
to $304,500.00
. Exact salary depends on several factors such as experience, skills, education, and budget. Salary range may vary based on geographic location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for participation in a highly competitive bonus program as well as participation in the share incentive plan. In addition,

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for participation in a highly competitive bonus program with the possibility for overachievement based on performance and company results. In addition, The Estée Lauder Companies offers a variety of benefits to eligible employees, including health insurance coverage (medical, dental, and vision insurance), wellness and family support programs, life and disability insurance, retirement savings plans, paid leave programs, education-related programs, paid holidays and vacation time, and many others. Many of these benefits are subsidized or fully paid for by the company.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Tort Unit
jobs.description:
The New York City Comptroller’s Office works to promote the financial health, integrity, and effectiveness of New York City government, in order to strengthen trust, secure a thriving future for all New Yorkers, and build a more just, equitable, and resilient city. Led by an independently elected citywide official, the comptroller’s office provides checks and balances needed to hold City government accountable for budgeting wisely, investing responsibly, operating efficiently, acting fairly, living up to its obligations and promises, and paying attention to the long-term challenges we face together.

Authorized by the New York City Charter, the Comptroller, through the Bureau of Law and Adjustment (BLA), negotiates and approves all monetary settlement of claims and lawsuits involving the City of New York. BLA investigates and, when in the best interest of the city, settles pre-litigation claims for and against the City of New York. In resolving claims before litigation is commenced, BLA protects the fiscal interest of the City while ensuring that pre-litigation claims are resolved in a fair and just manner, and in accordance with applicable laws. BLA furthers this goal in its review, evaluation, and authorization of requests to settle litigated cases involving the City and through diligent administration of disputes arising out of City contracts. BLA manages City risk by holding agencies accountable, rooting out fraud, and identifying trends, as well as, coordinating with the Law Department and other City agencies on issues that impact the public fiscal and public safety.

Responsibilities

The Deputy Director, Tort Unit reports directly to the Director, Tort Unit, under the general direction of the Assistant Comptroller for the Bureau of Law and Adjustment. Duties and responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to the following:

Advise and assist the Director in managing and directing all functions of the Tort Unit, including overseeing the day-to-day operations, and in the Director’s absence, perform the Director’s duties;
Supervise all Tort Division Chiefs and Claim Examiners and ensure duties are performed in accordance with the highest professional standards; manage the pre-litigation settlement process of tort claims and the 50h process, ensure the proper handling of no-fault claims and affirmative property damage claims and managing claim support;
Assist the Director in bureau-wide operational projects and managing the procurement of Bureau professional services such as the Statutory 50-h contract and the purchasing of those services;
Monitor high-profile and high-exposure claims and perform legal research and draft memoranda on critical issues affecting pre-litigation claims; delegate within independent authority and with discretion, appropriate monetary settlement authority to Tort Division staff;
Resolve claim payment issues including coordinating with Office of General Counsel on lien issues and serving as one of the principal liaisons between the Bureau of Law & Adjustment and the Office of Fiscal Services; assist in the managing of the Son of Sam process including coordinating with the NYS Office of Attorney General;
Coordinating with the FOIL Officer, Press Office and Community Action Center to respond to requests for information which includes validation of reports and information;
Identify trends and changes in municipal litigation, including recent case law developments, and provide relevant recommendations to the Director, Assistant Comptroller, and other executive staff;
Assist BLA units in liability and damages evaluation; provide efficient and effective risk management assessment strategies and recommendations with respect to claims filed against various City agencies;
Handle administrative matters, including but not limited to, data/technology, human resources, and any other administrative issues assigned by the Director; assist the Director in the annual staff evaluations in accordance with human resources protocol; develop and present professional development and legal training to new and existing staff; and,
Perform all other duties as requested by the Director and Assistant Comptroller as needed.

EXECUTIVE AGENCY COUNSEL - 95005

Minimum Qualifications

Admission to the New York State Bar; and four years of recent full-time responsible, relevant, satisfactory legal experience subsequent to admission to any bar, eighteen months of which must have been in the supervision of other attorneys, in an administrative, managerial or executive capacity, or performing highly complex and significant legal work.

Incumbents must remain Members of the New York State Bar in good standing for the duration of this employment.

Preferred Skills

Extensive legal experience that includes assessing all aspects of tort litigation and adjusting personal injury claims - 3+ years of supervisory experience, supervising attorneys or other professional staff - Strong management skills - Exceptional writing and verbal skills, attention to detail, and the ability to perform multiple tasks that require prioritization - Solid analytical and negotiation skills - Demonstrated proficiency in drafting clear, concise, and accurate memoranda - Excellent interpersonal and organization skills, with a demonstrated ability to interact professionally and effectively with all levels of management, government officials, attorneys, and the public - Fundamental understanding of the relationship between the Comptroller’s Office and the Law Department with respect to claims and lawsuits.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness

As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal loan forgiveness programs and state repayment assistance programs. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website at https://studentaid.gov/pslf/.

Residency Requirement

New York City Residency is not required for this position

Additional Information

The organization serves lakefront property owners, seasonal residents, recreational users, and the broader community.

The Executive Director reports to the Board President and will work closely with the chairs of the Membership, Communications and Fundraising working groups. This is a hands-on and leadership role within a working-board culture: board members will continue to be hands-on in carrying out committee-endorsed actions. The Executive Director does not intend to shift the Board to an exclusively advisory function, but rather to extend what the organization can accomplish.

Job Title: Open Rank Deputy Director Associate Professor or Professor

Job Summary:

The Deputy Director will serve as a senior leader within the Katy O. and Paul M. Rady Esophageal and Gastric Center of Excellence, supporting the continued growth and national visibility of the Center’s research, clinical, education, and outreach initiatives. This full-time faculty leadership position is based on the University of Colorado Anschutz in Aurora, Colorado, and will work collaboratively across the University of Colorado Cancer Center, School of Medicine, UCHealth, and partner institutions.

This role will focus heavily on advancing translational and clinically driven research initiatives in esophageal and gastric diseases while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration among clinicians, researchers, trainees, and institutional leadership. The Deputy Director will help shape the strategic direction of the Center and support the development of innovative programs that improve patient outcomes, expand research opportunities, strengthen education and mentorship initiatives, and elevate the Center’s national reputation.

The successful candidate will bring a collaborative and entrepreneurial leadership approach, strong emotional intelligence, and the ability to develop meaningful partnerships across academic medicine, philanthropy, and research communities.

Key Responsibilities:

Provide strategic leadership for basic, translational, and clinical research initiatives related to esophageal and gastric diseases.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary faculty, clinicians, researchers, and institutional leadership to advance the mission and strategic priorities of the Rady Center of Excellence.
Develop and expand research programs, including investigator-initiated studies, collaborative research efforts, and clinical trials.
Identify and pursue external funding opportunities, including federal grants, foundation funding, and philanthropic partnerships.
Mentor faculty, fellows, trainees, and early-career investigators in research development, academic advancement, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Represent the Rady Center at local, regional, national, and international meetings, conferences, and professional organizations.
Assist with the development and implementation of strategic plans, annual goals, and operational priorities for the Center.
Contribute to the preparation of annual reports, presentations, and programmatic updates for institutional leadership, advisory groups, and donors.
Support efforts related to education, outreach, advocacy, and community engagement initiatives aligned with the mission of the Center.
Evaluate research progress, data reporting, and continuous improvement activities to ensure alignment with institutional goals and regulatory standards.
Foster an inclusive and collaborative culture that promotes innovation, mentorship, and excellence in patient-centered research and care.

Work Location:

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, CO

Why Join Us:

The Katy O. and Paul M. Rady Esophageal and Gastric Center of Excellence was established in late 2022 in the hopes of advancing esophageal and gastric cancer research, clinical trials, screening, and treatments. This Center of Excellence was established through a generous gift from the Rady family in honor of their late family member, Paul R. O’Hara II, who was treated at the University of Colorado Anschutz Cancer Center.

The Esophageal and Gastric Cancer Multidisciplinary Clinic brings together a team of expert surgeons, gastroenterologists, pathologists, oncologists, radiologists, and more focused on the esophagus and stomach. Together, the team analyzes a patient’s diagnosis and recommends a specific treatment plan for the individual. Not only does the clinic focus on patients with precancerous and cancerous lesions of the esophagus and stomach, but they have also established a benign clinic that has a specialized team who treats patients with noncancerous conditions of the esophagus.
